Cargo: upgrade rand v0.9.4 → v0.10.1
description:
Major upgrade surfaced by cargo-upgrade survey 2026-05-04; RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-27 (audit bd-a0eyjshu) — still real, but the original description was imprecise.

Corrected state as of 2026-07-27:
- The only DIRECT declaration is 'rand = "0.9"' in crates/quarto-hub/Cargo.toml. It is not workspace-wide (the original 'range-pinned in workspace' wording was wrong).
- Latest stable upstream is 0.10.2 (the strand's original 0.10.1 target has itself moved on).
- Cargo.lock already carries rand 0.10.1 TRANSITIVELY via automerge 0.10.0, so the workspace is already building both 0.9.x and 0.10.x. Upgrading quarto-hub's direct dep would collapse that duplicate.
- A third copy, rand 0.8.6, comes via grass_compiler -> grass -> quarto-system-runtime and is NOT addressable from here (upstream's constraint).

Actionable work: bump crates/quarto-hub/Cargo.toml to rand 0.10, adapt to the 0.9 -> 0.10 breaking changes, run cargo xtask verify. Expected side benefit: one fewer duplicate in cargo tree --duplicates.

See claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-cargo-upgrade-survey.md and bd-hb8h.

c-122gx35c.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-122gx35c.text:
CORRECTION to my earlier description + work in progress (2026-07-27).

WRONG in the description I wrote earlier today: 'Expected side benefit: one fewer duplicate in cargo tree --duplicates.' It is not. Measured before/after: duplicate crate count is 101 both ways, and there are still three rand copies. Moving quarto-hub off 0.9 does not remove the 0.9 copy, because proptest 1.11.0 (a dev-dependency of our crates) requires rand ^0.9 independently. I asserted the collapse without checking who else needed 0.9.

FULL PICTURE of the three copies, from the real BUILD graph (cargo tree -i, not cargo metadata — the latter lists dev-deps of every registry crate and is badly misleading here):
- rand 0.10.2 <- automerge 0.10.0 + samod 0.12.1 (our fork) + NOW quarto-hub directly.
- rand 0.9.5 <- proptest 1.11.0, a dev-dependency. Not reachable from our manifests; would need proptest to move to rand 0.10. Dev-only, so it never ships in a binary.
- rand 0.8.6 <- grass_compiler 0.13.4 -> grass 0.13.4 -> quarto-system-runtime. grass 0.13.4 IS the latest release (checked crates.io), and it requires rand ^0.8. Not reachable at all short of patching or dropping grass.

So 'move everyone to 0.10.2' is not achievable; only our own declaration was.

WORK DONE on branch braid/bd-0a3b-rand-upgrade:
- crates/quarto-hub/Cargo.toml: rand "0.9" -> "0.10"; lockfile re-resolved (rand 0.9.4 -> 0.10.2; the 0.9.x line also moved 0.9.4 -> 0.9.5 for proptest).
- rand 0.10 API break, 3 sites (session.rs generate_sid, storage.rs server_secret + session_secret): 'use rand::RngCore' no longer resolves (not re-exported at crate root) and fill_bytes now comes from Rng. Changed to 'use rand::Rng'. All three generate security-sensitive values; rand::rng() is still ThreadRng (ChaCha CSPRNG) and Rng::fill_bytes delegates to the same RngCore impl, so randomness quality is unchanged. Noted in comments at each site.

REAL benefit (not duplicate reduction): quarto-hub now shares one rand with automerge and samod, the crates it actually hands RNGs to (e.g. DocumentId::new(&mut rand::rng())), removing a cross-version boundary at that call site.

cargo xtask verify running.

c-6zgpa6k0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-6zgpa6k0.text:
ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED 2026-07-27 — blocked upstream, not doable as a standalone bump.

Carlos asked whether we could move everyone to rand 0.10.2. Answer: no, and the reason is more interesting than the API rename.

What I tried (branch braid/bd-0a3b-rand-upgrade, now deleted, tree restored to main):
1. crates/quarto-hub/Cargo.toml rand "0.9" -> "0.10", lockfile re-resolved.
2. Fixed the rand 0.10 API break at 3 sites (session.rs generate_sid, storage.rs server_secret + session_secret): RngCore is no longer re-exported at the crate root and fill_bytes now comes from Rng, so 'use rand::RngCore' -> 'use rand::Rng'. cargo build -p quarto-hub then PASSED.
3. cargo xtask verify FAILED at clippy (--all-targets), exposing the real blocker: samod::DocumentId::new takes a rand 0.9 'impl Rng' in its public API, so 8 call sites in access_policy.rs's test module cannot pass a rand 0.10 ThreadRng. Filed as the blocking strand.

Also CORRECTING my own earlier claim on this strand: I said the upgrade would collapse a duplicate. It would NOT. Measured 101 duplicate crates before and after, still three rand copies. quarto-hub leaving 0.9 does not remove 0.9 because proptest 1.11.0 (dev-dep) needs it independently.

Final state of the three copies, from the build graph:
- rand 0.10.2 <- automerge 0.10.0, samod 0.12.1
- rand 0.9.5 <- proptest 1.11.0 (dev-dependency; never ships)
- rand 0.8.6 <- grass_compiler 0.13.4 -> grass 0.13.4 -> quarto-system-runtime. grass 0.13.4 is the LATEST release and requires rand ^0.8 — unreachable without patching or dropping grass.

So even after this strand and its blocker are done, two rand copies remain, both upstream-constrained. The real benefit of the bump is coherence — quarto-hub would share one rand with automerge/samod, the crates it hands RNGs to — not duplicate reduction.

Status back to open, now blocked.

title: Fix CRLF handling in tree-sitter-qmd grammar.js for pipe tables
description: Tree-sitter grammar at crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js parses pipe tables incorrectly when input uses CRLF line endings. With LF input, the pipe table closes at the blank line and following content becomes a separate block. With CRLF input, the table absorbs the following paragraph as a malformed body row. Bug propagates through pampa end-to-end: rendered Pandoc AST is structurally wrong for any Windows user with core.autocrlf=true (default) authoring a pipe table followed by a paragraph. Affects all output formats (HTML, PDF, Word) since Pandoc AST is upstream of every writer. Surfaced 2026-04-24 during PR 109 Windows verification as 5 failing pipe-table corpus tests; investigation in bd-ntnx classified it as a real grammar bug, not a corpus formatting issue. Full reproducer and observed parse trees in the design field. Cross-reference q2-windows-verify-tests memory note for related Windows CRLF failures.
design:
Reproducer. Two layers, both diagnostic. Layer 1 tests grammar.js directly. Layer 2 tests the full pampa pipeline that real users hit. Fixtures live in the tree-sitter-markdown directory so tree-sitter parse picks up the configured grammar without an init-config step.

Layer 1 (grammar.js):

printf "before\r\n\r\n| a | b |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| 1 | 2 |\r\n\r\nafter\r\n" > crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-crlf.qmd
printf "before\n\n| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |\n\nafter\n" > crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-lf.qmd
cd crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown
tree-sitter parse test-crlf.qmd > test-crlf.parse
tree-sitter parse test-lf.qmd > test-lf.parse
diff test-crlf.parse test-lf.parse

Layer 2 (pampa end-to-end):

cargo run --quiet -p pampa --bin pampa -- crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-crlf.qmd > pampa-crlf.out
cargo run --quiet -p pampa --bin pampa -- crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-lf.qmd > pampa-lf.out
diff pampa-crlf.out pampa-lf.out

Observed parse trees from Layer 1 on this branch (fix/windows-tree-sitter-crlf at 80f07171). Both trees agree on the prefix, so the divergence is the trailing block:

LF (correct, table closes at the blank line):
  pipe_table [2, 0] - [5, 0]
    pipe_table_header [2, 0] - [2, 9] ...
    pipe_table_delimiter_row [3, 0] - [3, 9] ...
    pipe_table_row [4, 0] - [4, 9] ...
  pandoc_paragraph [6, 0] - [7, 0]
    pandoc_str [6, 0] - [6, 5]

CRLF (buggy, table absorbs following paragraph):
  pipe_table [2, 0] - [7, 0]
    pipe_table_header [2, 0] - [2, 9] ...
    pipe_table_delimiter_row [3, 0] - [3, 9] ...
    pipe_table_row [4, 0] - [4, 9] ...
    pipe_table_row [6, 0] - [6, 5]   <- SPURIOUS, should be a separate paragraph
      pipe_table_cell [6, 0] - [6, 5]
        pandoc_str [6, 0] - [6, 5]

Observed Pandoc AST from Layer 2 (pampa default -t native), confirming the bug propagates past pampa input handling:

LF: [Para [Str "before"], Table ... [body row [1,2]], Para [Str "after"]]
CRLF: [Para [Str "before"], Table ... [body rows [1,2] AND [Plain "after"]]]   <- no trailing Para

Confirms pampa does NOT normalize line endings before feeding the grammar. End-user impact: any qmd document with CRLF endings, a pipe table, and following content produces structurally wrong output in every writer that consumes Pandoc AST.

Open design questions for the fix.

1. Locate the bug in grammar.js. Likely candidates: newline character classes that match only \n, or the external scanner (scanner.cc) handling of block boundary detection. Read both grammar.js and any external scanner before patching. Tree-sitter-markdown forks vary on this — confirm what our fork does versus what works.

2. Upstream vs local fix. This grammar is forked from MDeiml/tree-sitter-markdown (or whichever upstream we track — confirm in tree-sitter.json or README). If upstream already fixes this, cherry-pick. If not, patch locally and consider an upstream PR.

3. Test-corpus line-ending policy after the fix. Two viable strategies:
   a. Keep test/corpus/*.txt files materialized as CRLF on Windows checkout and rely on the fixed grammar to parse them identically. Tests then exercise CRLF on Windows and LF on Linux, which is useful coverage but creates a small risk that future grammar changes regress CRLF handling silently when only Linux CI runs.
   b. Pin test/corpus/*.txt to LF via .gitattributes (eol=lf for that subdirectory only) and add a separate Windows-only regression test that re-creates the fixtures with CRLF and asserts the parse trees match. More explicit, less coverage drift.

   The choice depends on whether we expect frequent grammar changes and whether ubuntu-only CI is sustainable. Recommend deciding before landing the grammar fix.

4. Audit other CRLF patterns. The 5 failing pipe-table tests are the surface; there may be other constructs whose grammar paths assume \n only. Grep grammar.js (and scanner.cc if present) for \n usages and audit each one.

Reference. Investigation history and original framing in bd-ntnx (closed). Memory note q2-windows-verify-tests catalogues related Windows CRLF failures.
acceptance_criteria: tree-sitter parse on matched CRLF and LF qmd inputs produces identical S-expression trees for pipe-table fixtures (Layer 1 reproducer diff is empty). pampa default native output is identical for the same matched inputs (Layer 2 reproducer diff is empty). All 5 originally-failing pipe-table tests under cd crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown && tree-sitter test pass on Windows: Example 201 (GFM), Pipe table can precede content (two variants), Pipe table can follow content, Pipe table with blank-line caption. cargo xtask verify step 4 (tree-sitter test) passes on Windows. cargo nextest run --workspace and cargo xtask verify continue to pass on Linux CI (no regression). Decision recorded in commit message or PR description for upstream-vs-local fix and for test-corpus line-ending policy. Audit findings recorded for any other CRLF patterns discovered in grammar.js or scanner.cc. q2-windows-verify-tests memory note updated with PR link and resolution.

title: nested_cell_mask doesn't cover inline expressions, so a displayed `{r} x` still executes
description:
The nested-cell mask (claude-notes/plans/2026-09-02-nested-cell-masking.md, "Make q2 self-documenting again: don't execute a cell that is being displayed") suppresses execution of an executable *fence opener* inside a markdown-displaying CodeBlock. It does not cover *inline* expressions, so an inline brace expression inside a display block still runs.

WHY IT DIDN'T APPLY BEFORE
The mask's Scope section lists what is deliberately out (RawBlock, doubled-brace, {=html} openers, cells nested in cells). Inline expressions are not on that list because they were not reachable: q2 never evaluated the `{r} expr` spelling at all. bd-inline-r-brace-spelling-not-evaluated-lk9s3iwe made that spelling live, which is what opens this hole. The fix for that strand is correct and matches Quarto 1; this is the follow-on the mask needs to stay whole.

MEASURED, q2 (with the inline fix) vs Quarto 1 99.9.9. Fixture: knitr document, `v <- \"EVALUATED\"`, then each form. EVALUATED means the escape failed.

  form                              q2              Q1
  plain prose                       executes        executes   (the feature)
  `` `{r} v` `` extra backticks     executes        executes
  `{{r}} v` doubled brace           shows {{r}} v   shows {r} v
  inside a ````markdown block       executes        executes
  inside a ````r block              executes        executes

Two consequences:
1. The escape q2 documents for cells -- wrap it in a longer fence -- does not work for inline expressions, so guides/authoring/computations.qmd has to document a different rule for the inline case than for the cell case.
2. The only working escape is the doubled brace, and q2 displays it verbatim ({{r}}) where Q1 collapses it to {r}. So a q2 author currently has no way to show a reader the text `{r} x`. Note q2's literal rendering is defensible on its own terms -- collapsing doubled braces is what Q-2-50 deliberately dropped so Jinja/Mustache templates render correctly -- which is why the fence-wrapper route, not brace-collapsing, is the right fix.

SHAPE OF THE FIX
Small and contained. `mask_code_block_text` (crates/quarto-core/src/engine/nested_cell_mask.rs) is the single rewrite site; add an inline pattern alongside MASK_OPENER_RE that rewrites an inline `{lang}` marker inside an in-scope CodeBlock the same way the opener is rewritten. `unmask` needs no change: UNMASK_OPENER_RE is deliberately not line-anchored (H4, for blockquote prefixes), so it already restores a mid-line occurrence.

Mind the plan's invariants: byte-exact restore is load-bearing for reconcile (spec section 'Reconcile -- why byte-exactness is load-bearing'), and the test-seam spec is frozen, so this wants its own tier rather than being bolted onto an existing one.

Also worth deciding: whether the empty-classes / `markdown`-only display-class predicate is right for inline too, or whether the inline case should be widened (an author writing ````r to show inline syntax gets nothing today -- the E row above).

Docs: guides/authoring/computations.qmd's 'Writing about an inline expression' section documents today's behaviour and should be simplified to match the cell rule once this lands.

Fixed on braid/bd-0gwekaem-nested-cell-mask-inline-expressions @ 8e13ecf8b (off main @ 914f20697). Not pushed.

MASKED SPELLING. One rewrite for both inline spellings: the marker is inserted directly after the opening backtick, so ````r v```` becomes ````q2-nested-executable r v```` and ````{r} v```` becomes ````q2-nested-executable {r} v````. unmask deletes the same fixed string. This departs from the strand's suggestion that UNMASK_OPENER_RE could restore the brace form for free: it can, but the classic spelling has no brace to work with and would need its own rule regardless, and two masked spellings buy nothing over one. Insert-only/delete-only also gives the strongest byte-exactness argument available, which the plan says is load-bearing for reconcile.

MASK_INLINE_RE = (^|[^`])`((?:\{[A-Za-z0-9_]+\}|r)[ \t#][^`]+)`

- Brace form: any [A-Za-z0-9_]+, engine-agnostic, matching MASK_OPENER_RE's language class and Q1's per-language executeInlineCodeHandler. Doubled braces excluded by the same first-char rule as openers.
- Classic form: literal r only. It is knitr's own rmarkdown syntax and is hardcoded to r in all_patterns$md$inline.code; generalizing it to any word would rewrite every ordinary code span in displayed prose.
- Separator [ \t#] is the union of knitr's [ #] and q2's [ \t] -- the mask has to be a superset of every scanner that could claim the expression.
- The (^|[^`]) guard is the bd-knitr-inline-r-eats-fence-2ofk91x1 shape: without it a nested fence's third backtick anchors a match. It excludes only a backtick, not a backslash -- knitr does not exclude one either, and the YAML-fallback case that motivates INLINE_R_PATTERN's backslash guard is text this mask never sees. Accepted limitation, shared with INLINE_R_PATTERN and Q1: two expressions with no character between them leave the second unmasked.

DISPLAY-CLASS PREDICATE: left narrow (empty or ["markdown"]), and filed as bd-tiidc899. Three reasons. It is not inline-specific -- the same predicate gates both rewrites, so widening changes the cell escape too, which 2026-09-02-nested-cell-masking.md scoped out explicitly. Widening for inline only would give the incoherent rule '````r protects your inline expressions but not your nested fences'. And T18 is frozen and revert-bound to the narrow predicate. Narrow is also parity: the strand's own matrix has Q1 executing in a ````r block too.

TESTS: new tier, own hunk ids, T1-T24 untouched. H14 mask rewrites an inline marker, H15 unmask restores it, H16 the guard. T25/T26 render-tier (real knitr); T27 x9 round-trip byte-exactness (classic, brace, tab, hash, two-on-a-line, bare fence, blockquoted, multiline body, opener+inline together); T28 a live cell's backtick-quoted R name untouched; T29 the guard; T30 engine-agnostic brace + doubled brace out of scope; T31 binds to the production scanner -- resolve_inline_r_expressions leaves the masked text alone while the control unmasked text is rewritten, which is the inline counterpart of T14 and starts discriminating the brace half automatically when the {r} alternation lands.

VACUITY FOUND AND FIXED: the first draft of T25 used INLINE-RAN as its runtime-only marker and passed with H14 reverted. q2's classic spelling escapes markdown specials, so the executed value reaches the HTML as INLINE\-RAN and the contains() check was blind to it. Marker changed to INLINERAN; both render rows confirmed RED under a reverted H14 before the fix was restored. A runtime-only marker used with an inline expression must survive .QuartoInlineRender's escaping unchanged -- recorded in the test file.

VERIFICATION: workspace 13692 passed / 199 skipped, +16 over the 13676 baseline, no removals. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean. End-to-end with a freshly built q2 on the strand's repro: the ````markdown row now renders 'Inline: `r v`' where main renders 'Inline: EVALUATED'; the ````r row still renders EVALUATED (bd-tiidc899).

DOCS: no change here. The 'Writing about an inline expression' section the strand names does not exist on main -- it is added by bd-inline-r-brace-spelling-not-evaluated-lk9s3iwe's second commit. Simplifying it belongs with that merge; docs/guides/authoring/computations.qmd on main only documents the cell rule, which stays accurate.

title: Five near-copies of pandoc stringify with subtly different semantics
description:
Rendering Inlines to plain text is implemented five times in the tree, and no two agree on the details. Any consumer picking one by name rather than by semantics gets a silent behaviour surprise.

- pampa::lua::utils::stringify_inline/stringify_inlines - private + behind the lua-filter feature. SoftBreak/LineBreak -> "\\n". Backs pandoc.utils.stringify.
- pampa::writers::plaintext::inlines_to_string - public. Keeps a Code span's backticks (locked by a test at plaintext.rs:483) and emits Math as raw TeX.
- quarto_core::template::inlines_to_text - private. Breaks -> " ", Code -> text without backticks.
- quarto_core::transforms::listing_render::inlines_to_text - private, another copy.
- quarto_core::transforms::reference_link_diagnostics::push_rendered - added by bd-q249-message-drops-inline-content-pacg3qeu, because none of the four above had the semantics that diagnostic needs (Code without backticks AND breaks as spaces, since the result goes inside a one-line warning).

The differences are real, not accidental: backtick handling and break handling each have a defensible answer per consumer. So this is not a straight de-duplication - it wants one canonical walk with explicit options (break rendering, code rendering) and the call sites migrated deliberately, each with a test pinning the choice it depends on.

Noticed while fixing Q-2-49's message. Out of scope there: that fix needed one correct string, not a refactor of the other four call sites.

title: Source-info threading through listing markdown re-parse
description:
L3's ListingRenderTransform invokes pampa::readers::qmd::read on doctemplate output to obtain Pandoc blocks, then discards the fresh SourceContext. Diagnostics from that re-parse are collapsed into a single Q-12-10 host-page warning naming the listing id and first message — not threaded back to the host page's SourceContext.

For a proper design, a way is needed to merge the fresh SourceContext from the re-parse into the host page's SourceContext, *and* preserve the chain 'host YAML key → template substitution → markdown span' through to the diagnostic. Likely cuts across quarto-source-map, quarto-doctemplate, and the diagnostic-builder layer. Worth its own design session.

Discovered while writing L3 (bd-ml8z) sub-plan; see D3 in claude-notes/plans/2026-05-06-listings-L3-resolve-transform.md.

title: Listings: field-required is parsed but never enforced (Q1 validateItem errors per missing field)
description:
Listing config accepts 'field-required: [title, date, ...]' — parse_listings stores it on Listing.field_required (crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/config.rs:492) — but nothing in the tree reads it. Q1 enforces it in validateItem (website-listing-read.ts): for each hydrated item, every field named in field-required must be present, otherwise the render fails with 'An item in the listing <id> is missing the required field <field>' (with per-source wording for files, YAML files, and inline records). q2 silently renders the listing as if the key were absent.

Applies to every item kind (glob-matched documents, and inline contents: records once bd-listing-inline-contents-tyy446ze lands — that strand's Q-12-21 covers only the no-title/no-path record case, not author-declared requirements).

Scope: after hydration/overlay and before include/exclude filters in ListingGenerateTransform, check each item against listing.field_required — curated fields via the same lookup filter.rs/sort.rs use, custom fields via extra. Decide severity with the user: Q1 is a hard error; a warning that drops the offending item (keeping the page renderable, like Q-12-20's fallback) may fit q2's diagnostics style better. New Q-12-* code + docs page + sidebar entry in the same commit. Document 'field-required' on the listings guide (docs/guides/projects/listings.qmd, seeded by the inline-records plan).

Found while planning bd-listing-inline-contents-tyy446ze (claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-listing-inline-contents.md §'Out of scope').

title: Phase D follow-up: SPA render-event hook + dep-graph filter regression tests
description:
Two related affordances needed once Phase D's dep-graph filter for re-render is implemented:

1. **SPA render-event hook.** PreviewApp's render useEffect re-fires for every contentTick bump. Today this is invisible at the DOM when neither active-page content nor merged metadata change. A small test-only counter (window.__renderTicks or similar) would let Playwright assert 'this edit did/didn't trigger a re-render' for cases where the rendered output is identical.

2. **Dep-graph filter regression tests.** Once Phase D filters re-renders against ProjectDependencyGraph, we need:
   - Active page re-renders when an edited sibling IS a dependency (positive case).
   - Active page does NOT re-render when an edited sibling is NOT a dependency (negative case — the savings).

Reframes the deferred Phase B.4 plan acceptance criterion 3 ('editing an unrelated sibling re-renders the active page only when there's a dep edge'). In Phase B the contract was relaxed to 'always re-renders' because no filter exists; Phase D restores the original strict contract.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-13-q2-preview-phase-b.md §B.4 (deferred criterion 3).
close_reason: Both items resolved: (1) window.__renderTicks render-event hook landed in D.3 (bd-kw93.9, commit 1ddcbeaf); (2) dep-graph filter regression tests landed in D.6 (bd-kw93.12, commit 7310d44b) — negative case in dep-graph-filter.spec.ts, positive case in the existing include-shortcode.spec.ts (Phase B.3).

title: Epic: light/dark theme support (dual CSS, toggle, highlight-style, brand, preview)
description:
TS Quarto supports a YAML-object form for 'theme:' in format.html, with 'light' and 'dark' keys whose values are theme-name + scss-file lists:

    format:
      html:
        theme:
          light: [cosmo, theme.scss]
          dark: [cosmo, theme-dark.scss]

Q2 currently rejects this: 'Invalid theme configuration: theme must be a string or array of strings'. quarto-web uses this form, so it's the next blocker after bd-47w7o for a full quarto-web render.

Discovered after bd-47w7o (directory-resource recursive copy) landed and the render progressed past resource copying. To investigate: find where theme parsing happens in Q2 (search for 'Invalid theme configuration'), check TS Quarto behavior at external-sources/quarto-cli (light/dark theme spec), design the parsing + rendering path. The render-side work likely interacts with the existing SCSS resolution pipeline. Likely larger than a one-shot fix; may want a plan doc when picked up.

title: Table/custom listing fields can't read bare frontmatter keys (Q1 reads all document metadata; Q2 requires listing-item.extra opt-in)
description: Discovered while fixing bd-listing-table-fields-peg1w3b3: docs/errors/index.qmd declares 'fields: [code, title, subsystem, status]' where code/subsystem/status are bare top-level frontmatter keys on each error page. Q1 listing items expose ALL document metadata, so such fields render. Q2's DocumentProfile is a typed, versioned contract: custom fields reach ListingItem.extra only via an explicit 'listing-item: { extra: ... }' frontmatter block (document_profile.rs L0 design, bd-n8a4), so those columns render empty. Options to evaluate: (a) auto-fill listing_item.extra from unrecognized top-level frontmatter scalars at profile extraction (Q1 parity; bloat + collision questions; contract doc calls reading extra from outside listings a design-review trigger); (b) keep opt-in and update docs/errors pages (and their scaffolding) to declare listing-item.extra; (c) hybrid: opt-in via a listing-level 'include-metadata-fields' key. The dynamic-column table fix (binding.rs item_field_display_value → extra_field_value with dotted-path lookup) already renders any key that lands in item.extra, so only the population side is open. Real consumer: docs/errors/index.qmd (Code/Subsystem/Status columns currently empty).

title: Website projects epic: multi-page sites with sidebars, shared resources, and hub-client integration
description:
Design and implement multi-page website projects for Quarto 2. Covers: typed static-document snapshots (PageSnapshot/DocumentProfile working name), pipeline resumability, ProjectType trait, website sidebars, scoped/relocatable artifact stores (site_libs), cross-doc link rewriting, sitemap/favicon/site-url, incremental rebuilds, and hub-client project rendering.

MVP scope explicitly excludes: search, listings/RSS, aliases, announcements, analytics, 404, reader-mode, repo-actions, breadcrumbs, book project type, quarto preview, freeze.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-23-website-project-epic.md

Design decisions from initial conversation:
- Snapshot is a typed serializable value produced at a pipeline checkpoint after MetadataMergeStage; downstream code consumes Vec<DocumentProfile>; user filters read but do not mutate.
- Pipeline stages up to snapshot are resumable (cloneable) to avoid redundant execution across pass 1 (snapshot sweep) and pass 2 (per-file render).
- ProjectType trait introduced now (website, default). Single-document renders go through DefaultProjectType.
- Artifact stores scope-aware (Page vs Project) and relocatable; single-doc = project with implicit _quarto.yml.
- Hub-client caches project nav state; renders active page with cached state. Design must leave room for Q2 'quarto preview' which will be a local hub-client instance.
- Naming TBD in Phase 0 (DocumentProfile working name; user dislikes Page*/Metadata*).

description: Follow-up from bd-heading-id-attr-duplicated-xbpcmejr (design question 4; user accepted the simple version for now). …
per such field. This is dynamic in EJS — there is no equivalent in doctemplate without server-side precomputation. L3 v1 ships the default listing with curated-fields-only output. title: Case-sensitivity of index-file stem matching is inconsistent across sidebar code
description: During bd-sidebar-dir-index-md-5khf3lds the user decided that section_for_dir's directory-index stem match must be case-SENSITIVE (stem == "index" exactly), because case-insensitive matching misbehaves across case-sensitive filesystems vs case-preserving/insensitive ones (macOS). But is_top_level_index in the same file (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/sidebar_auto.rs, ~line 300) still matches the stem with eq_ignore_ascii_case, so 'Index.qmd' at the project root is excluded from auto: true sibling lists while 'guides/Index.md' is treated as an ordinary child. Neither behavior is obviously wrong in isolation, but the codebase has no stated policy for path case handling, and macOS's case-preserving-insensitive default means a file can be openable under a name that differs in case from what discovery recorded. Low priority per the user ('case-sensitive errors are not particularly high-priority'), but worth a pass to (a) state a policy, (b) align is_top_level_index and any similar stem/extension matches with it, and (c) make sure nothing egregious (silent drop, wrong link) happens when only case differs.

title: HTML comments lost during incremental writes
description: HTML comments (<\!-- ... -->) are dropped from the Pandoc AST during parsing. tree-sitter parses them as 'comment' nodes which become IntermediateUnknown and are silently removed. This causes comments to be lost when the incremental writer rewrites blocks containing comments. Block-level standalone comments survive as empty Para blocks (preserved via source spans on KeepBefore), but inline comments within paragraphs are completely gone.

title: Browser sync offline-fallback race family: lost docs + failed opens (1ms peer wait, no re-announce, no find-retry)
description: The hub-client document path (App.tsx -> @quarto/preview-runtime automergeSync.connect -> quarto-sync-client connect) waits 1ms for the peer, always loses against real network latency, and silently proceeds in offline mode. title: Provenance follow-up: ValueSource anchor stamping for meta/var shortcodes
description:
Wires up the AnchorRole::ValueSource role (already defined in Plan 4's enum) so that meta/var shortcode resolutions carry a typed anchor pointing at where the value was defined (e.g., a key in _metadata.yml).

**Today (Plan 4 + Plan 6 baseline):**
- {{< meta footer >}} -> Generated { by: shortcode("meta"), from: [Invocation -> token_si] }

**After this issue:**
- {{< meta footer >}} -> Generated { by: shortcode("meta"), from: [Invocation -> token_si, ValueSource -> metadata_yml_si] }

The writer (Plan 7) keeps consulting invocation_anchor() only; ValueSource is diagnostic-only ("hover the resolved value to see where it was defined"). Doesn't affect round-tripping or attribution.

**Blocker:** the metadata loader doesn't expose per-key source-info on merged metadata today. Each YAML key has source_info at parse time, but the merge step strips it. Threading it through requires extending the metadata value types to keep source_info alive past the merge.

**Plan refs:**
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-4-source-info-types.md §"Deferred anchor role"
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md §"ValueSource follow-up"

**Compatibility:** pure addition. AnchorRole::ValueSource already exists in Plan 4's enum from day 1. Plan 6's stamper gains conditional ValueSource emission for meta/var shortcodes whose values came from outside the active document.

**Effort:** smaller than the Dispatch follow-up — self-contained (metadata loader + Plan 6 stamper). No new infrastructure crates.

title: D4/D5: HTML writer emits odd/even and header row classes
description:
## What

`write_table_row` in `crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:1490` emits bare `<tr>` for every row. Pandoc's reference HTML writer (which Q1 inherits) adds:

- `<tr class="header">` on header (thead) rows.
- `<tr class="odd">` / `<tr class="even">` alternating on body rows.

## Fix

## Tests (TDD)

Snapshot test on a 3-row table (1 header + 2 body) showing:
- header row: `<tr class="header">`
- first body row: `<tr class="odd">`
- second body row: `<tr class="even">`

## Plan

title: Callout default-title synthesizer + popup-menu callout-type switching (Plan 6 §B)
description: Plan 6's audit identified crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/callout_resolve.rs:267 (default callout title 'Note'/'Tip'/'Warning'/...) as an AST synthesizer that today emits SourceInfo::default(). To bring it into the Generated shape Plan 6 establishes, it needs: (a) a new By::callout() constructor in quarto-source-map, (b) an atomicity decision (is_atomic_kind), (c) the fix at callout_resolve.rs:267, (d) a per-transform test. Deferred from Plan 6 because it was not enumerated in the plan body and requires the new By constructor + atomicity decision.

c-gh26vk6d.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-gh26vk6d.text:
Why this matters beyond the audit fix: the React preview needs a UI affordance to **switch callout type** (Note → Tip → Warning → Important → Caution) via a popup menu on the callout block. For that to round-trip cleanly through Plan 7's writer, the default-title text ("Note", "Tip", …) must NOT be treated as user-editable Original content — otherwise typing-as-edit semantics would force the writer to materialize "Note" as literal text into source, even when the user only wanted to swap the type via the menu.

The `Generated { by: callout(), … }` stamping + the atomicity decision determine:

1. **React-side**: whether the title region is gated read-only via Plan 2A's atomic check (so the user can't accidentally type into it; the menu is the only path to mutation).
2. **Writer-side**: how a menu-driven type change serializes. The menu rewrites the Callout CustomNode's `plain_data` (e.g. `{"type": "tip"}`) and leaves the title-Generated either re-synthesized on next pipeline run or replaced with a fresh Generated whose `by.data` reflects the new type. Plan 7's let-user-win path handles the CustomNode rewrite naturally; the title region soft-drops on direct edits (Q-3-42-style).

Recommend `is_atomic_kind = true` for `By::callout()`'s title-synthesizer use so the title is non-editable text and only menu-driven type changes mutate it. The popup-menu component lives in hub-client's React framework registry (post-Plan 2B); this beads owns the Rust-side provenance support that makes the round-trip behave.

title: ExecuteResult.filters set by Knitr engine is never consumed downstream
description:
Workspace-wide grep for `result.filters` / `ExecuteResult.*filters` returns hits in tests, the Knitr write site, extension parsing, and a comment in capture-splice — but no production consumer.

Concretely:
- crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/mod.rs:215 sets `filters: result.filters` from the R subprocess output (test fixture asserts `vec!["rmarkdown/pagebreak.lua"]`, knitr/types.rs:281).
- crates/quarto-core/src/filter_resolve.rs only resolves filters from YAML `filters:` document metadata, not from ExecuteResult.filters.

So Knitr's pagebreak filter is silently dropped today. This also blocks any future engine (like a mermaid Lua-filter approach) that wants to declare filters dynamically.

Decision needed: wire ExecuteResult.filters into the resolver, or remove the field if the architectural direction is different (e.g. all engine-side filters should be expressed as AST transforms instead).

Discovered during mermaid engine design — see claude-notes/plans/2026-05-28-mermaidjs-engine-design.md gap G1.

title: Verify @tip-foo crossref of callouts still works after class-vocabulary alignment

title: Globals filter whitelist drops five dispatchable element tags
description:
get_filter_table (crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs:323) copies global handler functions into the filter table by walking a HARDCODED list of ~50 element names. That list has drifted from the walker's actual dispatch vocabulary, LuaInline::tag_name / LuaBlock::tag_name (crates/pampa/src/lua/types.rs:272,1155).

Five tags the walker CAN dispatch are absent from the whitelist:

  Attr, BlockMetadata, CaptionBlock, NoteDefinitionFencedBlock, NoteDefinitionPara

A filter defining any of these as a global function is silently dropped: the
handler is never copied into the table, so it never fires, with no diagnostic.

PROVEN, not inferred. The same handler name fires when handed to doc:walk as a
table (which bypasses the whitelist and goes straight to the name-agnostic
walker) and does not fire as a global:

  $ cat whitelist-gap.lua
  function NoteDefinitionPara(el)
    quarto.log.output('GLOBAL NoteDefinitionPara FIRED')
  end
  function Pandoc(doc)
    return doc:walk{ NoteDefinitionPara = function(el)
      quarto.log.output('WALK-TABLE NoteDefinitionPara FIRED') end }
  end

  $ pampa note.md -F whitelist-gap.lua -t plain
  WALK-TABLE NoteDefinitionPara FIRED        <- table path fires
  (no GLOBAL line)                           <- globals path silently drops it

where note.md is a document with a footnote definition.

FIX DIRECTION. Derive the copied name set from the same source of truth the
walker dispatches on (tag_name) plus the catch-alls (Pandoc/Doc/Meta/
Inline/Inlines/Block/Blocks) instead of maintaining a second hand-written list
that can drift again. The whitelist becomes unnecessary for the returned-table
form entirely (the walker is name-agnostic), so this only concerns the globals
path.

DISCOVERED during the investigation of bd-lua-filter-table-form-ignored-ph23becz
(see claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-lua-filter-returned-table-form.md). Related:
the 'unrecognized handler name' warning decided for that strand would surface
this class of drift to users automatically.

c-yzj97tpl.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-yzj97tpl.text: Fixed as part of PR https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/508. The globals scan now derives its name set from an element_tag_names! macro that generates both the tag_name match arms and the list of names it can return, so the whitelist can no longer drift from the walker's dispatch vocabulary. Regression test: test_globals_dispatch_name_outside_old_whitelist (a global NoteDefinitionPara handler fires). Do not close until the PR merges.

title: Fix file-locking test failures in quarto-hub on Windows
description: 2 storage tests fail because Windows uses mandatory file locking vs Unix advisory. File::create fails with sharing violation before try_lock_exclusive runs. Affects test_storage_manager_prevents_double_lock and test_storage_manager_standalone_prevents_double_lock.

title: Lua attribute-mutation: proxy tables so cb.attr.attributes[k]=v persists
description: Quarto 2's Lua bridge returns fresh copies of `cb.attr` (and of `cb.attr.attributes`) on every read. In-place mutation like `cb.attr.attributes["k"] = v` — the idiomatic Pandoc-Lua pattern — silently hits an ephemeral copy and is discarded. Surfaced while exercising Phase 3.5's filter-authored spans fixture (04-filter-authored-spans); the workaround there rebuilds the whole Attr with pandoc.Attr(...) and assigns as one value. Before we document the Lua-filter path to syntax highlighting as a user-facing feature, the idiomatic pattern must persist. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-20-syntax-highlighting-phase-3.5.md 'Follow-up task: Lua attribute-mutation proxy'. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-21-lua-attr-mutation-proxy.md

title: ipynb surface syntax: render .ipynb inputs with cell-coordinate source tracking (design + feasibility)
description: Design and implement .ipynb as a Quarto 2 input format: convert notebook JSON to qmd in-process, with per-cell ephemeral SourceFiles as the coordinate system so diagnostics read 'foo.ipynb[cell 3] line:col' with squiggles over the logical (unescaped) markdown. Supersedes the ipynb half of k-zr88's 2025-12-15 design (sidecar files + NotebookCell SourceInfo variant no longer needed: pipeline is in-memory and pampa's parent_source_info seam already exists). Stored outputs rendered via engine-layer replay (option B). Design doc: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-20-ipynb-surface-syntax-design.md

c-3wtgfedn.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-3wtgfedn.text: Design doc written after auditing the 2025-12-15 (k-zr88) and 2025-10-13 (converter registry) designs against the July-2026 codebase. Key findings: run_pipeline is fully in-memory; SourceContext is serde-serializable; pampa read() already accepts parent_source_info making every node SourceInfo a Substring of it (location.rs:214); produce_diagnostic_messages does NOT thread the parent (gap #1); quarto-source-map is affine-only by policy (Transformed variant was removed) — hence the per-cell virtual-file coordinate system design.

c-5p1zvvyy.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-5p1zvvyy.text:
.ipynb support now has a settled shape, from the ts-engine-extensions <- main merge (D3): it lands as an ENGINE THAT CLAIMS .ipynb, not as a SourceType variant. SourceType lost its Ipynb variant in that merge; the conversion seam is SourceConversionStage (renamed from EngineClaimsFileStage), which runs immediately before ParseDocumentStage on every target including WASM.

Prerequisite: bd-zlemoc6w (conversion provenance). The TS host already serializes a real source map for converted files and the wire type carries it (TsMappedStringWithMap.source_map), but Rust drops it — ts_engine.rs takes result.value and discards result.source_map, and the stage side drops it again in source_conversion.rs. Until that is fixed, diagnostics for a converted .ipynb point at the synthesized qmd rather than the notebook cell the user wrote. ParseDocumentStage compensates honestly today (it registers converted text under '<foo.ipynb (converted by jupyter)>'), so this is a quality gap rather than a correctness bug — but for .ipynb specifically it is the difference between usable and unusable error messages.

c-kksq9hrc.text:
Design body re-homed into Plan 7c (2026-07-08-plan7c-ipynb-content-processor.md),
landed on feature/ts-engine-extensions in e1174d9f8.

argument for why .ipynb bytes are the wrong coordinate root, per-cell ephemeral
SourceFiles as the root instead, Q1-compatible cell emission, front matter from a
leading cell staying source-mapped, the `#|` cell-options composition win,
presentation P1 (pseudo-path) → P2 (FileOrigin upstream), stored-output replay at
the engine layer (option B), and the three implementation seams.

Only the ATTACHMENT POINT changed, in two steps:
1. D3 (merge runbook) deleted SourceType::Ipynb — already noted in the previous
   comment here. Conversion is dispatched by SourceConversionStage.
2. The doc declined a ConverterRegistry as "speculative for one converter". Plan
   7b builds that registry anyway, for percent + spin, so ipynb is the THIRD
   converter, not the first — which is the exact condition this doc named for

Two of the doc's findings SIMPLIFY the plan and are adopted in 7c:
- No SourceInfo::NotebookCell variant (cell identity is per-file, not per-span) —
  the closed enum with ~8 upstream match sites stays untouched.
- No sidecar (run_pipeline is in-memory; no qmd intermediate on disk). This also

processor can hand back per-cell virtual files for SourceContext registration.
bd-zlemoc6w remains the provenance prerequisite.

New open question recorded in 7c: per-cell file scaling — a 500-cell notebook
registers 500 SourceFiles; nothing in the design sizes that. Measure before
Phase 2.

title: Incremental writer panics when original QMD lacks trailing newline
description: The incremental writer (incremental_write_qmd WASM entry point) panics with 'byte index out of bounds' when the original QMD text doesn't end with a newline. The QMD reader internally pads input with \n, producing source spans for the padded input, but incremental_write receives the unpadded string. Triggered by changing kanban card status when synced document text doesn't end with \n. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-02-11-incremental-writer-trailing-newline-bug.md
close_reason: Fixed: added ensure_trailing_newline normalization in incremental_write and compute_incremental_edits. The QMD reader internally pads input with newline, so source spans reference the padded length. The incremental writer now pads its input to match, then strips the padding from results. 6 new tests added, all 6408 workspace tests pass.

title: Jupyter cell tags ignored: remove-cell/hide-cell content is rendered instead of hidden
description:
CONTENT LEAK. A notebook cell tagged 'remove-cell' or 'hide-cell' through the JupyterLab UI is FULLY RENDERED by Q2. An author marks a cell for removal and Q2 publishes it anyway.

Q2's jupyter.toMarkdown never converts notebook cell TAGS into visibility options. Q1 does this at external-sources/quarto-cli/src/core/jupyter/jupyter.ts:910-915, on the same code path. Verified: ZERO occurrences of 'tagsToOptions' or 'metadata.tags' anywhere in Q2's ts-packages/quarto-api/src/jupyter/ directory.

Why P1 and not P0: this is a faithful-port omission with a known fix, not an active exploit, so it does not meet the repo's P0 bar (security / data loss / broken builds). But it IS unintended disclosure -- authors routinely put scratch work, debug output, and credentials in remove-cell cells -- so bump to P0 if that reading is preferred.

Independent of the JSR publishing work: this is a live rendering bug affecting Q2 users today, and is worth fixing whether or not we ever publish the SDK. That is why it is filed standalone rather than as a child of bd-ixz93hjp, though it is also conflict #1 on that epic's gate list.

ADJACENT (natural to fix together, conflict #2 on the same gate list): jupyter.toMarkdown also ignores cell.metadata chunk options, so captions/labels/echo set via cell metadata are silently dropped.

Detail + citations: claude-notes/research/2026-08-22-quarto-api-q1-vs-q2-status.md section 6.1 (four divergences in toMarkdown), on branch feature/jsr-publish.

TDD note: per CLAUDE.md, write the failing test first -- a notebook fixture with a 'remove-cell'-tagged cell, asserting the cell's content is absent from the rendered output.

title: annotated-qmd: source-tracking off-by-one in regenerated examples
description:
Two TS tests in ts-packages/annotated-qmd fail after regenerating example JSONs with the current pampa writer:

1. substring-invariant.test.ts: 'substring invariant - links.qmd: inline code' — expects substring(125, 133) to be '`x = 5`' but gets ' `x = 5`' (extra leading space).
2. block-types.test.ts: 'div-attrs.json - Div with attributes conversion' — key source text ' custom-key' has a leading space; the assertion 'should be a valid attribute key' fails because the substring extracted from source includes a preceding space.

Both fail in the same shape on the surface: the writer-recorded start offset for these tokens is 1 character too early, capturing the preceding whitespace. Whether they share a single root cause has not been confirmed.

## Why this surfaces now (not on main)

The failures only surface when example fixtures (ts-packages/annotated-qmd/examples/*.json) are regenerated against the current pampa. The committed fixtures (regenerated 2025-10-24, commit 2b2337be by Carlos) predate the pampa changes that introduced the offset drift. cargo nextest run --workspace doesn't touch the fixtures — they're inert JSON loaded by the TS test suite (loadExample(...) in test/document-converter.test.ts and others) — so main's CI has been green throughout while the underlying writer behavior drifted.

Plan 7f Phase 5 (wire-format rename attrS->a, sourceInfoPool->p) requires regenerating the fixtures because the TS code post-rename reads inline.a / astContext.p — old-format fixtures (attrS, sourceInfoPool) would be unreadable. Regeneration is a Phase-5 necessity. The regenerated fixtures capture current pampa writer behavior, including the off-by-one, and that's what trips these tests.

Phase 5 itself only renamed JSON keys — no offset computation was touched. So Phase 5 is the messenger, not the cause.

## Suspected commit for failure #1 (inline code) — NOT CONFIRMED

Plausible candidate: commit 38e889ad (Carlos, 2026-05-24, 'tree-sitter qmd: allow line breaks inside inline code spans and inline math (bd-ilv8p)'). The commit substantially reworked code-span tokenization in the tree-sitter scanner + grammar — SOFT_LINE_ENDING absorb logic, pandoc_soft_break aliasing, an extract_code_span_text helper. It's the only recent commit between 2b2337be (2025-10-24) and HEAD that touches code-span tokenization.

Hypothesis: the rework widened the pandoc_code_span tree-sitter node by one byte to the left, to include the preceding-space character. Since Inline::Code's source_info is computed via node_source_info_with_context(node, context) at crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/code_span_helpers.rs:171 — taking the whole node's byte range — that left-edge widening shows up directly as a 1-char-wider Code source range.

NOT YET BISECTED. The hypothesis is consistent with the failure shape but a clean bisect would confirm or refute it.

## Suspected commit for failure #2 (div key-source) — UNKNOWN

The div-attrs failure is in a different code path (attribute key-source recording during div parsing). The "leading space byte gets included" pattern matches surface-level, but I have NOT verified that this is the same code path or the same root cause. It could be:
* the same scanner-side absorb pattern leaking into adjacent attr/key-source tokens, OR
* a separate regression introduced by a different commit, OR
* older than 2025-10-24 and only now visible because the regenerated fixture happens to record a real source range where the old fixture had something stale.

A clean bisect against the example regen is the cheapest way to find out.

## Repro

  cd ts-packages/annotated-qmd
  npm test

Failures: 2 of 156 tests fail. The other 154 pass — including substring-invariant tests on Str / Space / Header / BulletList / ordered-list / link target / link text — which means the off-by-one is not pervasive; it's localized to specific token boundaries.

## Fix direction

1. Bisect each failure independently against the example fixture regen. Use a known-good baseline of pampa from 2025-10-24 (around commit 2b2337be) and walk forward.
2. If failure #1 lands on 38e889ad, audit pandoc_code_span node-range computation in the scanner — likely the absorb-leading-space behavior needs to start the node at the opening backtick.
3. If failure #2 lands on a different commit (likely), the fix is independent.
4. Add a CI lane that regenerates the annotated-qmd example fixtures (or at minimum diffs the writer output against them) so the next time a tree-sitter scanner change drifts the output, this catches at the PR level instead of accumulating until the next forced regen.

c-kaz1nqxj.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-kaz1nqxj.text:
Commit 5c6e793a8: tightness exclusion re-keyed to the abbreviation NBSP substitution exactly, after Gordon asked why it was not keyed to the specific producer behavior. It should have been — I wrote a general rule without reading postprocess.rs first.

The producer: the ends_with_abbreviation branch absorbs the Space after an abbreviation into the preceding Str as U+00A0 (Pandoc parity, so e.g. cannot be separated from its referent). 048.qmd hits the sub-case where the abbreviation is followed by a Code rather than a Str, so the Space is swallowed with no word to join. text_helpers.rs's backslash-space escape does the same substitution.

New rule: boundary chars must be U+00A0, IN MATCHING QUANTITY with the source space/tab bytes. A Str retaining a plain space is reported again; a range absorbing 2 spaces against 1 NBSP is reported. This also CLOSES review finding #8 (presence vs amount) rather than deferring it — dropped from bd-89jcn0uv's scope, so the tightening removed a follow-up instead of adding one.

Verified before narrowing that no other producer retains a plain boundary space (only code_span_helpers.rs writes whitespace into text, and that is Code, which passes None). Binding re-verified: reverting the attr-key fix still fails the corpus test naming the same 4 documents.

Plan 7g Phase 3 then fixed failure #1 at the WRITER layer and wrote the convention down: claude-notes/designs/provenance-contract.md section P1 (Tight ranges) mandates whitespace-excluded node ranges and names the helpers to use (tight_source_info_for_node, leading_whitespace_source_info). P1's 'Implemented' list is code_span_helpers.rs, citation.rs, quote_helpers.rs, postprocess.rs math-with-attr Span — the attribute path was never converted. Failure #2 is a missing P1 conversion, NOT a scanner bug. Do not touch the scanner.

(3) THE CODE POINTER HERE IS STALE. key_value_specifier.rs / process_key_value_specifier does not exist in the tree. The live seam is the 'key_value_key' arm at crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:1205, which has called .trim() on the key TEXT while keeping the untrimmed node_location(node) since 6b0c51d26. So the claim 'the writer faithfully reports the node range' is false there — the writer breaks its own text-to-range lockstep, which is why the writer-layer fix is correct rather than a workaround. bd-49cbyqbt's AttrSourceInfo framing is the durable one: the wrong key range ships to every consumer of the serialized provenance (hub-client click-to-source, diagnostics anchored at an attribute key), not just to the annotated-qmd fixtures.

Measured scope of the remaining defect (fixture claude-notes/plans/attr-key-range-early-investigation/scope.qmd): 2nd+ same-line kv keys absorb the separator (' bb' [26,29], ' ccc' [33,37]); ids, classes, values, 1st keys, and ALL multi-line-attr-list keys are correct (a soft line break is tokenized separately so the scanner is not entered at whitespace). One seam, leading-side only.

Also: why no auditor caught it — the Plan 7g tiling auditor enforces P3/P4. P1 has no auditor, and the key range does not overlap a sibling ([251,262] starts exactly where the previous value ends), so P4 was satisfied while P1 was violated.

Baseline at e3b3d7d4a: cargo nextest --workspace 12999 passed / 0 failed; preview-renderer integration 578 passed / 1 failed (bd-s36g9dav, katex 0.18.1 pin, unrelated); annotated-qmd 154 passed / 2 failed (this strand's pair).

title: AttrSourceInfo: caption-attr merge into table breaks positional alignment
description:
When the qmd parser merges caption attributes into a table's Attr at:

- crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/section.rs:85-113
- crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:1483-1496

it calls table.attr.2.insert(k, v) and table.attr_source.attributes.push(...). If a caption attribute key already exists on the table (e.g. both have id or class), LinkedHashMap::insert updates the existing entry in place while push always appends — leaving attr.2.len() and attr_source.attributes.len() out of sync. The positional alignment AttrSourceInfo.attributes[i] = (key_src, val_src) for the i-th entry in Attr.2 is broken whenever caption + table attribute keys overlap.

**Discovered while reviewing Plan 6's theorem.rs::extract_name_attr fix** (claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md §Scope theorem bullet). Plan 6 mitigates with a runtime guard but the underlying bug pre-dates Plan 6.

**Fix sketch:**
For each (k, v, key_src, val_src) being merged:
- If table.attr.2.contains_key(&k), find its position, overwrite both attr.2's value AND attr_source.attributes[pos] in lockstep.
- Else, append to both.

**Plan refs:**
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md §Scope theorem bullet (positional-alignment safeguards)
- crates/quarto-pandoc-types/src/attr.rs:27-32 (AttrSourceInfo definition)

c-e422v1z5.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-e422v1z5.text:
Small correction to this strand's plan (claude-notes/plans/2026-08-07-nested-include-expansion.md), surfaced by the Positron docs port and measured 2026-08-26 on Q1 99.9.9 vs q2 0.27.0. Recording it here so the closed strand does not read as settled on the point; the substance is in bd-whft9m1j comment c-83ey3eny. Consequence #2 says sibling-item injection 'was never expressible in Q1 either — includes in list items didn't work — so nothing regresses'. It was expressible, via a form the empirical matrix did not probe. The matrix tested '- {{< include >}}' (include as the item's own content), which indeed never worked in Q1. The working Q1 spelling is the continuation line: - item one - item two {{< include "_inc.qmd" >}} # _inc.qmd = '- item three' Q1: three sibling
  • s. q2:
  • item two ?include
    • So it is a genuine, small regression rather than a never-was. Same class covers a continuation line after a plain paragraph, which also expanded in Q1. Nothing here argues against the design or PR #467 — q2 still handles strictly more positions than Q1 overall, including the '- {{< include >}}' form in the original matrix, which q2 expands and Q1 did not. Only the no-regression claim needs adjusting, and the guide needs the caveat that adding the blank line Q-17-4 suggests yields two lists where Q1 produced one.

c-esabrk47.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-esabrk47.text: Assessment + implementation plan written: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-07-nested-include-expansion.md. Key findings: Q1 (verified empirically against the dev checkout) only supports includes at top level and inside fenced divs — blockquote/list positions silently pass the raw shortcode text through. Q1's textual model is why: directive recognition is line-based, no re-indentation. In Q2's AST model the indentation complication dissolves entirely (parsing happens before expansion on both sides), so the plan proposes one uniform rule: expand at every block-list position (div, blockquote, list items, definition lists, figure, footnote defs, table cells, captions). Recognizer must accept Plain as well as Paragraph (tight list items / table cells parse as Plain — probed). quarto-preview's dep scanner shares the recognizer and has the same top-level-only blind spot; plan keeps them in lockstep via a shared traversal. Awaiting plan review.

  from "crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/pkg/wasm_quarto_hub_client.js"

The wasm-bindgen-generated JS glue references an absolute path that
resolves correctly when vite roots at hub-client/ (which has
src/wasm-js-bridge/cache.js), but the demos do not have that file.

The demos likely need either:

  - vite alias config that resolves the path to hub-client's copy, or

(branch chore/e2e-ci). The workflow now builds only ts-packages +
hub-client to avoid this failure; the demos remain broken at build

title: Complete FootnotesTransform for reference-location: block/section
description:
FootnotesTransform at crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/footnotes.rs:99-105 currently no-ops for reference-location: block and section, leaving raw Inline::Note nodes in the AST with a stale comment claiming "Pandoc handles this". pampa's HTML writer (crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:806-817) also doesn't handle them correctly — it emits <sup>[N]</sup> where N is the length of the note content array, not a sequential number, with a TODO acknowledging the gap.

Neither layer numbers Notes correctly for these configs. The work is missing in both places.

The proper fix is to extend FootnotesTransform to handle block/section: number all Notes in document order (already done for document-mode) and emit per-block or per-section footnote sections at the right boundary instead of a single document-end section.

Discovered while reviewing q2-preview Plan 2B (claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-2b-builtin-components.md) — q2-preview's Note.tsx falls back to JS-side numbering with body-in-tooltip rendering for these configs as a temporary v1 measure. title: Decide: comrak/commonmark boundary — accept normalize+correction-map (strategy 3)?
description: The commonmark reader (crates/pampa/src/readers/commonmark.rs) delegates to comrak, which normalizes CRLF to LF internally per CommonMark spec 2.1 (LF, lone CR, CRLF all line endings), consuming CRLF as one break, with NO opt-out — source-confirmed at comrak-0.52.0/src/parser/mod.rs:205-211. This is the one boundary where pure-preserve (strategy 1) is impossible without forking comrak. Decision: accept strategy 3 (normalize + correction map) HERE — let comrak normalize but carry comrak's original-relative Sourcepos (it tracks a column_offset for consumed CR/LF) through our wrapper instead of recomputing against normalized text — OR fork/replace comrak. Strategy 3 keeps offsets honest against the original bytes; reference design is rustc normalized_pos, and its known relative-vs-absolute bug rust-lang/rust#149568 should be written as a test up front. Open questions that set urgency/priority: when is the commonmark reader actually exercised versus the main tree-sitter-qmd path, and does any current q2 output depend on its Sourcepos being original-relative? Only bites when the commonmark path matters for preserve; informational until then. Refs: claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-prior-art.md comrak + rustc + CommonMark-spec sections.

title: Engine failures report line numbers in the .rmarkdown intermediate, never the .qmd
description:
Split out of bd-render-failure-unattributed-yxe0v7th as the deliberately scoped-out half of its SHAPE 2 (agreed with Gordon 2026-08-24).

That strand fixed ATTRIBUTION: a failed page now always names its .qmd. It did not fix LINE NUMBERS, which still point into the generated engine intermediate.

Two surfaces, both still wrong:

1. knitr's own stderr traceback, passed through verbatim:

       Quitting from failing.rmarkdown:133-135 [unnamed-chunk-1]

   The .qmd name appears nowhere in it, and 133-135 are offsets into the
   generated file, not the source. The committed repro is
   /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/freeze-ignored-silent-failure/silent-failure/
   (run 'q2 render' in repro/ and in control/ and compare).

2. The ariadne frame for engine-OUTPUT parse errors, which the fix in
   bd-render-failure-unattributed-yxe0v7th newly made render. It is correct
   and useful -- it shows the offending line -- but it is anchored in the
   intermediate:

       error: while rendering /.../knit.qmd
       Error: [Q-2-34] Unquoted shortcode parameter starting with digit
            ╭─[ /.../knit.knitr.rmarkdown:138:23 ]
        138 │ {{< fa envelope size=1x >}}

   Surface 2 is arguably fine as-is for content the engine GENERATED (there
   is no .qmd line to point at). It is wrong for content the engine merely
   PASSED THROUGH, which is the common case -- a bad shortcode the author
   typed in the .qmd gets reported at an intermediate line number.

What this needs, and why it was scoped out: a line map from the serialized
intermediate back to the source, plus per-engine stderr parsing for surface 1.
The serialize step already computes a SourceInfo
(serialize_ast_to_qmd -> pampa::writers::qmd::write_with_source_info in
crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs), so the raw material
for surface 2 may already exist -- worth checking whether that SourceInfo can
carry the executed parse's spans back to .qmd offsets, rather than building a
new mechanism.

Note the engine intermediate is registered in the source context WITHOUT
content on the stage's Ok path (add_file_with_info sets file_info only), and
WITH content on the new Err path. Anything that renders frames against the
intermediate should check which it is getting.

title: Wire SassError::UnknownTheme through the structured diagnostic system
description:
Follow-up discovered after the bd-l26u6 epic merged. SassError::UnknownTheme (raised by BuiltInTheme::from_str when a theme name is not recognized) still surfaces as the span-less, code-less 'Error: SASS error / Unknown theme: default' line — the theme_diagnostic fallback path.

Reproducer: q2 render external-sources/quarto-web — emits both Q-14-1 (coalesced, from _quarto.yml:686) AND the bare 'Unknown theme: default' line (from docs/output-formats/html-themes.qmd:11, which has 'theme: default' in its document frontmatter).

Fix follows the bd-pgczr pattern:
- Add location: Option<SourceInfo> to SassError::UnknownTheme.
- Add SassError::with_location(self, SourceInfo) -> Self helper so the next variant migration is trivial.
- Propagate value.source_info.clone() at the ThemeSpec::parse call sites in extract_theme_specs (crates/quarto-sass/src/config.rs:455, :465).
- Allocate Q-14-2 'Unknown theme name' in error_catalog.json under the existing 'theme' subsystem.
- Extend theme_diagnostic::sass_error_to_parse_error to render UnknownTheme as a structured DiagnosticMessage with Q-14-2 + source span.
close_reason: UnknownTheme now flows through quarto-error-reporting as Q-14-2. Verified end-to-end: pandas-acting-on-data.qmd:7:12 'default' produces a proper ariadne block. No more plain-text SASS error fallback in quarto-web.

title: Inline grammar: post-codespan apostrophe trips Q-2-7 (Unclosed Single Quote)
description:
The inline grammar's smart-quote rule treats `'` immediately after a
closing-backtick (code span boundary) as an *opening* single quote,
even when followed by letters as in a possessive. Real Pandoc treats
the same construct as a possessive and emits no error. As a result,
common technical writing patterns trip Q-2-7:

  `setAst`'s callback         → FAIL (Q-2-7)
  `Para`'s rendering          → FAIL
  `framework/Ast.tsx`'s       → FAIL
  `<AssetManifestContext>`'s  → FAIL (the angle brackets are not the
                                      trigger — backticks alone suffice)

This has tripped the changelogRender.wasm.test.ts at least twice:
- 0c78b1a4 (2026-05-08): "fix(hub-client): rewrite changelog 2026-05-08
  entry to clear Q-2-7 parse error" — diagnosis blamed `<Tag>` HTML-
  like content; the angle brackets are coincidental.
- d7d7e063 (2026-05-10): same trigger pattern in Plan 2B Phase 1/2
  changelog entries; rewrote in plain prose.

## Empirical scope

| Pattern                            | Result | Why                              |
|------------------------------------|--------|----------------------------------|
| `` `code`'s gate ``                | FAIL   | post-codespan `'` promoted       |
| `` `code`'foo bar ``               | FAIL   | same                             |
| `` `code` 's gate ``               | FAIL   | whitespace between doesn't help  |
| `` `code`\'s gate ``               | PASS   | escaped apostrophe               |
| `` word's gate ``                  | PASS   | letter-letter → possessive       |
| `` `code`'s and `other`'s pair ``  | PASS   | two opens form a balanced pair   |
| `` `code`'s and word's pair ``     | FAIL   | only one promoted-to-opening     |

Reproducer: see /tmp/q27[a-e].qmd patterns in the discovery session
or just `printf "x \\\`code\\\`'s\\n" | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t json -i -`.

## Proper fix

In `tree-sitter-markdown-inline`'s grammar, extend the rule for
opening single quote so a `'` immediately after a closing-backtick
(or, more generally, after any inline-end token) is treated as a
possessive when the next character is a letter — same heuristic
that already saves `word's`. Pandoc proper does this; the smart-
quote algorithm there is "an apostrophe between letters or after a
markup boundary that resolves to letters is a possessive."

After regenerate + build, add a test case to the inline grammar's
test corpus and a passing case to resources/error-corpus
demonstrating that `` `code`'s `` no longer fires Q-2-7.

## Workarounds available today

1. Pair them deliberately within the same block (two close-backtick
   apostrophes form a smart-quote pair).
2. Backslash-escape: `` `code`\'s ``.
3. Rephrase to put the apostrophe inside a word (`the setAst
   callback's behavior`).
4. bd-kk0a's writer-side escape (separate issue, AST→qmd direction).

## Related

- bd-kk0a: writer-side escape for unbalanced apostrophes in JSON
  → qmd round-trip. Option-4-of-this-issue (parser fix) would
  obviate part of bd-kk0a's escape work.
- crates/pampa/snapshots/error-corpus/text/006.snap, 009.snap:
  current Q-2-7 examples for the parser-state mapping table at
  resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json:18686.
- Discovery transcript: changelog Q-2-7 thread in
  feature/q2-preview implementation session 2026-05-10.
notes: Pandoc-comparison findings posted to GH #221 (https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/221): symmetric notAfterString/notBeforeAlphanum predicates + speculative-balance fallback. Pandoc shares the same fundamental ambiguity but doesn't error — silently mis-quotes. Proposed fix scope: 'be at least as good as Pandoc' on the scope-table cases; a stricter fix (bias open-after-inline-end toward apostrophe) is harder design work.

title: Span writer: drop {} for empty attributes, use [ ] for empty span
description: Change the QMD writer so that a Span with empty content and empty attributes is written as '[ ]' (space between brackets) instead of '[]{}'. This improves readability for the checkbox use case in hub-react-todo.
close_reason: Implemented: spans with empty attrs drop {}, empty span writes as [ ]. All 6247 tests pass.

title: Code-block decorations (filename, copy, fold, line-numbers, annotations, preview)
description:
Port Quarto 1's code-block decorations to Quarto 2 using the existing Generate/Render transform pattern. One format-agnostic CodeBlockGenerateTransform extracts a typed CodeBlockDecoration from the AST; one CodeBlockRenderTransform per format emits the format-specific markup.

Features in scope (sized as phases in the plan):
1. Filename header  ({r filename="x.R"})
2. Code copy button (clipboard.js + scaffold)
3. Code folding ({code-fold: true|show}, <details>)
4. Line numbers ({code-line-numbers: true|"3,5-7"})
5. Code preview iframe ({code-preview="foo.qmd"})
6. Code annotations (# <N> markers + following ordered list)

Architecture, phase breakdown, open questions, and Q1 audit summary in:
  claude-notes/plans/2026-05-19-code-block-features.md

Out of scope (separate plans): LaTeX/PDF rendering, Reveal.js-specific line-number ranges, annotation tooltip interaction modes.

title: Suppress auto-generated header IDs in QMD writer roundtrips
description: Headers like '## project {.a-class}' roundtrip as '## project {#project .a-class}', adding an auto-generated ID that wasn't in the source. Similarly, '## project' becomes '## project {#project}'. The writer should detect auto-generated IDs (AttrSourceInfo.id is None) and omit them when they match what auto_generated_id() would produce. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-02-10-suppress-auto-header-ids.md
close_reason: Implemented. Auto-generated header IDs are now suppressed in QMD writer output. All 6394 workspace tests pass.

title: New file templates from project _quarto-hub-templates directory
description: Allow users to create new files from project-specific templates stored in _quarto-hub-templates directory. Templates are .qmd files with template-name metadata. The New File dialog shows a dropdown selector populated from available templates.

title: Apply assert_filtered_subset drift helper to build_analysis_transform_pipeline
description:
Plan 1 (`claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-1-pipeline.md` §"Resolved decisions / Drift-protection test") originally promised a follow-up applying `assert_filtered_subset` to `build_analysis_transform_pipeline`. Scope has narrowed since that promise.

## Background

The original drift helper (`assert_filtered_subset` in commit 60658a4e) was removed when q2-preview's pipeline was flipped to deny-list construction (`build_q2_preview_transform_pipeline` is now `build_transform_pipeline` filtered by `Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED`; `build_q2_preview_pipeline_stages` is similarly built from the HTML stage list with `Q2_PREVIEW_STAGE_EXCLUDED`). The drift mode the helper guarded against is now impossible by construction for q2-preview.

`build_analysis_transform_pipeline` (`crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:470`) is a different beast: a hand-written 6-transform sequence (sugar transforms + `crossref-index`) — *not* a deny-list of the full HTML transforms. Today it is protected only by:
- the doc-comment at `pipeline.rs:454-469` ("**Deliberately omitted**" rationale),
- a hand-rolled ordering test (`test_build_analysis_transform_pipeline_ordering`, `pipeline.rs:1392`) that asserts sparse position relations.

Because it's a hand-written allow-list (not a deny-list), the full HTML pipeline can grow new transforms relevant to outline analysis without anyone noticing — there's no test that fires when that happens.

## Work

This issue is now exclusively about the analysis pipeline. Two paths:

**Path A (cheaper)** — add a `seq_diff_eq` / `assert_seq_diff_eq` helper to the test module, expressing the analysis pipeline as `build_transform_pipeline` *minus* the exclusions documented at `pipeline.rs:454-469`. This treats the analysis pipeline as a deny-list at test time even though the runtime construction stays as an explicit allow-list.

**Path B (more work, more upside)** — flip `build_analysis_transform_pipeline` itself to deny-list construction (mirroring what was just done to q2-preview), with `ANALYSIS_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED` as a `const &[&str]`. The unknown-name validator pattern (see q2-preview tests in `pipeline.rs`) replaces the assertion. This makes drift impossible by construction.

Path B is preferred if the analysis pipeline really does want to be defined relative to the HTML pipeline (today it skips render-shape transforms, which is an HTML-pipeline-relative concept). Path A is the right choice if there's reason to keep analysis as a hand-written allow-list (e.g. its 6-transform shape is small enough that listing them is clearer than subtracting from HTML's 30+).

The doc-comment at `pipeline.rs:454-469` enumerates the deliberate omissions; the exclusion-list candidates are derivable from it. Verify each name against actual `Transform::name()` strings — the unknown-name validator catches typos / renames.

## Acceptance

Either:
- (Path A) New test in the `tests` module calls a deny-list-style assertion on `build_analysis_transform_pipeline`. Adding a new transform to `build_transform_pipeline` that isn't documented as either included or excluded in analysis trips the test.
- (Path B) `build_analysis_transform_pipeline` rewritten as `build_transform_pipeline(...).retain_excluding(ANALYSIS_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED)`. Existing `test_build_analysis_transform_pipeline_ordering` either becomes redundant (deny-list construction preserves order trivially) or stays for the cross-relation check. Unknown-name validator added.

## Notes

The naming question — if Path A is chosen and a helper is added: `assert_seq_diff_eq` was discussed (sequence difference `A - B = C` is the formal operation). See conversation around the deny-list flip for the naming rationale.

title: repo-actions assume GitHub URL shapes on every host
description:
repo-actions builds edit/source URLs with GitHub's path shapes on every host. GitLab uses /-/edit/<branch>/<path> and /-/blob/<branch>/<path>; Gitea and Codeberg use /_edit/ and /src/. On those hosts the 'source' link is wrong for every file type, and the 'edit' link is dropped entirely for .ipynb pages (deliberately -- Q1 commit 5c2186680 suppresses notebook edit links, 967197b12 carves out github.dev only, and that allowlist never grew).

Ported as-is in bd-repo-actions-missing-99ezd2fe for Q1 parity; this strand covers doing better. Needs a host-detection table mapping a repo-url host to its edit/blob path shapes, plus a decision on what to do for unrecognized hosts.

Upstream: quarto-dev/quarto-cli#5301 (open, 2023-04-25), with #7155 and #12138 closed as duplicates. None of those reporters mention notebooks.

title: pampa snapshot mismatches on Windows: stale source header + backslash in astContext name
description:
Two pending insta .snap.new files surface when running pampa tests on Windows (observed during bd-vxl8 work; NOT caused by it — bd-vxl8 only touched quarto-util path helpers and io_wasm/dofile_wasm Lua resolution, not the parser or snapshot generation).

1. crates/pampa/snapshots/native/007.snap — the committed snapshot's metadata header still reads 'source: crates/quarto-markdown-pandoc/tests/test.rs', a pre-rename / pre-consolidation path (crate was renamed to pampa and tests moved to tests/integration/, bd-xvdop). The actual snapshot BODY is identical (a CodeBlock); only the source header (and a missing assertion_line) is stale. Likely just needs the snapshot regenerated/accepted; probably not a hard test failure since insta compares the body.

2. crates/pampa/snapshots/json/001.snap — genuine content mismatch: astContext.files[].name is stored as 'tests/snapshots/json/001.qmd' (committed, forward slashes) but rendered as 'tests\snapshots\json\001.qmd' (backslashes) on Windows. The source-info/source-map serialization emits the input qmd file name with OS-native separators on Windows instead of normalized forward slashes. Fix is likely either normalizing the fixture path in the test harness or normalizing file names in the source-info serializer (quarto-source-map / pampa json writer). This one is a real Windows test failure.

Likely overlaps the existing Windows test catalog (memory://main/tasks/q2-windows-verify-tests). Investigate and decide: regenerate native/007; normalize path separators for json/001.
