title: q2 preview / hub-client: mermaid runtime still loaded from jsDelivr
description:
Follow-up to bd-mermaid-runtime-not-bundled-vxejw159, which bundles the mermaid runtime for the 'q2 render' path only. The preview path keeps its own independent CDN dependency.

WHERE. ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/MermaidCodeBlock.tsx: MERMAID_CDN_URL = https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@${MERMAID_VERSION}/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs, loaded by defaultLoader via a dynamic import marked /* @vite-ignore */ so vite deliberately does NOT bundle it. MERMAID_VERSION is pinned to '11.12.0' and kept in sync with the Rust constant by a test (MermaidCodeBlock.test.tsx:119). This component owns mermaid rendering for both q2-preview documents and q2-slides decks; the Rust mermaid-render transform is excluded from the preview pipeline (Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED), so the raw CodeBlock reaches the React layer.

Consequence: q2 preview and hub-client render no diagrams when jsDelivr is slow, blocked, or unreachable. Same defect class as bd-yvz2xqrm (Monaco stuck at 'Loading...' when the CDN was unavailable), which was fixed by bundling.

DIRECTION (from the design discussion on the parent strand). Do NOT simply bundle mermaid into the hub-client the way Monaco was bundled. Mermaid is 2.62 MiB and is used by only some documents, so putting it in the client distribution makes every user pay for it. Preferred shape: serve the runtime from the same vendored bytes the render path uses (resources/mermaid/mermaid.min.js, embedded via include_str!), delivered as an HTML dependency attached to the preview projects that actually contain diagrams -- i.e. an ordinary per-project JS dependency, resolved lazily, rather than part of the client bundle.

PRECEDENT NOTE -- read this before assuming revealjs already does the above; it does not, quite. The revealjs split today is: the RENDER path embeds vendored resources/revealjs/ via include_str! and emits site_libs/revealjs/ artifacts (crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs), while the PREVIEW path gets its JS from the npm packages bundled into the client (@revealjs/react 0.2.0 + reveal.js 6.0.0, in hub-client/ and ts-packages/preview-renderer/ package.json) and imports its CSS from the vendored files via vite (RevealDeck.tsx, reveal-reset-scope.test.ts). So 'vendored bytes served as a per-project HTML dependency to preview' is a NEW mechanism to design, not an existing pattern to copy. Reveal is also a reasonable thing to bundle (it is core to every deck) in a way mermaid is not.

Watch for: bundling Monaco pushed the vite build past the default ~2 GB Node heap and needed NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 (bd-yvz2xqrm comment c-iw7g59gg). A design that keeps mermaid out of the client bundle avoids that, which is a further argument for it.

Also note the version-parity test between MERMAID_VERSION in the TSX and in crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/mermaid.rs; whatever mechanism lands must keep the two in sync.

c-00tq71p6.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-00tq71p6.text:
Useful input from the render-path work (bd-mermaid-runtime-not-bundled-vxejw159, now implemented): the vendored mermaid bundle is ALREADY EMBEDDED IN THE WASM CLIENT.

quarto-core is linked into wasm-quarto-hub-client, and the runtime is embedded there via include_str! from resources/mermaid/mermaid.min.js. Measured: wasm_quarto_hub_client_bg.wasm went 38,935,233 -> 41,758,814 bytes (+2.82 MB, +7.3%). Confirmed directly by probing the .wasm for distinctive mermaid strings (__esbuild_esm_mermaid_nm, "Bezier curve function generator"), not inferred from the size delta.

Today those bytes are dead weight: the preview pipeline excludes the mermaid transform (Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED) and MermaidCodeBlock.tsx fetches its own copy from jsDelivr. So the client currently pays 2.8 MB for a runtime it does not use, AND still depends on a CDN.

This makes the direction chosen for this strand cheaper than expected: serving the vendored bytes as a per-project HTML dependency needs no new asset in the client bundle -- the bytes are already there, reachable from Rust. crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/mermaid.rs exposes register_mermaid_assets(&mut ArtifactStore) (pub, for exactly this reason), which stores the runtime as an ArtifactScope::Project artifact at mermaid/mermaid.min.js. Artifact flushing is path-driven, so the WASM/VFS resolver path should work the same way.

One design note to carry over: do NOT key the artifact under the js: prefix. ApplyTemplateStage emits a head <script> for every js: artifact (double-load), and the reveal scaffold collects only js:revealjs:* (no tag at all in decks). The render path keys it mermaid:runtime and emits its own <script src> + init into the after-body slot; unit test runtime_is_not_keyed_as_a_template_script and integration test revealjs_deck_bundles_the_runtime pin both halves.

Also: the render side deliberately did NOT cfg-gate the constant out of wasm32, because that would make this strand's design harder and would make any WASM-side HTML export silently produce CDN-dependent output. If this strand concludes the client should not carry the bytes, that decision can be revisited here.

title: macOS flake: hub admin scan mis-cases doc ids on case-insensitive filesystems
description:
crates/quarto-hub/src/admin/scan.rs:list_doc_ids_filesystem reconstructs a doc id as <level-1 dir name> + <level-2 dir name>. On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS default APFS, Windows), two docs whose ids differ only in the case of their first two characters share one on-disk level-1 directory, whose name preserves the case of whichever doc was created first. Enumeration then reports the OTHER doc's id with the wrong case.

Observed as a CI flake: run 31441577535 (macos-latest, main @ a429becc) failed collect_reverification_skips_rereferenced_candidate with left="2Nb28YwnAezDD1w1iyh29kQ916om" right="2nb28YwnAezDD1w1iyh29kQ916om" (crates/quarto-hub/tests/integration/admin_collect_lifecycle.rs:205). Passes 5/5 locally on macOS; the collision depends on the randomly generated ids, so it is low-probability per run.

Not a regression from PR #499 (which touches nothing in quarto-hub). Real user impact: 'quarto hub admin scan/collect' can mis-identify a doc on macOS/Windows stores, which matters because collect deletes chunks.

Fix direction: do not reconstruct ids from directory names on case-insensitive filesystems -- either verify each reconstructed id round-trips through the storage adapter, or read the id from the chunk contents rather than the path.
close_reason:
Duplicate of bd-eb2wnxkp (linked). That strand predates this one by two weeks (2026-07-28 vs 2026-08-11), diagnoses the same unsound id reconstruction in list_doc_ids_filesystem, and goes further: it identifies a SECOND instance of the class (normalize_id in classify.rs) that is NOT platform-gated and could read a referenced doc as an orphan on Linux production.

Filed during v0.17.0 release triage without checking for an existing strand — my error. The concrete recurrence I observed (a different call site: the collect path, run 31441577535) has been recorded as a comment on bd-eb2wnxkp so the evidence is not lost.

NOT closing as fixed: PR #501 shipped only Part A (path-side recovery) plus a collect guard. Parts B (content-side normalize_id) and C (thread DocumentId instead of String) remain, bd-eb2wnxkp is still in_progress, and bd-u0tldu4z holds the stress-verification obligation that is the actual flake close-out criterion.

title: Diagnostic popups clipped by navbar when near top/bottom of editor
description: Monaco diagnostic hover popups get clipped by the top navbar (and potentially the bottom edge) because the editor container uses overflow:hidden. When a diagnostic appears on a line near the top of the editor, the hover popup extends above the editor-main container and gets cut off. The fix should ensure the popup is shifted vertically to stay within visible bounds, rather than changing z-order.

title: Tree-sitter splits paragraph at line starting with * (emphasis or strong)
description:
Same class as bd-af1e. The scanner's line-break handler at scanner.c:2286-2291 and 2371-2376 excludes '*' from soft-line-break candidates whenever it appears at the start of a continuation line. But '*' only opens a block in specific contexts:
- '* ' followed by space → list marker
- '*** ' or longer with whitespace/eol → thematic break
- otherwise → inline emphasis ('*emph*') or strong ('**strong**'), which should soft-break

Verified pampa-vs-pandoc divergence:
  foo bar
  *emph* baz       → pampa: 2 paragraphs, pandoc: 1 with SoftBreak + Emph
  **strong** baz   → pampa: 2 paragraphs, pandoc: 1 with SoftBreak + Strong

Why this matters (severity sibling of bd-af1e): the asterisk IS the syntax for inline emphasis/strong. A user CANNOT work around the bug with backslash escaping (\\*emph\\* renders literally as '*emph*'). Underscore alternatives (_emph_, __strong__) work correctly already because '_' is not in the exclusion list, but many users prefer asterisks.

By contrast, '-', '+', '#', and digits at line start CAN be worked around via backslash escape (\\-text, \\#hashtag, \\123abc render as plain text starting with the punctuation), so we are deferring those.

Fix approach (same as bd-af1e — peek-count): when first_lookahead == '*', advance through consecutive asterisks. Then check what follows:
- whitespace/eol after a single '*' → list marker (interrupt)
- whitespace/eol after 3+ '*' → thematic break (interrupt)  
- anything else → inline (allow soft break)

Reference implementation: bd-af1e fix in scanner.c:2263-2308 (commit 274547af). The peek-without-mark_end + STATE_MATCHING-fallback pattern from that fix should generalize directly. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-tree-sitter-backtick-paragraph-split.md.

Test the fix doesn't break: '* item' (list opens), '*** ' (thematic break), '**foo**' at line start (inline strong), and '*foo*' / '**foo**' as continuation lines (soft break).
close_reason: Fixed: extended bd-af1e peek-count pattern to '*' at line start. Single '*' followed by ws/eol → list marker (interrupt); >=3 '*' followed by ws/eol → thematic break (interrupt); otherwise inline emph/strong → soft break. Tree-sitter test 462/462 pass; workspace 8125/8125 pass; pampa output matches pandoc.

title: qmd writer: missing @ escape in link text causes citation re-parse
description:
From issue #150 (item 1): When a link text contains an escaped @ like `[\@jjallaire](url)`, the qmd writer outputs the link text without re-escaping the @. Round-tripping turns the Str into a Cite. Repro:

  printf 'See [\\@jjallaire](https://github.com/jjallaire/) for details.\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd
  See [@jjallaire](https://github.com/jjallaire/) for details.

Reporter notes there are likely other cases where escaping is needed; this is the one they saw. Plan in claude-notes/plans/ to follow.
notes:
Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-at-escape-qmd-roundtrip.md
Root cause: crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:1226 escape_markdown omits @
Fix: lookahead-based escape of @ when followed by alnum/_/{
Bug also reproduces outside link context (any Str starting with @<ident>).
close_reason: Fixed in escape_markdown: always escape @ in Str bodies. Phase 2 audit of writer-escape gaps also identified { and } as same class; both fixed in this change. Position-dependent escapes (:, unbalanced ' ", line-start list markers 1./-/+) deferred to bd-kk0a. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-at-escape-qmd-roundtrip.md.

title: Windows: smoke-all suite has 21 failures — theme CSS/scss content missing, href separator, highlighting
description: cargo nextest run quarto::integration smoke_all::smoke_all fails on Windows: 21/90 smoke fixtures fail (49 passed, 20 skipped). Categories: (1) ALL theme-* fixtures using custom/project/metadata/relpath/crossdir/cascade scss (theme-array, theme-array-subdir, theme-cascade-three-layer, theme-crossdir-scss, theme-metadata-scss x2, theme-metadata-scss-relpath x2, theme-project-scss x2, theme-project-scss-relpath x2, theme-subdir-doc-override) fail ensureCssRegexMatches on their custom hex colors and marker classes AND on a common #170229 pattern shared by all of them -- suggests either the whole custom-theme scss layer is not being merged into compiled CSS on Windows, or a stale/shared compiled-CSS cache is being reused across docs with different themes (caching keyed wrong on Windows, e.g. by a path string with backslashes). (2) metadata/theme-inheritance/* fixtures (appendix-doc, custom-doc, chapter1, chapter2, deep-doc, root-doc) fail on missing --bs-primary:.*#HEX for their assigned bootswatch theme (darkly #375a7f, flatly #2c3e50, cerulean #2780e3, cosmo?) and root-doc.qmd additionally has an 'Illegal CSS pattern found: Base Styles' -- so even built-in bootswatch theme selection per doc/chapter is not taking effect on Windows, not just custom scss. This makes candidate root cause bigger than bd-oejuizi9 (which is specifically about relative-path resolution being document-dir vs project-dir) -- here root-level docs fail too, so it looks like theme resolution/compilation itself is broken or cached wrong on Windows, not just a path-base bug. (3) metadata/dir-metadata-paths/chapters/intro/doc.qmd: expected selector link[href="../../shared/styles.css"] not found -- looks like a Windows path-separator leak (backslash) into the generated href, same family as the already-fixed bd-dff27o04 (JSON writer backslash) but a different code path (HTML link href generation) that fix didn't cover. (4) highlighting/01-builtin-python.qmd: required CSS pattern \.hl-keyword not found -- syntax highlighting for python isn't emitting the hl-keyword class/rule on Windows; separate suspect, possibly a highlight grammar/theme resource path lookup that also breaks on Windows path separators. Full failing fixture list and expected-vs-actual is in the raw nextest output attached to this strand's originating session; rerun via: cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'binary(integration) & test(smoke_all)' to reproduce. Needs investigation to determine if (1)/(2) share one root cause (theme compile/cache keying) distinct from (3)/(4) (path-separator leaks into output), or if they're actually the same backslash-leak root cause manifesting in scss @import resolution too.
close_reason: smoke-all Windows failures resolved: 21->0. Three root causes fixed on branch braid/bd-22rtwdur-windows-smoke-all-suite (one PR): (A) CRLF SCSS layer markers + embedded @import separator [bd-3fgnmlco], (B) href backslash separator in !path metadata adjustment + POSIX-absolute rooted-path misdetection [bd-5rl408mv]. directory_metadata_tests 15/15, quarto-sass 221/221, smoke_all green. Residual 3 engine_execution failures are pre-existing, separate subsystem.

The other session confirmed Cause A with the built binary: revealjs render hard-errors on themes/default.scss; theme: flatly renders but drops #2c3e50 (silent base-CSS fallback). c-7me5a2vk.author: cderv
c-7me5a2vk.text:
Investigation 2026-07-03: root causes confirmed; original hypotheses corrected. This is a Windows-only code bug, not a Linux-only test — CI runs ubuntu+macos only (test-suite.yml:25), fixtures are correct and green there. quarto-sass unit tests also fail on Windows (20), confirming it is code, not fixtures.

TWO distinct root causes:

CAUSE A (20 of 21 failures = categories 1,2,4): CRLF, NOT cache-keying or scss-merge. resources/scss/**/*.scss are checked out CRLF on Windows (git autocrlf; .gitattributes does not cover scss) and embedded via include_dir with those CRLFs. parse_layer boundary regexes (crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs:49-56) are $-anchored (^/\*--...scss:...--\*/$); Rust (?m)$ matches before \n but leaves the trailing \r in the line, so NoBoundaryMarkers. Proven: parse_layer(CRLF)=false, parse_layer(LF)=true. Layer parse failure -> compile_with_doc_vars errors -> stage SILENTLY falls back to base styles.css (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/compile_theme_css.rs:547-554, warn suppressed by quiet). That fallback (7.3KB 'Base Styles') is why every theme fixture is missing its --bs-primary + custom marker, and why root-doc trips 'Illegal CSS pattern found: Base Styles'. highlight.scss is also CRLF (196) so .hl-keyword is dropped (category 4 = same cause, NOT a resource-path-lookup bug).

CAUSE B (1 failure = category 3, dir-metadata-paths): backslash leaked into HTML <link href>: rendered href="..\..\shared\styles.css", expected ../../shared/styles.css. Resolution logic is correct (../../shared is right); only the separator is wrong. Same family as fixed bd-dff27o04, different emission site (css/!path -> HTML link href).

RELATION TO bd-oejuizi9: NOT the same bug. bd-oejuizi9 is cross-platform per-doc-dir vs project-root theme resolution (would fail on Linux too). These fixtures (incl -relpath/subdir) pass on Linux CI, so that resolution already works here; on Windows Cause A masks everything uniformly, which is why root docs fail and it looked bigger than bd-oejuizi9. Only overlap: Cause B lives in the same !path area but is a separator leak, not resolution.

FIX DIRECTIONS (undecided, to discuss): Cause A = make layer parsing CRLF-robust (normalize \r\n before parse_layer, or tolerate \r?$) AND/OR .gitattributes '*.scss text eol=lf'; also decide whether theme-compile failure should stay a silent fallback or become a hard error (the silent fallback is what hid this). Cause B = to_forward_slashes at the css/include href emission site.

c-a9ge8g95.author: cderv
c-a9ge8g95.text: Decomposed into two root-cause strands (both now block this smoke-all umbrella): bd-3fgnmlco = Cause A (CRLF-terminated SCSS layer markers rejected by $-anchored regex in layer.rs, silent fallback to base CSS) covers 20 of 21 failures; bd-5rl408mv = Cause B (backslash separators in HTML <link href> for css/!path includes) covers the 1 dir-metadata-paths failure. Cause A is shared with bd-gl0bufxp (revealjs_cli, same root cause). This strand stays as the smoke-all tracking umbrella; it goes green once both cause strands land.

c-cb6t39fb.author: cderv
c-cb6t39fb.text: Progress 2026-07-03: two of the three root causes fixed on this worktree branch (unpushed). PR1 bd-3fgnmlco (parse_layer CRLF) commit 0e3cd389; embedded @import separator bd-nxxgg0pp commit 3a13b6b1 (reuses quarto_util::to_forward_slashes at EmbeddedResources::strip_prefix). Verified on a Windows checkout: quarto-sass 206/206; quarto-core 94->21 failures (proven improvement via revert-compare, residual 21 pre-existing/other-subsystem); smoke_all 21->1 failures. The single remaining smoke failure is category 3, the backslash in HTML <link href="../../shared/styles.css">, tracked as bd-5rl408mv (PR2, href separator) -- not yet started. Deferred discoveries filed: bd-jxkj05ys (unify embedded pools into WASM VFS), bd-vvxo9ln2 (windows-latest CI). Design doc: claude-notes/designs/embedded-resource-virtual-path-contract.md.

c-wnxrybwl.author: cderv
c-wnxrybwl.text: Cross-ref bd-gl0bufxp (revealjs, related): categories 1 and 2 (theme scss content missing) likely share one root cause with the revealjs failure -- parse_layer in crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs is not CRLF-tolerant. Its $-anchored marker regexes fail on CRLF (Windows core.autocrlf=true -> resources/scss/** are CRLF in the working tree, baked into include_dir!). parse_layer returns SassError::NoBoundaryMarkers; revealjs hard-errors, the bootstrap load_theme path appears to fall back to base CSS -> theme colours silently missing, matching cats 1/2. Worth checking user-authored/project scss too (also CRLF on disk on Windows). Cats 3 (href backslash) and 4 (highlighting hl-keyword) look like separate path-separator issues, not this. Full analysis in bd-gl0bufxp comment thread.

title: Hub-Client E2E logs are flooded with YAMLWarning [TAG_RESOLVE_FAILED] !str
description:
Playwright e2e runs produce hundreds of warnings of the form:

  (node:NNNNN) [TAG_RESOLVE_FAILED] YAMLWarning: Unresolved tag: !str at line 14, column 12:
          - [!str "<pre class=\"sourceCode toml\"",
             ^^^^

The yaml npm library is encountering explicit !str tags it doesn't have
a resolver for. It falls back to treating the value as a string, so tests
keep running — but the noise drowns out useful output.

Source of the warning: some fixture or generated YAML emits !str-tagged
scalars (looks like syntax-highlighted HTML being serialized into YAML).
Fix is either to register a custom tag resolver for !str, or change the
emitter to use plain quoted strings.

Discovered while getting hub-client-e2e.yml workflow to run on CI
(branch chore/e2e-ci). Not a test failure cause, just log noise.

title: Lua parity A: filter-return values through fuzzy peekers
description: filter.rs return handlers keep only userdata: bare-string returns are silent no-ops, non-userdata table entries silently dropped. Route all filter return paths through peek_inlines_fuzzy/peek_blocks_fuzzy. Differential cases: filter-return-string, filter-return-mixed-table. Catalog: claude-notes/research/2026-07-13-lua-api-mismatch-catalog.md. Epic plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-13-lua-api-pandoc-parity.md.
close_reason: Fixed: filter returns coerced via fuzzy peekers; differential 15/15, 0 xfail; commit 61790195

c-6d1e1iiu.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-6d1e1iiu.text:
HANDOFF (from the bd-grkrb9nj session that built the conformance harness, 2026-07-13).

CONTEXT. This strand is part of epic bd-grkrb9nj (Lua API Pandoc parity). Read first:
- claude-notes/plans/2026-07-13-lua-api-pandoc-parity.md (esp. Decisions + Current state)
- claude-notes/research/2026-07-13-lua-api-mismatch-catalog.md (cluster 3 is this strand)
Branch: work continues on top of feature/bd-grkrb9nj-lua-api-pandoc-parity (remote). Scoreboards at handoff: Track-1 conformance 90/133 passing, differential 6/8; the 2 differential xfails ARE this strand's failing tests (TDD step 1 done).

THE BUG. Filter RETURN values are interpreted by ad-hoc userdata-only logic in crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs — six handlers: handle_inline_return, handle_block_return, and four *_with_control variants (all take lua as first param). Each: nil -> keep original; userdata -> extract; table -> splice keeping ONLY userdata entries; anything else -> SILENTLY keep original. Result: 'return "replaced"' from a Str filter is a silent no-op, and a bare string inside a returned table vanishes. Pandoc coerces returns with the same fuzzy peekers used for constructor args.

THE FIX. Collapse the userdata/table/other arms into peek_inlines_fuzzy / peek_blocks_fuzzy (crates/pampa/src/lua/types.rs) — they already flush property caches (bd-hitjclzp), so mutation persistence is preserved. MUST NOT change: nil -> keep original; empty table -> delete; the *_with_control second return value (false -> stop traversal).

SUBTLETIES.
1. Oracle-probe BEFORE implementing (pinned pandoc 3.9.0.2, see tests/lua-conformance/differential/ORACLE_VERSION): does pandoc word-split a multi-word string return from an Inline filter ('return "two words"')? And what does a Block filter returning a string produce (expect Plain(word-split))? And what does pandoc do with 'return 5' / 'return true' (expect a raised error)? Use 'pandoc -f markdown x.md -L f.lua -t json' or 'pandoc lua'.
2. Behavior change: number/boolean returns go from silent no-op to LOUD error (per plan Decision: match pandoc where it accepts; error actionably where it errors). Make the message name the filter function and got-type; Q-coding comes later under bd-9p2686pc.
3. A3 audit (in scope): shortcode.rs classify_table_result drops non-userdata entries the same way; check Inlines/Blocks list-filter returns (handle_inlines/blocks_return_with_control cover typewise too?) and any doc/meta-level return paths.
4. In-file tests at the bottom of filter.rs (~line 2340+) pin CURRENT semantics incl. 'integer return keeps original' — update them deliberately to the new contract.

WORKFLOW. TDD via the harnesses: the failing tests exist (differential cases filter-return-string, filter-return-mixed-table). Add differential cases for the oracle probes in (1) (regen with tests/lua-conformance/differential/regen-oracles.sh; CI never needs pandoc). After the fix: LUA_CONFORMANCE_DUMP=1 to regenerate xfail lists (ratchet fails on unexpected passes — remove the two lines from differential/xfail.txt). Then: cargo nextest run -p pampa --features lua-filter (all must pass), cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build, e2e via the real binary (target/debug/pampa x.md -F f.lua -t html) compared against pandoc, per CLAUDE.md end-to-end policy. Update the plan checklist (item 2.2) + catalog progress log, close this strand with the scoreboard delta, commit on the feature branch. Do NOT import .braid/snapshot.jsonl; braid syncs itself.

c-ussa2kh0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ussa2kh0.text: DONE (2026-07-13 session). All filter-return paths route through peek_inlines_fuzzy/peek_blocks_fuzzy: six filter.rs handlers + the two ad-hoc typewise list-splice sites (apply_inlines_filter, walk_blocks_straight) which now delegate to new shared handle_inlines_return/handle_blocks_return. Contract oracle-probed (13 probes, pandoc 3.9.0.2): bare string -> word-split (Plain-wrapped in block position); table -> element-wise (string entry -> single Str, no split; number/nested-table entry -> error); Inline userdata from Block filter -> Plain-wrapped; number/boolean -> loud error naming filter fn + got-type (pandoc errors too; Q-coding deferred to bd-9p2686pc). Invariants kept: nil keep, empty-table delete, false stops topdown. A3: shortcode classify_table_result fixed same way (also un-drops inlines in mixed inline/block tables); dead extract_lua_*_from_table deleted; doc-level filter gap filed bd-a9g50za2. SCOREBOARD: differential 8 cases/2 xfail -> 15 cases/0 xfail (7 new oracle cases); Track-1 unchanged 90/133 (cluster was Track-2-only, as the handoff predicted). Verification: 4088/4088 pampa tests, full cargo xtask verify green (incl. WASM+hub legs), e2e byte-identical to pandoc via real pampa binary; 'return 5' exits 1 with actionable message. Commit 61790195 on feature/bd-grkrb9nj-lua-api-pandoc-parity (not pushed). Plan item 2.2 + catalog progress log updated.

title: Whitespace-only separator lines make lists tight where pandoc/Q1 say loose
description: A whitespace-only line (e.g. 4 spaces) between a list item's paragraph and a nested list yields a TIGHT first block (Plain) where a truly blank line yields loose (Para). pandoc and Quarto 1 treat whitespace-only lines as blank -> loose in both cases. Present in v0.18.0 and unchanged by the bd-j7be7kuc fix; happens with and without a wrapping div. Mechanism: list_item_has_blank_line_between_blocks (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs) detects blankness only via a block_continuation node INSIDE the paragraph spanning multiple rows; in the whitespace-only shape the continuation splits into a single-row node inside the para plus a sibling block_continuation between the blocks, so the detector misses it. Repro cells pinned (as current v0.18.0-compatible behavior) in test_indented_continuation::attributed_div_is_transparent_to_list_indentation ('repro A' = Plain vs 'control B' = Para) — update those expectations when fixing. Reference repro: q2-connect-docs llms-info/repros/attributed-div-ws-blank-list.

title: Website mobile secondary-nav bar (quarto-secondary-nav): sidebar toggle, collapsed breadcrumbs, search button
description:
Q1 gives every sidebar-bearing website page a <nav class="quarto-secondary-nav"> — the whole narrow-viewport navigation bar, hidden on lg+ viewports. It holds (a) the sidebar collapse toggle button (data-bs-target=".quarto-sidebar-collapse-item", the ONLY way to open the sidebar on a phone), (b) the page's breadcrumb trail in compact form (or the collapsed title when bread-crumbs: false), and (c) the search button. q2 has none of this machinery: no .quarto-sidebar-collapse-item markup in sidebar_to_html, no headroom JS hook, only vestigial color rules in _bootstrap-rules.scss (nav.quarto-secondary-nav.color-navbar).

Scope decided during bd-breadcrumbs-missing-1vpuqh34 (2026-08-14): that strand shipped the title-block breadcrumb instance (quarto-title-breadcrumbs, d-none d-lg-block) and deliberately did NOT emit the secondary-nav container, because a toggle wired to markup that doesn't exist would be broken UI. This strand owns the container.

What lands here:
- The container markup (Q1 template: external-sources/quarto-cli/src/resources/projects/website/templates/nav-before-body.ejs lines 63-93) — toggle button, flex-grow link, search button, aria wiring.
- The sidebar side: .quarto-sidebar-collapse-item class + Bootstrap collapse plumbing so the toggle actually opens the sidebar on narrow viewports.
- The mobile breadcrumb instance: reuse breadcrumb_trail + breadcrumbs_to_html (quarto-navigation) with NO extra classes (the title-block instance passes [quarto-title-breadcrumbs, d-none, d-lg-block]); render even for length-1 trails (Q1 renders the secondary-nav instance whenever bread-crumbs is enabled, unlike the >1 gate on the title instance); honor the bread-crumbs:false fallback (collapsed h1.quarto-secondary-nav-title from the page title).

Implementation complete on branch braid/bd-26bf3j1y-website-mobile-secondary-nav (7 commits, 4b1ee305..b720b39f). NOT pushed — awaiting review.

Mobile breadcrumb instance with no extra classes and no >1-crumb gate; bread-crumbs:false collapses the page title into the bar and hides h1.title below lg. No search button (bd-6cme), no headroom hooks (bd-ersobfbt).
- Sidebar collapse plumbing: collapse/collapse-horizontal/quarto-sidebar-collapse-item/overflow-auto on nav#quarto-sidebar, plus #quarto-sidebar-glass.

Verification: cargo xtask verify (full, incl. WASM + hub-client) exit 0. Workspace 12238 tests passing, clippy clean. E2E through the binary on a fixture and on docs/ (243 pages; 182 with sidebars get the bar). Headless-browser measurements at 620/900/1400px recorded in the plan.

FIVE findings, all in the plan — the first four came from checking Q1's RENDERED OUTPUT rather than its sources, and two are bugs the whole test suite could not see:

F1: Q1's title-block hiding is DEAD CODE. Its postprocessor selects 'header > .quarto-title-block', but every Q1 template puts that class ON the header, so the parent is never a header. 0 of 350 Connect pages have d-none on the title block. Decision 6's first half was therefore dropped — parity means NOT hiding — and pinned by a regression test instead.

F2: Q1's duplicate role="link" doesn't survive its own postprocessor; emitting only role="navigation" is byte-parity.

F3 (BUG, found in browser): the drawer never opened below 768px. nav[role="doc-toc"]{display:none} also matched nav#quarto-sidebar, because q2 puts that role on the sidebar as well as the TOC (the bd-eczdzfqo divergence). .show only defeats Bootstrap's own .collapse:not(.show), not an unrelated display:none. Toggle latched, glass dimmed, nothing appeared. Scoped to nav#TOC[role="doc-toc"].

F4 (BUG, found by looking at a screenshot): the drawer was transparent — q2 never ported Q1's sidebar background rule (quarto-nav.scss:543-551). Invisible while the sidebar sat in its own grid column; page text showed through once it overlaid the article. This makes sidebars paint $sidebar-bg on desktop too — verified as Q1 parity (identical rule, identical $sidebar-bg default expression in both projects).

F5: three loose-substring test proxies had to be tightened (not tweaked) — !contains("auto") vs overflow-auto, contains("quarto-page-breadcrumbs") vs the shared base class, and contains(".sidebar.sidebar-navigation:not(.rollup)") vs the new background rule. Each now asserts the property it always meant.

Worth reviewing specifically: the two browser-found bugs, and the fact that phases 3+4 must stay in one commit (the collapse class without the lg+ override hides the sidebar at every width, undetectably by markup assertions — quarto-sass's test_sidebar_stays_visible_at_lg_despite_collapse_class guards it).

title: sectionize_blocks does not recurse into Divs: q2 emits <div><h4> where Q1 emits <section class="level4 …">
description:
Found while investigating bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7. A heading nested inside any Div is never sectionized by q2. Given: ::: {.my-wrapper} #### Heading inside a plain div Body. ::: Q1 renders (the Div is absorbed into the section, its class merged in):

…

q2 @ 5b6774d1 renders (the Div survives, the header is never wrapped):

…

MECHANISM. pampa's sectionize_blocks (crates/pampa/src/transforms/sectionize.rs:75) walks only the top-level block list; it never recurses into Div content. Pandoc's makeSections recurses into Divs and, when the Div's id is empty, merges the Div's attributes into the section it creates. (makeSections does NOT descend into BlockQuote — see bd-8yjvs3bj.) WHY IT HAS GONE UNNOTICED. It cancels against a second divergence: q2's collect_toc_entries recurses into every non-section Div and collects bare Headers, so the TOC entry appears anyway and only the DOM differs. Fix one without the other and the TOC entry disappears — see the direction (A)/(B) discussion in claude-notes/plans/2026-08-18-tabset-headings-in-toc.md. IMPACT. DOM/CSS parity for the Connect docs port (section vs div affects section-scoped selectors, anchors, and scroll targets), and it is a prerequisite for making the TOC collector walk only the section tree. Probe: claude-notes/plans/tabset-headings-in-toc-investigation/div-toc-probe/. Blast radius: sectionize output feeds quarto-ast-reconcile hashing, transforms/llms.rs, the idempotence tests, and the HTML writer's 'section' class detection.
close_reason: Delivered by bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7 Phase 2: sectionize_div recurses into non-section Divs and applies pandoc's absorb rule (empty id + exactly one section -> replace the Div, merging classes and key-values). Rule pinned against Q1 by the five-case absorb-rule-probe. Connect corpus: <section> count 3626 -> 3678.

title: preview parity: Link drops kv attributes outside a narrow allowlist (role, aria-*, etc.)
description: Found by the preview<->render DOM parity harness (hub-client/src/services/smokeAllParity.wasm.test.tsx) on fixture crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/appendix/footnotes-heading.qmd. render: 1 preview: 1 render: ↩︎ preview: ↩︎ Native writer: crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:968 (calls write_attr, which at html.rs:520-529 emits every kv attribute, data-prefixing only those should_prefix_attribute (html.rs:463-481) flags as non-standard; role is an RDFa attribute and passes through bare). React: ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/inlines/Link.tsx:10-12 only forwards kv attrs matching k.startsWith('data-') || k === 'rel' || k === 'target' — everything else (role, aria-*, hreflang, type, download, ...) is silently dropped. This is broader than footnotes: any kv attribute on a Link outside that narrow allowlist is dropped by the preview. The footnotes transform (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/footnotes.rs:483 and :578) sets role="doc-noteref"/"doc-backlink", so this is an accessibility regression in the preview, not just a cosmetic DOM difference. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-preview-render-dom-parity-harness.md Fix should end with `parity: true` on the fixture.

title: Consider excluding bootstrap-js and clipboard-js stages from q2-preview
description:
BootstrapJsStage (added in bd-4eyf) and ClipboardJsStage (added in bd-j1trh) are in the q2-preview pipeline by default because Q2_PREVIEW_STAGE_EXCLUDED only names math-js, render-html-body, apply-template. Worth checking whether that's the intent.

Both stages are gated #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))], so the hub-client (WASM) preview never sees them. Native q2-preview does run them.

Their WASM-exclusion rationale (bootstrap_js.rs:48-55, clipboard_js.rs:45) is that the hub-client iframe reinitializes on every render tick, wiping any state held by Bootstrap components. That argument applies just as well to native q2-preview, which also targets the iframe.

Both stages mutate only ctx.artifacts; neither touches doc.ast.meta or doc.ast.blocks. The downstream consumer that turns js:* artifacts into <script> tags is ApplyTemplateStage, which q2-preview already excludes. Net effect: on native q2-preview these stages register JS artifacts that nothing reads.

Question: should Q2_PREVIEW_STAGE_EXCLUDED also list 'bootstrap-js' and 'clipboard-js'?

For exclusion:
- Matches the WASM HTML pipeline.
- Removes orphan artifact registration on native q2-preview.

Against:
- The deny-list framing at pipeline.rs:1170 says q2-preview opts a stage out only when there's a concrete reason. These stages are deterministic and harmless; the case for excluding them is tidiness, not correctness.
- If a future non-iframe q2-preview renderer wants to consume those artifacts, the exclusion would have to be undone.

Context: surfaced during Plan 3 (idempotence verification) review on 2026-05-20. Plan 3's hash test is unaffected either way — these stages don't write to the hashed surface — so this is filed separately rather than bundled into Plan 3.

References:
- crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:355 — Q2_PREVIEW_STAGE_EXCLUDED
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/bootstrap_js.rs:48-55
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/clipboard_js.rs:45
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-3-builtin-filter-idempotence.md

title: D2: HTML table emits Bootstrap 'caption-top table' classes
description:
## What

Every `Block::Table` should have CSS classes `caption-top` and `table` in its rendered HTML output (matches Quarto 1 / Bootstrap convention).

## Approach (chosen in plan)

New pipeline stage `HtmlTableClassTransform` in `crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/` that augments `Block::Table.attr.1` (class vec) with `caption-top` and `table` if missing. Stage runs only for HTML output formats; preserves round-trip qmd writer (writer does not see Quarto-added classes since classes are added post-AST sanitization for HTML output only).

Rationale for stage (vs writer hack): preserves separation of concerns — HTML writer renders what's in the AST; format-specific class augmentation happens in a stage. Mirrors TS Quarto's `quarto-bootstrap-table.lua` filter pattern.

## Tests (TDD)

1. Unit test on the transform: input table with no classes → output has `caption-top table`. Running transform twice doesn't duplicate (idempotent).
2. Unit test: input table with existing `my-class` → output has `my-class caption-top table` (preserves user classes, dedupes).
3. End-to-end render test against `tables.qmd` fixture → produced HTML contains `<table class="caption-top table">`.

## Plan

claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-table-default-rendering-parity.md (D2 section)
close_reason: Implemented in 987bdc9f via TableBootstrapClassTransform in FINALIZATION phase. Q1 markup parity for <table> classes achieved (still needs Bootstrap CSS — D7).

title: hub-mcp silently no-ops when invoked via a symlinked path (macOS /tmp, npm .bin shims)
description: index.ts gates main() on import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href. Node's ESM loader canonicalizes import.meta.url through realpath, but argv[1] is taken verbatim — so any symlink in the invocation path (macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp, /var -> /private/var, npm/npx .bin shims) makes the comparison fail and the process loads modules then exits 0 without ever starting the MCP server. Found when the bd-81cfshmw bundle smoke test spawned the bundle from os.tmpdir() (/var/folders/...). Would have broken the npx channel (bd-3tak0lyy) on day one. Fix: realpathSync(argv[1]) before comparing.
close_reason: Fixed in eb6da24f: realpathSync(argv[1]) before entry-module comparison. Regression test via explicit symlink in symlink-invocation.test.ts.

title: whitespace_re regex recompiles per inline-processing call in native_visitor
description:
crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:606 declares `let whitespace_re: Lazy<Regex> = Lazy::new(|| Regex::new(r"\s+").unwrap());` as a FUNCTION-LOCAL. The Lazy wrapper is pointless when local — a fresh Lazy is built (and \s+ recompiled on first touch) on every call to this per-node inline-processing function.

Evidence: samply profile of full q2 render of claude-notes/qmd-plans (565 files) attributes ~5% of ALL samples to the Thompson NFA compiler / Utf8State construction (regex::Regex::new), 100% under native_visitor's closure. See claude-notes/plans/2026-06-01-render-perf-profiling.md.

Fix: hoist to a module-level static (LazyLock<Regex> or once_cell Lazy). Must land before any Pass-2 parallelization, otherwise every worker thread recompiles it per node.

TDD: add a regression guard (e.g. a test/bench asserting the regex is shared / compiled once, or a micro-benchmark over the corpus). Verify end-to-end via q2 render wall-time before/after.
notes:
FIXED. Hoisted whitespace_re to module-level static WHITESPACE_RE in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs. Added regression test test_whitespace_re_compile_once (asserts \s+ compiles <=1x via WHITESPACE_RE_COMPILE_COUNT). Buggy compiled \s+ 20806x over the 565-file corpus; fixed compiles 1x.

Perf (median-of-5, release): isolated parse path -11.5% serial (2822->2496ms), -9.9% at 16 threads (391.6->352.7ms). End-to-end q2 render ~-24% (4720->3540ms) — render parses each file twice (Pass1 profile + Pass2 render) so the per-parse cost is paid 2x. Profile: regex-compile self-time 14.27%->0.02%, total CPU samples -17%.

Bonus finding: parse path parallelizes 7.1x on 16 threads with zero lock contention — confirms bd-3gj56 (parallelize Pass 2) is unblocked post-#247. Results in claude-notes/plans/2026-06-01-render-perf-profiling.md.
close_reason: Hoisted whitespace_re to module static; regression test + perf-harness driver added; ~24% end-to-end render speedup, regex-compile self-time 14.3%->0.02%. Full cargo xtask verify green.

title: Nested tight lists incorrectly marked as loose (Para instead of Plain)
description: In process_list() at crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:183-192, multi-block list items with at least one paragraph are unconditionally marked as loose. This is wrong: a list item containing [Paragraph, BulletList] (e.g., '* foo\n  * bar') has no blank line between blocks and should remain tight. The CommonMark spec says a list is loose only when items are separated by blank lines or contain two block elements WITH A BLANK LINE between them.
close_reason: Fixed: detect blank lines via tree-sitter block_continuation spans in process_list_item, propagate through IntermediateListItem

title: User filters default to pre-quarto, so they see CodeBlock where Quarto 1 gave them RawBlock
description:
QUESTION. A bare `filters: [x]` runs the filter at `pre-quarto`, so it sees a
mermaid diagram as a `CodeBlock` with class `mermaid`. Quarto 1 runs user
filters after its own diagram handling, so a Q1 filter sees a `RawBlock` of
HTML. Is `pre-quarto` the right default for ported extensions, and is the
alternative discoverable enough that an author finds it without a bisect?

NOT A PORT BLOCKER — verified by running it, not inferred. q2 already runs user
filters at TWO positions (`UserFiltersStage::pre()` / `::post()`, either side of
`AstTransformsStage`, where `MermaidRenderTransform` lives at
`TransformPhase::Finalization`), and `filter_resolve.rs` exposes a per-filter
`at:` field over eight entry points plus a `quarto` sentinel. Probing on q2 main
@ 808215fc with a filter that logs what it sees, against a plain ```mermaid
fence:

  filters: [probe.lua]                            -> CodeBlock [mermaid]
  filters: [quarto, probe.lua]                    -> RawBlock <pre class="mermaid">
  filters: [{path: probe.lua, at: post-quarto}]   -> RawBlock <pre class="mermaid">

So the Q1-equivalent view is reachable today with a one-line metadata change and
no code change. What is left is a defaulting and discoverability question, not a
capability gap.

WHAT TO DECIDE.
  1. Should a bare `filters:` entry default to `pre-quarto` (today) or to a
     post position? Changing the default would flip behavior for every existing
     filter that reacts to Quarto-generated structure, so this is not obviously
     a win — but the current default is the one that surprises people porting
     from Q1.
  2. If the default stays, how does an author DISCOVER `at:`? Today
     docs/guides/authoring/lua-filters.qmd documents neither the two positions
     nor the `at:` field nor the `quarto` sentinel. That gap is arguably the
     real defect here: the mechanism exists and works, and nothing tells you.
  3. Is there a diagnostic worth emitting? A filter that matches `RawBlock`
     with `class="mermaid"` and never fires is the exact shape of the
     mermaid-zoom port failure. Probably too specific to detect in general, but
     worth a thought.

CAVEAT for whoever picks this up: the class is `mermaid` only for the plain
```mermaid fence. Q1's ```{mermaid} executable-cell spelling stays a CodeBlock
with the literal class `{mermaid}` and renders no diagram at all — that is a
DELIBERATE, documented syntax decision
(claude-notes/plans/2026-07-20-mermaid-regular-rendering.md, section "Syntax
decision", guarded by a brace_form_mermaid_cell_untouched test), NOT a bug. A
ported extension must switch to the plain fence regardless of filter position.

DISCOVERED during the investigation of
bd-lua-filter-table-form-ignored-ph23becz (PR #508), where the same
extension - posit-dev/mermaid-zoom - was blocked on BOTH issues at once: the
returned-table form (now fixed) and this ordering difference. The strand that
was originally filed conflated them; they are independent.

See claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-lua-filter-returned-table-form.md, section
"Adjacent findings", for the probe transcript. Downstream consumer in the
connect-docs skein: br-vuf8asgk (verify mermaid-zoom once the filter fix ships)
and br-w296osbx (the port itself).

title: Metadata materialization drops source_info provenance
description:
MergedConfig::materialize() in quarto-config/src/materialize.rs loses source provenance that pampa's YAML parser correctly provides:
- Map container source_info replaced with heuristic/default (lines ~121-161)
- Map entry key_source always set to SourceInfo::default() (line ~132)
- Array container source_info uses only last item (lines ~109-113)

Scalar values are preserved correctly. Affects error reporting for any metadata-related diagnostics after the merge stage. The code has an explicit comment acknowledging the key_source loss: 'We lose key source info during materialization.'

Pre-existing since commit 955bc326 (2025-12-07, 'config merging in'). Not blocking Plan 0 but degrades the YAML frontmatter Concat piece in the QMD writer's SourceInfo output.
close_reason:
Fixed in d47b3799. materialize_cursor now preserves real container spans and key_source via two new MergedCursor accessors (container_source, key_source), both following the highest-priority layer -- the same one as_value/as_scalar pick for the winning value. unwrap_or_default() fallbacks replaced with SourceInfo::generated(By::unknown()).

Side effect: L5's categories_source anchor for Q-12-12 was inert (sentinel) and is now real -- confirmed empirically against a stashed tree.

Scope note for the record: the Array arm clones items verbatim rather than recursing through the cursor, so containers nested inside arrays always kept correct spans. Only map-valued keys went through the synthesizing arm.

Zero snapshot changes despite predicting tree-wide churn: no snapshot ever captured a materialized container span. Workspace 10877 passed; full cargo xtask verify clean.

Follow-up filed: bd-cwk7l4dl (xtask lint for unwrap_or_default on SourceInfo).

The CORRECT, durable fix is to upgrade @playwright/test from ^1.50.0 (locked 1.58.0) to >=1.60.0, which contains the upstream fix (microsoft/playwright#40747, issue #40724) and is compatible with Node 24.16+/26.

- Remove the 'node-version: 24.15.0' pin in .github/workflows/hub-client-e2e.yml (restore to '24' and delete the explanatory comment).
- Chromium goes 145 -> 148 (1.59=147), so the pixel-comparison VISUAL-REGRESSION baselines will shift. Regenerate them via the workflow_dispatch 'recreate-all-snapshots' path (baselines must be generated on the Linux runner, not locally) and review the snapshot diffs per the CLAUDE.md snapshot-review rules.
- Verify a full green e2e run (functional + visual) before merge.

title: Listing config: parse_sort scalar arm should accept PandocInlines via as_plain_text
description:
Q2's listing parse_sort (crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/config.rs:692) has inconsistent handling between its scalar and array arms:

- Scalar arm matches only ConfigValueKind::Scalar(Yaml::String(s)) — fails on PandocInlines.
- Array arm uses .as_plain_text() — handles PandocInlines fine.

Repro: in a listing block, write 'sort: code' (unquoted). Q2 metadata parsing turns it into PandocInlines('code'), parse_sort falls through to the _ arm, and emits Q-12-3 'sort: must be a string, array of strings, or false'. Workaround: 'sort: [code]' uses the array path and works.

Fix: change line 695 from 'ConfigValueKind::Scalar(Yaml::String(s)) => vec![parse_one_sort_key(s)]' to use 'value.as_plain_text()' like the array branch.

Discovered while authoring docs/errors/index.qmd as part of bd-nvlxn (error-docs foundation, parent bd-94x8a). The workaround in that file should be removed once this is fixed.

Related: sort-ui only accepts boolean in Q2 (line 452); Q1's 'list of allowed sort fields' form is not implemented. That's a separate feature gap, not this bug.
close_reason: Fixed in 00be9952: parse_sort routes string-shaped values (incl. PandocInlines) through as_plain_text, mirroring parse_contents; regression test sort_pandoc_inlines_scalar_parses; docs/errors/index.qmd workaround removed. (sort-ui list-form remains a separate feature gap, noted in the strand body.)

title: Investigate CSL manifest test failure after rebase
description: quarto-citeproc::csl_conformance::csl_validate_manifest fails. Was previously resolved as stale artifact but reappeared after rebasing windows-and-improvement on main. May be a lockfile mismatch that needs regeneration or a genuine regression from main.
close_reason: Root cause was not a build.rs rerun-if-changed defect (empirically disproved: add/remove detection works correctly on cargo 1.97-nightly). Fixed by moving csl_validate_manifest from a build-time-baked generated test to a hand-written runtime test that reads test-data/csl-suite/ + enabled_tests.txt live at test-run time, eliminating the time-of-check/time-of-use gap structurally. Verified behavior-preserving and coverage-increasing by independent agent review.

c-etuqhjgz.author: cderv
c-etuqhjgz.text: Reproduced on Windows: csl_validate_manifest lockfile mismatch is not real content drift. build.rs bakes an 'expected' enabled-test list from test-data/csl-suite/ + tests/enabled_tests.txt at build-script run time; the test compares that baked value against the live tests/csl_conformance.lock file at test-run time. git status showed enabled_tests.txt and test-data/csl-suite clean, and UPDATE_CSL_LOCKFILE=1 regenerated a byte-identical lockfile (cmp confirmed, both LF) - so there is no genuine data divergence. cargo clean -p quarto-citeproc followed by a fresh build made the test pass immediately with no lockfile change needed. Root cause: build.rs's cargo:rerun-if-changed=test-data/csl-suite watches a directory, and cargo's directory-mtime dependency tracking is known to be unreliable on Windows (NTFS mtime semantics differ from Linux ext4), so an incremental build can serve a stale generated_csl_tests.rs baked from an older listing. This likely explains why CI (Linux) doesn't see it but a Windows incremental build does.

c-iqyb300h.author: cderv
c-iqyb300h.text:
Correction to my earlier comment: the NTFS-vs-ext4 framing was wrong. Checked cargo version in use here (1.97.0-nightly, well past Cargo 1.50 where rust-lang/cargo#8973 landed) and empirically reproduced: manually adding then removing a fixture file under test-data/csl-suite/ (no cargo clean, no UPDATE_CSL_LOCKFILE) both correctly triggered a build.rs rerun and were detected. So directory-level rerun-if-changed does recurse and catch add/remove reliably on this toolchain - the 'shallow directory-mtime-only scan' theory from #2599 is stale for our cargo version, not the actual cause.

Bigger finding: the baked 'expected' string only ever depended on file names/counts, never file content - so an in-place edit could never have caused this mismatch either. Whatever caused the one observed failure was likely a Cargo mtime-comparison timing edge case around a git rebase (consistent with Cargo's own open issues on mtime-granularity fragility, e.g. #13119), not a fixable defect in our rerun-if-changed lines.

Real fix applied: stopped baking the validation state at build time entirely. csl_validate_manifest is now a hand-written runtime test in tests/integration/csl_conformance.rs that reads test-data/csl-suite/ and tests/enabled_tests.txt live at test-run time (via env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR), a compile-time constant path, not a baked computed value) and compares against tests/csl_conformance.lock in the same instant. No time-of-check/time-of-use gap, no dependency on build-script rerun timing for this specific check. build.rs now only handles per-fixture test codegen (unaffected). Duplicate/nonexistent-entry detection moved from a soft cargo:warning to a hard test failure (net improvement - warnings get missed). UPDATE_CSL_LOCKFILE=1 auto-update escape hatch preserved byte-for-byte (scripts/csl-test-helper.py depends on it in 3 places). TDD: added manifest_logic_tests unit tests for the extracted pure logic (red before implementation, green after); the original staleness bug itself isn't regression-testable since we can't force Cargo's build-script rerun timing deterministically - that's fixed architecturally, not by a reproducing test. Full crate suite green (863 passed, 0 failed). Decided not to pursue the per-file rerun-if-changed hardening idea from claude-notes/plans/2026-07-07-csl-lockfile-windows-rerun-if-changed.md for quarto-citeproc/quarto-sass - no reproducible defect was found for that angle, so adding unproven defensive code wasn't justified.

c-jzabs21l.author: cderv
c-jzabs21l.text: Independent verification pass (separate agent, diffed old build.rs-generated logic against new hand-written logic line-by-line): confirmed behavior-preserving. All checks retained byte-for-byte (duplicate/nonexistent detection, panic messages, lockfile format, UPDATE_CSL_LOCKFILE auto-update both branches, Count-changed diagnostic), per-fixture test codegen untouched, coverage strictly increased (4 new unit tests on the extracted pure logic that had no unit coverage before). One real delta found (scan_fixture_dir panicking vs old code's silent-skip on an unreadable dir entry) - fixed to match old behavior exactly. Only thing genuinely dropped: a redundant cargo:warning at compile time for dup/nonexistent entries; the actual enforcement (hard test failure) is retained and was already the enforcing mechanism. title: Heading ids do not reflect shortcode expansion (Q1 divergence)
description:
q2 derives a heading's auto id in the reader's postprocess pass (`crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:943`), which runs *before* shortcodes are expanded. An `Inline::Shortcode` in a heading therefore contributes nothing to the id:

    ## before {{< meta foo >}} after   ->   before-after

Quarto 1 expands shortcodes in a pre-Pandoc text pass, so its id reflects the *expanded* text.

Decided deliberately on 2026-08-13 while fixing bd-heading-id-drops-inline-content-fl84n3ql: `collect_text`'s match was made exhaustive, and `Shortcode` was given an explicit skip arm with a comment pointing here. Keeping the current behaviour was a no-regression choice, not an endorsement.

Matching Q1 means deriving heading ids *after* shortcode expansion, which moves id generation out of the reader entirely -- a much larger change that also has to keep the qmd writer's round-trip check (`crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:649`) in sync, since that recomputes `auto_generated_id` on already-parsed content.

Filed as p4 because nobody has asked for it. The plausible request is someone wanting an id to follow `{{< meta foo >}}`. Design it then, not now.

Regression test pinning the current behaviour: `test_auto_id_excludes_shortcode` in crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_heading_auto_id.rs.

Any per-document diagnostic anchored to an extension-contributed value carries an unregistered FileId, so its ariadne snippet silently drops (safe degradation, not misleading — unlike bd-m6wmztln). title: xtask stage-doc-examples stages into the main repo when run from a worktree
description: `repo_root()` (crates/xtask/src/create_worktree.rs:536) resolves via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, which from a worktree returns the MAIN repo's .git directory. That is correct for create-worktree (worktrees live under the main repo) but wrong for stage-doc-examples, which then writes docs/examples/ into the main checkout instead of the worktree it was invoked from. Symptom: running 'cargo xtask stage-doc-examples' in a worktree, then 'q2 render docs/' there, fails with "Declared resource '<worktree>/docs/examples' does not exist on disk" because docs/_quarto.yml declares 'resources: [examples]' and the staged dir landed elsewhere. Fix: give stage-doc-examples a worktree-aware root (git rev-parse --show-toplevel) rather than the common git dir. Found while verifying bd-mt7a6uc4 Phase 6.

c-1d5df9ut.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-1d5df9ut.text:
Hit again on 2026-08-24 from .worktrees/workspace-5 while verifying a docs render (plan claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-listing-inline-contents.md). This is now the fourth independent filing of this bug — see also bd-afi4avsf, bd-u7kdy6fy, bd-rbhfv5xx (all closed as duplicates of this one) — which is itself a signal of how often it costs someone a confusing detour.

Mechanism: `repo_root()` resolves via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, which always points at the main checkout rather than the invoking worktree, so `docs/examples/` gets staged in the main repo while the worktree's stays empty. Because `docs/_quarto.yml` declares `resources: - examples`, the follow-up `q2 render docs/` in the worktree then renders against missing resources.

Workaround used: copy the generated (gitignored) tree into the worktree. Likely fix: use `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` for output paths so staging lands in the invoking worktree.

c-vjbagxjk.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-vjbagxjk.text:
Fifth independent hit, 2026-08-25, from .worktrees/workspace-3 while planning bd-sidebar-title-with-navbar-82wxow6m (whose verification renders docs/ twice: a pre-fix baseline and a post-fix comparison). Same mechanism, same workaround — copied the staged tree from the main checkout by hand.

Two details from this encounter worth adding:

1. The failure is now load-bearing in a plan's verification steps, not just an ad-hoc render. Any plan that measures docs output before and after a change hits this twice.

2. `switch_task.rs:39-48` already carries a comment explaining precisely why `create_worktree::repo_root()` is wrong for per-worktree paths, and deliberately uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` instead. So the fix and its rationale are already written down in this repo, one file away from the bug. That makes this cheaper to fix than five filings suggest.

Also noting the plan for bd-sidebar-title-with-navbar-82wxow6m now documents the prerequisite inline, so the next person planning a docs-render verification in a worktree at least won't lose the time.

title: Decide: silent theme-compile fallback vs hard error (compile_theme_css.rs:547)
description: compile_theme_css.rs:547-555 silently falls back to the ~7.3KB base styles.css when theme SCSS compilation fails, emitting only a Warn trace event. This masked bd-3fgnmlco (CRLF layer-marker bug) for a long time: a hard compile failure rendered as a plausible-looking default document instead of an error. Cross-platform robustness question, NOT Windows-specific - once the CRLF bug is fixed the fallback stops firing on Windows regardless, so this is deliberately scoped OUT of the bd-3fgnmlco fix PR to keep it focused and avoid surfacing other currently-masked compile failures on all platforms. Decide: keep silent fallback (always produce output, hides real errors), make it a hard error (surfaces failures, may break currently-degraded renders), or a middle path (hard error under a strict/test flag, warn otherwise). If the decision is to change behavior, that ships as its own PR after auditing what else the fallback currently masks.

title: render-component loader: resolveComponentPath strips leading slash but fileContents keys it (unresolvable under /cscheid/ subtree)
description: In hub-client ReactRenderer, customComponentsCode does fileContents.get(resolveComponentPath(path, currentFilePath)). resolveComponentPath's normalize() always strips the leading slash, yielding e.g. 'cscheid/mermaid/mermaid.tsx'. But in the Demo Playground project, fileContents is keyed WITH a leading slash for the /cscheid,/charlie,/elliot,/winston subtrees ('/cscheid/mermaid/mermaid.tsx'), while root files and the gordon/ subtree are keyed WITHOUT. So a render-component under a slash-keyed dir never resolves ('Component file not found'). Confirmed live via React fiber on quarto-hub.com 2026-07-17. Secondary: customComponentsCode useMemo deps are [componentPathsKey, currentFilePath], NOT fileContents, so a first-render miss (e.g. content not yet synced) is memoized and never retried. Fix options: (a) make resolveComponentPath/lookup tolerant of both slash conventions (try both keys), and/or (b) normalize fileContents keys. See claude-notes/plans/2026-07-17-mermaid-render-component.md.

Triage (claude-notes/issue-reports/233/triage.md, branch issue-233) could NOT reproduce the reported asymmetry at HEAD: the sibling-failure banner shows consistently on every page of the project (existing pages on switch/edit, and new files), in both hub-client and q2 preview — this is bd-rqba by design. Two real presentation bugs remain: (1) hub-client renders the banner via the shared PreviewErrorOverlay, which is error-only — red 'Render Error' chrome for a warning-class condition (the active page rendered fine); the q2-preview SPA's PreviewDiagnosticsOverlay already has a --warning variant and shows 'Render Warning' for the same state. Give the shared overlay a severity prop (or reuse the SPA's variant mechanics) and have hub-client pass warning severity when the render succeeded and only pass1Failures are present (hub-client/src/components/render/Preview.tsx setCurrentError call). title: AttrSourceInfo: duplicate-key handling breaks positional alignment with Attr.2
description:
When the qmd parser sees an attribute list with a duplicate key like {foo=1 foo=2}, the construction loop in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/commonmark_attribute.rs:41-49 calls:

- attr.2.insert(key, value) -- LinkedHashMap::insert on a duplicate key UPDATES the existing entry in place without growing the map.
- attr_source.attributes.push(...) -- always appends.

After processing {foo=1 foo=2}, attr.2.len() == 1 but attr_source.attributes.len() == 2. The positional alignment AttrSourceInfo.attributes[i] = (key_src, val_src) for the i-th entry in Attr.2 is broken.

**Discovered while reviewing Plan 6's theorem.rs::extract_name_attr fix** (claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md §Scope theorem bullet), which indexes attr_source.attributes by the position of name in attr.2. Plan 6 mitigates with a runtime length-check guard and falls back to SourceInfo::default() when alignment is broken — but the underlying bug pre-dates Plan 6 and affects any future caller that relies on the invariant.

**Fix options:**
1. On duplicate keys, also overwrite attr_source.attributes[existing_idx] instead of pushing a new entry. Preserves alignment; loses the first key's source location (consistent with LinkedHashMap's value-overwrite behavior).
2. Reject duplicate keys at parse time with a diagnostic. More invasive; changes user-facing behavior.
3. Change attr.2 to allow duplicate keys (Vec<(String, String)>). Largest change; affects every consumer of Attr.

Option 1 is the minimum-blast-radius fix; Plan 6's guard handles the symptom either way.

**Plan refs:**
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md §Scope theorem bullet (positional-alignment safeguards)
- crates/quarto-pandoc-types/src/attr.rs:27-32 (AttrSourceInfo definition)

title: refactor canonicalize_within_project to take Option<&SourceInfo>
description: Plan 7f Phase 6.5 follow-up. Today's signature requires a SourceInfo, forcing Engine/Lua-filter resource-entry resolution (crates/quarto-core/src/project_resources.rs:541) to pass a sentinel `By::unknown()` value because those entries genuinely have no YAML source location. The receiver only uses the source location for diagnostic-span rendering, which already degrades gracefully. Refactoring the signature to `Option<&SourceInfo>` removes the sentinel from the call site and lets the receiver decide explicitly how to handle `None` for span-less diagnostics.

title: CI: assert released linux binaries run with no glibc (Alpine smoke test)
description:
The release runbook (claude-notes/instructions/release-runbook.md, step 6) says
the first release after the musl switch (bd-dofxhzaj) deserves a manual check
that the published linux artifact runs on a distro with no glibc:

    docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/w" -w /w alpine:latest /w/q2 --version

This is awkward to do by hand: it needs Docker (not installed on the
maintainer's machine), and on Apple Silicon it would only ever exercise
linux_arm64 — the amd64 artifact goes unchecked. So in practice the check gets
skipped, which is exactly the scenario the runbook was guarding against.

Move it into CI instead. The release workflow already has a per-target verify
gate after each build leg; a no-glibc assertion belongs there (or in a small
post-release job that downloads the published artifacts).

Sketch:
- For the two musl legs (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, aarch64-unknown-linux-musl),
  run the freshly built binary inside `alpine:latest` and assert `--version`
  prints the expected string.
- The x86_64 leg runs on ubuntu-latest and the arm64 leg on ubuntu-24.04-arm,
  so each can run its own arch's container natively — no qemu needed.
- Optionally also assert staticness, but note the runbook gotcha: `file` says
  "static-pie linked" on x86_64 and plain "statically linked" on aarch64, and
  `ldd` exits non-zero on both. Any check must accept both spellings.

Once this is in CI, delete the manual step from the runbook's step 6 (it
currently describes itself as a one-time check on the switch).

Discovered while cutting the v0.11.0 release — the first release after the musl
switch, i.e. the one the manual check was written for.

c-54md7nww.author: Carlos Scheidegger

Each leg runs its own arch's container natively, so both linux_amd64 and linux_arm64 are covered. Docker invocation reused verbatim from the bd-dofxhzaj spike, which was green on both runner images. Removed the manual runbook step 6 paragraph in favor of the CI gate. The container itself could not be run locally (no Docker on this machine) — agreed with Carlos to land on inherited spike evidence rather than a throwaway spike workflow, since the step fails before anything is published. title: Draft alert banner missing in q2 preview (preview-renderer has no draft-alert slot)
description:
Split out of bd-draft-banner-missing-hgx1gkqm, which ships the #quarto-draft-alert banner for 'q2 render'. VERIFIED MISSING in 'q2 preview' -- which is arguably where it matters most, since Q1's banner exists to tell an author previewing a site that the page is unpublished. Verified end-to-end, not inferred: with the parent's work built through the full WASM chain (npm run build:wasm -> cargo xtask build-q2-preview-spa -> cargo build --bin q2), 'q2 preview drafty.qmd' on claude-notes/plans/draft-alert-banner-investigation/repro/ renders the iframe with hasBanner=false. The 'q2 render' output of the same file has the banner. WHY the earlier trace was wrong (recorded so nobody repeats it): the preview DOES call the same quarto-core render_qmd_to_html, and DOES reach ApplyTemplateStage's no-custom-template arm, and is_minimal_html IS false -- but the preview never uses the resulting HTML page. It is a React SPA that mounts into
and RECONSTRUCTS the chrome from meta, slot by slot, in ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/{PreviewDocument.tsx,chromeSlots.tsx}. Those files mirror FULL_HTML_TEMPLATE explicitly (their comments cite template.rs line numbers) with NavbarSlot / SidebarSlot / TocSlot / PageNavSlot / FooterSlot. Adding a template slot in template.rs therefore reaches 'q2 render' ONLY. This is the preview-pipeline shape contract in claude-notes/designs/transform-pipeline-phases.md. Note the DOES appear in preview already: HeaderIncludesEffect (PreviewDocument.tsx:~187,269) applies meta.rendered.includes.header imperatively to document.head. So only the body-level banner is missing. The fix looks small (~20 lines): the transform already publishes the localized label at meta.rendered.draft-alert-text, so preview needs a DraftAlertSlot rendered immediately BEFORE NavbarSlot (PreviewDocument.tsx:271), matching the template where the banner precedes the navbar slot. Emit the identical markup:
{text}
. Bootstrap's .alert-warning and the #quarto-draft-alert rule both already reach the preview's CSS (same theme bundle), so no SCSS work -- but CONFIRM that, since the preview's stylesheet set is not identical to render's. Tests: q2-preview-spa/e2e/chrome.spec.ts is the existing home for preview chrome assertions; a smoke-all fixture will NOT catch this (the WASM smoke runner asserts on render output, not the SPA's reconstructed DOM). The /preview-parity skill covers this class of bug.
close_reason: Fixed in 42d91ad9 on braid/bd-kltzdhle-hub-client-make-q2: DraftAlertSlot in PreviewDocument, before the site header; verified in q2 preview and in the smoke-all e2e fixtures.

title: customRegistry accumulator bug in ast-renderer-entry.tsx loses earlier-loaded user TSX exports
description: In hub-client/src/ast-renderer-entry.tsx:72, the loadCustomComponents loop does: customRegistry = { ...componentRegistry, ...module } — overwriting customRegistry with the static componentRegistry plus only the current module's exports. Each iteration loses earlier modules' contributions. Should be: customRegistry = { ...customRegistry, ...module }. Affects multi-file render-components configurations where users split overrides across simple.tsx + html.tsx + comment.tsx etc. — only the last-loaded file's exports survive. The render_components.qmd docs describe the intended behavior correctly. q2-preview's entry (Plan 2A) will mirror the pattern but fix this bug; this issue tracks back-porting the fix to q2-debug.
close_reason: Fixed in 1e5a930f on branch bugfix/react-components-not-loading (q2-debug back-port of the customRegistry accumulator fix)

title: Writers emit input line-ending convention (round-trip the byte stream)
description: The largest gap in the preserve policy: no pampa writer chooses output EOL from the input convention. Every structural newline is a hardcoded line feed (writeln!) in writers/html.rs, writers/qmd.rs, writers/native.rs, etc. So even after the reader/AST byte-faithfulness fixes preserve content carriage returns, the qmd writer still emits LF-only structural newlines and does not round-trip CRLF input. Design questions to settle in this strand: (a) how does a writer detect 'the input convention' — per-document detection of the dominant ending? (b) mixed line endings within one document — last-wins, dominant, or preserve-each? (c) a document with no trailing newline; (d) an explicit override akin to Pandoc's --eol crlf|lf|native, applied at the output boundary so writer code stays convention-agnostic rather than threading EOL through every writeln!. doctemplate already implements preserve (PR #329) and is the in-tree precedent to mirror. Refs: claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-handling-analysis.md item 4; prior-art.md Pandoc --eol section.
notes: BYTE-EXACTNESS PRECONDITION (verified 2026-06-26). The engine provenance path write_with_source_info -> map_offset (qmd.rs:2742/2769) tiles one linear piece per top-level block; map_offset into a code body is byte-exact ONLY when output bytes equal source bytes. Under CRLF input this holds only if the writer preserves the input convention: if the writer emits LF while source is CRLF, every internal newline in a code body shrinks one byte in output, so map_offset drifts one byte per line. This is a CURRENT bug (not just the shelved per-line-provenance plan) and applies to top-level code cells too. Therefore writer-EOL preservation is a precondition for engine offset-exactness on CRLF. Line COUNT is unaffected (write_soft_break is 1:1); only BYTE exactness is at risk. If the per-line-provenance reimpl is ever revived, its 'code body is byte-verbatim' assumption (plan §2.6) depends on this strand on CRLF docs.

c-dw5loh5j.author: cderv
c-dw5loh5j.text: Live demo (2026-06-26): a uniform-CRLF qmd round-trips to MIXED endings; the qmd writer emits LF for structural newlines while code-body content keeps CRLF. Also absorb writer re-emit of a leading BOM here: BOM is preserve-correct at ingress (counted in offsets, not leaked), so the only open BOM question is whether the writer re-emits it. See research note 2026-06-26-line-ending-gap-characterization.md.

title: Windows: SCSS layer boundary regex rejects CRLF-terminated markers, causing silent fallback to base CSS
description: Root cause of the Windows theme-CSS failures across smoke-all (bd-22rtwdur) AND revealjs_cli (bd-gl0bufxp). On a Windows checkout, resources/scss/**/*.scss are checked out CRLF (git autocrlf default; .gitattributes does not cover *.scss) and embedded verbatim via include_dir. The layer boundary regexes in crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs:49-56 are $-anchored (^/\*-- scss:... --\*/$). Rust's $ matches before the \n but leaves the trailing \r in the line, so CRLF-terminated markers do not match. parse_layer (layer.rs:104) then returns NoBoundaryMarkers, theme/bootstrap/highlight layer loads fail, compile errors, and compile_theme_css.rs:547-555 SILENTLY falls back to the ~7.3KB base styles.css. Net: on Windows no theme variables (--bs-primary), no custom-scss markers, no highlight classes reach output. Proof: parse_layer(raw CRLF)=false and parse_layer(normalized LF)=true; _bootstrap-customize.scss=20 CRLF/0 LF, highlight.scss=196 CRLF. bd-gl0bufxp's error 'SCSS content doesn't contain any layer boundary markers in themes/default.scss' is this exact bug; its open hypotheses (empty content / wrong include_dir lookup) are BOTH disproven. Fix has two parts, deliberately opposite to the preserve-policy epic (SCSS to CSS via grass keeps no byte-offset map, so normalize/tolerate is correct here): (1) make layer.rs boundary regexes CRLF-tolerant (\r?$) - the real feature fix, also covers a Windows user authoring a CRLF custom.scss; (2) pin resources/scss/**/*.scss and the smoke-all tests/smoke-all/**/*.scss fixtures to LF via .gitattributes text eol=lf, mirroring closed bd-mv2ggmr5 - test determinism only. Open design question: should compile_theme_css.rs:547 keep the silent fallback or become a hard error so a compile failure is not masked as a plausible-looking default render.
close_reason: CRLF SCSS layer markers + embedded @import separator fixed on branch braid/bd-22rtwdur-windows-smoke-all-suite (commits for parse_layer CRLF and to_forward_slashes at embedded-resource boundary). Verified on Windows: quarto-sass 221/221.

c-4dunnc0s.author: cderv
c-4dunnc0s.text: Cross-session review (from the bd-gl0bufxp worktree): plan endorsed, converges on all load-bearing points (CRLF layer-regex root cause; feature not test; silent fallback at compile_theme_css.rs:547 explains HTML degrading quietly while revealjs hard-errors; related-not-child of the preserve epic). Four deltas: (1) bd-aamrec3j (include_str! CSS/JS OUTPUT-artifact CRLF, e.g. styles.css written verbatim) is a THIRD independent issue neither PR1 (parse_layer, internal) nor PR2 (path separator) covers -- keep it on the radar as a separate follow-up. (2) Mechanism: \r?$ works but leaves residual \r on the non-marker content lines that get re-joined with \n (mixed endings into grass, harmless but messy); normalizing CRLF->LF once at parse_layer entry is a ~2-line cleaner alternative giving pure-LF into grass -- implementer's call. (3) cat3 href = this strand's sibling bd-5rl408mv (pure separator emission), correctly NOT bd-oejuizi9 (resolution). (4) bd-36vmz7nk as its own post-audit PR endorsed. Worktree coordination: PR1 is a single edit to crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs -- to avoid collision it should be authored ONCE, in the bd-22rtwdur worktree that owns this strand. The bd-gl0bufxp worktree will NOT independently edit layer.rs; bd-gl0bufxp becomes post-PR1 Windows verification of revealjs_cli.

c-zs01r0lk.author: cderv
c-zs01r0lk.text: PR1 code fix implemented + verified on a Windows checkout (worktree bd-22rtwdur). parse_layer normalizes CRLF->LF at entry (single chokepoint; SCSS->CSS keeps no byte-offset map, so normalize is correct here). In-source CRLF unit test test_parse_crlf_terminated_markers added (inline \r\n, runs on Linux CI). TDD: RED = NoBoundaryMarkers{hint:theme.scss}; GREEN after fix. Regression delta on quarto-sass suite (Windows): 128 passed/76 failed -> 175 passed/30 failed; ALL 58 NoBoundaryMarkers failures eliminated (+47 tests). Design decisions: Q1 = normalize-at-entry (confirmed). CORRECTION: the revealjs-session rationale for normalize (residual \r bleeds into grass) is DISPROVEN -- str::lines() strips \r, so both options give identical pure-LF output; the ONLY CRLF failure point is the is_match gate at layer.rs:106. Q2 pin: RE-OPENED -- with the code fix, quarto-sass + smoke-all go green on LF AND CRLF with NO .gitattributes pin (parse_layer is the sole CRLF-fragile scss-content path, verified). Pinning smoke-all fixtures would also erase Windows-autocrlf E2E coverage. Recommending code-only PR1, pin dropped -- pending Chris confirm. NEW FINDING (separate root cause): fixing parse_layer UNMASKS a pre-existing @import "vendor/rfs" resolution failure (30 residual failures) that previously died earlier at parse_layer. vendor/_rfs.scss exists at resources/scss/bootstrap/dist/scss/vendor/; Linux CI green => Windows-specific import-path resolution, likely Cause-B/separator family (matches bd-22rtwdur category-1 hypothesis). Needs its own strand + triage; NOT in PR1 scope. So PR1 alone does NOT fully green smoke-all theme tests on Windows.
