title: q2-preview SPA boot fails: samod findDoc(indexDocId) times out at 5s
description:
**Reproducer:**
1. `cargo build --bin q2`
2. `./target/debug/q2 preview <any-fixture>.qmd`
3. Open the printed URL in a browser.
4. SPA displays "Initializing q2-preview" for ~5 seconds, then PreviewDiagnosticsOverlay shows:
   `Document automerge:<doc-id> is unavailable`
5. Boot state goes to `'error'` so the rendered content never appears.

Reproduces with any fixture (verified with callouts-matrix.qmd and basic-render.qmd, different doc ids each time). Hard refresh + restart of the server do not help.

**Investigation so far:**

- `/health` correctly returns the fresh `index_document_id` matching the one the SPA later tries to subscribe to (verified with curl).
- HTTP-level WS upgrade succeeds (`curl -H "Upgrade: websocket" /ws` returns 101 Switching Protocols with a valid Sec-WebSocket-Accept).
- The 5-second timeout in PreviewApp.tsx:505 (`connect(wsUrl, indexDocId, undefined, undefined, undefined, 5000)`) is firing on every cold load. The comment at lines 500-504 acknowledges this race was already mitigated once.
- onError handler at PreviewApp.tsx:494-497 sets `boot: 'error'`, so the SPA shows the error screen instead of the rendered content.

**Likely layer:** the samod protocol exchange ON TOP of the WS — peer announcement / sync messages aren't flowing within the 5s budget. Stack on this branch:
- Server: Rust `samod = 0.9.0` (quarto-dev/samod q2 branch) in quarto-hub.
- Client: JS `@automerge/automerge-repo@2.5.1` + `@quarto/quarto-sync-client` (workspace package).

**History:** commit 2541f228 ("Fix race condition in automerge sync causing document unavailable errors") fixed an earlier instance by adding `waitForPeer()`. The 5s extra timeout in PreviewApp was the second mitigation. The race is still winning at boot on at least one developer's machine consistently.

**Discovered during:** Phase 6 verification of the callout class-vocabulary fix
(claude-notes/plans/2026-05-22-callout-class-vocabulary-fix.md). Unrelated to
that work — callout HTML render path verifies fine through
`cargo run --bin q2 -- render <fixture>`.

**Possible next steps:**
- Add samod-protocol-level logging on both sides during the first 5s of a fresh q2 preview session to see what messages (if any) traverse the WS after the upgrade.
- Check whether samod 0.9.0 vs automerge-repo 2.5.1 have a protocol-version mismatch.
- Try clearing IndexedDB on the SPA origin — might rule out any client-side storage layer interaction.

title: Fix TOCTOU race in JupyterDaemon::get_or_start_session
description:
**Location:** `crates/quarto-core/src/engine/jupyter/daemon.rs:74-85`

**Race:** `get_or_start_session` reads `self.sessions` under a read lock, drops the lock, then calls `start_kernel(&key).await?` (which takes the write lock at lines 197-199 and inserts). Between the two lock acquisitions, a second concurrent caller for the same `(kernel_name, working_dir)` key can pass the same `contains_key` check and also enter `start_kernel`. The second `start_kernel` overwrites the first's entry in the sessions map, leaking a kernel subprocess (the first kernel's handle is dropped without shutdown).

**Mitigation today:** the render pipeline runs single-threaded (`pollster::block_on`, `?Send` async), so no two callers race in practice.

**When it surfaces:** as soon as parallelism is added — `rayon`-per-worker is foreshadowed in `crates/quarto-core/src/project/orchestrator.rs` docstrings ("a future rayon + pollster-per-worker parallelism path"). Also surfaces under any future async runtime that schedules tasks across threads.

**Fix sketch:** acquire the write lock first, re-check `contains_key` under the write lock, and either return the cached session or insert a placeholder before calling `start_kernel`. The standard \"upgrade and re-check\" pattern, equivalent to `entry().or_insert_with(...)`.

**Discovered:** during the TS engine extensions plan-review session on 2026-04-28. The TS engine work explicitly chose a different concurrency strategy (harness-side idempotency on repeat \`LoadEngine\`/\`LaunchEngine\`) precisely so it wouldn't inherit this pattern. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-plan1a-protocol-and-core.md \"Race-free init via harness idempotency\" and the corresponding section in claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-plan1b-engine-host-deno.md.

**Related:** lines 244-260 and 263-270 in the same file have the same shape but each takes the write lock atomically, so they are not racy. Only `get_or_start_session` at lines 74-85 needs fixing.

title: Parallelize Pass-2 render loop (orchestrator.rs) with rayon
description:
Pass 2 (qmd->HTML render-to-file) is a serial for-loop at crates/quarto-core/src/project/orchestrator.rs:1013, awaiting each page sequentially on the main thread. It is ~98% of full-project render wall time (Pass 1 is already parallel: perf.pass1 docs=565 threads_used=16 wall_ms=19).

Evidence: samply profile of q2 render of claude-notes/qmd-plans — main q2 thread holds 93% of samples, 16 quarto-pass1 workers idle (6.9% combined). See claude-notes/plans/2026-06-01-render-perf-profiling.md.

The locale-lock that previously blocked MT scaling (bd-b7eb7) is FIXED by PR #247 (verified: lock waits dropped 77% -> 0.65% in the profile). Parallelism is now unblocked.

Infrastructure already laid for this: pass2_renderer.rs:73 names 'a future rayon-per-worker parallelism path', the Pass2Renderer trait is ?Send, per-render args are Arc-wrapped. Main obstacle: the &mut self.project_artifacts accumulator (each page drains project-scoped artifacts into it) — needs per-worker accumulators merged at end. Must preserve deterministic output ordering and fail-fast semantics. Land bd-2ercw (regex recompile fix) first.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED (pending full verify + commit). Approach: Pass2Renderer::render_batch trait method, default serial (WASM/tests untouched, no Send bounds); RenderToFileRenderer overrides with rayon fan-out. Refined per-worker -> PER-DOCUMENT artifact stores merged in doc order = exact serial parity for conflict attribution. ProjectPipeline::with_jobs(n) for test-pinned parallelism; worker_count() shared with Pass 1 (QUARTO_JOBS, cap 16). perf.pass2 gauge added.

Results (qmd-plans 565 files, release, median-of-5): end-to-end 3650ms(j=1) -> 500ms(j=16) = 7.3x; Pass-2 itself 3551 -> 446ms (~8x). Byte-equivalence: diff -r of serial vs 16-thread _site IDENTICAL (571 files). Tests: pass_two_preserves_input_order, pass_two_parallel_matches_serial (byte-exact), pass_two_parallel_renders_all_pages; deliberate-break sanity confirmed order guard bites. All 2163 quarto-core tests pass. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-01-parallelize-pass-two.md

title: Reader rejects valid 4-space-indented list-item continuations as a parse error (issue #196)
description:
Regression from PR #194 (closes #184, Q-2-35). The new `INDENTED_CODE_BLOCK_DISALLOWED` external token in `crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c` (line 2128) fires on list-item continuation lines whose preceding blank line carries >= 4 columns of trailing whitespace (4+ spaces or a tab). The result is a generic 'Parse error' (the (state, sym) pair at the recovery point isn't in the Q-2-35 friendly-error table) where the previous behaviour produced an OrderedList AST with two Para children.

Trigger threshold is exactly 4 columns on the blank line. 2 trailing spaces still parses; 4 spaces or 1 tab does not. Independent of list marker kind (ordered, bullet) and continuation content kind (image, plain text).

In the wild: three real-world occurrences in quarto-dev/quarto-web (see triage doc for links).

Triage: .worktrees/issue-196/claude-notes/issue-reports/196/triage.md
Worktree branch: issue-196
Upstream: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/196

Fix should land in the scanner — either reset `s->indentation` on the BLANK_LINE_START path, or tighten the gate to skip list-item continuation contexts. See triage doc § 'Where the fix should land' for angles, and add a tree-sitter corpus regression alongside a positive Q-2-35 case to confirm the original PR's diagnostic still fires on real top-level indented blocks.

title: Hub-Client E2E: smoke-all preview-iframe tests fail (401 + peer-connection timeout) in CI
description:
Surfaced once the Playwright install hang was unblocked (PR #249 / bd-2njja pin). The Hub-Client E2E suite now RUNS to completion for the first time since ~2026-05-27, and reveals pre-existing failures in e2e/smoke-all.spec.ts (NOT caused by the Node pin, which only affects browser install).

Run 26764975242 result: 84 passed, 2 failed, 6 flaky.

Hard failures (fail after 2 retries):
- extensions/builtin-placeholder-shortcode/test.qmd [html]
- q2-preview/multi-element-project/index.qmd [q2-preview]

Flaky (passed on retry): builtin-lipsum-shortcode [html], highlighting/05-theme-none [html], includes/basic [html], metadata/appendix-style-inheritance/doc-override-default [html], q2-preview/body-container-full-layout, q2-preview/body-container-minimal.

Signature: waitForPreviewRender (hub-client/e2e/helpers/previewExtraction.ts:87) throws 'Timed out after 75000ms waiting for preview iframe to render', with console error 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401 (Unauthorized)'. Throughout the run, repeated 'Peer connection failed, creating project in offline mode: Error: Timeout waiting for peer connection'.

Hypothesis: in the CI e2e environment the preview iframe cannot auth/connect to the hub peer/sync (401 + peer-connection timeout), so it never renders within 75s. Likely a hub auth/signaling or globalSetup wiring issue in CI, or a genuine regression on main masked since the install started hanging. Needs investigation with the uploaded Playwright trace/video artifacts (playwright-report artifact on the run).

NOTE: this is the real blocker to a green Hub-Client E2E once the install hang is resolved.
design:
CHOSEN FIX: Tier 2 (deterministic readiness gate) -- keeps the full Automerge sync path end-to-end, just stops the test racing it. Rejected Tier 1 (seed content locally) because it would bypass the very integration smoke-all exists to exercise.

Exact race confirmed by code read: seedProjectInBrowser -> projectStorage.addProject writes IDB ONLY. The seed reaches the SYNCED project set only via reconcileIntoConnectedProjectSet, which the app runs in a useProjectSet effect keyed on the status->connected TRANSITION (useProjectSet.ts:90) and which requires projectSetService.isConnected(). Because the test seeds AFTER bootstrapProjectSet already reached connected, that effect does not re-fire, so the seed lands in the set only if a fortuitous WS reconnect re-triggers reconcile -> flaky, and worker-count-independent (confirmed: workers:1 did not help).

Implemented in PR #249:
- hub-client/src/test-hooks.ts: expose the live projectSetService singleton (projectSet) + reconcileIntoConnectedProjectSet (reconcileProjectSet) on window.__quartoTest.
- hub-client/e2e/helpers/testHooks.ts: matching QuartoTestHooks types.
- hub-client/e2e/helpers/projectFactory.ts seedProjectInBrowser: after addProject, (1) wait up to 30s for projectSet.isConnected(), (2) call reconcileProjectSet() (idempotent) and wait until projectSet.getProject(indexDocId) is defined, before returning. Bounded waits fail loudly if the sync server is truly unreachable.
- workers reverted to 2 (parallelism was never the cause).

FOLLOW-UP (product, separate): the app arguably should reconcile IDB->set on IDB change, not only on the status transition -- so a project added while already-connected appears without a reconnect. Out of scope for the test fix.
notes:
VERIFIED: Tier-2 readiness gate landed in PR #249 -> CI run 26772812401 GREEN (78 passed / 14 flaky / 0 failed functional, 6 visual passed, ~13m, workers:2). The gate eliminated the hard failures (project-set seed/sync race) AND kept parallelism (workers reverted to 2; workers:1 had not helped).

RESIDUAL (keep this bead open): 14 tests still pass-on-retry ('flaky'), up from ~6. Since 0 hard-failed, the gate never threw -- so the residual is in the TEST BODY (75s waitForPreviewRender occasionally needing a retry), most likely the project's FILE doc sync during render (a different doc than the project-SET seed race fixed here). Within the 2-retry budget so the run is green, but worth hardening: extend a similar 'await synced' gate to the project file docs before asserting render, or raise/justify the render wait. Plus the product follow-up: app should reconcile IDB->set on IDB change, not only on the status transition.

title: hub-client: expired session presents as permanent offline (WS 401 retry loop)
description:
When the Google ID token (1h exp) expires and One Tap renewal is unavailable (gsi/status 403), the auth cookie is evicted and every Automerge WS upgrade gets 401. The SPA never notices: WS failures trigger no auth probe (browser hides the 401), and useAuth's visibilitychange handler resets cookieSetAt on refocus without a new cookie, drifting assumed expiry past the real one. UI stays 'logged in' showing 'Connection lost - working offline' with endless retries.

Fixes (this strand): (1) probe /auth/me when sync WS is down — only definitive 401/403 escalates (triggerRefresh, then clear auth on second strike); network errors never clear auth (preserves offline mode). (2) /auth/me returns token exp; client schedules refresh/expiry from real exp; remove drift reset; make refocus/expiry catch branches offline-safe (they currently setAuth(null) on network error). (3) distinct 'Session expired — sign in again' message on LoginScreen instead of generic offline banner.

Out of scope, separate strand: hub-minted sliding sessions to decouple session lifetime from Google's 1h token.
close_reason: Fixed: /auth/me exposes exp; client schedules from real expiry (drift bug removed); WS-disconnect auth probe with two-strike 401 escalation; network errors never clear auth; session-expired login message. Commits 58727d3a + changelog. Full cargo xtask verify green.

title: Plan 3: q2-preview orchestrator emits AST JSON that fails to round-trip through pampa::readers::json::read for lipsum content (MalformedSourceInfoPool)
description:
Surfaced by Plan 3's idempotence gate (`crates/quarto-core/tests/idempotence.rs::lua_shortcode_lipsum_fixed`). Reproduce:

  cargo nextest run -p quarto-core --test idempotence lua_shortcode_lipsum_fixed

The `SingleFile` `DriveMode` passes — the fixture is genuinely idempotent at the pipeline level. The `ProjectOrchestrator` mode panics inside `run_orchestrator`:

  re-parse AST JSON from orchestrator: MalformedSourceInfoPool

i.e. the JSON the orchestrator emitted via `Pass2Payload::AstJson` (writer config `include_inline_locations: true`) is not parseable back by `pampa::readers::json::read`. This is a JSON-writer/reader round-trip bug, not a transform-determinism finding.

**Root cause (confirmed 2026-05-21).** Type-code `3` mismatch between writer and reader in the `sourceInfoPool` wire format:

- Writer (`crates/pampa/src/writers/json.rs:115,180-182`) emits `FilterProvenance` as type code `3` with `d = [filter_path: string, line: number]`.
- Reader (`crates/pampa/src/readers/json.rs:252-283`) still treats code `3` as the long-removed `Transformed` variant and parses `d[0].as_u64()` for a parent_id. On the lipsum fixture `d[0]` is the `filter_path` string → `as_u64()` returns None → `MalformedSourceInfoPool`.

Lipsum trips this because the lipsum Lua shortcode synthesizes inlines whose `SourceInfo` is `SourceInfo::FilterProvenance { filter_path, line }` (via `crates/pampa/src/lua/diagnostics.rs`). Every other Phase 3/4a fixture's content is `Original` / `Substring` / `Concat` (codes 0/1/2), so they round-trip fine. The lipsum fixture is the first one in Plan 3's gate whose pipeline emits a `FilterProvenance` SourceInfo across the AST-JSON boundary.

**Fix-owner: Plan 5 (`claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-5-wire-format.md`).** Plan 5 already covers exactly this bug as part of the wire-format extension for `Generated { by, from }` (Plan 4's typed-provenance variant; the anchor list field is named `from`, holding `SmallVec<[Anchor; 2]>`). Plan 5 retires `FilterProvenance`, adds wire code `4` for `Generated`, and makes the reader's code-`3` branch dispatch on `d[0]`'s JSON type:
- numeric `[parent_id, ...]` → legacy Substring approximation (back-compat),
- string-headed `[filter_path, line]` → `Generated { by: By::filter(...), from: smallvec![] }` (the latent FilterProvenance path).

Per the long-lived-branch policy in Plan 3 §\"Phase 5 — Failure triage\", this issue stays open until Plan 5 lands. Do not fix locally on `feature/provenance`; close as duplicate when Plan 5's PR merges.

This blocks closing `lua_shortcode_lipsum_fixed` in the Plan 3 gate but does not block the other Phase 4 work.

Refs:
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-5-wire-format.md (fix-owner; §Goal calls this bug out by name)
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-3-builtin-filter-idempotence.md (§\"Phase 5 — Failure triage\", §\"CI failure policy & sub-agent prompt template\")
- branch: feature/provenance
close_reason: Fixed in Plan 5 Phase 1 (commit d7b8450a on feature/provenance): the JSON reader's code-3 arm now dispatches on data[0]'s JSON type — numeric-headed legacy Transformed → Substring (back-compat); string-headed [filter_path, line] → Generated { by: filter, from: [] } (recovers the latent FilterProvenance shape). lua_shortcode_lipsum_fixed now passes; full Plan-3 idempotence suite is 27/27 green.

title: Hephaestus (.hep plot document) support: render-time conversion + preview client
description:
Design + implementation umbrella for consuming hephaestus .hep plot documents (posit-dev/hephaestus, cloned at external-sources/hephaestus) in Quarto 2.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-17-hephaestus-hep-integration.md

Recommended shape (see plan for the survey behind it):
- Native q2 render: a Finalization-phase AstTransform (after resource-collector, HTML-family self-gated, excluded from the q2-preview pipeline like mermaid) that reads each Image whose target is a .hep, renders it with hephaestus's renderer-free SVG backend (--no-default-features --features document-read,svg,png; no wgpu, pure Rust), stores an image/svg+xml Page-scoped artifact under figure-html/, and rewrites Image.target. Later: latex -> hephaestus pdf backend, typst -> SVG. PNG is NOT the first target: hephaestus's raster backends need a wgpu adapter (fails headless, non-deterministic); a CPU PNG route would be SVG -> resvg if ever needed.

- Then: brand.yml typography -> document generic families; light/dark via Theme::invert / PlotView.setColorScheme (needs a light/dark image-pair convention Q2 lacks); progressive enhancement of rendered sites (optional).

description: From the Q1 engine-CLI survey (claude-notes/research/2026-07-03-q1-engine-cli-survey.md). Q1 'quarto serve' renders (unless --no-render) then serves a Shiny interactive doc by invoking the ENGINE INSTANCE's optional run() member — src/execute/types.ts:131 'run?: (options: RunOptions) => Promise<void>' with RunOptions {input, render, browser, tempDir, reload?, format?, projectDir?, port?, host?, quiet?, onReady?} (types.ts:231-243). Implemented by exactly TWO engines: knitr (rmd.ts, Shiny R) and jupyter (jupyter/jupyter.ts, Shiny Python) — a genuine multi-engine optional interface member, same family as populateCommand/checkInstallation (Plans 9/10 establish the q2 trait+wire pattern to follow). q2 'serve' is a NotImplemented stub (crates/quarto/src/commands/serve.rs). CHALLENGING: recreating the Shiny server handoff for two languages; marimo is a plausible future third implementer (server-shaped islands runtime). STATUS: research-first — per Gordon 2026-07-03, worth background research but NOT ready to plan. Next step when picked up: study both Q1 run() implementations end-to-end (process lifecycle, port/reload handling, browser open, proxying) before any design.

title: Engine resolver treats doubled-brace display fences ({{python}}) as engine cells, demanding Jupyter
description:
Q2 deliberately rejects Quarto 1's doubled-brace display escape: pampa keeps the class as `{{python}}`, warns Q-2-50, and the fence is documented to render as a literal code block (bd-escaped-executable-fence-uuvv37pk). But `engine_cell_lang` (crates/quarto-core/src/engine/capture_splice.rs) strips one brace layer from `{{python}}` and returns `{python}`, so `resolve_engines` sees a computational language and puts jupyter in the sequence. On a machine without Jupyter the render then fails hard: "Engine 'jupyter' is registered but its runtime is not available".

Found cutting v0.27.0: the release workflow's `web-payloads` job renders `docs/` on a fresh runner (new since bd-hwop1zii) and died on docs/guides/authoring/figures.qmd, which uses the Q1 escape in its display examples. Repro without docs: a single-file doc containing a ```{{python}} fence, rendered where `jupyter` is not on PATH.

Fix: `engine_cell_lang` must return None when the stripped token still contains a brace (i.e. any `{{…}}` class), matching the parser's declared semantics.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #596 (d85a33567 on main): engine_cell_lang rejects doubled-brace classes; docs render no longer needs Jupyter.

title: Link URL corrupted on write-back: a new/edited link in a multi-link paragraph gets an adjacent link's URL
description:
Repro (found via rich-text editor, but the bug is in the shared text-channel write-back, NOT the editor): editing a paragraph that ends up with two links commits correct markdown but persists the wrong URL.

TS commit (verified via console log) sends:
  dest = {t:0, r:[75,208], d:0}
  newText = 'This is an [ordinary](https://example.org/ord) paragraph with **bold text**, *italic text*, some `inline code`, and a [hyperlink](https://quarto.org) to click.'

After commitTextEdit -> parse_qmd_content(newText) -> apply_node_edit -> incremental_write, the file becomes:
  'This is an [ordinary](https://quarto.org) paragraph ... and a [hyperlink](https://quarto.org) ...'

i.e. the NEW link 'ordinary' gets the OTHER link's URL (quarto.org) instead of its own (example.org/ord). The serializer/round-trip is fine (a TS round-trip with two distinct links keeps both URLs). The corruption is in crates/pampa/src/apply_node_edit.rs + incremental writer / reconcile, likely in Link target source-info (targetS / url pool) handling when a paragraph is re-serialized after a link is added/changed. Because the text channel (commitTextEdit) is shared with the monospaced textarea editor, this affects link editing there too — suspected pre-existing. Single-link or no-link paragraph edits are unaffected (round-trips clean in the rich-text suite).
close_reason: Merged as PR quarto-dev/q2#336

c-hw3md4bm.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-hw3md4bm.text: Root-caused + fixed on branch braid/bd-3zp3z4jx-link-url-corrupted-write (off origin/main 19aff019), commit be7a6d20. Root cause: reconciler matched container inlines by type discriminant only, so a new Link matched an old Link regardless of target; the inline splice then copied the old link's ](url) delimiter verbatim. Fix: require non-child identity (Link/Image target+attr, Span attr) to match before recursing; else UseAfter re-serializes via the qmd writer. TDD tests added (failing first). Full workspace nextest: 10337 pass, 0 regressions. NOT pushed yet (awaiting permission).

title: q2 preview: active page outside _quarto.yml render: list shows "Project render produced no output"
description:
In project preview, navigating to (or launching on) a page that is NOT in the project's `render:` list (e.g. a scratch .qmd at the project root) shows the Render Error banner "Project render produced no output for the active page", even though the page is valid.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): RenderMode::ActivePage filters project.files, which discovery builds from the render: globs. A page outside those globs is absent from project.files, so pass_two produces zero outputs; the WASM entry point (wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1633) then hits the catch-all because the active page is not among pass1_failures either. It is NOT sibling-capture-failure poisoning and NOT a poisoned engine host (fail_fast defaults false; proven with a clean no-broken-siblings native repro at the orchestrator level).

Q2 has no single-file escape hatch for an in-project file: crates/quarto/src/commands/preview.rs resolve_project_and_initial_page forces project mode for any file under a _quarto.yml ancestor (single_file: None, pinned by test at preview.rs:575); --no-project is mutually exclusive with a positional path. So without a fix, a render:-excluded in-project page is unreachable in preview.

Q1 (TypeScript quarto-cli) comparison, source-read only: it is mode-dependent. Direct 'quarto preview foo.qmd' renders a render:-excluded file (cmd.ts single-file render() fallback bypasses project.files.input). But navigating to a non-member inside a running project preview REFUSES via previewUnableToRenderResponse() (serve.ts:877) / 404 -- the direct analog of Q2's message. So Q2's current behavior matches Q1's navigation mode; the real defect is (a) the confusing message and (b) no way to preview the page at all.

DESIGN DECISION (open -- no fix landed):
- Option 1: orchestrator injects the ActivePage target into project.files so it renders on-demand in project mode. Prototyped and verified end-to-end (native RED->GREEN test + q2 preview + headless Chromium: sum_sines2.qmd rendered with 5 marimo islands). BUT the render:-excluded page renders with DEGRADED nav chrome: sidebar container present but EMPTY (no links, missing 'nav-sidebar docked' body classes) because the page is not a member of any website.sidebar.contents entry. Looks half-wired.
- Option 2: route the render:-excluded active page through the single-doc renderer (standalone, no project chrome) -- closer to Q1's direct-invocation single-file semantics; sidesteps the empty-sidebar artifact; but does not give project theme/nav and is a larger CLI+WASM change.

STATUS: Option 1 prototype was REVERTED at Gordon's request pending the design decision above. Nothing committed. See conversation 2026-07-24.

c-0b5awo7m.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-0b5awo7m.text: 2026-07-24: Prototyped Option 1 (orchestrator injects ActivePage target into project.files). Reverted the prototype (both orchestrator.rs and the regression test) pending decision between Option 1 (project render, degraded nav) and Option 2 (single-file render for excluded pages, Q1-parity). No code committed.

title: Preview capture-splice mis-pairs cells when a hidden cell is immediately followed by another cell
description:
Found while implementing bd-nn2fou8h (execute-visibility). PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by that work — but bd-nn2fou8h makes it reachable in more documents.

The A1<->B1 walk in crates/quarto-core/src/engine/capture_splice.rs (derive_cell_outputs) pairs each engine cell in A1 with 'the next cell wrapper Div in B1'. Its doc comment states the invariant 'the engine always emits exactly one wrapper Div per executed cell'. That invariant is FALSE for a fully hidden cell, which emits nothing at all:
- knitr has always done this: a chunk with #| include: false produces no wrapper. Verified on main before any bd-nn2fou8h change: a two-cell doc (first #| include: false) renders with exactly one class="cell" div.
- bd-nn2fou8h makes jupyter do the same, and extends it to document-scope execute: include:/echo:+output: combinations.

WHEN IT IS FINE: prose between the cells re-anchors the walk. Traced: A1=[prose, cell(hidden), prose, cell(visible), prose] against B1=[prose, prose, Div.cell, prose] pairs correctly, because the lookahead hits a non-wrapper, takes the conservative break branch, and leaves j in place for the following prose match.

WHEN IT BREAKS: two ADJACENT cells with no prose between, the first fully hidden. A1=[cell(hidden), cell(visible)], B1=[Div.cell(visible)]. The hidden cell's key maps to the VISIBLE cell's wrapper, then the visible cell finds nothing and falls through to raw source. Net effect in q2 preview: the hidden cell displays the next cell's output, and the next cell shows its raw source. Render (non-preview) is unaffected — the splice is preview-only.

FIX DIRECTIONS (not chosen):
1. Make the pairing verify the wrapper belongs to the cell before consuming it (e.g. compare the wrapper's .cell-code content to the A1 cell's code). Has false negatives: an echo:false wrapper carries no code to compare.
2. Carry explicit cell identity through the capture rather than inferring it positionally — the robust fix, but it changes the capture wire shape ({input_qmd, result.markdown}).
3. Give the engines a marker block for hidden cells so B1 keeps one block per cell. Rejected while implementing bd-nn2fou8h: an empty ::: {.cell} paints a real <div class="cell"> box in the output, and knitr's suppression happens inside R where q2 cannot inject a marker anyway.

Repro sketch: a two-cell jupyter doc, first cell '#| include: false', no prose between, opened in q2 preview.

Analysis: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-14-issue-523-execute-visibility.md

c-2wn1ccmb.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-2wn1ccmb.text:
EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED in a live q2 preview session (2026-08-14), replacing the code-trace reasoning in the description. Both halves of the claim reproduce exactly as predicted.

REPRO (jupyter). Single-file 'q2 preview' on:

  Prose before.

  ```{python}
  #| include: false
  hidden = 1
  ```
  ```{python}
  print("SECOND_CELL_OUTPUT")
  ```

  Prose after.

Rendered iframe DOM (read via CDP):
  div.cell count: 1
  pre classes: ['sourceCode python :: print("SECOND_CELL_OUTPUT")',
                'code-with-copy :: SECOND_CELL_OUTPUT',
                '{python} code-with-copy :: print("SECOND_CELL_OUTPUT")']
  visible text: Prose before. / print("SECOND_CELL_OUTPUT") / SECOND_CELL_OUTPUT / print("SECOND_CELL_OUTPUT") / Prose after.

So: the HIDDEN cell's position renders the SECOND cell's spliced output, and the second cell's own position falls through to raw source (note the literal '{python}' class — the un-executed pre-engine form). The second cell's content therefore appears TWICE, and the cell the author asked to hide is the one showing output.

PRE-EXISTENCE PROVEN, not merely argued. The identical fixture with engine: knitr and an R chunk (`#| include: false`, then `cat("SECOND_CELL_OUTPUT\n")`) produces the same DOM: 1 div.cell, ['sourceCode r :: cat(...)', 'code-with-copy :: SECOND_CELL_OUTPUT', '{r} code-with-copy :: cat(...)']. knitr's include:false path is untouched by bd-nn2fou8h — it has always emitted no wrapper — so this is a splice defect that predates the visibility work. bd-nn2fou8h only widens the set of documents that can reach it (jupyter cells, and document-scope execute: options).

METHOD NOTE for whoever picks this up: editing the .qmd while 'q2 preview' is running did NOT trigger a re-capture in single-file mode — the page kept rendering both cells as raw source (the documented no-capture fall-through), which masks the bug. Restarting 'q2 preview' against the final content is what makes the initial capture match the document and exposes the mis-pairing. Budget for that or you will misread a stale-capture render as a fix.

The prose-separated case renders correctly, as traced in the description — the intervening prose re-anchors the two-pointer walk.

title: Investigate compressed compile-time asset embedding (include_compressed_str!) for vendored JS/CSS
description:
Vendored browser assets are embedded uncompressed at compile time via include_str! / include_bytes!, so every q2 binary carries their full uncompressed size whether or not a given render uses them.

Current embedded assets: resources/revealjs/ (~175 KB: reveal.js 117 KB, reveal.css 54 KB, theme, quarto-reveal.css) and, once bd-mermaid-runtime-not-bundled-vxejw159 lands, resources/mermaid/mermaid.min.js at 2,748,992 B (2.62 MiB). That mermaid figure was accepted as the price of an offline-correct render path, but it is ~15x the whole reveal bundle and it is unconditional.

INVESTIGATE. Whether a macro along the lines of include_compressed_str! / include_compressed_bytes! is worth building: store the asset gzip/zstd/brotli-compressed in .rodata and decompress on demand at the point of use (artifact registration), instead of carrying the plaintext. Minified JS compresses well -- expect roughly 3-4x on mermaid.min.js, i.e. ~700-900 KB embedded instead of 2.62 MiB. Measure before committing to a design.

Points to settle:
- Where decompression happens, and whether the cost is paid per render or once (OnceLock/LazyLock cache).
- Whether the decompressed bytes can be handed straight to the artifact store without a second copy.
- Whether an existing crate covers this (there are several include-with-compression macro crates) or a small proc-macro/build.rs in-tree is cleaner.
- WASM: wasm-quarto-hub-client links quarto-core; confirm the decompressor builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown and that the size trade still makes sense there.
- Whether the drift tests (vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package and the mermaid equivalent) still work, since they compare embedded content against node_modules -- they would now need to decompress first.

Not urgent: the accepted position is that 2.62 MiB is acceptable for now. This is an optimization to size the q2 binary sensibly as the vendored-asset set grows.

title: quarto-yaml drops YAML tags on sequences and mappings (!prefer/!concat never reach merge for non-scalars)
description: quarto-yaml 0.1.1 (external crate, posit-dev/quarto-yaml) only captures tags in Event::Scalar; Event::SequenceStart and Event::MappingStart discard their tag parameter (src/parser.rs:441/470 in the 0.1.1 sources). Consequence in q2: '!prefer' / '!concat' written in _quarto.yml on an array or map value parse with merge_op=Concat — MergedConfig implements Prefer correctly (merged.rs as_array), but no YAML-authored tag on a non-scalar ever reaches it. Discovered implementing custom project types: '!prefer' is the sanctioned way for a project to replace an extension-contributed list (include-in-header, render globs), so this blocks that documented pattern. Repro: quarto_yaml::parse_file("k: !prefer\n  - a\n") -> no node carries a tag. Fix belongs upstream (capture tag in SequenceStart/MappingStart + tag span discovery for block collections), then a version bump in q2. Ignored test pinning the desired behavior: crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/custom_project_type.rs user_prefer_replaces_extension_array.
close_reason: Fixed upstream in quarto-yaml 0.1.2 (posit-dev/quarto-yaml#14); q2 bumped to 0.1.2 on branch braid/bd-ad7i1pc6-custom-project-types, pinning test un-ignored and passing, !prefer-on-array verified end-to-end through q2 render.

title: Replay engine: deterministic in-Rust engine for tests
description:
From the bd-o8pr Phase 2 work session: writing E2E tests for engine-emitted resources (and other engine-channel features) requires either real R/Python/jupyter installs or a custom test injection point. Both are heavy.

Idea: build a 'replay engine' that can reproduce the behavior of any existing engine but runs entirely in Rust. Records a real engine's transcript (markdown output, supporting_files, includes, …) into a fixture; replays deterministically without the engine runtime. Useful for:

- CI tests that exercise engine paths without R/Python
- Reproducing flaky engine bugs by capturing the real engine's output once
- Fixture-driven testing of engine-channel features (resources, filters, ExecuteResult fields)
- Especially valuable for Jupyter where custom kernels are common and impossible to test against

Discovered while writing tests for project resources (bd-o8pr). Filed for next session.

References:
- crates/quarto-core/src/engine/registry.rs (where it would register)
- crates/quarto-core/src/engine/{markdown,knitr,jupyter}/* (existing engine impls to model)

title: q2-preview: render tabsets as a React Tabset component
description: Follow-up to bd-toc-tabset-titles-zq93gjvf. The tabset transform pair is excluded from the q2-preview transform pipeline (Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED in crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs) because the resolve half builds its nav from split RawInlines, which the React RawInline component (per-fragment dangerouslySetInnerHTML) cannot render without collapsing. Preview therefore shows the pre-tabset passthrough (stacked headings, tab titles in any preview TOC). Proper fix: keep the parse half in preview so CustomNode(Tabset) reaches the React layer, and add a Tabset component in ts-packages/preview-renderer that renders slots as real tabs (mirroring how Callout custom nodes are preview-rendered). Until then hub q2-preview diverges from q2 render for tabset pages.

title: Block-level HTML tag mid-paragraph does not interrupt the paragraph, so a trailing lands inside
description:
Pre-existing, not a regression: identical on q2 0.28.0, 0.29.0 and current main. Found while fixing bd-block-html-adjacent-markdown-unparsed-0qnjuwuy; PR #646 recorded it as a deliberate known gap ('a block-level tag mid-paragraph does not interrupt the paragraph (pandoc's would)'). The lift only fires when a block-level tag is the *first* inline of a paragraph. A closing tag that follows prose on the previous line with no blank line between is therefore mid-paragraph, stays inline, and is emitted inside the

:

Example Intro text. By applying these rules you get consistent formatting.
renders the last paragraph as

By applying these rules you get consistent formatting.

which is the same invalid-HTML shape PR #646 fixed for the opening tag: is flow content, so a browser force-closes the

and reparents what follows. Quarto 1 and pandoc both close the paragraph before the tag. Fixing this means interrupting a paragraph at a block-level tag, which is a larger change than the opening-tag lift: the paragraph node has already been assembled by the time process_paragraph sees it, so the split would have to run over the inline vector the way the markdown_in_html_blocks split now does — plausibly the same machinery, extended to fire when the tag is not first. Reproduce with the fixture in /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/block-html-adjacent-markdown-unparsed/ by removing the blank line before the closing tag.

title: Attribute key ranges start one byte early for any non-first attribute
description:
In the serialized AttrSourceInfo, the *key* Range for any attribute after the first begins one byte too early — it includes the preceding separator space. Observed via annotated-qmd: key `data-value` resolves to the source text ` data-value` (leading space).

Rust-side, in the key Range that Plan 2's task D1 deliberately left as a raw span (D1 changed only the *value* slot to content provenance). Pre-existing on main, unrelated to value provenance, and it was already failing a test in ts-packages/annotated-qmd before task D3 touched anything.

Found during Plan 2 of the provenance epic (task D3). Out of scope there: D3's constraints forbade touching AttrSourceInfo, and no sibling task's brief mentions the key slot at all — the epic's three plans are all about the value slot's decoded-vs-raw drift.

Fix belongs wherever AttrSourceInfo's key ranges are constructed (pampa's commonmark_attribute / treesitter attribute path). Check whether the off-by-one is in the key's start or in the separator's attribution before changing it.
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-1d6io failure #2 (attr key range absorbs the inter-pair separator). bd-1d6io is the superset: same defect, plus failure #1 (code span, now fixture-only), plus the CI guard, plus the dated bisect. This strand's three durable contributions — the AttrSourceInfo framing, the live code seam (treesitter.rs:1205, not the nonexistent key_value_specifier.rs), and the finding that bd-1d6io's scanner-side fix direction was superseded by Plan 7g Phase 3's P1 tight-range convention — are recorded in comment c-qn11q3g6 on bd-1d6io. Work continues on branch braid/bd-1d6io-annotated-qmd-source-tracking.

title: q2 preview: audit HTML preview CSS for the same render-drift class (codepath + version)
description:
Sibling of bd-ibqkf9ry (reveal preview convergence). That strand fixed reveal: q2 preview drew CSS from a DIFFERENT source than q2 render (npm reveal.js vs vendored resources/revealjs) and leaked the app's HTML-theme/Bootstrap CSS onto the deck. Question for THIS strand: does the same drift class exist for the HTML preview formats (q2-debug / q2-preview)?

Specifically audit: (1) does the HTML preview's CSS come from the SAME code path as render's CompileThemeCssStage (SCSS->CSS theme compilation, bootstrap), or a separate/divergent bundle? The q2-preview iframe injects a <link data-q2-theme> in entry.tsx (document.head) — is that link's CSS byte-identical to what q2 render emits for the same doc/theme, or built differently? (2) Is the bootstrap version/source pinned + shared between render (resources/scss/bootstrap, resources/js/bootstrap) and preview, or can they drift (cf. reveal's reveal.js version pin + vendored<->npm sync test in bd-ibqkf9ry Prong A)? (3) Any DOM/computed-style divergences between HTML preview and render beyond what the existing /preview-render-parity skill already tracks per-node.

If drift exists, apply the same convergence pattern: single CSS source/codepath + a sync/identity check, keeping the React preview path (required for AST<->source mapping). Reference: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-10-preview-reveal-convergence.md (the reveal precedent), and the /preview-render-parity skill. The reveal fix shipped on the same branch as bd-jij5gge2/bd-ibqkf9ry (not yet merged at filing time).

(2) KaTeX had real drift (render CDN @latest vs npm ^0.16.28 vs sandboxed ^0.16.11): pinned 0.16.28 everywhere + sync test (verified failing first). (3) Bootstrap single vendored source confirmed; added JS<->SCSS-README version-pairing test. (4) q2-debug entry + hub editor deck renderer converged to vendored reveal CSS. title: Draft alert banner in revealjs decks (resolve the deferred before-body anchor)
description:
Follow-up to bd-draft-banner-missing-hgx1gkqm, which ships the #quarto-draft-alert banner for HTML output only. Revealjs decks with 'draft: true' still render with no draft indication.

Quarto 1 also excludes slides, but the exclusion is INCIDENTAL, not principled: the 'isHtmlOutput() and not isHtmlSlideOutput()' guard arrives in quarto-cli commit 99e47b461 -- three commits BEFORE the banner exists -- for the feature that EMPTIES draft documents (emptying a deck's blocks would break the presentation, a good reason to guard THAT). The banner lands in 5b06ea3af and inherits the guard for free, because it keys off meta[name=quarto:status], which only the already-guarded filter emits. No stated rationale anywhere in quarto-cli. So consistency argues for supporting decks.

The cost in q2 is real and is why it was split out:

1. Separate template. apply_template.rs routes revealjs to revealjs::render_revealjs_document (crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs:369), a hand-built format! scaffold that bypasses doctemplate entirely. The $if(draft)$ slot added to FULL_HTML_TEMPLATE by the parent strand does nothing here.

2. Separate CSS bundle, without Bootstrap. Reveal gets quarto-revealjs.scss (quarto-sass/src/bundle.rs:369), not _bootstrap-rules.scss. NEITHER '#quarto-draft-alert' NOR Bootstrap's '.alert.alert-warning' exists there. Both need authoring; alert-warning is a themed Bootstrap component, not a one-liner, so it needs a reveal-appropriate design rather than a copy.

3. No natural anchor, already deferred in-tree. assemble.rs:424 documents: 'before-body has no natural anchor in the deck scaffold -- reveal.js owns everything inside .reveal -- and is deferred until a concrete consumer appears.' The draft banner is exactly a before-body-shaped element. Q1 ships NO reference output for this case, so there is nothing to port -- placement over a deck is an original design decision (fixed overlay? inside the first section? a reveal-native affordance instead of a banner?).

This strand IS that concrete consumer: resolving it should settle the before-body anchor question on its own terms.

Depends on the parent landing first (shared: the localized 'draft' term lookup and the draft-detection transform, which should be reusable).

title: Investigate tree-sitter ':' handling in line-break: definition list / fenced div edge cases
description:
Sibling of bd-af1e/bd-wv4e investigation. The line-break handler also excludes ':' as a paragraph interrupter. ':' has more entangled semantics in qmd:
- Definition list term/definition (':' at start of line after a paragraph defines a definition list).
- Fenced div marker (qmd-specific, ':::' or more).
- Plain text otherwise.

Verify whether ':something' (single colon then content) at line start is correctly soft-broken. Initial pampa output appeared to error on the test fixture; needs investigation.

Reference fix pattern: bd-af1e (claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-tree-sitter-backtick-paragraph-split.md).
close_reason: Re-scoped: ':' has backslash-escape workaround (\:foo). Not severe enough to fix in this pass.

title: Port TS Quarto _quarto-rules.scss to Q2 for HTML DOM parity
description:
TS Quarto's src/resources/formats/html/_quarto-rules.scss (774 lines, ~80 top-level selectors) has NO single counterpart layer in Q2. Its rules were ported into Q2 piecemeal (into _bootstrap-rules.scss and title-block.scss) and the port is incomplete. The title-block bottom-margin bug (bd-btjkyylx, PR #406) was one missing slice; this epic brings over the rest to the extent Q2's emitted DOM matches, and adapts the ones that make sense.

Approach (see plan): the FIRST child is an AUDIT task that categorizes every selector as (1) port-now — DOM Q2 already emits, (2) blocked-on-emitter — CSS would be dead until Q2 emits the DOM, or (3) intentionally-dropped. The audit's output becomes the themed port-now child strands (grouped e.g. figures/floats, code-overflow, footnotes, layout panels) plus blocked strands that get 'blocks' deps on their emitter features. Do NOT port CSS for DOM Q2 doesn't emit.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-21-quarto-rules-scss-parity-epic.md

title: Bootstrap JS runtime injection for HTML output
description:
Auto-include Bootstrap 5 JS (bundle, with Popper) for HTML renders that use a Bootstrap-backed theme, mirroring Quarto 1's behavior but via q2's artifact-store pipeline.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-bootstrap-js-injection.md

Scope:
- Vendor bootstrap.bundle.min.js (5.3.1, ~80KB, includes Popper) under resources/js/bootstrap/.
- Add BootstrapJsStage in crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/, run after CompileThemeCssStage.
- Predicate: !is_minimal_html(meta) — same condition that triggers Bootstrap CSS compilation.
- Register js:bootstrap as Project-scoped artifact; ApplyTemplateStage emits the <script> tag automatically, no separate raw-HTML injection step.
- DO NOT add the stage to build_wasm_html_pipeline() — hub-client's iframe-reinit-per-render breaks stateful Bootstrap components. Same skip pattern as EngineExecutionStage.

Out of scope:
- MathJax/math-mode injection (next session; q2 cannot delegate to Pandoc the way Q1 does because the q2 HTML pipeline doesn't invoke Pandoc — see plan doc for notes).
- Any richer JsFeature/registry abstraction. Defer until a third concrete consumer arrives.

TDD per CLAUDE.md: write the predicate-matrix unit tests + end-to-end render-through-CLI tests + WASM-pipeline omission test before implementing.

title: Multi-sidebar project: a sidebar defined only by auto: <dir> is never selected, losing the sidebar entirely
description:
In a project with more than one sidebar, a sidebar whose membership comes only from an 'auto:' entry is never selected for the pages it would contain, so those pages render with no #quarto-sidebar element at all.

Cause is an ordering gap in SidebarGenerateTransform (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/sidebar_generate.rs): sidebar_for_page() is called at :89, but expand_auto() only at :127. Selection therefore runs against unexpanded contents, and contains_source_path (crates/quarto-navigation/src/sidebar.rs:647) explicitly ignores SidebarEntry::Auto(_) at :663.

Single-sidebar projects are unaffected, which is why this went unnoticed: sidebar_for_page Rule 2 (sidebar.rs:637) applies a lone id-less sidebar regardless of containment. With two or more sidebars, Rule 3 containment matching runs and finds nothing.

Confirmed at main @ 152ed8fb with a probe committed at claude-notes/plans/sidebar-contents-dir-shorthand-investigation/multi-sidebar-auto/ (two id-bearing sidebars, one defined as 'auto: how-to'). Rendering it gives sidebar=0 on how-to/index.html, how-to/one.html and how-to/two.html, while other/alpha.html (which names its page directly) gets sidebar=1.

Uses only syntax q2 supports today, so this is independent of the 'contents: <dir>' shorthand bug — but that strand's real-world hit (the Posit Connect docs) cannot be fixed without also fixing this. Candidate fix: hoist expand_auto above sidebar_for_page and expand each candidate sidebar before picking; alternative is to make contains_source_path match Auto specs against the glob directly.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-sidebar-contents-dir-shorthand.md (design question Q2/Q4).

c-c6j4cwhd.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-c6j4cwhd.text:
Fixed on branch braid/bd-sidebar-contents-dir-shorthand-z7arvhx8 (commit 0a3a99fa), together with its parent strand. Not yet pushed.

SidebarGenerateTransform now resolves hrefs and expands auto: for EVERY parsed sidebar before calling sidebar_for_page, then picks. Because the transform runs once per page, each sidebar expands into its own diagnostics sink and only the picked sidebar's diagnostics reach ctx.diagnostics — otherwise every page in the project would carry the Q-13-5/Q-13-6 warnings of sidebars it doesn't use. A regression test fences that leak.

Verified on the committed probe: how-to/index.html, how-to/one.html and how-to/two.html go from sidebar=0 to sidebar=1, and each page gets the correct sidebar rather than merely some sidebar (how-to/one.html carries 'How To'; other/alpha.html still carries 'Other'). Single-sidebar projects are unchanged.

Close when the parent's PR merges.

title: Nested (non-top-level) MetaMap JSON encoding is not valid real-Pandoc JSON
description:
Discovered during P2 Task 7 (emitting meta.quarto_pandoc_reader_opts), unrelated to that task's
own scope — flagged rather than fixed.

crates/pampa/src/writers/json.rs's stream_write_config_value (the ConfigValueKind::Map arm, used
for *nested* metadata maps, i.e. not the top-level document meta which goes through the separate
stream_write_config_value_as_meta) encodes a MetaMap's `c` field as an array-of-entries
(preserving key_source: [{key, key_source, value}, ...]) rather than a plain JSON object. Real
Pandoc/aeson's MetaMap Content is `{"c": {<key>: <MetaValue>, ...}}` — an object, not an array.

Consequence: if a document's *nested* metadata (a map value inside another map/list, not the
top-level front matter) is ever fed through a real external `pandoc` filter or Lua filter that
expects standard Pandoc JSON shape, it will misread nested MetaMap content. Top-level meta is
unaffected (stream_write_config_value_as_meta already emits a plain object there).

This surfaced only because Task 7 needed to trace how MetaMap values round-trip through this
writer for the new quarto_pandoc_reader_opts key (which is top-level, so it doesn't hit this
path) — the bug itself is pre-existing and orthogonal to P2's wire-schema work. Worth revisiting
before any plan that feeds real nested-metadata documents through actual pandoc/Lua (P4/P5 territory,
but not decided here — filed as a standalone strand per this repo's beads-vs-plans policy since it
belongs to no current plan's checklist).

title: Unexecuted braced cell renders with the braces as a CSS class: <pre class="{r}">, unhighlighted and undiagnosed
description:
Found while spiking bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj on q2 HEAD eac0c7acf. REPRO (no engine involved, so this is not an engine bug): unexec.md --- title: unexec --- (a braced r cell containing cat("NEVER-RAN")) 'q2 render unexec.md --to html'. A .md document never executes engines (engine_execution.rs:207), so the braced cell reaches the HTML writer unexecuted. Output: 
cat("NEVER-RAN")
Three things wrong, all silent (exit 0, no warning): 1. The braced language string is emitted verbatim as a CSS class name. Braces are not valid in a class attribute. 2. No syntax highlighting. An executed r cell on the same page gets 
 plus hl-* spans; this gets none.
3. The fence spelling is lost from the reader's view — only the body shows, so the reader cannot tell it was a cell at all. Same failure shape as a top-level doubled-brace {{r}} (see claude-notes/research/2026-09-02-engine-markdown-dataflow.md section 1, row 1).

REACHABILITY: any path that leaves a braced cell unexecuted. Confirmed via .md. Also reachable when the qmd writer destroys a container's nesting and a downstream step declines to execute the freed cell.

NOT a blocker for the masking work: masking scoped to markdown-displaying CodeBlocks never produces this state (verified across seven fixture shapes). It is filed because the render is wrong on its own terms, independently of engines.

title: hub-client: _brand.yml change doesn't recompile preview theme CSS for AST/slides previews (revealjs)
description:
In a live hub-client session, when _brand.yml changes (e.g. arriving via Automerge sync from a collaborator), the preview theme CSS is NOT recompiled for AST-path previews (revealjs/q2-preview/q2-slides) — the user must reload the page. The HTML preview (Preview.tsx) updates correctly.

Root cause: asymmetric React effect deps. Preview.tsx (HTML) re-render effect depends on [content, fileContents, ...] (Phase 9 Decision 6), so any sibling edit (incl. _brand.yml) re-fires it. ReactPreview.tsx (AST/slides path) re-render effect (ReactPreview.tsx:647-657) depends on [content, updatePreview, scrollSyncEnabled, currentFile?.path, onDiagnosticsChange, attributionPayload] — fileContents is MISSING. So sibling _brand.yml edits never re-render the active slides doc.

Everything downstream already works: automergeSync onFileChanged (ts-packages/preview-runtime/src/automergeSync.ts:98) vfsAddFile()s every changed file incl _brand.yml; compile_theme_css cache key includes the brand YAML (compile_theme_css.rs:202-214) so a re-render yields a fresh fingerprint + recompile; renderPageForPreview reads _brand.yml from the fresh VFS.

Fix: add fileContents to ReactPreview's re-render effect dep array (parity with Preview.tsx). Coarse re-render-on-any-sibling-change is the established pattern; fine-grained 'doc depends on _brand.yml' tracking is an optional optimization, not required. Affects all AST-path previews, not just revealjs.

Repro: needs two windows (A views slides.qmd, B edits _brand.yml) — single-window file-switch masks it because changing currentFile re-renders anyway.

Diagnosis doc: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-22-hub-client-brand-live-recompile.md
close_reason: Fixed in f4e2c25e (pushed to main, b639033b): added fileContents to ReactPreview's re-render effect deps so sibling config edits (esp. _brand.yml via sync) re-render the active AST/slides deck and recompile its theme. TDD test red->green; verified live in two windows (brand colour recompiled with no reload); tsc -b + 614 unit + 75 integration + production build green.

title: Table floats render their caption twice (inner <table><caption> + synthesized <figcaption>)
description:
Found by end-to-end render while preparing the bd-hcp8m3ve PR; the 10511-test workspace suite does not catch it. A crossref table float emits the caption text TWICE:
Confirmed that
is the normal non-float table rendering (a bare captioned table with no #tbl- id renders the same inner caption), so the float transform synthesizes the figcaption from the table's caption without clearing the table's own. Q1's shape 1 carries the caption only in the figcaption — design doc says table floats 'replace the current Div+caption-paragraph shape with shape 1 (figure.quarto-float-tbl +
close_reason: MERGED: fixed in 32f06010, shipped with PR #423 (4310c173 on main). Table floats no longer emit their caption twice — the Table's own caption is elided at figcaption-synthesis time in render_float_ref_target, matching Q1's parse-time elision, so both the pampa writer and the React preview renderer get it. TDD (table_float_clears_the_tables_own_caption watched red first); verified e2e on both repro forms.

c-8egiwxw2.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-8egiwxw2.text:
FIX IMPLEMENTED (TDD) on the bd-hcp8m3ve branch, commit b1d72b25, folded into PR #423 per the where-to-fix decision.

RED first: new unit test table_float_clears_the_tables_own_caption in crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/crossref_render.rs, watched failing with 'the table's own caption must be cleared once hoisted into the figcaption, else it renders twice: Some([Paragraph(...Cap...)])'.

Root cause of the test-coverage gap, worth recording: the existing table_target_renders_q1_float_shape supplies the caption as a SIBLING PARAGRAPH (content: vec![table, para("Table caption")]), never as the Table's own caption.long — so the duplicating path had no coverage at all. That is why 10511 passing tests missed it and only an e2e render caught it.

FIX: in render_float_ref_target, inside the html_float_dom && is_float_kind branch, clear caption.long/short on top-level Block::Table entries in the float content. Guarded by !is_uncaptioned — when the float is uncaptioned nothing was hoisted, so the Table's caption is the only copy of that text and must be preserved.

Chose the transform rather than the writers deliberately: the caption is gone from the AST before either writer runs, so the pampa HTML writer AND the React preview renderer (Figure.tsx) both get the fix, with no parity drift between render and preview.

VERIFIED end-to-end through the real binary on BOTH repro forms (': Cap {#tbl-one}' and '::: {#tbl-one}'): 'Cap' now appears exactly once each, inside <figcaption id="tbl-one-caption">; the inner <table><caption> is gone. Workspace 10512/10512 (one more than before = the new test), ZERO snapshot churn, only crossref_render.rs touched. Full cargo xtask verify running before push (quarto-core change -> WASM leg).

Still open and NOT addressed here: the figcaption carries quarto-float-caption-bottom while the inner table carries caption-top. Left alone deliberately — it is a caption-location question, not a duplication one.

c-jqv57yno.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-jqv57yno.text:
CHECKED AGAINST MAIN (2026-07-27) — the duplication is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by PR #423. Built origin/main's q2 (78d55deb, detached worktree, shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR) and rendered the identical minimal fixture: MAIN (78d55deb):
...
Cap
Cap <-- bare trailing text node
PR #423 branch:
Both emit the caption text twice. #423 changes the SHAPE of the second copy (stray trailing text node -> proper figcaption) but does not fix the double emission. So #423 is not a regression on this axis; it is arguably an improvement, since the duplicate is now at least semantic markup. Q1'S SOLUTION CONFIRMED (Carlos's recollection is right — elide the table's own caption when it becomes a float). Two sites in quarto-cli, both in quarto-pre/parsefiguredivs.lua, at float-PARSE time rather than render time: - line 280 (div-wrapped case): walks the div content for a Table with a non-empty caption, hoists it into the float caption, then 'table caption should be removed from the table as we'll handle it' -> table.caption = pandoc.Caption{} - line 544 (caption-attr case, startsWith(attr.identifier, 'tbl-')): 'we've parsed the caption, so we can remove it from the table' -> el.caption.long = pandoc.Blocks({}) RECOMMENDATION ON WHERE TO FIX: on top of PR #423, not against main. The duplication predates #423, but #423 rewrites render_float_ref_target — the exact code a fix must touch — so a fix landed on main would conflict. Cleanest: fold it into #423 or ship it as the immediate follow-up PR after #423 merges. Note Q1 elides at parse time; Q2's float DOM is built in the Finalization-phase transform, so the natural Q2 site is wherever the figcaption is synthesized (clear the Table's own caption at the same moment).

c-jri7zqih.author: Carlos Scheidegger

c-ophsw8e3.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ophsw8e3.text:
MINIMAL REPRO (verified 2026-07-27). Five lines, no front matter, no cross-reference, no div wrapper:

| a |
|---|
| 1 |

: Cap {#tbl-one}

Render with: cargo run --bin q2 -- render tbl.qmd

Output has 'Cap' twice — once in <table class="caption-top table"><caption> inside the aria wrapper, once in <figcaption id="tbl-one-caption" class="quarto-float-caption-bottom quarto-float-caption quarto-float-tbl">.

Controls:
- Remove the {#tbl-one} id -> single <caption>, no float wrapper, no figcaption. So it is the float path, not table rendering in general.
- No @tbl-one reference is needed; being a float target is sufficient.
- The ::: {#tbl-one} div-wrapped form behaves identically, so it is not specific to caption-attr syntax.

NOT yet established: whether main (pre-bd-hcp8m3ve) also duplicates via its older Div+caption-paragraph shape, i.e. whether PR #423 introduces a user-visible regression or merely carries an existing one into the new DOM. Needs a build of main to settle.

title: quarto-hub-mcp 'live:' vitest suites are network-flaky and unconditionally gate cargo xtask verify
description: ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp/src/hub-mcp.test.ts has two 'live:' describe suites (~12 tests, 15s timeouts each) that hit the third-party public sync server wss://sync.automerge.org with no gate: plain 'vitest run' — the ts-packages step of cargo xtask verify — always runs them. Observed 2026-07-14: two of three full verify runs failed with 'Test timed out in 15000ms' on a DIFFERENT subset of live tests each time (9 then 2), while direct vitest reruns minutes later and GitHub Actions CI were green; the changed code (pampa lua) was unrelated. Two problems: (1) an external-network hiccup fails the whole pre-push verify gate; (2) the 'live: create project and mutate files' suite creates an orphan project on the public server on EVERY full test run, from every dev machine and CI job. Proposed: gate live suites behind an opt-in env var (describe.runIf(process.env.HUB_MCP_LIVE_TESTS)), keep them enabled in a dedicated CI job, and consider pointing the mutate suite at a locally spawned hub binary (hub --allow-insecure-auth) instead of sync.automerge.org.

title: Engine-output headings can collide with document heading ids (dedup runs pre-engine)
description: Follow-up scoped out of bd-duplicate-heading-ids-mou5z7ux by design decision (2026-08-18): the document-level heading-id dedup pass runs at the tail of IncludeExpansionStage, but EngineExecutionStage runs later, so a heading emitted by a knitr/jupyter code cell can still duplicate an existing heading id. Q1 does not have this problem because engines run before pandoc parses (ids assigned last). Fixing it in q2 means renumbering after engine execution — in tension with DocumentProfileStage (outline) running pre-engine and wanting final ids. Needs its own design pass: either a second post-engine dedup for engine-inserted headers only, or moving the authoritative pass later and teaching the profile to tolerate it. No known real-world hit yet; filed for bookkeeping.

c-hrdrt8vt.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-hrdrt8vt.text: Design note from parent strand (2026-08-18): the include-stage fix landed on a scoped uniqueIdent mechanism (renameable set = injected headers, seen-set = whole document, ids monotonic once assigned). This strand's intended fix is re-running that same routine post-engine with scope = engine-inserted headers — no renaming of ids DocumentProfileStage already observed, so the profile tension noted in the description dissolves.

title: SPA getBinaryDocById missing automerge: URL prefix → binary capture docs never reach WASM
description: ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/client.ts:getBinaryDocById passes the bare docId from the IndexDocument capture sidecar straight to repo.find(). The samod TS library rejects this with 'Error: Invalid AutomergeUrl: <id>' because it requires the 'automerge:' scheme prefix. The text-doc loader (loadFileDocuments) prepends the prefix explicitly (lines 305-307); getBinaryDocById doesn't. Net effect: every project-mode q2 preview render falls back to the default registry because captureGzJson is undefined, and code cells render as inert source — the exact user-reported bug. Diagnosed end-to-end on 2026-05-18 against the fixture website. Trivial fix: same 'automerge:' prefix-normalize pattern as loadFileDocuments. Critical because it makes the entire Phase C.4 replay path silently inert for real users.
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-b2vk (identical accidental double-create, same deps/description, 7s apart).

title: hub-client: connection indicator shows Offline before Online on open
description: The connection indicator always shows Offline first then flips to Online when opening a document. Root cause: two-state boolean isOnline initialized false; the indicator (in MinimalHeader, mounted post-connect) renders whatever connect() decided, and connect()'s 1ms peer wait almost always resolves offline-first. Fix: (1) widen production peer wait 1ms -> ~400ms so the common case resolves Online at mount with the live doc; (2) hide-until-resolved three-state indicator (connecting/online/offline) so the slow/offline tail never flashes Offline.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #424 (commit 581e45c0). Widened production peer wait 1ms->400ms so the common fast connect mounts Online with the live doc, avoiding the Offline->Online flash. Local branch and worktree cleaned up.

title: ~80 silent-skip sites let engine tests pass vacuously in CI

title: Q2 has no number-sections / @sec- header-numbering implementation for any format
description:
Confirmed by direct code investigation (2026-09-17), while auditing the pandoc-writer-hybrid
epic's crossref-numbering:external mode for docx/pptx.

Q2 appears to have NO implementation of two related, standard Quarto/Pandoc features, for ANY
output format (not just Pandoc targets):

1. `number-sections: true` — visible "1.2 Section Title" numbering injected into headers.
2. `@sec-<id>` crossref resolution — resolving a `@sec-intro` reference to a linked, numbered
   section reference (e.g. "see Section 1.2").

Evidence:
- `grep -rn number-sections crates/quarto-core/src/` finds exactly 2 hits, both metadata
  passthrough/tests (extension/read.rs, stage/stages/metadata_merge.rs) — no header-numbering
  logic anywhere.
- `grep -rln number-sections resources/scss/` finds nothing — not even a CSS-counter-based
  implementation (a common alternative for HTML).
- `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/crossref_index.rs` DOES track a section-counter stack
  (`advance_sections`, driven by `Header` blocks) — but its own module doc says this exists only
  to compute compound numbers for OTHER crossref targets ("Figure 1.2.3"), not to number or
  register sections themselves. `visit_header` never calls `index_custom_target` for the header
  itself, and never injects a number into the header's own inline content.
- `crates/quarto-core/src/crossref/registry.rs:83` registers `sec` → "Section" as a builtin
  ref-type display name, but `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/crossref_resolve.rs` has no
  handling at all for a `sec`-typed ref or for `CrossrefIndex::headings` (the `HeadingRecord` list
  `crossref_index.rs` does populate, apparently for a different, not-yet-built future use —
  "needed for cross-file book fixup in future phases").

Relevance to the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic (see `claude-notes/designs/pandoc-hybrid-architecture.md`
§11): under `crossref-numbering: external` (the mode the epic sets for docx/pptx targets), Q1's
own `sections.lua` — which normally provides BOTH capabilities natively via Pandoc's own header
numbering — is suppressed wholesale as part of the same filter group P3 audited
(`quarto_crossref_filters`, gated at `main.lua:718`). If Q2 has no replacement, `--to docx` with
`number-sections: true` (or any `@sec-` reference) will silently produce unnumbered headers /
unresolved section refs, with no error. This is a real regression risk for docx/pptx v1, not a
theoretical one.

Scope note: this strand is about whether/how to implement the feature at all (which predates and
is broader than the pandoc-hybrid epic — it would also be missing for a plain HTML render today,
if anyone tested it, which nobody appears to have). The pandoc-hybrid epic itself should NOT try
to build this from scratch as part of its own scope; the epic's design doc records this as an
open, not-yet-assigned-to-a-plan question and should reference this strand instead of
re-investigating.

title: Video shortcode renders as plain link in q2 preview / hub-client (Lua FORMAT carries preview pseudo-format)
description:
The {{< video >}} shortcode embeds an <iframe> in 'q2 render' (html + revealjs) but degrades to a plain <a> link in 'q2 preview' and the hub-client WASM preview.

Root cause: video.lua gates on quarto.doc.is_format('html:js'). The Lua FORMAT global is set verbatim from the pipeline target_format. In preview that is the pseudo-format 'q2-preview' (html) / 'q2-slides' (revealjs), which is_html_output() does not recognize, so the format check fails and the shortcode falls through to its pandoc.Link fallback. This affects ALL format-gated Lua shortcodes/filters under preview, not just video.

Proposed fix: normalize the Lua FORMAT global to the canonical pandoc output format (q2-preview/q2-debug/q2-raw -> html, q2-slides -> revealjs) at the quarto-core boundary, keeping target_format unchanged for pipeline decisions. Plan + verified reproduction in claude-notes/plans/2026-06-22-video-shortcode-preview.md.

Secondary (separate): revealjs render emits a bare unsized iframe; needs SCSS sizing.

Status 2026-06-22: diagnosis complete and reproduced end-to-end (render html iframe OK, preview html plain link confirmed in browser). Awaiting go-ahead to implement.

title: brand.yml font weight ranges (400..700) silently collapse to 400; no variable-font axis support for google or file sources
description:
brand.yml allows variable-font weight ranges written as a string, e.g. `weight: 600..900` (spec: https://posit-dev.github.io/brand-yml/brand/typography.html — "Variable font weights can be written as a string `600..900`"). Quarto 2 parses that value without complaint and then silently substitutes weight 400. Observed with q2 0.28.0, HEAD 85e98fb02.

## Repro

_brand.yml:

    typography:
      fonts:
        - family: EB Garamond
          source: google
          weight: 400..700
      base: EB Garamond

Rendered CSS contains:

    @import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=EB+Garamond:ital,wght@0,400;1,400&display=swap")

Only 400 is requested; bold text falls back to synthetic bold. No warning anywhere. The same value on a typography slot (`base: {weight: 400..700}`) passes through `font_weight_to_scss` (brand_layer.rs:350) as the raw string and produces `$font-weight-base: 400..700 !default;`, which then hits the silent compile fallback of the sibling strand — so two silent failures stack.

## Where

- crates/quarto-brand/src/types.rs:625-636 — `BrandFontWeight` is Number | Name(String) | List; a range string deserializes as `Name("400..700")`.
- crates/quarto-sass/src/brand_layer.rs:538-551 — `enumerate_weights` does `weight_name_to_number(s).unwrap_or(400)` for any unrecognised name. Quarto 1 (external-sources/quarto-cli/src/core/sass/brand.ts:42-66) throws `Unknown font weight ${weight}` here, so the silent 400 is a Q2 regression on top of the missing feature.
- crates/quarto-sass/src/brand_layer.rs:466-497 — `google_font_import_string` only ever emits discrete `wght@` values joined by `;`, never the `wght@400..700` axis form Google Fonts uses to serve one variable font file.
- crates/quarto-sass/src/brand_layer.rs:553-584 — `file_font_face_block` emits a single `font-weight: <n>` per file, so a local variable .woff2 (e.g. Google's `*-VariableFont_wght.woff2` downloads) cannot be declared with `font-weight: 400 700` either.

## Fix shape

1. Parse `N..M` into a `BrandFontWeight::Range(u32, u32)` variant (both for `fonts[].weight` and file entries).
2. Google/Bunny: emit `wght@N..M` (and `ital,wght@0,N..M;1,N..M` when italic is requested) so the variable font is served.
3. `source: file`: emit `font-weight: N M` in the @font-face block.
4. Any weight string that is neither a known keyword nor a range should be a hard diagnostic (Q1 parity), never a silent 400.

Docs note for bd-qnylgu69: until this lands, guides/authoring/brand.qmd should say ranges are unsupported and that fonts are requested at discrete weights only.

Discovered 2026-09-08 while testing brand.yml Google/local variable fonts for cscheid-net-2026.

title: hub: assert verbatim CRLF flow disk to automerge to WASM
description: The automerge Text blob is the cross-user canonical byte store and must hold the user's bytes verbatim including CRLF. byte-offset-invariant.md marks disk to automerge to VFS to WASM as preserve-mandatory, but no test owns it. Add a Rust guard that the WASM parse entry in wasm-quarto-hub-client receives a CRLF document byte-identical to disk, and a quarto-sync-client vitest that a CRLF document survives the Monaco splice round-trip without normalization. Both pass today since no normalization exists; they are regression guards protecting the property the preserve policy depends on. Scope is the verbatim byte flow only; the LF-only line and column converter on the TS side is bd-b1291v6g. See claude-notes/designs/line-ending-test-harness-spec.md gap G2 and byte-offset-invariant.md hub row.

title: Code-cell shorthand: quoted YAML values keep their quotes in the figcaption
description:
crossref/codeblock_shorthand.rs::parse_cell_options splits `#| key: value` with split_once(':') + trim() instead of parsing YAML, so `#| fig-cap: "A caption."` renders as `Figure 1: "A caption."` with literal quote characters in the <figcaption>.

Affects every `#|` code cell, not just mermaid — reproduced on a plain ```python cell (claude-notes/plans/mermaid-cell-options-investigation/probe3.qmd) and on a ```mermaid fence (probe2.qmd, section C2).

The fix falls out of migrating codeblock_shorthand onto the real cell-options facility (quarto-core/src/cell_options/mod.rs::partition_cell_options, which parses YAML with source attribution). That module's own doc names this matcher as a consumer that "should migrate here"; the migration never happened.

Expect snapshot movement. Discovered while investigating bd-mermaid-cell-options-9wo3crl0; see claude-notes/plans/2026-08-10-mermaid-cell-options.md (defect D1). Whether this is fixed on that strand or separately is open design question 3 there.

title: q2 preview capture-splice cannot splice engines that emit unwrapped output (marimo islands never reach the pane)
description: Plan-4c FINDING #5 (2026-07-03, task 4cH, Opus e2e agent, evidence in .superpowers/sdd/task-4cH-report.md in the ts-engine-extensions worktree). derive_cell_outputs/is_cell_wrapper (crates/quarto-core/src/engine/capture_splice.rs) map engine captures onto ::: {.cell} Div wrappers only. Echo emits them; julia gets them from the engine-host's mdFromCodeCell. Marimo's execute() builds processedMarkdown itself: each executed cell is a bare {=html} raw block (<marimo-island>/<marimo-cell-output>), zero .cell wrappers — so the capture RECORDS server-side ('recorded engine capture(s) engines=marimo count=1', ~2s) but never splices; the preview pane shows inert source forever. q2 render is unaffected (works fully). Fix is a design decision: (a) q2-core — teach capture_splice to anchor unwrapped engine output at the original code-cell position; or (b) host/engine-side — route marimo-style engines through mdFromCodeCell-style .cell wrapping (upstream render-output.ts change; would also alter static render DOM). A limitation-pinning playwright canary (engine-capture-splice-marimo.spec.ts, seam SC21-NEG, opt-in QUARTO_SC21_LIVE=1) asserts the current behavior and is EXPECTED to redden when this is fixed — flip it to the positive splice test then (assertion sketch in plan 4cH section).

title: Emit and activate the document-wide .anchored class (heading anchor links)
description:
q2 never emits the `anchored` class and ships none of the anchor-link machinery Quarto 1 has. bd-v9zs83zj adds `anchored` to the five appendix headings (matching Q1's headingClasses), but the class is INERT there until this strand lands.

## What Quarto 1 does

1. EMIT, document-wide. format-html.ts:828-848 adds `anchored` to every h2-h6, .quarto-figure[id] and div[id^=tbl-] inside `main` (Bootstrap) or `body`, gated on the `anchors` format option, skipping #toc-title and anything with .no-anchor.
2. PRE-APPLY in the appendix. format-html-appendix.ts:98 and :363, because appendix headings are synthesized by a different postprocessor. classList.add is idempotent so the passes do not collide.
3. CONSUME via AnchorJS, not CSS. quarto-html-after-body.ejs:38-46 does anchorJS.add('.anchored'), injecting an a.anchorjs-link (the paragraph-mark hover link) into each match. _quarto-rules.scss:147-175 styles .anchorjs-link — the element AnchorJS creates. There is NO .anchored rule anywhere; the class is purely a JS selector hook.

## What q2 has

Nothing: no `anchors` option (grep -rn '"anchors"' crates/ returns zero), no anchor.min.js, no quarto.js, no .anchorjs-link styling, no .anchored rules. Only the appendix headings from bd-v9zs83zj will carry the class.

## Scope

- The document-wide pass over h2-h6 / figures / tables.
- The `anchors` format option (including its icon-string form: `anchors: true` vs a custom glyph).
- The .no-anchor and #toc-title exclusions.
- The runtime: vendor anchor.min.js into resources/ (NEVER reference external-sources/ per CLAUDE.md) plus the .anchorjs-link SCSS, or implement the hover link natively.

## THE NON-OBVIOUS CONSTRAINT

The document-wide pass must be an AST TRANSFORM, not a DOM postprocessor — q2 has no post-Pandoc DOM stage and CLAUDE.md forbids introducing one.

That matters because Q1 relies on classList.add being IDEMPOTENT. Pushing onto a Vec<String> of classes is NOT. The appendix headings are h2 and would be caught by the general pass as well, producing class="anchored anchored quarto-appendix-heading". The general transform MUST skip headings that already carry the class.

Ordering also matters: the general transform has to run in Finalization AFTER AppendixStructureTransform, or it will miss the synthesized appendix headings entirely (they do not exist yet at Normalization time). See claude-notes/designs/transform-pipeline-phases.md.

Investigation context: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-footnotes-appendix-heading.md (Finding 5).

title: cargo xtask verify: tree-sitter grammar step is not hermetic across checkouts (shared ~/.cache/tree-sitter/lib/markdown.dylib keyed by grammar name)
