title: capture-splice: source-level RawBlock at an unfilled engine-cell position can be mis-consumed as the cell's output
description: Discovered in the Plan 4c.2 final review (bd-5jxcio5d). The preview capture-splice matcher was generalized so `is_engine_output_block(b) = is_cell_wrapper(b) || matches!(b, Block::RawBlock(_))` — a cell pairs with its lockstep-positioned B1 block whether a .cell Div or a RawBlock island (marimo). Residual edge the doc comment now records: if an engine cell emits NO output block at its lockstep B1 position (e.g. include:false, empty/error cell) AND is immediately followed by a SOURCE-level RawBlock (user-authored {=html}/{=latex}), the matcher consumes that passthrough RawBlock as the cell's output (wrong), then the following A1 RawBlock diverges and the walk stops. Trace: A1=[CodeBlock(engine, no output), RawBlock(user html)], B1=[RawBlock(user html)] -> map records cell->user RawBlock. OLD behavior fell through safely (is_cell_wrapper false -> break -> cell raw source, alignment preserved); the generalization introduced this. Properties: PREVIEW-ONLY (never render), fail-soft, and NOT reachable on marimo's normal path (every marimo cell emits an island) nor for wrapper engines (jupyter/knitr/echo/julia hit the .cell arm first). Fix idea: only consume a B1 RawBlock at a cell position when it is NOT structurally-equal to the next A1 block (a2.blocks[i+1]) — i.e. it's genuinely the cell's output, not the following passthrough. Add a regression test in capture_splice.rs #[cfg(test)] for the [cell-no-output, user RawBlock] shape. Location: crates/quarto-core/src/engine/capture_splice.rs derive_cell_outputs_walk engine-cell branch.

title: local-prod static/proxy server dies on unhandled ECONNRESET (scripts/local-prod-server.mjs)
description:
`scripts/local-prod-server.mjs` (the port-8080 static + reverse-proxy leg of `npm run local-prod`) exits on an unhandled ECONNRESET rather than logging and continuing. Observed **twice** in one session on 2026-08-21 while two different agents drove a local-prod hub with Playwright plus periodic `curl` health checks; the hub (:3000) and sandboxed-preview (:8081) legs stayed healthy both times, so it is specific to the static/proxy leg.

Impact: a long-lived local-prod session dies mid-use for a transient socket reset, which is exactly the failure mode local-prod exists to avoid (it is the setup we use to mirror production and to demo features interactively). Project data on disk survived both crashes; only the process needed restarting.

Likely fix: attach an `'error'` handler on the proxy/upstream sockets (and/or `server.on('clientError')`) that logs and destroys the individual socket instead of letting the exception reach the process. Worth auditing for the same gap on the request stream and the websocket upgrade path.

Found while executing claude-notes/plans/2026-08-21-preview-click-to-editor-scroll.md; entirely unrelated to that plan's changes.

Related doc bug found at the same time: CLAUDE.md's local-prod section says the hub listens on port 3001, but it actually listens on 3000.

title: q2 preview drops engine include-in-header (marimo islands script) — widgets never hydrate
description:
ROOT CAUSE (code + browser confirmed). In q2 preview, marimo cells render their static server-side island markup but never hydrate / execute dynamically. The engine's include-in-header content (the @marimo-team/islands cdn.jsdelivr.net <script type=module>, the __MARIMO_EXPORT_CONTEXT__ trust-marker, the <marimo-code hidden> notebook source, and islands style.css) never reaches the preview pane's <head>.

MECHANISM: On the render path, EngineExecutionStage (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs:416-424) copies result.includes.header_includes into ctx.includes, and apply_template.rs:149 late-folds ctx.includes into the rendered <head> slots. On the PREVIEW path, EngineExecutionStage is bypassed and CaptureSpliceStage (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/capture_splice.rs:138-146) extracts ONLY capture.result.markdown, explicitly discarding capture.result.includes. So ctx.includes.header_includes stays empty -> the islands <script> is never emitted -> no client JS -> inert widgets. The full ExecuteResult (incl. includes.header_includes) IS present in the capture (serialized at engine_execution.rs:385-391); it is dropped only by the splice stage.

BROWSER EVIDENCE (headed Chromium via q2 preview on the marimo mo.ui.slider fixture): iframe __MARIMO_EXPORT_CONTEXT__=undefined; <marimo-code> absent; <marimo-island>/<marimo-ui-element> present (body markup delivers fine); ZERO network requests to jsdelivr (script tag simply absent, not blocked); console clean (matches 'no errors'); iframe sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin'; CSP meta = [] (empty). q2 render of the same doc emits all three markers inside <head>. => Hypothesis #1 (dropped include-in-header) CONFIRMED; hypothesis #2 (CSP/sandbox blocking) REFUTED.

PROPOSED FIX: In CaptureSpliceStage, after (or alongside) the block splice, read capture.result.includes.{header_includes,include_before,include_after} and extend ctx.includes.* with them — mirroring engine_execution.rs:416-424. The existing apply_template.rs:149 late fold then delivers them to the head via the same channel q2 render uses. Small, surgical, no new architectural surface. Multi-engine: fold each capture's includes in the same order the blocks are folded. Needs a native seam test (ctx.includes populated after splice) + an e2e assertion that the islands <script src=jsdelivr> is present in the preview iframe <head> (extend engine-capture-splice-marimo.spec.ts SC23, whose header currently scopes hydration as out-of-scope).

Related: bd-5jxcio5d (splice, CLOSED — block delivery is correct and separate). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-07-plan4c2-marimo-preview-e2e.md (Open decision / FINDING #5). Do NOT conflate with bd-5m1ni9if (RawBlock-misconsume edge).

Spun out of bd-45yw (replay engine). Once traces double as replay fixtures (and as user-attached bug-report artifacts), trace size becomes a real constraint — they will be checked into the repo as regression fixtures and posted by users in issues.

Current quarto-trace output captures per-stage pipeline state (see crates/quarto-trace/src/lib.rs and crates/quarto-core/src/stage/trace.rs::JsonTraceObserver), which is already on the heavy side for routine diagnostic use.

Investigate:
- Where the bulk lives in current traces (per-stage AST snapshots? supporting_files content? something else?)
- Which content is actually load-bearing for replay vs. diagnostics, and whether the two roles can share one artifact (the design preference noted in bd-45yw's plan)
- Compression on disk; lazy loading on read
- Whether per-stage AST snapshots can be elided/diffed when not needed
- Size budgets — what is reasonable for (a) checked-in CI fixtures and (b) user-attached bug reports

Goal: make 'one trace serves both diagnostic and replay roles' practical. If size cannot be bounded, fall back to two separate artifacts and document why.

- crates/quarto-trace/src/lib.rs (TraceDocument, TraceEntry)
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/trace.rs (JsonTraceObserver)

title: Reader does not strip a leading UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF); it becomes prose content
description: A file starting with the UTF-8 byte order mark (EF BB BF, U+FEFF) is not special-cased anywhere in the qmd reader. At 7ef59618 it is a hard parse error (U+FEFF is category Cf, which the prose regexes reject). Once bd-wuiu1of7 lands (\p{Cf} accepted in prose) the file will parse, but the BOM survives as the first character of the first Str — and, when the file starts with YAML front matter, likely breaks the '---' delimiter match. Pandoc strips a leading BOM before parsing (Text.Pandoc.Readers.Markdown / the shared input normalisation). Fix shape: strip a leading U+FEFF once at the reader entry point (readers::qmd::read), before tree-sitter sees the bytes, keeping source offsets honest (the BOM is 3 bytes; source_info must account for it or the reader should record the trim). TDD: fixture with BOM + front matter + heading; assert metadata parsed and first Str has no U+FEFF.

title: qmd writer/reader: backslash in a quoted shortcode argument doubles on every round-trip
description:
The qmd writer and the tree-sitter reader disagree about backslash inside a quoted shortcode argument, so backslashes double on every write/read cycle.

Writer (crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:2219, write_shortcode_string_value) escapes both quote and backslash when it quotes a value:
    '"' => buf.write_all(b"\\\"")?,
    '\\' => buf.write_all(b"\\\\")?,

Reader (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:1000, the extract_quoted_text closure in the "shortcode_string" arm) unescapes ONLY the quote character:
    inner.replace("\\\"", "\"")     // double-quoted
    inner.replace("\\'", "'")       // single-quoted
There is no \\\\ -> \\ step, so the writer's backslash escape is never undone.

Repro (no code change needed, reproduces on main at 596ceb572):

    $ printf 'x: {{< kbd "a\\b" >}}\n' | pampa -t qmd
    x: {{< kbd "a\\\\b" >}}
    $ # feed that output back in:
    x: {{< kbd "a\\\\\\\\b" >}}

Each round-trip doubles the run of backslashes. Read-side behaviour on first parse is correct and matches Q1 -- both q2 and Q1 give the shortcode the literal string a\\b for input "a\\b" (backslash is literal inside quotes; only the quote character is escapable). The defect is purely that the writer adds an escape the reader does not remove.

Affects any AST path that writes qmd and re-reads it: --to qmd, the hub-client incremental write-back, and the native-pampa round-trip tests.

Fix direction: make the pair symmetric. Either teach extract_quoted_text to unescape \\\\ -> \\ (matching the writer, and matching what the writer already does for the quote char), or stop escaping backslash in the writer. The former is preferable -- it keeps a literal quote-plus-backslash sequence unambiguous. Note the reader currently uses str::replace, which is order-dependent for overlapping escapes; a single left-to-right scan is the safer shape once two escapes exist.

Discovered while investigating bd-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-2u79bqp1 (escaped '\>' in a NAKED shortcode argument). The two are independent: that strand's fix routes '\>' to the AST as '>', which the writer then quotes as ">" and round-trips cleanly, so no backslash reaches the AST. This bug is reachable today without that change.

c-09tguqzj.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-09tguqzj.text:
SCOPE WIDENING: bare (unquoted) arguments are now a second entry point, not just quoted ones.

This strand's title and description scope the defect to a QUOTED shortcode argument. After the shortcode naked-string widening (branch braid/bd-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-2u79bqp1-shortcode-escaped-gt, commits e223edd52..2477d2816), the bare path reaches the same doubling.

Mechanism: the widened naked token admits backslash-escape pairs, and the reader applies CommonMark semantics -- '\\X' collapses to 'X' only when X is ASCII punctuation. When X is NOT punctuation the backslash is preserved into the AST, which is exactly the input this strand is about. That behaviour is asserted by the widening branch's own test test_naked_arg_backslash_before_non_punctuation_is_literal (crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_shortcode.rs:527).

Measured on the widened parser at 2477d2816:

    {{< kbd \n >}}        -> {{< kbd "\\n" >}}   -> {{< kbd "\\\\n" >}}
    {{< kbd a\b >}}       -> {{< kbd "a\\b" >}}  -> {{< kbd "a\\\\b" >}}
    {{< kbd "a\b" >}}     -> {{< kbd "a\\b" >}}  -> {{< kbd "a\\\\b" >}}   (quoted, unchanged from main)

i.e. bare and quoted now converge on the same doubling.

NOT A REGRESSION from that branch. Every affected bare input was a FATAL whole-document parse error before the widening, so each one is strictly better off -- it went from killing the page to round-tripping wrongly. The widening branch's plan originally justified scoping this strand out with the claim 'this plan's naked path never puts a bare backslash in the AST'; that claim was false and has been corrected in the plan (commit 07fdbd7f6), which is why this note exists.

Action for whoever picks this up: widen the title/description to cover both paths. The quoted route is the local ad hoc unescaper closure at treesitter.rs:997; the bare route is text_helpers::extract_quoted_text via shortcode::process_shortcode_naked_string. A fix that only touches the closure will now leave half the defect in place.

c-p4q7t1zg.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-p4q7t1zg.text:
Confirmed as a Q1 DIVERGENCE, not only an internal round-trip asymmetry. Measured against quarto 99.9.9:

  input {{< kbd "a\\\\b" >}}   (quoted arg, escaped backslash)
    Q1  -> a\\b        (\\\\ collapses to one backslash)
    q2  -> a\\\\b      (no collapse; both backslashes survive)

So the missing \\\\ -> \\ step in the local closure at treesitter.rs:997 is also the thing that makes q2 disagree with Q1 on this input, which raises the value of fixing it.

Full Q1 escape behaviour, measured across 12 cases (naked and quoted, both quote styles):
  - NAKED args: Q1 collapses \X for ASCII punctuation only (\> -> >, \* -> *, \- -> -); \n stays literal. This is the CommonMark/Pandoc rule, i.e. exactly what unescape_punctuation implements.
  - QUOTED args: Q1 collapses NOTHING except \\\\ -> \\. Punctuation escapes are preserved verbatim (\> stays \>), matching q2's current quoted behaviour.
  - Escaping the enclosing quote (\" inside "...", \' inside '...') is NOT a working escape in Q1 at all -- the double-quote case mis-terminates the string and errors the shortcode call, the single-quote case silently truncates. q2 handles both correctly (see test_parse_escaped_double_quote / test_parse_escaped_single_quote), so q2 is a strict superset there and must not regress to Q1's behaviour.

Consequence for scoping: the naked/quoted asymmetry itself is Q1's own design and is NOT a bug to fix -- bd-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-2u79bqp1's reader change makes q2's naked path match Q1 exactly, and quoted already matches. The only real defect left in this area is the \\\\ collapse, which is this strand.

description: Client renameFile (ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/client.ts:1400) reuses the same doc_id under the new path, and sync checkpoints are keyed by doc_id — so a renamed file HAS a checkpoint and sync_all_documents classifies it as deleted-on-disk: the new path is never created on disk. title: llms companions of listing pages may contain unsubstituted placeholder envelopes

Options: run an equivalent substitution over the captured markdown in llms_post_render, teach the capture cleanup to drop/simplify listing envelopes, or exclude listing placeholders from companions entirely. Found during bd-llms-txt-unimplemented-oih6z6j7 implementation (not yet observed in practice — connect-docs has no listing pages).

title: Sequential multi-engine execution (engine: [a, b, ...])
description:
Investigate and design support for running multiple Quarto 2 execution engines in sequence for a single document.

Two coupled changes:

1. YAML config: allow 'engine:' to be an ordered array (e.g. engine: [knitr, mermaidjs]) in addition to the current singular string/map forms. Distinct engines only; order is significant (engine N may emit code cells consumed by engine N+1). Array merge across config layers uses the existing default (!concat); no engine-specific tag default for now.

2. Pipeline: thread N engines through EngineExecutionStage. The AST->text->engine->text->AST->reconcile loop already type-checks end-to-end; each subsequent engine starts from the AST after the prior engine's results were reconciled in. Generalize the FileId/intermediate-file slot handling (currently 2 slots: .qmd + one .rmarkdown) to N+1 slots.

Tracing/replay/preview redesign: TraceDocument.engine_capture (single Option slot, name-keyed replay) becomes per-engine. Capture one AST snapshot + one EngineCapture per engine invocation within the stage, mirroring the existing transform:<name> sub-entry pattern. Preview record/replay (record_capture, with_replay, preview cache) generalize from one capture to an ordered list.

Validation/testing uses a simple file-backed test engine (reads a results file and splices per-cell outputs in order) so multi-engine sequencing can be exercised deterministically without R/Python/Jupyter, and without committing to a real second engine (e.g. mermaidjs) yet.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-27-multi-engine-execution.md

Status: design/investigation. Implementation gated on user go-ahead after plan review.

title: tree-sitter inline-multiline-attrs tests fail with 20 parse errors on main
description:
Running 'tree-sitter test' from crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/ reports 20 failing test cases in the inline-multiline-attrs corpus group (cases 95-104 plus a heading case), with 'Total parses: 508; successful parses: 488; failed parses: 20; success percentage: 96.06%'. This trips 'cargo xtask verify' at Step 4/12.

Confirmed pre-existing on origin/main HEAD (3e781667 at time of report) by stashing all local changes and re-running the test — same failures. The failing cases overlap with the feature that landed in 1afd5a6ac95dd ('tree-sitter-qmd - allow multi-line attribute lists on inline images/spans (#209)', merged 2026-05-17).

Failing case names include:
- image with multi-line class-only attrs (quarto-web hero-banner case)
- image with multi-line mixed class + key=value attrs
- image with single-line class + leading and trailing whitespace inside braces
- span with multi-line class attrs
- span with multi-line key=value attrs
- heading with leading whitespace inside block attribute_specifier braces
- bulleted/ordered list item with multi-line span/image attrs
- nested bulleted list with multi-line span attrs in inner item

Likely causes (need investigation):
1. The compiled parser.c committed in 1afd5a6a doesn't match the grammar.js changes — needs regeneration.
2. The test corpus expectations were updated but the parser output diverged.
3. The 'tree-sitter test' tool version disagrees with what was used at merge time.

Discovered-from: bd-j73yw (Phase 1 of bd-1tl09, code-block decorations) — surfaced while running cargo xtask verify after Phase 0 / Phase 1 commit 1 work. Not caused by that work; clean stash confirms regression on main.

Workaround for the dependent epic: run 'cargo xtask verify --skip-treesitter-tests' (or call cargo nextest / cargo build steps directly) until this is fixed.

title: Lua: doc:normalize() — inline whitespace coalescing + table row padding

title: incremental writer: block_source_span/inline_source_span use the silently-wrong start_offset/end_offset pair
description:
Two helpers in crates/pampa/src/writers/incremental.rs read a span as `si.start_offset()..si.end_offset()`, the accessor pair the provenance rule calls **silently wrong** on a `Concat`: it returns `0` and the *content* length, never the source hull.

- `block_source_span` (fn at :550, the pair at :552) — one production caller, `assemble`, which computes `first_block_start` from `blocks[0]` (:369).
- `inline_source_span` (fn at :1033, the pair at :1035) — `pub`, but **no production caller**; reached only from `crates/pampa/tests/integration/inline_splice_safety_tests.rs`.

**Failure mode is worse than a wrong offset: it silently drops the front matter.** `assemble` tests `start > 0` (:376) to decide whether a front-matter region exists and, if so, copies `original_qmd[..start]` into the output (:381). A `Concat` first block makes `start_offset()` return `0`, so the branch is skipped entirely and the front matter never reaches the incremental output — no panic, no diagnostic, no wrong bytes, just missing bytes.

**Latent today, not live.** Every production `original_ast` is an untransformed, parent-less parse whose body is all `Original`. That invariant is pinned for the capture path by `preview_untransformed_baseline_body_pool_is_all_original_own_file` (crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs); `apply_node_edit` inherits it by consuming the pinned artifact; `incremental_write_qmd` (crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:2952) re-parses raw bytes under an analogous invariant that no test exercises.

**The fix** is to return `Option<Range<usize>>` from both helpers (via `preimage_in(target_file_id)`, matching every other span read in the file) and thread the `None` case through callers — for `assemble`, `None` must be distinguished from `Some(0)`: the former means "cannot tell", not "no front matter". Needs its own tests, including a `Concat`-first-block fixture asserting the front matter survives.

**Why this is out-of-plan.** Plan 3 Phase 1 enumerated and classified the 26 `preimage_in` call sites and decided guard-not-fix for that class. These two are `start_offset`/`end_offset` consumers, which no phase of the provenance epic enumerates — so a fix for them is genuinely outside every active plan. Recorded (not fixed) in Plan 3 § Evidence -> Phase 1, with a doc comment at each function.

Ironic detail worth keeping: this same file already carries two comments warning against this exact accessor pair (:714 in `assemble_inline_splice`, :805 in `assemble_inline_content`), both added when the pair caused earlier bugs.

title: Website render errors copying engine supporting DIRECTORY as a flat resource (file_copy on a dir)
description:
A project (website) render of a document whose engine reports a supporting DIRECTORY (e.g. julia-engine sends supporting: [<stem>_files] per its faithful Q1 port) FAILS in copy_resources_to_output_dir (crates/quarto-core/src/project_resources.rs:816): runtime.file_copy is called on the whole plot_files directory and errors 'the source path is neither a regular file nor a symlink to a regular file'.

Path: engine_execution.rs:426 add_engine_files(supporting_files) -> DocumentResourceReport -> resolve_reported_resources (does NOT walk directories, project_resources.rs:515) -> ResolvedResource{source=<dir>} -> copy_resources_to_output_dir -> file_copy(<dir>) -> ERROR. SystemRuntime has file_copy but no dir_copy.

The figure itself DOES land in _site/plot_files/figure-html/*.png (via the artifact-flush path) BEFORE this step, so output is produced but the render returns Err. Surfaced by Phase 4H (Plan 4 Julia validation) J5/J6 — the first file-based julia figure to reach the project resource copier (4CD's single-doc plot was inline base64, no file). Existing resource unit tests (project_resources.rs:1160/1594) only pass individual FILES, so no coverage caught it.

Fix is a design decision: (a) recurse in the copier / add a dir-copy to SystemRuntime (WASM/VFS implications); (b) exclude supporting DIRECTORIES from the resource report since artifact flush already lands them (double-handling smell); or (c) expand supporting dirs into individual files at add_engine_files time. Blocks Plan-4 J5/J6 (currently #[ignore]d in crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/julia_engine_e2e.rs with this id).
close_reason: Fixed via controller-adjudicated option (c): DocumentResourceReport::add_engine_files expands engine-reported supporting DIRECTORIES into contained files recursively (SystemRuntime is_dir/dir_list); report stays file-only, resolve/copy/SystemRuntime unchanged. TDD unit test at the seam (RED: left=[plot_files] verbatim, then GREEN); J5+J6 un-#[ignore]d and GREEN with real julia+deno (~30s each, frozen assertions intact; J6 pinned QUARTO_JOBS=1 so its tracing capture observes the spawn). Full quarto-core 2622 passed; workspace 10575 passed. Code commit 650a6b694, docs 5085ea5d6 on feature/ts-engine-extensions.

description: Investigation-only: characterize H1 (CollectionSynchronizer.addPeer dedup guard skipping resync on peer-candidate reordering) and H2 (Repo.saveSyncState per-storageId throttle dropping a document's persisted sync-state write) as manufacturable mechanisms behind a hub-client user's IndexDocument going stale over weeks. c-3duiavi4.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-3duiavi4.text: Built the full end-to-end H4 repro through the real SyncClient/Repo/DocSynchronizer stack, per the 2026-09-17 handoff: ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/full-stack-actor-collision.test.ts. Two real SyncClients share one actor id against a real startTestHub(); each commits its own index-doc edit synchronously (no await between the two createFile() calls) so neither sees the other's edit first -- no holdUpgrades race needed, JS run-to-completion semantics are enough. Confirmed: (1) the real console.log('error receiving message', {err: RangeError duplicate-seq...}) swallowed-catch fires through a real hub relay, not a hand-rolled harness; (2) a subsequent unrelated edit from a third, non-colliding-actor client lands on the hub and a fresh connection within ~5s, but at least one of the two colliding clients never receives it even given the same window, and stays stuck identically for a second follow-up edit -- a durable stall, not one dropped message. Which of the two clients loses the race is real timing (test asserts 'at least one', not 'reader specifically'); reproduced identically across 5 consecutive local runs. npx tsc --noEmit clean; full package suite 142/142 (25 files, up from 24). Research doc and CLAUDE.local.md updated. Still investigation-only -- no fix attempted; next call (fix vs. chasing a real specimen) is Gordon's.

c-9fh0imqv.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-9fh0imqv.text: Checked whether the in-progress automerge upgrade would fix H4 -- no, on both halves. (1) Repo.ts's swallowed .catch(console.log) for the sync-message path is byte-identical from v2.5.6 through the newest fetched refs (v2.6.0-alpha.3/.5, v2.7.0-authors.1); a real sibling bug WAS fixed upstream (PR #673 / 4f0ba092, a sync throw escaping the outer dispatcher and crashing a Node server) but it doesn't touch our already-caught async path. (2) The actor-id-stability primitive that would fix the likely root cause (RepoConfig.actorIdPrefix: stable prefix + unique-per-session suffix) was written upstream (31f12b13, Jan 2024, branch 'stable-actor-ids') but never merged/shipped in any release. Conclusion: upgrade is good hygiene, doesn't fix this. A fix needs to be q2-side (actorIdFromUserId) or upstream-contributed. Committed e878f00d1.

c-b685s2zt.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-b685s2zt.text: Implemented and tested a client-side fix for H4's 'get an already-stuck client unstuck' half, per Gordon's explicit request (does NOT stop the actor-seq collision itself -- that still needs actorIdFromUserId changes or an upstream fix). Presented 2 design axes (detection mechanism: wrap synchronizer.receiveMessage vs sniff console.log; recovery scope: index-doc-only vs generalize to file docs); Gordon chose synchronizer-wrap + index-doc-only. Implementation in ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/client.ts: installDuplicateSeqRecovery wraps the connection's own repo.synchronizer.receiveMessage (instance-level monkeypatch, no automerge-repo source touched) to detect the swallowed duplicate-seq RangeError for this connection's index doc; recoverIndexDocument then does repo.delete(indexDocId) [drops the wedged DocSynchronizer/SyncState + purges persisted storage for that one doc, confirmed against source] followed by a fresh repo.find(), swaps in the new handle, and reconciles file/identity/capture state. Extended (not duplicated) full-stack-actor-collision.test.ts to verify: temporarily disabled the fix, confirmed the test failed exactly as expected (collision still occurs, no recovery log); restored the fix, confirmed green, 8/8 repeat runs stable at ~0.4-0.6s (vs ~10.3s pre-fix). Full package suite 142/142; npx tsc --noEmit clean. One incidental fix along the way: added a defensive guard since 3 existing test files mock Repo without a .synchronizer, which crashed without the guard. Research doc updated with a new 'Fix: automatic index-document self-heal' section.

c-gbv4lpgf.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-gbv4lpgf.text: Both H1 tier 1 and H2 confirmed mechanically against vendored automerge-repo v2.5.6 source. H2: Repo#saveSyncState throttles per storageId, shared across all docs with that peer -- overlapping sync-state events within 100ms silently drop the earlier doc's persisted save (live protocol still converges after). H1 tier 1: CollectionSynchronizer.addPeer's dedup guard really does suppress beginSync on a repeat peer-candidate with no intervening peer-disconnected, and NetworkSubsystem doesn't cover for it (own TODO comment acknowledges the reconnect-ordering problem). This promotes H1 from 'plausible, sibling to bd-jit6pdwq' to a confirmed second defect. Tests: ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/{sync-state-save-throttle,collection-synchronizer-peer-dedup}.test.ts (committed 8914f9750 on explore/automerge-index-resync). Research doc updated with Characterization results section. Next: Gordon's call on H1 tier 2 (real-socket confirming test) vs a production fix -- neither attempted here per investigation-only scope.

c-xluays6r.author: Gordon Woodhull

Now the leading candidate, written up as H4 in the research doc. Root cause of the actor/seq collision itself (candidate: actorIdFromUserId's deliberately-stable actor id) is plausible but unconfirmed. Also corrected the Carlos capture plan's framing (reload/wipe was always the bug's defining fact, not new info) and dropped the step telling him to apply the known fix, since he's deliberately staying stuck to preserve the repro. Committed 515d7af59 on explore/automerge-index-resync.

title: Cargo: knitr format config structs use #[serde(flatten)] HashMap for passthrough keys (determinism rule)
description:
Noticed during bd-nn2fou8h's pre-commit determinism check; PRE-EXISTING, not introduced there.

crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/format.rs declares 'extra: HashMap<String, Value>' with #[serde(flatten)] on four structs (PandocConfig, ExecuteConfig, RenderConfig, and the identifier config). CLAUDE.md's coding rules and claude-notes/instructions/review.md both call this out explicitly as a red flag: '#[serde(flatten)] on HashMap fields (serialization order becomes non-deterministic)' and 'Field with #[serde(flatten)] -> LinkedHashMap only'.

PRACTICAL IMPACT IS LOW, which is why this is p3 and not p1: the serialized JSON is consumed by the knitr R scripts, which index it by key (format$execute[['echo']] etc.), so key ORDER does not change behavior. There is no snapshot test over this JSON today. The risk is latent — a future snapshot test or a diff-based debugging workflow over the R payload would be flaky in a way that is annoying to diagnose.

FIX: swap the four 'extra' fields to hashlink::LinkedHashMap, which is already a workspace dependency and is what the rule prescribes. Should be mechanical; watch for the Deserialize side and for any code that constructs these structs with HashMap::new() (with_defaults does).

Not touched by bd-nn2fou8h: ExecuteConfig::overlay_document_scope only writes the typed fields, never 'extra'.

title: quarto-parse-errors produce_diagnostic_messages panics on invalid UTF-8 input (lossy-string / tree-sitter offset mismatch)
description:
## Symptom

```
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs:121:35:
start byte index 7748 is not a char boundary; it is inside '�' (bytes 7746..7749 of string)
```

Triggered today by feeding a PNG to the parse pipeline (sibling bd-i6jy4). Even with that upstream fixed, this function should not panic on any input — it is a diagnostic generator and must degrade gracefully.

## Root cause

`crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs:112`:

```rust
let input_str = String::from_utf8_lossy(input_bytes);
let byte_offset = calculate_byte_offset(&input_str, parse_state.row, parse_state.column);
let substring = &input_str[byte_offset..];   // line 121, panics
```

`from_utf8_lossy` replaces each invalid byte (or invalid sequence) with `U+FFFD` (3 bytes), so `input_str` is longer than `input_bytes` whenever the input is not valid UTF-8. Tree-sitter, however, reports `row` and `column` as byte offsets into the *original bytes*. `calculate_byte_offset` walks `input_str` using those numbers as if they referred to the lossy string, so the result can land inside a 3-byte `�` and the slice panics.

The same pattern repeats at `error_generation.rs:196` inside the per-note span-end loop, so any error with a successful note-emission path on UTF-8-invalid input would also panic.

## Fix approach

Operate on `input_bytes` directly for offset arithmetic (which is what tree-sitter's offsets describe), and only convert to a `Cow<str>` for the *small* slice that needs char-counted span-end advancement. Specifically:

1. `calculate_byte_offset` should take `&[u8]` and walk byte-wise: count newlines, then add column. That maps 1:1 to tree-sitter's reported positions.
2. The char-counted span-end loop (`size` chars, line ~120 and ~194) should slice `input_bytes[offset..]` first, then `from_utf8_lossy` only the slice, then advance by `ch.len_utf8()`. That keeps the byte-domain offsets honest while still handling multi-byte characters correctly when the input *is* valid UTF-8.
3. `quarto_source_map::utils::offset_to_location` is called on `&input_str` — it likely expects a `&str`. Need to pass a lossy conversion at the call site or extend the source-map API to take bytes. Investigate which is less invasive.

A blanket `floor_char_boundary` would silence the panic but produce incorrect locations under the same byte/string mismatch. Do not paper over.

## Tests

Add a unit test in `quarto-parse-errors`:
- `produce_diagnostic_messages` over a binary input (e.g., the embedded PNG fixture or any `vec![0xff, 0xfe, ...]`) must return a Vec without panicking. Content of the diagnostic is not asserted — only "does not panic".
- Add a property-style test that feeds random byte sequences via `proptest` or hand-rolled corpus and asserts no panic.

## Out of scope

Filtering binaries out of the upstream callers — that is bd-i6jy4. This issue is purely the defensive contract that diagnostic generation never panics regardless of input.
close_reason: Implemented in bd20002e (merged via 52de7fc2). error_diagnostic_from_parse_state now operates entirely in the input_bytes domain — calculate_byte_offset takes &[u8], new advance_chars + offset_to_location_bytes helpers keep all offsets honest, and the leading/trailing-space trim loops are byte-level. Regression test produce_diagnostic_messages_does_not_panic_on_invalid_utf8 reproduces the panic on parent commit; passes here. Full workspace 9187/9187 green; no snapshot drift on valid UTF-8 paths.

title: xtask build-all/verify never build ts-packages (MCP server dist missing at runtime)
description: cargo xtask build-all claims to be the fresh-clone source of truth but never builds ts-packages/* dist output. hub-client consumes ts-packages from source (exports map points types/source at src/index.ts), so nothing in build-all or verify ever emits their dist/. Fix: add a ts-packages build step to build-all and verify, plus a smoke check in verify that spawns node ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp/dist/index.js and confirms it survives module resolution. title: quarto-yaml: expose content spans for quoted scalars (diagnostics land one column early)
description: Scalar spans in quarto-yaml deliberately include the surrounding quotes (parser.rs test_quoted_scalar_spans_cover_the_whole_scalar). Any diagnostic that composes 'offset into the scalar CONTENT' with that span — e.g. a re-parsed config-markdown string's image-target span (parse_config_string_as_markdown threading the scalar's SourceInfo; see bd-page-footer-image-items-stmpikgo Phase 4) — renders one column early for quoted scalars, since content starts one byte after the opening quote. Escaped scalars would be off by more (escape sequences make the content-to-source mapping non-linear); block scalars differ again. Robust fix: quarto-yaml exposes a content span (or a content-to-source offset map) alongside the whole-scalar span, and q2's substring-composition sites use it. Observed: footer Q-5-6 for a single-quoted page-footer scalar underlines starting at the paren before the URL instead of the URL's first character — right file, right line, one column off. Repro: claude-notes/plans/page-footer-image-items-investigation/repro-missing/ in q2.

title: Migrate remaining destructive write paths onto validated OutputSink
description:
Phase 3 follow-up from bd-cfl67 (render truncates source images). That fix introduced `OutputSink` (crates/quarto-core/src/output_sink.rs), which validates every destination is absolute, lexically clean, and under `allowed_roots`, and skips Copy ops where src == dest. `write_artifacts`/`enqueue_artifacts`, `flush_site_libs`, `ResourceCollectorTransform`, and the pass-2 WASM renderers were migrated onto it. Three write paths were left unmigrated and were never filed as strands at the time (discovered 2026-07-27 during strand cleanup — the plan doc said 'separate beads issues' but none existed):

A1 (MEDIUM) — Migrate `copy_resources_to_output_dir` onto the sink.
A2 (LOW) — Migrate `copy_favicon` / `copy_robots_txt` onto the sink.
A3 (LOW) — Migrate engine intermediate writes onto the sink. Requires a design decision: keep `intermediate_dir` as an allowed root, or lift it under `output_dir/.intermediate/`.

Why it matters: these are the remaining destructive-write paths that bypass the sink's allowed-roots validation — the same class of unguarded write that truncated user-authored images to 0 bytes in bd-cfl67. This is hardening, not a live bug: no known reproduction truncates source files today.

Plan doc: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-render-truncates-source-images.md (Phase 3 checklist, items A1-A3).

title: Review category click-handler encoding scheme (b64+percent-encoding)
description: L5 (bd-5vsr) ships b64(percent-encoded UTF-8) on the Rust encoder side and inherits the matching decodeURIComponent(atob(...)) decoder on the JS side via the vendored quarto-listing.js. The scheme works but inherits Q1's choice without revisiting it. Open questions for the review: (a) is data-category better off carrying the raw category string instead, with the JS reading it directly (no encode/decode pair, simpler in both halves)? (b) if we keep an encoded form, should we move to a single Rust crate's idiom (e.g. base64-only on UTF-8 + matching Rust-style decoder in JS) and drop the percent-encoding round-trip? (c) does any reserved character in category names interact poorly with HTML attribute values, JS string literals, or URL hash routing — and would a different scheme avoid those edge cases? Out of scope for L5 (we want Q1 parity first); file when encoding lands so the discussion isn't lost. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-06-listings-L5-categories-sidebar.md §'Filing reminder' #2.

title: quarto-error-reporting: test_location_in_to_text_with_context fails under --no-default-features
description:
Pre-existing failure in the external repo posit-dev/quarto-error-reporting (not q2).

`cargo test --no-default-features test_location_in_to_text_with_context` fails with `assertion failed: text.contains("2:1")` when NO renderer feature is enabled at all (neither ariadne nor annotate-snippets).

Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to the provenance epic: reproduced at commit 4da3385 (before any of Plan 2 Phase 1's commits, still on quarto-source-map 0.1.0), independently verified twice — once by the implementer of Plan 2 Phase 1 and once by its reviewer in a scratch worktree.

Why nothing caught it: that repo's CI runs `cargo test --locked` (default features) and `cargo test --all-features --locked`, plus clippy on default and --all-features. Plan 2 Phase 1 additionally required clippy on --no-default-features, ariadne-only and annotate-snippets-only, but NOT `cargo test` in those configurations. So the no-renderer test path is unexercised by both CI and the plan.

Two possible fixes, not decided: (a) fix the test so it passes with no renderer (the structured tidyverse text path presumably does not emit "2:1"), or (b) gate the test on `any(ariadne, annotate-snippets)` if asserting a source position is meaningless without a renderer. Worth also considering adding a `cargo test --no-default-features` leg to that repo's CI, since it is a published crate and a consumer can select that configuration.

Discovered while executing claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-2-consumers.md Phase 1 (epic bd-mxa44voa). Out of scope for all three provenance plans.

New regression test website_render_omits_empty_stem_files_dirs in tests/artifact_scoping_pipeline.rs. End-to-end verified across 5 example projects: 0 empty dirs in any _site tree.

title: SCSS cache key hashes the document-relative theme path: 97% miss rate, 78% of q2 render time on the Connect docs
description: compile_theme_css::cache_key hashes theme_context.resolve_path(path).to_string_lossy() for ThemeSpec::Custom. For an extension-bundled theme (posit-docs: theme.scss / theme-dark.scss), project/mod.rs::rebase_fragment_paths turns the path into a ConfigValueKind::Path that the per-document metadata merge rebases to the document dir, so the resolved string (e.g. admin/appendix/cli/../../../_extensions/posit-dev/posit-docs/theme.scss) is unique per directory even though the file and contents are identical. Result on the Connect docs (352 docs, 349 dirs): perf.sass hits=22 compiles=682 (704 variants), ~48 ms/compile, 78% of serial render CPU (samply, compile_theme_css inclusive). The key already hashes the file CONTENTS, so the path component is redundant for identity; fix = drop the path from the hash or canonicalize it (note @import resolution is relative to the theme file's dir, which is the same file either way). Verify with QUARTO_PERF_STATS=1 → perf.sass compiles ≈ number of distinct variants (2–4), hits ≈ 2×docs. Research note: claude-notes/research/2026-09-13-connect-docs-render-profile.md
close_reason: Fixed in PR #679 (4a2d219fe): ThemeContext::resolve_path lexically normalizes, so one custom theme file gets one sass cache key. Connect docs cold serial: 42.0 s -> 6.68 s, compiles 682 -> 2.

title: Surface FormatIdentifier::Custom discriminant in TS engine protocol
description:
TsEngine::execute (Plan 1a Phase 1) asserts !matches!(fmt.identifier, FormatIdentifier::Custom(_)) because Custom(u32).as_str() returns the literal "custom" and drops the u32 discriminant (crates/quarto-core/src/format.rs:44-58). The assert means TS engine extensions cannot run against any custom format.

Resolution path:
- Decide where the per-Custom(u32) format name lives. Either add a registry that maps the discriminant to a name string, or include the discriminant in the protocol via a new field (e.g., add an optional "custom-name" field to TsFormatIdentifier).
- Plumb it through TsFormatIdentifier.base-format (or a sibling) so the harness can pass it to TS engines correctly.
- Remove the assert in TsEngine::execute.

Land before the first custom format ships to production. No urgency today (no in-tree custom formats); urgency rises when a downstream extension defines one.

Context: discovered during Plan 1a editorial review. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-plan1a-protocol-and-core.md ("Custom-format gotcha" in the format.identifier mapping section).

title: Two error-corpus snapshot tests glob a path that matches nothing and silently iterate zero files
description:
test_error_corpus_text_snapshots and test_error_corpus_json_snapshots in crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_error_corpus.rs both build the glob

    let pattern = "resources/error-corpus/*.qmd";   // lines 263 and 340

There are no .qmd files at that path. The corpus's generated case files live one directory deeper, in resources/error-corpus/case-files/ (684 files) -- which is what the sibling test_error_corpus_ariadne_output correctly uses at line 16. Confirmed on the current tree: 'ls crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/*.qmd' returns 'no matches found'.

Both tests therefore iterate an empty set and pass unconditionally. They are green, they are counted in the suite, and they assert nothing. Whatever snapshot coverage they were written to provide has never run.

Impact. These are the two tests that would catch drift in the rendered text and JSON shapes of corpus diagnostics. Their silence was noticed only because a grammar change made someone ask which tests actually guard the error corpus -- the answer is one test, not three.

Fix direction: point the pattern at case-files/ (matching line 16), then deal with whatever the newly-live assertions report -- expect the first run to be noisy, since these snapshots have never been exercised against the current renderer. That second half is the real work and is why this is not a one-line change. A guard against the class of bug would be to assert a non-zero file count before the loop in each of the three corpus tests, so an empty glob fails loudly instead of passing silently.

Found during a blank-slate review of claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-shortcode-naked-string-widening.md, while establishing which tests protect the error corpus against a tree-sitter grammar change. Unrelated to that plan's subject matter; filed separately because it predates it and affects all corpus work.

title: Add 'cargo xtask setup' for fresh clone/worktree bootstrap
description:
Fresh worktrees (and fresh clones) currently fail 'cargo xtask verify' because the hub-client TypeScript build depends on node_modules/ that isn't created by verify. Discovered while bootstrapping the issue-152 worktree on 2026-05-03 — verify ran the WASM build successfully, then hub-client's tsc step failed with 'Cannot find module' for every npm dep until 'npm install' was run manually from the worktree root.

Proposal: introduce 'cargo xtask setup' as a discrete bootstrap verb that runs 'npm install' (and any future first-run prerequisites like rustup component add). Then either:
  (a) have 'verify' detect a missing node_modules/ and exit with 'run cargo xtask setup first', or
  (b) have 'verify' call into the same setup logic when it detects first-run state.

Other large Rust+JS monorepos (Deno, Tauri) keep these separate; rust-analyzer hard-fails with a hint. Keeping 'verify' semantically about checking (not network installs) seems preferable.

Cross-reference: this snag should also be documented in the upcoming triage/diagnose skill (.claude/skills/triage.md, not yet created) so that running the skill on a fresh worktree picks up bootstrap as a prerequisite step. Until 'cargo xtask setup' exists, the skill should explicitly run 'npm install' before 'cargo xtask verify'.

title: q2 preview: figure-labeled engine cells never splice — capture walk was top-level only
description: User-visible symptom: a julia doc whose cell output is a figure renders all TEXT in the q2 preview pane but the plot never appears (Chrome + Firefox), even though the server logs 'recorded engine capture(s)' and the capture bin contains the full figure (data-URI in result.markdown). A cell with '#| label: fig-*' is wrapped in a '::: {#fig-...}' float Div by pre-engine sugaring, so the engine cell is nested; the A1/B1 walk hit two structurally-unequal Divs, stopped fail-soft with an empty cell-output map, and the cell rendered as raw source. PC5/PC6 stayed green because their cells are top-level (no fig label) — exactly the tier gap in claude-notes/research/2026-07-03 (features test green but arrive broken). Fix: recurse into Div content on both the derive side (derive_cell_outputs_walk) and the splice side (splice_blocks_walk), sharing the (hash, occurrence) counter across nesting levels so keys stay in document order. Covers fig floats, callouts, margin/column divs, tabset panels. Tests: unit cell_nested_in_figure_div_splices + nested_and_top_level_cells_share_occurrence_ordering (RED confirmed pre-fix); browser-tier PC6-FIG in q2-preview-spa/e2e/engine-capture-splice-julia.spec.ts asserting a LOADED, laid-out (naturalWidth>0 + non-collapsed rect), QUARTO_PC6_LIVE=1-gated like PC6 (RED against pre-fix binary, GREEN after). title: cargo xtask verify can fail on a stale tree-sitter markdown.dylib build cache
description:
`cargo xtask verify` step 4 ("Testing tree-sitter grammars") can fail with a spurious corpus failure when the gitignored compiled parser is stale. The grammar is fine; the build cache is not.

## Observed 2026-08-12

On a checkout of main whose only modifications were in `crates/quarto-core` (a quarto-core AST transform, plus smoke-all fixtures — nothing under crates/tree-sitter-qmd), verify failed:

    Total parses: 582; successful parses: 581; failed parses: 1
    461. x  5 - multiple punctuation marks
    Error: Tree-sitter grammar tests failed

The failing case is `test/corpus/punctuation-vs-image.txt` ("5 - multiple punctuation marks", input `...`), which expects three pandoc_str nodes and got one.

## It is the cache, not the grammar

- Reproduced with the working tree fully stashed — i.e. on pristine main. So it is not caused by any local edit.
- `git status crates/tree-sitter-qmd/` clean; `tree-sitter generate` produced NO diff, so the committed parser.c is in sync with grammar.js. The grammar source is not the problem.
- After running `tree-sitter generate` (which rewrites parser.c with fresh mtimes and so forces `tree-sitter test` to rebuild), the test passes — 3/3 consecutive runs, `failed parses: 0`.
- The only gitignored artifact in the grammar dir is `markdown.dylib`, the compiled parser. That is the stale input.
- The same commit had passed `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` about 3.5 hours earlier, so the dylib went stale in between. (`--skip-hub-build` does NOT skip step 4; `skip_treesitter_tests` is an independent flag.)

## Why it matters

The failure is indistinguishable, from the operator's seat, from a real grammar regression — and it points at a corpus case the current session never touched, which is maximally confusing. Anyone hitting it will burn time bisecting a grammar they did not change. It also undermines verify as a release gate in the other direction: a stale dylib could in principle mask a real failure.

## Possible fixes

- Have step 4 remove `markdown.dylib` (or run `tree-sitter generate`) before `tree-sitter test`, so the parser is always built from current sources.
- Or determine why `tree-sitter test` (CLI 0.26.8) does not rebuild when it should — this may be an upstream mtime/staleness-detection issue worth reporting rather than papering over.

Prefer understanding the trigger before adding an unconditional rebuild: a forced regenerate on every verify would cost wall-clock on a step that is currently fast.

Environment: macOS (darwin 25.5.0), tree-sitter CLI 0.26.8.
Discovered while verifying bd-v9zs83zj; context in claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-footnotes-appendix-heading.md.

title: TsEngine swallows load/transport failures in claims_language and claims_file (silent no-op, exit 0)
description:
Both dynamic claim verbs on TsEngine discard the error when the engine fails to load or the wire request fails, and answer 'no claim' instead: - crates/quarto-core/src/engine/ts_engine.rs:794 -- claims_language: 'Err(_) => LanguageClaim::None' - crates/quarto-core/src/engine/ts_engine.rs:881 -- claims_file: 'Err(_) => false' Neither pushes a diagnostic (contrast intermediate_files at ts_engine.rs:977, which at least pushes a warning -- though into the never-drained registry.diagnostics; see bd-exhbc6h8). Failure modes: (1) claims_language -- SILENT WRONG OUTPUT. A legacy (claims-less) engine that fails to load claims nothing, so its languages go unowned, resolve_engines returns an empty sequence, and the cells are emitted unexecuted as plain code blocks. Exit 0, no error, no warning. Verified E2E on feature/ts-engine-extensions (HEAD 645845ea2): a scratch project with the legacy-python fixture (whose .js deliberately throws on load) and a '{python}' cell rendered '1 of 1 files' successfully, output containing: 
print("hi")
The user gets a page with their code echoed instead of executed, and nothing anywhere says the engine failed to load. (2) claims_file -- MISLEADING ERROR. A failed load makes the engine answer 'unclaimed'; if no other engine claims the file, EngineClaimsFileStage reports 'Can't determine execution engine for ' -- which points the user at engine *configuration* when the real cause was an engine *load failure*. Note the asymmetry with the static path: a declared 'claims:' / 'claims-files:' answer never loads, so this only bites legacy (undeclared) engines -- exactly the population that is already degraded, and exactly where a diagnostic matters most. Suggested shape: keep answering None/false (resolution must stay infallible and pure), but record the load failure and surface it once per engine per render. Depends on there being a project-grain diagnostic sink to surface it into -- see bd-exhbc6h8, which builds one. TDD note: the legacy-python fixture already fails deliberately on load ('legacy-python.js must never be loaded'), so it is a ready-made harness for a test asserting that a load failure produces a user-visible diagnostic rather than a silent pass-through.
close_reason: Q-16-12 emitted once per engine per render via sticky load_failed OnceLock, which also kills the per-probe retry storm. Commit 8b02c8651.

title: q2-slides/slide thumbnails: pipe table renders as [Table] — add Table case to legacy renderBlock (GH #251)

This strand covers the SPECIFIC fix only: a self-contained case 'Table' in renderBlock, structurally mirroring ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/Table.tsx (caption/thead/tbody/tfoot, alignment, row/col spans) but recursing through the local renderBlock/renderInlines. title: Q-2-35: Reject 4-space indented code blocks with a custom parse error (issue #184)
description:
Indented (4-space) code blocks are currently parsed as paragraphs whose leading whitespace is dropped, corrupting documents on a qmd → qmd round-trip (GH issue #184). Per project policy (https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/184#issuecomment-4426182995) Quarto Markdown does not support indented code blocks; the parser must reject them with a high-quality error message instead.

Approach: mirror the Q-2-32 (TRIPLE_STAR) pattern — emit an external token from scanner.c that is declared in grammar.js but consumed by no rule body, then map the resulting (state, sym) pair through the Merr-style error table in crates/quarto-parse-errors/ to a Q-2-35 diagnostic.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-14-q-2-35-indented-code-block-error.md (TDD, six error-corpus cases including a negative one, full xtask verify, no writer changes).
Triage: claude-notes/issue-reports/184/triage.md
Branch: issue-184 (worktree at .worktrees/issue-184/)
Repro: claude-notes/issue-reports/184/repro.qmd

Scope confirmed with @cscheid (2026-05-14):
- Error fires on >= 4 leftover indentation (after container matchers consume their share), so well-indented list continuations are unaffected but extra-indented ones are flagged.
- Error code Q-2-35.
- Message suggests fenced code blocks (```) as the replacement.
- Documentation note added to tree-sitter-markdown CONTRIBUTING.md mirroring the Q-2-32 precedent.
close_reason: Implemented and verified end-to-end on branch issue-184 (commit e2d224f6). Reporter's repro now produces Q-2-35 diagnostic spanning the full offending line. Full cargo xtask verify (Rust + WASM + hub-client) passes; tree-sitter test 480/480; pampa test suite 3687/3687; xtask lint clean. Conservative detection rule (ATX_H1_MARKER || BLANK_LINE_START) avoids false positives in multi-line shortcodes and lazy paragraph continuations — see the plan doc for the rationale and the rejected alternatives.

title: qmd writer drops empty pipe-table header row, promotes first body row to header (issue #175)
description:
Round-trip bug: pipe table with all-empty header row parses as Table with TableHead [] [] (zero header rows). The qmd writer's write_table path unconditionally emits row_contents[0] as the header line, so it promotes the first body row, and the re-parser then reads that body row as the header. Silent data loss: head$rows goes 0→1 and the body loses a row.

Root cause: crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:1184-1190 (write_table). Predicate table_can_use_pipe_format at lines 870-910 also needs a multi-header guard if the fix touches it.

Fix scope: branch on table.head.rows.is_empty(); when zero, emit a synthetic empty header line (matches pandoc -t gfm) and treat every collected row as body. Add round-trip regression to tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd.

Full triage record: claude-notes/issue-reports/175/triage.md on branch issue-175.
Real-world impact: quarto-web docs/authoring/callouts.qmd, docs/output-formats/all-formats.qmd.
close_reason: Fixed in 9457afe3 on branch issue-175. Adds synthetic empty header row in write_table when table.head.rows is empty; regression fixture pipe_table_empty_header.qmd in qmd-json-qmd/. cargo xtask verify passes.

title: Rich-text editor should handle Plain blocks (tight list items)
description: In format: q2-preview, the tiptap rich-text block editor only activates for a subset of Pandoc block types. RICHTEXT_SUPPORTED_TYPES in ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/richTextSupport.ts is {Para, Header}; it omits Plain. Because tight bullet/ordered lists store each item's content as a Plain block (loose lists use Para), clicking to edit a tight-list item's content resolves a sourceNode of type Plain, richTextAvailable() returns false, and the editor falls back to the monospaced textarea instead of the rich-text surface. Goal: make tight-list item content rich-text editable. The AST->PM converter (astToProseMirror.ts) already maps Plain -> paragraph, so the surface gate is the main blocker, but the commit/round-trip path (does a Plain-block edit re-parse back to a tight Plain, or flip the list to loose Para?) needs verification. TDD tests + E2E verified (text edit round-trips, list stays tight). All 8 CI checks green. Pre-existing bold-commit data-loss tracked separately as bd-hafs0qho.

title: Add webtex/gladtex/mathml/plain math methods
description:
bd-w5ov shipped MathJax + KaTeX. Pandoc and Quarto 1 also support 'webtex' (image rendering), 'gladtex' (alt-text), 'mathml' (pass-through), 'plain' (no rendering). Each has a different output markup contract.

Add these as additional MathEngine variants when there's user demand. Today, an unsupported method falls through to None and the math stage no-ops — the user's HTML still renders, just without typesetting.

Acceptance: extend MathEngine::from_meta() to accept these strings, render appropriate markup in render_math_slot(), and add tests.

title: .quartoignore support in project file discovery
description: Phase 1's discovery walker honors underscore/dot components, README names, output-dir, .quarto/, .git/, node_modules/ — but not a user-provided .quartoignore file. Q1 supports .quartoignore (gitignore-style patterns for files to exclude from render). Implement in crates/quarto-core/src/project/discovery.rs with tests.

title: Q-2-10: suggest \' escape for possessive apostrophes
description:
In Quarto 1 and other permissive Markdown dialects, users write plural possessives like 'Is these users' opinions, ...'. Q2's grammar reads an apostrophe after a word character (followed by a space) as a closing quote with no matching opener and raises Q-2-10 (Closed Quote Without Matching Open Quote). We want to keep the strictness — mismatched quotes must be reported — but this case is common enough that the diagnostic should explicitly suggest escaping the apostrophe as \' (backslash escapes the next character in qmd).

Repro at HEAD: 'Is these users' opinions, for what it's worth.' → [Q-2-10] at the users' apostrophe (col 16). The existing note ('This is the opening quote. If you need an apostrophe, escape it with a backslash.') is worded for the quote-start framing and reads confusingly for the possessive case; 'it's' later in the same line is correctly fine.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-q-2-10-possessive-apostrophe.md
close_reason: Won't fix. Rationale (Carlos): CommonMark uses ambiguous characters (the same ' is both quote mark and apostrophe). CommonMark refuses to emit syntax errors, and so forces a disambiguation that means typos are misinterpreted and leak into output. We want to stay close to CommonMark and believe we can't force people to use different characters for quotes and apostrophes. We want to emit good error messages, but that's impossible here: the attached (users') and detached (users ') shapes fail in the same LR state with the same token, so the parser cannot tell a plural possessive from a stray closing quote. Escaping as \' (or writing U+2019 ’ directly, which the grammar admits as plain text) remains the answer.

c-6gyq34j6.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-6gyq34j6.text: Debug session confirmed: attached (users') and detached (users ') shapes both fail at (state 751, _whitespace) with identical single_quote capture token (lrState 751) — the error table cannot distinguish possessives, so the fix is uniform neutral wording: 'No opening quote was found before this mark. If you meant an apostrophe, escape it with a backslash.' Also found: the note was copied from Q-2-7 where it is accurate; punctuation shape (users'.) routes to Q-2-7, not Q-2-10. Full findings in claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-q-2-10-possessive-apostrophe.md

title: HTML preview stacks a click listener on every internal link per App render; one click fans out into N pushState calls (Firefox 'Too many calls to Location or History APIs')
description: postProcessIframe (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/utils/iframePostProcessor.ts) attaches a fresh per-element click listener to every internal link each time it runs and never removes the previous ones. MorphIframe re-runs it whenever internalPostProcess changes identity, which is every App render (App passes an inline onNavigateToFile arrow to Editor -> handlePreviewFileChange -> Preview.handleNavigateToDocument -> MorphIframe.handleQmdLinkClick). Measured in Chromium via Playwright: 10 Cmd+S presses -> +4 listeners; 25 keystrokes -> +50 listeners (2 per keystroke). A same-file link click with 57 stacked listeners produced 58 history.pushState calls in 216 ms, and because each listener's navigation re-renders App, the click itself doubled the count to 115. Firefox with 212 listeners: 213 pushState calls in 2.4 s from one click. Firefox rate-limits History API calls (200/10 s) and throws 'The operation is insecure' past that, which matches the quarto-hub.com console report of 2026-09-09 (stack: navigateToRoute <- navigateToFile <- onNavigateToFile <- handlePreviewFileChange <- MorphIframe.handleQmdLinkClick <- postProcessIframe click listener). Cross-file clicks are masked in Chromium because the iframe is replaced after the first listener runs. The keydown (Ctrl+S) listener and the injected <style data-hub-client> accumulate the same way. Failing regression test already added: ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/utils/iframePostProcessor.integration.test.ts ('re-running on the same document'). Fix direction: delegated document-level handlers as iframeLinkHandlers.ts already does for q2-preview, or make MorphIframe's post-process identity-stable via refs. title: Rich-text editor remounts (focus blip, caret reset, draft loss) on offset-shifting remote CRDT changes (GH #420)
description: GH https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/420. Diagnosed 2026-08-26 via live q2 preview --allow-edit + chrome devtools. Root cause: on an incoming remote change, PreviewRoot renders the new astJson against the STALE editTarget; the dispatcher's anchor match (editTarget.anchorR0 === resolved.sourceEntry.r[0]) fails for any byte-offset-shifting change, unmounting the RichTextEditor for one render; the P2.3b self-heal useLayoutEffect then re-anchors and a second render mounts a FRESH editor seeded from the AST — focusout/focusin blip (~30ms), caret reset to end, and any uncommitted rich-text edits silently discarded (textarea mode reseeds from the preserved editDraftRef so it only blips; the rich surface loses data). Validated fix: derive the re-anchored target DURING render (findReanchorCandidate in a useMemo over [editTarget, pool, renderedContent]) so the first post-change render already matches and React never unmounts the editor — browser-verified: same DOM node, no focus events, caret + typed draft preserved; full preview-renderer test suite green. Known boundary (follow-up): block insert/delete ABOVE the active block shifts index-based keys (key={i}) and still remounts; remote edits to the ACTIVE block itself still DROP (close) the editor. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-26-gh420-editor-focus-crdt.md
close_reason: Fixed in PR #618 (merged): PreviewRoot derives the re-anchored edit target during render (effectiveEditTarget), so the open editor survives offset-shifting remote CRDT changes — same DOM node, focus/caret/draft preserved. TDD tests in editor-survives-remote-shift.integration.test.tsx; full verify + browser e2e green. Follow-ups: bd-vrdglm6m, bd-yu5uj8am.

Fix proposal: mirror the lib_dir branch in `RenderToHtmlRenderer.render` (Option B in the plan) so default projects flush in-place via the per-page (vfs_root) resolver. title: hub-client: link-project-set boot handler races the collections pointer read (can overwrite connected with needs-setup)

If the pointer read resolves after establishRoot has written the pointer, it sees the pointers and connects (fine); if it resolves before, it sets status to needs-setup/needs-migration while the link action is mid-flight, and its later 'connected' can be clobbered or a second setup path can fire. title: Unify the tiling auditor's two whitespace-exclusion mechanisms
description:
The tightness check now has TWO exclusion mechanisms where one would do, and the seam leaves a gap.

1. A wholesale type skip in audit_inline_siblings (crates/pampa/src/writers/incremental.rs:1367): Space/SoftBreak/LineBreak are skipped before check_tightness is called at all.
2. The text-keyed 'retained' parameter on check_tightness, added for bd-1d6io so a node whose own text keeps the boundary whitespace is not flagged (the abbreviation handler substitutes NBSP into a Str and keeps it).

bd-1d6io's commit message and plan claimed the second GENERALIZES the first. It does not — the wholesale skip is still there, and the two apply in different places. The gap: audit_custom_node's Slot::Inline arm (incremental.rs:1311) has no type skip and goes through inline_retained_text, which returns None for Space. So a Space inside a single-Inline CustomNode slot is still flagged. That gap is pre-existing, not introduced by bd-1d6io, but the new parameter makes it cheap to close.

Proposed: have inline_retained_text return Some(" ") for Space and Some("\n") for SoftBreak/LineBreak, then delete the wholesale matches! skip. One mechanism, and the CustomNode slot gap closes for free.

CAUTION — this is not purely mechanical. The wholesale skip is currently BLIND to a Space claiming NON-whitespace bytes (see bd-riu2dvcf: meta.author.c[1] is a Space with range covering the byte 'e'). A naive Some(" ") only checks that the boundary char is whitespace, so it would inherit the same blindness. Doing this properly means comparing the node's whitespace against what the range actually covers, which is the stricter check the wholesale skip was avoiding. Decide deliberately whether to (a) preserve current permissiveness with one mechanism, or (b) tighten to catch Space-claims-non-whitespace, which may surface existing violations.

Related: check_tightness tests PRESENCE of boundary whitespace, not amount — a Str whose text ends in one NBSP can absorb an unbounded run of trailing source spaces unflagged. Sibling disjointness defends that in depth, so it is not a live hole, but comparing counts would close it directly and belongs in the same pass.

Found during code review of bd-1d6io (branch braid/bd-1d6io-p1-attr-key-tightness).

c-7axzshck.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-7axzshck.text:
Scope reduced: the presence-vs-amount item is DONE, not pending. Commit 5c6e793a8 on braid/bd-1d6io-p1-attr-key-tightness re-keyed the exclusion to the abbreviation NBSP substitution exactly — boundary chars must be U+00A0, in matching quantity with the source space/tab bytes. So a Str whose text ends in one NBSP can no longer absorb an unbounded run of trailing spaces: 2 spaces against 1 NBSP is now reported. Tested both directions.

What REMAINS in this strand: the two mechanisms are still two (the wholesale Space/SoftBreak/LineBreak type skip at incremental.rs:1367 plus the own_text parameter), and the CustomNode Slot::Inline gap is still open. The caution in the original description stands — the wholesale skip is deliberately blind to a Space claiming NON-whitespace bytes, so unifying is a semantic decision, not a mechanical one.

title: q2 over-requires Q1-optional _extension.yml fields (author, title?) → Q1 extensions silently fail to load
description: q2's extension-manifest reader (crates/quarto-core/src/extension/read.rs) hard-requires title (~L79), author (~L90), and contributes (~L111). Q1 (quarto-cli) requires none of these by name in readExtension/validateExtension: it reads title/author leniently and enforces only that contributes yields >=1 non-empty contribution plus the quarto-required semver check. So an otherwise-valid Q1-era extension whose _extension.yml omits author (confirmed: e.g. julia-engine, marimo) fails read_extension -> Err, and discover.rs logs only a WARN and skips it; the engine/filter never registers and the document renders as raw code, misattributed to the user's doc. author is required-but-unused in q2 (nothing production reads Extension.author). Introduced in 68420002b (2026-03-16) by transcribing TS Quarto's documented field list into required status, though TS Quarto never enforced it. Fix: audit all over-required fields (top-level + nested), then relax them to match Q1's leniency while keeping contributes-non-empty required (Q1-faithful). TDD via prevalidating-test-seams; flip test_read_extension_missing_title if title is confirmed over-required.

c-4j7j1e4l.author: Gordon Woodhull

title: Design note: TS-engine wire lacks a positive 'languages assigned to you' signal (engines must infer ownership from the leave-alone handledLanguages complement)
description: Discovered during plan-4c 4cB2 (compat doc §13). handledLanguages in TsExecuteOptions is the leave-alone set (HANDLED_LANGUAGES ∪ langs-owned-by-others, resolution.rs:292). An engine executing a presence-gated Interop language (marimo bare-sql, the first such feature) must infer 'I own lang' as !handledLanguages.includes(lang) — sound today because resolution assigns every present language an owner or hard-fails before execute, but implicit. Consider a positive ownedLanguages/assignedLanguages wire field for clarity, or pin the complement semantics in engine-resolution.md §5 + the extension-author guide. The inversion bug this caused (4c0-eng used includes() as positive ownership; feature never fired) shows the trap is real for engine authors.
