title: Precise cross-engine source attribution in EngineExecutionStage
description: EngineExecutionStage threads the document's top-level source_context (constant) to every engine for error attribution. This is exact for engine 1; for engine 2+, offsets into content produced by an earlier engine don't resolve (their FileIds live only in the merged ASTContext), so error mapping is best-effort (None = no precise location). Matches the existing single-engine code's stated tolerance. A future refinement could thread the accumulating merged context. See engine_execution.rs run loop comment.

c-1h9zaydp.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-1h9zaydp.text: TS-engine-extensions epic shares this exact gap and folds the fix in. TS engines inherit the same engine-2+ attribution problem: the source_map q2 sends an engine at sequence position k is built from serialize_ast_to_qmd of the post-engine-(k-1) AST, whose blocks carry intermediate-slot FileIds that don't resolve against the document's source_context -- identical to the built-in engine-2+ case this strand describes. The rebase plans (plan1c / plan0 source machinery) treat this as one problem: thread the accumulating merged ASTContext into each engine's per-position source_map so engine-k offsets resolve, designed ONCE for built-in and TS engines rather than twice. See claude-notes/designs/engine-resolution.md §11 and §13. This strand's 'future refinement (thread the accumulating merged context)' is the shared fix.

title: L1 listings: filter unresolved shortcodes in image-src auto-fill
description: ListingItemInfoStage (bd-izqh) runs after IncludeExpansionStage but BEFORE PreEngineSugaringStage. An Image node whose original src was a shortcode like '{{< meta thumbnail >}}.png' will still carry that literal text in target.0 at L1 time. L1 currently does not filter such cases when picking the first body image. When listings consume this field (L3+), unresolved shortcode markup could leak into rendered listings as the . Investigate: - Real-world cases where image src is set via shortcode (Q1 examples worth grepping). - Whether the literal markers are limited to '{{<' / '>}}' or whether other deferred-substitution forms (e.g. '$var$') also reach this point. - Whether pre-engine sugaring resolves these in time for L1's data to be useful, or whether shortcode-bearing images need their own pass. - Resolution choice: skip such images entirely (use second image, or none); or store the unresolved form and have L3 strip; or wait for sugaring before extracting. Out of scope: L1 itself. This issue is the dedicated study; no behavior change in bd-izqh.

title: QMD writer's Concat pairs source spans with written byte lengths — engine source maps drift on every multi-block document
description:
Discovered by the Plan 3 Phase 5 characterization probe (T4),
`probe_build_source_map_over_writer_concat` in
`crates/quarto-core/src/engine/ts_engine.rs` (currently `#[ignore]`d,
pointing here).

## The defect

`write_impl_tracked` (`crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:2876-2903`) builds its
`SourceInfo::Concat` by pushing, for each top-level block,

    pieces.push((block.source_info().clone(), buf.len() - start));

i.e. it pairs each block's **source** span with the number of bytes the writer
**wrote**. Piece lengths therefore live in written-QMD coordinates while the
spans they are paired with live in original-source coordinates. `map_offset`
locates the right piece and then recurses with a *local* offset that is only
meaningful if the writer reproduced the block byte-for-byte.

That `Concat` is what `serialize_ast_to_qmd`
(`crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs:729-732`) returns and
what `engine_execution.rs:467` installs as `ExecutionContext::source_info`
alongside the written QMD as the engine `input`. Two production consumers map
offsets against it:

- `build_source_map` (`quarto-core/src/engine/ts_engine.rs:683`) — the wire
  source map handed to TS engines; its doc comment promises each entry's
  `source` is "the line's start offset in `input`" resolved "to its original
  file + byte offset". The Julia engine's `buildSourceRanges` consumes this.
- `describe_location` (`quarto-core/src/engine/jupyter/text_execute.rs:494`) —
  renders `path:line:column` in jupyter diagnostics.

## Measured (2026-08-23, this branch)

Two independent drift mechanisms, isolated by running the same chain over a
non-identity fixture and an identity control.

Fixture `"Intro paragraph.\n\n  - alpha\n  - beta\n  - gamma\n\nOutro.\n"` (55
bytes). Writer emits 49 bytes, rewriting each `  - x` to `* x`:

    line 0 "Intro paragraph." @ 0  -> reported 0  | true 0
    line 1 ""                 @ 17 -> reported 18 | true 17
    line 2 "* alpha"          @ 18 -> reported 19 | true 18
    line 3 "* beta"           @ 26 -> reported 27 | true 28
    line 4 "* gamma"          @ 33 -> reported 34 | true 37
    line 5 ""                 @ 41 -> reported 48 | true 47
    line 6 "Outro."           @ 42 -> reported 49 | true 48

Identity control `"Intro paragraph.\n\n* alpha\n* beta\n* gamma\n\nOutro.\n"`
(writer round-trips it byte-for-byte, verified with `cmp`):

    line 0 @ 0  -> 0  | true 0
    line 1 @ 17 -> 18 | true 17
    line 2 @ 18 -> 19 | true 18
    line 3 @ 26 -> 27 | true 26
    line 4 @ 33 -> 34 | true 33
    line 5 @ 41 -> 42 | true 41
    line 6 @ 42 -> 43 | true 42

So:

1. **Constant +1 on every block after the first**, present even under a
   byte-identical round trip. `write_impl_tracked` writes the separator
   `writeln!` *inside* the measured piece ("include preceding blank line in
   measurement") but pairs it with a span that starts at the block's first
   content byte, so every local offset in the piece is one too high.
2. **Accumulating drift inside a normalized block**, present only under a
   non-identity fixture: +1, -1, -3 across the three list items, stepping by
   -2 per item — exactly the two bytes each `  - ` -> `* ` rewrite removes.

## Scope

This is a **writer-provenance** defect, a different bug class from the
decoded-vs-raw-span family the provenance epic (bd-mxa44voa) is fixing;
`ProvenanceBuilder` does not address it (see
`claude-notes/research/2026-08-21-provenance-audit-findings.md` § 6, "The
engine `map_offset` pair"). It was deliberately left unfixed by Plan 3 Phase 5,
which only characterized it.

## Reproduce

    cargo nextest run -p quarto-core --run-ignored all \
      -E 'test(probe_build_source_map_over_writer_concat)' --no-capture

The test prints the full measurement table and lists every drifted line.

c-axifcrbt.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-axifcrbt.text:
**Correction to comment c-bl1zsr0x, and an additional exposure the fixer must handle.**

**1. The ground I gave for the jupyter site was wrong.** c-bl1zsr0x said the two
consumers "make the identical `info.map_offset(offset, &ctx.source_context)`
call against the same `ExecutionContext` provenance … differing only in
rendering `row`/`column` vs `offset`". That is stronger than the code supports.

`describe_location` is **never called on `ctx.source_info` itself.** Its three
call sites — `crates/quarto-core/src/engine/jupyter/text_execute.rs:314`,
`:315`, `:339` — pass either `body_source`, built at `:305-309` as

    SourceInfo::substring(ctx.source_info.clone(),
                          block.code_start,
                          block.code_start + block.code.len())

or a YAML error's `e.location()` derived from that same `body_source`, and
**always with `offset: 0`**. So the receiver is a *derived* `Substring` queried
at a fixed zero offset, not the provenance at arbitrary offsets.

The conclusion is unchanged — a `Substring` whose bounds are written-QMD
coordinates, taken over a `Concat` whose piece lengths are written but whose
spans are source, inherits the drift — but the corrected ground is: **"a
`SourceInfo::substring` of the same `ExecutionContext` provenance
(`text_execute.rs:305-309`), always at offset 0."**

**2. An ADDITIONAL exposure at the jupyter site, which "verify both consumers"
does not convey.** `block.code_start` is itself a **written-coordinate** bound.
It comes from `parse_code_blocks` (`text_execute.rs:124-147`), which regex-scans
the engine `input` — i.e. the QMD the writer emitted — and stores
`code_start: code_match.start()` (`:147`). That offset is then used directly as a
`Substring` bound over `ctx.source_info`, whose spans are in *original-source*
coordinates.

So the jupyter path has **two** coordinate-space mismatches stacked, not one:
the `Concat` mismatch this strand is about, plus a `Substring` whose bounds are
in the wrong space to begin with. Fixing `write_impl_tracked` alone will not
make `describe_location` correct; the `Substring` construction at `:305-309`
needs its own treatment. Note also that `describe_location` renders
`mapped.location.row`/`.column`, so a wrong offset inside a multi-line block can
land on a plausible-looking but wrong row rather than failing visibly.

**Still measured only on `build_source_map`.** Everything above is from reading
call sites, not from running the jupyter path. What would demonstrate it: a
probe against `describe_location` over the same non-identity fixture, asserting
the rendered `path:line:column` names the line the cell text actually came from.

c-bl1zsr0x.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-bl1zsr0x.text:
Two clarifications from the Plan 3 Phase 5 review (2026-08-23).

**1. `describe_location` was reasoned about, not exercised.** The measurements
in the description come from `build_source_map`
(`quarto-core/src/engine/ts_engine.rs:683`) only. The claim that
`describe_location` (`quarto-core/src/engine/jupyter/text_execute.rs:494`)
surfaces the same drift is a **code-reading argument**: both sites make the
identical `info.map_offset(offset, &ctx.source_context)` call against the same
`ExecutionContext` provenance — installed once at
`stage/stages/engine_execution.rs:467` — and then
`ctx.source_context.get_file(mapped.file_id)`; `describe_location` differs only
in rendering `mapped.location.row`/`.column` where `build_source_map` renders
`mapped.location.offset`. That argument was **not** mechanically demonstrated,
and a second probe was deliberately declined rather than adding a second red
`#[ignore]`d test for an already-measured upstream fact.

**Whoever fixes this must verify both consumers.** What would demonstrate the
jupyter half: a probe against `describe_location` over the same non-identity
fixture, asserting the rendered `path:line:column` names the line the text
actually came from. Note it consumes `row`/`column`, not `offset`, so a fix
that corrects byte offsets still needs checking there — a wrong offset inside a
multi-line block can land on a plausible-looking but wrong row.

**2. Title/priority now reflect mechanism 1's reach.** The original title said
"drift within a block", which undersold it. Mechanism 1 — the constant +1 from
the separator `writeln!` being measured into the piece but not into the span —
fires on **every block after the first in every multi-block document fed to an
engine**, whether or not the writer normalizes anything; the identity control
in the description shows it with zero normalization. Mechanism 2 (the
accumulating -2/item) is the narrower half and needs a rewritten block. Retitled
accordingly and raised to priority 1.

Mechanism 1 looks like a one-line off-by-one, but it was deliberately not fixed
as a drive-by inside a characterization task: `write_impl_tracked` is a `pampa`
writer with other consumers, and any fix needs its own tests plus the
both-consumers check above.

title: attach_config_source's read-and-register may be dead weight: MetadataMergeStage already pre-registers every candidate it can name
description:
Design question surfaced while executing claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-2-consumers.md Phase 3 (epic bd-mxa44voa). Not a bug; out of scope for all three provenance plans.

MEASURED: `bind_source_candidates` (crates/quarto-core/src/config_sources.rs) reads the candidate file and registers its content into the SourceContext when the id matches. For the plain project-config case this branch appears to be dead weight, because `MetadataMergeStage` (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/metadata_merge.rs:308-350) ALREADY pre-registers _quarto.yml's content unconditionally, under the same filename-hash FileId, earlier in the pipeline, for every candidate `attach_config_source` can ever be given (config_path, profile_config_paths, dir_layer paths, extension_manifest_paths). That registration survives into RenderOutput.source_context and hence into the coalesced group's source_context, so `ctx.get_file(file_id)` succeeds at print time whether or not the binder ever succeeded.

HOW IT WAS FOUND: Plan 2 Phase 3 predicted that threading YAML content provenance would make per-page config diagnostics Concat-backed, so `bind_source_candidates`' opening `resolve_byte_range()?` would return None, the config file would never be registered, and the diagnostic would render with NO SOURCE SNIPPET. The fix (use `root_file_id()` instead, which handles Concat and Substring{parent: Concat}, and which the renderer itself already uses at quarto-error-reporting diagnostic.rs:819/:1022) is correct and has landed. But the predicted SYMPTOM does not manifest: the CLI fixture passed pre-fix. Instrumenting the binder confirmed resolve_byte_range() really does return None and the binder really does register nothing — the snippet renders anyway, because of the pre-registration above.

THE QUESTION: does `attach_config_source` still need to do its own read-and-register at all, or could a candidate arise that MetadataMergeStage does not cover?
- If the masking is INTENTIONAL defence-in-depth, it is undocumented as such, and a comment at both sites would stop the next person concluding one of them is redundant.
- If it is NOT intentional, the binder's registration branch may be removable, or MetadataMergeStage's pre-registration may be broader than it needs to be.

Either way the two mechanisms currently overlap without either referencing the other, which is how a future narrowing of one silently changes the behaviour of the other. Suspected origin of the pre-registration: bd-mg3ckvp7 Phase 4 / bd-r64mj1aa.

NOTE the Plan 2 work left a CLI end-to-end fixture in place specifically as a standing guard: if MetadataMergeStage's pre-registration is ever narrowed, that call path starts depending on the root_file_id() fix for real, and the fixture should catch it.

title: Writer: emit `\'` for apostrophes in letter+whitespace context (issue #201)
description:
qmd writer drops the `\'` escape on apostrophes that the reader would re-reject as a smart-quote open. Round-trip qmd → AST → qmd produces output that fails to re-parse with Q-2-10.

Triage: claude-notes/issue-reports/201/triage.md (on branch issue-201).
Worktree: .worktrees/issue-201
GitHub: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/201

Fix scope (per triage):

1. TDD: add roundtrip fixture under crates/pampa/tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/ — e.g. apostrophe_before_space.qmd containing 'reveal.js\' jump-to-slide.'. Confirm it fails at HEAD.
2. Implement: extend write_str / write_inline in crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs (1379, 1414, 2159) to emit '\'' instead of bare '\'' when the char to the left in the Str body is a Unicode letter AND the next char the writer would emit is ASCII whitespace (Space / SoftBreak / etc.).
3. Verify: cargo nextest run --workspace; round-trip the two quarto-web fixtures cited in the issue through 'pampa -t qmd | pampa' cleanly.

Out of scope: reader changes; over-escaping safe contractions like project's, can't.

the theme JS is loaded). The q2-preview SPA doesn't ship Bootstrap
JS, so this needs a React-side state hook:

\`\`\`tsx
const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(!startsCollapsed);
// onClick handler on header that flips expanded
// className toggles 'show' based on expanded
// header gets aria-expanded={expanded}
\`\`\`

Discovered during: callout class-vocabulary alignment (claude-notes/
plans/2026-05-22-callout-class-vocabulary-fix.md). Explicitly scoped
out of that plan — Phase 3 emits the markup but no interactive
state. UX: minor — most q2-preview users see the body open by
default (the common case in TS Quarto fixtures is \`collapse=\"false\"\`
or no collapse attr at all).

title: Audit all hand-written scanners for non-ASCII byte handling
description: Audit *every* hand-written scanner in the workspace for predicates that reject or misclassify non-ASCII bytes. Output: a table in the plan doc. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-unicode-whitespace-handling.md. Discovered from bd-rmx3.

title: [websites] Refactor compile_theme_css cache_key to a structured CompileInputs value type
description:
Background: Phase 2 of bd-k8y0 (sidebar vertical border) extended cache_key in CompileThemeCssStage to hash doc-derived SCSS variables in addition to theme config + custom file contents + minified flag. Hand-assembling these hash inputs is fragile: future ports (sidebar bg/fg, navbar bg/fg, footer bg/fg, brand colors, ...) each have to remember to add their input to BOTH the compile call AND the cache key. Forgetting one path produces a silently stale cache (the regression class that motivated the SCSS_RESOURCES_HASH + CSS_BUILD_ID work).

Proposed shape: introduce a CompileInputs struct that holds every piece of state that affects the compiled CSS (theme_config, doc_vars, minified, future fields). compile_with_doc_vars takes &CompileInputs; cache_key takes the same. Adding a new input is a single struct field, and the type system enforces both sites see it.

Alternative considered: hash the assembled SCSS string directly. Rejected because assemble-failure paths become awkward and we'd assemble even on the cache-hit-precompute path.

Pre-req: bd-k8y0 (Phases 1-4) lands first. Plan reference: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-sidebar-vertical-border.md (see 'Code-quality flag' section in Phase 2).

title: Thread title source_info onto DocumentProfile for nav-text ValueSource anchors
description:
Plan 6 Phase 5 (claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md) fixes three ConfigValue navigation sites (sidebar_generate.rs:228, sidebar_auto.rs:311, navigation_enrich.rs:59) that build sidebar/navbar entries from DocumentProfile.title. Plan 6 ships them with Generated{by: nav_text, from: smallvec![]} (empty from) because DocumentProfile.title is currently Option<String> with no source-info link.

This follow-up adds the source-info threading so those sites can attach an Anchor::value_source(title_source_info) anchor, enabling proper attribution back to the source qmd's title metadata bytes (e.g. a sidebar entry can be git-blamed back to the frontmatter line that produced it).

## Scope

1. Add title_source_info: Option<SourceInfo> field to DocumentProfile (crates/quarto-core/src/document_profile.rs:271+, also the Default impl at :487).
   - Use #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] — same pattern as `order: Option<i32>`.
   - NO DOCUMENT_PROFILE_VERSION bump required (additive Option<_> with default; per document-profile-contract §"Serialization and versioning").
   - Update the contract's §Change log.

2. Update DocumentProfile::extract (line 529): replace `title: plain_text_field(meta, "title")` with code that also captures `meta.get("title")?.source_info.clone()`. Either:
   - Add a sibling helper `fn plain_text_field_with_source(meta, key) -> (Option<String>, Option<SourceInfo>)`, or
   - Inline the two-field extraction at the call site.

3. Update the three Plan-6 Phase-5 consumer sites to read both fields and attach the ValueSource anchor when title_source_info is Some:
   - sidebar_generate.rs:228
   - sidebar_auto.rs:311 (only when reading from profile.title; the file-stem fallback at :318 keeps `from: smallvec![]`)
   - navigation_enrich.rs:59

4. Test: extend Plan 6's multi-page audit-completion fixture to assert that nav-text ConfigValues built from profile.title carry a ValueSource anchor whose source_info chain-walks to the source qmd's title metadata range.

## Out of scope

- subtitle, description, date, image, etc. (not consumed by nav sites today; can be added when needed).
- Inline-rich titles (title: "**Bold**" → ConfigValue::PandocInlines). Today plain_text_field handles only flat strings; this follow-up preserves that contract.

## Why a follow-up, not part of Plan 6

Plan 6 is already ~1150 LOC across 7 phases. This is forward-compatible — once the field lands, the three Phase-5 sites get an extra ValueSource anchor without changing their by-kind or stamping shape. Small enough to be a single self-contained PR.

## Estimated scope

~30-50 LOC + 1 fixture extension. No version bump, no contract semantics change.

title: quarto-brand BrandMeta rejects spec-legal extra meta fields (description, founded, custom keys)
description: Found during GH #581 triage while checking whether brand.meta needs exclusion from the PlainString annotation. The brand-yml spec (https://posit-dev.github.io/brand-yml/brand/meta.html) says 'Both name and link are optional fields, and you can add additional fields as needed for your specific use case', and its comprehensive example includes meta.description (block scalar prose) and meta.founded. q2's BrandMeta (crates/quarto-brand/src/types.rs:104-112) is #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] with only name+link, so a spec-legal brand fails to deserialize: 'inline brand block: unknown field description, expected name or link'. Reproduced via _quarto.yml (the currently-working path) at main 05b6fd75c; fixture: claude-notes/issue-reports/581/exp-meta/ on branch issue-581. Fix sketch: capture unknown meta fields via #[serde(flatten)] map (or drop deny_unknown_fields on BrandMeta only) so extra fields round-trip; no consumer reads them today.

title: qmd writer emits a numeric-prefixed shortcode arg bare, which re-parses as a fatal Q-2-34
description:
shortcode_string_looks_like_number (crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:2279) tests whether the WHOLE string is a number, so a value that merely STARTS with digits is judged not-number-like and emitted without quotes. On re-parse, shortcode_number's token(prec(3, ...)) (grammar.js:706) wins on lexical precedence over the naked-string token and matches the leading digits, splitting the value and erroring.

Measured round-trip:

    {{< kbd "800px" >}}   --(pampa -t qmd)-->   {{< kbd 800px >}}   --(re-parse)-->   fatal Q-2-34

So the writer produces output its own parser rejects: a document that round-trips through 'pampa -t qmd' acquires a hard parse error it did not have.

PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by the naked-string widening. The old ASCII allowlist already admitted [A-Za-z0-9], and neither shortcode_string_looks_like_number nor shortcode_number is touched by branch braid/bd-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-2u79bqp1-shortcode-escaped-gt (commits e223edd52..2477d2816). Found by that branch's final whole-branch review while probing writer/grammar agreement; confirmed identical on main.

Why it is worth tracking now: that branch's new doc comment on is_shortcode_naked_char says the predicate 'mirrors the blocklist in grammar.js'. The mirror is CHARACTER-CLASS-ONLY -- it does not model lexical precedence between competing tokens, which is what this bug turns on. A reader trusting that sentence would conclude the writer can never emit unparseable output, which is not true.

Suggested fix direction: make the quoting decision consider whether shortcode_number would match a PREFIX of the value, not only the whole value. A caveat on the doc comment should land with it.

title: HTML title block renders structured authors as boolean garbage ('truetrue')
description: With a structured author list (name/orcid/email/affiliations maps), the full HTML template's $author$ variable flattens the config maps and emits 'truetrue' (boolean leaf values concatenated) in the quarto-title-meta-contents div. Repro: render a qmd with two structured authors (one with corresponding: true) via cargo run --bin q2 -- render. Root cause: template.rs excludes author from RICH_TITLE_BLOCK_FIELDS and config_value_to_template_value stringifies map leaves. Will be fixed properly by the author-model phase of bd-gx9cic8z.

Fixed in title-block P1 (bd-tezzk9vp): AuthorsNormalizeTransform derives by-author (name.literal per entry) + author-meta; the title block renders one

per author name and the head emits one per author. Boolean garbage gone; regression tests: metadata/authors.rs corresponding_bool_does_not_leak, authors_normalize.rs structured_authors_produce_names_not_booleans, smoke-all title-block/rich-authors.qmd (must-NOT-match truetrue). Full structured model (orcid/email/affiliations) still lands in P2 bd-ez0hiowa.

title: hub: --allowlist-file with live reload (no-restart allowlist updates)
description:
Requested by the quarto-hub.com deployment (quarto-hub-deployment repo, strand bd-qglf7ckq there; plan .claude/plans/2026-08-28-allowlist-updates-without-redeploy.md in that repo). Today the deployment passes --allowed-emails/--allowed-domains/--additional-audiences as CLI flags generated from /etc/quarto-hub/allowlist.yml by a shell script; the lists live in AuthConfig inside AuthState, installed into a OnceLock on HubContext (context.rs), so every allowlist change requires a process restart. Enforcement is already per-request (check_allowlists_for on session claims, context.rs), so if the process could see a new list, changes would bite instantly with zero connection churn.

PROPOSAL: add --allowlist-file <path> accepting the deployment's existing YAML schema (allowed_domains / allowed_emails / additional_audiences). Live-reload ONLY allowed_emails + allowed_domains: hold them in a swappable cell (e.g. arc_swap::ArcSwap<Allowlists>) read by check_allowlists_for; reload via a periodic mtime/hash check task (or SIGHUP). Keep additional_audiences startup-only: it is baked into the jsonwebtoken Validation::set_audience inside the decoder at build_auth_state_from_parts (auth.rs) and also feeds validate_azp_and_iat via AuthState::audiences(); live-reloading it means rebuilding the decoder — not worth it, audience changes are rare and can keep the restart path.

DESIGN POINTS TO GET RIGHT: (1) Fail closed on reload: a missing, unreadable, or invalid file must keep the last-good lists and log loudly — it must NEVER widen to the 'no allowlists = allow all verified users' semantics that absent flags mean today. Decide startup semantics for a bad file too (refuse to start seems right). (2) Precedence: if --allowlist-file is given, it supersedes --allowed-emails/--allowed-domains (error on combining, probably); existing flags stay for compat. (3) Workspace already has serde_yaml 0.9 for parsing. (4) Tests: unit tests for the swap + fail-closed reload; integration suite already covers allowlist behavior (tests/integration/session_auth.rs, auth_bearer.rs) — add a reload-takes-effect test. (5) Deployment follow-up (their repo, not here): systemd unit switches to --allowlist-file, quarto-hub-read-allowlist script retires for emails/domains.

title: Warn when two headings carry the same explicit {#id}
description: Follow-up from bd-duplicate-heading-ids-mou5z7ux (design decision 4, 2026-08-18): the include-boundary dedup fix deliberately never renames author-written ids, and today nothing warns when two explicit {#id} attributes collide (invalid HTML, ambiguous anchors/TOC targets). Implementation sketch: AttrSourceInfo.id is Some(source-span) exactly when the author wrote the id (qmd writer precedent at crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:647-649), so a collision among attr_source.id.is_some() headers is detectable with source locations for both occurrences. Emit a warning diagnostic (new Q-* code required — catalog entry + docs/errors page in the same commit per the error-docs-page-missing lint). Decide during design whether the check lives in the reader's postprocess (per-file) or document-level after include expansion (catches cross-include collisions too; likely both-worthy). Also decide whether non-header explicit ids (divs, spans) are in scope.

title: Dangling index entry on playground: file doc never synced to hub (silent offline creation in another client)
description: /cscheid/hello-claude.qmd in playground SNHcgVzUkWpGFmcxkCkpCDfFtmu maps to automerge:3HJoqsM56QxwVmMNnsjkjoE6Mwcr, which is absent from the hub's storage (verified: no JoqsM* in /mnt/hub-data/automerge/3H/ at 2026-06-12 15:35Z) while the index entry IS on the hub. Same bug class as bd-xnmd5ni1 (index update synced, file doc never pushed) but exhibited by a different client — hub-client browser or the autosync R app (charlie.gao's peers were first to request the missing doc at 15:31:21Z). Need: how the file was created (Carlos/Charlie), whether the creating session can still push it (IndexedDB cache), and an audit of doc-creation paths in hub-client/amsync for the offline-creation race.
close_reason: Resolved 2026-06-12 ~17:15Z by Path B surgery (Carlos-approved): dangling entry /cscheid/q2-mcp-hello.qmd removed from the playground index via authenticated raw automerge edit (storage backed up first: hub-data-backup-20260612T165936Z.tgz instance+local); verified absent from a fresh connection; connect_project lists 27 files; hello-claude.qmd (never actually lost — hidden by the project brick) read and edited normally afterward. Root cause was NOT browser durability: bd-10deu8h4 (MCP server exit races outbound sync). Doctor tool (bd-10bdjmjb Phase 1.5) remains the standing guard against recurrence.

c-hkabhg1g.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-hkabhg1g.text: MECHANISM CONFIRMED 2026-06-12: hello-claude.qmd's doc is STILL absent from hub storage after the creator profile hard-refreshed and reconnected online — docs created during the offline-fallback window are never (re)announced to the hub on reconnect, while the index entry (changes to an already-synced doc) does propagate. This is how dangling index entries are minted. Repro recipe for the fix's red test: sync-client session, peerTimeoutMs=1 against a slow-to-connect hub, create file during fallback, let peer connect, assert hub storage receives the doc (fails today). Recovery for the specific doc: if the creating session's IndexedDB still holds it, a re-announce fix or devtools extraction recovers it; else recreate + remove the dangling index entry.

title: Headings inside a blockquote leak into the TOC (Q1 excludes them)
description:
Found while investigating bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7. Same root cause, different container.

A '#### Heading' written inside a blockquote appears in q2's nav#TOC; Q1 excludes it.

Probe: claude-notes/plans/tabset-headings-in-toc-investigation/div-toc-probe/ (render with both, compare nav#TOC data-scroll-target ids). q2 @ 5b6774d1 emits real-heading-one, plain-div, heading-inside-a-plain-div, callout, blockquote, heading-inside-a-blockquote, real-heading-two; Q1 emits the same minus heading-inside-a-blockquote.

MECHANISM. Pandoc's TOC is exactly the section tree: makeSections does not descend into BlockQuote, so the header stays a bare Header and sectionToListItem (which matches only Div(_,_,Header:rest)) never sees it. q2's collect_toc_entries (crates/pampa/src/toc.rs:341) has an explicit Block::BlockQuote arm that recurses, and its Block::Header arm then collects the bare header.

SCOPE. Falls out for free if bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7 takes direction (B) (make collect_toc_entries walk only the section tree). Under direction (A) (narrow panel-tabset skip) it needs its own two-line fix — delete the BlockQuote arm. This is design question 3 in claude-notes/plans/2026-08-18-tabset-headings-in-toc.md; close as duplicate if that strand absorbs it.
close_reason: Absorbed by bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7 Phase 3: the BlockQuote arm was removed from collect_toc_entries, so a quoted heading is no longer collected. Regression tests: smoke-all toc-containers/blockquote-heading-not-in-toc.qmd and the unit tests test_blockquote_heading_is_not_collected (toc.rs) / test_sectionize_does_not_descend_into_blockquote (sectionize.rs).

title: quarto-cache IndexedDB (wasm-js-bridge cache.js) accumulates per ephemeral preview origin
description: ts-packages/wasm-js-bridge/src/cache.js (Rust WASM-driven SASS/artifact cache, called from quarto-system-runtime/src/wasm.rs) always opens a 'quarto-cache' IndexedDB. Every q2 preview session is a fresh origin, so these DBs accumulate (LRU-capped at 200 entries/50MB per origin, but never cleaned). Affects the viewer SPA too — pre-existing, not covered by bd-sw4xy1vw's ephemeral storage mode (that covered the automerge + quarto-hub DBs). Fix needs a WASM-side config bit or a JS-global switch threaded into whatever realm runs the WASM (main frame/worker/iframe). E2E: indexedDB.databases() empty in editor and viewer sessions across boot+reload. All suites + xtask verify green.

title: Warning suppression v1 follow-ups: validation, rot control, --show-suppressed, wider coverage
description:
Deferred scope from the v1 warning-suppression mechanism shipped for bd-lone-bracket-diagnostic-mxu41qbt (plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-warning-suppression-and-lone-bracket-diagnostic.md).

v1 ships a per-code `diagnostics:` map with a single level (`off`), resolved in MetadataMergeStage from merged metadata and applied in run_pipeline (the one seam every per-document diagnostic passes through, for every frontend). Carlos chose 'minimal suppression + Q-2-49 together', deferring the following:

1. Unknown-code validation. Suppressing a code that is not in error_catalog.json is currently silent. Q2 has no config schema layer (see render.rs:894), so a typo'd code looks exactly like a suppression that failed. Needs its own Q-code.

2. Unused-suppression reporting. A code suppressed but never fired should get an info diagnostic ('remove it'). Must be project-render-only: on a single-file render a project-wide suppression legitimately will not fire. This is the main defense against suppression lists rotting into graveyards.

3. --show-suppressed (or --no-suppress): CLI escape hatch reporting everything, for audit and CI.

4. Per-path globs: `Q-2-49: {level: off, files: ['legacy/**']}`.

5. Per-line suppression (a `<!-- quarto: allow Q-2-49 -->` comment). Needs comment-to-node attachment that does not exist today, but HTML comments now survive as RawInline, so it is reachable.

6. Project-scoped diagnostic coverage. ProjectRenderSummary::project_diagnostics and the eprintln! config-diagnostic path at render.rs:897 do not flow through run_pipeline and are therefore not suppressible. Note this is NOT the same as 'suppression in _quarto.yml does not work' -- that works, because project config is merge layer 1 of the per-document merge.

7. An xtask lint requiring .with_code on new DiagnosticMessage::warning/::error, so the uncoded-warning gap stops growing while bd-m2w7a drains it. Carlos did not select this for v1.

8. Additional levels beyond `off` (`warning`, `error`), i.e. per-code strictness. The config shape was chosen as a per-code map specifically to make this reachable without a competing key.

Also see the separate deferral of re-keying qmd-syntax-helper's literal-brackets rule to q_2_49.rs (documented in the plan).

title: Mermaid diagram styling/theming parity with Quarto 1 (mermaid.css, embed-mermaid.css, theme wiring)
description:
Follow-up to bd-mermaid-runtime-not-bundled-vxejw159. That strand makes the mermaid runtime offline-correct; it deliberately does not touch how diagrams are styled. q2 currently ships no mermaid CSS or theming at all, so diagrams render with stock mermaid defaults and do not follow the document theme.

WHAT QUARTO 1 SHIPS (external-sources/quarto-cli/src/resources/formats/html/mermaid/):
- mermaid.css (281 B) -- .mermaidTooltip and friends
- embed-mermaid.css (6.4 KB)
- mermaid-init.js (14 KB) -- initializes the runtime AND wires theming: it reads meta[name="mermaid-theme"] and, when absent, injects a large default themeCSS string driving everything off CSS custom properties (--mermaid-fg-color, --mermaid-node-bg-color, --mermaid-edge-color, --mermaid-label-bg-color, --mermaid-font-family, ...) so diagrams inherit the Quarto theme, including dark mode.
- mermaid-postprocess-shim.js (1.5 KB)

WHAT Q2 SHIPS. Only the runtime plus mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false }) and mermaid.run({ querySelector: 'pre.mermaid' }) -- see mermaid_script_block() in crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/mermaid.rs. No CSS artifact, no themeCSS, no theme meta tag. Diagrams therefore look unthemed and, in particular, do not adapt to dark themes.

SCOPE TO SETTLE. Which of Q1's CSS actually needs porting versus which is Q1-DOM-specific; whether the custom-property theming should be driven from the resolved Quarto/bootstrap theme variables q2 already computes; and whether the brand/theming work has a better hook for this than a hard-coded default CSS string. Note the repo rule against DOM postprocessors -- Q1's mermaid-postprocess-shim.js is a postprocessor, so any behavior it provides has to be re-expressed as an AST transform or as emitted markup, not ported as-is.

MECHANICS. The runtime asset registration landing in the parent strand (vendored resources/mermaid/ -> Project-scoped artifact -> _site/site_libs/mermaid/) gives a natural place to register a CSS artifact alongside it; crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs::register_reveal_assets is the model for registering CSS and JS together with cascade-ordered keys.

Also relevant: bd-1vwtdwtq (preview-path mermaid runtime) -- whatever theming lands should hold for q2 preview / hub-client too, where MermaidCodeBlock.tsx currently calls mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false }) with no theme wiring either.
close_reason: Duplicate. title: Parser rejects combining characters (decomposed Unicode) in prose text
description: Literal combining marks in prose cause a hard parse error: printf 'x \xe2\x89\x82\xcc\xb8 y' (x ≂̸ y, U+2242 U+0338) fails with 'unexpected character or token here' pointing at the combining solidus overlay; 'e' + U+0301 (combining acute) fails the same way, while precomposed é (U+00E9) parses fine. So any NFD/decomposed Unicode text — e.g. pasted from macOS filename APIs or produced by some editors/IMEs — is rejected by the grammar. Discovered while fixing bd-named-entities-w6xbfftj: entities decoding to combining sequences (e.g. ≂̸ -> U+2242 U+0338) convert to the AST fine, but the qmd writer's output is then un-reparseable, breaking qmd->json->qmd roundtrip. The roundtrip fixture crates/pampa/tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/named_entities.qmd deliberately omits multi-codepoint entities because of this bug — when fixing, add '≂̸' back to that fixture as the regression test. Likely home: tree-sitter-qmd grammar character classes (what counts as word/text characters) rather than pampa.
close_reason: Fixed: PANDOC_COMBINING_MARKS (\p{M} + ZWNJ/ZWJ) added to pandoc_str content classes in grammar.js; parser regenerated. Commit on main following 9509f8d2 (entity-decode branch). Devanagari, NFD accents, enclosing marks, ZWNJ/ZWJ all parse as verbatim Str now, matching Pandoc.

c-5y2sz8xe.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-5y2sz8xe.text: Scope update from investigation: broader than decomposed Latin. ALL of these are parse errors today: Devanagari matras (का = क U+0915 + ा U+093E Mc — i.e. any Hindi text with vowel signs), enclosing marks (a + U+20DD Me), ZWNJ U+200C / ZWJ U+200D between letters (Persian/Indic joining control), and mid-word decomposed accents (cafe + U+0301). Pandoc folds every one of these into Str verbatim (verified: 'cafe\769', 'ab\8204cd', 'a\8413'). Fix scope: add \p{M} (Mn/Mc/Me) + U+200C/U+200D to pandoc_str content classes in grammar.js (same bug family and fix shape as bd-6kewx, which added non-ASCII Po/Pc). Given plain Hindi prose cannot parse, this is arguably P1.

title: hub-client: connection indicator flashes Offline on page reload
description: Follow-up to bd-53501yf7 (widen-only fix). On a page reload straight into a document the peer lands after the 400ms budget (cold DNS/TLS/WS upgrade plus bundle+WASM main-thread contention), so connect() resolves offline-first and the indicator mounts Offline then flips to Online. Fix: three-valued indicator state (unresolved/online/offline) via useConnectionIndicatorState — render no indicator until the peer lands or a 2.5s grace window expires; once resolved, track isOnline exactly so mid-session drops report immediately.

title: Syntax highlighting: investigate native tree-sitter-highlight event-stream end-byte behavior for same-start nested captures
description:
Surfaced during Phase 4.4 native-vs-browser parity work (2026-04-21).

Native collect_spans in crates/quarto-highlight/src/{registry,user_grammar}.rs uses tree-sitter-highlight's HighlightEvent stream with cursor-based span boundaries. When two captures open at the same start byte (e.g. (bare_key) @type + (pair (bare_key)) @property on a TOML pair), tree-sitter-highlight emits HighlightStart events back-to-back with no intervening Source event. collect_spans records both spans with the outer capture's end byte, because the cursor only advances on Source events.

Result: [0, 14, "type"] for a (bare_key) @type capture that should cover 0-4. Both the browser golden (via web-tree-sitter Query.captures, which gives node-exact ranges) and the query pattern say 0-4.

For HTML rendering this means the native path wraps the inner capture's CSS class around the whole outer range, not the actual capture's range. For the TOML fixture: .hl-type wraps the whole 'name = "value"' pair instead of just 'name'.

Impact: cosmetic; users see hl-* classes applied to broader ranges than intended for nested same-start captures. Not a correctness regression (classes are all applied; just overlap more than necessary).

Fix path: replace the cursor-based collect_spans with node-range-aware span extraction. tree-sitter-highlight's event stream doesn't carry node ranges, so we'd either need to (a) use Query::captures() directly (bypassing tree-sitter-highlight's event stream, but losing its precedence resolution) or (b) augment the collect_spans walker to track per-nesting-level cursors.

Regenerating the golden at crates/quarto-highlight/tests/snapshots/golden__user_grammar_toml.snap will be part of the fix.

Out of scope for Phase 4.4; parity test documents and bounds the divergence.
close_reason: Fixed by Phase 0 (committed 79edee27 on branch beads/bd-t4ezufyg-monaco-highlighting): native Registry::highlight + UserGrammars::highlight AND the JS-side user-grammar highlighter now use Query.captures() + innermost-wins flatten_spans instead of the lossy collect_spans event stream. user_grammar_toml golden flips from [0,14,type] to node-exact type=[0,4]; native and browser render identically.

c-pikjz1em.author: shikokuchuo
c-pikjz1em.text: Fixed by Phase 0 of bd-t4ezufyg (Monaco highlighting epic): Registry::highlight + UserGrammars::highlight now extract node-exact Query.captures() spans + innermost-wins flatten_spans instead of the lossy collect_spans event stream. The user_grammar_toml golden flips from [0,14,"type"] to node-exact type=[0,4] with property split around it. Closing once committed.

title: EPIC: display an executable cell without executing it (self-documenting cells)
description:
Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-02-self-documenting-cells-epic.md Quarto's self-documenting function - showing a reader what a Quarto cell looks like - does not work in q2 in ANY spelling today. Q1 does it with a doubled brace; q2 deliberately reserved 'nesting inside a markdown block' to mean the same thing and says so in Q-2-50's own hint. Neither works. TARGET OUTPUT, recorded from the Q1 dev build (99.9.9) rendering a bare four-backtick fence containing a doubled-brace r cell. Four properties: 1. not executed - no ::: {.cell}, no output 2. class markdown - even though the author wrote a BARE fence (Q1 inserts it, engine-escape.lua:55) 3. highlighted as markdown - 
, fence lines as 
  4. the R inside highlighted as R - cat - markdown DELEGATING to the R highlighter, i.e. a syntax INJECTION

In q2 the same output must come from the single-brace spelling nested in a markdown block. Span class names will differ (q2 tree-sitter hl-* vs Q1 skylighting fu/st); parity is on the four properties.

WHAT MEASURING AGAINST THOSE PROPERTIES REVEALED: the blockers are NOT the engine hand-off assembler. They are (3) quarto-highlight has no markdown grammar - BUILTIN_BUILDERS at registry.rs:170 has 13 entries and markdown is not one - and (4) quarto-highlight forbids injections by design, with builtin_configs_have_no_injection_or_locals (registry.rs:263) failing loudly if any grammar carries an injection query. A plain markdown block with no cell already renders unhighlighted in q2 where Q1 highlights it fully, so 3 and 4 are missing highlighter capabilities, unrelated to cells or engines.

FOUR PLANS:
  1. Masking at the engine hand-off seam + class-marking a bare display fence + extending Q-2-50 to the nested doubled-brace form. Delivers properties 1-2. Absorbs bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj and bd-q250-nested-fence-blind-spot-t68z1lsw.
  2. A markdown grammar in quarto-highlight. Delivers property 3. Independently valuable for every markdown block in every document.
  3. Injection support in quarto-highlight. Delivers property 4. Architectural - must move off Query.captures() or handle injections explicitly, then retire that test.
  4. The engine hand-off assembler (claude-notes/designs/engine-handoff-assembler.md). Retires the decay class incl. two FATAL bugs, fixes the RawBlock family plan 1 leaves alone, and replaces plan 1's pattern-matched marker with a minted token. Absorbs bd-iu5otya7.
  5. (optional) Fix the partitioners we own - bd-jupyter-parse-code-blocks-regex-z1ehfla6, bd-breakquartomd-indented-display-fence-1wxmf0bh - narrowing masking to knitr alone.

ORDER: 1, 2, 3, 4. Plan 1 is the most testable (a spike already proved it, commit c5d1754b0 on branch spike/nested-cell-mask) and the only piece delivering user-visible value alone; it builds the regression suite the rest is measured against. Plan 4 is the least testable and most dangerous - its failure mode, emitting stale bytes for a node a transform legitimately changed, is SILENT - so it should land against a green suite rather than create one.

title: staleness integration test fails on macOS — FSEvents starved by hub-server boot
description:
The integration test \`cell_edit_flips_staleness_in_sidecar\` in
\`crates/quarto-preview/tests/staleness.rs\` fails reliably (15.6 s
timeout, "staleness never flipped") on cscheid's machine
(macOS 26.4.1 Tahoe, Darwin 25.4.0, Apple Silicon).

## Reproduces at

- Merge tip \`feature/q2-preview-command\` (4cd5a5ff)
- Pre-merge tip (0df1f0ea)
- The very commit that added the test (\`cc180477\`, where bd-u3ze
  closed with "5/5 stable reruns")

So it is NOT a regression introduced by any later commit on the
branch. Something about the environment changed since the test
landed on May 14 — but per the user, the laptop has not rebooted
since (so it is not an OS version bump).

## What was tried and what was learned

1. The hub-server's \`FileWatcher\` task starts (\`run_file_watcher\`
   entered), but the \`notify-debouncer-mini\` callback **never
   fires** during the 15 s window. FSEvents is not delivering events
   to the consumer.

2. Adding a control \`FileWatcher::new\` in the *test* code just
   before the file edit works around it: 5/5 pass in ~2.3 s.

3. Adding the same kicker pattern *inside* \`FileWatcher::new\` (or
   in a background thread after a 500 ms delay, or as a permanent
   secondary debouncer kept alive in the FileWatcher struct) does
   NOT work: 5/5 still fail.

4. Sentinel write/delete of a throwaway file in the watched root
   does NOT kick the stream: 5/5 still fail.

5. An isolated probe (plain tokio + notify + notify-debouncer-mini,
   no hub, no axum, no samod) reliably delivers events for
   single-watcher, two-watchers-immediate, and two-watchers-delayed
   modes. So FSEvents on this machine works in isolation.

6. The real \`q2 preview\` binary works in normal user workflows
   (verified with /tmp fixture + 3 sequential edits): every edit is
   detected and \`recompute_staleness\` runs. The bug does not break
   user-facing behavior — likely because real user edits come after
   the periodic-sync tick at T+5 s.

## Updated theory

The bug is not an FSEvents stream-startup warm-up issue (the probe
disproves that). It looks like *something specific that runs during
hub-server boot* — samod init, axum listener setup, eager-capture
spawn, periodic-sync task spawn, or some interaction among them —
silences the FSEvents stream until another stream is created late
in the boot sequence, after that disruptive thing has settled.

The throwaway-in-test-code workaround happens to run after all the
disruptive boot work; a kicker inside FileWatcher::new runs before
it and is therefore ineffective.

## Next steps

Bisect through the hub-server boot path to identify which specific
step silences FSEvents. Candidates: samod runtime construction,
axum::serve listener, the spawn_blocking eager-capture driver,
tokio::time::interval setup in run_periodic_sync. Recommended
method: progressively strip down the integration test to find the
minimum boot configuration that reproduces.

Until root cause is found, the test is \`#[ignore]\`d. The plan is
to NOT patch production code blindly — a kicker watcher in
FileWatcher::new is harmless cargo-culting if we don't understand
why the real fix has to live somewhere else.

## Files

- crates/quarto-preview/tests/staleness.rs  (the test)
- crates/quarto-hub/src/watch.rs              (FileWatcher impl)
- crates/quarto-hub/src/server.rs:run_file_watcher (event consumer)
- crates/quarto-preview/src/lib.rs:run_with_on_ready (boot path)

## Related

- bd-u3ze: the issue that added this test, claimed-stable at cc180477
- \`.config/nextest.toml\`: serializes the three preview integration
  tests to work around an earlier (different) FSEvents flake

title: Single-file q2 preview: resolve the deck's full transitive sibling deps (includes + their assets), and re-resolve on edit
description:
Follow-up to bd-kpuweafo. ROOT CAUSE (verified E2E 2026-06-16): single-file q2 preview (no _quarto.yml) only syncs a narrow, statically-parsed set of siblings into the VFS, whereas q2 render reads the whole filesystem and project-mode preview walks the whole dir. So in single-file preview, anything the deck transitively needs that isn't pre-synced is broken.

Verified matrix (single deck main.qmd with {{< include part.qmd >}} where part.qmd has ![](./inc-image.png)):
- q2 render (single file): include resolves + image displays (naturalWidth 320). WORKS (reads disk directly).
- q2 preview project (touch _quarto.yml): include resolves + image displays (blob). WORKS (dir walk syncs part.qmd + image).
- q2 preview single-file: include renders as literal '?include' placeholder; 'Included Section' absent; image absent. BROKEN.

So the user's presumed inconsistency (includes work but their images don't) is actually: INCLUDES DON'T WORK EITHER in single-file preview - same root cause as the direct-image gap. bd-kpuweafo fixed only DIRECT image refs in the deck (parse deck -> collect Image URLs -> sync). It did NOT fix: (a) {{< include >}} of sibling .qmd (included file not in VFS -> shortcode fails); (b) images referenced INSIDE included files (transitive); (c) refs added mid-edit (resolution is one-shot at session start in build_hub_config).

WHY HARD: bd-tnm3k single-file mode deliberately does NOT walk the directory (a bare 'q2 preview ~/Downloads/x.qmd' must not index all of ~/Downloads). So every sibling the deck needs must be DISCOVERED BY PARSING. quarto-hub has no qmd parser; extraction lives in quarto-preview (config::resolve_single_file_assets) and is injected via HubConfig. Includes also can't be resolved on-demand mid-render because the WASM include-expansion reads synchronously from the VFS - the file must be pre-synced.

PROPOSED FIX: make single-file extraction TRANSITIVE and recursive: parse deck -> collect {{< include >}} targets (extract_include_path, already used by deps.rs) + Image URLs; for each included .qmd, recursively parse it -> collect its includes + images; sync included .qmd as text and all images as binary into the VFS. Bonus: re-run extraction on deck-change watch events so mid-edit-added refs sync without reload. Keep the under-deck-dir canonicalization guard (no ../ escape). This makes single-file preview match render/project for the deck's own dependency closure without a full dir walk. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-16-single-file-preview-referenced-assets.md (v1 limits section).
close_reason: Implemented + merged in PR #300 (feature/bd-9cyza5vy-single-file-preview-transitive-deps). Single-file q2 preview now resolves the deck's full transitive include + image closure via the renderer's own include-expansion run natively; included .qmd sync as invisible text deps; the watch set covers the closure. TDD + E2E verified; CI clean. Render-side nested-include retargeting bug remains open as bd-udrn0q47.

c-bni1dft5.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-bni1dft5.text: Design-exploration plan written: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-16-single-file-preview-vfs-bootstrapping.md. Frames the bootstrapping paradox (populating the ephemeral VFS requires parsing files, but parsing requires the VFS to be populated), the verified behavior matrix, why single-file can't walk the dir (bd-tnm3k), the full set of dependency channels, and 5 design options (A transitive static extract / B lazy on-miss fetch / C render-driven fixpoint reusing pipeline deps / D bounded walk / E async file_read) with eval criteria + a tentative lean toward C. No implementation beyond bd-kpuweafo's direct-image sync; this is the explore-the-space step the user requested.

c-podosqfn.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-podosqfn.text:
Implementation complete (pending review/commit). All 4 phases + spike done, TDD throughout.

Phase 0 (spike): chosen entry point = run the renderer's OWN ParseDocumentStage + IncludeExpansionStage natively via pollster::block_on, so include path resolution matches q2 render exactly (incl. the bd-udrn0q47 nested-include behavior — preview inherits it automatically).

Phase 1 (quarto-preview/config.rs): resolve_single_file_deps -> SingleFileDeps { qmd_files, binary_files }. Text deps = doc.recorded_includes (transitive, cycle-truncated); binary deps = collect_referenced_asset_urls over the EXPANDED AST, deck-dir-anchored (render parity / no retargeting). Under-root guard preserved. Deleted superseded resolve_single_file_assets. 6 new tests.

Phase 2 (quarto-hub + preview): included .qmd ride a new text-only path — HubConfig.single_file_text_deps -> ProjectFiles.text_dep_files + with_text_deps (in text_files()/all_files()/counts, NOT qmd_files, so invisible/no nav). build_hub_config rewired to one resolve_single_file_deps call filling both fields. discovery.rs + context.rs tests.

Phase 3 (quarto-hub/watch.rs + server.rs): WatchConfig.single_file_deps; FileWatcher subscribes deck + each closure dep (NonRecursive, best-effort) and accepts only allow-set members. server.rs builds the set from project_files().all_files() minus the deck. bd-tnm3k safety preserved (unrelated siblings still ignored) — pinned by test.

Phase 4 (E2E): q2 preview main.qmd (no _quarto.yml), browser inspection of the render iframe: 'Included Section' renders (include expanded, no literal ?include), and the image INSIDE the include displays via blob URL (naturalWidth 1, the 1x1 PNG loaded).

title: reference-location ignored from front matter (as_str vs PandocInlines)
description:
reference-location set in document YAML front matter is silently ignored in ALL placements (top-level, nested under format.html) and for ALL values (margin/block/section) — rendering always falls back to the 'document' default.

CONFIRMED root cause (runtime dump of get_reference_location in the real q2 render pipeline):

  reference-location: margin   -> kind=PandocInlines, as_str()=None,        as_plain_text()=Some("margin")
  reference-location: !str margin -> kind=Scalar,    as_str()=Some("margin")

In document-metadata context, a bare YAML string value is parsed as markdown and stored as ConfigValueKind::PandocInlines (see quarto-pandoc-types/src/config_value.rs:189-195), NOT Scalar(String). ConfigValue::as_str() (config_value.rs:641-649) returns None for PandocInlines. So:

  FootnotesTransform::get_reference_location (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/footnotes.rs:76-81)
  AppendixStructureTransform reference-location read (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/appendix.rs:92)

both call .and_then(|v| v.as_str()) and get None -> ReferenceLocation::default() = Document.

The key is PRESENT; the accessor is wrong. The codebase already has the right convention: ConfigValue::as_plain_text() (config_value.rs:675-684) handles both Scalar(String) and PandocInlines, and is used deliberately elsewhere for exactly this (filter_resolve.rs:90,212 with the comment 'handle both Scalar(String) and PandocInlines forms'; document_profile.rs reads all meta strings via as_plain_text). The !str tag is a working-but-undocumented escape hatch today.

FIX: replace .as_str() with .as_plain_text() in footnotes.rs:78 and appendix.rs:92 (audit appendix.rs for other reference-location reads too). Low risk, matches existing convention. TDD: add a failing e2e render test (front matter reference-location: margin -> margin-note class, no doc-endnotes section) before fixing.

Distinct from bd-po3gn41h (named [^id] footnote refs, PR #264) and from bd-1kly (block/section numbering). Discovered while verifying bd-po3gn41h margin-mode parity.
close_reason: Fixed and merged via PR #265 — reference-location honored from front matter (as_str -> as_plain_text).

title: package-lock.json missing @esbuild/* platform packages — clean npm ci breaks esbuild (quarto-hub-mcp bundle test)
description: The committed root package-lock.json has the esbuild@0.28.0 entry (with its optionalDependencies list) but ZERO node_modules/@esbuild/* package entries — the known npm optional-deps lockfile bug (npm/cli#4828, typically introduced by regenerating the lockfile on a tree whose node_modules already lacked the other platforms' packages). Consequence: a clean 'npm ci' or fresh 'npm install' produces a node_modules with esbuild but no @esbuild/darwin-arm64 (or any platform binary), and ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp's scripts/bundle.mjs fails at runtime ('The package "@esbuild/darwin-arm64" could not be found'), failing cargo xtask verify's hub-mcp test leg. Existing checkouts hide this because their node_modules predates the esbuild 0.28.0 bump. Surfaced 2026-08-18 in room-2 after a root npm install refresh. Machine-local workaround applied there: npm install --no-save @esbuild/darwin-arm64@0.28.0 (does not touch the lockfile; breaks again on the next clean install). Proper fix: regenerate the lockfile so all @esbuild/* platform entries are present (e.g. delete node_modules + package-lock.json and npm install with a current npm, or 'npm install esbuild --save-dev' to force re-resolution), verify grep -c 'node_modules/@esbuild/' package-lock.json > 0, and commit. Also worth checking the same symptom for other platform-optional packages (rollup, swc). Separately noticed: hub-client/package-lock.json is a git-tracked stray (May 18) despite the npm-workspaces root-lockfile setup — evaluate whether it should be deleted.

title: hub-mcp does not exit on stdin EOF while sync connections are live
description: quarto-hub-mcp wires shutdown to SIGINT/SIGTERM only. MCP hosts terminate stdio servers by closing stdin; after stdin EOF the StdioServerTransport closes but live websocket/reconnect timers keep the event loop alive, so the process lingers forever (confirmed: still running 4s after EOF in bd-81cfshmw Phase 0 spike; only exits 'naturally' when no sync client was ever created). Every agent session would leak a node process — multiplied by the q2 mcp launcher. Fix: transport/server onclose -> shutdown (guard against re-entrancy with server.close()).
close_reason: Fixed in d7225dff: process.stdin 'end' watcher + server.onclose both route to a guarded shutdown. Root cause: SDK StdioServerTransport never observes stdin EOF. Regression test in stdio-hygiene.test.ts.

title: Harden q2 provide-hub: interactive consent gate + one-shot default (no auto-watch)
description:
Security review of the always-on provide-hub raised the risk of a live server auto-executing requests if the CRDT document is hijacked. Two default changes:

1. Interactive consent gate (default ON): when a request would execute, show a prompt naming a temp file containing the resolved document to be evaluated (the post-include AST serialization — what we'd hand knitr), with options accept / reject / accept-this-and-future. Bypass with --dangerously-accept-requests.

2. One-shot default (no watch): default mode ephemerally connects, pulls project docs, executes once (still showing the consent prompt), then shuts down. The current watch-the-ephemeral-requests behavior moves behind --watch.

Requires synthesizing the post-include QMD (quarto_core::engine::preview_record::compute_input_qmd already produces this) into a reviewable temp location before engine invocation, from the SAME materialization that is executed (review-equals-execute). Linked plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-02-provide-hub-consent-gate.md. Part of bd-sfet3264.

title: stage-doc-examples / build-agents-docs rebuild q2 for every example project (~1.5 min x 14 on the release runner)
description:
Observed in the v0.27.0 release run (32815089965, web-payloads): every one of the 14 example renders in `cargo xtask stage-doc-examples` recompiles quarto-mcp-launcher, quarto-preview and quarto (~1m27s each), then `build-agents-docs` recompiles once more for the docs render. Locally the same happens whenever `agents-docs-dist/` is absent (15 recompiles in one run).

Cause: the xtasks invoke `cargo run --bin q2` per project, and the embed build scripts emit `cargo:rerun-if-changed=<dir>` unconditionally — including when the directory does not exist yet (`crates/quarto/build.rs:41` for agents-docs-dist, `crates/quarto-mcp-launcher/build.rs:47` for dist-bundle). Cargo treats a missing rerun-if-changed path as always stale, so the build script re-runs and the crate recompiles on every cargo invocation until the directory appears. On the runner both dirs are missing during web-payloads (dist-bundle is built per-leg; agents-docs-dist is what this xtask produces), so nothing is ever cached.

Fix: build `q2` once (`cargo build --bin q2`) and run `target/debug/q2` directly for each example project and for the docs render, instead of `cargo run` per project. Keep the unconditional rerun-if-changed: dropping it for a missing dir would mean a later `cargo xtask build-agents-docs` no longer triggers the re-embed — the stale-embed trap CLAUDE.md warns about.

title: Find a proper home for Q2 CLI user docs
description:
Phase D.5 (bd-kw93.11) shipped user-facing docs for q2 preview at docs/q2-preview.qmd, the most natural existing home — but docs/ is titled 'Quarto-markdown' and is pitched as a reference for the markdown dialect + library internals (Syntax / Writers / Library Docs sections). It is not currently designed as a front door for Q2 CLI commands.

As more Q2 commands gain user-facing surface area (q2 render, q2 trace-view, future q2 hub, etc.), they will face the same placement question. Some options to consider:

- A dedicated 'CLI' or 'Q2 Commands' section under docs/ with its own landing page.
- A separate site (e.g. q2.quarto.org or similar) wholly oriented to Q2 users.
- Fold Q2 CLI docs into the existing quarto-dev/quarto-cli docs site when that catches up to Q2.

Discussion settled with carlos@ during D.5: docs/q2-preview.qmd lives in the existing site for now (single-page, single-decision); structural reorganization deferred to this issue. The page itself is fine; the question is whether the IA around it should change.

Existing related pages worth considering when designing the home: docs/quarto-hub/preview.qmd (in-browser live preview, different surface). q2 preview --help (always-accurate inline reference; less discoverable than a docs site).

title: q2 preview: bring hierarchical block navigator to --allow-edit; fix breadcrumb/rich-text toolbar overlap

Fix: lay them side by side with the breadcrumb to the RIGHT of the fixed-position rich-text controls (keeping toolbar position independent of the variable-width breadcrumb).

title: Diagnostics blame the wrong key: materialized map/array spans (folds in bd-2mxo)
description:
Rendering a ported Q1 site (Posit Connect docs) emits:

  Warning: [Q-12-7] `template:` was set but `type:` is not `custom`; falling back to the built-in template for the declared type.
  ╭─[ cookbook/vanities/index.qmd:4:11 ]
  4 │     sort: false
    │           ──┬──

The caret points at `sort: false` — a sibling key with nothing to do with the diagnostic. Three defects behind one symptom:

A) Wrong blame span. quarto-config materialize.rs:142-158 gives a materialized Map ConfigValue the source_info of its FIRST child's value (arrays get their LAST item; key_source is discarded for the programmatic-config sentinel). Every diagnostic that blames a Map-kind ConfigValue lands on an arbitrary sibling. Same root cause as bd-2mxo.

B) Wrong diagnostic identity. Q1 (website-listing-read.ts:1316-1320) makes `template:` IMPLY `type: custom`. The user's YAML is valid Q1; Q2 asserts intent the user never expressed, and "the built-in template for the declared type" is false when no `type:` was declared at all.

C) Silent garbage on the neighbouring path. Adding `type: custom` to that same file makes Q2 emit the raw EJS (`<% for (const item of items) { %>`) into the HTML with NO diagnostic. Q-12-9 only fires on `.ejs.md`, not `.ejs`. So the correct message for this corpus is an EJS-migration diagnostic, not Q-12-7 — and naively adopting Q1's implies-custom rule would make these sites worse, not better.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-06-q12-7-listing-template-diagnostic.md

c-atl1v096.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-atl1v096.text:
Phase 0 + Phase A landed in 4698b85f (not pushed).

Phase 0: quarto_config::span_assert behind a span-assert feature; quarto-core enables it as a dev-dependency. Chose quarto-config over the plan's guess of quarto-test -- quarto-test is a document-level _quarto.tests smoke runner that DEPENDS on quarto-core, so it sits above both consumers; quarto-config is the lowest crate carrying both quarto-source-map and quarto-error-reporting.

Key harness decision: existing listing tests stamp every value with SourceInfo::for_test(), so a wrong span is indistinguishable from a right one -- the bug is invisible by construction. parse_from_yaml drives the real path (YAML -> yaml_to_config_value -> MergedConfig -> materialize -> parse_listings), matching what transforms/listing_generate.rs:72 reads at render time.

Failing test confirmed before the fix:
  diagnostic [Q-12-7] underlines the wrong text
    expected: "../template.ejs"
    actual:   "false"
    at:       index.qmd:3:11

Phase A: Q-12-7 blames the template: entry; Q-12-4 blames the duplicate id: value (previously underlined the whole map entry). Both confirmed failing first.

Audit of remaining container-blaming sites: Q-12-2 (inline contents record), Q-12-1 (non-map listing entry), Q-12-3 (sort shape) already blame the semantically right value and read wrong only because the container span is wrong -- Phase B/bd-2mxo territory. So Phase A does not close this strand.

Full workspace: 10869 passed, 197 skipped. cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build clean. Zero snapshot changes.

Next: Phase B (bd-2mxo) -- preserve real container spans and key_source through materialization.

c-d7pnjs9m.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-d7pnjs9m.text:
Phase B landed in d47b3799 (not pushed). bd-2mxo closed.

Two findings that corrected the plan's expectations:

1. ZERO snapshot changes, against a plan that predicted tree-wide churn. Reason worth keeping: no existing snapshot ever captured a materialized CONTAINER span. The same 154-vs-12 assertion imbalance that hid the bug made the fix invisible to the suite. Scalar spans were never affected -- the 'winning layer' test passed from the start and independently bounds the defect.

2. Phase A's audit was partly wrong. materialize_cursor's Array arm clones items verbatim (no recursion through the cursor, since array items have no path), so containers nested INSIDE arrays always kept correct spans. Only map-valued keys went through the synthesizing arm. So Q-12-2 (inline contents record) was never broken -- regression test added -- and Q-12-4's pre-fix span was the genuine mapping span, making Phase A's Q-12-4 change a wrong-NODE fix rather than a wrong-SPAN fix. Q-12-3 was genuinely broken (underlined 'title') and is fixed. Each verified by running against a stashed tree rather than by re-reading code.

Also fixed as a side effect: L5's categories_source anchor for Q-12-12 was inert (Generated sentinel), confirmed empirically; now resolves to the real categories: key.

End-to-end: all 15 Q-12-7 instances in the Connect docs now point at 'template: ../template.ejs', including the reported cookbook/vanities/index.qmd (4:11 -> 5:15). Site still renders poorly (9 errors, 310 warnings) -- bd-oywyaouf and bd-lu16jgxq own the rest, as scoped.

Full cargo xtask verify (including WASM leg) clean. Remaining before close: nothing in the plan except the deferred lint, filed as bd-cwk7l4dl.

c-j3o5hc7a.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-j3o5hc7a.text:
Root cause for defect A traced and confirmed. The YAML->ConfigValue bridge is NOT at fault: pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs:175-193 carries a real map span and real key_source, and meta.rs:384-389 even re-stamps the top-level frontmatter map to the whole YAML body. All of it is discarded at quarto-core/src/stage/stages/metadata_merge.rs:266-288, which replaces doc.ast.meta wholesale with merged.materialize(). materialize_cursor's Map arm (quarto-config/src/materialize.rs:142-158) then synthesizes the container span from the first entry's VALUE.

Constraint on the broad (bd-2mxo) fix: MergedCursor exposes no per-key spans at all -- MergedMap carries only keys: Vec<String> (quarto-config/src/merged.rs:396-413). Restoring key_source needs an API change, not a local edit. Also note quarto-yaml computes a mapping's span as first-key-start -> MappingEnd (quarto-yaml 0.1.0 src/parser.rs:513-525), so even a fully-correct map span would not give Q-12-7 the caret a reader expects. Both argue for the narrow per-key blame fix in Phase A here, with bd-2mxo staying separate.

c-l1estlik.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-l1estlik.text:
bd-2mxo folded into this strand per user (2026-08-06). Earlier reading was WRONG and is corrected: bd-2mxo is not blocked on an API change and needs no external-crate work.

MergedConfig holds layers: Vec<&'a ConfigValue> (merged.rs:100-107) -- borrowed ORIGINALS with spans and key_source intact. MergedMap is a virtual map computed over them, not a copy. MergedCursor::keys() (merged.rs:216-222) already iterates the real ConfigMapEntry structs and keeps only entry.key, discarding entry.key_source; as_value()/navigate_to() (merged.rs:238-245) already return the winning layer's &ConfigValue with a correct source_info. So the fix is additive accessors + rewiring materialize.rs's two synthesis arms, entirely inside crates/quarto-config.

quarto-yaml needs no change (it already emits correct key spans -- that is how the in-tree bridges capture them). quarto-source-map needs no change to unblock this; its Default impl returning Original{FileId(0),0..0} instead of a sentinel is written up separately for a different session at claude-notes/scratch/2026-08-06-memo-quarto-source-map-default-sourceinfo.md. In-tree we avoid Default rather than wait on it.

Phase A (blame the right key) is NOT subsumed by Phase B: quarto-yaml computes a mapping span as first-key-start -> MappingEnd, so even perfect materialization would underline the whole listing: block starting at sort:.

Added Phase 0 (span-assertion helper). Motivating measurement: 154 assertions in crates/ check a diagnostic's .code; ~12 touch its location. config.rs:1233 is typical -- asserts the code only, passes with a garbage span. That asymmetry is why this survived.

c-nlu7vdpp.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-nlu7vdpp.text:
Scope narrowed per user (2026-08-06): this strand is now the source-mapping defect ONLY. The two other defects found during investigation are split out:
- bd-oywyaouf -- unsupported EJS listing templates render as raw <% ... %> with no diagnostic. Q2 dropped EJS deliberately (doctemplate replaced it so untrusted contexts like hub-client never execute arbitrary JS); user confirmed the plan's design question Q3: warning + fall back to built-in, not a hard error.
- bd-lu16jgxq -- Q-12-7's text asserts a `type:` the user never declared, and the docs page misstates Q1 behavior.

User explicitly accepted that the Connect docs render worse in the interim: that site is more than a single fix away from rendering well. The sequencing constraint the original plan was built around (EJS detection must precede Q1 implies-custom parity) therefore no longer gates this strand.

Plan rewritten and narrowed: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-06-q12-7-listing-template-diagnostic.md

title: revealjs auto-stretch: crossreferenceable figure (::: {#fig-id}) hoist (Case 2)
description:
Case 2 from bd-38ioql41 (deferred as Option 2A). A crossreferenceable figure (::: {#fig-id} ![](x) caption :::) on a single-image reveal slide is NOT stretched: at RevealAutoStretchTransform time it is still a plain Block::Div(#fig-id) (crossref->Figure conversion runs later), so the standalone-block gate skips the nested image. Q1 parity (applyStretch): hoist img to direct section child, MOVE figure id onto img (so @fig-id resolves), add quarto-figure-center, caption ->

. HARD CONSTRAINT: crossref-render is excluded from the q2-preview pipeline (Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED), so crossref targets stay FloatRefTarget CustomNodes in preview and never become Pandoc Figures -> there is no single late AST shape common to render AND preview. Options: 2B reveal-aware crossref render in BOTH CrossrefRenderTransform and the React FloatRefTarget component (full parity, large, touches hub-client); 2C render-only late hoist (parity in render, preview gap, must be logged/documented). Recommend revisiting alongside a Q2 figure-alignment story (same milestone that would add quarto-figure-center). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-17-revealjs-autostretch-figures.md (Case 2 section + options 2A/2B/2C).

title: Migrate q2 issue tracking from beads_rust to braid
description:
Replace beads_rust (br) with braid as q2's issue tracker. braid stores issues in a single automerge CRDT (a 'skein') synced via a sync server; no git involvement, no daemon. This epic and its plan deliberately stay in beads so they survive if the migration is abandoned.

ID preservation is the critical property (412 distinct bd- ids referenced across 1141 tracked locations) and is ironclad via braid import's upsert-by-id.

Decisions locked: (1) public relay sync server for the experiment; (2) committed braid export snapshot is backup-only and strictly one-directional, never re-imported; (3) build 4 braid 0.3.0 features first (dep tree, create --deps, import skip-tombstones, agents-info skill installer).

title: WASM VFS: populate PathMetadata.modified from Automerge change history
description:
Today crates/quarto-system-runtime/src/wasm.rs::path_metadata returns modified: None with a 'VFS doesn't track modification times' comment. Hub-client and the future quarto preview need this populated so listings, blog-style 'last changed on:' displays, and other date-modified consumers work in Automerge-backed projects.

Design notes:
- Native (filesystem): already works — modified comes from std::fs::metadata().modified().
- WASM (Automerge VFS): each document path lives in an Automerge CRDT; every change op has a wall-clock timestamp attached (peer-local clock, not authoritative across peers). Candidate semantics: 'most recent local-or-remote change op affecting this path's document.'
- Edge cases: project just synced from peer with no local edits (use peer timestamp), document never edited (use creation time, or None and let consumers fall back to listing-item.date), Lamport vs wall-clock ordering, peer clock skew.
- Test surface: unit-test the WASM VFS impl with synthetic Automerge histories; smoke-test in hub-client that a sibling-page edit updates the listing host's date-modified column.

Surfaced during L1 sub-plan review (bd-izqh) on 2026-05-06. L1 ships using the existing path_metadata API; on WASM date_modified just stays None until this issue lands. No L1 code change needed when this issue resolves.
