title: q2 preview: browser opens before server accepts connections (race on larger projects)
description: q2 preview opens the browser (open::that) synchronously in crates/quarto/src/commands/preview.rs:145, but the HTTP server that actually binds+accepts only starts at line 189 via quarto_preview::run(config).await. The port printed in the URL comes from a throwaway probe listener (probe_free_port, lines 194-202) that is dropped immediately, so nothing is accepting on that port until axum::serve() runs deep inside quarto-hub::server::run_server_with (bind at server.rs:1204, accept at ~1273), after the expensive HubContext::new() (samod init + project discovery + index load + initial fs sync). On small/single-file projects context init is fast enough that the browser's first connection lands after accept; on larger projects it loses the race and Firefox shows 'Unable to connect'. Reloading works because by then the server is up. Fix: gate the browser-open on the server actually accepting connections (poll TcpStream::connect to host:port with backoff + timeout fallback, on a spawned task while the main task awaits the server), rather than opening unconditionally before run(). Reported by Carlos 2026-06-15 with two screenshots. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-15-q2-preview-browser-race.md
close_reason: Fixed in commit d4073f88 (merged to main, pushed to origin/main). q2 preview gates the browser-open on the server actually accepting connections via wait_until_accepting (TcpStream::connect, decaying backoff 20ms->1s cap, 10s ceiling+warn) on a spawned task. Closes the ~250ms race that showed 'Unable to connect' on larger projects. TDD red-first 3 unit tests + 15/15 preview unit; workspace 10043/10043; cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build passed; e2e confirmed 'opening browser' fires ~62ms after 'Hub server listening'. Follow-up (unfiled, pending user): profile the ~250ms HubContext::new startup floor; see plan claude-notes/plans/2026-06-15-q2-preview-browser-race.md.

c-idvgiyir.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-idvgiyir.text:
Diagnosed 2026-06-15. Confirmed ordering bug by reading the code: crates/quarto/src/commands/preview.rs run() opens the browser at line 145 (open_browser_or_log -> open::that, synchronous) but does not start the server until line 189 (quarto_preview::run(config).await). The printed port comes from probe_free_port (194-202), a throwaway StdTcpListener bound on (host,0) and dropped immediately, so nothing accepts on that port until axum::serve runs deep in quarto-hub::server::run_server_with (bind server.rs:~1204, accept ~1273) AFTER the size-dependent HubContext::new (samod init + project discovery + index load + initial fs sync). Larger project => longer context init => browser loses the race => Firefox 'Unable to connect'; reload works because the server is up by then.

Caveat for the fix: the existing on_ready seam in quarto-preview/src/lib.rs fires AFTER context-init but BEFORE TcpListener::bind, so reusing it would shrink but not close the race.

Recommended fix (Option A in the plan): gate the browser open on the real accept condition -- spawn a task that polls TcpStream::connect(host,port) with backoff + a timeout fallback, then opens; keep the server on the main task to avoid imposing a Send bound (see .claude/rules/wasm.md). Full writeup + test plan + alternatives (B: new accept-signal callback; C: fixed sleep, rejected) in claude-notes/plans/2026-06-15-q2-preview-browser-race.md. Awaiting go-ahead before implementing.

c-rfroorgn.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-rfroorgn.text:
Benchmark (2026-06-15, release q2, claude-notes/research/bench-preview-port-ready.py): measured the race window for 'q2 preview docs/' (167 qmd files) = time from URL-print (when open::that fires today) to port accepting TCP. Result over 5 trials: min 248.5 / median 250.0 / max 280.8 ms. So the window is ~250ms even on a medium project — easily enough for a launching/running browser to connect-and-fail (= the reported bug). Tight clustering (variance <35ms) points to a fixed-cost startup step (samod init or a debounce) dominating rather than per-file work; flagged as a separate follow-up to profile HubContext::new, NOT part of this fix.

Revised Option A backoff per Carlos's input: poll connect() starting ~20ms, decay to a 1s cap, 10s total ceiling; on ceiling open anyway AND tracing::warn! so a slow start is visible instead of silent. Plan updated with the benchmark table + revised design.

c-sxhmcy1y.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-sxhmcy1y.text:
Implemented on branch beads/bd-a6dvrdg1-preview-browser-race (commit d4073f88), Option A.

Change (crates/quarto/src/commands/preview.rs only): added async wait_until_accepting(host, port, total_timeout) -> bool that polls TcpStream::connect with a decaying backoff (20ms ×1.6 → 1s cap) until the port accepts or a 10s total ceiling. run() now spawns a task (guarded by !no_browser) that awaits readiness then calls open_browser_or_log; on ceiling-miss it opens anyway and tracing::warn!s. Added an info! 'preview server accepting connections; opening browser' right before the open (operational + the e2e observable). Server stays on the main task → no Send bound imposed; browser-open stays a CLI concern (no quarto-hub/quarto-preview signature changes).

TDD: 3 unit tests written red-first (E0425), then green — returns_true_when_listener_present (9ms), times_out_when_nothing_listening (~161ms), unblocks_when_listener_appears_late (~205ms, the direct race regression). Full preview unit set 15/15.

Verification: cargo nextest --workspace 10043/10043; cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build = All steps passed (Rust-only change, nothing hub-client depends on touched). E2E (release, q2 preview docs/, harness claude-notes/research/e2e-preview-open-after-ready.py): binary logged 'Hub server listening' at 20:05:21.772704Z and 'opening browser' at 20:05:21.834530Z — open fired ~62ms AFTER bind, gated correctly; browser tab opened against the live preview.

Follow-up noted in plan (NOT this fix): ~250ms startup floor on docs/ has variance <35ms → likely a fixed-cost step in HubContext::new worth profiling separately.

Status: code complete + committed, NOT pushed (git policy). Awaiting user review for merge/push.

title: Consolidate the accumulated WASM build toolchains (wasm-pack vs wasm-bindgen-cli + wasm-opt)
description:
We now maintain two parallel WASM build toolchains plus three different version-pinning strategies for the same class of tool. Discovered while trying to rebuild WASM to verify a preview change: the build failed on a hard dependency (binaryen/wasm-opt) added one day earlier, which had never been provisioned locally.

## Two toolchains, split by crate

- crates/wasm-qmd-parser -> 'wasm-pack build --target web --dev' (.github/workflows/build-wasm.yml:50), with hand-rolled CFLAGS_wasm32_unknown_unknown and a local wasm-sysroot.
- crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client -> hub-client/scripts/build-wasm.js: cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown, then wasm-bindgen-cli, then wasm-opt -Oz.

cd2817e1 ('replace wasm-pack with pinned wasm-bindgen-cli in dev setup') migrated one of these but not the other, and wasm-pack is STILL installed in hub-client-e2e.yml:93 alongside wasm-bindgen-cli — possibly vestigial, worth confirming.

## Three pinning strategies for the same class of tool

1. wasm-bindgen-cli in hub-client-e2e.yml:99 — DERIVED from Cargo.lock by awk. Self-maintaining, correct.
2. wasm-bindgen-cli in ts-test-suite.yml:135 — HARDCODED 'cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.108'. Drifts silently from Cargo.lock; build-wasm.js verifies the CLI matches Cargo.lock, so this workflow breaks whenever the crate is bumped.
3. binaryen — HARDCODED 'npm install -g binaryen@132.0.0' in CI, with the comment: 'Pinned to the version local dev uses (Homebrew binaryen 132) so CI and dev builds produce the same bytes.'

## The sharpest problem: the binaryen pin is one-sided

That CI comment states an invariant local dev does not uphold. There is no local binaryen pin — the documented install is 'brew install binaryen' / 'npm install -g binaryen', both of which give whatever is current. Today Homebrew happens to ship 132, so the bytes match by luck. When Homebrew ships 133, local and CI silently produce different WASM bytes and the stated invariant breaks with no warning and no check.

## Local provisioning is manual and unpinned

crates/xtask/src/dev_setup.rs:211 check_wasm_opt() deliberately does not install binaryen (the wasm-opt crate would build all of binaryen from C++ source). It only warns with install hints. So 'cargo xtask dev-setup' leaves a developer with a broken 'npm run build:wasm' and a manual, unpinned install to perform.

Consequence observed: this checkout could not rebuild WASM at all, which also left q2-preview-spa/dist/ without a viewer manifest and made quarto-preview::integration config_endpoint::config_reports_embedded_asset_manifest_hashes fail locally. That failure looked like a mysterious stale artifact; the actual cause was the day-old toolchain requirement. Completing the chain after installing binaryen made it pass.

## Questions to answer

- Can wasm-qmd-parser move to the same cargo + wasm-bindgen-cli + wasm-opt path, retiring wasm-pack entirely? What do the CFLAGS/wasm-sysroot bits need?
- Should all tool versions derive from one source of truth (Cargo.lock / a pins file) rather than three hardcoded spots?
- Should dev-setup install binaryen from the pinned npm package ('npm install -g binaryen@<pin>') rather than only warning? That would make local provisioning both automatic and pinned, and it is not the heavy C++ source build the comment rules out.
- Is wasm-pack in hub-client-e2e.yml:93 still needed?

Context: wasm-opt was added 2026-08-13 by 1eeaae5d (live-share payload reduction, bd-ee0qcq3c); 8024198b then added binaryen installs to three CI workflows.

title: Windows-from-source builds emit CRLF in verbatim-embedded CSS/JS output assets
description:
SYMPTOM: On a Windows-from-source build of q2, static text resources embedded via include_str!/include_bytes! and written verbatim to the output tree carry CRLF, while the shipped binary (built on Linux CI, LF) emits LF. So the emitted CSS/JS output convention differs by build host, and Windows contributors get non-reproducible CRLF output artifacts.

EVIDENCE: q2 render of a single-file HTML doc produced page_files/styles.css containing 138 CRLF (0d0a) sequences (hexdump). styles.css comes from crates/quarto-core/src/resources.rs:51 DEFAULT_CSS = include_str!("../resources/styles.css"), written verbatim via DEFAULT_CSS.as_bytes() at resources.rs:118. git ls-files --eol shows all these resource files are i/lf w/crlf (LF in index, CRLF in working tree under core.autocrlf=true), and no .gitattributes covers resources/ or crates/quarto-core/resources/. include_str! bakes the working-tree bytes at compile time, so the CRLF ends up in the binary and then in the output verbatim.

MECHANISM: include_str! embeds working-tree bytes -> CRLF on Windows checkout -> written to output unchanged. Not grass output (grass regenerates CSS with its own \n) and NOT the parse_layer bug: this is an OUTPUT-artifact convention issue, whereas bd-gl0bufxp is internal SCSS layer parsing. Distinct code paths, distinct symptom.

AFFECTED (verbatim-written text resources, all i/lf w/crlf, no gitattributes): crates/quarto-core/resources/styles.css; resources/attribution/viewer.css + viewer.js; resources/revealjs/reset.css, reveal.css, quarto-reveal.css, theme/white.css (reveal.js too); resources/listing/quarto-listing.js (and list.min.js via include_bytes); resources/bootstrap-icons/bootstrap-icons.css. pampa templates (resources/templates/html/*.html, main.html, styles.html) are the same class if written verbatim -- verify.

BINARY HAZARD: some assets go through include_bytes! and MUST NOT be eol-converted: resources/bootstrap-icons/bootstrap-icons.woff (font, binary), resources/js/bootstrap/bootstrap.bundle.min.js and resources/js/clipboard/clipboard.min.js (minified). A blanket 'resources/** text=auto eol=lf' would corrupt the woff. Any fix must scope to text globs (*.css *.js *.html) and explicitly mark *.woff (and other fonts/images) as binary/-text.

RELATION TO CRLF EPIC (bd-eehxwr29): these are generated/copied output artifacts, not byte-offset-mapped document content, so the preserve invariant does not apply -- the Layer-0 determinism approach fits (mirror bd-mv2ggmr5 pampa pin and crates/quarto-doctemplate/.gitattributes: text eol=lf for the relevant globs + git add --renormalize + re-checkout).

OPEN QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE (why this is 'understand more' not 'fix now'): (1) Is CRLF in emitted CSS/JS actually harmful to end users, or only a reproducibility/consistency wart? Browsers tolerate CRLF; the real cost is host-dependent output + noisy diffs for Windows contributors. (2) Fix locus: pin sources to LF via .gitattributes (deterministic, mirrors precedent) vs normalize-on-write in the resource-writer (covers any future CRLF source). (3) Should compiled/copied output CSS have a defined convention at all, or is LF-everywhere the target? (4) Confirm grass-compiled theme CSS convention once bd-gl0bufxp is fixed (currently unobservable -- every theme fails parse_layer on Windows build). (5) Full audit of which include_str!/include_bytes! assets actually reach the output tree vs are only inputs to compilation.

REPRO: on a Windows checkout (core.autocrlf=true), cargo build --bin q2; q2 render a minimal HTML doc; hexdump the produced *_files/styles.css and grep for 0d0a.

c-ib1p4tfl.author: cderv
c-ib1p4tfl.text:
Design discussion (2026-07-08, via bd-ol45i8oe) reframes this class: on the current architecture it is COSMETIC, not a correctness bug.

Why cosmetic:
- Served assets are Artifact { content: Vec<u8>, .. } with NO SourceInfo/offset field (crates/quarto-core/src/artifact.rs:53). They never enter automerge: register_*/render flush them to a LOCAL synthetic VFS (/.quarto/project-artifacts), regenerated per-client per render, not synced source. So they are DISJOINT from the byte-offset/provenance invariant this epic enforces -- that invariant governs document source (qmd text), not served build output.
- CRLF vs LF in served CSS/JS is byte-identical to every browser. Nothing hashes/SRIs/snapshots these bytes for a hard failure (checked: no integrity attrs, no .snap embeds the content; theme_fingerprint only self-references; computeSHA256 is a per-build cache key, not a cross-build assertion).
- Shipped binaries (native + hub WASM, pkg/ is gitignored) are CI-built on Linux -> LF. Only a local Windows-from-source build embeds CRLF, and that never ships.

Not in this class: SCSS. grass's lexer collapses CRLF/CR/FF -> LF before parsing (empirically verified on windows-msvc: 8 CR in, 0 out), and q2 also strips at parse_layer() (bd-3fgnmlco). User-CRLF SCSS cannot leak CRLF into compiled CSS.

Sanctioned pattern for the verbatim-served class = normalize EOL in the TEST comparison (see bd-ol45i8oe, assemble.rs vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package), NOT a .gitattributes per-dir pin. gitattributes is checkout-dependent (existing CRLF working copy stays stale until --renormalize) and would need ~9 dirs pinned with no central guardrail enforcing coverage.

Decision needed: only pursue an actual code fix (normalize-on-embed for all verbatim-served assets -- checkout-independent, LazyLock on the include_str constants) IF cross-build-host byte-determinism becomes a stated goal. Otherwise downgrade/close as cosmetic-wontfix.

title: Preview rich-text editor: open with drag-selection preserved (not just caret)
description: In q2 preview (--allow-edit) and hub-client's format: q2-preview, clicking a block opens the rich-text editor with the caret near the click point. But when the user *drags* a selection within a single block, the editor currently opens with only a caret at the mouse-release point, discarding the selection. Improve this: when the DOM selection at mouseup is fully contained within the block being activated, open the rich-text editor with an equivalent editor selection (anchor+head mapped from the DOM Range), so selection-dependent rich-text controls (bold, link, etc.) are immediately usable. Selections spanning multiple blocks are out of scope (current caret behavior is acceptable there). Plan doc to be linked.

title: julia e2e tests race on cold QNR control-server start: concurrent cold starts spawn N servers, last transport-file writer wins, clients fail with 'Incorrect HMAC digest'
description: Observed 2026-07-03 during bd-l9jhy5u0 pre-flight verify in a cold world (no QNR control server running): nextest ran the 4 julia_engine_e2e tests concurrently; each hit startOrReuseJuliaServer's TOCTOU (if !existsSync(transportFile) -> spawn detached server, julia-engine.ts:330-448), so 4 detached control servers started. Each server binds its own port, generates its own key, then OVERWRITES the single global transport file (quartonotebookrunner.jl: serve() then open(transport_file, 'w')) and rm's it at exit. All 4 renders failed with 'Julia server returned error after receiving "isopen" command: Incorrect HMAC digest' (client's polled {port,key} pointed at a different server generation than the one listening). One orphan server survived (script path = deleted nextest TempDir) owning the transport file; a follow-up serial run of j1 against that warm server PASSED (reuse path is fine). Implications: (1) any cold julia-equipped machine fails the julia suite on first parallel run and passes thereafter — masked until now because leaked workers (bd-l9jhy5u0) kept a server permanently alive; (2) future CI with julia would hit this every run (fresh runner = cold); (3) bd-l9jhy5u0's test plans that use an isolated-HOME harness re-enter the cold world each run and must serialize julia tests or pre-start the server. Upstream Q1 has the same code shape (single-render CLI rarely races). Fix directions: nextest test-group serialization for julia tests, a pre-started server in the harness, or an engine-side lock/retry around cold start (upstream-mergeable).

title: add_html_dependency: version field unimplemented, and the Q-11-1 warning fires once per call instead of once per dependency
description:
quarto.doc.add_html_dependency accepts a 'version' field; q2 ignores it and emits Q-11-1 "add_html_dependency: field 'version' is not yet supported and will be ignored". Q1 accepts it silently and folds it into the asset directory (_site/site_libs/quarto-contrib/<name>-<version>/); q2 writes an unversioned path (_site/site_libs/libs/<name>/).

Two separable issues, and the second is the one that bites:

1. The field is unimplemented ('version' sits in UNSUPPORTED_FIELDS alongside meta/links/resources in crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_doc.rs). Mostly cosmetic — one dependency at one version has nothing to collide with — and the unversioned site_libs/libs/{name}/ layout is documented in crates/quarto-core/src/dependency.rs, so it may be deliberate design.

2. The warning fires per CALL, not per distinct dependency. In the add_html_dependency closure (quarto_doc.rs, the 'Check for unsupported and unknown fields' loop around line 230), the field-validation loop runs BEFORE the dedup-by-name check on quarto.doc._dependencies. Since add_html_dependency de-duplicates by name, extensions are written to call it unconditionally for every matching element — that is the documented idiom — so every call warns even though only the first registers anything.

Suggested fix: either honor 'version' in the output path (Q1 parity), or if unversioned paths are the deliberate design, keep the warning but move the field check after the dedup early-return (or otherwise dedup the diagnostic) so it fires once per distinct dependency. Deciding point 1 either way, the point-2 reorder is a small self-contained fix.

Real-world hit: the Posit Connect docs use the mermaid-zoom extension, which calls add_html_dependency (with version:) once per mermaid diagram — 33 diagrams across 14 pages yields 33 identical warnings per full render, turning one distinct diagnostic into a flood. Worked around docs-side with the diagnostics: level-off suppression for Q-11-1 (the 0.20.0 suppression feature's first real use in that project), to be removed when this is fixed.

Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/add-html-dependency-version/ — 'q2 render .' there; a filter calls add_html_dependency on two paragraphs and produces two identical Q-11-1 warnings, with assets at _site/site_libs/libs/versioned-dep/ (Q1 comparison output committed at _site-q1/). See README.md. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-zax2g85q. Observed with q2 0.20.0, re-verified on 0.21.0; unfixed at HEAD (3ac596e0).

c-0fnhh85u.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-0fnhh85u.text:
Investigated 2026-08-14 on main @ 3ac596e0; plan skeleton at claude-notes/plans/2026-08-14-add-html-dependency-version.md (commit 4ed62ce8), repro committed alongside.

Three findings that change the strand's framing:

1. The Lua state is per (document, filter, pass) — create_filter_environment runs on every apply_lua_filter (filter.rs:250), and UserFiltersStage runs in both pre() and post() (pipeline.rs:346,348). So _dependencies always starts empty and the suggested point-2 reorder yields N warnings for N pages, not 1 — 14 for the Connect docs, down from 33. Point 2 alone does NOT resolve the reported symptom; only making 'version' non-warning gets to zero.

2. Q1's version buys directory NAMING only, not multi-version coexistence. Q1's Lua add_html_dependency does no dedup at all (init.lua:815-870, always external=true) and the TS side dedups by name BEFORE consulting version (pandoc-dependencies-html.ts:230-238). A second version of a same-named dep is silently skipped in Q1 too.

3. Full Q1 path parity is two changes, not one: Q1 writes quarto-contrib/{name}-{version}/ for external deps; q2 writes libs/{name}/ and has no notion of external deps at all ('quarto-contrib' appears nowhere in crates/ or docs/). Adopting only the version suffix produces a third layout neither tool has.

Also noted: Q-11-1 is the generic Lua diagnostic code, so the docs-side 'Q-11-1: level: off' workaround silences every Lua warning in that project, not just this one.

Awaiting user decision on 5 design questions in the plan; my recommendation is (B) accept 'version' silently plus the field-loop split (keeping unknown-field errors before the dedup early-return).

c-dj1fnk8t.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-dj1fnk8t.text:
Implemented in 6f316c90 (branch main).

Both points fixed:

1. Field loop split (not moved wholesale): unknown fields still hard-error on every call; the unsupported-field warning moved after the dedup early-return, so it fires once per distinct dependency.

2. 'version' implemented. libs/{name}/{version}/{file} plus a versioned artifact key; unversioned deps keep libs/{name}/{file} byte-identical. The key is the half that matters for freeze — without it two renders producing different versions collapse onto one artifact. Intra-document dedup stays name-only (so the call-once-per-element idiom is silent), but same-name/different-version now warns.

Also documented quarto.doc.add_html_dependency in docs/guides/authoring/lua-filters.qmd — it had no user-facing coverage at all.

End-to-end verified through 'q2 render' on the committed repro (claude-notes/plans/add-html-dependency-version-investigation/repro/): zero warnings, previously 2; asset at _site/site_libs/libs/versioned-dep/1.0.0/versioned-dep.js; emitted <script src> agrees with the on-disk path. Full 'cargo xtask verify' green, 14/14 including the WASM leg. Workspace tests 11940 passed.

Remaining before close: the connect-docs project should drop its 'diagnostics: Q-11-1: level: off' suppression, which was silencing every Lua warning in that project, not just this one.

Follow-up filed while working: bd-mcy2316m — a scripts/stylesheets entry's 'name' sub-field is accepted and silently ignored (Q1 uses it as the output filename).

c-flpdr63i.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-flpdr63i.text:
Design decisions 2026-08-14 (commit 9526e2ca):

1. Implement 'version' — do NOT silently ignore. Rationale is freeze, which the investigation had missed: engine outputs reused across renders can produce dependencies that change, and the version tag keeps an update from clobbering an older rendering's assets. Q2 has no freeze yet (eventual design likely reworks the execution-output automerge sidecar into a portable .ipynb-based format), but it will need multi-version dependency support, so the field must mean something now rather than be trained out of users' extensions.

This amends Finding 2 in the plan. Q1's name-only dedup does block coexistence WITHIN a render, but the case version actually serves is ACROSS renders, where that dedup never applies. So q2 should not copy Q1's name-only dedup into the versioned world — the artifact key in dependency.rs:50,78 must gain the version or freeze is lost.

2. New disk layouts acceptable — no _site longevity promise — so quarto-contrib/ is not required.

3. Cross-document diagnostic dedup filed separately as bd-k2ox4tqq; residual N-warnings-per-N-pages accepted here.

4. Split the field loop (unknown-field error before the dedup early-return, unsupported-field warning after).

5. Other UNSUPPORTED_FIELDS keep warning; version leaves the set because we are implementing it.

Still open before implementation: (a) does version participate in the Lua-side intra-document dedup key as well as the artifact key — recommendation is name-only for Lua (prevents double-injection on one page), (name, version) for artifacts (preserves cross-render coexistence); (b) flat libs/{name}-{version}/ vs nested libs/{name}/{version}/ — recommendation is nested.

title: Adjacent footnote definitions merge — the second note is silently lost
description:
Two footnote definitions on consecutive lines are parsed as one. The second is absorbed as lazy paragraph continuation into the first note's body, and its reference renders as an EMPTY span, so the reader sees no footnote marker at all and note 1 has a foreign sentence glued onto it. No diagnostic is emitted. ## What happens vs Quarto 1 App modes: `python-api` (flask[^wsgi]) and `python-fastapi`[^asgi]. [^wsgi]: Other WSGI-compliant application frameworks may be served via this app mode. [^asgi]: Other ASGI-compliant application frameworks may be served via this app mode. Quarto 1: two numbered notes; both references resolve. q2 0.19.0: one note, and in the body text

App modes: python-api (flask…1…) and python-fastapi.

— the second reference is an empty . The note list then contains note 1 with the second definition pasted into it as literal text:

First note. : Second note.…

Separating the two definitions with a blank line parses correctly; that is the only workaround. ## Root cause The block form of a footnote definition is inline_ref_def: seq(ref_id_specifier, _whitespace, pandoc_paragraph) (crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js:283). Its body is a pandoc_paragraph, so it keeps consuming continuation lines — and nothing stops it at the next definition, because neither SOFT_LINE_ENDING gate in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c treats '[' as a line that opens a block. The gates' leader list (scanner.c ~2939-2945 for gate 1, ~3120-3123 for gate 2) covers '>' , ':', '#', fences, '*' via a peek, and '-'/'+'/digits via the peeks added in 92737cdd. '[' is absent, so a '[^asgi]:' line is lazy paragraph text. This is the same class of bug as bd-digit-line-splits-paragraph-w6tod0gh, and the inverse symptom: there a line that was NOT a block opener ended the paragraph; here a line that IS a block opener fails to. ## Suggested fix direction The recognizer already exists — parse_ref_id_specifier (scanner.c:1795) — so this should follow 92737cdd's shape exactly: add a shape-only peek_ref_id_specifier helper next to peek_ordered_marker / peek_dash_plus_opens_block, wire it into both gates on a '[' lookahead, and let it block the soft break when the line really forms a '[^id]:' specifier (and only then — '[not a footnote] in prose' must stay paragraph text). Note the same gate addition is what a link reference definition needs ('[ref]: url' on a continuation line, the sibling issue), so it is worth designing the peek to answer for both bracket forms rather than footnotes alone. Please also apply the indent x context sweep from claude-notes/instructions/scanner-indentation-contexts.md — that note was written after the last two scanner gate changes each regressed a case the other missed. ## Real-world hit in the Connect docs user/manifest/index.qmd carries exactly the [^wsgi]/[^asgi] pair above: the python-fastapi app-mode note disappears and its text is glued onto the flask note. admin/integrations/tableau loses a note the same way and renumbers 3 to 2 with the body gone. Both pages currently differ from the Q1 reference render because of this. ## Repro /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/adjacent-footnote-definitions/ Run 'q2 render' there and compare with 'quarto render'. Section A is the failing pair; section B is the same content with a blank line between the definitions and parses correctly. Observed from q2 0.16.0 through 0.19.0 (re-verified against the released 0.19.0 binary; HEAD 1ba0f2ec). Origin strand in the q2-connect-docs skein: br-pj9i6ejq.

c-3g062yl4.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-3g062yl4.text:
Investigated at c28cfd81 (pre-flight `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green: 11728 passed). Plan skeleton + committed repro/sweep artifacts: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-adjacent-footnote-definitions.md (commit c11abfa1). Verdict: ready to design, pending 5 questions in the plan. Root cause confirmed exactly as filed; every cited line still holds (gate 1 now 2940-2947, gate 2 now 3118-3125; grammar.js:283 and parse_ref_id_specifier@1795 unchanged). Reproduced at three levels: CST (inline_ref_def [4,0]-[6,0] spans both definition lines), AST (the Q-3-10 diagnostic underlines lines 5-6 as one node), and rendered HTML (empty , second definition glued into note 1's body). Dependency graph is EMPTY - no edges at all; the real context is the prose reference to bd-digit-line-splits-paragraph-w6tod0gh, whose fix 92737cdd is on main and is the template. Eight things the investigation adds: 1. THE BUG IS BROADER THAN THE TITLE. It is not specific to adjacent definitions: no '[^id]:' line ever opens a definition after a non-blank line. 'hello there.' / '[^b]: two.' yields one paragraph. Definition-after-definition is just the case real documents hit, because a note body is itself a paragraph. 2. BUT PANDOC AGREES WITH q2 ON THAT BROADER CASE, and this is the one thing that complicates the fix. Pandoc does not treat a footnote definition as a paragraph-interrupting block opener; its note body is a raw-line collector that stops at a blank line or the next '[^id]:'. So it interrupts a DEFINITION BODY, never an ordinary paragraph. A naive "add '[' to both gates" repairs the reported symptom and simultaneously moves 'hello there.' / '[^b]: two.' away from pandoc. This is the central design question (Q1 in the plan). 3. THE ESCAPE HATCH: q2's note body is ALREADY an ordinary paragraph and already diverges from pandoc. '# Heading' and '- item' after a definition line both interrupt in q2 and are both absorbed as literal text by pandoc. So making '[^id]:' interrupt is the CONSISTENT answer under q2's own model, and case B's divergence is the same one q2 already accepts for '#' and '-'. Matching pandoc instead would need the scanner to know "am I inside an inline_ref_def body" - state it does not have, since inline_ref_def is a grammar rule, not a scanner open-block. Recommendation: diverge deliberately and document. Note Q-2-30 already narrows q2's note-def body relative to pandoc's on purpose (verified firing at HEAD). 4. THE INDENT RULE COMES OUT RIGHT FOR FREE. 92737cdd's guards (indentation <= claimable_list_indentation+3 at gate 1, residual <= 3 at gate 2) reproduce pandoc's indent column exactly: indent 0/1/3 opens a new definition, indent >=4 is body content. Indent 4 already behaves correctly today by accident and the guard preserves it. No new indent policy to invent. 5. THE LINK-REFERENCE-DEFINITION PREMISE IN THE DESCRIPTION IS FALSE. There is no such construct in qmd and no such sibling strand: CLAUDE.md states qmd supports only inline link syntax, grammar.js has no link_reference_definition rule, and 'hello there.' / '[ref]: http://example.com' parses to a pandoc_span plus literal text. Designing the peek "to answer for both bracket forms" would build a mechanism with no consumer. Recommend scoping to '[^id]:' only (Q3). 6. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT - this is the "silently" in the title and it SURVIVES this fix. transforms/footnotes.rs:445-450 leaves an unresolved reference "as-is (broken reference)", and the span pampa lowers '[^id]' into is EMPTY, so a broken reference renders as an invisible with no marker, no text and no diagnostic. Pandoc keeps the literal '[^id]' and warns. Any typo'd note id will keep vanishing after the parser is fixed. Not filed yet - Q5 asks whether to. 7. The repro README's adjacent finding is real: no

Footnotes

appendix heading is emitted (only
+
    ). `grep -rn '"Footnotes"' crates/ --include='*.rs'` returns zero hits - nothing in the tree ever emits it. Cosmetic; also unfiled, also Q5. 8. BLAST RADIUS IS ESSENTIALLY NIL. Zero tree-sitter corpus cases have a '[...]:' line after a non-blank line; the pandoc-match corpus has no footnote fixtures at all, so unit_test_corpus_matches_pandoc_markdown cannot be perturbed by the case-B divergence; the single repo-wide .qmd match is inside a fenced code block in docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-30.qmd. Residual risk is snapshot churn - predicted for 92737cdd too, where it did not materialize. Also relevant, not batched: bd-mt1ksg9b (the '*' gate peeks still lack the indent guard) touches the same two gates and would conflict. Q4 asks whether to batch; recommendation is to keep them separate and do this one first, since '[^id]:' has no emphasis ambiguity. Final gate must be full `cargo xtask verify` (NOT --skip-hub-build) - the grammar feeds the WASM parser.

c-9ved6p3m.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-9ved6p3m.text:
IMPLEMENTED on branch braid/bd-adjacent-footnote-definitions-miif1k1z-adjacent-footnote-definitions-merge, commit 1699b853 (investigation plan at 0dc232e1). Based on main @ 7bcddf61. NOT pushed — awaiting review.

Plan updated with the full implementation record: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-adjacent-footnote-definitions.md.

WHAT LANDED. scanner.c only; no grammar change, so parser.c is untouched and there are no generated diffs. One peek helper (peek_ref_id_specifier) wired into both SOFT_LINE_ENDING gates on a '[' lookahead, under 92737cdd's indentation rule.

THE SUBTLE PART, and the thing to review hardest: THE PEEK MUST NEVER BE LOOSER THAN THE PARSER. inline_ref_def is seq(ref_id_specifier, _whitespace, pandoc_paragraph), so the whitespace AND a non-empty body are both mandatory — '[^x]:two.' (no space) and '[^x]:' (empty body) parse to an ERROR node even at block start. Had the peek merely mirrored parse_ref_id_specifier as the strand suggested, those lines would have had their soft break suppressed and then failed to form any block: a hard parse error, which drops the WHOLE FILE from the render. That is the bd-j7be7kuc failure mode. The helper is deliberately stricter and the invariant is written into its comment.

DEPARTURE FROM 92737cdd's SHAPE. The dash/plus branch sets first_peeked OUTSIDE its indentation guard, with a comment saying the over-indent verdict must still take the peeked emission path. Copying that verbatim for '[' was wrong, and the over-indented-list-item corpus case caught it — it regressed from passing to failing, gaining a block_continuation inside its pandoc_soft_break. The '[' branch never advances on the over-indent path, so leaving first_peeked false reproduces byte for byte what the line did before '[' had a branch at all. Both first_peeked and second_peeked are set INSIDE the guard, noted in the code so nobody "restores symmetry" later.

DESIGN ANSWERS FROM THE USER (all five questions in the plan are closed):
1. '[^id]:' DOES interrupt an ordinary paragraph — 'hello there.' / '[^b]: two.' is now paragraph + definition. Deliberate pandoc divergence, same direction q2 already diverges for '#' and '-'.
2. Code comment is enough; no user-facing docs pass.
3. Peek scoped to '[^id]:' only. The strand's link-reference-definition premise was false: qmd has no such construct (CLAUDE.md, no grammar rule, and '[ref]: url' parses as a bracket span plus literal text).
4. bd-mt1ksg9b kept separate.
5. Both spin-offs filed: bd-jttkymsw (p2, unresolved reference renders as an invisible empty span with no diagnostic — SURVIVES this fix, since this only removes one cause of unresolved references) and bd-v9zs83zj (p3, missing Footnotes appendix heading).

TESTS. 11 corpus cases covering the required indent x context sweep. Confirmed failing FIRST and failing in the right places: 6 failed / 5 passed, the 5 passers being cells that must NOT change (indent 4, over-indented in a list, and three negatives). After the fix 11/11. tree-sitter test 593/593 overall, zero regressions.

RESULTS. Full `cargo xtask verify` (NOT --skip-hub-build — the grammar feeds the WASM parser): all 14 steps passed, Rust tests 11728 passed / 197 skipped. ZERO snapshot files changed. Pre-flight verify was green before any change.

END-TO-END. cargo run --bin q2 -- render repro.qmd --to html, HTML inspected: both references resolve to real superscript links (fnref1/fnref2), four correctly-numbered notes, note 1's body no longer carries the second definition, and no quarto-note-reference span survives anywhere in the output. The committed repro fixture is the exact [^wsgi]/[^asgi] pair from the Connect docs.

PROCESS NOTE. The implementation was originally done in the main checkout; partway through, a concurrent session working bd-7vz18qht reset main and switched branches IN THAT SAME WORKING TREE, discarding the uncommitted scanner work. Nothing was lost — the investigation commit was recovered from the reflog (pinned as recover/bd-miif1k1z-investigation in the main checkout) and cherry-picked into a dedicated worktree, where the fix now lives. Work here, not in the main checkout.

ALSO FIXED: the committed sweep.sh used an absolute path into the main checkout, so running it from a worktree silently swept the unmodified parser and reported pre-fix results. It now resolves the grammar dir relative to BASH_SOURCE.

title: Block-level attrs on list items (<li class>) via child-block trailing Inline::Attr
description: Follow-up to bd-itqcfxc3 (Para capability merged in PR #310). Extend block-level attributes to list items (<li class>). DISTINCT mechanism from Para: a Pandoc list item is [[Block]] with no per-item attr, so an injected trailing Inline::Attr lives inside the item's last child block (a Plain/Para). The list writers must HOIST the resolved attr from that child block up to the <li> element. Reuse the existing block-agnostic helper crates/pampa/src/writers/block_attr.rs split_trailing_block_attr (returns (content, Attr)); the hoist is list-writer-specific. Touch points: html.rs list_item_open (html.rs:1272 — must compose with the incremental 'fragment' class) + Bullet/OrderedList writers; json.rs streaming list-item emission (carry attr on the <li>/item shape); React ts-packages/preview-renderer BulletList.tsx/OrderedList.tsx (read & apply). Decide the JSON wire form for an item attr (Para already uses an extra 'attr' object key Pandoc ignores; list items need an analogous safe carrier). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-17-block-level-attrs-inline-attr.md

title: Tree-sitter parser splits paragraph at line starting with backtick
description:
Lines beginning with a single backtick (inline code span) are incorrectly treated as paragraph-interrupters by the tree-sitter scanner, splitting one paragraph into two pandoc_paragraph nodes. Should only interrupt when 3+ consecutive backticks (fenced code block start).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-tree-sitter-backtick-paragraph-split.md

Root cause: crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c lines 2263-2272 and 2291-2315 unconditionally exclude backtick from soft-line-break candidates. CommonMark only treats >=3 backticks as a fence; <3 is an inline code span and should soft-break.

Pure tree-sitter repro (from crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown):
  printf 'foo bar\n`code` more text\n' | tree-sitter parse -
=> two pandoc_paragraph nodes (bug). Should be one with pandoc_soft_break.
notes: See plan file for full reproduction set, fix sketch (peek_paragraph_interrupting_backticks helper), and test plan.
close_reason: Fixed: peek-count backticks in scanner line-break handler; <3 → soft break, >=3 → paragraph break (fence). All 456 tree-sitter tests pass; 8125 workspace tests pass; pampa output now matches pandoc.

title: cargo xtask stage-doc-examples writes to the main checkout from a worktree
description:
Running `cargo xtask stage-doc-examples` from inside a git worktree stages into the MAIN checkout's `docs/examples/`, not the worktree's. The worktree is left without the directory, so a subsequent `q2 render docs/` there fails with:

    Error: Declared resource '<worktree>/docs/examples' does not exist on disk

Cause: `stage_doc_examples::run` takes its root from `create_worktree::repo_root()`, which is

    git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir

then `.parent()`. In a worktree the *common* dir is deliberately the main repo's `.git`, so the parent is the main checkout. That resolution is correct for repo_root's original callers (create-worktree needs the main repo, and the braid/worktree helpers do too) but wrong for anything that wants 'the checkout I am standing in'.

Observed 2026-08-17 while running Phase C of the ts-engine-extensions merge from `.worktrees/ts-engine-extensions`: the command reported success ('staged 2 item(s) to docs/examples/...') while writing to `/Users/gordon/src/q2/docs/examples`. Silent because the output is gitignored on both sides, so nothing shows up in `git status` to contradict it.

Worth checking whether other xtask subcommands share the mistake — `repo_root()` is shared, so any subcommand that means 'this checkout' rather than 'the main repo' has the same bug. Grep the callers before fixing.

Suggested fix: add a sibling helper (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, the *current* worktree root) and switch callers that operate on working-tree content to it, leaving `repo_root()` for the genuinely main-repo-scoped callers. Naming them distinctly matters — the two are indistinguishable at the call site today.

Workaround: copy `<main>/docs/examples` into the worktree (it is generated, gitignored content).
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-32c8egkf (same xtask worktree/repo-root bug); detail folded into that strand

title: aliases: is silently ignored — no redirect stubs written for renamed/moved pages
description:
q2 silently ignores the 'aliases:' document metadata key. No redirect stubs are written and no diagnostic is emitted, so a site that moved or renamed pages serves 404s at every old URL after a port from Quarto 1.

## What happens vs Quarto 1

Given a page declaring:

    ---
    title: Current page
    aliases:
      - /old-name.html
      - ../previous/index.html
    ---

Quarto 1 writes a small HTML redirect stub at each alias path (_site/old-name.html, _site/previous/index.html). The stub is a <title>Redirect</title> document whose inline script does window.location.replace to the canonical page, preserving both hash and query string:

    var redirects = {"":"../index.html"};
    var hash = window.location.hash.startsWith('#') ? window.location.hash.slice(1) : window.location.hash;
    var redirect = redirects[hash] || redirects[""] || "/";
    window.document.title = 'Redirect to  ' +  redirect;
    if (!redirects[hash]) { redirect = redirect + window.location.hash; }
    redirect = redirect + window.location.search;
    window.location.replace(redirect);

q2 writes only the canonical pages. The key is dropped with no warning, which is the part that makes this expensive: a porting project gets no signal at all that its redirects are gone.

## Root-cause area

Nothing in crates/ reads 'aliases' — verified at HEAD (1ba0f2ec, the v0.19.0 release merge); every grep hit for the word is an unrelated use (SASS theme aliases, YAML anchor aliases, path aliases). This is unimplemented, not broken.

Two pieces are needed:

1. DocumentProfile (crates/quarto-core/src/document_profile.rs:351) has no aliases field. Add 'pub aliases: Vec<String>' and extract it next to the sibling frontmatter keys around line 695 — extract_string_list(meta, "aliases") is exactly the shape categories: already uses. This bumps DOCUMENT_PROFILE_VERSION (currently 9, line 83).

2. crates/quarto-core/src/project/website_post_render.rs is the natural home for the writer. It already owns exactly this class of work — per-project post-render side files, walking index.profiles(): the favicon copier (line ~66) and the sitemap.xml emitter (line ~150), the latter already iterating profiles and mapping them to output paths.

## Suggested fix direction

Add a write_alias_redirects pass in website_post_render.rs alongside the sitemap writer: for each profile with a non-empty aliases list, resolve each alias against the output directory (absolute aliases are site-root-relative; relative ones resolve against the page's own output location), compute the relative href from the stub back to the page's output_href, and write the Q1 stub template. Worth deciding explicitly: whether to warn or error when two pages claim the same alias, or when an alias collides with a real output path — Q1 lets the stub overwrite, which on a case-insensitive filesystem produces a genuinely confusing result we have already hit in the Connect docs.

## Real-world hit in the Connect docs

69 source files declare aliases:. The Quarto 1 reference site contains 99 redirect stub HTML files that the q2 render omits entirely — that is the whole 451-vs-352 HTML file-count gap between the two rendered sites. Every external link, bookmark and search-engine result pointing at a pre-reorganization Connect docs URL would 404. This is the single largest remaining structural difference between the Q1 and q2 renders of that project; content-wise the port is otherwise at 352 of 352 pages with zero errors.

## Repro

/Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/aliases-redirects-missing/

Run 'q2 render' there: 2 HTML files are written (index.html and current/index.html) where Quarto 1 writes 4, the two extra being the redirect stubs for the aliases declared in current/index.qmd. Compare with 'quarto render'.

Observed continuously from q2 0.15.0 through 0.19.0. Origin strand in the q2-connect-docs skein: br-aliases-redirects-8gk18exz.

c-6wpn8y9p.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-6wpn8y9p.text:
Design decisions settled with the user 2026-08-12 (commit 672cb26f, plan § Design decisions):

1. bd-hzwecpyk closed as duplicate; this is the implementation strand.
2. Collisions are HARD ERRORS, diverging from Q1's warn-and-skip. Three conditions: stub-vs-rendered-page, same alias + same fragment key from two pages, and case-only collisions. New codes Q-5-23+ in the 'project' subsystem.
3. Case-only collisions error on EVERY platform, not just case-insensitive filesystems, so Linux CI fails the same way macOS does.
4. OPEN: stub template. Two candidates written out under the investigation dir. Byte-parity with Q1 explicitly not required; recommendation is the improved stub (noscript meta-refresh fallback, rel=canonical, charset, DOCTYPE, body link).
5. 'aliases:' in a non-website project warns rather than staying silent.
6. Hash fragments implemented properly in the first cut.
7. draft: true pages emit no stubs — leaking a draft's existence via a live redirect is worse than over-hiding it. Cross-linked to bd-4zdf so the sitemap resolves the same way.
8. Stale-stub cleanup deferred to bd-wdhhl0t9.

Consequence worth flagging: decision 2 makes this a breaking change for existing Q1 sites. A project whose alias collisions Q1 tolerated will now fail to render. Phase 6 must check whether the Connect docs' 106 aliases trip it.

c-l7unwmt5.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-l7unwmt5.text:
IMPLEMENTED on branch braid/aliases-redirect-stubs (commit 7c30181d, unpushed). cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build green; 11793 workspace tests pass.

Result: the Connect docs now render 451 HTML files against Q1's 451 — the gap is closed exactly, with all 99 stub paths identical to Q1's.

MAJOR FINDING: the first render of the unmodified Connect docs FAILED with two Q-5-25 case-only-collision errors, and both are real bugs that Q1 has been silently shipping. cookbook/content/integrations/{msgraph,sharepoint}/viewer/r/index.qmd each declare an alias '/…/viewer/R/' (capital R) while rendering to '…/viewer/r/index.html'. On macOS those are one file. Q1's guard is an exact string compare, so it writes the stub on top of the rendered page. Verified in docs-quarto-1/_site: both of those files are redirect stubs whose target is '../r/index.html' — pointing at themselves. Two documentation pages are destroyed in the published Q1 site, replaced by infinite redirect loops.

So the counts reconcile as Q1 = 350 real pages + 101 stubs, q2 = 352 real pages + 99 stubs. Same total; q2 has the two pages Q1 ate.

ACTION NEEDED IN THE PORT REPO (not here): those two aliases must be removed before docs-quarto-2 renders under q2. The 451-vs-451 measurement was taken on a scratch copy with them removed, so the port repo was never modified.

Also fixed two things found on the way:
- config_sources::rebase_source_candidates — a collision diagnostic spans two documents and both root front matter at the dense FileId(0), so the existing binder would have rendered the second document's offsets against the first document's text (the bd-m6wmztln mis-pairing, reached from the other direction).
- orchestrator no longer stringifies post_render errors that already carry diagnostics.

Remaining: user review, then push + PR. Follow-up bd-wdhhl0t9 (stale stubs) still open.

c-o0vzdywr.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-o0vzdywr.text:
Investigated on main @ db075676. Plan skeleton: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-aliases-redirect-stubs.md; artifacts under claude-notes/plans/aliases-redirect-stubs-investigation/.

Verdict: ready to design, pending 7 policy questions in the plan.

Corrections to this strand's description:
- Q1 does NOT let an alias stub overwrite a real output. It warns and skips (website-aliases.ts, 'would overwrite the target. Skipping.'). What Q1 misses is the case-insensitive-filesystem variant, since its guard is an exact string compare.
- Duplicate of bd-hzwecpyk (cderv, 2026-06-23), which already carries the 'blocks bd-0tr6' edge. Dedup is the user's call.

New findings:
- q2 needs none of Q1's ~60-line incremental workaround: Pass 1 profiles every file regardless of RenderMode, so index.profiles() always carries the full alias set in post_render.
- Measured the Connect-docs corpus: 106 unique alias entries across 69 files. 76 site-root-relative, 30 page-relative, 77 trailing-slash, 18 .html, 5 with #fragments. Every Q1 fixupHref branch is exercised.
- Hash fragments are NOT deferrable: cookbook/off-host-execution/creating-execution-environments/index.qmd and cookbook/operations/deploying-content/index.qmd both claim /cookbook/custom-execution-environments/index.html with different fragments pointing at different targets. A fragment-less first cut would emit wrong redirects, not just incomplete ones.
- Ordering hazard: post_render runs before the resource-copy pass, so a declared resource could silently clobber a stub.

title: Project-scoped diagnostics cannot be suppressed by `diagnostics:` policy
description:
The `diagnostics: <CODE>: off` suppression policy (crates/quarto-core/src/diagnostic_policy.rs, bd-lone-bracket-diagnostic-mxu41qbt) cannot reach project-scoped diagnostics. This is documented as a v1 "deliberate limit" in the module doc, but it now has a concrete forcing case.

MECHANISM
Suppression requires all three of:
1. the diagnostic carries a code (`DiagnosticPolicy::suppresses` returns false for `code == None`);
2. it is not an Error (errors are never suppressed, deliberately);
3. it flows through `run_pipeline` -- suppression is applied at exactly ONE site,
   `crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:744`, over `stage_ctx.diagnostics`. That single
   application point is deliberate (see the comment there): every per-document diagnostic
   leaves the pipeline through it, and every frontend reads it from there.

`ProjectRenderSummary::project_diagnostics` (orchestrator.rs) and
`ProjectConfig::config_diagnostics` (project/mod.rs) are assembled OUTSIDE any
StageContext and never pass through `run_pipeline`, so requirement 3 fails for both.

WHY IT WAS PUNTED
The policy is resolved from MERGED DOCUMENT metadata (`MetadataMergeStage`,
metadata_merge.rs:429) -- project -> directory -> document. A project-scoped diagnostic
has no document, so "which document`s policy applies?" has no general answer. Folding
project diagnostics into every document`s set would make them suppressible but print them
once per page (explicitly rejected -- see the `config_diagnostics` doc comment).

WHY IT IS NOW WORTH FIXING
bd-exhbc6h8 routes engine diagnostics into `project_diagnostics` with codes Q-16-10 /
Q-16-11 / Q-16-12. Per Gordon`s D1(c) ruling, Q-16-10 fires for every installed engine
extension that still claims dynamically, whether or not this render used it -- and
`--strict` promotes it (`should_exit_nonzero`, render.rs:1124). So:

  `q2 render --strict` + a third-party Q1-style engine extension
  = a build that cannot be made green by any durable local action.

The user`s only remedies are editing someone else`s `_extension.yml` under `_extensions/`
(lost on the next extension update), uninstalling it, or dropping `--strict`.

FEASIBILITY (the reason this is a task, not an epic)
The "which document" ambiguity does NOT apply to a policy written in `_quarto.yml` --
that is unambiguously project-scoped. The pieces already exist:
- `load_project_config_layers` (project/mod.rs:132) returns `Vec<(PathBuf, ConfigValue)>`,
  so the project-root layer is available as a `ConfigValue`;
- `DiagnosticPolicy::from_metadata` takes exactly a `&ConfigValue`.
So a project-level policy resolution is a few lines. What v1 avoided was introducing a
SECOND resolution path with its own precedence story alongside the merged one -- that is
the design decision to make, not a plumbing problem.

Timing is no longer an obstacle either: bd-exhbc6h8 drains at END of render (so
bd-7keh8iwn`s render-time diagnostics are captured), by which point every document has
been through MetadataMergeStage.

SCOPE
- Decide the precedence story for a project-only `diagnostics:` policy.
- Apply it to `ProjectRenderSummary::project_diagnostics` and (decide whether to)
  `ProjectConfig::config_diagnostics`.
- Keep the "errors are never suppressed" rule.
- Related: bd-m2w7a (backfill codes onto the ~25-30 bare `DiagnosticMessage::warning`
  call sites) is a prerequisite for any diagnostic not already coded.

title: citeproc: locale load failure silently degrades to English citations
description: When a CSL locale fails to load, quarto-citeproc silently produces English output (terms, quotes, date formats) with no diagnostic. A document requesting fr-FR/de-DE/etc. citations can render with English 'and', curly quotes, and English date formats and the user is never told. See GitHub issue (linked) for the full write-up; code refs: crates/quarto-citeproc/src/locale.rs load_embedded_locale (240-266) swallows file-not-found AND parse errors via .ok()?/None; load_locale (41-62) gives up silently; get_term (79-86) and get_quote_config (165-185, e.g. unwrap_or_else(|| "\u{201C}")) substitute hardcoded English. Locales are rust-embed compiled-in, so a None for a known-embedded locale is a build/bug signal, not a normal 'unshipped locale' case. Fix: distinguish unshipped-locale (warn + en-US fallback via DiagnosticMessage) from embedded-locale-load-failure (surface loudly); emit a diagnostic whenever rendered language != requested language. Discovered 2026-06-02 during bd-ooleh when stale-cache pollution (bd-gpyup) made a dead-path locale load return English, surfacing only because a test asserted on French.

title: Import a project from a ZIP archive (hub-client)
description:
Add an 'Import from ZIP' action to the hub-client project selector that creates a NEW project from an uploaded .zip — the inverse of the existing 'Export to ZIP' (ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/export-zip.ts).

Design: parse ZIP (fflate unzipSync) into a file list in the shape createNewProject already accepts (base64 binary, plain-string text), then reuse the existing onProjectCreated path (App.handleProjectCreated -> createNewProject -> IDB + project set + navigate). No Automerge-layer changes needed.

New code:
- ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/import-zip.ts  (parseProjectZip, pure, mirrors export-zip.ts)
- preview-runtime wrapper importProjectFromZip -> ProjectFile[]
- ProjectSelector 'Import from ZIP' button + form (title default from filename, sync server, file picker)

Edge cases: strip common top-level dir (GitHub zips), skip __MACOSX/.DS_Store/dirs, zip-slip guard, binary-vs-text via isBinaryExtension (+ optional UTF-8 sniff), empty/invalid zip errors, export->import round-trip fidelity.

TDD: unit tests for parse (round-trip headline test), preview-runtime shape conversion test, ProjectSelector component test, Playwright e2e + manual browser verification. hub-client change -> npm run build:all + changelog two-commit workflow.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-01-import-from-zip.md
close_reason: Implemented import-from-zip: parser + wrapper + UI + tests + e2e; verified end-to-end in real browser.

title: Render panics in the diagnostic renderer when a config-sourced span ends inside a multi-byte char (k-330 regression; quarto-error-reporting length()-1 fallback)
description: A flagless project render aborts with a Rust panic, exit 101, inside the diagnostic renderer, when a diagnostic's highlighted span ends inside a multi-byte character in a YAML config value: thread 'main' panicked at ariadne-0.6.0/src/write.rs:84:59: end byte index 37 is not a char boundary; it is inside '' (bytes 35..38 of string) The site is written BEFORE the panic, which makes this unusually expensive to diagnose: _site/ is complete and correct, the exit code says total failure, and the rest of the diagnostic stream is silently truncated. On an 85-file project the panic fires ~4s in and cuts off the tail of the log, so a reader sees far fewer problems than actually exist while the exit code claims catastrophe. Neither --json-errors nor NO_COLOR / NO_EMOJI / QUARTO_NO_EMOJI / TERM=dumb avoids it. Q1 behavior: renders the same site with no crash, exit 0, and a complete log. WHAT IS LOAD-BEARING is the multi-byte character's POSITION relative to the span end -- not which character it is, and not "an emoji in a span". Measured on 0.24.0, varying only navbar.left[0].text and holding everything else constant: 'Ask AI ' -> PANIC, end byte 37 inside the char ' Ask AI' -> clean, exit 0 'Ask AI' -> clean, exit 0 'Ask AI ' -> PANIC (not emoji-specific; U+2192 does it too) 'Ask AI ' (no raw HTML) -> clean, exit 0 Two preconditions: (1) a diagnostic must fire on that line at all -- here Q-2-9 "HTML element converted to raw HTML" -- so Q-2-9's noisiness is what escalates this from cosmetic to a crash; and (2) the span must come from the YAML/config path. The same raw HTML with a trailing multi-byte char in a .qmd BODY renders clean at exit 0. PRIOR ART: this looks like the same defect as k-330 (P0, closed 2025-11-05) -- "Error reporting crashes when trying to display errors in text with multi-byte UTF-8 characters. The byte indices don't align with character boundaries when passed to ariadne." The signature also matches k-328 (P0, closed): the reported end offset is 2 bytes into a 3-byte character, the same off-by-two as k-328's checkmark case. Those fixes appear to have covered spans over markdown source; the config/YAML path is uncovered. ROOT CAUSE, located: the panic is in the EXTERNAL crate quarto-error-reporting (workspace dep, version 0.2.1 -- not in this repo), in src/diagnostic.rs. Two adjacent problems there: 1. The ariadne path builds its label range from raw mapped offsets with no char-boundary check: :861 let main_span = start_mapped.location.offset..end_mapped.location.offset; :876 report = report.with_label(Label::new((display_path.clone(), main_span.clone())) ... 2. The end-offset fallback just above it subtracts ONE BYTE, which is precisely how you land mid-character: :808-818 let end_mapped = main_location .map_offset(main_location.length(), ctx) .or_else(|| { // Clamp: if length() fails, try length()-1, which should be the last valid byte if main_location.length() > 0 { main_location.map_offset(main_location.length() - 1, ctx) Its comment says it handles "off-by-one end offsets", but length()-1 on a span ending at a 3-byte character yields an offset 2 bytes into that character -- exactly the observed end=37 for a char occupying bytes 35..38. 3. The sibling (non-ariadne) path DOES clamp, but only against EOF, not against char boundaries: :989 let clamp = |start: usize, end: usize| -> std::ops::Range { let s = start.min(content_len); let e = end.min(content_len).max(s); s..e }; :1008 let main_span = clamp(start_mapped.location.offset, end_mapped.location.offset); So neither path is char-boundary safe; the ariadne one simply panics first. SUGGESTED FIX: make both offsets char-boundary safe before handing them to ariadne -- walk back to the previous boundary rather than the previous byte (str::is_char_boundary in a loop, or floor_char_boundary / ceil_char_boundary), and extend the clamp closure at :989 to do the same so the JSON path cannot silently mis-slice either. Doing it once in the shared span-to-ariadne conversion is preferable to patching the config path only, since that is how the markdown-path fix (k-330) failed to cover this one. Note the fix lands in quarto-error-reporting 0.2.x and will need a release plus a workspace bump, unless q2 clamps before calling it. Worth considering separately: printing a diagnostic should not be able to abort a render whose output has already succeeded, nor discard the diagnostics queued behind it. A panic boundary around diagnostic rendering would have turned this from "render unusable" into "one diagnostic renders badly". REAL-WORLD HIT in the Positron docs: exactly one character in the whole site. _quarto-positron.yml's navbar entry is - text: 'Ask AI ' and that single U+2728 makes every full-project render exit 101 with a truncated log. Triaging the port at all requires stripping the character for the duration of each render and restoring it afterwards; every comparative sweep taken against such a render then shows a spurious navbar difference on all 66 pages, which is itself a false lead. MINIMAL REPRO: /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/ariadne-emoji-panic/ -- two 2-file website projects differing only in the emoji's position. cd repro && q2 render -> exit 101, ariadne panic, _site/index.html still written correctly cd control && q2 render -> exit 0, clean README.md carries the full measured case table above. Origin strand in the Positron-website porting skein: br-ariadne-emoji-panic-va7ekbu8. Observed with q2 0.24.0 (source fdf55e777 = tag v0.24.0, i.e. HEAD; 0 commits after the tag, so not fixed post-release).
close_reason: Fixed and published: quarto-error-reporting 0.2.2 (char-boundary snap) + quarto-source-map 0.1.3 (Location.offset floor), both resolved in q2's root and nested lockfiles; full cargo xtask verify green. Regression coverage re-anchored at unit level and the zero-width consequence measured for both renderers. The panic-boundary class remains open as bd-chmbr0zl (Phase 5).

c-1cxprknq.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-1cxprknq.text:
CRASH FIXED in quarto-error-reporting (local checkout ~/src/quarto-error-reporting, branch main, not yet committed/released). Two corrections to this strand's stated root cause, both measured rather than inferred:

1. The length()-1 fallback at :808-818 is NOT involved. Instrumentation shows used_fallback=false on both diagnostics in the repro.

2. The offending offset is the span START, not the end, and it arrives already-bad from map_offset(0, ctx): start=104, which is 2 bytes into the U+2728 at 102..105. The underlying defect is that config/YAML scalar spans are shifted one byte left onto the opening quote — unconditional, present in the control too, merely invisible on ASCII. Filed as bd-jfl1ba13 (discovered-from this strand); that is where the caret accuracy gets fixed.

The fix here is the defensive half the strand also asked for, done once at the shared conversion as recommended: a DiagnosticMessage::snap_span_to_char_boundaries helper that clamps into the file, floors start / ceils end onto UTF-8 boundaries, and cannot invert. Applied at all four sites that feed a byte offset to a renderer:
  - ariadne Report::build anchor span  (this one also panicked, at write.rs:267, after the label span was fixed — the strand missed it)
  - ariadne main label span            (write.rs:84)
  - ariadne detail label spans
  - the annotate-snippets clamp closure at :989, which now delegates to the helper

Third correction: annotate-snippets is NOT safe-but-wrong as the strand implies. It panics identically (annotate-snippets-0.12.16/src/renderer/source_map.rs:71) on the same input; it just was not the default renderer. Both paths are now covered by tests.

Tests (red before, green after, verified in that order):
  ariadne_span_starting_inside_multibyte_char_does_not_panic
  annotate_snippets_span_starting_inside_multibyte_char_does_not_panic
  snap_span_widens_to_whole_characters   (helper contract: clamp, widen, never invert)
cargo xtask verify green (fmt + clippy -D warnings across feature sets + all tests).

End-to-end against q2 @ workspace-1 with a [patch.crates-io] path override:
  repro/   q2 render -> EXIT 0, no panic, BOTH Q-2-9 warnings printed in full (previously the stream was truncated at the first one)
  control/ q2 render -> EXIT 0, unchanged
_site/index.html still written with the emoji intact.

Still open here: the strand's last point — a panic while printing a diagnostic should not be able to abort a render or discard queued diagnostics. The boundary fix removes this instance but not the class; a catch_unwind boundary around diagnostic rendering is still unimplemented and deserves its own strand if wanted.

Remaining to ship: commit + PR in posit-dev/quarto-error-reporting, release 0.2.2, bump the q2 workspace dep, and drop the local [patch.crates-io] line from workspace-1's Cargo.toml.

c-oz0pmjgz.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-oz0pmjgz.text: CORRECTION to this strand's SUGGESTED FIX section, for anyone working from it later. The strand says: 'extend the clamp closure at :989 to do the same so the JSON path cannot silently mis-slice either.' That conflates two different things. :989 is the ANNOTATE-SNIPPETS RENDERER path (render_annotate_snippets_source_context), not the JSON path. The actual JSON wire shape is produced by diagnostic_to_json in a different file, src/json.rs:169-181, which the strand never mentions. Consequence: following the strand literally fixes :989 (correct, and done) while leaving json.rs untouched under the belief that the JSON path is covered. It is not. AUDIT of what remains liable, after the char-boundary fix: Panic liability: NONE remaining. All six sites that hand a byte offset to a renderer are snapped (ariadne Report::build anchor, ariadne main label, ariadne detail labels, annotate-snippets primary and detail via the clamp closure). The crate's only other byte-slicing sites are safe by construction: - extend_hyperlink_to_include_line_column (diagnostic.rs:1120) indexes at offsets from str::find (always a boundary) and from find_line_column_end, which advances only over ASCII ':' and digits, so every index it returns is a boundary. - the no-renderer structured-text fallback (diagnostic.rs:506) only reads row/column for display; it never slices. src/json.rs:169-181 carries an INDEPENDENT DUPLICATE of the length()-1 fallback that the diagnostic.rs fix did not touch. It cannot panic, and the reason is worth recording: it never slices a string, and map_offset yields CHARACTER columns, not byte columns. Measured on the repro with --json-errors: start_column=15 end_column=28 start_column=36 end_column=43 Byte 104 is mid-emoji; a byte column would be 38, but it reports 36 — a mid-character byte offset collapses to the containing character's column. Lossy but not splittable. What json.rs DOES carry is bd-jfl1ba13's one-off error, silently: '' occupies character columns 37..44, and the wire shape reports 36..43. So the JSON consumers (Monaco/IDE) get the same wrong span as the text path, with no visible caret to reveal it. bd-jfl1ba13 must fix both. Minor inconsistency noticed in passing, not a live bug: json.rs's main-location branch has the length()-1 fallback but its details branch (:210) does not, so the two disagree about how to handle an unmappable end offset.

c-pc5pb5mj.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-pc5pb5mj.text:
SHIPPED AND PUBLISHED. Everything this strand listed as "Remaining to ship" is done.

quarto-error-reporting **0.2.2** published to crates.io 2026-08-22 (PR posit-dev/quarto-error-reporting#5, merge commit 87f1d38a1, CI green on all four checks; Trusted Publishing, release workflow run 32577564699 succeeded). Contents:
- the char-boundary snap (`snap_span_to_char_boundaries`) at the three call sites covering four offsets — the ariadne Report::build anchor and main label (one shared call), the ariadne detail labels, and the annotate-snippets clamp closure;
- that crate's own uptake of quarto-source-map 0.1.3, whose `Location.offset` floor is the upstream half of the fix.

q2 now resolves it: root Cargo.lock and the nested crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/Cargo.lock both at quarto-error-reporting 0.2.2 / quarto-source-map 0.1.3 / quarto-yaml 0.1.3. No [patch.crates-io] override remains in either manifest (confirmed by name in both). Full `cargo xtask verify` green, all 14 steps including the WASM leg, tree clean.

TWO THINGS WORTH RECORDING BEYOND THE FIX.

1. The two regression tests this strand's comment cites (`ariadne_span_starting_inside_multibyte_char_does_not_panic` and its annotate-snippets sibling) STOPPED COVERING THE SNAP the moment the crate took quarto-source-map 0.1.2+. Both build `SourceInfo::original(fid, 21, 28)`, and the floor snaps 21 to 19 in `map_offset` before any renderer is reached — so they stay green while guaranteeing nothing. Before taking the floor we deliberately ran the binding experiment on the old lock (reverting the snap, watching the ariadne test go red with `end byte index 21 is not a char boundary; it is inside U+2728` at ariadne-0.6.0/src/write.rs:84:59) because that evidence becomes unrecoverable afterwards. Both tests were then renamed to `..._renders_diagnostic_with_originally_mid_character_span`, their doc comments rewritten to say what they now cover and why, with an explicit accepted-unbound note; the real coverage moved to `snap_span_widens_to_whole_characters`, extended with the same 21..28 pair over the same content, asserted directly against the helper (19..28).

2. The strand's comment noted the zero-width consequence as a likelihood ("a zero-width label very likely renders"). It is now MEASURED, for both renderers, on `x = 'A U+2728 B'` with `original(fid, 7, 8)` (both ends inside the character): after the floor both ends arrive as 6, so the highlight is zero-width. ariadne draws a bare vertical bar; annotate-snippets draws a single caret. At the whole-character span (6,9) they draw the T-shape and a double caret respectively. The test keys on that marker SHAPE, and its discrimination was verified twice independently (implementer and reviewer each swapped the fixture to (6,9), observed the failure, and restored).

The class-level concern this strand raised last — that printing a diagnostic should not be able to abort a render or discard queued diagnostics — is NOT closed here. It is bd-chmbr0zl, and it is Phase 5 of claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-2-consumers.md (still to do).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-2-consumers.md, Phase 1. Epic bd-mxa44voa.

title: Hub: AuthMeResponse.exp is semantically polymorphic (sliding session exp vs fixed Google exp)
description: GET /auth/me returns exp = sliding session expiry on the cookie path but the Google token's fixed exp on the Bearer path, with nothing in the response distinguishing them (crates/quarto-hub/src/server.rs:1268-1288). Harmless today (only the SPA reads it) but a latent trap for any Bearer caller. Fix: add a credential discriminator field to AuthMeResponse, document exp semantics per kind, update authService.AuthState, and remove useAuth's dead pre-sliding DEFAULT_SESSION_MS=1h fallback (hub-client/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:42). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-03-bearer-revocation-and-mcp-auth-followups.md (F3).
close_reason: Implemented: AuthMeResponse.credential session|bearer discriminator (additive, exp unchanged); SPA AuthState carries it and the dead 1h DEFAULT_SESSION_MS fallback is removed (absent exp -> no scheduled expiry re-check). TDD both halves; full cargo xtask verify green; e2e against the real hub binary verified both discriminator values and exp semantics. Changelog two-commit workflow applied. Merged --no-ff into feature/auth-review-followups.

title: Hoist nested-cargo env stripping into shared xtask helper
description:
Every xtask subcommand that shells out to a nested cargo (verify, build-all, test, stage-doc-examples) inherits the outer 'cargo xtask' process's package env vars — most importantly CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=.../crates/xtask. The ring build script (base of the rustls/reqwest TLS stack) fingerprints CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, so the inherited value marks it dirty and forces a full multi-minute rebuild of that dependency closure on EVERY nested invocation whenever the prior build came from a plain shell (or 'cargo build --workspace', which CLAUDE.md tells everyone to run). Diagnosed via CARGO_LOG=cargo::core::compiler::fingerprint=info while investigating a 'stage-doc-examples hangs' report: dirty: EnvVarChanged { name: "CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR", old_value: None, new_value: Some(".../crates/xtask") }.

stage-doc-examples is already fixed inline (strips the vars before spawning + dropped --quiet). This strand hoists that env-stripping into a shared helper in crates/xtask/src/util.rs (strip_inherited_cargo_env / nested_command) and routes the other nested-cargo sites through it: verify.rs run_command, build_all.rs run_command (currently duplicated), test.rs. This removes avoidable minutes from 'cargo xtask verify' and de-duplicates the two identical run_command impls.

TDD: test via Command::get_envs() that the helper marks CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/CARGO_PKG_*/OUT_DIR as removed. Verify end-to-end with the ping-pong scenario (cargo build --workspace; then cargo xtask <cmd>) showing no TLS-stack rebuild via the fingerprint log.
close_reason: Implemented + verified e2e; committed a0e88619 on branch beads/bd-awchm8w7-nested-cargo-env. Shared util::strip_inherited_cargo_env / nested_command; routed stage-doc-examples, verify, build-all, test through it; dropped --quiet. 0 TLS rebuilds in nested xtask builds, 80/80 xtask tests pass.

- verify (rust-build leg): after a one-time cache-settling rebuild (my earlier pre-fix runs had polluted ring's fingerprint with CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=Some(xtask)), stable at 0 rebuilds. Proven both directions: clean-shell build -> verify -> clean-shell build all show 0 TLS rebuilds, 0 CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR-dirty events.

title: Monaco .qmd highlighting applied immediately on file open (skip debounce)
description: On file open the editor remounts and re-registered the intelligence providers, which made Monaco reschedule the semantic-tokens fetch behind its adaptive debounce (~300ms) instead of the immediate schedule(0) a freshly-attached model gets. Fix: register providers once (idempotent), expose a provider onDidChange emitter fired on mount (forces schedule(0)), and re-fire once on WASM loading->ready to cover the cold-start first file. Follow-up to the merged highlighting epic bd-t4ezufyg.

title: hub: diffToMonacoEdits offsetToPosition LF-only misplaces edits on CRLF
description: In the hub editor, hub-client/src/utils/diffToMonacoEdits.ts offsetToPosition around line 32 scans for newline only and counts carriage return as a column character, while Monaco line and column exclude the line ending, so on CRLF documents the computed Monaco positions can be off by one column and misplace edits. The hub pipeline otherwise preserves bytes end to end (disk to Automerge to VFS to WASM, no normalization), so CRLF genuinely reaches this code. Make offsetToPosition CRLF-aware and reconcile with Monaco position semantics. Windows-testable end to end against a running hub with a CRLF document. Reference claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-prior-art.md hub section.

Q1 and Q2 both request 400;700 (crates/quarto-sass/src/brand_layer.rs enumerate_weights default). Decide whether to follow the reference (heavier font download, but bold/light slots always resolve) or keep Q1 parity, then document the choice in docs/guides/authoring/brand.qmd.
