title: SPA getBinaryDocById missing automerge: URL prefix → binary capture docs never reach WASM
description: ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/client.ts:getBinaryDocById passes the bare docId from the IndexDocument capture sidecar straight to repo.find(). The samod TS library rejects this with 'Error: Invalid AutomergeUrl: <id>' because it requires the 'automerge:' scheme prefix. The text-doc loader (loadFileDocuments) prepends the prefix explicitly (lines 305-307); getBinaryDocById doesn't. Net effect: every project-mode q2 preview render falls back to the default registry because captureGzJson is undefined, and code cells render as inert source — the exact user-reported bug. Diagnosed end-to-end on 2026-05-18 against the fixture website. Trivial fix: same 'automerge:' prefix-normalize pattern as loadFileDocuments. Critical because it makes the entire Phase C.4 replay path silently inert for real users.
close_reason: Fixed. getBinaryDocById now calls normalizeDocId() before findDoc() (ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/client.ts:1145) — the same normalization the text-doc loaders use. Landed in 6bd9d591 (bd-81cfshmw MCP/sync-reliability PR), which is why this strand was never closed: the fix and its tests are labeled with the dead duplicate id bd-4uvv (closed 2026-06-08 as dup of this strand). Regression tests at client.test.ts:335 cover bare-id and already-prefixed cases; both pass (verified 2026-07-27). Caveat: verified via code path + unit tests (which mock repo.find()); not re-verified through a live q2 preview browser session.

title: Preview does not apply user-declared css (VFS mode)
description: q2 preview (and the hub-client) render via the WASM pipeline in VFS-root mode, where FormatCssTransform deliberately no-ops (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/format_css.rs) — so format.html.css / document css: stylesheets are linked and applied in q2 render output but not in the preview iframe (verified 2026-08-14 in a real browser session: preview page renders, no user css link, marker custom property absent). Q-5-29 emission is also cfg-gated to native because the VFS is not authoritative for non-qmd project files — a stylesheet present on disk may not be synced, which produced false warnings in the preview overlay before the gate. Fixing this needs the preview to sync declared css files into the VFS (or serve them from the source tree) and the transform to emit VFS-mode hrefs; see /preview-parity skill and the design notes in claude-notes/plans/2026-08-14-format-css-not-copied.md.

title: bootHarness identity probe never waits: waitForFunction treats promise predicate as truthy
description: Playwright 1.60 waitForFunction does not await a promise-returning predicate; the Promise object is truthy so it returns after one poll. bootHarness's identity probe therefore never waited; the identity write raced app boot. Masked under vite dev by slow module loading (occasional CI beforeEach flakes); deterministic 30s deadlock per test under vite preview (write's transaction throws on the missing store, leaking a connection that blocks the app's schema migration). Fixed with a Node-side poll loop guarded by indexedDB.databases().

title: Website render: files referenced via format.html.css are not copied to the output dir

description:

Examples missing from the preview UI: [Q-13-4] body-link-references-missing-document, [Q-1-20] failed-to-parse-metadata-as-markdown — emitted by the WASM render pipeline (arrive in result.warnings) and by three server-side callsites (capture_driver.rs, deps.rs, re_execute.rs) that tracing::warn!() to stderr today.

Scope (post user sign-off 2026-05-21):
(1) Per-page WASM-render diagnostics threaded into a forked PreviewDiagnosticsOverlay (in q2-preview-spa/, not the shared @quarto/preview-renderer one — keeps the two surfaces free to evolve independently). Collapsed by default for warnings.
(2) Server-side infrastructure: DiagnosticSink in crates/quarto-preview/ + GET /api/preview/diagnostics endpoint + migration of the three existing tracing::warn!() callsites. Avoids paying the plumbing tax every time someone adds a new warning.
(3) Out of scope: project-wide aggregation UI, richer engine diagnostics, CLI parity, re-converging the forked overlay.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-21-q2-preview-diagnostics-surface.md (DESIGN APPROVED — ready for TDD implementation).

End-to-end verified against docs/ — both [Q-13-4] body-link and [Q-1-20] metadata-as-markdown warnings from the original problem statement surface in the overlay. Merged to main as merge commit. title: sidebar.auto: drops invalid and project-escaping glob patterns silently
description:
After bd-mt7a6uc4 Phase 4, sidebar.auto: uses the shared glob API, but auto_matcher() (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/sidebar_auto.rs) discards GlobResolution::escaped and ::invalid. So 'auto: "a**b.qmd"' (uncompilable) and 'auto: "../outside"' (escapes the project root) contribute nothing with no message. If every pattern in a spec fails, the pre-existing Q-13-6 fires but blames 'matched no documents' rather than naming the bad pattern; if one pattern of several fails, nothing is reported at all.

The other three glob consumers report all three failure modes (Q-5-13/14/15 for project.render, Q-5-1/2/16 for resources, Q-12-17/18/19 for listings). Sidebar is the last silent case.

Wiring is easy on one side: expand_spec already receives &mut Vec<DiagnosticMessage> (that is how Q-13-6 is emitted), so it is two new Q-13-* codes plus crate::glob::diagnostics builders. The catch is provenance: sidebar_auto synthesizes SourceInfo::generated(programmatic_config) because AutoSpec carries no source info, so the diagnostics would name the pattern but point at no line. Matching the quality of Q-5-13/Q-12-19 means teaching AutoSpec to carry SourceInfo through quarto-navigation's parser (Sidebar::parse_list_from_config), which is a larger change in a crate bd-mt7a6uc4 otherwise did not touch.

Cheap version: report both failures span-less. Proper version: add provenance to AutoSpec first.

title: preview parity: inline <code> forwards data-hl-spans instead of decoding it
description:
Fixture: highlighting/02-inline-code.qmd. This fixture trips the harness's forbid rule rather than reaching the mismatch/norm.txt path, so there is no render.norm.txt/preview.norm.txt pair — the harness aborts as soon as it sees the forbidden attribute.

## Evidence

survey.json entry:
```json
{
  "rel": "highlighting/02-inline-code.qmd",
  "status": "rule-violation",
  "detail": "forbidden attribute 'data-hl-spans' on <code> — see PARITY_RULES.forbidAttrs"
}
```

## Root cause

`ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/inlines/Code.tsx:8-9` forwards every `data-*` kv verbatim onto the `<code>` element:
```
for (const [k, v] of kvs) {
    if (k.startsWith('data-')) props[k] = v;
}
```
This includes `data-hl-spans` (the encoded highlight-span data Rust attaches to a highlighted inline code span), which should never reach the DOM as a raw attribute — it needs decoding.

The native writer decodes it instead of forwarding it: `crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:938-949` (the `Inline::Code` arm) calls `read_hl_spans(&c.attr)` and, when present, `write_highlighted_body(&c.text, spans, ctx)` to emit the nested `<span>` highlight markup, rather than emitting `data-hl-spans` as an attribute.

bd-nxslt (closed) fixed the analogous problem for block-level code (`CodeBlock.tsx`) — this is the same defect in the inline `Code.tsx` component, which was apparently not covered by that fix.

Fix should end with `dom-parity: true` on the fixture(s). Found by the DOM parity harness (whole-corpus survey, 2026-08-24). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-preview-render-dom-parity-harness.md

title: Q-10-* code collision: citeproc and doctemplate emit the same Q-10-* codes for different errors
description:
While authoring template subsystem error-docs (bd-4ltdl) the following code collision surfaced.

The catalog assigns Q-10-1 through Q-10-7 to the 'template' subsystem with these titles:
- Q-10-1: Template Parse Error
- Q-10-2: Undefined Variable
- Q-10-3: Partial Not Found
- Q-10-4: Recursive Partial
- Q-10-5: Unresolved Partial Reference
- Q-10-6: Unknown Pipe
- Q-10-7: Invalid Pipe Arguments

These match the doctemplate emit sites in crates/quarto-doctemplate (Q-10-2 at evaluator.rs:224, Q-10-5 at evaluator.rs:336, Q-10-6 at pipes.rs:64, Q-10-7 at pipes.rs:209+).

HOWEVER, crates/quarto-citeproc/src/error.rs also emits Q-10-1 through Q-10-5 for completely different errors:
- citeproc Q-10-1: Locale Parse Error
- citeproc Q-10-2: Reference Not Found
- citeproc Q-10-3: Invalid Reference
- citeproc Q-10-4: Missing Required Field
- citeproc Q-10-5: Invalid Date

This is a code collision. Q-10-2 and Q-10-5 are emitted by BOTH crates with different meanings, and Q-10-1/3/4 are emitted by citeproc with meanings that contradict the catalog.

Additionally, Q-10-1, Q-10-3, Q-10-4 from the catalog (template subsystem) have no doctemplate emit site at all — only the contradictory citeproc emit sites.

Resolution options:
1. Reassign citeproc to a new subsystem range (e.g., Q-10b-* or rename to citation subsystem with Q-NN-*).
2. Reassign template to a new subsystem range.
3. Audit which interpretation is canonical and add catalog entries for the unclassified emit sites.

The docs/errors/template/Q-10-*.qmd pages document the catalog's template meanings (doctemplate); they will be misleading for users who hit the citeproc errors.

Sibling drift issues: bd-xly8b (markdown), bd-fiv9u (writer).

title: preview parity: callout body heading not sectionized in preview
description:
Fixture: toc-containers/callout-body-heading-not-in-toc.qmd. Render sectionizes the callout body's heading (`

`); preview keeps it flat (`

`). Which side is "right" needs a decision — the sectionize-into-callout-body behavior looks like a possible render-side quirk (Q1 explicitly does NOT sectionize into a `div.callout`, per the fixture's own doc-comment quoted below), and the fixture's own assertion is only that the heading stays out of the TOC, which both sides satisfy. This may be "preview is correct, render should stop sectionizing here" rather than "preview needs to sectionize." ## Evidence render.norm.txt: ```

"Quarto 1 sectionizes it (" "

" ") but the walk stops at the enclosing " "div.callout" "." ...
...

"Body heading" ``` preview.norm.txt: ```
...

"Body heading" ``` ## Root cause `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/sectionize.rs:56` delegates to `pampa::transforms::sectionize_blocks` (`crates/pampa/src/transforms/sectionize.rs:75`), a flat `Vec` walk that only recognizes plain `Div`/`Header` blocks — it does not recurse into a `CustomNode`'s slot content. `"callout-resolve"` is on `Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED` (`crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:1524`). In the render pipeline, `callout-resolve` runs BEFORE `sectionize`, converting the `Callout` CustomNode into a plain `div.callout > div.callout-body-container` tree — so `sectionize` walks into that div and wraps its `

` into a `
`. In preview, `callout-resolve` is skipped, so `sectionize` runs while the callout body is still opaque `CustomNode` slot content and never sees the `

`; React's port (`ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/custom/Callout.tsx`, body rendered around lines 202-206 via `renderSlot(contentSlot, ...)`) then renders the still-unsectioned heading directly. Fix should end with `dom-parity: true` on the fixture(s). Found by the DOM parity harness (whole-corpus survey, 2026-08-24). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-preview-render-dom-parity-harness.md

title: WebsiteProjectType::post_render has no format gate, unlike Q1's own websitePostRender
description:
Confirmed 2026-09-18 during the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic's user-facing/backward-compat review,
then independently verified against Q1's real TypeScript source per Gordon's direction.

Q2's WebsiteProjectType::post_render (crates/quarto-core/src/project/orchestrator.rs:481-575)
runs its full hook sequence (copy_favicon, copy_navbar_logo, copy_footer_images, write_sitemap,
write_robots_txt, write_alias_redirects, substitute_listing_placeholders,
complete_staged_feeds) against whatever outputFiles it's given, with no format check anywhere in
the file.

**Verified what Q1 actually does** (src/project/types/website/website.ts): Q1's own
`websiteProjectType.postRender` calls `websitePostRender(context, incremental,
websiteOutputFiles(outputFiles))` - and `websiteOutputFiles` FILTERS its input to HTML files
only: `outputFiles.filter((outputFile) => isHtmlFileOutput(outputFile.format.pandoc))`
(website.ts, the function immediately following postRender). So updateSitemap,
completeListingGeneration, updateAliases, and updateLlmsTxt in Q1 only ever see HTML outputs -
they are structurally incapable of pointing a sitemap/redirect at a docx file, because non-HTML
files are removed from their input list before they run. (One exception: `ensureIndexPage` runs
unconditionally and writes a redirect index.html if none exists and can resolve a target from
the first project input - this one may need a closer look for a pure non-HTML project render,
but it is a narrower, more contained behavior than "run the whole post-render suite
unconditionally".)

Q2 has no equivalent filter. This is a pre-existing gap (not introduced by the
pandoc-writer-hybrid epic - the bug has just never been reachable before, since Q2 previously
only supported HTML/revealjs, both website-appropriate formats). The pandoc-writer-hybrid epic
makes it reachable: `q2 render <website-project> --to docx` today would run every website
post-render hook against docx-only output, producing e.g. a sitemap.xml with `<loc>` entries
pointing at `.html` files that don't exist.

**Not epic scope**: this is a general Q2 project-orchestration correctness fix (match Q1's own
established behavior), not new functionality, and not specific to the pandoc-hybrid work - it
belongs in crates/quarto-core/src/project/orchestrator.rs's existing website post-render code,
independent of any Pandoc-specific plan. Fix: filter outputFiles to HTML-only (matching Q1's
`isHtmlFileOutput` check) before running sitemap/search-index/alias/feed update logic; audit
`ensureIndexPage`-equivalent code for the same nonexistent-target-target case.

See claude-notes/designs/pandoc-hybrid-architecture.md for the epic context that surfaced this.

title: theorem.rs miscomments the attribute value span as excluding quotes
description:
crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/theorem.rs:317-319 documents AttrSourceInfo.attributes[i].1 as 'an Original covering the bytes between the = and the matching quote'. It actually covers the quotes INCLUSIVELY: the tree-sitter rule aliases a token that contains the delimiters (crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js:580-585), and commonmark_attribute.rs:39-51 records the full node range. extract_quoted_text testing text.starts_with('"') on the node's own text only makes sense if the quotes are inside the node.

Comment-only fix, but the comment is load-bearing: it is the doc future callers read before deciding how to map an attribute value span, and believing it produces an off-by-one. Same wrong assumption would have shipped in the callout title= fix. See claude-notes/plans/callout-title-attribute-investigation/escape-drift-probe.md.

Check proof.rs:170-190 for the same wording while fixing.

title: Regression in 0.29.0: markdown on the line after a raw HTML block line is emitted verbatim
description:
Since 0.29.0, a line of prose immediately following a raw HTML block line is emitted verbatim instead of being parsed as markdown. Backticks, asterisks and every other inline construct survive into the rendered page as literal text. Quarto 1 (99.9.9) parses them, as does bare pandoc 3.8.1, and so did q2 0.28.0 and 0.27.0. Introduced by bd-block-html-wrapped-in-p-w8qebxig (PR #646, commit bdacd1122); that fix is otherwise correct and its own four cases all now match Q1 and pandoc byte for byte. User-visible symptom, on a real page:
Example custom instructions This example demonstrates how a `quarto.instructions.md` file shapes ... renders as Example custom instructions This example demonstrates how a `quarto.instructions.md` file shapes Positron Assistant behavior ... anything ending with `.instructions.md`.

By automatically applying these rules to all .qmd files, ... Note the next paragraph — separated by a blank line — renders its code spans correctly. A blank line is where the parser recovers, which is why this reads to an author like a content typo rather than an engine bug. ROOT CAUSE. crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/paragraph.rs, process_paragraph(). A paragraph whose first inline is a block-level HTML tag is lifted into a VERBATIM Block::RawBlock: if paragraph_starts_block_html(&inlines) { let text = verbatim_text(node, input_bytes); return ...Block::RawBlock(RawBlock { format: "html", text, ... }) The commit justifies this on extent: 'a markdown paragraph and a CommonMark type-6 HTML block both run to the next blank line, so lifting the whole paragraph reproduces the HTML block exactly.' The extent reasoning is correct. What it does not address is CONTENT TREATMENT — whether the interior is still parsed. Pandoc and Q1 lift the extent AND keep parsing inside it; this lift stops parsing. The commit message records the consequence as an accepted limitation ('a tight

/
with no blank lines stays one verbatim RawBlock, so markdown inside it is not processed'), but Q1 processes it, so for anyone porting a Q1 project it is a parity break rather than a gap in an unsupported form. THE CONFLATION, which is the useful part for a fix. The commit dismisses pandoc's native_divs/native_spans with 'they need balanced tag matching across block content, which is the backtracking approach syntax-notes.md rejects, and the HTML output is identical without them.' That last clause holds for native_divs alone but does not cover this change. Measured on a tight
containing a code span and emphasis: pandoc -f markdown ->

wrapper, / (native_divs promotes to Div) pandoc -f markdown-native_divs -> no

, / pandoc -f markdown-native_divs-markdown_in_html_blocks -> no

, literal backticks q2 0.29.0 -> byte-identical to the third row Dropping native_divs costs the

wrapper and the Div AST node, which is exactly what PR #646 wanted. It does NOT cost inline markdown parsing — that is markdown_in_html_blocks, a separate pandoc extension that both pandoc and Q1 leave on, and which the verbatim lift switched off as a side effect. The two extensions were conflated. SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION. No balanced tag matching and no native_divs are needed. Keep the lift and its extent; change the lifted block's interior so it still goes through the inline parser (markdown_in_html_blocks behaviour), emitting the raw tag lines as raw and the intervening text as parsed content. That is compatible with the no-backtracking constraint dev-docs/syntax-notes.md imposes, since the extent is already decided by the paragraph boundary. SCOPE NOT YET MEASURED. The lift applies to the whole BLOCK_TAGS whitelist in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/html_block.rs (~60 pandoc block tags). Only

and
/ have been measured; the blast radius is likely wider. REAL-WORLD HIT. Positron docs, assistant-chat-instructions.qmd:61-63 — the
/ shape above. The rendered page carries literal backticks around 'quarto.instructions.md' and '.instructions.md'. In the 0.28.0-to-0.29.0 A/B over that site this is the only new visible-text difference (1 line, 1 page), against 73 chrome lines and 1 text line the same release fixed. REPRO: /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/block-html-adjacent-markdown-unparsed/ — run 'sh check.sh', or 'sh check.sh ~/.local/bin/q2.0.28.0-backup' for the pre-regression behaviour. It renders one fixture with q2, Quarto 1 and bare pandoc and reports per case whether markdown was parsed. Case C (the same prose in a ::: fenced div) is the control and parses on every engine; case A2 (prose after a blank line, still inside
) shows where the parser recovers, and is the one row where Q1 and pandoc disagree — Q1 parses it, pandoc does not, and q2 0.29.0 already matches Q1 there. Observed with q2 0.29.0 (official release build). q2 HEAD is 0551c54e4, the v0.29.0 tag itself, with no commits after it, so this is not fixed upstream. Origin strand: br-block-html-adjacent-markdown-unparsed-utxvuyue in the q2-positron-docs skein.

title:
Block-level raw HTML is parsed as inline, so a standalone
or
is wrapped in a spurious
description:
CommonMark and Pandoc both treat a line beginning with a block-level HTML tag as an HTML block. q2 has no HTML-block concept at all: every raw HTML tag becomes an Inline::RawInline, so a standalone
or
lands inside a paragraph and the emitted output carries a spurious

wrapper. Source:

SHA-256 checksums Text inside the details.
Quarto 1 (and bare pandoc) emit:
SHA-256 checksums

Text inside the details.

q2 emits:

SHA-256 checksums

Text inside the details.

This is invalid HTML.
and
are flow content, not phrasing content, so a browser's HTML5 parser force-closes the

and reparents everything that follows. The DOM the page ends up with is not the one the markup describes, which can change what CSS selectors match — descendant and child combinators especially. The failure mode is a styling one, invisible to any text-level comparison. WHAT CORRECT IS (measured, not assumed) Quarto 1's rendered body is byte-identical to bare pandoc 3.8.1's across the whole fixture, so this is pandoc's own behaviour rather than a Quarto convention. Pandoc's block-level AST for the four cases: Para Div <- case 1, bare

Para RawBlock '
' <- case 2 RawBlock '' Plain RawBlock '' Para RawBlock '
' Para RawBlock '' <- case 3 Para Div <- case 4, fenced div Note the asymmetry, which a fix should not flatten: a *balanced
* is not passed through verbatim. Pandoc's native_divs extension (default-on for the markdown reader) promotes it to a real Div node, so a bare
and a ::: fenced div produce the SAME AST, and the text between the tags becomes a proper Para. native_spans does the same for inline. Every other block-level tag —
, , an HTML comment — becomes a RawBlock, one per tag line. Confirmed by toggling: `pandoc -f markdown-native_divs` turns the bare
into RawBlock / Para / RawBlock. The HTML output is identical either way, so the user-visible requirement is unambiguous (no

wrapper), but the AST distinction matters for filters and non-HTML writers. ROOT CAUSE There is no HTML-block production. `html_block` appears zero times in both crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js and its src/scanner.c. `$.html_element` appears only in the inline choice list (grammar.js:645) and in the externals list (grammar.js:1192), where its comment reads "best-effort lexing of HTML elements simply for error reporting." The conversion itself is the html_element arm in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:~1653, which emits the Q-2-9 warning "HTML element converted to raw HTML" and produces an Inline::RawInline. That is the design from k-334 (Convert naked HTML elements to warnings with auto-fix to RawInline, plan claude-notes/plans/2025-11-12-html-element-warning-autofix.md), which deliberately routed all naked HTML to RawInline. The defect is that the design has no block-level case, not that the inline case is wrong. Both target node types already exist and are wired through: Block::RawBlock is produced in several places (fenced_code_block.rs:75 for {=html} fences, section.rs:32, document.rs) and the HTML writer handles it at crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:1482; Div is constructed in treesitter_utils/fenced_div_block.rs. The missing piece is purely the parse. SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION Add an HTML-block production to the markdown grammar following CommonMark's seven HTML block types (leaf blocks, section 4.6), and have the reader map it to Block::RawBlock — with the native_divs/native_spans case routed to Div/Span instead, matching pandoc. Q-2-9's message will want revisiting at the same time: it says "converted to RawInline nodes with format 'html'" and suggests ``{=html}, neither of which is right for a block, and it does not mention that a

was introduced. REAL-WORLD HIT The Positron docs page download.qmd:190-191 authors

/ SHA-256 checksums as raw HTML. The rendered page carries '

', three '

' and one '

'. It is malformed enough that a tag-stack based HTML comparator loses
and reclassifies the entire SHA-256 checksums table — platform names, installer filenames, sizes, hashes — as page chrome: 74 lines, and the ONLY chrome difference across the whole 113-page site at 0.28.0. The page's visible text diff is zero, so this is invisible to a text-level sweep and shows up only as an unexplained region shift. That page became observable only recently: it could not render at all until the knitr inline-R fix landed in 0.28.0, which is why the instance surfaced now. The defect is not a 0.28.0 regression — the fixture wraps identically on 0.24.0, 0.26.0, 0.27.0 and 0.28.0. A second instance, docs-quarto-2/index.qmd, was fixed docs-side by switching to a ::: fenced div, which is better authoring anyway and is the recommended migration. But a site that genuinely needs raw block HTML has no way to get it. REPRO /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/block-html-wrapped-in-p/ cd && sh check.sh Four cases plus a fenced-div control. check.sh renders with q2, then Quarto 1, then bare pandoc, and prints both the paragraph-wrapping evidence and pandoc's block-level AST. Pass a different binary as $1 to check another build. VERSION Verified at q2 0.28.0 and at q2 source main 9ad1d4420 (no HTML-block or raw-HTML commits since the v0.28.0 tag). References: quarto 99.9.9 dev build, pandoc 3.8.1. Origin strand: br-block-html-wrapped-in-p-x2qqchu3 in the q2-positron-docs skein.

or after

c-l2od6rmn.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-l2od6rmn.text: Fixed on braid/bd-block-html-wrapped-in-p-w8qebxig-block-html-wrapped-in-p (bdacd1122), not yet pushed. APPROACH. Reader-level lift rather than a grammar/scanner HTML-block production. A paragraph whose first inline is a block-level raw HTML tag becomes a Block::RawBlock carrying the paragraph's verbatim source text. This works because a markdown paragraph and a CommonMark type-6 HTML block have the same extent — both run to the next blank line — so the cheap rule reproduces type 6 on the shapes that matter, with no external-scanner work. POSTURE. The strand proposed following pandoc (CommonMark seven types + native_divs). Research turned up q2's documented position, which points the other way: crates/pampa/README.md:79 lists 'no naked HTML support: use {=html} raw blocks and inlines' among *intentional* divergences, and dev-docs/syntax-notes.md:235 rejects pandoc's approach by name because it 'relies heavily on backtracking through parser combinators'. The README line was re-asserted 2025-12-04, three weeks after k-334 softened Q-2-6 to the Q-2-9 warning — so k-334 changed the enforcement, not the posture. Every user-facing docs example uses {=html}. Gordon confirmed: reader-lift, keep the warning. So this is a bug fix that makes a deprecated fallback emit valid HTML, not a new feature. SCOPED OUT, with reasons in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/html_block.rs: - CommonMark type 7 (any complete tag alone on a line). Measured against pandoc 3.8.1: it would newly break Q1 parity for , , , — all common. Tag set is pandoc's blockTags + eitherBlockOrInline instead. - pandoc's DocBook names (, , ...) and the type-6 names pandoc lacks (,

title: provide-hub reads 0 files from a hub-client project: JS stores files-map ids as automerge Text, Rust get_all_files uses to_str()
description:
q2 provide-hub cannot sync a project created/edited in hub-client: the samod provider peer materializes 0 files for a document authored by a JS automerge-repo peer, so materialization + execution fail with "project discovery failed: Failed to canonicalize path: No such file or directory". Discovered during Phase 4 manual e2e (bd-sfet3264).

RELIABLE HEADLESS REPRO (all local, no browser):
1. Standalone storage hub: q2 hub --no-project --data-dir /tmp/hd --port 3033
2. JS creator (stand-in for hub-client; @automerge/automerge-repo 2.5.6): new Repo({network:[WebSocketClientAdapter('ws://127.0.0.1:3033')]}); handle=repo.create(); handle.change(d=>{d.files={'index.qmd':'x'}; d.version=2}); print handle.documentId; stay alive.
3. Provider probe: PROBE_SERVER=ws://127.0.0.1:3033 PROBE_DOC_ID=<id> cargo nextest run -p quarto-hub-provider --test integration probe_live_doc_sync --run-ignored all --no-capture
   => find returns Some(handle) but get_all_files() == 0 for 20s+ (never syncs). Also repros against wss://sync.automerge.org and against q2 hub --project for a hub-client-created (foreign) doc. Killing the JS peer leaves find=Some (hub stored the doc) but still 0 files.

WHAT WORKS (isolation, in crates/quarto-hub-provider/tests/integration/):
- relay_sync.rs (2 tests, self-contained, PASS): samod peer A creates a doc, samod peer B syncs it through a bare relay AND through a NeverAnnounce relay. So it is NOT the announce policy and NOT the BearerDialer.
- sync_probe.rs::probe_create_then_find (ignored, network): two SAMOD peers via sync.automerge.org — B syncs A's doc instantly.
=> The gap is specifically DOCUMENTS CREATED BY A JS automerge-repo PEER being read by a Rust samod peer.

LIKELY CAUSE: version/protocol gap. hub-client uses @automerge/automerge-repo 2.5.6 + @automerge/automerge 3.2.6 (JS); samod q2 fork uses Rust automerge 0.8.0. samod-as-relay (JS<->JS, the shipping product) works; samod-as-peer reading a JS-authored doc's content does not. Check whether the samod q2 fork's target automerge-repo/automerge version predates hub-client's, and whether samod↔automerge-repo-2.5.6 sync is supported.

WHY PHASE 4 TESTS MISSED IT: the Phase 4a integration test (execute.rs) used a bare samod acceptor as the stand-in "editor" (samod-created doc), not a real automerge-repo/JS peer — so samod↔samod passed while the real hub-client↔samod path is broken. Repro/regression harness now added (relay_sync.rs + sync_probe.rs + a JS creator).

IMPACT: the remote-execution feature does not work end-to-end with a real hub-client project as-is (likely including quarto-hub.com, which is also samod-based; unverified due to auth). Reverse direction (samod-authored capture doc -> JS hub-client display) is also suspect and untested. NEXT: dedicated investigation of the samod<->automerge-repo-2.5.6/automerge-3.2.6 sync compatibility.
close_reason: Landed: fix ac1457d4 on main (read Text-valued file ids). Audit bd-a0eyjshu.

c-hynrayt9.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-hynrayt9.text:
FIX IMPLEMENTED + verified end-to-end (commit ac1457d4). crates/quarto-hub/src/index.rs: new read_str_or_text helper; get_all_files/get_file now accept scalar Str OR Text-object string values. Rust-authored (project-mode) docs unaffected; hub-client (automerge 3.x Text) docs now read.

Tests: index.rs get_all_files_reads_text_valued_ids; materialize.rs materializes_a_js_authored_index_with_text_valued_ids. 306 quarto-hub+provider tests pass, clippy clean, full cargo xtask verify green.

E2E (headless, real JS automerge-repo peer): JS creates a project (Text-valued files map + qmd file doc with engine:knitr) -> provider (with fix) lists 1 file (was 0) -> materializes -> runs knitr (cat(1,2,3)) -> writes capture doc + CaptureRef sidecar -> a JS peer reads it: state=idle, and the decoded capture shows STDOUT '1 2 3'. Reverse direction (provider's CaptureRef -> JS peer) confirmed working via a fresh JS reader. The whole remote-execution loop works with a hub-client-style project.

Not closing yet: follow-ups worth considering — (a) other Rust readers of JS-authored string map values (identities map; resource.rs mimeType/hash for hub-client-uploaded binaries) have the same to_str() pattern and would silently drop Text values; (b) optional TS-side cleanliness: write ids as immutable strings. Neither blocks the feature.

c-r4ym5ap0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-r4ym5ap0.text:
CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (confirmed + fix validated). Earlier diagnoses in this strand ("samod can't sync JS docs" / "nested maps don't sync") were WRONG — artifacts of a probe that only read ROOT.files via to_str(). The document syncs COMPLETELY from a JS automerge-repo peer to a Rust samod peer.

ACTUAL BUG: hub-client (@automerge/automerge 3.2.6 via automerge-repo 2.5.6) stores `files[path] = docId` string values as automerge TEXT objects, not scalar Str. quarto's Rust IndexDocument::get_all_files()/get_file() (crates/quarto-hub/src/index.rs) read values via ScalarValue::to_str(), which returns None for a Text object -> the JS-authored files map reads as EMPTY -> provider materializes 0 files -> "project discovery failed: canonicalize No such file or directory".

EVIDENCE (interop-repro, all local, no browser): JS peer creates {value:42, files:{'index.qmd':'x','about.qmd':'y'}} via a minimal JS sync server; Rust samod reader dumps ROOT and gets: `files=map{about.qmd=Some("Object(Text)"), index.qmd=Some("Object(Text)")} value=Scalar(Int(42))`. So keys + scalar sync fine; the map string VALUES are Text objects. A probe that reads each value as Str-OR-Text (doc.text() for Text objects) RECOVERS the 2 ids. Same class as the repo's existing metadata-as-str lint.

FIX (validated in principle): teach the Rust index readers to accept BOTH scalar Str and Text-object string values. Minimal: get_all_files + get_file in crates/quarto-hub/src/index.rs (value -> if Scalar(Str) use it, else if Object(Text) use doc.text(&objid)). Existing Rust-authored docs (project-mode hub, scalar Str) keep working; JS-authored docs now read. Optional cleanliness follow-up: have the TS side (client.ts:1182,1237,1501,1516) write ids as immutable strings instead of Text, but that won't fix already-created docs, so the Rust read-side fix is required regardless.

Repro/regression harness added: crates/quarto-hub-provider/tests/integration/{relay_sync.rs (self-contained, pass), sync_probe.rs (ignored network probes incl. probe_root_keys + probe_files_str_or_text)} + interop-repro/js-peer/{server.mjs, peer.mjs} (minimal JS automerge-repo server + peer). NOTE: the samod↔samod-only Phase 4a test (execute.rs) is why this was missed — need a JS-authored-doc case in the feature's e2e coverage.

title: Decide: knitr convert_includes silently drops unreadable include files (diverges from TS-engine loud-error contract)
description: Discovered during plan-4c 4cB-fix2 (commit 13f697c85). The TS-engine wire boundary now errors loudly on an unreadable engine-contributed include path (ts_engine.rs read_include_contents, per ratified contract: values are file paths, no sniffing, loud failure naming engine+key+value). knitr's native convert_includes (crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/mod.rs:310-339) silently drops unreadable files instead ('if let Ok(content) = std::fs::read_to_string' — behavior pinned by test_convert_includes_missing_file). Cross-engine inconsistency: same conceptual contract, different failure mode. Decide deliberately: tighten knitr to loud-error (changing its pinned test), or document the divergence as intended. Out of plan-4c scope (knitr untouched by the plan).

title: Reader extension surface for L9 (RSS feed extraction)
description:
L7 ships the listings-only subset of Q1's `readRenderedContents` in `crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/post_render_upgrade/reader.rs`. The `ReaderOptions` struct has two flags (`remove_links`, `remove_images`) currently no-op in v1's plain-text output.

L9 (RSS feeds, `bd-o90m`) will need:
- math handling
- syntax-highlight class maps
- urls-to-absolute (configurable base URL)
- anchor stripping

Each is opt-in via a new `ReaderOptions` field. Implement as private functions in the same file gated by their flag. Do not introduce a trait-based plugin architecture (Q1's single-function reader has been stable for years).

Filed at L7 close-out per the L7 plan §"Filing reminder" follow-up #2.

title: q2-preview comments: resolving a comment leaves an empty bubble and a lingering hover glow
description: In hub-client with a q2-preview document, hovering a block in the preview lets the user add a comment via the + affordance. After adding a comment and then clicking the resolve checkbox in the bubble, the preview shows a small empty pill where the bubble was and the block's hover/focus glow never clears. Reproduction, diagnosis and fix plan tracked in claude-notes/plans/2026-09-09-preview-comment-resolve-artifacts.md.
close_reason: Fixed on branch braid/bd-bpt089zw-q2-preview-comments-resolving: 0242ab91e (fix + 8 jsdom regression tests, verified in Chrome, cargo xtask verify green) and the changelog follow-up. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-09-preview-comment-resolve-artifacts.md. Pending push/PR.

c-7mqmmvtb.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-7mqmmvtb.text: Reproduced in Chrome (DevTools MCP) against a local vite dev server and diagnosed. Both artifacts are React state-lifecycle bugs in CommentWrapper (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/custom/CommentBlock.tsx): (1) selfExpanded stays true after the last comment is resolved, so the expanded branch renders with zero rows = the empty pill; (2) bubbleHovered is set by the bubble's onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave, and the leave is lost because the resolve re-render removes the button under the pointer (Chrome updates :hover after layout without boundary events; the next mouseout comes from the new hovered node, which the bubble is not an ancestor of). Plan with DOM probe evidence + TDD fix proposal: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-09-preview-comment-resolve-artifacts.md (committed on braid/bd-bpt089zw-q2-preview-comments-resolving). Awaiting review before implementing.

c-9vncytan.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-9vncytan.text: Fix implemented on branch braid/bd-bpt089zw-q2-preview-comments-resolving (uncommitted pending cargo xtask verify): (1) useLayoutEffect collapses selfExpanded when comments hit zero with no input open; (2) bubbleHovered is derived on the wrapper's mousemove (containment) / mouseleave, bubble enter/leave handlers removed; (3) a layout effect re-derives the glow from geometry whenever the bubble changes shape, so a stationary pointer gets the right answer. 8 new jsdom tests in CommentBlock.resolveLast.integration.test.tsx (T1-T7 + T6b), each verified failing first. Full preview-renderer suites green; end-to-end verified in Chrome. Changelog entry to follow in a second commit.

title: Listings: shared shape walker for parse_listings + extract_content_globs
description:
Today extract_content_globs (project/listing/config.rs) calls parse_listings and discards diagnostics, then plucks Glob entries from each Listing.contents. This re-runs the full listing parse just to read the glob strings.

Cleaner approach: factor a shared 'walk_listing_shape' helper that both parse_listings and extract_content_globs can use, so the dep-graph extractor only does the work it needs (walk shapes, collect content globs) and never produces diagnostics.

This is option 3 from L6 (bd-xbnf) planning. We chose option 1 for L6 because it gives a single source of truth on shape with minimal new code; this issue tracks the refactor for when someone has a reason (perf hot spot, or a second narrow extractor lands).

Origin: discussed in claude-notes/plans/2026-05-07-listings-L6-dep-graph.md §'Where the globs come from' and during L6 planning.

Reference: extract_content_globs in crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/config.rs has a pointer comment back to this issue.

c-41a9oh2d.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-41a9oh2d.text:
Both `Inline` arms now agree on records, so the walker unification this strand describes has a concrete shape to unify toward. As of the listing inline-records work (plan claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-listing-inline-contents.md, branch braid/bd-listing-inline-contents-tyy446ze-listing-inline-contents):

- `parse_contents` (config.rs) builds `ListingContents::Inline(ConfigValue)` carrying the whole record — span and per-key `key_source` intact.
- `flatten_content_globs` (config.rs) walks the same shape and emits a record's document `path:` as a literal `Glob` pattern with the path value's own provenance, so it feeds the dependency graph.

Previously these two disagreed (one built a BTreeMap and warned Q-12-2, the other dropped records entirely). They now read the same variant for the same reasons, which is the precondition for folding both into one walker.

title: hephaestus: PNG output as an opt-in (CPU route via SVG -> resvg), and PDF/typst outputs when those formats land
description: Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-17-hephaestus-hep-integration.md (§PNG, Phase 5). Not needed for HTML. title: pampa: bare-brace parse error should hint at escaping literal braces
description: A bare brace run in prose — e.g. 'the request returns the task {guid} immediately.' — is a fatal parse error in q2, reported only with the generic fallback diagnostic 'Parse error: unexpected character or token here'. In a single-file render no output is produced; in a project render the page is silently dropped from the site ('warning: profile-pass skipped <file>'). Pandoc/Quarto 1 treat brace runs that are not valid attribute syntax as literal text, so this is a common stumble when porting Q1 projects — REST API docs in particular write path parameters as {name} constantly. The brace reservation itself is by design and not in question here: escaped braces \{...\} parse cleanly in q2 and render identically under Pandoc, so escaping is the correct Q1-compatible source fix. This strand asks only for a targeted diagnostic: when the fallback branch in crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs fires at a brace run, hint something like 'curly braces are reserved for attributes in Quarto markdown; escape literal braces as \{...\}'. Both bare-paragraph braces and braces inside link text hit the generic fallback, while valid attribute syntax ([text]{#id}, [text](url){.cls}) parses fine; the grammar lives in crates/tree-sitter-qmd. Precedent for targeted parse-error messages: #152 (old-style chunk options), #156 / Q-2-39 (grid tables). Real-world hit: the generated Posit Connect API reference (docs-quarto-2/api/index.qmd, ~160 endpoints) hit this dozens of times via path parameters like /v1/content/{guid}/bundles before the docs-side generator learned to escape. Repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/bare-braces-parse-error/ — run 'q2 render repro.qmd' there; README.md states expected vs actual. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-brace-escape-hint-z8vy6sis. Observed with q2 0.14.0 and a HEAD build (4bb32844).
close_reason: Implemented: Q-2-41 targeted diagnostic for bare-brace parse errors (corpus entry + catalog + docs page). PR #483 merged.

title: Q-2-41 misses literal braces inside emphasis: the brace-escape hint fires in prose and link text only
description:
Q-2-41 ("Curly braces are reserved for attribute syntax") fires for literal braces in prose and in link text, but not for literal braces inside emphasis or strong. Those still get the generic uncoded 'Parse error / unexpected character or token here', with the caret on the brace and no mention that braces are reserved.

Measured on the 0.26.0 release. All five brace cases are fatal; only two explain themselves:

    the request returns the task {guid} immediately.      Q-2-41
    a [{PLACEHOLDER}] run here.                           Q-2-41
    a *{PLACEHOLDER}* run here.                           uncoded Parse error
    a **bold {PLACEHOLDER} run** here.                    uncoded Parse error
    **Debug [*{SUPPORTED_APP_TYPE}*] App in Terminal**.   uncoded Parse error

Being inside brackets is not the variable -- '*{X}*' on its own misses too. Emphasis is.

Quarto 1 renders all of them: Pandoc treats a brace run that is not valid attribute syntax as literal text. That difference is NOT what this strand asks about. The brace reservation is settled design (ruling recorded on the Connect side as br-bare-braces-parse-error-cr3dentw; escaped '\{...\}' parses in q2 and renders identically under Pandoc, so escaping is the correct Q1-compatible source fix). This asks only that the remaining brace failures say so.

What the covered cases already say, and what the missed ones should:

    Error: [Q-2-41] Curly braces are reserved for attribute syntax
     5 │ a [{PLACEHOLDER}] run here.
       │     ─────┬─────
       │          ╰─────── Curly braces are reserved for attribute syntax in Quarto
       │                   markdown. To write literal braces, escape them as `\{...\}`.
       │                   If you meant to attach an attribute, use `.class` / `#id` /
       │                   `key="value"` syntax, e.g. `[text]{.class}`.

That wording is exactly right for the missed cases too; nothing new needs writing.

Root cause. Q-2-41 was implemented as a pure corpus addition, no grammar change, under bd-brace-escape-hint-0tmemkyt (closed 2026-08-10, PR #483). Its investigation captured two parser states -- 2613 (prose braces) and 2589 (link-text braces), both symbol _language_specifier_token -- and added corpus entries for them. The parse-error table (crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json, consumed via crates/pampa/src/readers/qmd_error_message_table.rs) is keyed on tree-sitter parser state + symbol, so an input that fails in any unclaimed state falls through to the generic branch in crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs. Braces inside emphasis land in states nobody claimed.

This is not a criticism of that work: the Connect corpus that motivated it was REST path parameters ('/v1/content/{guid}/bundles'), which are prose and link text, so two states covered it completely. A second port simply produced a third shape.

Suggested fix: same shape as the original -- capture the states the three missed cases produce and add corpus entries. The Q-2-36 path-B precedent cited in the parent strand applies unchanged.

Worth considering alongside it: this is the second coverage gap of the same kind found from the Positron port in as many weeks. bd-shortcode-naked-value-nonascii-47fzbmow is the mirror image -- there an input inherits a WRONG code (Q-2-34, 'value starts with a digit') because it happens to fail in a state another corpus case claimed, and the author is sent looking for a digit that does not exist. State-keyed diagnostics are precise when the state is claimed and silent-or-wrong when it is not, and both failure modes reach users as confident, specific text. A validation step at emit time -- check that the captured span actually satisfies the claimed condition, fall back to the generic error when it does not -- would make the wrong-code half safe; the silent half needs corpus coverage, which is what this strand is. Precedent for tracking a coverage gap as its own strand: bd-q250-nested-fence-blind-spot-t68z1lsw.

Real-world hit. develop-data-apps.qmd:57 in the Positron website writes a placeholder as '**Debug [*{SUPPORTED_APP_TYPE}*] App in Terminal**'. The page is one of only four in the whole site that still fail to render, and 63 of 89 rendered pages link to it. The author gets no indication that braces are the cause; worse, q2 reports a second, cascading error on line 58 pointing at an innocent 4-space-indented list item, so the visible evidence points away from the real problem. With Q-2-41 firing, the fix is immediate.

Repro: /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/brace-hint-misses-emphasis/
Run 'q2 render' there: 'Rendered 1 of 6 files ... 5 errors' -- two files diagnosed Q-2-41, three with the generic parse error, and index.qmd (the escaped control) renders. 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1' renders all six. README.md carries the boundary table and the captured diagnostic text. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path.

Observed with the official q2 0.26.0 release build. The q2 source checkout was at 596ceb572 (v0.26.0-28) at the time, so 28 unreleased commits are not covered.

Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-brace-hint-misses-emphasis-yzxxgdng. Parent: bd-brace-escape-hint-0tmemkyt.

c-3mojhy2q.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-3mojhy2q.text:
Fixed on branch braid/bd-brace-hint-misses-emphasis-4fzv1n93-q-2-41-misses, commit 168bcdbae (not yet pushed).

The gap was wider than the three reported cases. The LR state follows the *innermost enclosing inline container*, so I probed every grammar rule that wraps $._inlines rather than only the reported shapes. Eleven unclaimed states, not two:

    2596  _emph_             2612  **strong**        2623  [!! ..] [-- ..] [++ ..] [>> ..]
    2597  ~~strikeout~~      2617  ^superscript^     2626  *emph*
    2598  ~subscript~        2619  __strong__        2627  'single quote'
    2599  "double quote"     2602  ^[inline note]

Note the underscore spellings are distinct states from the star spellings, and the four editorial spellings share one state.

Block context turned out to be a non-issue: headings, captions, block quotes, list items, table cells and div bodies all reduce to 2601, the paragraph state already claimed; link text, image alt and bracketed span text share 2604, also already claimed. That is why the two original cases went as far as they did.

Fix is the same shape as the original -- pure corpus addition, no grammar change. The regenerated table is a strict addition (165 lines added, none removed, no other code's entries touched). Claiming these is safe because _language_specifier_token is only ever emitted for a brace, so it cannot mislabel a non-brace input.

Verified end-to-end through 'q2 render', not just in-process: the develop-data-apps.qmd:57 shape now reports Q-2-41 with the caret on the brace run, and the escape it recommends renders to literal braces.

Regression test: crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_brace_hint_contexts.rs -- 28 rows across every inline container plus nesting combinations, and a companion test pinning the places braces are legal (code spans, inline math, link titles, escaped \{...\}, real attributes). 21 of the 28 rows failed before the fix. Also documented the state-per-inline-container trap in crates/pampa/CLAUDE.md, since the failure mode is silent.

cargo nextest run --workspace: 13132 passed, 199 skipped (+2 = the new tests). xtask lint and clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean.

Digression filed, NOT fixed here: bd-m20x2zrp -- literal braces in a link/image *destination* hit (3047, _close_block), a state Q-2-31 legitimately owns for the genuine backtick spelling, so they inherit 'This opening backtick begins an invalid code execution attempt' for a source with no backtick. That is the wrong-code half of this failure mode (the mirror image you flagged via bd-shortcode-naked-value-nonascii-47fzbmow) and needs the emit-time validation, not another corpus case.

c-gop00ijy.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-gop00ijy.text:
Code review found a real gap in the first pass; fixed and amended to ed6b59f8c.

MISSED: pipe-table cells. Bare braces in a table body cell (state 2610) and header cell (state 2613) were still uncoded. So it is thirteen states, not eleven.

Two causes, and the second is the one worth remembering:

1. My probe harness wrote table rows through printf '%b' with backslash-escaped pipes, so that one probe row landed on disk as literal '\| a \| b \|' -- a paragraph, not a table. It reported the paragraph state and I concluded table cells were already covered.

2. The real cause: I swept the grammar for rules wrapping $._inlines. That predicate is wrong. pipe_table_cell (grammar.js:393) is built on _line_with_maybe_spaces, a *sibling* of _inlines (grammar.js:606-607), so grepping for _inlines structurally cannot find table cells. The correct predicate is 'every rule that reaches $._inline_element', whose only two consumers are _inlines and _line_with_maybe_spaces.

Worse than the two missing rows: I had written the false claim ('a paragraph case covers ... table cells ...') into crates/pampa/CLAUDE.md, the document added specifically to stop this bug class recurring. Corrected, with the _inline_element vs _inlines distinction spelled out. Also noted there that a nested case does not cover the bare one -- '| *{X}* |' reduces to the emphasis state, so it passes while bare '| {X} |' falls through; my original test row was that disguised duplicate.

Note bd-j30t7 is open with exactly this gap for a different diagnostic: 'Q-2-32 not emitted for `***` inside pipe-table cells'. Same blind spot, independently found.

Also fixed from review:
- The legal-braces test asserted only 'no error'. It now renders through the plaintext writer and asserts the braces SURVIVE. My first attempt used format!('{pandoc:?}') and was vacuous -- Rust's Debug emits braces for every struct, so it passed for any input. Each legal row now declares where its braces should end up (literal text / consumed as attribute / link-title attribute); mutation-tested to confirm it actually discriminates.
- That test's doc comment claimed to guard against a corpus case over-claiming a state. It cannot: the table is consulted only after a parse has already failed, so no corpus row can redden it. Reworded to what it does guard (grammar regressions).
- deno.lock also carried an undisclosed katex 0.17.0 -> 0.18.1 reconciliation (package.json:26 already pins 0.18.1). Now called out in the commit message, given GH #250.

Verified: '| /v1/content/{guid} | GET |' now reports Q-2-41 through q2 render. Workspace 13132 passed, lint and clippy clean.

Reviewer verdict on the rest: the safety argument holds (exact-match lookup, no state stolen from any other code, confirmed independently), the TDD claim checks out arithmetically, and bd-m20x2zrp was correctly scoped out.

One observation, not a defect in this change. The cascading second error on line 58 is unaffected and still prints as a bare 'Error: Parse error / unexpected character or token here' with the caret on an innocent 4-space-indented list item:

        │   ╰─── unexpected character or token here

Before this change that was the more legible of the two errors, so it was actively misleading -- our port spent time investigating it as an indented-list bug before establishing it was a cascade. With line 57 now named, the harm is much reduced. Whether a cascade after a fatal parse error should be suppressed is a separate question and I have not filed one.

title: Website breadcrumbs (quarto-secondary-nav) are not rendered
description:
Quarto 1 gives every sidebar-bearing website page a breadcrumb trail; q2 emits no breadcrumb markup at all, and there is no breadcrumb code in the tree (the only 'bread-crumbs' hits are a config-passthrough assertion in quarto-core/tests/integration/custom_project_type.rs and a Q1 schema copy in pampa/test-fixtures/schemas/definitions.yml). Setting website.bread-crumbs: true changes nothing and produces no diagnostic — though that silence is not itself evidence of deliberate acceptance, since an entirely made-up website: key renders silently too. What Q1 emits, on a page whose sidebar path is Getting Started > Local Execution > Server Installation:
  1. Getting Started
  2. Local Execution
  3. Server Installation
Two Q1 behaviours worth copying deliberately rather than by accident: the trail includes the current page as its own final (linked) crumb, and a section crumb — a sidebar section has no href of its own — links to the section's FIRST DESCENDANT DOCUMENT. That is why 'Getting Started' above points at requirements/index.html. In a one-child section the section crumb and the page crumb therefore resolve to the same URL, which looks like a bug in a minimal repro but is Q1's actual rule. Scope note that makes this bigger than a decorative trail: in Q1 the breadcrumbs live inside
, which is the whole narrow-viewport navigation bar — it also holds the sidebar toggle button (data-bs-target=".quarto-sidebar-collapse-item") and the search button, and it is hidden by CSS on wide viewports. On a phone that toggle is the only way to open the sidebar. So 'no secondary nav' is not merely 'no breadcrumbs'; whoever implements this should decide whether the container is in scope or whether q2's mobile sidebar affordance is handled elsewhere. Root cause area: nothing to fix, only to add. The natural home is crates/quarto-navigation — render_html.rs already owns navbar_to_html / sidebar_to_html / page_navigation_to_html and the escaping and href helpers a breadcrumb renderer needs. The trail data is already computed and then discarded: sidebar.rs's resolve_active_state (:678) delegates to mark_active_in (:687), a post-order walk that marks the active leaf and bubbles up through every wrapping Section (setting expanded = true on each). That chain of ancestor Sections IS the breadcrumb trail, in order. Suggested fix direction: have that walk return (or accumulate) the ancestor path it just proved, hand it to a breadcrumbs_to_html sibling of the existing renderers, and resolve each section crumb's href to its first descendant leaf. Q1's default is bread-crumbs: true whenever a sidebar is present, so the option needs honouring on both sides once the markup exists. Connect docs impact: all 352 pages lose the trail. It is the single largest systematic chrome difference in the port after tabset TOC entries — big enough that the porting project's site-comparison tool has to run with --skip-attr quarto-secondary-nav to see anything else, which means it is also masking any other difference in that region. Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/breadcrumbs-missing/ (see README.md; run 'q2 render' there and compare with 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1'; the committed _site-q1 has the Q1 markup above). Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-breadcrumbs-missing-3bt7vhtl. Observed with q2 0.19.0, re-verified failing on 0.21.0 (q2 main 3ac596e0 has no breadcrumb work; the 'breadcrumb' commits in the log are the preview/hub-client block-editing chrome, unrelated).
close_reason: Implemented on main, commit 66bd2284 (title-block instance): breadcrumb_trail + breadcrumbs_to_html in quarto-navigation, BreadcrumbsRenderTransform in quarto-core consuming the resolver settled by bd-tef2lm9j/bd-root-absolute-dir-link (final commit 57f89387 — crumb hrefs route through resolve_href_for_html, no path logic of their own, exactly the constraint this strand recorded). Q1 parity: self as final linked crumb, section crumbs borrow first direct child's href, bread-crumbs default-true with page-level override, >1-crumb gate on the title instance. TDD (15 tests failing-first), e2e on a fixture + dogfooded on docs/ (240 pages). The quarto-secondary-nav mobile container (toggle/search/compact trail) is deliberately NOT included — filed as bd-26bf3j1y with the scope rationale.

c-az4q2a54.author: Claude (q2-connect-docs)
c-az4q2a54.text:
Correction to the example markup in the description: the third crumb's href is

  ../../../../admin/getting-started/local-install/server-install/index.html

(the 'local-install/' segment was dropped when the example was transcribed). c-j7hs8usr.author: Claude (q2-connect-docs)
c-j7hs8usr.text:
Sequencing recorded, at Carlos's request, for a single long session covering all three strands: fix the two structural href strands FIRST, implement breadcrumbs after.

Dependency edges updated to encode that — this strand is now blocked by:
  bd-tef2lm9j                        nav hrefs to static files not page-relativized
  bd-root-absolute-dir-link-58eh8834 body links to directories not page-relativized

The earlier 'related' edge to bd-tef2lm9j has been replaced by the blocks edge, which supersedes it. 'braid ready' no longer offers this strand; 'braid blocked' shows it with both blockers.

Why this order rather than the reverse, restating the argument now that the second half is filed: those two strands are one unanswered question — what a resolver should do when the ProjectIndex does not know the target — living in two sibling functions of navigation_href.rs. Breadcrumbs are not a third instance of that bug; they are a prospective CONSUMER of its answer. Every crumb is a nav-surface href, and section crumbs are the demanding case: a sidebar section has no href of its own, so its crumb must resolve to the section's first descendant document. Implementing breadcrumbs against today's miss branch would bake the same verbatim fallthrough into every crumb on every page — 352 pages of it at once in the Connect port — and would then need unpicking rather than extending.

Practical consequence for the session: by the time breadcrumbs are built, the resolver should be a settled call, so the breadcrumb renderer can route crumb hrefs through it and grow no path logic of its own. If for any reason breadcrumbs are taken first, that constraint is the thing to preserve.

c-xm296zx7.author: Claude (q2-connect-docs)
c-xm296zx7.text:
Linked related: bd-tef2lm9j (nav hrefs to static files not page-relativized).

The connection is the resolver, and it matters for sequencing rather than for either fix in isolation. Every crumb in a breadcrumb trail is a nav-surface href, and the section crumbs are the awkward kind: a sidebar section has no href of its own, so its crumb has to be resolved to the section's first descendant document. That means breadcrumbs will be a NEW CONSUMER of exactly the href resolution bd-tef2lm9j is about — crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_href.rs, and specifically the question of what happens on a ProjectIndex miss.

Today that miss branch returns raw.to_string(), emitting the href verbatim (leading slash and all). If breadcrumbs are implemented against the resolver as it currently behaves, every crumb href inherits the same defect the moment a trail passes through anything that is not an indexed .qmd, and the port gains 352 pages' worth of it at once.

So the useful order is: settle the miss-branch behaviour first (bd-tef2lm9j, and the parent design bd-root-relative-paths-design-fc5pvkcv), then build breadcrumbs on the settled resolver. If breadcrumbs land first, they should at least route crumb hrefs through whatever helper the design lands on rather than growing their own path logic.

Third instance of the same miss-branch fallthrough, for whoever scopes the design session: the BODY-LINK version, where a markdown link to a directory (e.g. [text](/guide/)) is left root-absolute because a directory is not a source path. That one is filed in the Posit Connect docs porting skein as br-h5wdib27 with a Q1-verified repro at /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/root-absolute-dir-link/, and has not been handed off to this skein yet. Nav surface (bd-tef2lm9j), body links (br-h5wdib27) and breadcrumbs (this strand) are three faces of one decision about what a resolver should do when the index does not know the target.

title: breakQuartoMd requires an exactly-equal closing fence, and silently eats the opening line when none arrives
description:
Finding 2a of bd-ts-engine-display-fence-joy59gkr. Verified on q2 HEAD 00a1c1702.

CommonMark: a closing fence must be AT LEAST as long as the opener. ts-packages/quarto-api/src/markdownRegex/index.ts:946-948 requires exact equality:

  (line.substring.match(endCodeRegEx)!)[1].length === inCode

REPRO (probe D_longer_close): a three-backtick {r} opener closed by a four-backtick fence. breakQuartoMd returns ONE markdown cell whose value is 'cat("A")\n````\n\nafter\n'.

Two defects, not one:
  (a) the block never closes, so it is never emitted as a code cell;
  (b) the OPENING fence line is dropped from the output entirely. flushLineBuffer('markdown') already ran and inCodeCell was set, so the opener never re-enters the line buffer, and the final flush emits only what is left. That is content loss, not a mis-split.

FIX: === becomes >=. Keep it a separate commit from the leading-whitespace fix (bd-breakquartomd-indented-display-fence-1wxmf0bh) — this changes what CLOSES a block, that one changes what OPENS one, and the risk profiles differ.

Low frequency in practice; filed because (b) makes it lossy rather than merely wrong.

Full analysis: claude-notes/research/2026-08-27-ts-engine-display-fence.md

title: breakQuartoMd fails open on an INDENTED display fence: example content inside a list item is split out as a cell
description:
Finding 2b of bd-ts-engine-display-fence-joy59gkr. Verified on q2 HEAD 00a1c1702.

ts-packages/quarto-api/src/markdownRegex/index.ts:779-785 has three regexes with three different opinions about leading whitespace:

  startCodeCellRegEx = /^\s*(```+)\s*\{...\}\s*$/   <- indent OK
  startCodeRegEx     = /^```/                          <- column 0 ONLY
  endCodeRegEx       = /^\s*(```+)\s*$/               <- indent OK

startCodeRegEx (:959) is the guard that sets inCode for a PLAIN fence — i.e. the thing that stops a display block's contents from being read as cells. It is the only one anchored at column 0. So an indented display fence never sets inCode, and the indented cell opener inside it, which startCodeCellRegEx happily matches, opens a code cell.

tickCount (:890) compounds it: it reads s.split(' ')[0], which is '' for any line starting with a space, so even a relaxed startCodeRegEx would count 0 backticks.

REPRO (probe E_indented_outer): a list item containing a four-backtick markdown fence whose content is a three-backtick {r} fence. breakQuartoMd returns 3 cells, the middle one code:r holding the DISPLAY content. Identical with marimo's own MARIMO_CELL_REGEX as startCodeCellRegex (probe M3).

WHY P1 — end-to-end silent destruction, verified through the committed marimo fixture. Document: real {python .marimo} cell, then a list item containing an indented display block, then a SECOND real cell. Rendered output: the display block is EMPTY, cell B's marimo island is spliced where the display cell was, and cell B's own source is left over as literal un-executed text. The author's example is deleted. q2 render exits 0; the engine's own console.warning about the output-count mismatch never reaches the render log.

m3 (no second real cell) looks correct only by accident of marimo's marimoIndex >= outputs.length fallback pushing sourceVerbatim.

FIX DIRECTION: make the three regexes agree — startCodeRegEx allows the same leading whitespace, tickCount stops using split(' ')[0]. Do NOT try to make breakQuartoMd CommonMark-correct about list continuation columns; it is a line-oriented approximation and should stay one.

WHAT BREAKS: chunk boundaries change for any document with an indented plain fence containing a cell-opener-shaped line — the same set that is broken today, so a strict improvement, but it is a shared partitioner used by marimo and any third-party engine. Land regression tests over the E / M3 / m4-misalign shapes with it; probes are committed at claude-notes/research/2026-08-27-ts-engine-display-fence-probes/.

Full analysis: claude-notes/research/2026-08-27-ts-engine-display-fence.md (branch braid/bd-ts-engine-display-fence-joy59gkr).

title: Hub-client math rendering blocked by iframe sandbox
description:
bd-w5ov shipped MathJax + KaTeX for HTML output. Live Chromium smoke confirmed correctness on the native CLI render path. However, a post-implementation regression test in hub-client preview shows raw \(e=mc^2\) text — math is NOT typesetting there.

Root cause: the hub-client preview iframe is sandboxed without 'allow-scripts'. Set in DoubleBufferedIframe.tsx:347,355 and MorphIframe.tsx:564 (sandbox='allow-same-origin allow-popups'). iframePostProcessor.ts:149-167 documents that script inlining is disabled for the same reason. No <script> in the iframe executes today, so MathJax/KaTeX CDN loaders never run, and our inline window.MathJax config block also doesn't execute.

The WASM pipeline IS correctly wired to MathJsStage and meta.math IS populated; the iframe sandbox just drops everything on the floor.

Resolution: blocked on the existing (separate) plan to isolate the preview iframe on a subdomain via service workers, which would let us re-enable allow-scripts safely. Once that lands, math typesetting in hub-client should 'just work' with no changes to MathJsStage.

Alternatives considered (not pursued in v1):
- Add allow-scripts unconditionally — strictly weaker security model; rejected by user.
- Server-side pre-typesetting (KaTeX renderToString or MathJax Node) on the WASM pipeline — non-trivial and not needed once scripts run.
- Switch hub-client default to Temml/MathML (no JS runtime needed) — bd-si8b tracks this independently; would not fix MathJax/KaTeX users.

Acceptance: when service-worker iframe isolation is in place, set sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-popups' (and re-enable script handling in iframePostProcessor.ts), then re-run a hub-client smoke against the user's reproducer doc:

---
format: html
title: Math maybe?
---
Hello, world. Will this work? $e=mc^2$.

— and confirm typeset output in the preview.

title: Plumb SourceInfo into Q-13-4 body-link 'missing document' warnings
description:
Today the Q-13-4 'Body link references missing document' warning is emitted without a source location, so a user running 'q2 render' on a website sees only the missing target — not which file or line introduced the broken link.

Example, running 'cargo run --bin q2 -- render docs/' on this repo's docs site today:

  Warning [Q-13-4]: Body link references missing document
  'authoring/markdown/markdown-basics.qmd' is not in the project index.
  i Check the spelling, or confirm the target file is included in the render set.

There is no 'at file:row:col' line, even though the body-link rewriter has the full Link node in hand and Link.target_source.url already carries a SourceInfo populated by the parser (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/span_link_helpers.rs:109).

bd-qor9a already plumbed source-info into the nav-surface Q-13-* diagnostics (sidebar / navbar / footer / page-nav) via the paired href_source field. bd-hjv5o lists this body-link follow-up as item #1 — 'lightweight follow-up' because resolve_doc_relative_href already takes an Option<SourceInfo> location parameter; the body-link callsite just passes None at crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/link_rewrite.rs:224.

Scope:

1. Pass link.target_source.url.clone() to resolve_doc_relative_href in LinkRewriter::visit_inline.
2. Extend the Q-13-4 unit test (link_rewrite_diagnostic_uses_body_link_label) to assert d.location.is_some() and that the location maps back to the URL substring.
3. Extend the integration test in crates/quarto-core/tests/link_rewriting_pipeline.rs that exercises Q-13-4 to assert on location.
4. End-to-end: re-run 'q2 render docs/' and confirm the warning gains an 'at file:row:col' line under each Q-13-4.

Out of scope:
- Other Q-13-* surfaces (already covered by bd-qor9a).
- Image href diagnostics (images aren't checked against the index).
- RawHtml links (no SourceInfo on the URL portion).

title: Theme compile errors (Q-14-6): map the assembled-bundle line back to the user's theme file and line
description: Q-14-6 (bd-jsvetdea) surfaces grass/dart-sass failures as a hard error, but the compiler only knows lines of the SCSS bundle Quarto assembles (`./stdin:3269:24`), and the failing excerpt is often Quarto's own line reacting to a theme variable (e.g. `$grid-body-column-min` when a user sets `$grid-body-width: 52rem`). The diagnostic therefore anchors at the whole `theme:` value in YAML and says so in its hint. Follow-up: record each layer's line range while `quarto_sass::bundle::assemble_scss` concatenates sections (framework / quarto / merged user layers, per section), keep the originating file for user layers (`process_theme_specs` knows it), and translate the compiler's line into (layer, file, line). Then Q-14-6 can point at `theme.scss:2` when the failing line is in a user layer, and say 'in Quarto's Bootstrap layer, triggered by your theme's defaults' otherwise. Needs care with `merge_layers` (defaults are reversed) and with dart-sass (WASM) whose error text differs from grass. Deferred from bd-jsvetdea on 2026-09-08 because cross-tool source tracking infrastructure is not there yet; plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-08-theme-scss-compile-error-swallowed.md.

title: CLAUDE.md's 'Full Project Verification' section is stale: documents 5 steps, cargo xtask verify runs 14
description:
CLAUDE.md:571-580 enumerates what `cargo xtask verify` runs as five steps. `TOTAL_STEPS` in `crates/xtask/src/verify.rs:28` is 14. The actual sequence:

     1  Custom lints + clippy
     2  Rust formatting (rustfmt --check)
     3  Build Rust workspace (warnings denied)
     4  Tree-sitter grammar tests (incl. CRLF parity)
     5  Rust tests
     6  Build ts-packages workspaces
     7  Build hub-client (includes WASM)
     8  hub-client tests (test:ci)
     9  Build trace-viewer SPA
    10  trace-viewer tests
    11  Shared preview-* package tests
    12  hub MCP package tests
    13  Build q2-preview-spa placeholder
    14  q2-preview-spa Playwright E2E (--e2e only)

Nine steps are undocumented, and the four that are documented are described in the wrong order (the doc leads with the workspace build; the command leads with lints + clippy).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. The same CLAUDE.md section is what tells you to run verify at all, and specifically says it 'is the step that matches CI's -D warnings strictness; plain cargo build / cargo nextest do not'. A reader who takes the five-step list as the contract will not expect a red from rustfmt, from tree-sitter, from trace-viewer, or from any of the preview-*/MCP package suites — all of which can and do fail there. Concretely: bd-c72wsugj is a flake at step 12, a step the documentation does not mention exists.

It also under-sells the command. Someone deciding whether verify is worth the wall-clock is reading a list that omits two thirds of what it covers.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, rather than transcribing 14 lines that will drift again: group them (Rust: lints/fmt/build/grammars/tests; TypeScript: ts-packages, hub-client, trace-viewer, shared preview, MCP; SPA: placeholder build, optional E2E), name the skip flags against the groups they skip, and point at `verify.rs` as the source of truth. A pointer that stays true beats an enumeration that goes stale — this list has already drifted once.

Noticed while running full verify for bd-listing-inline-records-order-eq8n2usm.

title: Fix Windows test failures: lua system command tests use Unix-only programs
description: Three tests in crates/pampa/src/lua/system.rs fail on Windows because they call Unix-only programs: test_command_success uses 'echo' (shell built-in on Windows, not a standalone binary), test_command_failure uses 'false' (Unix utility, absent on Windows), test_command_with_input uses 'cat' (not reliably available on Windows). All three panic with RuntimeError('I/O error: program not found'). Fix: use platform-appropriate commands via cfg(windows)/cfg(unix) — e.g. 'cmd /C echo' or 'cmd.exe' with args for echo, skip or use 'cmd /C exit 1' for false, and for cat use a platform-appropriate alternative or skip on Windows. Surfaced 2026-06-25 running cargo nextest run on Windows after bd-vxl8 (io_wasm fix) merged.
close_reason: Merged via PR #341

description:

- **Q-A — RESOLVED.** PR #238 lands engine: [knitr, mermaidjs] sequencing. Mermaid is a first-class ExecutionEngine impl. Cell-class ownership disjoint (`{r}` vs `{mermaid}`) so the two compose cleanly. The v1 'AST transform' framing is obsolete.

- **Q-C — unchanged.** Recommend C1 (inline RawBlock(HTML) for the jsdelivr script tag at end of body, encoded into the engine's markdown output). Survives bd-cp3em (capture-splice aux drop).

- **Q-D — redirected.** PR #238 documents bd-iq0hp ('no browser E2E of multi-engine preview was possible'). Mermaid + knitr is the first real-engine pair with disjoint cell ownership; our preview-e2e task (bd-my0o5) effectively closes bd-iq0hp.

Output: plan doc has v2 with these decisions recorded. User confirmation of B2c recommendation needed before impl.
