title: quarto-sync-client doc-inventory.test.ts is flaky: binary-file entry intermittently missing, reddens cargo xtask verify
description:
`ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/doc-inventory.test.ts` > getDocInventory > 'reports index, text, and binary docs with states and heads' fails intermittently at step 12 of `cargo xtask verify` (Running hub MCP package tests), aborting the run.

The assertion compares the inventory's (role, path) pairs. On a failing run the binary entry is absent:

    - Expected
    + Received
        [ "index", null ],
    -   [ "binary-file", "logo.png" ],
        [ "file", "main.qmd" ],

so the index and text docs arrive but the binary doc does not, i.e. the inventory is read before that doc has synced rather than the entry being wrong.

TIMING, NOT LOGIC. The surrounding output is full of peer-connection churn — repeated 'Waiting for peer connection...' / 'Peer connected - online mode' pairs for this one test, and three `TimeoutNegativeWarning: -N is a negative number. Timeout duration was set to 1.` warnings from separate worker pids (-2, -32, -5). A negative computed timeout clamped to 1ms is consistent with a deadline being derived from an already-elapsed budget, which would make the wait for the binary doc effectively zero.

REPRODUCTION IS THE PROBLEM. Observed once during a full `cargo xtask verify`. Does not reproduce on demand:

    npx vitest run src/doc-inventory.test.ts    3/3 runs, 6/6 passed
    npm test (full package)                     2/2 runs, 137/137 passed

So it likely needs the load of a full verify (parallel vitest workers across packages competing with the Rust build) to surface. Anyone chasing this should reproduce under `cargo xtask verify` rather than in isolation, and should suspect the timeout derivation before the inventory logic.

IMPACT. `cargo xtask verify` aborts on step failure, so steps 13-14 never run. A developer who hits this sees a red verify on a change that touches no TypeScript, and the honest response — re-run and confirm — costs a full verify cycle. Worth fixing rather than tolerating, because a known-flaky gate trains people to re-run reds without reading them.

Found while verifying bd-listing-inline-records-order-eq8n2usm, a Rust-only change touching zero TS files; a second verify run passed all 14 steps.

title: DocumentProfile outline lists callout titles the rendered TOC omits
description:
Found while implementing bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7 Phase 3.

extract_outline (crates/quarto-core/src/document_profile.rs) now sectionizes a copy of the blocks before calling generate_toc, because the collector walks only the section tree and DocumentProfileStage (pipeline.rs:314) runs long before SectionizeTransform (:1332). Without that, every heading written inside a ::: block vanished from the outline.

REMAINING GAP. Transforms that CONSUME a heading run after the profile checkpoint. A callout title written as a heading is absorbed into a section by the profile's local sectionize pass and appears in profile.outline, while the rendered TOC omits it -- CalloutTransform ate the Header before SectionizeTransform saw it. Tab titles and tabset/callout BODY headings are excluded correctly, because those wrappers hold more than one section and are never absorbed.

IMPACT TODAY: none observable. No in-tree consumer reads profile.outline yet. Filing so the discrepancy is not discovered by the first consumer.

FIXING IT properly means running the heading-consuming transforms before the profile checkpoint, which the profile contract deliberately does not do (claude-notes/designs/document-profile-contract.md). Alternatives worth weighing: teach the profile a list of heading-consuming container classes; or move the checkpoint after Normalization.

Pinned by the test outline_sees_headings_inside_divs in document_profile.rs.

c-e102601n.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-e102601n.text:
Widened slightly by the fix for bd-toc-skips-headings-in-id-div-1jorg679 (branch braid/bd-toc-skips-headings-in-id-div-1jorg679-toc-skips-headings-in-id-div, not yet pushed).

collect_toc_entries now descends through a Div whose sole content is another Div (pandoc's toTOCTree clause, jgm/pandoc#8402). extract_outline shares generate_toc and runs pre-transform, so single-child id-bearing containers now reach profile.outline where they previously did not: ':::  {#cal .callout-note}' holding one heading, ':::  {#tabs .panel-tabset}' with one tab. The rendered TOC still excludes both, because by TocGenerateTransform the callout and tabset are resolved into multi-child chrome.

This strand's text needs a correction either way: it says tab titles and callout body headings are excluded 'because those wrappers hold more than one section', which was already only true of the resolved shapes and is now not the rule at all. The rule is that a wrapper is descended through iff its content is exactly one Div.

Same family as what this strand already describes -- profile outline computed pre-transform diverges from the post-transform TOC -- and nothing outside tests consumes profile.outline today, so it was left in scope here rather than fixed on that branch.

title: Callout title= attribute is ignored; header shows the type name instead of the author's title
description:
A callout written with the title as a div attribute -- ::: {.callout-note title="Off-Host Execution"} -- renders a header reading "Note". The author-supplied title never appears anywhere the reader can see it; it survives only as the title= attribute on the outer div (which is also what Q1 emits, so that part is fine). The output is otherwise a correct titled callout: class callout-titled is set and the callout-title-container div is present, but its content is the injected type display name. Q1 renders '
NoteOff-Host Execution
' -- user title visible, type name kept for screen readers. Root cause is in the div-to-CustomNode step, not the resolver. crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/callout.rs::convert_div_to_callout builds the "title" slot from a leading Header block only (the "Check if the first block is a Header" branch); it reads appearance/collapse/icon through extract_attr_value(&div.attr, ...) but never reads "title". So for an attribute-titled callout the title slot is empty, and crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/callout_resolve.rs::resolve_callout takes its default-title-injection path (appearance=default + empty title -> inject displayName), which also sets title_is_user_supplied = false and therefore skips the screen-reader-only type span. Both files are otherwise correct -- callout_resolve already implements the exact Q1 shape for a user-supplied title. Q1's precedence, for reference: external-sources/quarto-cli/src/resources/filters/customnodes/callout.lua:48-50 does local title = string_to_quarto_ast_inlines(div.attr.attributes["title"] or "") if not title or #title == 0 then title = resolveHeadingCaption(div) end i.e. the title= attribute WINS over a leading heading, and its string is parsed as markdown inlines (so '::: {.callout-tip title="Use `renv`"}' gets a code span in the header). Suggested fix: in convert_div_to_callout, read extract_attr_value(&div.attr, "title") first and parse it as inlines; fall back to the leading-Header branch when it is absent or empty. Leave the title= key on div.attr (Q1 keeps it on the rendered div). Everything downstream then works unchanged, including the screen-reader-only span, because title_is_user_supplied becomes true. Worth a test for each of: attribute only, heading only, both (attribute wins), and markdown inside the attribute value. Real-world hit: the Posit Connect docs use the attribute form throughout -- about 25 pages lose their callout titles, e.g. admin/directories/index.md ("Off-Host Execution"), user/pins ("When not to use pins"), user/structuring-content ("Data loss on deployment"), admin/getting-started/requirements ("RHEL Alternatives", "Internet Explorer 11 - End of Support"), user/oauth-integrations ("How token refresh works under the hood"), and the twelve user/* guide pages that share a "Documentation for Posit Connect Administrators" note. Readers see an unlabeled "Note"/"Warning"/"Important" with no indication of what it is about. No warning is emitted. Minimal repro (two attribute-titled callouts plus an untitled control): /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/callout-custom-title-dropped/ -- run 'q2 render' there and compare with 'quarto render'; README.md has the expected and actual markup side by side. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-de85v0a8. Observed with q2 0.16.0; re-checked against origin/main @ 3ef77da8, where convert_div_to_callout still has no "title" attribute branch.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #496 (merge commit d05e021e, implementation dfe651c1). Callouts now honor the title= attribute with Q1 precedence and markdown parsing; the screen-reader-only type span comes back with it. All 8 CI checks green (Rust on ubuntu + macos, WASM, hub-client E2E, both Snyk). Follow-ups filed: bd-mxa44voa (nested-parse span drift, shared with YAML/ipynb), bd-bhxeoqoj (theorem.rs span miscomment), bd-ieei6osu (no callouts feature page under docs/).

c-869gsr8x.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-869gsr8x.text:
Design settled with user 2026-08-10. Plan updated at claude-notes/plans/2026-08-10-callout-title-attribute.md (branch braid/callout-title-attribute off main @ b2b6100c; commits 9fb8a4a2, c74402c5). Ready to implement, Phase 0 first.

Decisions: (1) full markdown parse of the title= value, performance deferred; (2) single-block-single-paragraph PandocBlocks -> take inlines, anything else -> warning + ignore; (3) attribute AND heading both present -> warn and consume either (deliberate, warned divergence from Q1, which silently prefers the attribute and leaves the heading in the body); (4) remove the level >= 2 heading check to match Q1's resolveHeadingCaption; (5) no worktree, branch only.

Main design finding: naive nested parsing would silently corrupt source locations. Attribute values are stored UNESCAPED and unquoted while their AttrSourceInfo span covers the RAW quote-inclusive text, so the map is piecewise-affine -- but SourceInfo::substring composes only affine maps. Measured drift: +1 immediately (the opening quote) plus one byte per collapsed escape. Filed as bd-mxa44voa (shared infrastructure; the YAML path has the same latent bug).

Workaround adopted here needs no new infrastructure and no SourceContext access: derive the parent from lengths alone. span_len == value.len() -> bare value, substring(src, 0, n), exact. span_len == value.len() + 2 -> quoted with no escapes collapsed, substring(src, 1, 1+n), exact. Otherwise escapes were collapsed -> fall back to the whole-value span. The fallback is bounded and safe because unescaping only shrinks, so offsets always stay inside the attribute's raw extent. The exact path covers every fixture case and all ~25 affected Connect pages.

Also filed bd-bhxeoqoj (p3): theorem.rs:317-319 documents this span as excluding the quotes, which is wrong and would have propagated the off-by-one.

Evidence artifacts committed: escape-drift-probe.md/.qmd (measured spans + raw bytes) and observed-output.md (per-case render at HEAD).

c-ecbqzqc5.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ecbqzqc5.text:
Implemented on branch braid/callout-title-attribute (commit dfe651c1, off main @ b2b6100c). Ready for review/push -- not pushed.

All five decisions implemented as agreed. Q1 precedence (attribute wins, parsed as markdown inlines), heading removal moved into the fallback branch only, level >= 2 check removed, Q-2-43 warn-and-consume when both are present, Q-2-44 for block-valued titles.

Source mapping: attribute_value_source derives the parent SourceInfo from lengths alone -- span_len == n (bare) and span_len == n + 2 (quoted, nothing collapsed) are exact; anything else falls back to the whole-value span, bounded because unescaping only shrinks so offsets cannot leave the attribute. No SourceContext dependency, no new infrastructure. Exact non-affine mapping remains bd-mxa44voa.

DISCOVERY worth knowing: escaping a leading # in a title takes TWO backslashes, not one. Two unescape layers run in sequence -- the attribute layer collapses \# to a bare #, which the markdown parser then reads as a heading (the very error being avoided); \\# survives the first layer as \# and parses as a literal #. I asserted the single-backslash form in a docs draft, then verified by render and found it wrong. Now pinned by double_backslash_escapes_a_leading_hash / single_backslash_hash_is_still_a_heading and documented in docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-44.qmd. This is pre-existing attribute behavior that only becomes reachable now that attribute values are parsed as markdown.

Verification: cargo nextest run --workspace 11471/11471 passed (a first fail-fast run tripped the known flake bd-u0tldu4z; complete rerun of the identical tree was green). cargo xtask verify FULL including the WASM leg, all 14 steps, exit 0 -- clippy caught two needless_borrow in the new test code on the first attempt, fixed. End-to-end q2 render of the 7-case repro inspected: case 1 is now byte-identical to the Q1 markup quoted in this strand's description. Zero snapshot files touched.

Scope note: there is no callouts FEATURE page anywhere under docs/, so title= has no user-facing home to be documented in -- only the two new error pages. Worth a separate strand if callout docs are wanted.

c-iphlzihg.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-iphlzihg.text:
Investigated 2026-08-10. Plan skeleton + repro committed at claude-notes/plans/2026-08-10-callout-title-attribute.md (commit 7a576d60, on branch docs/feature-porting-process -- implementation should move to its own worktree off main).

Verdict: ready to design. Root-cause analysis in the description is accurate at HEAD; pre-flight 'cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build' passed (exit 0).

Reproduced end-to-end with a 7-case fixture (claude-notes/plans/callout-title-attribute-investigation/repro.qmd; per-case output in observed-output.md).

NEW FINDING not in the description -- the 'both attribute and heading' case is a DOUBLE divergence, and it changes the fix. q2 currently lets the heading WIN and CONSUMES it from the body. Q1 gives the attribute precedence AND leaves the heading in the body, because the heading is only removed inside resolveHeadingCaption (common/pandoc.lua:130-138), which is never called when title= is non-empty. So the suggested fix ('read the attribute first, fall back to the header branch') is necessary but not sufficient: the header removal at callout.rs:204 must MOVE into the fallback branch, otherwise precedence is fixed while the body silently loses its heading.

Good news on the parsing question: the Q1-faithful 'parse the attribute as markdown inlines' path is cheap. pampa::pandoc::meta::parse_config_string_as_markdown(&str, &SourceInfo, &mut Vec<DiagnosticMessage>) -> ConfigValueKind (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs:34) is sync, wasm-safe, and already called from an AstTransform at crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/config_markdown.rs:164. Open sub-question: it returns PandocBlocks (not Inlines) if the value contains block syntax, which a title slot cannot hold.

For the value's source span, use the guarded pattern from crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/theorem.rs:336-360 -- AttrSourceInfo.attributes is positionally aligned with Attr.2 but that invariant is known-broken in two parser paths (bd-3aolj, bd-1e6a5), so length-check + debug_assert + fall back to None.

Also noted: title= is preserved on the outer div in all cases (read it, do not remove it); title="" is emitted as a literal empty attribute; no diagnostic is emitted in any case. Separate possible divergence, not filed: Q1's resolveHeadingCaption accepts ANY Header level, q2 requires level >= 2 (callout.rs:202), so an H1-led callout titles in Q1 but not in q2 -- see design question 4 in the plan.

5 open design questions for the user in the plan; not starting implementation until they are answered.

title: Flaky: admin_collect_lifecycle::collect_reverification_skips_rereferenced_candidate fails on case-insensitive filesystems
description:
Observed 2026-07-28 during an unrelated verify run on macOS. The assert at crates/quarto-hub/tests/integration/admin_collect_lifecycle.rs:205 compared manifest.candidates[0].doc_id against orphan_id and got '3Y3QamdZPUgcWJsd4ZU9N4Xb9ZzD' vs '3y3QamdZPUgcWJsd4ZU9N4Xb9ZzD' — identical apart from the case of one character.

Automerge document ids are random base58, so two ids in one test run can differ only by case. On a case-insensitive filesystem (APFS/HFS+ by default on macOS, and NTFS on Windows) the two per-doc directories collide, and scan_store then reports the wrong candidate.

Random-dependent, so it reproduces rarely: the test passed 3/3 on immediate re-run. Unrelated to the change being verified at the time (bd-1vlw8) — quarto-hub depends on none of the crates it touched.

Likely fix: make the store's on-disk directory naming case-unambiguous (e.g. encode the id, or lowercase it with a disambiguating suffix), or have the test assert on a case-insensitively-unique id set.

c-01l41h03.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-01l41h03.text: 2026-07-29: sibling test admin_collect_lifecycle::collect_lifecycle_quarantine_restore_purge also failed once (0.04s, macOS, under full-workspace parallel load during cargo xtask verify on braid/bd-r1by4u2a-blog-scaffold); passed on 4 immediate re-runs and in an adjacent full-workspace run. Same-module flake family — worth auditing the whole admin_collect_lifecycle module, not just the one test.

c-7cj3ekzw.author: shikokuchuo
c-7cj3ekzw.text: Another sighting, 2026-08-03, during a full 'cargo xtask verify' on macOS for bd-aw8f3sp8 (F3, an /auth/me JSON field — no plausible relation to store scanning): sibling test admin_collect_lifecycle::collect_lifecycle_quarantine_restore_purge failed in the full run, passed immediately in isolation. Failure stderr lost to output truncation, so the case-collision shape is inferred (same build_store/scan_store fixture, same random-base58-id-as-directory-name scheme), not confirmed. Suggest widening this strand's title beyond collect_reverification_skips_rereferenced_candidate — the whole file shares the hazard.

c-wcbci7m1.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-wcbci7m1.text:
Mechanism confirmed by reading the code rather than inferring it.

quarto-hub/src/admin/scan.rs:80 list_doc_ids_filesystem reconstructs each doc id by concatenating two directory-name levels: 'out.push(format!("{prefix}{rest}"))', where prefix is the level-1 dir name and rest the level-2. So the id round-trips through the filesystem rather than being read from document metadata.

On a case-insensitive but case-PRESERVING filesystem (APFS/HFS+ default on macOS; NTFS), two doc ids whose shard prefixes differ only in case resolve to the same level-1 directory. Whichever document is created first fixes that directory's on-disk casing; the second document is then stored under it. Reading back, the second document's id is reconstructed with the FIRST document's prefix casing.

The observed failure matches exactly: '3Y3QamdZPUgcWJsd4ZU9N4Xb9ZzD' vs '3y3QamdZPUgcWJsd4ZU9N4Xb9ZzD' differ at index 1 only, and are equal when lowercased — i.e. the corruption is confined to the shard prefix, precisely where a colliding directory name would put it.

Frequency follows: base58 is case-sensitive, so two random ids colliding case-insensitively in their prefix but differing in case is uncommon but not rare enough to never happen. build_store() creates exactly two documents per run.

This is a correctness bug in the store, not only a test bug: any code path that recovers doc ids from disk can hand back an id that does not match the document. The test is just where it surfaced.

title: q2 render truncates source images referenced in qmd documents
description: ResourceCollectorTransform stores image source paths as artifacts with empty content; write_artifacts then opens the source path for writing and truncates it to 0 bytes. Confirmed via 'q2 render docs/authoring/markdown/index.qmd' which truncates docs/authoring/markdown/elephant.png from 126124 bytes to 0. Plan doc: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-render-truncates-source-images.md
close_reason: Fixed in ad18adcb — destructive writes routed through validated OutputSink. ResourceCollectorTransform no longer stores source paths as empty-content artifacts; it emits (src, dest) copy ops into RenderContext::resource_copies, and OutputSink validates every dest is under allowed_roots and skips copies where src == dest. Verified 2026-07-27 by running the tests: quarto-core::integration render_preserves_source_files (4/4 pass, incl. render_does_not_truncate_referenced_image) and the CLI end-to-end quarto::integration render_cli_e2e::render_preserves_source_image_and_copies_to_site, which spawns the real q2 render binary and asserts the source PNG is byte-unchanged. Original repro not re-runnable: the docs fixture moved from docs/authoring/markdown/elephant.png to docs/guides/authoring/elephant.png. Phase 3 hardening follow-ups (A1-A3 in the plan doc) were never filed at the time; now tracked as bd-72f43umg.

title: Rendering a diagnostic must not be able to abort a render or discard queued diagnostics (panic boundary)
description:
Hardening, not a live defect. The specific panic that motivated this is fixed (char-boundary snapping in quarto-error-reporting); this strand is about the CLASS, which that fix does not address.

THE PATHOLOGY OBSERVED. In bd-ariadne-config-span-char-boundary-panic-rkqmhzrg, a single bad byte offset in one warning produced: exit 101 on a render whose _site/ was COMPLETE AND CORRECT, plus silent loss of every diagnostic queued behind the failing one. On the real Positron site the panic fired ~4s in, so a reader saw far fewer problems than actually existed while the exit code claimed catastrophe. None of that is proportionate to 'a warning printed badly'.

WHAT THE EXISTING FIX DOES NOT COVER. Snapping offsets to char boundaries removes one CAUSE. It does nothing for: a future ariadne release that panics on some other input (quarto-error-reporting is coupled tightly enough to ariadne's internals that it mirrors a private constant from ariadne 0.6.0 src/lib.rs:543); a different index assumption not yet imagined; arithmetic bugs in quarto-error-reporting's own future code; or the length()-1 fallback producing something else pathological.

PROPOSAL. A catch_unwind boundary around the PER-DIAGNOSTIC render, so any panic degrades to one ugly diagnostic instead of killing the render and dropping the rest of the stream.

Two constraints, both deliberate:

1. Put it in q2, NOT in quarto-error-reporting. q2 owns the 'render succeeded, now emit warnings' loop and owns the exit code. A library silently swallowing panics on its callers' behalf is presumptuous; a CLI deciding that its warning printer cannot kill the build is just correct.

2. Surface it loudly; do not swallow it. Emit something like 'internal error rendering diagnostic Q-2-9 (details suppressed)' and continue. A silently-caught panic is how the NEXT bug of this shape never gets filed at all. Arguably it should also be reported through the normal diagnostic channel so --json-errors consumers see it.

KNOWN COSTS / THINGS TO CHECK.
- catch_unwind requires UnwindSafe; the diagnostic render closure captures &DiagnosticMessage and &SourceContext, so this needs checking (AssertUnwindSafe may be justified here since nothing is mutated, but that reasoning should be written down, not assumed).
- catch_unwind is a no-op under panic=abort. Check the wasm profile: .cargo/config.toml sets panic=unwind for wasm32 deliberately (the wasm-c-shim needs catch_unwind for Lua's setjmp/longjmp replacement), so wasm is probably fine, but confirm the native release profile too.
- Must NOT change exit-code semantics: a caught panic while printing a WARNING must not turn into a failed render.

Scope: the diagnostic emission loop, not the render pipeline generally.
close_reason: Implemented in 73673ba48 (Plan 2 Phase 5, feature/yaml-provenance). catch_unwind around the PER-DIAGNOSTIC render at all 8 sites in crates/quarto/src/commands/render.rs (3 text + 5 json) — per-diagnostic, not per-loop, since wrapping the loop would still discard everything queued behind a bad one. Surfaces loudly: 'internal error rendering diagnostic <CODE>' on stderr, asserted by the tests, so a swallowing boundary cannot pass. Fault injection is env-gated AND cfg(debug_assertions)-gated at both the fn and its sole call site, so arming it in release is structurally impossible (confirmed by strings/nm on target/release/q2). All three of this strand's 'things to check' are discharged: (1) UnwindSafe reasoning is not merely written down, it is COMPILER-PROVEN — the bound is an explicit non-asserted std::panic::UnwindSafe at every site, so AssertUnwindSafe turned out NOT to be needed and a future edit dragging &mut across the boundary now fails to build; (2) panic=unwind confirmed for native and wasm32, so catch_unwind is not a no-op; (3) exit-code invariant tested — a caught panic on a warning still exits 0, and the exit code is computed from diagnostic_counts() before printing. 4 new tests drive the real q2 binary (12918/198, delta +4). DEVIATION from this strand's text, deliberate: the internal-error line is NOT reported through the normal diagnostic channel for --json-errors consumers (the strand said 'arguably'). A new Q- code would require a docs page plus an in-code-order sidebar entry in the same commit per cargo xtask lint, and it is not a user-actionable catalog error; the plain-text line matches unchanged precedent at render.rs:1685. Deferred to the final review: the line names the CODE but not the DOCUMENT, and 6 of the 8 sites have no fixture reaching them.

title: Heading-id deduplication can still emit duplicate ids
description:
The `seen_ids` counter in the reader's header filter (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:946-952) never records the ids it *generates*, only the base ids it derives. A generated `base-N` can therefore collide with a later (or earlier) heading, and q2 emits the same `id` twice — invalid HTML, and a deep link to the anchor silently resolves to whichever section comes first.

```rust
let final_id = if let Some(count) = seen_ids.get_mut(&base_id) {
    *count += 1;
    format!("{}-{}", base_id, count)   // <- never inserted into seen_ids
} else {
    seen_ids.insert(base_id.clone(), 0);
    base_id
};
```

## Measured 2026-08-13

q2 at commit 6af97135 (branch braid/bd-heading-id-drops-inline-content-fl84n3ql) vs pandoc 3.9.0.2 (`pandoc -f markdown+smart -t html --section-divs`). Two independent collisions, one in each direction:

Source `## a` / `## a` / `## a-1`:

| | Pandoc | q2 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `a` | `a` |
| 2 | `a-1` | `a-1` |
| 3 | `a-1-1` | `a-1`  **(duplicate)** |

Source `## b` / `## b-1` / `## b`:

| | Pandoc | q2 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `b` | `b` |
| 2 | `b-1` | `b-1` |
| 3 | `b-2` | `b-1`  **(duplicate)** |

Case 1: a heading whose *literal* text slugs to `a-1` collides with the id generated for a repeated `## a`. Case 2: the generated `b-1` for the second `## b` collides with an *earlier* literal `b-1`. Note the counter is not even consulted for the literal ones, so the order does not matter.

## Why Pandoc does not have this

`uniqueIdent` keeps a `Set` of every identifier already handed out and searches for the first free `base-N`, rather than keeping a per-base counter. Note the resulting rule in case 1: `a-1` is treated as its own base, so the third heading becomes `a-1-1`, not `a-2`.

## Suggested fix direction

Replace the `HashMap<String, usize>` counter with a used-set (or keep the counter as a search hint but verify membership before emitting, and insert the emitted id). Matching Pandoc exactly means: given `base`, if `base` is free use it, else try `base-1`, `base-2`, ... until free, and record whatever is emitted.

Watch for snapshot churn: unlike bd-heading-id-drops-inline-content-fl84n3ql (which touched zero snapshots and zero docs/ anchors) this changes ids only in documents that already have a collision, but any such document in the fixture corpus will move.

## Provenance

Found by reading `postprocess.rs` while fixing bd-heading-id-drops-inline-content-fl84n3ql, then confirmed by rendering. Pre-existing and independent of that fix — the collector fix makes empty-derived ids much rarer, which if anything makes this *less* likely to be hit, not more. Filed at the user's request rather than folded in, since it is a different defect in a different function.

p2 rather than p3 because the failure mode is duplicate `id` attributes in shipped HTML, which is invalid and breaks anchors silently.

title: qmd-syntax-helper: re-key literal-brackets to the q_2_49.rs convention
description:
Now that Q-2-49 (lone bare bracket group) exists, qmd-syntax-helper's literal-brackets rule has a diagnostic code to key off and could join the q_2_NN.rs convention its siblings follow.

Deliberately out of scope for the v1 change (see claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-warning-suppression-and-lone-bracket-diagnostic.md):

- It touches a user-visible CLI surface. `-r literal-brackets` is documented in docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-46.qmd, the new docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-49.qmd, and the rule's own module header. A rename needs those updated together, or an alias.
- It is not a pure rename. The sibling q_2_NN rules derive violations from parse errors; literal_brackets.rs derives them from its own bracket_analysis module. Folding it into the convention means reconciling those two shapes.

Whatever happens, the rule should STAY opt-in for `convert -r all`, for the reason its own header gives: an escape is a source edit that cannot afterwards be distinguished from an author's intent, so it must never be made unasked. That reasoning is independent of whether a diagnostic code now exists.

title: Lint: ban as_plain_text()+parse() numeric chains outside blessed accessors

title: q2 preview: project-level custom SCSS theme fails with Q-14-4 (theme file never reaches the VFS)

title: q2 preview: Div with class='section' emits <div>, not <section> — breaks Quarto's :has(+ section) margin rules
description: The native HTML writer (crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:1129-1142) emits <section>...</section> for Pandoc Div blocks whose class list contains 'section'; the React Div component in ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/Div.tsx always emits <div>. Consequence: Quarto theme CSS rules keyed on the <section> tag (e.g. 'main.content > p:has(+ section) { margin-bottom: 2rem }') don't apply to preview, causing visible spacing drift. Concrete repro: the 'This is an extremely basic website' paragraph in the fixture has 17px bottom margin in preview vs 34px in render. Fix: mirror the native writer — emit <section> when classes contains SECTION ('section').
close_reason: Implementation complete: Pandoc Divs with class='section' now render as <section> in q2 preview, matching the native HTML writer. Visible result: 'This is an extremely basic website' paragraph margin-bottom now 34px (was 17px), matching q2 render exactly. Quarto theme's main.content > p:has(+ section) selector now matches in preview. 2 new SPA tests; 152/152 green; cargo xtask verify 12/12 green.

title: CaptureSpliceStage drops includes/filters/supporting_files from recorded ExecuteResult
description:
crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/capture_splice.rs explicitly only consumes `result.markdown` from the captured ExecuteResult JSON. Comment in the code:

> We don't need the rest of the ExecuteResult shape here (filters, includes, supporting_files) — those are engine-side concerns the splice doesn't reproduce in the AST.

**Verified still present in PR #238 (`feature/multi-engine` branch)** — the new fold-over-Vec<EngineCapture> path drops aux fields per-iteration, same comment. So this is a multi-engine bug as well as a single-engine bug.

Engines emitting side effects via `ExecuteResult.includes` (e.g. CSS/JS injection) work on `q2 render` but silently fail on `q2 preview`. Same shape as the CodeHighlightStage incident in CLAUDE.md.

For the mermaid first ship (bd-gwfdo), the plan v2 routes the jsdelivr <script> via the engine's `markdown` output (Q-C → C1) which dodges this gap. Fixing bd-cp3em would let us migrate to the cleaner ExecuteResult.includes path (Q-C → C2/C3) in a follow-up.

Discovered during mermaid engine design — see claude-notes/plans/2026-05-28-mermaidjs-engine-design.md gap G6.

title: Flaky: preview-renderer integration run fails on an unhandled elementFromPoint error
description:
cargo xtask verify step 11 (shared preview-* package tests) intermittently fails with ALL TESTS PASSING: 'Test Files 48 passed (48) / Tests 565 passed | 1 skipped (566) / Errors 1 error'. Vitest treats an unhandled error as a run failure, so the whole verify goes red on a green test suite.

The error: TypeError: (intermediate value).elementFromPoint is not a function, thrown from prosemirror-view's posAtCoords (node_modules/prosemirror-view/dist/index.js:465) via placeCaretFromClick (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/richtext/caretFromClick.ts:32) called from RichTextEditor.tsx:235. Originates in src/q2-preview/p3-4-inline-breadcrumb.integration.test.tsx, last test 'renders the breadcrumb INSIDE the toolbar row and suppresses the standalone chip (rich Para)'.

Root cause shape: jsdom does not implement document.elementFromPoint, and RichTextEditor.tsx:235 schedules the caret placement in a requestAnimationFrame. When the rAF callback happens to fire AFTER the test that set it up has finished, it throws outside any test, so no test catches it and vitest reports an unhandled error. Timing-dependent, hence intermittent.

Reproduction: intermittent. Observed once on 2026-07-28 during bd-dofxhzaj's pre-push verify; 3 immediate consecutive re-runs of 'npm run test:integration' in ts-packages/preview-renderer were all clean.

Likely fixes (pick one, don't do all): (a) stub document.elementFromPoint in the integration-test setup file — jsdom will never have it, and every consumer of posAtCoords has this exposure, not just this test; (b) cancel the pending rAF in RichTextEditor's cleanup so no callback can outlive the component; (c) guard placeCaretFromClick on typeof document.elementFromPoint === 'function'. (a)+(b) together is probably the honest fix: (a) removes the crash, (b) removes the leak that makes it escape the test.

NOT caused by the bd-dofxhzaj musl work — that branch's diff is .yml + .md only. Filed because a flake that reddens verify on an all-green suite will waste someone's afternoon.

c-dxc5bisx.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-dxc5bisx.text:
PR opened: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/431 (bugfix/bd-cpyq99ps-elementfrompoint-flake -> main, 1 commit). cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build green exit 0.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is NOT what this strand originally guessed: one unguarded line in ProseMirror's posAtCoords — 'let elt = (view.root.elementFromPoint ? view.root : doc).elementFromPoint(...)' — guards view.root but not the doc fallback, and jsdom implements elementFromPoint on neither. The strand's guesses (b) 'cancel the pending rAF in cleanup' and (c) 'guard placeCaretFromClick' were both wrong: the mount effect ALREADY does 'return () => cancelAnimationFrame(raf)' AND guards editor.isDestroyed, and caretFromPoint (the sibling helper on the same path) already guards both of its own APIs. Only (a) — stub elementFromPoint in the test setup — was right, and for a better reason than I first gave.

Two things made it a flake rather than a failure: the call runs in a requestAnimationFrame (deliberately, so the editor box is laid out first), so machine load decides whether the throw is attributed to a test or escapes it; and NOTHING ever exercised the real path — caretFromClick.test.ts uses a fake editor with a vi.fn() posAtCoords, RichTextEditor.caret.integration.test.tsx vi.mocks the whole module, and the file that tripped it mocks nothing and reached real ProseMirror by accident. So caretFromClick.ts's own comment 'jsdom returns null from posAtCoords' was FALSE and had never been checked.

Fix: stub Document.prototype.elementFromPoint -> null in src/test-utils/setup.ts. Harness, not production — every real browser implements it, so a guard in caretFromClick.ts would be dead code papering over a jsdom gap; null is the honest answer (no layout, nothing under any point) and makes posAtCoords return the miss callers already handle. Follows a precedent already in the same file (getClientRects stubs on Text/Range for ProseMirror coordsAtPos, same rAF, same remedy).

New caretFromClick.integration.test.ts drives a REAL tiptap editor, nothing mocked, closing the coverage gap: 5/5 fail before with the exact prosemirror-view:465 stack, 5/5 pass after. Full integration suite x6 before (fails every run), x4 after (49 files, 570 tests, 0 errors). Unit suite unaffected.

HONEST LIMIT: reproduced and fixed the root cause deterministically; did NOT reproduce the original intermittent unhandled-error form on demand (needs the rAF to lose its race against teardown, i.e. machine load). Does not weaken the fix — posAtCoords now has nothing to throw from regardless of when the frame fires.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-28-preview-renderer-elementfrompoint-flake.md

title: qmd writer: implicit-figure path drops trailing newline, collapses next block (issue #180)
description:
Triage doc: claude-notes/issue-reports/180/triage.md on branch issue-180.

Root cause: write_figure (crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:759) implicit-figure branch returns directly from write_image without emitting the trailing \n that every block writer is expected to produce. When such a Figure is followed by another block (top-level or inside a Div), the inter-block separator collapses to a single \n instead of a blank line, and the re-parser glues the two blocks into one Para. Affects every layout/subfigure div in the docs corpus.

Reports covered (both same root cause):
- Bug A: top-level Figure followed by Para -> one Para after round-trip
- Bug B: Div with multiple Figure children + caption -> one Para inside the Div after round-trip

Fix (TDD-first per crates/pampa/CLAUDE.md):
1. Add failing roundtrip tests under tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/
   - figure_implicit_then_para.qmd
   - layout_div_subfigures.qmd
   - figure_implicit_then_figure.qmd (extra coverage)
2. Verify they fail.
3. Fix write_figure: replace 'return write_image(...)' with 'write_image(...)?; writeln!(buf)?; Ok(())'.
4. Verify tests pass.
5. cargo nextest run --workspace to catch downstream snapshot updates.

Not a duplicate of bd-emr4 — that is about non-implicit Figure shapes hitting the fallback fenced-div path. This bug is in the implicit-figure code path; different code, different fix.

title: Document include expansion semantics: AST-splice at block positions vs textual splice inside code fences
description:
The `include` shortcode is absent from user-facing documentation, and the distinction that bd-include-in-code-block-f8mvtczn introduces has nowhere to live.

GAPS FOUND (docs/ audit, 2026-08-10):

1. `docs/guides/authoring/shortcodes.qmd` has a 'Built-in shortcodes' table listing only `meta`, `env`, `var`. `include` is not mentioned anywhere on the page.

2. Its 'Where shortcodes are evaluated' section already draws the textual/non-textual line for other shortcodes — it says include-files and 'code and other text contexts' get *textual* substitution — but says nothing about `include` itself, which is the one shortcode whose two contexts behave by two different mechanisms.

3. There is no includes guide page at all. `ls docs/guides/authoring/` has no `includes.qmd`; includes are documented only indirectly through the four Q-17-* error pages (`docs/errors/include/`), which are troubleshooting references, not authoring guidance.

WHAT NEEDS SAYING. After bd-include-in-code-block-f8mvtczn, `include` has two distinct expansion mechanisms and users can observe the difference:

- At block-list positions (own paragraph, or nested in a div/callout/blockquote/list item/table cell/figure), the target is *parsed as qmd* and its **AST blocks are spliced** into the document. Nested includes recurse; cycles are detected.
- Inside a fenced code block, the target's **bytes are spliced textually** into the fence, unparsed. No recursion (deliberate divergence from Q1 — see the parent strand). `shortcodes="false"` opts out.

The consequences users can actually hit: a `.qmd` included into a fence shows its include lines literally rather than expanding them; a file included into a fence is never interpreted as markdown; and only the block-position form participates in cross-references, crossref numbering, etc.

SCOPE. At minimum add `include` to the built-ins table and a paragraph to 'Where shortcodes are evaluated'. Better: a dedicated `docs/guides/authoring/includes.qmd` covering both forms, path resolution (relative to the declaring file; leading `/` is project-root-relative), and the code-fence listing idiom — which is the single most common real-world use (the Posit Connect docs port has ~44 such listings).

Blocked-ish: the code-fence behavior does not exist yet. Write this once the parent lands, so the docs describe shipped behavior.

title: A custom listing template that uses no doctemplate directives is spliced into the page verbatim, with no diagnostic
description:
A `type: custom` listing whose `template:` file contains no doctemplate directives is copied byte-for-byte into the rendered page, with zero diagnostics and exit 0. The reader sees the raw template. Quarto 1, whose custom listings are EJS, renders real cards from the same file.

## Symptom

listing: {type: custom, template: welcome-card.ejs, contents: ["item-*.qmd"]}

_site/index.html contains, verbatim:

    <div class="custom-card-grid<%= items[0].columns === 2 ? ' columns-2' : '' %>">
      <% for (const item of items) { %>
        <a href="<%= item.link %>" class="custom-card-wrapper">

Rendered N of N files, no warnings, exit 0. A link checker then reports pages linking to the literal target `<%= item.link %>`.

## Root cause

Three verified links, all at v0.27.0:

1. The doctemplate grammar treats `$` as its ONLY special character — crates/tree-sitter-doctemplate/grammar/grammar.js: `text: ($) => /[^$]+/`. A template containing no `$` therefore parses as a single literal-text node and compiles "successfully"; rendering it emits the input unchanged.

2. load_custom_template (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/listing_render.rs:375) does a plain fs::read_to_string with no content validation. The only diagnostic on that path is Q-12-8, for I/O failure.

3. Nothing anywhere checks that a compiled template actually used a directive. This is an absent check, not a weak one.

Q-12-7 structurally cannot cover this: it fires only when `l.template.is_some() && l.kind != ListingType::Custom` (crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/config.rs:593). Here `type: custom` is set correctly, so the config is valid and the template is simply never templated.

## The exact silence boundary

Two existing guards accidentally catch some bad templates. Measured:

  template body                                    result
  "HAS A BARE $ SIGN AND NO DIRECTIVES"            Q-12-10 "template failed to compile: ParseError ... unexpected ' SIGN AND NO '"
  bare EJS markup, no $, does not re-parse         Q-12-10 "Re-parsing rendered listing `c` failed ... first: Parse error"
  the same EJS wrapped in a ```{=html} block       SILENCE, dumped verbatim

So the trigger is not merely "contains no bare `$`" — it is "contains no bare `$` AND the unchanged text re-parses cleanly as markdown". Wrapping the template in a raw-HTML block satisfies both, and that is exactly how a well-formed HTML card template is naturally written. The better the template, the likelier the silence.

A stray dollar sign gets you a diagnostic; a carefully written HTML template gets you none.

## Suggested fix direction

Cheapest reliable signal: compare the compiled output against the template source — byte-identical means no directive was ever applied. That catches all three rows above uniformly and needs no grammar change. More thorough: have the compiler report whether any directive node was present, and warn when a custom template compiled to pure literal text.

Either way the diagnostic should name the template path and say the file appears not to be a doctemplate, since the common cause will be a Quarto 1 EJS template carried over unconverted.

## Real-world hit

Positron website docs: 11 listings across 8 pages use templates/welcome-card.ejs or templates/feature-card.ejs, carried over from Quarto 1. Affected pages: welcome, features, assistant, assistant-getting-started, ai-features, language-guides, older-releases, tutorials — the site's entire landing and navigation surface. Every one renders raw EJS to the reader with no warning of any kind.

## Repro

/Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/ejs-template-dumped/

`q2 render`, then compare _site/repro.html against _site/control.html. Both declare the same listing over the same file-glob contents; only the template differs.

  repro.qmd    template: welcome-card.ejs (copied byte-for-byte from the Positron site)
               -> 9 literal '<%' in the output, ZERO warnings
  control.qmd  template: a valid q2 doctemplate
               -> 0 literal '<%', real cards, correct href="item-one.html"

Quarto 1 on the same repro renders real cards and exits 0. The repro uses a file-glob `contents:` deliberately, so it is independent of inline-record handling.

Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-ejs-template-dumped-e7491tmf. Observed with q2 0.27.0 (official release build); origin/main == v0.27.0 == d05e96ee8 as of 2026-08-25.

NOTE ON SCOPE: this is not a request for EJS support. Converting these templates to doctemplates is the porting project's own work and is tracked there. The ask here is only that q2 not emit an untemplated template into the page silently.
close_reason: Fixed and shipped: Q-12-24 (untemplated/EJS custom template warns and skips) plus Q-12-9 widened to .ejs, merged as PR #603, verified in q2 0.28.0

c-kpccral0.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-kpccral0.text:
ADDITIONAL FINDING: q2 already has a diagnostic for precisely this situation, and it misses the more common file extension.

Q-12-9 "Deprecated .ejs.md Template Extension" — "The `.ejs.md` template extension is a Q1 idiom and is not supported by Q2 doctemplate. See the Q1 → Q2 migration guide." That is exactly the message an author carrying a Q1 custom listing template needs.

Its trigger is a literal suffix test, crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/config.rs:518:

    if path.ends_with(".ejs.md") {

So `template: card.ejs.md` warns, and `template: card.ejs` does not. Verified end to end on 0.27.0 with two otherwise identical projects, same template body, differing only in the file extension:

    template: card.ejs     -> Rendered 2 of 2, NO diagnostic, template dumped verbatim
    template: card.ejs.md  -> Rendered 2 of 2, Q-12-9, template dumped verbatim

Both dump. Only one warns. Q1's own listing templates ship under both spellings (item-default.ejs.md, sidebar.ejs), and the Positron site — the real-world hit on this strand — uses plain `.ejs`: templates/welcome-card.ejs and templates/feature-card.ejs. So the eight affected pages sail past the one warning that exists for their exact situation.

This strengthens the case for the output-vs-source check proposed above rather than weakening it: an extension-based test cannot be the mechanism, because the extension is a naming convention and the failure is a content property. But widening Q-12-9 to `.ejs` as well is a cheap, independent improvement worth taking regardless — it costs one condition and would have caught the Positron case at config-parse time, before any rendering.

VERIFIED against the fix branch, 2026-08-25. Built binary from worktree .worktrees/workspace-2, branch braid/bd-custom-template-not-templated-e5t6m0i0-custom-template-not-templated, tip 900cfdccc. Rendered the full Positron site on main (templates still .ejs, port not applied). The fix does everything asked, and the extension widening as well: Q-12-9 11 occurrences — widened from `.ejs.md` to also match `.ejs`, which is exactly the additional finding recorded on this strand. Blames the `template:` value and says Quarto 2 listing templates use doctemplate syntax. Q-12-24 11 occurrences — new code. Names the listing id AND the template path, identifies `<% … %>` as Q1 EJS, states that Quarto 2 does not evaluate EJS, points at the Listings guide "Custom templates" section, and ends "Listing skipped." 11 and 11 is exactly the number of listings on this site using an .ejs template, so both codes fire on every affected listing and nowhere else. Behavioural change, which is the important half: RAW EJS NO LONGER REACHES THE PAGE. welcome.html contains 0 occurrences of `<%` (previously the template body was spliced in verbatim). The listing renders as an empty `
` instead. site-asset-check's `<%= item.link %>` broken-reference group is gone entirely — 214 broken refs across 8 distinct names, down from 221 across 9. So the silent-and-reader-visible failure is now loud-and-safe. Note the diagnostics are warnings, not errors: the render summary is unchanged at 97 of 98 files, 2 errors (both the unrelated download.qmd), with warnings 1717 -> 1739 (+22 = 11+11). Side effect worth knowing: the visible-text diff against Q1 goes slightly UP on the affected pages (features 47->51, ai-features 12->13, welcome 12->13, tutorials 11->12, assistant-getting-started 6->7). That is not a regression — it is the numbers becoming honest. Previously the dumped EJS contributed junk text lines that coincidentally offset some of Q1's real card lines; with the listing skipped the diff is now the clean statement "Q1 has N cards here, q2 has none". The same observation was made independently while porting the templates.

title: xtask lint: flag unwrap_or_default() on SourceInfo-typed expressions
description:
quarto-source-map deprecates SourceInfo::default() via an inherent method that shadows Default::default(), and its doc comment says the residual unwrap_or_default() / #[derive(Default)] hole is 'caught by separate grep tooling'.

That tooling does not exist. crates/xtask/src/lint/ has exactly two rules (external_sources.rs, metadata_as_str.rs), neither related, and there is no CI grep either. The hole was load-bearing in bd-2mxo: materialize.rs reached for unwrap_or_default() at all three container-span sites, producing Original{FileId(0), 0..0} -- a well-formed span indistinguishable from a real location at the first byte of file 0.

Those specific sites are now fixed, so this is prevention rather than an active bug.

Deferred from bd-2mxo's Phase B because doing it accurately needs type information a grep-level rule lacks: the receiver of .unwrap_or_default() has to be known to be Option<SourceInfo>. Options worth weighing: (a) heuristic grep on identifiers named *source_info*/*key_source*, accepting false negatives; (b) a clippy lint via dylint; (c) skip the lint and instead remove/redefine the Default impl upstream (see claude-notes/scratch/2026-08-06-memo-quarto-source-map-default-sourceinfo.md), which makes the lint unnecessary. (c) is probably the better buy.

Related: claude-notes/designs/provenance-contract.md sec.10 already declares SourceInfo::default() a bug everywhere outside the JSON reader and test scaffolding.

title: Continuation line starting with ':' silently drops the colon
description:
A soft-wrapped paragraph continuation line whose first character is ':' loses that character entirely — the text is silently corrupted rather than merely re-blocked. REPRO: Defined at :host scope. q2 @ fc2895b2 emits one paragraph, but the colon is gone: [ Para [Str "Defined", Space, Str "at", SoftBreak, Str "host", Space, Str "scope."] ]

Defined at host scope.

Pandoc (both the commonmark and markdown readers) emits '

Defined at :host scope.

' with the colon intact. This is worse than the sibling digit bug (bd-digit-line-splits-paragraph-w6tod0gh): that one mis-blocks text but preserves every character, whereas this one deletes an author's character with no diagnostic. CSS pseudo-selectors (':host', ':root', ':hover') and Windows drive-relative paths are realistic ways to hit it in prose. LIKELY AREA. crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c: ':' is blanket-excluded from both SOFT_LINE_ENDING gates (lines ~2748 and ~2887, 'first_lookahead != ':'' / 'second_lookahead != ':''), the same no-peek pattern that causes the digit bug. But the digit path merely ends the paragraph, whereas here a single paragraph survives WITH the colon missing — so the character is being consumed somewhere else as well, most likely the fenced-div (':::') or definition-list marker path. That consumption site, not just the gate, is what needs finding. Do not assume the gate fix alone will resolve it. DISCOVERED. While investigating the digit bug, checking whether the sibling blanket exclusions ('-', '+', ':') reproduced the same way. '-5 degrees' and '+5 percent' split the paragraph exactly like digits; ':' turned out to do something different and worse. Fixture: claude-notes/plans/digit-line-splits-paragraph-investigation/colon.qmd

title: TS-engine host applies format-agnostic execute defaults; Q1 hides echo/warning by default for presentation formats (revealjs/beamer/pptx/dashboard)
description:
Plan 4 (julia-validation) Phase 4F V-6 Q1-comparison finding, 2026-07-02.

engine-host-deno's applyExecuteDefaults (ts-packages/quarto-engine-host-deno/src/metadata-as-format.ts:217-224, kExecuteVisibilityDefaults) fills absent execute-visibility keys with a single fixed set (echo:true, warning:true, etc) regardless of target output format. This is CORRECT for plain html/pdf/latex/docx — verified empirically: a live Q1 render (quarto-cli dev checkout, ~/bin/quarto) of the Plan-4 minimal.qmd fixture shows the cell source by default in plain HTML output too (Q1's createHtmlFormat / defaultFormat in src/format/formats-shared.ts do NOT override echo/warning), matching q2's behavior exactly. So the earlier "q2 shows cell source by default where Q1 HTML hides it" note in claude-notes/research/2026-07-02-julia-engine-q2-compat.md section 9 overstates the gap for plain HTML.

The REAL, narrower gap (confirmed by reading Q1 source): Q1's writer-format-defaults layer overrides echo:false/warning:false specifically for PRESENTATION-family formats only:
- revealjs: createHtmlPresentationFormat (formats-shared.ts:139-142)
- beamer: formats.ts:324-325 (via createFormat override)
- pptx (PowerPoint): formats.ts ~324
- dashboard: format-dashboard.ts:80-81

q2 has no writer-format-defaults layer at all (no per-format branch), so a Julia (or any TS-engine) document rendered to revealjs/beamer/pptx/dashboard in q2 will echo source code by default, where Q1 would hide it. This only manifests for presentation-family formats, not general HTML/PDF/LaTeX rendering.

Fix requires a real writer-format-defaults layer (format-name-keyed override table), analogous to Q1's createFormat/createHtmlPresentationFormat pattern, consumed before/alongside applyExecuteDefaults in the TS engine host. Out of scope for Plan 4 (documentation-only phase); tracked here as a real, evidence-scoped follow-up.

See claude-notes/research/2026-07-02-julia-engine-q2-compat.md section 14 for the full V-6 comparison and the Q1 source citations (src/format/formats-shared.ts, src/format/formats.ts, src/format/pdf/format-pdf.ts, src/format/dashboard/format-dashboard.ts in the quarto-cli checkout).

c-7j0oumpb.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-7j0oumpb.text: Correction to the citation list above: beamer's echo:false/warning:false override lives in src/format/pdf/format-pdf.ts:74-89 (beamerFormat(), its own execute literal), NOT formats.ts. formats.ts:314-329 is powerpointFormat() (pptx) with the same echo:false/warning:false override. Plain pdfFormat()/latexFormat() in format-pdf.ts do NOT get the override -- confirmed by reading the full file, only beamerFormat() does. Verified while writing compat-log section 14.

title: q2 preview reveal theme omits quarto chrome layer (footer/logo position rules)
description:
Discovered verifying F3 (bd-n2w0sxgd): with the footer/logo DOM now emitted in preview, they render UNSTYLED (position:static) because the preview's runtime-delivered reveal theme (data-q2-theme blob) does NOT contain the .reveal .footer / .reveal .slide-logo positioning rules.

Render: footer position:fixed bottom:18px; logo position:fixed bottom:0 right:12px — rules sourced from the per-doc theme-<fp>.css (compiled from resources/scss/revealjs/quarto-revealjs.scss).
Preview: both position:static; theme blob (1784 rules) has neither rule.

So the preview's compiled theme is missing the quarto-revealjs.scss chrome layer that render's theme includes. This is a theme-CONTENT parity gap (sibling of bd-y259zb57's theme delivery), distinct from the DOM emission fixed in bd-n2w0sxgd.

Likely fix direction: either (a) ensure the preview theme compilation includes the same quarto-revealjs.scss partials render uses, or (b) move theme-independent Quarto chrome rules (footer/logo position) into the statically-imported resources/revealjs/quarto-reveal.css so preview gets them without the theme. Decide under the theme-parity design.

Repro: q2 preview examples/presentations/10-footer-logo/slides.qmd, inspect getComputedStyle(.footer).position (static; should be fixed). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-17-revealjs-preview-render-parity-audit.md (F4).
close_reason: Not reproducible on a clean build. The 'position: static' reading came from a binary whose embedded WASM theme artifact was stale (built via build-q2-preview-spa WITHOUT a WASM rebuild — the stale-WASM-in-q2-preview trap in CLAUDE.md). After cargo xtask verify rebuilt the WASM, the runtime-delivered reveal theme DOES contain .reveal .footer/.slide-logo; footer renders position:fixed bottom:18px and logo position:fixed bottom:0 right:12px, stable across reloads and 500ms-5s time samples. Verified Chrome on examples/presentations/10-footer-logo @ 8782. Reopen if it recurs on a freshly-built binary.

title: !str cannot opt a project-config key out of markdown parsing
description:
MARKDOWN_CONFIG_PATHS (quarto-core/src/transforms/config_markdown.rs) blesses a growing set of project-config presentation keys for markdown parsing. The authoring escape hatch for that — `!str` — does not work in project config, so a blessed key cannot be opted out from _quarto.yml.

## Why

Interpretation is resolved at YAML-load time by InterpretationContext (quarto-pandoc-types/src/config_value.rs:104-135). The two contexts have opposite defaults:

| source | untagged string | opt out / in |
|---|---|---|
| front matter (DocumentMetadata) | parsed as markdown -> PandocInlines | `!str` keeps it literal |
| _quarto.yml (ProjectConfig) | kept literal -> Scalar(String) | `!md` parses it |

In ProjectConfig, `!str`-tagged and untagged strings both resolve to Scalar(String) — the tag is consumed and leaves no trace. config_markdown then re-parses every blessed Scalar(String), so it cannot tell 'author explicitly wanted this literal' from 'author wrote a plain string'. Documented as a known limitation at config_markdown.rs:40-45.

## Why it matters more over time

The project direction is to bless more keys (user, 2026-08-13: 'It's good for us to parse more YAML fields into Markdown in general, especially since we have !str and !path as mechanisms for controlling that behavior in Quarto 2'). That rationale rests on an opt-out that is absent in exactly the context blessing applies to. Each newly blessed key widens the set of _quarto.yml strings that silently change meaning if they happen to contain markdown syntax, with no author-side recourse short of escaping.

Currently blessed: website.title, navbar/sidebar titles, page-footer regions and nav-item text (config_markdown.rs:84-122). Queued: toc-title (bd-toc-smart-quotes-6nro57ed phase 3), sidebar section: (bd-xygsu15r).

## Today's mitigations, and their limits

config_markdown.rs:43-45 argues escaped shortcodes ({{{< ... >}}}) and the absence of markup cover the practical cases. That holds for shortcodes but not for emphasis: a _quarto.yml `toc-title: 'Notes on *nix'` or a page-footer entry containing underscores has no documented way to stay literal.

## Fix directions (not decided)

1. Preserve the tag through load — carry Interpretation::PlainString on the ConfigValue (a kind variant, or a flag) so config_markdown can skip explicitly-literal values. Most faithful; touches the ConfigValue shape.
2. Make ProjectConfig honor !str by resolving blessed keys at load time instead of transform time. Rejected once already for this class — see the 2026-08-10 plan and bd-qzn1azon; load-time parsing is the wrong seam for presentation strings.
3. Document-only: state the limitation in user docs and give an escaping recipe. Cheapest, leaves the sharp edge.

Related: bd-qzn1azon (the two registries and when to pick which). Surfaced while settling bd-toc-smart-quotes-6nro57ed's phase 3 on 2026-08-13.

title: q2-preview chrome: replace HTML injection with React components
description:
Phase F (q2-preview website chrome) ships Strategy A: include the *-render transforms (navbar-render, sidebar-render, page-nav-render, footer-render, toc-render) in the q2-preview pipeline so meta.rendered.navigation.* is populated with Bootstrap HTML; the React PreviewDocument injects via dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

This is the pragmatic first cut — shippable in days, byte-identical to q2 render. The tradeoff is DOM stability inside the chrome: open dropdowns, sidebar collapse state, scroll position inside the sidebar, etc., are blown away every time the chrome re-renders. In practice the chrome only re-renders on _quarto.yml edits, page switches, or sidebar reorderings — uncommon during normal authoring — so the cost is bounded.

This follow-up tracks the proper Strategy B: replace the HTML-injection path with React components that render from the structured meta.navigation.* (the ConfigValue form populated by the *-generate transforms before *-render runs). Each component mirrors the Bootstrap HTML the corresponding render transform emits.

What this unlocks:
- Stateful chrome (open Bootstrap dropdowns, collapsed sidebar sections, scroll position inside the sidebar) survives chrome re-renders.
- React owns the click handlers natively rather than going through iframePostProcessor's after-the-fact .qmd-link rewriting.
- The drift risk between server HTML emission and React component output goes away (the React components ARE the renderer; q2-render's HTML stays the source of truth for non-preview pipelines).

Scope:
- Mirror Navbar / Sidebar / PageNav / Footer / Toc / Breadcrumbs from the Bootstrap HTML the *-render transforms emit today.
- TypeScript types matching the structured ConfigValue shape each *-generate transform writes.
- Remove the corresponding entries from Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED in pipeline.rs — those transforms become unused in the preview pipeline, so the *-render Rust modules either stay (for q2 render) or get factored to a shared HTML emitter consumed only by the q2 render pipeline.
- Snapshot tests asserting the React components emit markup matching the *-render Rust HTML output.

Filed during Phase F planning (2026-05-14). Parent edge to the F epic to be added once F itself is filed.

title: Jupyter engine hardcodes 'python3' kernel name instead of resolving by language
description: text_execute.rs:61,70-81 map_language_to_kernel() literal-matches language strings to fixed kernel names (python->python3, r->ir, etc.) instead of querying registered kernelspecs. kernelspec.rs already has find_kernelspec_for_language() (line 96) and resolve_kernel() (line 129) doing the correct language-based lookup with metadata override, both marked #[allow(dead_code)] with a doc comment saying they await wiring into the engine. quarto-cli's equivalent (src/core/jupyter/kernels.ts jupyterKernelspecForLanguage, verified) does exactly this lookup in production and is why jupyter works on Chris's Windows machine for quarto-cli despite no kernel literally named python3. Any OS with a Python kernel registered under a non-python3 name (conda env, versioned kernel, renamed kernel) hits KernelspecNotFound in q2 where quarto-cli succeeds. Separate from bd-fu0l (venv path-discovery blindness -- kernel exists but wrong search dirs); this is a name-matching-by-language gap, independent and additive. Fix: wire resolve_kernel/find_kernelspec_for_language into text_execute.rs's kernel-name resolution call site instead of map_language_to_kernel.

title: LRU sass cache leaks orphaned entries under parallel Pass 2 (index lost-update): 101 MB in .quarto/cache/sass
description: cache_set_lru writes the value, then read-modify-writes the JSON _lru_index; with 16 rayon workers the index updates race and lose, so entries are written to disk but never tracked and never evicted. Measured on the Connect docs from a cleared cache: serial render → 31 files / 31 index entries / 10.3 MB (budget respected); one parallel render → 70 files, index still 31; second → 93 files, 30 MB. The pre-existing dir had 315 files / 101 MB. Side effect: orphans still serve cache_get hits (lookup is by key, not via the index), which masked the key-variation bug (bd-…) by ~30%. Fix options: mutex around the index RMW within a process, or a per-process in-memory index flushed once at end of render, or reconcile the index against the directory on load. Research note: claude-notes/research/2026-09-13-connect-docs-render-profile.md
close_reason: Fixed in PR #679 (fbda74d92): async mutex around the LRU index RMW plus SystemRuntime::cache_list + reconcile-on-write; orphans are adopted and evicted, pre-fix cache dirs self-heal on the next compile.

title: Windows: JSON writer emits backslash path separators in output
description: On Windows the JSON writer emits astContext file names verbatim from ast_context.filenames, so input paths are backslash-separated (e.g. tests\snapshots\json\001.qmd) and snapshot json/001 mismatches against the forward-slash form committed on macOS/Linux. This is a cross-platform path-separator difference in output determinism, NOT a line-ending issue: normalizing separators does not shift any source byte offset, so it is independent of the preserve policy. Fix: normalize to forward slashes via quarto_util::to_forward_slashes, best applied at ingress in ASTContext::with_filename (crates/pampa/src/readers/qmd.rs around line 98) so diagnostics also get a stable path. Emission sites: crates/pampa/src/writers/json.rs lines 1812 and 3967. The helper already exists and is used elsewhere (PR #340 Lua side, HTML resource paths, DocumentProfile, listings). TDD: read a fixture via a backslash path, assert forward slashes in output. Originally filed under the line-ending epic because it shared the json/001 failure; detached 2026-06-26 as a distinct Windows/Linux parity topic.

c-62fpbe0g.author: cderv
c-62fpbe0g.text:
Implementation complete. Summary of decisions for PR body:

Root cause: ASTContext::with_filename/add_filename stored raw (possibly
backslash-separated) filenames verbatim; JSON writer and CLI diagnostics
both read from that same storage.

Fix (2 commits):
1. 44b75bcc — normalized at ASTContext::with_filename/add_filename via
   quarto_util::to_forward_slashes (matches existing codebase convention,
   also matches TypeScript Quarto's pathWithForwardSlashes, source-verified
   via deepwiki). Also fixed a second ingress point found during E2E CLI
   verification: main.rs's ad hoc fallback SourceContext on the
   hard-parse-error path, which bypassed ASTContext entirely.
2. f5a93fa4 — roborev review (job 1726) caught that readers::qmd::read and
   readers::commonmark::read each re-add the raw filename to
   context.source_context right after with_filename normalized it. qmd.rs's
   case was live (it fully replaces source_context, discarding the
   normalized entry) — this meant warnings on a *successful* parse still
   showed backslashes, even though the JSON writer and hard-error path were
   already fixed. commonmark.rs's case was verified inert (dead duplicate
   entry, FileId(0) hardcoded and already normalized) but fixed anyway for
   consistency.

Explicitly NOT changed, by design: main.rs's "Missing Newline at End of
File" CLI warning interpolates the raw CLI arg into a plain sentence —
that's echoing the user's own typed path back to them, not a portable
identifier, so native separators are correct there (matches rustc/cat
convention). Confirmed with user.

Verification: full pampa crate suite run before and after each fix
(baseline comparison via git stash), 8 pre-existing CRLF-related failures
confirmed unrelated (same catalogued Windows issue) both before and after,
zero new regressions. Full `cargo nextest run --workspace` was
intentionally skipped per user direction (CI covers it; known Windows
issues aren't fully resolved yet, so no new signal). Grep-based check
confirmed no crate outside pampa reads ASTContext.filenames as a literal
disk path. End-to-end CLI checks done for both JSON output and diagnostics.

Design questions (all confirmed by user before implementation):
normalize at with_filename ingress (not per-writer-site); normalize
add_filename too for consistency; regression tests run on all platforms
(no cfg gate, literal-string reproduction); diagnostics should also show
forward slashes (accepted as intended, not just JSON output).

title: Reveal reset.css leaks globally in preview — kills <em> italics in format:html
description: RevealDeck.tsx imports resources/revealjs/reset.css as a side-effecting CSS import; Vite hoists it into the global q2-preview SPA stylesheet bundle, so reveal's Meyer reset (html,body,...,em,i,cite,var{...font:inherit...}) applies to ALL preview content, not just .reveal decks. font:inherit resets font-style on <em>/<i>/<cite> to inherit, overriding the UA default em{font-style:italic}, so emphasis renders upright in q2 preview for format:html documents (and decks). Verified: computed font-style on a preview <em> is 'normal'. reveal.css and quarto-reveal.css are fully .reveal-scoped (no leak); reset.css is the sole global offender.
