title: Continuation line starting with a digit terminates the paragraph (fatal inside link text)
description:
WHAT HAPPENS. A soft-wrapped paragraph line whose first character is a digit terminates the paragraph. Two paragraphs come out where the author wrote one, splitting a sentence mid-clause: input q2 0.17.0 Quarto 1 "...license leases last\n30 minutes you..."

...leases last

30 minutes... one

, text intact "...greater than\n1000, the base filter..."

...greater than

1000, the... one

, text intact "...leases last\nthirty minutes you..." one

(correct) one

It fires on ANY digit-leading continuation line, whatever follows. Verified against '30 minutes', '1000,', '1 apple', '9', '3.14', '0', and a 14-digit run — longer than the 9-digit maximum CommonMark allows in an ordered-list marker, so no marker could possibly form. Only a non-digit first character ('x30') stays in the paragraph. This is a line-start character class, not a mis-parse of a list marker. FATAL VARIANT. When the wrap falls inside link text, the block ends before the closing ']' and the render fails outright: The set of characters that must be encoded can be found in [Section 3.2.1 of RFC 3986](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986#section-3.2.1). Error: [Q-2-1] Unclosed Span I reached the end of the block before finding a closing ']' Authors cannot reasonably be expected to avoid wrapping before a number, and the failure gives no hint that the line break is what caused it. WHERE IT LIVES. crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c, in the two SOFT_LINE_ENDING gates of the main scan function (first gate ~line 2739, second ~line 2878). Both conditions end with: first_lookahead > ' ' && !(first_lookahead >= '0' && first_lookahead <= '9') A digit-leading continuation line fails both gates, falls through to the LINE_ENDING branch just below them, and LINE_ENDING terminates the paragraph. The asymmetry with '*' in the very same condition is the tell. For '*' the scanner peeks first — first_starts_with_star_block / second_starts_with_star_block (~2690-2708, ~2840-2862) measure the delimiter run and require trailing whitespace or EOL, so the soft break is blocked only when a list marker or thematic break really forms. The digit branch has no equivalent peek; it is a blanket exclusion of the character class. ('-' and '+' are blanket-excluded too, but harmlessly: a '-'-leading continuation line genuinely can open a list.) Note that parse_ordered_list_marker (~line 1195) is already correct and already implements the CommonMark interruption rule — it requires digits followed by '.' or ')', caps at 9 digits, and sets dont_interrupt for anything but a leading '1'. It just never gets consulted, because the paragraph has already been ended by the time it would matter. SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION. Mirror the star handling: add a first_starts_with_ordered_marker / second_starts_with_ordered_marker peek that consumes the digit run (bailing past 9 digits), then requires '.' or ')' followed by a space or EOL, and — to match parse_ordered_list_marker's own dont_interrupt rule — only counts as paragraph-interrupting when the run is a single '1'. Gate the digit exclusion on that flag instead of on the raw character class. Everything else keeps working, since the marker path downstream is unchanged. Worth settling in the same pass: section D of the repro is a genuine '1. apples' interrupting a paragraph after 'Buy these:'. q2 opens a real

    ; Quarto 1 keeps one paragraph, because Pandoc's markdown reader forbids list interruption entirely while CommonMark permits it for '1.'. Defensible either way, but the two behaviors come from the same rule and a fix here will touch it. REAL-WORLD HIT (Posit Connect docs, 8+ pages). Sentences split mid-clause wherever a version number, port, timeout or RFC number happened to land at the start of a wrapped line: admin/licensing ('...to make license leases last' / '30 minutes you would use the following syntax', and again for lease renewal), admin/nodejs (twice, on Node version numbers), admin/process-management ('e.g. Red Hat Enterprise Linux' / '7)'), admin/appendix/advanced-ldap ('greater than' / '1000,'), admin/appendix/cli (RFC-3339 timestamp formats), user/troubleshooting (Python version numbers). admin/database/postgres hit the fatal variant inside a callout body; the page only builds today because the porting session hand-escaped the number as '\3986', which then renders as a visible backslash — it has since been rewrapped instead. REPRO. /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/digit-line-splits-paragraph/ — run 'q2 render' there and compare with 'quarto render'. index.qmd has sections A (digits), B (digits + punctuation), C (word-leading control) and D (a real ordered list); link-across-lines.qmd is the fatal variant and is the file that errors. README.md carries expected vs actual output and the character-class evidence above. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-mtg8ts05. Observed with q2 0.16.0 and re-verified failing on 0.17.0 / origin/main @ 001cb6a5, where nothing has touched the soft-break gates.

c-ilyz8vr9.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ilyz8vr9.text:
Investigated at fc2895b2 (pre-flight `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` clean). Plan skeleton + committed repro fixtures: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-digit-line-splits-paragraph.md (commit 813ad059). Verdict: ready to design, pending 4 questions in the plan.

Root cause confirmed exactly as filed — scanner.c gates at 2750 and 2889-2890. Four things the investigation added:

1. THE REPO ALREADY CARRIES A HAND-ESCAPED WORKAROUND FOR THIS BUG. test/corpus/new-spec.txt:2039 is CommonMark Example 284 with the input rewritten from '14.' to '\14.' and the title "qmd: start your soft breaks with \1, i'm sorry." A prior session hit this, couldn't fix it, and encoded the workaround into the conformance suite — the same escape hatch the connect-docs porting session independently invented ('\3986'). Fed the real spec input, q2 doesn't merely split the paragraph, it invents <ol start="14">. Restoring that test to unescaped spec input is the natural acceptance criterion.

2. The "worth settling in the same pass" item (section D, '1.' interrupting) needs no new decision. q2 already matches CommonMark and diverges from pandoc-markdown on '-', '1.' AND '1)'. Adopting Q1's never-interrupt rule would mean changing '-' too — a separate, larger call. The proposed fix lands all six interruption-matrix rows on CommonMark.

3. The fix repairs '2. apples' for free. Today it opens a spurious <ol start="2"> — wrong under BOTH specs — because the blanket exclusion closes the paragraph before parse_ordered_list_marker runs, making its correct dont_interrupt logic dead code on this path. Worth calling out in the eventual commit as a behavior change beyond the reported symptom.

4. The '-' and '+' exclusions are NOT harmless, contra the description. "Temperature dropped to" / "-5 degrees overnight." splits identically, as does "+5 percent". Same bug, different character class, same fix shape. Open question in the plan is whether to fold them into this strand.

And ':' does something worse than any of the above — it silently DELETES the colon. "Defined at" / ":host scope." parses to [Str "at", SoftBreak, Str "host"]; the character is gone with no diagnostic. Since one paragraph survives, it is being consumed beyond the gate (likely the ':::' fenced-div or definition-list path), so the gate fix will not necessarily cover it. Filed as bd-cxiopjw7 (discovered-from this strand).

Blast radius on existing tests is small: scanning all 50 corpus files for a digit-leading line preceded by a text line yields only Example 285 (must stay interrupting) and a display-math case in issues.txt. Main risk is downstream snapshot churn, since this changes block structure. Full `cargo xtask verify` (not --skip-hub-build) required — the grammar feeds the WASM parser.

c-kwys52a9.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-kwys52a9.text:
Implemented on branch braid/bd-digit-line-splits-paragraph-w6tod0gh-continuation-line-starting-digit, commit 92737cdd. Plan updated with the full implementation record. NOT pushed — awaiting review. WHAT LANDED. scanner.c only; no grammar change, so parser.c is untouched and there are no generated diffs. Two peek helpers mirroring the existing '*' peek: peek_dash_plus_opens_block, and peek_ordered_marker returning {well_formed, may_interrupt} with a bail past 9 digits. THE SUBTLE PART (two failed attempts, both recorded in code comments so nobody retries them): The two gates need DIFFERENT answers from the same peek. Gate 1 runs before match_line, so it cannot distinguish a sibling list item from a paragraph continuation and has no all_will_be_matched guard — it may only ask well_formed. Gate 2 runs after match_line, where all_will_be_matched proves the line belongs to the open blocks, and is the only place the CommonMark interruption rule applies. Attempt 1 applied the "only a bare 1 interrupts" rule in both gates. That broke six existing tests — issues.txt #72, list.txt 4/15/16, and CommonMark Examples 261/282 — all sibling list items like "1. a / 2. b", where gate 1 swallowed '2.' into item 1's paragraph. Attempt 2 consulted valid_symbols[LIST_MARKER_*] the way parse_ordered_list_marker does. That fails because at line-ending scan time the parser is asking for LINE_ENDING / SOFT_LINE_ENDING, so the marker symbols are not in the valid set and read false for every marker. It broke '1.' interruption (Example 285 and two new tests). Also: the mark_end guard after gate 2 was keyed on the character (!= '`' && != '*'). With three more peeking branches that proxy no longer holds, so it is now an explicit second_peeked boolean — otherwise a peeked run gets swallowed into the SOFT_LINE_ENDING token range. A THIRD ESCAPED WORKAROUND, found during implementation. Beyond new-spec.txt Example 284, block_quote.txt test 4 carried '> 2 / \1' with the title "softbreaks ignore block structure; but don't start continuation line with 1" — a lazy-continuation case. Restored to '> 2 / 1'. All three escaped inputs (284, block_quote 4, and 284's expected tree) failed before the fix and pass after. BEHAVIOR CHANGES BEYOND THE REPORTED SYMPTOM, batched per the user's instruction that such changes are better learned once: - '2.' / '14.' after a paragraph no longer open a spurious
    (was wrong under BOTH specs). - '-5 degrees', '+5 percent', '-- em dash' stay in the paragraph. RESULTS. tree-sitter test 572/572 (12 confirmed failing first, per TDD). cargo nextest run --workspace: 11626 passed, 197 skipped. cargo xtask verify full including the WASM leg: green. ZERO snapshot files changed — the churn flagged as the main risk did not materialize. END-TO-END. cargo run --bin q2 -- render doc.qmd, HTML inspected: the digit continuation is one

    , the link that previously failed with Q-2-1 renders intact, a real ordered list still works. pampa -t native now matches pandoc -f commonmark -t native EXACTLY on the committed interrupt.qmd (all six matrix rows) and dashplus.qmd — including Str "+5", confirming the two pandoc_str CST nodes for '+5' (pre-existing '+' tokenization, present mid-line too) merge into one Str at AST level. OUT OF SCOPE, left alone as agreed: the ':host' colon-dropping bug (bd-cxiopjw7) still reproduces. INCIDENTAL, NOT COMMITTED: running the WASM build refreshed crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/Cargo.lock from 0.16.0 to 0.17.0 version strings — pre-existing staleness after the 0.17.0 bump, unrelated to this fix. Reverted to keep the commit focused; worth a separate cleanup. npm install also rewrote package-lock.json peer-dependency metadata; also reverted.

title: Fenced div with no whitespace after the colons is silently dropped (and with a closing fence becomes a cascading uncoded parse error)
description:
A fenced div whose colons are not followed by whitespace is not parsed as a div. Quarto 1 and Pandoc both accept the tight form. What q2 does next depends only on whether a closing fence is present, and both outcomes are bad.

WITHOUT a closing fence, q2 renders CLEAN, exit 0, ZERO diagnostics — and emits no div at all. Given ':::{.myclass}' followed by body text, 'myclass' is absent from the output entirely and the body survives as bare prose. The opening line is consumed: it does not appear as text, which it would if the parser had given up and treated it as a paragraph. It is consumed, and then the div and its whole attribute block are discarded silently. A callout becomes plain prose with no wrapper, no classes, and no warning. This is the serious half — silent content loss is worse than a fatal error, because an error at least tells the author the page is wrong.

WITH a closing fence, it surfaces as an uncoded 'Error: Parse error … unexpected character or token here' reported at the CLOSING ':::' rather than at the opening line that actually differs, so following the error leads to the wrong place in the source. It also cascades: the committed repro produces 3 errors from one cause, the later ones landing inside a json code fence on '{' characters. Those are not code-block bugs — the control file has the same fence after a spaced div and parses cleanly. In the Positron port this cascade produced errors pointing at JSON and JavaScript inside code fences, which reads like 'q2 parses markdown inside code blocks' and is not that at all.

IT IS NOT ABOUT THE ATTRIBUTE BLOCK. A bare info string with no braces fails identically, so the requirement is whitespace after the colons regardless of what follows:
  :::{.foo}    q2: 1 error              Q1: <div class="foo">
  :::foo       q2: 1 error              Q1: <div class="foo">
  ::: {.foo}   q2: <div class="foo">    Q1: same
  ::: foo      q2: <div class="foo">    Q1: same
Quarto 1 (99.9.9) accepts all four.

AND q2 ALREADY DOES THIS CORRECTLY FOR CODE FENCES, which is the strongest single piece of evidence here. The same lexical job — fence marker, optional whitespace, then either an attribute block or a bare word — on a code fence in the same grammar file: three-backtick forms with an attribute block and no space, with an attribute block and a space, and with a bare word and no space are ALL accepted and all emit <pre class="foo">. So 'no space after the marker' is not intrinsically hard for this parser; it is solved a few hundred lines away in the same file. There appears to be no design reason for divs to differ.

WHERE THE CAUSE IS NOT, recorded so it is not re-derived. The grammar: pandoc_div (crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js:975-983) declares optional($._whitespace) between $._fenced_div_start and the info-string-or-attribute choice — the tight form appears permitted. The scanner: crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c:644-652 consumes spaces and tabs after the colons and then decides FENCED_DIV_END vs FENCED_DIV_START purely on whether the next character is a newline, logic that is whitespace-count-independent and behaves the same with zero spaces. Both appear to permit the tight form, so the failure is downstream of both. Where exactly has NOT been traced and no mechanism claim is made.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION. The plausible reading is that choice(alias($._commonmark_naked_value, $.info_string), alias($._pandoc_attr_specifier, $.attribute_specifier)) at grammar.js:978 resolves differently when no whitespace precedes it, which would explain both the lost attributes and the desynchronised closer — that is a hypothesis to check first, not a spec. Whatever the mechanism, the acceptance criteria are: all four spellings above produce <div class="foo">; the silent-drop path stops existing; and if any input is still to be rejected it must be rejected with a coded diagnostic pointing at the OPENING line, not the closer. The code-fence path is the reference implementation to compare against.

DO NOT FOLD THIS TOGETHER WITH bd-shortcode-no-space-gspu6l5s. The two look like the same bug and are not. There _shortcode_sep (grammar.js:650) is a choice with NO empty alternative, so the separator is mandatory by construction and rejecting the tight shortcode form is deliberate — that strand asks only for a better diagnostic and explicitly must not loosen the grammar. Here the grammar says optional and content is being lost silently. Different defects, different fixes.

Real-world hit in the Positron docs: 7 of the 19 pages that failed to render on the first full pass — guide-r.qmd, guide-r-debugging.qmd, guide-r-air.qmd, extensions.qmd, extension-development.qmd, quarto.qmd, data-explorer-summary-panel.qmd. They render today only because the source was migrated by hand, so the cost now falls on other Quarto 1 projects during migration.

Minimal repro: /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/div-attr-no-space/ — run 'sh check.sh' there (it takes an optional path to a q2 binary, defaulting to ~/.local/bin/q2). Five fixtures: repro.qmd (tight opener plus closer, 3 errors), control.qmd (spaced, renders the callout), infostring.qmd (bare ':::foo', 1 error, no braces involved), silent.qmd (tight opener, no closer — clean exit 0 and NO BLOCK EMITTED), codefence.qmd (the same shape on a code fence, all three variants accepted).

Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-div-attr-no-space-itqfay4p. Observed with q2 0.28.0 (official release build); re-checked against q2 HEAD 103af4445, where neither grammar.js nor scanner.c has changed since v0.28.0 and pandoc_div still declares optional($._whitespace).
close_reason: Shipped in q2 0.29.0. Verified downstream by re-running llms-info/repros/div-attr-no-space/check.sh: all five fixtures render clean and emit their block, including :::{.callout-note} with a closer (was 3 errors), :::foo (was 1 error) and the silent-loss case :::{.myclass} with no closer (was clean-exit with the block missing).

c-c0zht23e.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-c0zht23e.text:
ROOT CAUSE (traced, not hypothesised). Not the grammar and not parse_fenced_div_marker — both were correctly cleared in the strand. `tree-sitter parse` shows :::{.foo} parsing to a clean pandoc_div when it is the FIRST thing in the document, and failing only when a paragraph or metadata block precedes it. That narrowed it to the soft-line-break path in scanner.c's scan().

The `:::`-peek at scanner.c:2858 (added for issue #206, pipe-table termination) walks the whole colon run with advance() and never restores the lexer. The two SOFT_LINE_ENDING gates below it then read `lexer->lookahead` — which by then is the character AFTER the colons. For `::: {.foo}` that is a space, so `first_lookahead > ' '` fails and the gate correctly declines, falling through to LINE_ENDING (whose token range is still at post-newline, so the colons survive for the next scan). For `:::{.foo}` it is `{`: every gate test passes, `first_peeked` is false, so the gate's `lexer->mark_end(lexer)` fires at the CURRENT position — past the colons. The debug trace shows it exactly: `lexed_lookahead sym:_soft_line_ending, size:4` for a token that should be size 1. The `:::` is inside the soft-break token, so the grammar never sees a div opener, only a stray attribute_specifier mid-paragraph.

The hypothesis named in the strand (info_string vs attribute_specifier choice at grammar.js:978) is DISCARDED — that choice resolves fine; the tokens never reach it.

SECOND BUG, same cause: the swallow also ate colon runs that open nothing. `:hello` as a paragraph continuation rendered as `hello`, `::world` as `world` (verified against the 0.28.0 release binary). Same silent-content-loss class, wider blast radius than divs.

FIX (committed on braid/bd-div-attr-no-space-ne0fudkw-div-attr-no-space, 5c815d158, NOT pushed). The peek records whether it consumed a colon run and whether that run opens a block (>=3 colons = fenced div whatever follows; 1 colon + whitespace = caption start; anything else = ordinary text). Both gates test that flag instead of comparing the corrupted lookahead against ':', and take the PEEKED emission path so mark_end cannot absorb the run. The fenced-div test also loses its "followed by whitespace" requirement.

VERIFIED. check.sh in the committed repro: all five fixtures clean, repro/control/infostring/silent all emit their div (was 3 errors / clean / 1 error / NO BLOCK EMITTED). Also checked by hand: nested tight divs, tight div in a blockquote, tight div in a list item, tight div immediately after a pipe-table row. tree-sitter test 613/613. cargo nextest run --workspace 13490 passed / 0 failed (baseline on main lists 13483; delta is exactly the 7 tests added). clippy -D warnings clean, cargo xtask lint clean, cargo xtask verify (incl. WASM + hub-client) all steps passed.

OUT OF SCOPE, unchanged, pre-existing: a genuinely malformed attribute block (`:::{.foo` with no closing brace) still produces an uncoded "unexpected character or token here" pointing at the line after the opener. That is identical for `::: {.foo` and so is not a whitespace divergence — worth its own strand if we want it coded.

Did not touch the shortcode path (bd-shortcode-no-space-gspu6l5s).

c-z5h5zbal.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-z5h5zbal.text:
Dispatched to agent fenced-div-no-spaces on workspace-7 (branch braid/bd-div-attr-no-space-ne0fudkw-div-attr-no-space, created fresh from main at 103af4445). Origin strand br-div-attr-no-space-itqfay4p in the Positron-docs porting skein now carries external_ref q2:bd-div-attr-no-space-ne0fudkw.

The agent was pointed at codefence.qmd as the reference implementation — the code-fence path in the same grammar accepts all three shapes this one rejects — and told the grammar.js:978 choice-resolution reading is a hypothesis to verify or discard, not a diagnosis. It was also warned not to fold this with bd-shortcode-no-space-gspu6l5s (in progress on workspace-6), since the correct fixes are opposite: that one must not loosen its grammar, this one must.

title: Sidebar auto: expansion is one level deep; Q1 nests arbitrarily
description:
When a sidebar 'auto:' spec (or the equivalent 'contents: <dir>' shorthand) matches documents nested more than one directory deep, q2 emits them as flat links inside the top directory's section. Q1 builds an arbitrarily deep tree of nested sections.

Example: with docs/top.qmd and docs/deep/nested.qmd, 'auto: docs' yields a single 'Docs' section whose children are two flat links — one of them labelled from docs/deep/nested.qmd — rather than a 'Docs' section containing a nested 'Deep' sub-section.

Cause: group_with_subdirs (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/sidebar_auto.rs) partitions candidates by their FIRST path component only, and section_for_dir builds its children with link_entry, never recursing. Q1's nodesToEntries (external-sources/quarto-cli/src/project/types/website/website-sidebar-auto.ts) recurses over the full split path.

This predates bd-sidebar-contents-dir-shorthand-z7arvhx8 — that fix routes bare directories through the same group_with_subdirs machinery, so it inherits the depth limit rather than introducing it. Recorded there as a deliberate known limitation and pinned by the test auto_bare_directory_still_matches_nested_documents.

Fix would make section_for_dir recursive (build a sub-section per nested directory, using that directory's index.qmd for title/href as the one-level case already does). Priority 3: only bites projects whose auto-generated sidebar directories have sub-directories. Not needed for the Posit Connect docs port, which motivated the parent strand.

title: Ship Bootstrap Icons font + CSS with Quarto 2 HTML output
description: Quarto 2 HTML renders Bootstrap-icon markup (``) for navbar tools and footer nav items, but the Bootstrap Icons package (font file + icon CSS that maps class names to glyphs) is not shipped, so the icons render as empty boxes. Quarto 1 handles this via a separate bootstrap-icons dependency. Scope: vendor vs CDN decision (prefer vendor, to match SCSS strategy); where the font file lives in artifact storage; template link (``); interaction with the planned JS-deps mechanism (bd-ulgr). Companion to bd-ulgr (Bootstrap JS). Both issues concern static Bootstrap-ecosystem resources that Q2 needs to ship to match Q1 UX; worth designing them together. Surfaced during bd-imiw visual testing — navbar/footer DOM is correct, icons are invisible.

title: Expose the embedded docs as q2 mcp tools (search/fetch)
description: 'q2 docs llms' (bd-hwop1zii) makes the documentation available to any agent that can run a shell command. Agents driving q2 through the MCP server (q2 mcp) would benefit from the same corpus as tools — e.g. docs_search(query) over titles//content and docs_fetch(href) returning one page — so the docs are reachable without shelling out. Shares the embedded tree; no new artifact.

title: Pass-1 head pipeline omits IncludeResolveStage: profile.includes never populated for cache invalidation?
description: Found while investigating bd-listing-default-no-derived-desc-m0wrr8ty: orchestrator.rs::pass1_profile_single_file_live hand-lists its pre-checkpoint stages and has drifted from pipeline.rs build_transform_pipeline — ListingItemInfoStage is missing (that strand) and IncludeResolveStage is too. IncludeResolveStage writes profile.includes for bd-r82e cache invalidation. Verify whether Pass-1 profiles actually lack includes entries and whether that breaks incremental rebuild invalidation; consider a shared head_stages() builder.

title: Switch linux release targets to static musl (rusty_v8 blocker removed)
description: The release workflow builds linux on *-unknown-linux-gnu (ubuntu-22.04, glibc 2.35 floor) because rusty_v8 had no musl prebuilts. rusty_v8/deno_core have since been removed from q2 (bd-3e3sam51), so static musl is now viable: one artifact per arch covering every distro incl. Alpine, no glibc floor. Remaining consideration is openssl/aws-lc (vendorable / musl-buildable). Work: flip the linux matrix targets in .github/workflows/release.yml to x86_64/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl, restore musl-tools install, confirm vendored-openssl + aws-lc build static, drop the glibc-floor note from release notes. Discovered cutting v0.1.1 (bd-yomgkxoc).
close_reason:
Merged as PR #428 (https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/428), 7 commits, 8/8 CI checks green. Linux release legs now build x86_64/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl on ubuntu-latest/ubuntu-24.04-arm: one static artifact per arch, no glibc floor, Alpine works with no gcompat shim. No gnu artifact ships (D2 — install.sh --from-source covers anyone needing a dynamic build); install.sh and bootstrap_sh.rs needed ZERO changes because detect_platform is os x arch only.

Validated before touching release.yml by a throwaway branch-only spike workflow (D1, deleted in Phase 5, recoverable at fe016a4b): run 30375857883, BOTH ARCHES GREEN FIRST TRY, every step. aws-lc-sys — the one risk static inspection could not settle, flagged 'historically finicky' by the 2026-06 S2 spike — is a non-issue at v0.40.0: ~17s/~16s per leg, no bindgen, no libclang, nothing beyond musl-tools. None of the fallback ladder (CC=musl-gcc, cmake, promoting bd-r7s13dfb to prerequisite) was needed. Both binaries rendered a document inside alpine:latest 3.24.1 (musl libc, no glibc), and styles.css came out byte-identical at 318,718 bytes on the CI runner, in Alpine, and on local macOS arm64 — so grass/SCSS and the HTML writer emit identical bytes across two libcs and two OSes.

Gotchas recorded in release-runbook.md: musl-tools is the only extra package; file(1) says 'static-pie linked' on x86_64 but 'statically linked' on aarch64, so any staticness check must accept BOTH spellings; ldd exits non-zero on a static binary so it cannot be a bare assertion. Also added a ONE-TIME post-publish check for the next version cut (run the published artifact under alpine:latest), since CI only proves it runs on the runner.

Deliberately unchanged: keyring platform lists stay libc-plural (the addon matches the user's NODE, not how q2 was linked), now with a comment so a future cleanup does not 'fix' it and silently break q2 mcp on Alpine.

Prose: release.yml header/matrix/release-notes table, release-runbook.md, and D4 of the 2026-06-12 release plan marked SUPERSEDED. Self-review also caught two release.yml signing comments whose stated premise ('jammy has no minisign apt package') this branch invalidated.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-28-linux-release-static-musl.md. Follow-ups: bd-r7s13dfb (unify on rustls, would delete vendored-openssl entirely), bd-cpyq99ps (pre-existing preview-renderer flake found during pre-push verify).

c-0gbn8jc0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-0gbn8jc0.text: Investigated (2026-07-28). Plan skeleton: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-28-linux-release-static-musl.md. Verdict: ready to design. Findings: (1) bd-h7s7bsbk is an open DUPLICATE of this strand (same body, same discovered-from parent, filed 16h earlier) — needs reconciliation. (2) aws-lc-sys 0.40.0 ships pregenerated bindings for BOTH musl targets (src/{x86_64,aarch64}_unknown_linux_musl_crypto.rs) and libc-agnostic cc_builder configs (builder/cc_builder/linux_{x86_64,aarch64}.rs) — the 'historically finicky' risk from the S2 spike looks resolved on static inspection. (3) openssl enters solely via our samod fork hard-wiring tungstenite/native-tls; the existing target-agnostic 'vendored-openssl' feature carries over unchanged. (4) install.sh detect_platform is os x arch only (no libc sniff), so a musl-only switch needs ZERO installer or bootstrap_sh.rs changes; README/docs never mention the glibc floor, so prose is confined to release.yml + release-runbook.md. (5) No dlopen/libloading and no hand-set thread stacks anywhere in crates/ — the classic musl traps don't apply; the residual runtime risk is musl mallocng perf on q2's allocation-heavy parsing. (6) release.yml cannot dry-run as-is (repo-gated, requires a tag == Cargo.toml version, hard-fails on empty bundled secrets, publishes on success) — plan proposes a throwaway branch-triggered spike workflow, which is independently what bd-h7s7bsbk recommended. 6 open design questions for Carlos in the plan.

title: A `$` in prose that is not valid inline math is a fatal parse error (Pandoc renders it literally), and Q-2-23 fires only for a trailing bare `$`
description:
A dollar sign in prose that does not form valid inline math is a fatal parse error; the whole page is lost. Pandoc and Quarto 1 render it as a literal `$`. Two separable problems, found together.

## A. Parity: no literal-text fallback

  "priced at $20/month for individual users."   q2 FATAL, Q1 renders
  "cost $20 and $30 depending on the plan."     q2 FATAL, Q1 renders
  "$x + 1$ is a formula."                       both render
  "costs \$20 per seat."                        both render
  no dollar at all                              both render

The last three are controls: real inline math works and \$ works, so the defect is specifically the FALLBACK path. Pandoc opens math at `$` only if it can also find a closing `$` not preceded by whitespace in the same block; failing that it emits a literal dollar. q2 has no such fallback.

The second row matters: this is NOT only about an *unmatched* $. In "$20 and $30" there are two dollars, but the candidate closer is preceded by a space, so under Pandoc's rule neither forms math and both are literal. q2 still dies.

## B. Diagnostic: Q-2-23 exists but fires only for a trailing bare `$`

Q-2-23 "Unclosed Inline Math" is already defined (crates/quarto-error-catalog/error_catalog.json:324, "I reached the end of the block before finding a closing '$' for the inline math."), with a docs URL and a qmd-syntax-helper conversion rule at crates/qmd-syntax-helper/src/conversions/q_2_23.rs. Filed as k-357 under epic k-345, closed 2025-11-14.

Measured on 0.27.0:

  $                 -> Q-2-23
  x $               -> Q-2-23
  $a                -> uncoded Parse error
  This is $x + y    -> uncoded Parse error
  $20               -> uncoded Parse error

Any content after the opening `$` — the realistic case — falls through to the generic branch at crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs:243-249:

    .unwrap_or(
        // Fallback for errors not in the table
        DiagnosticMessageBuilder::error("Parse error")
            .with_location(source_info)
            .problem("unexpected character or token here")

Note row 4: "This is $x + y" is the catalog's OWN documented example, quoted verbatim in the q_2_23.rs header comment, and it does not produce Q-2-23.

Caret placement is bad independently of the code: on a 315-character line with the `$` at column 162, the error reports column 316 — one past end of line, ~150 characters downstream of the offending character.

## Suggested fix direction

For B: the corpus entry crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/Q-2-23.json has a single case whose content is "$\n" — a bare dollar at end of block. That is why only that shape resolves to a code and everything else falls through the table lookup. Adding cases for an opening `$` followed by block content (and regenerating the table) should widen it. Precedent: Q-2-41 for literal braces had the same too-narrow shape, missing every emphasis context, and was widened in 0.27.0 via ed6b59f8c (bd-brace-hint-misses-emphasis-4fzv1n93).

For A: a routing decision, not obviously a defect. The equivalent question for braces was ruled by-design in the Connect port (escape them), so `\$` may be the intended answer here too. If so, B becomes the whole ask — but see the trap below, because B cannot be shipped alone.

## TRAP: the existing auto-fix would corrupt prose

q_2_23.rs fixes Q-2-23 by APPENDING a closing `$`:

    Input:  This is $x + y
    Output: This is $x + y$

Correct for genuinely unclosed math. Wrong for every currency case: applied to "priced at $20/month for individual users." it appends a `$` and turns a sentence into math. The correct fix there is \$20. So widening Q-2-23 without teaching the conversion rule to distinguish currency-like from math-like content would corrupt documents. There is precedent for a qmd-syntax-helper rule damaging prose (the q-2-11 curly-quote rule).

## Real-world hit

Positron website docs, release-notes/release-2026-05.qmd:59, announcing Posit AI at "$20/month". That one character loses the entire page. It is the only one of 13 release-notes pages that fails, and one of two errors that currently suppress the site's post-render hook (which writes 7 redirect stubs), so it also costs every /blog and /redirect path. Prices, currency and shell variables ($HOME, $PATH) are common in technical prose, so exposure is broad wherever a corpus has them.

## Repro

/Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/dollar-not-math-fatal/

Seven fixtures, each its own project; run `q2 render` inside each, and `quarto render --output-dir _site-q1` for the Q1 side, which renders all seven. single/ and two-dollars/ are the parity cases; math/, escaped/ and none/ are controls; q223-fires/ and q223-misses/ pin the diagnostic boundary.

Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-dollar-not-math-fatal-q32gcirl. Observed with q2 0.27.0 (official release build); origin/main == v0.27.0 == d05e96ee8 as of 2026-08-25, so nothing post-release addresses it.
close_reason: Not fixable as asked: a $ in prose is ambiguous (currency vs inline-math delimiter) and no good diagnostic is possible -- nothing in the parser, the AST or the fixer can recover the author's intent. q2 accepts the divergence from Pandoc/Q1: an unescaped $ that does not form inline math is an error, and \$ is the escape, as docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-23.qmd already prescribes. Auto-fix corruption split out as bd-vz340zg6.

c-8ej3fqjo.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-8ej3fqjo.text:
Investigated on branch braid/bd-dollar-not-math-fatal-fpnqrpil-prose-that-not-valid (worktree .worktrees/workspace-2), off main @ d05e96ee8. Plan skeleton: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-25-dollar-not-math-fatal.md; measurements: claude-notes/plans/dollar-not-math-fatal-investigation/observed-behaviour.md (+ probe-states.sh).

Verdict: ready to design. Three reframings:
(1) Part A is not $-specific -- q2 treats every unclosed inline delimiter as fatal (* -> Q-2-12, _ -> Q-2-5, [ -> Q-2-1, " -> Q-2-11, ` -> uncoded). $ is the only one that dies UNCODED, and docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-23.qmd already prescribes \$ for currency. Exposure is wider than prices: there is no literal-$ path in the grammar at all, so 'a $ b', 'a$b', 'US$' and '50$' are fatal too.
(2) Part B needs 15 content-bearing corpus cases (one per inline container), not one. All 15 (state, _close_block) pairs measured and verified absent from _autogen-table.json, so no bleed risk. PLUS a second gap the strand missed: bare $ in pipe-table cells is uncoded on a different symbol -- header (3970, _whitespace), body (4373, _whitespace).
(3) The look-ahead for part A exists but was orphaned: grammar.js:1137-1138 declares _latex_span_start/_latex_span_close, no rule references them, parse_latex_span (scanner.c:1945) is dead code. Added ab92d47fb, orphaned by the grammar unification 4ededc50c which introduced pandoc_math on bare '$' literals.

TRAP confirmed live: q_2_23.rs is not opt_in_only, so 'convert --rule all' would append a closing $ to currency prose the moment the code fires widely.

Five design questions in the plan, awaiting Gordon.

c-uxxhe05l.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-uxxhe05l.text:
Closing per Gordon (2026-08-25), with Carlos' statement about apostrophes, which applies to dollar signs unchanged:

  The problem is that:
  - CommonMark uses ambiguous characters.
  - CommonMark refuses to emit syntax errors, and so forces a disambiguation that means typos will be misinterpreted and leak into output.
  - We want to be close to CommonMark and believe we can't force people to use different characters for quotes and apostrophes.
  - We want to emit good error messages but that's impossible here.

Transposed to `$`:

1. `$` is an ambiguous character -- the currency symbol and the inline-math delimiter, exactly as `'` is the apostrophe and the single quote.
2. Pandoc refuses to error, so it disambiguates silently: math opens at `$` only if a closing `$` not preceded by whitespace exists in the block. A dropped closing `$` -- a real typo in real math -- is therefore reinterpreted and leaks into the output as literal text, with the author never told.
3. We want to stay close to CommonMark/Pandoc, and we cannot ask people to write currency with some other character. `$20` and `$HOME` are how technical prose is written.
4. We want a good error message, and here it is impossible -- not hard, impossible. Measured:
   - The parser carries no signal: `$20`, `$x + y`, `$abc` and the full Positron sentence all fail in the SAME LR state (3157). The state follows the enclosing inline container, never the content.
   - The AST-shape technique that makes bracket_analysis.rs safe is unavailable: it works because `[...]` parses, whereas an unmatched `$` means there is no AST. The parser failed precisely because it could not decide.
   - The apostrophe precedent does not transfer: q2 disambiguated `'` by splitting the CODE (Q-2-10 vs Q-2-7), which works only because the grammar already distinguishes the two apostrophe shapes. Nothing comparable exists for `$`.
   - So any fix is a guess, and guessing wrong corrupts prose -- demonstrated live at HEAD.

Consequence q2 accepts deliberately: an unescaped `$` that does not form inline math is an error, and `\$` is the escape. Consistent with the whole delimiter family (`*` Q-2-12, `_` Q-2-5, `[` Q-2-1, `"` Q-2-11 all error when unclosed) and already what docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-23.qmd prescribes. A deliberate divergence from Pandoc/Q1, not an oversight.

WHAT CLOSING GIVES UP, so it can be picked up later: the part-B corpus widening was measured and is low-risk -- 15 unclaimed (state, _close_block) pairs, none colliding with an existing entry -- and would turn today's uncoded "Parse error / unexpected character or token here" into a coded Q-2-23. That stays undone; the realistic case still reports an uncoded error with the caret at end-of-line. Every measurement needed is in the investigation notes, and the state numbers stay valid for as long as the grammar does not change.

FILED SEPARATELY: bd-vz340zg6 (discovered-from) -- the q-2-23 auto-fix corrupts currency prose today. `The upgrade costs 50$` becomes `50$$`, which still does not parse, and the rule is not opt_in_only so `convert --rule all` does it unasked. Tractable; does not close with this strand.

Record on branch braid/bd-dollar-not-math-fatal-fpnqrpil-prose-that-not-valid (worktree .worktrees/workspace-2), commits 3f30817c2, ed63f653f, 7b25d86e3, a12465e94:
  claude-notes/plans/2026-08-25-dollar-not-math-fatal.md
  claude-notes/plans/dollar-not-math-fatal-investigation/observed-behaviour.md
  claude-notes/plans/dollar-not-math-fatal-investigation/autofix-architecture.md
  claude-notes/plans/dollar-not-math-fatal-investigation/probe-states.sh

title: Draft pages render without Q1's draft alert banner (#quarto-draft-alert)
description:
A page with 'draft: true' in its front matter renders in q2 with no visual indication that it is a draft. Quarto 1 emits a banner as the first child of the page header:
Draft
with the accompanying rule '#quarto-draft-alert { margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; padding: .3em; text-align: center; font-size: .9em }' (plus '#quarto-draft-alert i { margin-right: .3em }') in the bootstrap bundle. The banner is what tells an author previewing a site that the page they are looking at is unpublished; without it, a draft page is indistinguishable from a finished one. Root cause area: q2 parses the flag — DocumentProfile.draft is populated in crates/quarto-core/src/document_profile.rs (field at :407, read from meta at :746) — but its only two consumers are crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/sidebar_auto.rs (:195/:204/:213, filtering drafts out of auto sidebars) and crates/quarto-core/src/project/aliases.rs (:340, skipping alias redirect stubs for drafts). Nothing in the HTML chrome reads it: FULL_HTML_TEMPLATE in crates/quarto-core/src/template.rs (body opens at :194, navbar slot at :195) has no draft conditional — 'draft' does not appear in template.rs at all — and there is no '#quarto-draft-alert' rule anywhere in the sass bundle (crates/quarto-sass). Suggested fix: emit the banner from FULL_HTML_TEMPLATE at the top of , before/inside the navbar slot. Front-matter keys reach the template context through add_metadata_to_context (template.rs:898), so a '$if(draft)$' guard around the div should have the value available without new plumbing; verify that and add the two CSS rules to the theme bundle. Note Q1 places the div inside '#quarto-header', which q2's navbar does not emit (see the comment at crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/title_banner.rs:39), so the exact DOM position will differ — top-of-body is the closest equivalent. Whether the banner should also be gated on draft-mode is a follow-up: q2 has no draft-mode config yet (bd-w0o9), and in Q1 the banner appears whenever a rendered page is a draft. Real-world hit: the Posit Connect docs port has four draft pages — admin/llm-gateway/index.qmd, admin/opentelemetry/llm-gateway.qmd, admin/opentelemetry/content-telemetry.qmd, user/content-telemetry/index.qmd. All four carry the banner in the Q1 site and lose it under q2, so the ported site publishes four unmarked draft pages. Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/draft-banner-missing/ — run 'q2 render' there and grep _site/drafty.html for 'quarto-draft-alert' (absent); the committed _site-q1/drafty.html, from 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1', has it. See README.md. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-draft-banner-missing-mo42fmdn. Re-verified failing with q2 0.20.0 against q2 checkout HEAD 0dcd7e83 (v0.20.0 plus 4 commits) — no draft-banner work upstream.

c-1hxn04da.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-1hxn04da.text:
IMPLEMENTED for 'q2 render' in commit 1ce09c88. New DraftAlertTransform (Normalization) writes rendered.draft-alert-text (localized via LanguageTerms, toc_generate.rs precedence) and a quarto:status header include; FULL_HTML_TEMPLATE gates the markup on the first key, making the transform the single gate bd-w0o9 will need for draft-mode: gone.

Verified end-to-end: 'q2 render' on the committed repro emits markup BYTE-IDENTICAL to the Q1 reference, and computed styles read back in Chrome confirm the already-shipped CSS applies (margins 0, padding and icon margin .3em = 4.59px, font-size .9em = 15.3px, alert-warning colors rgb(255,243,205)/rgb(102,77,3), bootstrap-icons glyph U+F4CA) with the banner as body.firstElementChild.

ONE PREDICTION OVERTURNED: 'q2 preview' does NOT show the banner. Every step of my earlier trace was individually correct (preview calls the same render_qmd_to_html, reaches the no-custom-template arm, is_minimal_html is false) and the conclusion was still wrong -- the preview never uses the rendered HTML page; it is a React SPA reconstructing chrome slot by slot in ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/. The quarto:status meta DID appear (head includes applied imperatively by HeaderIncludesEffect), which made the partial success misleading. Split to bd-3cpv7dah with the ~20-line fix identified.

Also split: bd-4c7n9o1h (revealjs), bd-98lngao9 (docs -- there is no drafts page at all, and writing one now would document a half-shipped feature pending bd-w0o9).

Snapshots: ZERO changed, but not for free -- the first template edit put $if(...)$ and its markup on one line, adding a stray blank line to every NON-draft page and breaking two byte-identity tests (single_doc_render_unchanged_under_scope_refactor, attribution_off_html_baseline). The own-line directive idiom the navbar slot already uses restores byte-identity; worth knowing before anyone edits that template again.

Tests: 14 unit tests + 4 smoke-all fixtures (confirmed failing first), covering draft:false vs absent key as separate fixtures, localization, English fallback, label HTML-escaping, re-run idempotency, and the html/q2-preview/revealjs/q2-slides/pdf gate matrix. Full cargo xtask verify green 14/14, 11846 tests passed.

Leaving this strand open pending your call on whether it closes here (render-side complete, preview split out) or waits for bd-3cpv7dah.

c-3js79t91.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-3js79t91.text: Source pointers re-checked against q2 HEAD 0dcd7e83 (v0.20.0+4); the description was filed against 1ba0f2ec (v0.19.0) and had drifted. Corrections: DocumentProfile.draft field :395 -> :407 and the meta read :698 -> :746 in document_profile.rs (shifted by the aliases work in 7c30181d); and the draft flag now has a second consumer, project/aliases.rs:340, which skips alias redirect stubs for drafts. Unchanged and re-verified exact: template.rs :194/:195 (body open, navbar slot), title_banner.rs:39 (the #quarto-header deviation note), no '#quarto-draft-alert' rule anywhere in crates/quarto-sass, no 'draft' mention in template.rs. The repro still fails on the 0.20.0 binary: _site/drafty.html has no quarto-draft-alert, _site-q1/drafty.html does. No draft-banner work landed upstream in 1ba0f2ec..0dcd7e83.

c-9tffhwrw.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-9tffhwrw.text:
Design decisions settled (plan updated, commit d94039c6). (1) Localized string via a TRANSFORM following toc_generate.rs/appendix.rs, not inline in template.rs -- chosen for consistency over simplicity. (2) 'bi bi-pencil-square' font class, Q1-identical. (3) DO also emit meta[name=quarto:status] content=draft, even though nothing consumes it yet -- llms.txt support is coming and this is one fewer thing to patch later.

(4) PREVIEW IS FREE, traced but not yet verified end-to-end (needs the feature to exist first). The WASM client calls the same quarto-core render_qmd_to_html (lib.rs:1521); its _template_bundle param is documented 'currently unused' (lib.rs:1084) so it lands in ApplyTemplateStage's no-custom-template arm; is_minimal_html (format.rs:489) is false for normal docs, so preview selects FULL_HTML_TEMPLATE and gets the banner. Caveat: minimal mode (theme: none/pandoc) gets no banner, which is correct -- Bootstrap's alert-warning is not loaded there. Confirm in Phase 2 via the WASM rebuild chain; follow-up strand only if the trace is wrong.

(5) REVEALJS still open, and the answer changed once cost was known. Q1's exclusion IS incidental as suspected: the isHtmlSlideOutput guard arrives in 99e47b461, three commits BEFORE the banner, for the feature that EMPTIES draft docs -- breaking a deck is a good reason to guard that; the banner (5b06ea3af) inherits it for free by keying off meta[quarto:status]. No stated reason anywhere in quarto-cli.

But q2's cost is real, and this CORRECTS my earlier correction 1: 'the CSS already ships' holds for HTML only. Revealjs is a separate path end to end -- render_revealjs_document (revealjs/assemble.rs:369) is a hand-built format! scaffold that bypasses doctemplate entirely, and its bundle is quarto-revealjs.scss, which has neither #quarto-draft-alert nor Bootstrap's .alert.alert-warning. And assemble.rs:424 already documents that before-body 'has no natural anchor in the deck scaffold -- reveal.js owns everything inside .reveal -- and is deferred until a concrete consumer appears'. The banner is exactly that shape, and Q1 ships no reference output for it, so this is design work with no port to copy.

Recommendation: ship HTML here, file revealjs as a follow-up -- which then becomes the concrete consumer that motivates resolving the deferred before-body anchor question, rather than deciding it as a side effect of this strand. Awaiting user call.

c-izhcz7w3.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-izhcz7w3.text:
Investigated at HEAD 0dcd7e83; plan skeleton at claude-notes/plans/2026-08-13-draft-alert-banner.md (commit 3a2b2eb2), repro committed under claude-notes/plans/draft-alert-banner-investigation/repro/. Verdict: ready to design, and smaller than this description implies -- the work is HTML emission only.

Four corrections to the description. (1) The CSS ALREADY SHIPS: the #quarto-draft-alert rule (plus the nested 'i { margin-right: .3em }') is at resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss:2604 -- not crates/quarto-sass, where this description looked -- and reaches the emitted _site/site_libs/quarto/quarto-theme-*.css. No SCSS work needed. (2) Bootstrap Icons already ships to _site/site_libs/bootstrap/, so 'bi bi-pencil-square' renders. (3) The banner text is LOCALIZED in Q1 (format-html.ts:911 uses format.language.draft) and q2 already has 'draft: "Draft"' at resources/language/_language.yml:130, fully translated (Borrador/Brouillon/Rascunho/...). This description does not mention localization; hardcoding "Draft" would repeat the section-title-* miss bd-v9zs83zj had to fix. (4) The $if(draft)$ plumbing WORKS -- verified, not assumed: a temporary probe div at top of body in FULL_HTML_TEMPLATE appeared in drafty.html and not index.html, landing just above #quarto-content (the closest equivalent to Q1's inside-#quarto-header position). Probe reverted.

Also: Q1 does not read 'draft' at the HTML stage. normalize/draft.lua emits meta[name=quarto:status] (content 'draft', or 'draft-remove' when draft-mode: gone, which blanks the page and suppresses the banner); format-html.ts:902 keys off that. Since q2 has no draft-mode at all, 'banner whenever draft: true' is exactly Q1-correct today -- so bd-w0o9 does NOT block this, it only needs to add a suppression condition later.

Five open design questions for the user, the load-bearing one being where the localized string is computed: inline in template.rs (LanguageTerms::from_meta needs only meta, which add_metadata_to_context already has) vs a small transform following the toc_generate.rs/appendix.rs precedent. Others: bi font class vs inline SVG; whether to also emit meta[quarto:status]; whether q2 preview's WASM path shares FULL_HTML_TEMPLATE (unverified); HTML-only/not-slides scope.

title: hub-client: link-project-set on an already-established browser leaves an empty auto-created root beside the linked set
description: Since bd-4h1hv60p the personal root collection is created silently on first run. A user who lands on the empty home and *then* opens another browser's link-project-set URL gets the linked set as a secondary collection while the empty auto-created 'My projects' stays the root (same as any already-set-up browser today; the boot-URL case is handled). Consider replacing the root when it is empty and not shared, or offering 'make this my main list' in the link handler. title: Heading identifiers are not disambiguated across include boundaries, so a repeated include collides
description:
A fragment that carries a heading, included more than once in a page, produces that heading's identifier verbatim every time.

WHAT HAPPENS

shared.qmd holds one heading:

  #### Create the integration

and index.qmd includes it once per provider:

  ## Provider A
  {{< include shared.qmd >}}
  ## Provider B
  {{< include shared.qmd >}}
  ## Provider C
  {{< include shared.qmd >}}

Quarto 1 runs its identifier counter over the whole assembled document and emits create-the-integration, create-the-integration-1, create-the-integration-2. q2 0.23.0 emits:

  <section id="create-the-integration" class="section level4">
  <section id="create-the-integration" class="section level4">
  <section id="create-the-integration" class="section level4">

Two consequences, both reader-visible:

1. Invalid HTML — three elements share one id.
2. Two of the three TOC entries are dead. The TOC lists the heading three times and every entry carries data-scroll-target="#create-the-integration", so clicking the second or third jumps the reader to the first provider's section.

No diagnostic is emitted; the render is clean and exits 0.

It is specifically the include boundary. Write the three repeated headings inline in one file and q2 disambiguates correctly, matching Q1 — so this is not a gap in the dedup logic, it is a gap in its scope.

ROOT CAUSE

The dedup registry is a local in the reader's postprocess pass. crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:903 creates

  let mut seen_ids: HashMap<String, usize> = HashMap::new();

and the with_header closure at :931 consults it when (and only when) the heading has no author-written id: auto_generated_id derives the slug at :943 and :946-:951 appends -1, -2 on collision. That map lives and dies with one parse.

IncludeExpansionStage (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/include_expansion.rs) resolves {{< include >}} by parsing the included file STANDALONE and splicing its blocks in — its own module header says so. Each standalone parse gets a fresh seen_ids, so the counter restarts at every include and the assembled document is never looked at as a whole.

Quarto 1 does not have the problem because its include is a textual splice performed before pandoc parses, so pandoc's uniqueIdent pass sees one document.

This is the same "auto id is decided too early and too locally" shape as bd-2wv8431v (heading ids do not reflect shortcode expansion, because the id is derived in the reader's postprocess before shortcodes expand). Worth fixing together: both go away if auto-id assignment moves out of the per-parse pass.

SUGGESTED FIX

Do not thread a shared seen_ids through IncludeExpansionStage into each standalone parse. That would make a parse result depend on where it is spliced, so the same fragment would parse differently in two documents and the results would stop being independently cacheable.

Better: defer auto-id assignment to a document-level pass that runs on the assembled AST, after include expansion (and, for bd-2wv8431v, after shortcode expansion) and before SectionizeTransform — sectionize copies the header id onto the section Div, and both the TOC collector and crossref read ids downstream, so the pass has to land before that. The parser then leaves the id empty rather than guessing, which also removes the need to distinguish an auto-generated id from an author-written one later: the postprocess already only assigns when attr.0 is empty, so "still empty at document level" is exactly the set that wants an auto id.

A duplicate-id diagnostic is worth considering alongside, for the case the author writes the same explicit {#id} twice — the fix above deliberately will not renumber those, and today nothing complains.

REAL-WORLD HIT

Posit Connect docs port: 7 duplicate heading ids on 2 pages, against 0 on 451 pages in the Quarto 1 render of the same sources.

  admin/integrations/oauth-integrations/microsoft/index.html  (4)
  admin/integrations/oauth-integrations/google/index.html     (3)

Both include oauth-integrations/include/_azure_intro.qmd — which carries "#### Create integration in Posit Connect" — once per tab of a five-tab provider tabset. The microsoft page's TOC therefore shows five identical "Create integration in Posit Connect" entries under "Connect configuration", all five pointing at the first tab. (That those headings reach the TOC at all is a separate bug, bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7; this strand is why they collide once they are there.)

Found by a site-wide duplicate-heading-id scan over both rendered trees.

REPRO

/Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/duplicate-heading-ids/

Run `q2 render` there and compare _site/index.html against the committed Q1 render in _site-q1/ (regenerate with `quarto render --output-dir _site-q1`). Expected: create-the-integration, -1, -2. Actual at 0.23.0: three identical ids and three TOC links to the first. README.md states expected vs actual and shows the inline-headings control that disambiguates correctly.

Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-duplicate-heading-ids-ye3j3gkr. Observed with q2 0.23.0; q2 origin/main at 5b6774d1 has nothing past the 0.23.0 tag touching this.

Follow-ups: bd-4qjl87ax (engine-output headings), bd-8wf5brc8 (duplicate explicit-id diagnostic). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-18-duplicate-heading-ids-includes.md

title: D7: Default HTML format ships Bootstrap-derived stylesheet
description:
## What

`q2 render`'s default HTML format ships a minimal `tables_files/styles.css` (from `crates/quarto-core/resources/styles.css`). For tables to actually look styled even with `class="caption-top table"` applied, the CSS bundle must include Bootstrap's `.table` and `.caption-top` rules.

The project already has Bootstrap SCSS sources at `resources/scss/bootstrap/`. This task wires the SCSS compilation/loading into the default HTML format so the produced HTML links a stylesheet containing those rules.

## Scope

Just enough to make a default render's tables look like Q1's tables. Custom themes, dark mode toggle, font scales etc. are out of scope.

## Tests

End-to-end test via `render_document_to_file` (per CLAUDE.md end-to-end requirement) that renders `tables.qmd` and asserts the produced HTML links a stylesheet whose contents contain `.table` selector + the expected rules (border, padding, font-weight on th).

Visual re-verification in Chrome required before closing.

## Plan

claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-table-default-rendering-parity.md (D7 section). Phase 2 work — blocks on D1-D6 only for visual verification, not for code.
close_reason: No code change needed. CompileThemeCssStage already ships the full Bootstrap 5.3.1 bundle as _files/styles.css for default renders. The original 'unstyled table' symptom was 100% markup-side — once D1/D2 added the caption-top/table class hooks and thead/th promotion, the existing CSS styled the table identically to Quarto 1. Visual verification 2026-05-20 confirms byte-identical computed styles to Q1.

title: Upstream PR: thread custom headers through automerge-repo's BrowserWebSocketClientAdapter
description:
Follow-up noted in Phase 8 (bd-mqa4j) of the hub-mcp auth epic but never filed.

Upstream `BrowserWebSocketClientAdapter` (@automerge/automerge-repo) constructs its socket as `new WebSocket(url)` and does not thread custom headers, which makes it unusable for Bearer-authenticated WS upgrades. We worked around this by forking the adapter as the Node-only `ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/NodeWebSocketClientAdapter.ts`, which mirrors the upstream wire protocol exactly but constructs `new WebSocket(url, [], { headers })` against the Node-native `ws` package (see its module doc-comment, lines 1-19).

Cost of the workaround: the adapter is a maintained copy of upstream's protocol handling — it must be kept in sync with upstream changes to the v1 wire protocol, peer handshake, and retry loop.

Note the portability caveat recorded in the file (:28-30): the `headers` option is not available on a browser `WebSocket`, so an upstream fix cannot simply add headers to the browser path. A viable upstream shape is probably a pluggable socket-factory hook rather than a headers option. Scope the PR accordingly before writing it.

Deliverable: either an accepted upstream PR (after which NodeWebSocketClientAdapter can be deleted in favour of the upstream adapter plus a factory), or a decision to keep the fork permanently, recorded in the file's doc-comment.

title: Support fnm and nvm-windows Node discovery in quarto-mcp-launcher's well-known-paths probe
description: crates/quarto-mcp-launcher/src/node.rs default_well_known() probes nvm-sh, fnm, and volta on unix but only Program Files and Volta on Windows. Two Windows-native version managers are unprobed: nvm-windows (coreybutler), which uses a flat layout %NVM_HOME%/vX.Y.Z/node.exe with no bin subdir, unlike highest_version_node's current bin/node and installation/bin/node sub-path search; and fnm on Windows, which uses a per-version layout similar to unix under %APPDATA%/fnm/node-versions/vX.Y.Z/installation/bin/node.exe. This is a fallback layer only used when PATH lookup fails, so priority is low, but it is a real gap for Windows contributors using either tool without a PATH shim.

title: Audit trace_event!(Warn) sites for user-facing conditions; -v filter never shows quarto_core warnings
description: Two findings from bd-jsvetdea. (1) Every `trace_event!(ctx, EventLevel::Warn, ..)` in the pipeline is invisible on the CLI: RenderContext defaults to NoopObserver (crates/quarto-core/src/render.rs) and the CLI installs no other observer; only `trace: true|summary` in document metadata does (metadata_merge.rs activate_trace_from_metadata). Decision (2026-09-08, with Carlos): keep trace_event! as a trace-only channel and use ctx.add_diagnostic for anything user-facing, because add_diagnostic feeds the summary counts, --warnings-as-errors, JSON output, and coalescing. Audit the 10 remaining Warn sites (after bd-jsvetdea removed the three theme fallbacks): bootstrap_js.rs / tabsets_js.rs 'failed to parse theme config, skipping' (likely unreachable now that compile-theme-css errors first — confirm and simplify), capture_splice.rs 'failed to parse capture ... skipping this capture' (user-affecting: silently drops engine output), engine_execution.rs trace serialization, compile_theme_css.rs 'failed to compute cache key', metadata_merge.rs WASM trace notice. Convert the user-affecting ones to structured diagnostics. (2) Even with TracingObserver, `quarto_util::verbose_to_filter` maps -v to `quarto=warn,q2=warn` etc.; those directives match the `quarto`/`q2` targets only, so tracing::warn! from quarto_core, pampa, etc. is filtered at every -v level. Either widen the directives (quarto_core=..., pampa=...) or set a global level with per-crate overrides. Plan context: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-08-theme-scss-compile-error-swallowed.md (design question 6).

title: q2 preview gives mermaid diagram blocks copy-button chrome that q2 render suppresses
description:
In the render pipeline, transforms/mermaid.rs runs at TransformPhase::Finalization deliberately ordered *before* CodeBlockRenderTransform, so a ```mermaid block is already a RawBlock by the time the copy-button/filename chrome would be added — the module doc calls this out explicitly.

In the q2-preview pipeline mermaid-render is on Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED (the raw CodeBlock has to reach MermaidCodeBlock.tsx), so CodeBlockRenderTransform *does* see the mermaid block. The preview AST shows it wrapped in a `code-copy-outer-scaffold` Div with the copy `<button>` RawBlock as a sibling, and the CodeBlock class list grown to ["mermaid","code-with-copy"].

Observed in the preview AST emitted by render_qmd_to_preview_ast (see the pin test pipeline::tests::render_qmd_to_preview_ast_processes_mermaid_cell_options in crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs).

Pre-existing and independent of cell options — a bare ```mermaid block with no options gets the same treatment. Whether it is actually *visible* depends on how MermaidCodeBlock.tsx and the SPA CSS handle the scaffold; worth checking in a real preview session before deciding severity. The likely fix is to make CodeBlockRenderTransform skip blocks carrying the `mermaid` class rather than relying on transform ordering, so both pipelines agree regardless of which transforms are excluded.

Related: bd-c3dtpe36 (mermaid render component for q2-preview). Discovered while investigating bd-mermaid-cell-options-9wo3crl0.

title: Q2 website JS library loading (native + hub-client incremental-stable)
description:
Q2 doesn't yet have a story for shipping JS modules with website renders. The hub-client live-preview path adds an additional constraint: JS modules must not be re-parsed/re-executed on every incremental HTML re-render (debounced renders fire on every keystroke; a Bootstrap collapse module that re-initializes per-render would lose state and likely break event handlers).

Required for: bd-f5yi-followup full Q1 sidebar rollup parity (hamburger toggle = Bootstrap collapse JS), and any future website feature that needs interactive JS (search, copy-button, etc.).

Design space:
- Where do JS bundles live in the rendered HTML? (Currently no <script> tags emitted for site libs.)
- How does hub-client's iframe lifecycle preserve module state across renders? Options: (a) load scripts in the iframe's outer wrapper that persists; (b) keep the iframe document but only swap inner-body innerHTML; (c) use a separate stable script-host iframe.
- For native render, scripts should be self-contained under site_libs/ and emitted as <script src="site_libs/..."> tags.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-01-website-sidebar-breakpoints.md (Resolved Decision 2 records the dependency chain).

Parent epic: bd-0tr6 (websites).

title: hub-client: source editor blank on project open — Monaco mount never triggers Automerge reconciliation
description: Preview loads but Monaco stays empty until refresh. Root cause: useAutomergeSync's reconciliation effect deps are [currentFile, fileContents, replayIsActive]; onEditorMount only sets the ref. If content arrives in the same React commit that creates the Monaco editor (editorRef still null — onMount fires one commit later in @monaco-editor/react), reconciliation takes the 'Monaco isn't ready' branch (setContent only) and never re-runs. Uncontrolled MonacoEditor (defaultValue) never receives later values. Fix: make editor mount a reconciliation trigger (mount-generation state in the effect deps).
close_reason: Fixed in 21142631 (PR #411, merged as 2d7a88fb): editor mount now triggers Automerge reconciliation via editorMountGen counter; two hook-level regression tests.

c-biob5y6b.text: Diagnosis confirmed and fix implemented. Root cause: useAutomergeSync reconciliation effect deps [currentFile, fileContents, replayIsActive] — editor mount was not a trigger; onEditorMount only stored the ref. @monaco-editor/react creates the editor in a passive effect but delivers onMount one commit later, so content arriving in the creation commit was reconciled into React state only (preview fine) while the uncontrolled Monaco (defaultValue) stayed empty; on a quiescent doc no dep ever changed again → blank until refresh. title: list_doc_ids_filesystem reconstructs doc ids unsoundly on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS flake)
description:
`list_doc_ids_filesystem` (crates/quarto-hub/src/admin/scan.rs:80-106) rebuilds an automerge document id by concatenating directory names from the 2-level store layout: `<2-char prefix>/<rest>/` -> `format!("{prefix}{rest}")`. Base58 doc ids are case-SENSITIVE, but macOS APFS (and Windows NTFS) are case-INSENSITIVE by default. When two doc ids in one store have 2-char prefixes that are equal case-insensitively but differ in case (e.g. `3J` and `3j`), both land in a single on-disk directory, and every id read back through that directory gets the *first-created* directory's casing. The reconstructed id is then wrong and no longer matches the real document id.

Observed as a flake in `quarto-hub::integration admin_scan_real_store::scan_real_store_finds_orphaned_capture_only` during a full-workspace `cargo nextest run --workspace` on macOS:

    left:  ["3jFfb9qiz49L2qKnBikMt9QMGEoe"]
    right: ["3JFfb9qiz49L2qKnBikMt9QMGEoe"]

Differs only at index 1 (j vs J). The test passes in isolation and passed 392/392 when quarto-hub ran alone; it is probabilistic because doc ids are randomly generated, so it needs two ids per store colliding case-insensitively on the first two chars.

Not caused by the branch that found it (bd-v8gx/bd-gdhk touched only quarto-core artifact writing; no crates/quarto-hub/ file changed). Pre-existing and platform-dependent.

Impact beyond the test: any admin scan / GC path that trusts these reconstructed ids on macOS or Windows could mis-identify a document — e.g. classify a live capture as orphaned, or fail to find one it just listed. Worth checking whether the collector can act on a mis-cased id.

Possible fixes: read the id from inside the document rather than from path components; store the id in a sidecar; or make the store layout case-safe (e.g. lowercase-with-escape, or a hash-based prefix).

c-4a6zatgo.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-4a6zatgo.text:
PLAN WRITTEN (awaiting user review, no implementation yet):
claude-notes/plans/2026-07-28-doc-id-identity-from-paths.md
Branch: braid/bd-eb2wnxkp-listdocidsfilesystem-reconstructs-doc-ids @ f3b7ff4e (off main 270d58b5)

The plan found a SECOND instance of the same class, and this one is NOT platform-gated:

Instance B — normalize_id (classify.rs:162) is 'strip automerge: prefix' only, a string normalization rather than a parse. samod's DocumentId::from_str accepts bs58check OR a legacy UUID form, while Display always emits bs58check. So a sidecar holding automerge:<uuid> normalizes to UUID text and never matches a path-derived bs58 id -> the referenced doc reads as an orphan, on ANY platform including Linux production. Reachability is unconfirmed (older JS automerge-repo clients used UUID doc ids), so confirming/ruling it out is Phase 1 of the plan — it could raise priority again.

Shared fix for A and B: compare parsed DocumentIds, not strings.
- Part A (path side): recover_doc_id(prefix, rest) tests the <=4 case variants of the 2-char level-1 component against bs58check's checksum; exactly-one-parses => recovered (with a warn), zero or multiple => hard error. Only level-1 can fold (level-2 is created fresh inside it), and the hard-fail arms guard that assumption so it breaks loudly if ever violated.
- Part B (content side): normalize_id parses into DocumentId and re-encodes canonically, unifying UUID and bs58 forms.
- Part C: thread DocumentId instead of String through LoadedDoc / live_doc_ids so the class cannot recur. Constrained by ScanManifest being a serialized format with MANIFEST_VERSION.

Rejected: case-insensitive comparison (could conflate two genuinely distinct ids — trades a false-orphan bug for a wrong-document bug); changing samod's layout (breaks existing stores + JS interop); a hub-maintained id manifest (introduces drift-from-storage as a new bug class with the same failure mode).

Five open questions are left in the plan for the user rather than decided unilaterally — notably whether an unparseable reference should abort the scan (loud, safe, but one corrupt sidecar blocks all GC) or keep the doc alive and warn (fail-safe), and whether to fix here or upstream in our samod fork given that whole-store enumeration is admittedly outside samod's Storage contract.

c-5jxjomz9.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-5jxjomz9.text:
CONFIRMED PRE-EXISTING AND REPRODUCED ON main (581e45c0), independent of any branch.

Stress-running the single test on a clean main worktree:
  cargo nextest run -p quarto-hub -E 'test(scan_real_store)'
  -> 2 failures in 60 iterations (~3%), and 1 more at iteration 80 of a second sweep.

Captured assertion on main:
  left:  ["2Kd28qzkGdDCtFGS7ZkVJk1QBTEb"]
  right: ["2kd28qzkGdDCtFGS7ZkVJk1QBTEb"]
                ^ index 1: K vs k

Compare the failure originally seen on the bd-v8gx branch:
  left:  ["3jFfb9qiz49L2qKnBikMt9QMGEoe"]
  right: ["3JFfb9qiz49L2qKnBikMt9QMGEoe"]
                ^ index 1: j vs J

Identical signature in both: 27 of 28 characters match, differing only at index 1, and only in case. That is one document id read back with the wrong casing — not two colliding documents — which is exactly what `format!("{prefix}{rest}")` over a case-folded prefix directory produces. It requires a second doc in the same store whose 2-char prefix case-folds equal, hence the low per-run probability.

Rate measured: ~3% per invocation. Under a full-workspace run (10.6k tests) it surfaces often enough to look like a load-dependent flake, which is misleading — load is irrelevant, the doc-id draw is what matters.

Ruled out as caused by bd-v8gx/bd-gdhk: that branch touches only quarto-core artifact writing; no crates/quarto-hub/ file changed; and the failure reproduces on main with the branch absent.

Note for whoever fixes this: verifying the fix needs a stress loop (60+ iterations), not a single run. A single green run means nothing at a 3% rate.

c-87pzldt0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-87pzldt0.text:
SEVERITY ESCALATED p2 -> p1. This is not test-only, and the collector's re-verification does NOT protect against it.

Reachability: list_doc_ids_filesystem has three non-test callers —
  - crates/quarto-hub/src/main.rs:226        (hub admin scan)
  - crates/quarto-hub/src/admin/collect.rs:162 (hub admin collect, which QUARANTINES docs)

The data-loss path:
  1. live_doc_ids (scan.rs:165) builds the live set from DOCUMENT CONTENTS — referenced_doc_ids() reads capture_doc_id out of index sidecars, which carry the TRUE casing.
  2. The candidate set comes from PATHS via list_doc_ids_filesystem, which can be mis-cased.
  3. Both are compared as exact String / HashSet<String> members.
  => A LIVE capture whose path-derived id is mis-cased does not match its own sidecar reference, so it classifies as ORPHANED.
  4. If it also passes the age gate (default >30d), collect() quarantines it: std::fs::rename(doc_dir(automerge_dir, mis_cased_id)) — and because the filesystem is case-insensitive, that path resolves to the real directory, so it moves the LIVE document.

Why re-verification does not save us: collect() re-runs list_doc_ids_filesystem + live_doc_ids + verify_candidate against current storage (collect.rs:160-179). That recomputes the SAME wrong answer deterministically. The scan.rs module doc claims re-verification means 'scan-time staleness cannot cause an unsafe collection' — true for staleness, but this is systematic mis-identification, not staleness. That doc claim should be narrowed.

Mitigating factors (why p1 and not p0):
  - Production is Linux/ext4 (case-SENSITIVE) — immune. Exposure is macOS/Windows: dev machines, and any non-Linux deployment.
  - Requires a prefix case-collision, measured at ~3% per store.
  - Requires the affected doc to be live AND a capture AND past the age gate.
  - Quarantine is a rename into trash/ and restore() exists (collect.rs:297), so it is recoverable until purge() (collect.rs:381).

KEY ENABLER FOR A FIX: samod's DocumentId::from_str uses bs58::decode().with_check(None) — base58CHECK, with a 4-byte SHA256d checksum (samod-core/src/document_id.rs:58-60). So a mis-cased id FAILS TO PARSE with ~2^-32 false-accept odds. Detection is reliable and free; recovery is also possible because only the 2-char level-1 splay dir can be case-folded (level-2 is created fresh inside it), giving <=4 case variants to test against the checksum.

c-chwy4fzk.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-chwy4fzk.text: PART A IMPLEMENTED on main @ fb1e2818 (user-scoped 2026-08-10: Part A only, done on main rather than this strand's branch). recover_doc_id in crates/quarto-hub/src/admin/scan.rs tests the <=4 case variants of the 2-char splay prefix against DocumentId's bs58check checksum; zero/multiple distinct matches hard-fail (Unidentifiable/Ambiguous); list_doc_ids_filesystem is fallible; scan + collect abort on error; recovery warns when casing changed. One deviation from the plan sketch: recover returns the recovered id STRING (deduped by parsed DocumentId, preferring as-read casing) rather than a canonical re-encoding — legacy-UUID hex parses case-insensitively, so several casings name one id (must not read as Ambiguous), and re-encoding UUID-form ids to bs58check would break their path round-trip; this keeps instance B fully untangled for Part B. Also landed: module-doc safety claim narrowed (plan Phase 6), st/ adapter-dir collision test (every store has st/, so any St/sT/ST-prefixed doc id is guaranteed a folding partner), reverification test now asserts candidate count before indexing. Verification: TDD red confirmed pre-fix; 11479/11479 workspace tests; 150/150 clean stress iterations post-fix (3/142 failed pre-fix); E2E via 'hub admin scan' on a hand-built folded store (warn + true id in manifest; refusal exits 1). REMAINING OPEN (Parts B/C + questions 1-5 of the plan): normalize_id is still a string strip (instance B unconfirmed), ids still thread as String, manifest typing depth, upstream-samod question, unparseable-reference policy, belt-and-braces collect guard. Keep this strand open until those are resolved or explicitly descoped.

title: Outbox semantics for legacy projects IDB store
description:
Deferred follow-up from the tombstone fix. The legacy projects store is a permanent shadow of the synced set (rows re-created on every project open because URL routes key on the IDB row uuid). Best practice is outbox semantics: rows written only when the set is unreachable, drained by the reconciler once confirmed (deleteProjectByIndexDocId is already the drain mechanism).

Staged path:
1. Route by indexDocId instead of local row uuid (legacy fallback for existing bookmarks/history): utils/routing, App.tsx, ProjectSelector, ProjectsHome, share handler.
2. Remove the shadow writes the routing coupling forces (handleOpen in ProjectsHome, ProjectSelector open paths).
3. Reconciler drains rows after addProjectsBulk confirms them.
4. Optional: drain post-migration backup rows after pointer commit; v6 migration normalizing automerge:-prefix duality.

Tombstones stay regardless: only a deletion record can order a pending add on an offline browser against a deletion made on another browser.

See 'Deferred: outbox semantics' in claude-notes/plans/2026-08-21-project-set-deletion-tombstones.md
