title: Invite card: dark-mode elevation inverted, and type off the scale
description:
InviteLanding.css was left out of bd-g0uyp2v1 by scope decision (Andrew wanted only the login/front page changed). Two things remain there:

1. .il-wrap still derives its page surface as color-mix(--border-color 14%, --bg-modal). In dark mode --border-color (--posit-blue-dark-1) is lighter than --bg-modal (--posit-blue-dark-2), so the page renders LIGHTER than the card it frames, at 1.06:1 — elevation inverted, card findable only by its border. Fix: consume --bg-page-recessed (added to theme.css in 80a4e8c5), then extend the CARD_SURFACES loop in e2e/invite-landing-theme.harness.spec.ts back to the .il-wrap/.il-card pair; the spec was scoped down to the landing page in that commit and the comment there records why.

2. Off-scale type: .il-title 23px, .il-inviter 13.5px, .il-file-summary 11.5px, against theme.css's 13/18/24 scale (--text-base/lg/xl). lint:css does not catch raw px font sizes.

Also optional: .il-lockup is semibold with a 16px logo while the landing masthead is bold with a logo sized in em; the mark reads slightly differently across two surfaces an invitee sees within a minute. A ratio-parity test existed on the bd-g0uyp2v1 branch and was removed with the scope revert — see the plan file, decision 12.

title: Enforce preserve line-ending policy across q2

title: Extract quarto-yaml-validation into a standalone, non-Quarto-specific repository
description: Architectural investigation + design for moving quarto-yaml-validation (and its outbound dependency closure: quarto-source-map, quarto-yaml, quarto-error-reporting) out of quarto-dev/q2 so non-Quarto developers can use the YAML-schema-validation infrastructure. Key design problem: error codes (Q-1-x) and the centralized catalog/docs URLs are Quarto-specific; the standalone library needs its own error-code provider while the q2-embedded build keeps existing codes. Requires extracting quarto-error-reporting into a reusable library with pluggable/remappable error-code catalogs. This session gathered current-state architecture; see linked research doc.

c-4iakr487.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-4iakr487.text:
Design refinement 2026-06-26 (cont.). User decisions:

SEQUENCING (firm): extract-first, migrate-q2-LAST. Order: (1) foundation repo under posit-dev/ = quarto-source-map + error-reporting-core (split-out catalog-agnostic half), publish to crates.io, validate standalone; (2) yaml repo = quarto-yaml + quarto-yaml-validation as the FIRST CLIENT of the discipline, delete validate-yaml; (3) q2 migrates to published crates last. Rationale: invisible internal Posit consumers of quarto-yaml-validation need a real standalone repo; and the error-code discipline is a HOST contract that must be proven before its first client (error-reporting before yaml-validation). This inverts the earlier 'P0-P3 in q2 first' ordering.

ERROR-CODE DISCIPLINE crystallized into claude-notes/designs/cross-package-error-codes.md:
- Fallback hierarchy: tier1 remapped to Q-code (best) > tier2 library origin code passthrough (acceptable) > tier3 codeless (FORBIDDEN). Library contract guarantees tier3 never happens (every emittable diagnostic carries a stable namespaced origin code), so the embedder remap is a pure upgrade tier2->tier1, optional/per-code. Refines I3: unmapped is acceptable, audit WARNS not fails.
- Three contracts spelled out: library-author (own namespace, every error coded, stable, self-describe docs a la ESLint meta.docs.url), embedder/product (own remap+catalog, choose unmapped policy, never leak scheme upstream), shared-infra error-reporting-core (namespace-agnostic, provides CatalogProvider trait + remap hook + renderer = rustc LintStore analog).
- n2 case (a non-q2 embedder) resolved: supplies its own remap+catalog over the same core; remap is per-embedder, not a q2 feature -> remap hook MUST live in error-reporting-core.
- Clippy (clippy:: tool-lint namespace, own docs site, no E-codes) and ESLint (plugin/rule namespacing + meta.docs.url self-description) researched: both namespace + self-describe but EXPOSE the decomposition (they are platforms); q2 is a product that HIDES it, so q2 adds the remap they omit. TS = the compiler (flat numeric central, no cross-package design), good for presentation layer only.

OPEN FORKS for user: repo granularity (1 foundation repo + 1 yaml repo [rec] vs single 4-crate workspace repo); keep dormant Q-1-* yaml catalog entries vs remove; project naming.

c-d6qo0047.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-d6qo0047.text:
Discipline refinement 2026-06-26 (cont.3): APPEND-ONLY codes ('cool URLs for error codes', Berners-Lee 1998 applied to error ids). Folded into the design note + plan Q6.

Principle: codes are unique and never deleted/repurposed. Lifecycle = Active -> Retired -> (never deleted). Legal transition Active->Retired (stop emitting, keep documented); FORBIDDEN: Active->Never (deletion) and code->different-meaning (repurposing, stronger than a major bump - simply off the table). A docs page accumulating no-longer-emitted codes is correct/expected (old versions, external references). This also protects the provenance breadcrumb: never-delete means a disclosed upstream code degrades to retired-but-documented, never 404 or silent-redefinition.

Freeze binds at first PUBLIC exposure (emission or documentation), not first commit - pre-release dev churn is fine (semver pre-1.0 logic).

Enforce intra-repo, encourage cross-repo (same asymmetry as provenance staleness): append-only is checkable within a repo (diff catalog vs git history/snapshot); not checkable across repos.

CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE (the one place this bites existing code): q2's scripts/audit-error-codes.py is currently BIDIRECTIONAL. Must become: keep forward (every emitted code is documented), DROP reverse (every documented code is emitted - contradicts retirement), ADD append-only check. A retired/dormant code = legitimate catalog-only entry. ErrorCodeInfo.since_version already covers 'introduced'; optional retired_in/last_emitted for the window. This also largely settles the dormant-Q-1-* fork toward KEEP: any published yaml docs page is under the covenant.

c-dhnsz7ix.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-dhnsz7ix.text:
Design session 2026-06-26. Two artifacts written:

1. claude-notes/plans/2026-06-26-extract-quarto-yaml-validation-design.md — resolves the 7 open questions given the user's 'new repo owns foundation crates' lean. Key reframe: quarto-error-reporting is q2's whole diagnostics substrate (~19 dependents + shared JSON wire format), NOT an interchangeable foundation crate. Decision: split it into error-reporting-core (externalize, catalog-agnostic, CatalogProvider trait, no schemars, no quarto.org URLs) + quarto-error-catalog (stays in q2: Q-* catalog, quarto.org URLs, audit) + a thin quarto-error-reporting façade so the 19 call sites keep compiling. JSON wire types stay q2-side. Phased P0..P5 with P0-P3 landing entirely in q2 (deliver the seam) and P4-P5 the cross-repo commitment (separate go/no-go).

2. claude-notes/designs/cross-package-error-codes.md — the general philosophy the user asked for. Two-identity model: ORIGIN codes (namespaced, package-owned, e.g. yaml-schema/type-mismatch — Clippy/ESLint precedent) + PRESENTATION codes (flat, product-owned Q-<subsystem>-<n> — TS-compiler precedent). Product owns the remap. Invariant I1: subsystem != package, so q2 users never see the package decomposition. Corrected: 'TypeScript' = the language/compiler (flat central catalog, no cross-package design), not TS Quarto.

User clarifications folded in: validate-yaml to be DELETED (demo only; the ONLY in-repo consumer) -> quarto-yaml-validation will have ZERO q2 consumers, so the yaml remap is forward-looking/dormant until q2 wires the validator into config. c-szmu8xji.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-szmu8xji.text:
Discipline refinement 2026-06-26 (cont.2). Folded into claude-notes/designs/cross-package-error-codes.md:

ROLES ARE PER-NODE: 'library' vs 'product' collapses into one role applied at each hop. Every node = a DEFINER (mints terminal codes) + optional REMAPPER (relabels dependency codes). Q2 is just the TERMINAL remapper (its codes are user-facing). Chains bottom out at terminal codes; the library contract (every error has a stable code) guarantees every chain terminates.

TERMINAL vs REMAPPED provenance lane added (developer-facing, not user-facing; structured/JSON only). Three rules: (1) provenance is INERT DATA {code, source_url?}, never a typed dependency on the upstream error enum (would rebuild the coupling we're removing); (2) disclose the IMMEDIATE upstream + self-declared terminal flag, NOT a resolved-ultimate pointer (stale-proof under no-traversal; immediate==terminal in the common 1-hop case); (3) NO automated cross-repo traversal and no resolved-ultimate; disclosure is best-effort breadcrumb, optional version/commit pin, no cross-repo CI possible. Design-for-1-hop: permit chaining, build zero resolver.

error-reporting-core naming flagged: general infra under posit-dev/, likely drops quarto- prefix (candidates: diagnostic-core/reportkit/etc) — deferred, bikeshed.

Remaining nit: terminal as explicit bool flag vs implied-by-absence-of-provenance (lean: implied-by-absence).

title: revealjs code blocks: highlight spans emitted but highlight CSS missing (uncolored code)
description:
In format: revealjs, code cells get the tree-sitter hl-* span annotations (CodeHighlightStage runs) but render UNCOLORED because the compiled reveal theme CSS contains no .hl-* rules. HTML/q2-preview bundle highlight.scss into styles.css via the highlight_layer in every compile_theme_css variant; the reveal path (quarto-sass assemble_reveal_scss / compile_reveal_theme_css) omits highlight_layer entirely. Reproduces in all three paths (q2 render, q2 preview, hub-client) since it is shared Rust.

highlight.scss (resources/scss/html/templates/highlight.scss) is self-contained (/*-- scss:rules --*/, literal colors, no theme-variable deps), so the fix is to include the highlight layer in assemble_reveal_scss/compile_reveal_theme_css. Watch CSS specificity: reveal's own .reveal pre code rules may override bare .hl-* selectors; verify computed colors and scope under .reveal if needed.

Fix location: crates/quarto-sass/src/bundle.rs assemble_reveal_scss (~382) + crates/quarto-sass/src/compile.rs compile_reveal_theme_css (~374). TDD: assert reveal compiled CSS contains .hl-keyword, mirroring the existing HTML test (~compile.rs:620).

Verified end-to-end on q2 render (native) and hub-client/q2 preview (WASM) — identical colours to HTML. TDD test added; full workspace nextest + cargo xtask verify green.

title: Capture docs: uncompressed audit/GC metadata envelope (createdAt, sourcePath, engines)
description: Engine-capture binary docs (mimeType application/x-engine-capture+gzip) are orphaned in samod storage on every re-execution: perform_re_execute creates a new binary doc and repoints the index sidecar's CaptureRef, and nothing ever deletes the old doc. On quarto-hub deployments these accumulate forever, and bd-qbhp2cvv (embedding engine supporting-file bytes in captures) will make each one substantially bigger. Proposal: add a small UNCOMPRESSED top-level automerge 'meta' map beside content/mimeType/hash (via a create_binary_document_with_meta variant in quarto-hub/src/resource.rs) with kind:'engine-capture' + schema version, createdAt, sourcePath (project-relative qmd path), and engines (e.g. ['knitr']). Placement matters: mimeType already classifies capture docs without gunzipping, but anything inside the gzipped content payload is invisible to sync-server audits. With provenance in place, a storage-hygiene job gets a safe policy: capture-MIME docs not referenced by any index sidecar AND older than N days -> collect, with per-project accounting. Touches all three capture writers: quarto-preview/src/capture_driver.rs, quarto-preview/src/re_execute.rs (write_capture_doc), quarto-hub-provider/src/execute.rs. Context: discussion recorded in claude-notes/plans/2026-07-23-preview-engine-supporting-files.md (bd-qbhp2cvv).

title: D4/D5 react: preview Table.tsx emits header/odd/even row classes
description:
## What

D4/D5 in pampa's HTML writer (closed as bd-12fpz, commit c02a405a) emit `<tr class="header">`, `<tr class="odd">`, `<tr class="even">` on rendered HTML. `q2 preview` does not benefit because it doesn't go through the pampa HTML writer — its iframe renders directly from AST JSON via the React Table component at `ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/Table.tsx`. That component currently emits bare `<tr>`.

## Fix

In Table.tsx, extend `RowNode` to accept the row's class ("header" / "odd" / "even" / null). Caller (`Table`) computes it based on:
- head rows: always "header"
- body rows: alternating "odd" / "even" per TableBody, starting at "odd"
- foot rows: null (no class)

Mirrors the pampa writer change (bd-12fpz) exactly.

## Tests

Vitest test for Table.tsx that builds a minimal Table AST and asserts on the rendered DOM.

## Plan

claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-table-default-rendering-parity.md — discovered during preview e2e verification on the table-rendering-parity epic.

title: Jupyter environment health check under 'q2 check' (distinguish absent/broken/no-kernel)
description: q2 check exists as a CLI stub (crates/quarto/src/commands/check.rs -- 'Verify correct functioning of Quarto installation', currently returns QuartoError::NotImplemented) but has no implementation yet. Concrete motivating case: on Chris's Windows machine, 'jupyter' resolves on PATH (which::which succeeds, so JupyterEngine::is_available() reports true) but the binary is an orphaned pipx trampoline pointing at a deleted venv -- it crashes on every invocation (exit 1, no output). Today nothing in q2 distinguishes: (a) jupyter not installed at all, (b) jupyter on PATH but non-functional (this case), (c) jupyter working but the requested kernel isn't registered. All three currently surface as the same downstream KernelspecNotFound message once a render is attempted. A 'q2 check jupyter' (or similar target) should actively probe: is the jupyter binary on PATH, does it actually run (e.g. jupyter --version or --paths --json succeeds), what kernelspecs does it report, cross-referenced against what runtimelib's static-dir search finds -- giving an actionable diagnostic before a user ever gets to a confusing render-time error. COORDINATION NOTE: 'q2 check' is also the target of an existing in-progress strand, bd-4qflzhwh (Gordon Woodhull), which is wiring TS-engine checkInstallation (marimo/julia) into the same command's dispatch -- Plan 10 already authored, frozen test-seam spec, branch braid/bd-4qflzhwh-wire-ts-engine-checkinstallation on feature/ts-engine-extensions, ready for execution. Whoever picks up this jupyter-check strand MUST read that plan first and slot a jupyter-specific check into the same dispatch structure rather than building a parallel/competing one. Related to bd-gdco7syg (the ask_jupyter() silent-failure gap this check would want to surface).

title: Smart punctuation: '...' converts to an ellipsis only when preceded by a word character
description:
Pandoc's `smart` extension rewrites every run of three dots to a HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS. q2 does it only when the dot run follows a word character, and silently does not when it follows a space, an opening paren, or the start of a block. The other three substitutions (curly quotes, en dash, em dash) are correct in every position.

## What happens vs Quarto 1

Quarto 1 converts all of these. q2 0.19.0:

| input | q2 output | |
|---|---|---|
| the ... menu | the ... menu | wrong |
| **...** | ... | wrong |
| ... and then (paragraph start) | ... and then | wrong |
| see (...) here | see (...) here | wrong |
| a...b | a…b | correct |
| Wait for it... | Wait for it… | correct |
| 1...2 | 1…2 | correct |
| a,...b | a,…b | correct |

The control that makes this specific: `x -- y` becomes `x – y` even though the dash run follows a space. Only the dot path is position-dependent. No diagnostic is emitted.

## Root-cause area

The conversion itself is implemented and correct. `apply_smart_typography` in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/text_helpers.rs:161 handles dot runs at lines 188-201 — taking three at a time as U+2026 and leaving a remainder of one or two dots literal, exactly Pandoc's rule from Text/Pandoc/Parsing/Smart.hs. The passing rows above prove the function is reachable and working.

So the defect is upstream of it: in the failing positions the dot run does not arrive as part of a prose-str node that the function is applied to. The function's own doc comment is the pointer — it "must be applied per prose-str node, before merging adjacent strings", and explains that escaped punctuation arrives from tree-sitter as its own single-character node.

One hypothesis worth checking first: a '.' at the start of an inline token is a candidate class marker for attribute syntax ({.class}, [text]{.class}), so a dot-leading token may be routed down a path that never reaches apply_smart_typography. That would explain why a space and '(' both break it while a letter, digit or comma do not — those are exactly the positions where a new attribute-candidate token could start.

## Suggested fix direction

Find where a dot-leading inline token is produced and make sure its text still passes through apply_smart_typography, rather than changing the function (which is correct as written). Worth adding the position dimension to whatever test covers smart typography: the existing coverage evidently exercises only word-adjacent dot runs, since the three failing positions are the common ones in prose.

## Real-world hit in the Connect docs

user/api-keys and user/plumber both document the overflow menu as "the **...** menu", which Quarto 1 renders as "the **…** menu". Both are space-preceded, i.e. the failing case. Two pages in the current corpus, but "the ... menu" is a common construct in UI documentation generally, and the failing positions are the ones prose actually uses.

## Repro

/Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/ellipsis-not-smart/

Run "q2 render repro.qmd" there and compare with "quarto render repro.qmd --to html -o q1.html". Section A is the failing positions, section B the working ones, section C the three controls including the space-preceded en dash.

Observed on q2 0.17.0 through 0.19.0 (re-verified against the released 0.19.0 binary; HEAD 1ba0f2ec). Origin strand in the q2-connect-docs skein: br-ksfjyxaa.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #518 (merged). Added a '[.]+' alternative to PANDOC_REGEX_STR in grammar.js so a dot run lexes as one pandoc_str token, letting apply_smart_typography (unchanged) see the whole run. Root cause was startStrRegex admitting '-' but not '.' as a token-start character -- not the attribute-class routing originally hypothesized. Also brings four-dot runs in line with Pandoc ('....' -> ellipsis plus literal remainder). CI green on all 8 checks including WASM and Hub-Client E2E.

Two incidental findings deliberately NOT filed as follow-ups, per user: q2's heading-id algorithm does not strip punctuation (q2 gives 'heading-with-...-dots' where Pandoc gives 'heading-with-dots'), and the related question of docs coverage. Both judged too low-priority to track speculatively; will revisit if a user reports them.

c-6u70lxy3.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-6u70lxy3.text:
Correction to this strand's closing note, measured 2026-08-13 on main @ b677afd4 against pandoc 3.9.0.2: the unfiled finding recorded above -- 'q2 gives heading-with-...-dots where Pandoc gives heading-with-dots' -- no longer reproduces. PR #518 fixed it as a side effect: a dot run now lexes as one token, so q2 converts it to U+2026, which its heading-id slug filter drops exactly as Pandoc's does. Both '## with ... dots' and '## trailing dots ...' now agree between the two engines.

The heading-id area does still diverge, but in two other ways, both now filed with measured evidence: bd-heading-id-drops-inline-content-fl84n3ql (the collector drops whole inline subtrees) and bd-sdalit9y (no dropNonLetter, no empty-id fallback). c-q1i65hmi.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-q1i65hmi.text:
Investigated at HEAD 7bcddf61; plan skeleton at claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-ellipsis-not-smart.md (commit 27f96dfb).

Root cause found, and it is NOT the attribute-class routing hypothesis in the description. apply_smart_typography IS reached in the failing positions; it just never sees more than one dot. tree-sitter emits ' ... ' as three separate single-character pandoc_str nodes, conversion runs per node (a run of 1 correctly stays literal), and merge_strs concatenates them afterwards.

The asymmetry is grammar.js:99 -- startStrRegex includes '-' but not '.' in the token-START class, while the continuation class (line 130) has both. So '--' lexes as one node (hence the passing dash control), 'a...b' lexes as one node, but a dot can only match the single-char alternative '[>.,;!?]' (line 127).

Decisive probe: 'x -... y' renders '-...' as an en-dash-free '-U+2026' -- prefixing a hyphen REPAIRS the ellipsis. Same for a smart quote. No attribute-routing story explains that.

Recommended fix: add a dedicated dot-run alternative to PANDOC_REGEX_STR rather than adding '.' to startStrRegex (which would make '.class' a single token, next door to the attribute grammar). Main risk is parser regeneration shifting the LR states that resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json maps to diagnostics.

Test-coverage gap confirmed as the description suspected: smart-typography.qmd only has word-adjacent dot runs, and dashes_spaced.qmd starts from an already-converted U+2026 so it tests roundtripping, not conversion.

Awaiting design alignment; not started.

c-u11fuz6j.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-u11fuz6j.text: Fixed on branch braid/ellipsis-not-smart-48bv2pe6, commit 727673b2. NOT pushed (awaiting permission). Fix: added a '[.]+' alternative to PANDOC_REGEX_STR in grammar.js so a dot run lexes as ONE pandoc_str token. apply_smart_typography is unchanged, as the investigation predicted. Chose this over adding '.' to startStrRegex, which would make '.class' a single token adjacent to the attribute grammar. Also in scope per user decision: four dots now give an ellipsis plus a literal remainder ('....' -> '.'), matching Pandoc's three-at-a-time rule. title: Bare email autolinks <user@example.com> parsed as raw HTML — address invisible in output
description:
CommonMark email autolinks ('Contact <sales@example.com> now.') should render as mailto links with the address as visible text. q2 0.15.0 lexes the construct as an HTML element instead: it lands in the output as a raw '<sales@example.com>' tag that browsers swallow — the address is completely invisible on the rendered page. The only signal is a generic Q-2-9 'HTML element converted to raw HTML' warning, which is easily lost (the Posit Connect docs emit 2833 legitimate Q-2-9s). The '<mailto:sales@example.com>' URI-autolink form works in both q2 and Q1 (visible text keeps the mailto: prefix in both).

This is core CommonMark, not a Pandoc-ism (ruling by Carlos 2026-08-10: fix belongs in q2): the email autolink is an explicit spec production (spec.commonmark.org, Autolinks). Supported by original Markdown.pl (2004), pandoc (all of markdown/commonmark/gfm readers, verified; the markdown reader adds class=email, matching Q1), cmark, comrak, markdown-it, goldmark (Hugo), pulldown-cmark (mdBook), micromark/remark, kramdown (Jekyll), Python-Markdown (MkDocs); GFM even autolinks bare emails without brackets. Sole mainstream exception: MDX (reserves <...> for JSX) — and it fails loudly with a parse error rather than silently dropping content.

Root cause: the hand-rolled '<...>' disambiguator in the external scanner (crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c, ~line 1878) only emits AUTOLINK after seeing a 'url-like character' (':' or '%', had_url_like_character) before '>' — bare emails have neither, so they fall through to HTML_ELEMENT.

Suggested fix: additionally qualify AUTOLINK on 'saw @, no whitespace' in the same scanner loop (over-approximation is safe in C — HTML tag names cannot contain '@'), then do precise validation in pampa's process_uri_autolink (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs, 'autolink' arm): if the content has no scheme and matches the CommonMark email-autolink regex, emit href='mailto:...' with class='email' and the bare address as link text; otherwise fall back to current behavior. Fallback design position if angle-bracket-means-HTML is a line q2 wants to hold: detect email-shaped 'elements' and emit a specific actionable diagnostic (like MDX) instead of generic Q-2-9 — but full support is the spec-compliant choice.

Real-world hit: Posit Connect docs admin/user-management/index.md originally used '<sales@posit.co>' (Q1 source); during porting it was changed to the '<mailto:...>' form to keep a working link, regressing the visible text to 'mailto:sales@posit.co'. The docs side will revert to the bare form once this is fixed.

Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/email-autolink-dropped/ (see README.md; run 'q2 render repro.qmd' there; exercises both forms, Q1-verified). Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-email-autolink-dropped-287gi3pl. Observed with q2 0.15.0; checked origin/main (59d1edf9): no autolink fix (bd-ly83qewg only changed whitespace-after-'<' lexing).

title: qmd writer/reader: explicit Figure shapes don't round-trip (caption ≠ alt, multi-block content, etc.)
description:
Discovered while implementing bd-f5qd. The implicit-figure round-trip is fixed (write_figure now detects the implicit shape and emits bare image syntax). Figures with shapes other than the implicit one have no syntax in qmd that round-trips back to a Figure: the writer's fallback emits a fenced `::: {}` div with the caption as a sibling block, and the reader has no rule that turns that back into a Figure.

Concrete minimal repro (caption text differs from image alt):

  $ cat > /tmp/explicit_fig.json <<'EOF'
  {
    "pandoc-api-version": [1, 23, 1],
    "meta": {},
    "blocks": [{"t":"Figure","c":[
      ["",[],[]],
      [null,[{"t":"Plain","c":[{"t":"Str","c":"A different caption."}]}]],
      [{"t":"Plain","c":[{"t":"Image","c":[["",["lightbox"],[]],[{"t":"Str","c":"Image alt"}],["image.png",""]]}]}]
    ]}]
  }
  EOF
  $ cat /tmp/explicit_fig.json | cargo run --bin pampa -- -f json -t qmd
  ::: {}

  ![Image alt](image.png){.lightbox}

  A different caption.

  :::

  $ cat /tmp/explicit_fig.json | cargo run --bin pampa -- -f json -t qmd | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t native
  [ Div ( "" , [] , [] ) [
    Figure ( "" , [] , [] ) (Caption Nothing [Plain[Str "Image",Space,Str "alt"]]) [...],
    Para [Str "A",Space,Str "different",Space,Str "caption."]
  ] ]

The original caption is gone (replaced by the implicit-figure rule firing on
the inner image-only paragraph, which copies the alt text into the caption).
The original caption text becomes a free-standing sibling Para. The outer
Div wraps the whole thing.

Other shapes that hit the same fallback:
- Figure with caption.short set
- Figure with multiple content blocks
- Figure with classes or kvs on the figure itself (not just the image)
- Figure whose content isn't a single Plain[Image]

Fix needs reader-side support: design a qmd syntax for explicit figures and
add a reader rule that converts it back to a Figure block. Likely shape:
fenced div with a recognizable class/id marker plus a convention for which
block is the caption (TS Quarto uses crossref-style `#fig-id` divs).

For now the writer's fallback path stays as-is; users get a structurally
incorrect div until this is fixed.

title: raw-json: pampa-native lossless JSON reader/writer (GH #11)
description: Add a pampa-specific 'raw JSON' format whose contract is that write-then-read is the identity on the full pampa AST, including extensions Pandoc JSON cannot represent (standalone Inline::Attr, NoteReference, CriticMarkup inlines, Shortcode, CaptionBlock, full ConfigValue metadata). title: Project _environment files are not loaded (env shortcode resolves against process env only)
description:
Quarto 1 loads project environment-variable files before rendering: _environment, _environment.local, _environment.required, and profile variants (_environment-<profile>); already-set process variables win over file values. q2 0.15.0 never reads these files, so '{{< env NAME >}}' resolves only against the process environment — with the variable defined solely in _environment, every use renders the unresolved marker '?env:NAME' plus a Q-16-5 warning per use.

Root cause: EnvShortcodeHandler (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/shortcode_resolve.rs, ~line 213) calls std::env::var directly, and nothing in project discovery/load (crates/quarto-core/src/project/mod.rs) looks for _environment files — 'rg _environment crates/' has no hits.

Suggested fix: load _environment(.local/.required/-<profile>) during project load and inject into the process env (or a project env map consulted by EnvShortcodeHandler), with Q1 precedence: real environment > _environment.local > _environment; _environment.required lists variables that must be defined.

Real-world hit: the Posit Connect docs set CONNECT_VERSION/CONNECT_SHORT_VERSION/CURRENT_YEAR in _environment; under q2 every processed '{{< env CONNECT_VERSION >}}' (page subtitles, body text, news page) renders '?env:CONNECT_VERSION' markers site-wide unless the caller exports the variables manually. (Uses inside website.title/page-footer/HTML includes fail differently — see bd strand filed alongside this one, slug shortcodes-in-metadata.)

Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/environment-file-ignored/ (see README.md; run 'q2 render' there WITHOUT exporting REPRO_VERSION). Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-environment-files-n0joqkug. Observed with q2 0.15.0; checked origin/main (8518ac79): no _environment handling.
close_reason: Merged in PR #486 (https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/486): _environment/_environment.local loaded with Q1 precedence into a project env map (no process-env mutation); env shortcode, knitr/jupyter subprocesses, and render scripts consume it; _environment.required gets real span-carrying diagnostics; docs at guides/projects/environment.qmd. title: Quarto 1's doubled-brace escape for showing a cell is unsupported: literal in a fence, bare parse error in prose
description:
Quarto 1's way of *showing* an executable cell rather than running it — doubling the braces in the fence opener — has no q2 equivalent, and the two contexts fail differently. Both matter to anyone porting docs that document Quarto syntax.

## What happens vs Quarto 1

### Inside a displayed code fence — silently wrong output

    ````markdown
    ```{{python}}
    1+1
    ```
    ````

Quarto 1 collapses the doubled pair and shows the reader ```{python}```. q2 0.19.0 leaves it doubled: the reader is shown ```{{python}}```, which is not valid Quarto syntax, presented as the thing to copy. No diagnostic.

### In prose — a bare parse error

    X {{python}} Y

fails the whole file with

    Error: Parse error
     1 │ X {{python}} Y
       │    ┬
       │    ╰── unexpected character or token here

No error code, no hint. The single-brace form "X {python} Y" is much better served: it gets [Q-2-41] with an actionable message ("To write literal braces, escape them as \{...\}"). So the form a porter's source actually contains — the Q1 escape — produces the least helpful failure q2 has.

## What already works (so this is narrower than it looks)

- A fence opener with SINGLE braces inside an outer ````markdown fence renders correctly in q2. Fence bodies are verbatim; there is nothing to escape there.
- In prose, both \{python\} and a code span render {python} cleanly.

So q2 already has expressive coverage for every case. What is missing is (a) accepting or rejecting Q1's spelling deliberately, and (b) not falling off a cliff when it appears.

## Root-cause area

Fence bodies are assembled verbatim from source bytes in process_code_fence_content (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/code_fence_content.rs) — it splices around block_continuation markers and does no unescaping, which is why the doubled pair survives to output. The prose path is the attribute-syntax reader that raises Q-2-41 (catalog entry in crates/quarto-error-catalog/error_catalog.json:450); the doubled form evidently reaches the parser before that check and dies as an uncoded parse error instead.

## Suggested fix direction

The design question is the important half, and it should be answered before any code moves: does q2 adopt {{...}} as an escape at all?

Recommendation is NO for a blanket collapse, for a reason we hit in practice — see the counter-case below — and instead:

1. In prose, make {{...}} produce Q-2-41 (or a sibling code) rather than a bare parse error, with a hint naming the forms that work (backslash-escaped braces, or a code span). Cheap, and it converts the worst failure into the best one.
2. For fences, decide explicitly and document it. If q2's answer is "write single braces, fence bodies are verbatim", that is a perfectly good answer and only needs a migration note plus, ideally, a qmd-syntax-helper rule that rewrites a doubled-brace fence opener to the single-brace form inside displayed fences.

## Counter-case that should shape the decision

user/fastapi/index.qmd in the Connect docs shows a Jinja template containing a genuine {{ request.headers[...] }}. Quarto 1 unescapes it to a single brace pair, which is WRONG for that page — the reader needs both braces. q2's literal output is the correct one there. A blanket collapse of every doubled brace would regress that page; whatever q2 does should be an explicit, documented escape rather than a global rule.

## Real-world hit in the Connect docs

user/quarto/index.qmd (5 blocks), user/rmarkdown/index.qmd (2), how-to/publish-databricks-quarto-notebook/index.qmd (1) — all pages whose subject IS how to write Quarto cells, all currently showing the doubled-brace form as the example to copy. These are 5 of the ~47 pages that still differ from the Q1 reference render.

## Repro

/Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/escaped-executable-fence/

Run "q2 render" there and compare with "quarto render". The repro covers the fence case; the prose parse error is the one-liner "X {{python}} Y" above.

Observed from q2 0.16.0 through 0.19.0 (re-verified against the released 0.19.0 binary; HEAD 1ba0f2ec). Origin strand in the q2-connect-docs skein: br-xa5oawj0.
close_reason: Implemented as Q-2-50 (prose merr-corpus error + fence-opener warning in postprocess), plus docs page and migration note. No {{...}} escape adopted; no qmd-syntax-helper rule (design decision). Commit 297f5cc2; plan claude-notes/plans/2026-08-17-doubled-brace-escape.md

title: cargo xtask verify can run tree-sitter test against a stale parser library
description:
A full 'cargo xtask verify' run failed at Step 4/14 with 'Total parses: 609; successful parses: 599; failed parses: 10', then passed cleanly on an immediate rerun with no source change. It is not a random flake -- the failing set identifies the cause exactly.

The ten failures were:
  110. LaTeX and link clashes (parse error)
  527. Q-2-35: 4-space indent rejected (issue #184)
  545-552. the eight 'naked shortcode arg: ...' tests

That is precisely, and only, the set of tests whose expectations changed in commit e223edd52 (the shortcode_naked_string widening): the 8 tests it added, plus the 2 (parse error) recovery snapshots it updated to the post-widening recovery tokenization. Every other corpus test passed. In other words the run behaved exactly as if 'tree-sitter test' had loaded the PRE-widening parser library while checking the POST-widening corpus. A random flake would not select that set.

Concurrency is the likely trigger: cargo logs from the same window show 'Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory', so more than one cargo/tree-sitter process was active in the worktree. verify's Step 4 runs generate/build/test, and if the built grammar library is stale or mid-write when the test step loads it, the corpus is validated against the wrong parser.

Why this matters beyond one red run: the failure mode is symmetric. Here it produced a spurious FAILURE that a rerun cleared, which is annoying but loud. The same staleness on a branch that has not changed the grammar would produce a spurious PASS -- verify would validate the committed corpus against an older parser and report green. That is the dangerous direction, and nothing in the current chain would catch it.

Ruled out during investigation: 'tree-sitter generate' immediately afterward produced a ZERO diff against the committed parser.c/grammar.json (so grammar and generated parser were in sync on disk), and three back-to-back direct 'tree-sitter test' runs each reported 609/609. A subsequent full 'cargo xtask verify' passed all 14/14 steps including the WASM/hub leg.

Suggested direction: have verify's tree-sitter step assert freshness rather than assume it -- e.g. make the build step's output a hard dependency of the test step, or stamp/compare the built library against the grammar hash before running the corpus. Repo rules already require the generate/build/test chain by hand; verify should not be able to skip a link in it silently.

Observed on branch braid/bd-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-2u79bqp1-shortcode-escaped-gt at commit 2477d2816. Full log retained at /tmp/task4-verify.log (937 lines, exit code 1).

title: Render profiles: --profile / QUARTO_PROFILE plumbing and profile-aware config (_quarto-<profile>.yml, _environment-<profile>)
description:
q2 parses 'quarto render --profile' (crates/quarto/src/main.rs:144) but drops it: the Commands::Render destructure (~main.rs:748) elides it with '..' and RenderArgs has no field for it. There is no QUARTO_PROFILE handling anywhere in crates/ — q2 has no active-profile concept.

Quarto 1 semantics to port (external-sources/quarto-cli/src/quarto-core/profile.ts + src/project/project-profile.ts): QUARTO_PROFILE env var holds a comma/colon-separated profile list; --profile sets it; a 'profile' config key supports default profiles and profile groups (at least one member of each group active); active profiles select _quarto-<profile>.yml config layers merged over _quarto.yml (validated per layer), and profile variants of environment files (_environment-<profile>). Bootstrap wrinkle: Q1 allows QUARTO_PROFILE itself to be defined in _environment/_environment.local (dotenvQuartoProfile in src/quarto-core/dotenv.ts), read before profile resolution.

Scoped out of bd-environment-files-372u9qbs by design (2026-08-10 session): the _environment work ships without profile variants; when this strand lands, its active-profile list should feed (a) profile config merging and (b) _environment-<profile> loading in the loader introduced there (plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-09-environment-files-loading.md). Needed for the Posit Connect docs port. Note Q1 implements --profile by mutating the process env (Deno.env.set in setProfileFromArg); q2 policy decided in that plan is to NOT mutate the process environment — plumb the active-profile list as data instead.

title: Engine registry init-time diagnostics never reach the user (drain registry.diagnostics; route pass-1 warning through the sink)
description:
Two related gaps in how project-scoped ENGINE diagnostics reach the user. Found while investigating pass-1 engine resolution on feature/ts-engine-extensions (worktree .worktrees/ts-engine-extensions, HEAD 645845ea2). NOT part of the current merge runbook (claude-notes/plans/2026-08-13-ts-engine-extensions-merge-main.md) -- this is unfinished work from plan1c.

(1) registry.diagnostics is written but never drained.
- Producers: engine_contribution_missing_fields_warning (crates/quarto-core/src/extension/types.rs:283) pushed at crates/quarto-core/src/project/mod.rs:1576, and TsEngine's intermediate-files failure warning (crates/quarto-core/src/engine/ts_engine.rs:977).
- Consumers in production code: NONE. The only reader is a test (crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/engine_registry_build.rs:626). The leftover marker is still in place: '// Task: drain registry.diagnostics at orchestrator (plan step 10)' at crates/quarto-core/src/project/mod.rs:1645.
- 'plan step 10' = claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-plan1c-extension-integration.md, registry-build step 10 ('Drain registry.diagnostics and emit directly to the user-facing diagnostic sink'). It was prose inside the spec, never a checklist item, so it was never reconciled. Both the producer and the marker landed in the same commit, 171aef17f (Engine stop B).
- User-visible effect: an engine extension missing name/claims/file-extensions/claims-files gets a precise, actionable warning naming exactly which fields are missing -- and it is silently discarded. Verified E2E: rendered a scratch project with the legacy-python fixture (missing claims, file-extensions, claims-files); nothing printed.

(2) The pass-1 fall-through warning bypasses the diagnostic pipeline.
- pass1_engine_resolution_warning (crates/quarto-core/src/project/orchestrator.rs:278) IS emitted -- but via bare eprintln! at orchestrator.rs:1114, not into any diagnostic collection.
- Consequence: it is not counted by ProjectRenderSummary::diagnostic_counts and is not promoted by promote_warnings_to_errors, so --strict-style warning promotion (bd-yjs54ptg / GH #220) does not see it.
- This is the natural landing site for (1): the orchestrator already has a project-grain engine-warning print point; both should go through the same sink.

Suggested shape: give the orchestrator one project-grain diagnostic channel, drain registry.diagnostics into it after build_engine_registry, and route pass1_engine_resolution_warning through it too, so both are counted and promotable.

TDD note: (1) needs a test that a legacy extension's missing-fields warning actually reaches user-visible output (the existing test only reads the vec in-process); (2) needs a test that a fell-through render's warning increments ProjectRenderSummary::diagnostic_counts().warnings and is promoted under strict mode.
close_reason: Drained at end of render into project_diagnostics; Q-16-11 routed off eprintln!. 9 e2e tests, workspace 12,635 passed, full cargo xtask verify green. Commit 8b02c8651.

c-3v8cshbg.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-3v8cshbg.text:
CORRECTED VERSION of comment c-g8a3nwky (that one lost several backticked
fragments to shell mangling — read this one instead).

Design note on message SHAPE — draining as-is is not enough.

`engine_contribution_missing_fields_warning` builds its message with
`DiagnosticMessage::warning(msg)`, which puts the ENTIRE ~380-char text in the
diagnostic's *title* (quarto-error-reporting 0.2.1: `DiagnosticMessage::warning`
-> `Self::new(kind, title)`, diagnostic.rs:301). `to_text` does not wrap. So
draining it verbatim would print one run-on line:

    Warning: Engine extension 'acme/legacy-python' (path: /abs/path/_extensions/acme/legacy-python/dist/legacy-python.js) is missing static declarations: claims, file-extensions, claims-files. An engine missing name/claims/claims-files is treated as a legacy Q1 engine and LoadEngined on every render (slow dynamic path) vs. zero-load when declared. Declare [] or {} to silence a field the engine genuinely has none of.

Compare the pass-1 warning, which uses `DiagnosticMessageBuilder`
(subject / problem / add_detail / add_hint) and renders as a structured block.
Rebuild the missing-fields message the same way before draining it — roughly:

    Warning: engine extension `acme/legacy-python` is missing static declarations
    so q2 must load it on every render instead of resolving statically.
    ✖ missing: claims, file-extensions, claims-files
    ℹ declare each missing key in _extension.yml; `[]` / `{}` counts as declared
      ("this engine genuinely has none"), e.g. `claims: [python]`.

Also: the path currently shown is the engine's `.js` bundle (the `path` field of
`EngineContribution::External`), while the pass-1 warning shows the
`_extension.yml`. The `_extension.yml` is the file a user would EDIT to fix
this, so prefer `extension_yml_path` (already carried on the contribution for
exactly this reason — see its doc comment at extension/types.rs:105) or show
both.

COALESCING: a single legacy engine will now trigger BOTH warnings in one render
— missing-fields at registry build (fires regardless of impact) and pass-1
fall-through at end of Pass-1 (fires only when >=1 doc is affected). In the
legacy-python E2E both would print, naming the same engine, with overlapping
hints. Decide the relationship when wiring the shared sink: suppress the
missing-fields warning for engines the pass-1 warning already names, or merge
them into one engine-grain diagnostic.

title: Pipe table parser commits to caption when ':::' follows a row (issue #206)
description:
Parse error when a fenced-div close `:::` directly follows a pipe table row without an intervening blank line. The first `:` of `:::` is shifted by the parser as the start of a `caption` rule (the caption first-token literal is `:`); once shifted, tree-sitter cannot back out, and the second `:` produces 'unexpected character or token here'.

Triage doc: claude-notes/issue-reports/206/triage.md
Worktree branch: issue-206
GitHub issue: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/206
Reporter: @rundel
Real-world example: quarto-dev/quarto-web docs/websites/website-navigation.qmd L155-L159

Confirmed not a fenced-div bug — bare pipe table + `:::` reproduces identically. The fenced div in the reporter's example is incidental.

Recommended fix shape: introduce an external `_caption_start` scanner token that only matches a `:` not immediately followed by another `:` (and followed by inline whitespace). Re-key the `caption` rule on `_caption_start` instead of the literal `:`. Add tree-sitter corpus tests for `:::`-after-table, `: caption`-after-table, bare `:::` after table, and a pampa round-trip test for the repro fixture. Re-test on quarto-web after fix.

Out of scope here, file separately if desired: pipe-table parser also silently absorbs trailing headings/paragraphs as one-cell rows when no blank line intervenes (see triage doc 'Adjacent finding').
close_reason: Fixed by PR #208 (merged as f0a1fd53)

title: hub: server-minted sliding sessions (decouple session lifetime from Google 1h ID token)
description: Decouple hub session lifetime from the Google 1h ID token. Today the auth cookie IS the Google ID token (1h exp, JWKS-validated per request); the only renewal path is GIS One Tap, unavailable in many environments (FedCM/3p-cookie, unregistered origins). Design: validate the Google token once at login, then mint a hub-signed compact HttpOnly session cookie with sliding expiry (stateless v1; revocable session store deferred). Reuses the existing HMAC server_secret pattern; adds kid/versioned rotation. Also fixes the >3800-byte cookie silent-drop risk (build_auth_cookie warning). Structural fix for bd-3o8zmz46 (tactically mitigated only). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-06-hub-server-minted-sliding-sessions.md (phases C0-C7 held until kickoff). Part of the 2026-07-06 auth reshape; umbrella: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-06-connection-gated-auth-and-auth-unification.md

Hub validates Google once at login, mints compact HS256 session cookies (idle 7d / absolute 30d, sliding re-issue), kid-based rotation with graceful+emergency modes, revocation store (logout-everywhere + bans), client keep-alive replacing the One-Tap renewal dependency, e2e-verified against the real binary (scripts/hub-sliding-sessions-e2e.mjs). cargo xtask verify fully green. title: qmd writer drops table caption attributes (issue #152)
description:
GitHub: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/152
Triage: claude-notes/issue-reports/152/triage.md
Worktree: .worktrees/issue-152 (branch issue-152, based on main @ 132c13c8)

The pipe-table branch of write_table (crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:1120-1239) ignores Table.attr entirely. A caption-attached attribute block like ': caption {tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}' is parsed correctly into Table.attr.2 (verified via 'cargo run --bin pampa --' on claude-notes/issue-reports/152/repro.qmd) but is dropped by 'pampa -t qmd', producing a lossy round-trip.

The list-table branch (write_list_table at lines 928-1118) already handles id/classes/keyvals correctly. The pipe-table branch needs analogous handling at the caption emission point (lines 1217-1235): after writing ': <caption-text>', emit ' {<attrs>}' via the existing write_attr helper (qmd.rs:396) when is_empty_attr(&table.attr) is false.

Open questions resolved during triage:
  1. Empty-id auto-suppression NOT NEEDED. The reader (pipe_table.rs:148-200) only sets Table.attr.0 from explicit {#id} in the caption attr block; no implicit tbl-foo numbering exists.
  2. Caption-suffix is the only valid placement for table attributes. Verified against pandoc 3.9.0.2: prefix form '{attrs}<newline>table<newline>: caption' is not parsed as a table by pandoc OR pampa (pampa raises Q-0-99 + Q-3-32). Suffix form ': caption {attrs}' produces byte-identical AST in both engines, including the mixed id+classes+keyvals shape.

Fix workflow per crates/pampa/CLAUDE.md:
  1. Add failing fixtures under crates/pampa/tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/ (table-caption-with-keyval.qmd, table-caption-with-id.qmd, table-caption-with-classes.qmd, table-caption-with-mixed-attrs.qmd).
  2. Verify each fixture fails the round-trip equality check.
  3. Implement: emit write_attr(&table.attr, buf, ctx) after the caption text (qmd.rs:1228-1234), guarded by !is_empty_attr(&table.attr). No id-suppression guard needed.
  4. Verify new fixtures pass and existing table-caption.qmd snapshot is unchanged (its Table.attr is empty).
  5. cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build (Rust-only, no quarto-core/pandoc-types touched).

Existing parser-side snapshot covering this fixture: crates/pampa/tests/snapshots/json/table-caption-attr.qmd. Read-side contract: docs/syntax/desugaring/table-captions.qmd.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #154 / commit 688ac678. Pipe-table writer now appends Table.attr via write_attr() on the caption line; 4 round-trip fixtures cover id, classes, keyval, and mixed-attr shapes.

title: Project-set deletions resurrected on reload by IDB reconciler
description:
Deleting a project from the synced project set only mutated the Automerge doc; the legacy IDB projects row survived, and the on-load reconciler (reconcileIntoConnectedProjectSet) re-added it on next page load — same-browser and cross-device.

Fix (applied on branch bugfix/project-set-deletion-tombstones): per-key deletion tombstones on ProjectSetDocument (tombstones?: Record<key, deletedAtISO>), written by removeProjectFromSet, cleared by addProjectToSet and all re-add paths. Reconciler is now latest-wins: rows at/older than their tombstone are purged from IDB (deleteProjectByIndexDocId), newer rows are re-added. Tombstones sync with the doc, so deletions made on one browser win on every browser's reconcile.

Verified: schema 72 tests, hub-client 68 tests on affected files, both typechecks clean.

title: qmd writer: Figure node emits empty div wrapper and duplicates caption
description:
From issue #150 (item 2): The qmd writer for Figure nodes produces an empty `::: {}` div wrapper and emits the caption text after the image as a separate paragraph, duplicating it. Round-tripping qmd -> ast -> qmd -> ast produces different ASTs.

Repro:
  printf '![Webpage](image.png){.lightbox}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd
  ::: {}

  ![Webpage](image.png){.lightbox}

  Webpage

  :::

Expected: round-trip should be stable; for an Image with caption inside a Figure with no extra attrs, output should likely just be the bare image syntax (`![Webpage](image.png){.lightbox}`) since pandoc auto-wraps it in a Figure. Plan in claude-notes/plans/ to follow.

When Figure shape matches what the reader's implicit-figure rule produces (single Plain[Image] content, caption=alt, attr split between figure id and image classes/kvs), the writer now emits bare image syntax. title: verbose_to_filter directives match no first-party tracing targets
description:
The `-v` flag on `q2` and `hub` does not actually surface any first-party `tracing` events from the workspace.

`quarto_util::verbose_to_filter` emits directives like `quarto=info` / `quarto=trace`, but every first-party crate that uses `tracing` emits events under a different target prefix:

- `q2` binary (from `quarto` package): target prefix `q2::…`
- `hub` binary (from `quarto-hub` package): target prefix `hub::…`
- `quarto-core` library: target prefix `quarto_core::…`
- `quarto-preview` library: target prefix `quarto_preview::…`

`EnvFilter` matches by `::`-separated path segments. `quarto=info` only matches a target of exactly `quarto` or one starting with `quarto::`. It matches none of the above.

Empirical confirmation (commit 2b21ee60): `q2 render docs/ -vvv` shows zero per-file `Output: …` lines; `RUST_LOG=q2=info q2 render docs/` shows all 148.

Consequences:
- `-v` is effectively a no-op for first-party observability today.
- Newly added `info!` calls have no audience and may be migrated to `eprintln!` (or a workaround like `quarto_util::user_status!` introduced 2026-05-24) without anyone noticing the filter is the problem.
- `pampa`, `qmd-syntax-helper`, etc. do not install a subscriber at all — separate issue in the same family.

Fix requires design work:
1. Audit which `tracing` calls in `quarto` / `quarto-core` / `quarto-hub` / `quarto-preview` are intended for user visibility vs developer telemetry.
2. Decide structural shape: curated target list, custom `Filter` predicate over `metadata().target()`, or explicit `target: "quarto::…"` on every macro call.
3. Coordinate with the hub binary (110 call sites, different audience than the CLI).
4. Decide what `--quiet` means for `tracing` (today it's only checked at explicit call sites).

Full audit + design questions: claude-notes/research/2026-05-24-tracing-envfilter-mismatch.md

title: Hub-client: sidebar missing from website preview

2. Project not detected — render_page_in_project falls through to single-doc branch when no _quarto.yml ancestor is found (race with VFS hydration on first load?).

title: Incremental writer slices original_qmd with foreign-file offsets when preimage_in misses
description: Audit finding P2 (claude-notes/research/2026-08-09-fileid-span-integrity-audit.md). writers/incremental.rs:704-708: preimage_in(target_file_id).unwrap_or_else(|| inline_source_span(..)) then result.push_str(&original_qmd[range]) — preimage_in returns None precisely when the inline's Original belongs to a DIFFERENT file (include-spliced content), at which point the fallback supplies the foreign file's offsets and slices them out of original_qmd: wrong bytes copied into the rewritten qmd, or panic on out-of-range/char-boundary. The comment justifies the fallback for Concat/Generated sentinel-0 cases but it also catches the foreign-file case. assemble_recursed_container (:747-766) slices with no file check at all. target_file_id is guessed from the first block reporting one (:238-243). Fix: on preimage_in miss, re-serialize the inline (write_inline_to_string) instead of falling back to foreign coordinates; audit assemble_recursed_container the same way. TDD: mixed-provenance AST via include expansion, assert rewritten output.

title: q2 preview drops the TOC copy of repo actions at the default toc-location
description:
q2 render shows repo-action links twice on a page with a TOC (once at the foot of the TOC, once in the page footer); q2 preview shows them only once at the default toc-location: right.

Root cause: the preview pipeline includes repo-actions-render and footer-render, so the footer copy appears. But the TOC copy only reaches the DOM via the FULL_HTML_TEMPLATE's TOC_BLOCK_PARTIAL (rendered server-side) or its Rust twin toc_block_html (used inside sidebar-render for toc-location: left). Preview's own TOC chrome slot injects meta.rendered.navigation.toc alone and never reads rendered.navigation.toc-actions.

Fix site: ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/chromeSlots.tsx:94-103 (the TOC slot), and PreviewDocument.tsx:185 where it's wired in. The slot needs to also read/append toc-actions the way the Rust twin does for sidebar-render's toc-location: left case (which already agrees between render and preview, since the twin runs inside sidebar-render, included in preview).

Scoped out of bd-repo-actions-missing-99ezd2fe deliberately (plan said: "if the preview turns out to drop it, that is follow-up work, not a defect in this port"). Flagged in the branch's final review as M3, with the note that this repo has a /preview-parity skill and an unrecorded render/preview divergence will otherwise be rediscovered as a bug report.

title: StageError fallback arm discards the document's real SourceContext (span loss for config/include-anchored diagnostics)

The sibling Structured(pe) arm exists to pass a full context through. Fix: thread the real context (or its relevant fragment) into the fallback arm.

c-kpugxmnj.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-kpugxmnj.text: Deferred with evidence (phase A close-out): only three stage_error_with_diagnostics emitters exist — engine_execution x2 (diagnostics anchored in the engine intermediate) and parse_document (anchored at the doc's FileId(0), which the fallback arm's fresh context already renders correctly). Every config-anchored stage diagnostic uses the PipelineError::Structured path since PR #478, so the span-loss scenario this strand targets is unreachable today and a red test cannot be constructed through the real pipeline. Re-activate if a stage ever emits config-anchored diagnostics via the plain StageError arm; the Option B/C redesign (spans carrying their bindings) dissolves the issue structurally. Cheap interim if it ever fires: enrich the fallback arm's context with register_config_source over config+manifests+layers. Note: pipeline.rs:834/:1006 (success-path output contexts) are P4 positional-serialization territory, not this strand.

title: qmd writer: class values outside the .class token charset cannot round-trip
description: Follow-up from bd-heading-id-attr-duplicated-xbpcmejr (design question 3; user chose to defer). write_attr/write_code_attr in crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs always emit classes as .class shorthand, but the grammar's attribute_class token is [.][A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]* (grammar.js:582) — a class value that does not fit (e.g. starts with a digit, or contains other characters, reachable via class="..." kv promotion or via filters/JSON reader) round-trips into a parse error or a different attr. Fix mirrors the id fallback shipped with the parent strand: emit class="..." kv form when a class is not shorthand-expressible. Note pandoc splits kv class values on whitespace, so promoted classes never contain spaces; the hazard is other charset violations.

title: Engine inference: {python}/{r} cells with no engine: key silently fall back to the markdown engine (and leak a literal {python} class)
description:
Adjacent observation #1 in GH issue #523: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/523 A .qmd with {python} cells and no engine: key falls back to the markdown engine, executes nothing, and reports nothing - 'q2 render -v' prints no engine-selection or skipped-execution line. Q1 infers the jupyter engine from the presence of executable cells and runs them (verified: Q1 emits both .cell-code and the cell's stdout for the same fixture). Two defects, arguably separable: 1. No inference from cell languages. crates/quarto-core/src/engine/detection.rs:20-25 lists this under 'Future Enhancements' - the fallback is deliberate, but silent. 2. Cosmetic leak: the un-executed cell renders as 
print(...)
. A literal '{python}' CSS class is never meaningful; worth fixing independently of inference. At minimum the fallback should be loud (a warning naming the cells that were not executed and the engine: key that would run them). Whether q2 should infer, or require the explicit key and diagnose, is a product decision. Verification detail in claude-notes/plans/2026-08-14-issue-523-execute-visibility.md section 5.

c-tueqwy2m.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-tueqwy2m.text:
SCOPE NOTE (2026-08-14): the cosmetic half of this strand — the literal '{python}' CSS class — is far more common than the no-engine framing above suggests, because q2 preview hits it on a NORMAL path. Observed in a live preview session while verifying bd-nn2fou8h: whenever the capture-splice has no entry for a cell (a stale capture, an edited cell, or the bd-42202ipf mis-pairing), the cell falls through to raw source and renders as: 
#| include: false
  hidden = 1
So a user who edits a code cell in preview sees the '{python}' class — and the raw '#|' directive lines — until they re-execute. That is not an error state: preview re-execution is deliberately user-triggered (/api/preview/re-execute plus eager captures at boot, crates/quarto-preview/src/re_execute.rs), so 'stale capture, showing source' is an ordinary, expected preview state. That raises the value of fixing the class leak independently of engine inference: it is the visible spelling of a routine preview condition, not just a corner case of a document with no engine: key. The two halves of this strand can be split if inference turns out to be the slower half. Filed alongside: bd-42202ipf (splice mis-pairing), also labelled q2-preview.

title: ci-test-suite-unwired: wired-matching is whole-script and prefix-loose
description: Follow-up from the GH #250 final review. The match is script.contains(rel) || script.contains(name) over a whole step script. Two consequences, neither firing on today's tree: a step that builds one package and tests another marks both wired (the module doc's 'a build step must not count' holds at step granularity only — today's smoke check being its own step is what makes the patch-out check pass); and plain substring matching means 'ts-packages/quarto-api' would be satisfied by a step testing a future 'ts-packages/quarto-api-v2'.

title: Windows: intermediate_filename() leaks native path separator in ast_context filenames
description: engine_execution.rs intermediate_filename() (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs:492-501) builds VFS-style paths via Path::with_file_name().display(), which on Windows renders the joined filename with backslash while the leading VFS root stays forward-slash (e.g. /project\test.mock-includes.rmarkdown instead of /project/test.mock-includes.rmarkdown). Existing quarto_util::to_forward_slashes helper (crates/quarto-util/src/path.rs:23) already used elsewhere in the codebase is not applied here. Not test-only: this is a real VFS path-format bug, since downstream code may key on forward-slash paths in ast_context filenames on Windows renders. Fails 4 tests: test_engine_execution_merges_original_and_intermediate_filenames (line 1454), test_engine_execution_remaps_new_blocks_to_intermediate (line 1056), test_markdown_in_sequence_is_skipped (line 1257), and likely test_two_engines_run_in_sequence_with_handoff (line 1170, same pattern, not yet confirmed failing).
close_reason: Fixed: intermediate_filename() now wraps result in quarto_util::to_forward_slashes. RED confirmed (3 tests), fix applied, GREEN confirmed on same 4 tests. Committed a5491f57 on braid/bd-fn05e8pg-windows-path-separator, not pushed.

title: Footer/nav config markdown drops Link attributes and unwraps attributed Spans
description: A page-footer or navbar text region is parsed as markdown, but the config-inline HTML renderer loses attributes on two node kinds. A link written [link](url){#id .cls title="T"} renders as a bare link — id, classes, title and any key-value attributes are gone. An attributed span [text]{#id .cls} loses its wrapper entirely and renders as plain text. Images are the working control: ![img](p.svg){.cls style="..."} keeps every attribute. All of this happens at region level (page-footer.center) and item level (item text:) alike, in the same render where identical markdown in a document body keeps everything. Quarto 1 comparison: Q1 does not parse item-level text: as markdown at all (the literal markdown string lands in the HTML), so q2 parsing items is an improvement, not a regression. But at region level Q1 parses AND preserves both the link's id/class/title and the span with its attributes — that is the parity target. Root cause, at origin/main 87c0e21a (= v0.25.0): crates/quarto-navigation/src/render_html.rs, fn inline_to_html. The Inline::Link arm (~line 989) emits only the href and the *target* title and never reads l.attr; the Inline::Image arm directly below it shows the full id/class/kv treatment the Link arm is missing. The Inline::Span arm is explicit: '// Drop attributes for simplicity; render content.' Suggested fix: factor the Image arm's attr emission into a helper and use it from Link (target title and attr title need a precedence choice; pandoc's HTML writer emits the target title) and from a real wrapper when the span's attr is non-empty (an attr-less span can stay unwrapped). Real-world hit in the Connect docs: the footer cookie-preferences control is a link whose id (#open_preferences_center) is what the cookie-consent JS hooks on; written as markdown, the id is silently dropped and the cookie dialog dies on every page. The port currently works around it by keeping the anchor as raw ``{=html} inline HTML around markdown images (raw HTML passes through verbatim, and the images still get path-rebased since bd-page-footer-image-items-stmpikgo). Repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/footer-link-attrs-dropped/ — q2 render, then inspect _site/index.html's footer vs the body-control paragraph in the same page; quarto render --output-dir _site-q1 shows Q1's region-level behavior. README states expected vs actual. Observed on q2 0.25.0. Origin strand in the q2-connect-docs skein: br-footer-link-attrs-dropped-0ltf6v96.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #568 (merged): push_attr_html helper in quarto-navigation's render_html.rs — Links keep id/class/kv attrs (target title wins, title kv suppressed only when a target title exists), attributed Spans keep a real <span> wrapper (attr-less spans stay unwrapped), inline Code keeps its attrs, Image refactored onto the same helper. Verified end-to-end via q2 render; repro + plan at claude-notes/plans/2026-08-19-footer-link-attrs-dropped.md. Body writer's duplicate-title quirk tracked separately as bd-nkk2z7on.

c-cgrdypqk.text: Implemented on branch braid/bd-footer-link-attrs-dropped-1axx82op (commit f434e0e0). push_attr_html helper in render_html.rs; Link/Span/Code arms keep attrs (target title wins over title kv, attr-only span wrapping per design alignment with Carlos). TDD: failing tests first (3 unit + e2e), then fix; 12951 workspace tests green, full cargo xtask verify green, zero snapshot churn (verified structural — no .snap covers footer/nav HTML), e2e-verified via q2 render of the committed repro. c-qoao6a5u.author: Carlos Scheidegger

Verdict: ready to design — open questions: title precedence (target vs kv), span wrap policy (attr-only vs always), whether Code attr drop joins the fix, snapshot-churn tolerance.

title: format.html.css files are neither copied into the site nor rebased per page
description:
A project that declares stylesheets the ordinary way

  format:
    html:
      css:
        - styles.css
        - _extensions/acme/widget/widget.css

gets a <link> to each file on every rendered page, and neither file is written into the output tree — so every link 404s and the site renders with none of its project CSS. Q1 copies both (project-root css to _site/styles.css; extension css under site_libs/quarto-contrib/...) and rebases the href per page depth (../../styles.css two levels down). No diagnostic: the q2 render is clean, exit 0.

Two independent defects, either one fatal:

1. NOT COPIED — breaks even the page at the site root, so this is the primary one. Same config-declared-asset boundary that copy_favicon (crates/quarto-core/src/project/website_post_render.rs) sits on the other side of: the favicon IS copied and warns when its source is missing; format.html.css is neither copied nor warned about. The css is not folded into the theme bundle either — marker custom properties from the declared files appear nowhere in site_libs/quarto/quarto-theme-*.css.

2. NOT REBASED — identical in shape to the navbar-logo case fixed in 0.21.0 (bd-root-relative-paths-design-fc5pvkcv case A). The control is on the same page: q2 rebases the built-in stylesheet hrefs (../../site_libs/quarto/quarto-theme-*.css) and leaves the user-declared ones beside them verbatim.

Not to be confused with bd-of20unsb (contributes.formats fragment theme/css paths, fixed in 0.21.0): here the paths are in the project's own _quarto.yml; the second one merely happens to point into _extensions/.

Suggested fix direction: treat format.html.css entries as first-class project assets on the copy_favicon side of the boundary — resolve each against the project root, copy into the output tree (extension-owned files under site_libs/quarto-contrib/ as Q1 does), and emit the href through the same per-page rebasing used for the theme bundle. Warn when a declared file is missing, matching favicon behavior.

Real-world hit (Posit Connect docs port): all 352 rendered pages link two stylesheets that do not exist — 205 lines of project CSS missing from the entire site. Most visible on the landing page, whose product-panel grid loses its card layout, hover styling, and 40px icon sizing (icons render at natural size). title: quarto-ast-reconcile: structural_eq_block for tables is simplified (attr/colspec/caption only) — cells invisible to property tests
description: Discovered while investigating bd-9fwn1504. structural_eq_block for Block::Table (hash.rs:860-865) compares only attr, colspec, and caption.long, while the table hash (hash.rs:194-224) covers head/bodies/foot/cells. Consequence: reconciliation_preserves_structure_full_ast cannot detect cell-content divergence — e.g. the needs_plan cell-site bug (bd-9fwn1504 site 2) produces corrupted cell content that the property test passes. Tightening eq has blast radius: eq would become stricter than hash in places (hash covers only ColWidth discriminants, not values), making hash-equal-but-eq-unequal pairs possible; every compute-side 'hash match then eq confirm' site needs review. See claude-notes/plans/2026-07-27-reconcile-proptest-counterexample.md.

title: hub-client block-editing e2e suite red since rich-text default-on (12 specs wait for textarea, none pin richText)
description:
All 12 hub-client/e2e/q2-preview-*.spec.ts that activate an editor wait for a <textarea> (via iframe.locator('textarea')) but none pin richText. Since bd-j1nto6eq made rich-text the q2-preview/hub-client default (richText preference .default(true) in hub-client/src/services/preferences/schema.ts; commit a6f16a1e, 2026-06-24), Para/Header blocks open in the rich editor (ProseMirror), so no textarea mounts and these specs time out. bd-038tnyqy ('pin richText OFF as the textarea baseline') only pinned a subset; these 12 were missed.

Affected: q2-preview-block-nav-p2-5b, q2-preview-crumb-no-carry-expansion, q2-preview-inline-edit, q2-preview-expand-on-edit, q2-preview-item-edit-size, q2-preview-self-heal-on-write, q2-preview-breadcrumb-geometry, q2-preview-nesting-size-in, q2-preview-breadcrumb-isolation, q2-preview-nesting-caret-in, q2-preview-delete-by-emptying, q2-preview-scrolljack.

Fix: pin ?richText=0 (the textarea baseline) in each spec's addInitScript preferences (set richText:false), OR better, add a shared e2e preferences default. NOTE for bd-9x3zbuj8 Task 2 (inline breadcrumb): the 3 breadcrumb specs (geometry/isolation + nesting) test the STANDALONE floating chip; with richText ON they would now get the INLINE breadcrumb and a suppressed standalone chip, so pinning richText=0 is the correct way to keep their standalone-geometry coverage valid. Not in default 'cargo xtask verify' (test:e2e is opt-in / --e2e), so CI did not catch it. Equivalent q2-preview-spa case (edit-cell-sizing.spec.ts) was fixed under bd-n4v4phe4.

c-h0hn6ci0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-h0hn6ci0.text:
Diagnosis + fix plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-25-bd-fpys25b0-richtext-e2e-diagnosis.md

VERDICT: does NOT reproduce on main (c64e391e). All 12 specs are GREEN — verified by running them against a fresh VITE_E2E rich-text-on build (42 passed). The underlying mechanism is real (control: flipping bootstrapProjectSet's richText:false->true makes Para/Header specs time out on locator('textarea'), 8 failed), but it is ALREADY FIXED by bd-038tnyqy's chokepoint merge (commit b91d7277).

The strand premise ('bd-038tnyqy only pinned a subset; these 12 were missed') is incorrect: bd-038tnyqy pins at the single chokepoint bootstrapProjectSet that every editing spec routes through, and its merge addInitScript is registered AFTER each spec's own pref-overwrite, so it runs LAST and restores richText:false on every navigation. Plus the nesting/list specs edit list items (not in RICHTEXT_SUPPORTED_TYPES={Para,Header}) so richText can't affect them.

Real risk = latent fragility: the green state relies on an implicit registration-order invariant (bootstrap's merge must stay last-registered). bd-9x3zbuj8 is editing these specs, so Option B (shared seedE2EPreferences helper with explicit richText:false baseline) is recommended before closing.

SEPARATE GOTCHA likely hit by the other agent: this checkout's node_modules was missing tiptap/prosemirror deps (declared in ts-packages/preview-renderer/package.json, not installed) -> VITE_E2E build fails (tsc TS2307) -> stale dist served -> vacuous pass. Fix: npm install from repo root. See doc.

title: Jupyter engine: discover venv kernels and improve 'kernelspec not found' diagnostics
description:
Quarto 2's Jupyter engine cannot find kernelspecs installed in Python virtualenvs (e.g. `/Users/.../venv/share/jupyter/kernels/python3`), even when `jupyter kernelspec list` finds them. Root cause: `runtimelib::list_kernelspecs()` searches a fixed set of dirs (JUPYTER_PATH, ~/Library/Jupyter, /usr/[local/]share/jupyter) and ignores sys.prefix; the runtimelib source even has a TODO acknowledging this. Confirmed unchanged in 2.0.0 (dirs.rs is byte-identical to 1.6.0).

Strategy: fix in our fork of runtimelib (cscheid/runtimelib), patch our Cargo.toml to use the fork, validate end-to-end against the original failing fixture from a venv shell, THEN open the upstream PR. Quarto-side wraps the runtimelib error with a remediation hint.

Ordering principle: finish all Quarto-side work first to avoid upstream PR thrash if validation reveals fork-API tweaks. Phase 4 (upstream) is intentionally last and blocked by both bd-34wy and bd-ij1l.

Phases tracked as discovered-from children. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-jupyter-kernelspec-discovery-and-errors.md
Reported via render of /Users/cscheid/Desktop/daily-log/2026/05/04/convert-test-3.qmd on 2026-05-04.
close_reason: User-visible failure resolved end-to-end via Phases 1-3 (bd-maz5, bd-34wy, bd-ij1l). Original failing render of convert-test-3.qmd now succeeds; missing-kernel error renders an actionable diagnostic. Tracking the remaining upstream-PR step in bd-875x.

title: revealjs: empty unstyled code-copy button renders next to every code cell
description:
format: revealjs emits the code-copy button scaffold (CodeBlockGenerate/Render add code-with-copy + the .code-copy-button) for every code cell, but the copy feature's support is HTML-only: the .code-copy-button CSS, the Bootstrap Icons clipboard glyph (<i class=bi>), and clipboard.js (ClipboardJsStage is HTML-pipeline-only, and deliberately excluded from the WASM pipeline) are all absent in reveal. Result: a tiny empty box with the UA default button border (2px outset, ~16x6px, empty icon) next to each code cell, and it never copies. format: html shows no such box (it's styled + hover-hidden + functional).

Reproduces in all three paths (q2 render / q2 preview / hub-client) since the scaffold is emitted by the shared, format-agnostic CodeBlockGenerate transform.

Fix (scoped): force CopyMode::Off for revealjs targets in CodeBlockGenerateTransform::transform (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/code_block_generate.rs:211), gated on crate::format::is_revealjs_target(&ctx.format.target_format) — so no scaffold/button is emitted. Mirrors the is_revealjs_target gate used in compile_theme_css/assemble_reveal_scss.

Follow-up (optional feature): properly support code-copy in reveal (port the CSS + Bootstrap Icons + a clipboard-init that works in the reveal/hub-client iframe). File separately if wanted.

title: Flaky: quarto-sync-client doc-inventory test drops the binary doc under load
description:
ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/doc-inventory.test.ts, test
"getDocInventory > reports index, text, and binary docs with states and heads"
fails intermittently under full `cargo xtask verify` load (step 12/14, "hub MCP
package tests").

FAILURE
The binary doc is missing from the inventory; the text doc and index are present:

    - Expected            + Received
        [ "index", null ],
    -   [ "binary-file", "logo.png" ],
        [ "file", "main.qmd" ],

Assertion at src/doc-inventory.test.ts:140.

EVIDENCE IT IS A FLAKE, NOT A REGRESSION
- Passed in a full `cargo xtask verify` run earlier the same day (commit
  8b02c8651), then failed in the next run with ZERO TypeScript changes between
  them — the intervening work was Rust-only (engine diagnostics / source
  conversion).
- 3/3 passes when run in isolation:
  `cd ts-packages/quarto-sync-client && npx vitest run src/doc-inventory.test.ts`
- The test log is full of "Waiting for peer connection..." / "Peer connected -
  online mode", so the inventory is read against a doc set that is still
  syncing. The binary doc is plausibly the last to arrive, which is exactly the
  entry that goes missing.

HYPOTHESIS
The test reads the inventory before the binary doc has finished syncing to the
peer. Under parallel load (the full verify runs vitest alongside a heavy Rust
test suite) the window widens enough to lose the race. Needs a proper await on
the binary doc being present rather than whatever implicit settle it relies on
now — but confirm the mechanism before fixing; do not just add a sleep.

IMPACT
Makes `cargo xtask verify` non-deterministic, which is the command the repo
rules require green before any push. A developer hitting this has no signal
that it is unrelated to their change — I lost time to exactly that.

NOT MINE TO FIX: found while verifying bd-exhbc6h8 / bd-7keh8iwn, unrelated to
that work (Rust-only).
