title: Defensive percent-encoding of listing.id in L7 image marker
description:
L7's image-placeholder begin marker embeds `listing.id` unescaped between `:` separators:

`<!-- img-begin(<TOKEN>)[<attrs>]:<id>:<idx>:<href>:<b64-default> -->`

Today the schema implicitly constrains listing ids to identifier-shape (no `:`, no whitespace). If a future schema change permits richer ids, the regex (`([^:]*)`) silently mis-parses.

Defensive options:
1. Validate listing ids at parse time, rejecting `:` / whitespace.
2. Percent-encode the id segment in the marker, percent-decode at L7 substitution time.

Q1 is silent here too. File only if a real user complaint surfaces, OR if the schema gains permissive id syntax.

Filed at L7 close-out per L7 plan §D19.

title: D1: list-table defaults header-rows to 1 (not 0)
description:
## What

Change `transform_list_table_div` default for `header-rows` from 0 to 1 so a list-table with no explicit `header-rows` attribute promotes the first row to `<thead>` with `<th>` cells — matching Quarto 1 behavior.

## Where

`crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:308`

```rust
let header_rows: usize = div
    .attr
    .2
    .get("header-rows")
    .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
    .unwrap_or(0);  // <- change to 1
```

## Tests (TDD)

Add fixtures under `crates/pampa/tests/`:

1. `list_table_default_header.qmd` — bare `::: list-table`, no `header-rows` attr. Assert JSON output has `TableHead` with one row of cells.
2. `list_table_no_header_rows.qmd` — same with explicit `header-rows: 0`. Assert `TableHead` is empty.
3. `list_table_two_header_rows.qmd` — explicit `header-rows: 2`. Assert `TableHead` has 2 rows.

Run failing first, then implement, then re-run.

## Plan

title: Phase 3: code folding decoration
description:
Phase 3 of bd-1tl09 (blocked by Phase 0 skeleton; should be sequenced after Phase 1 so the composition with filename is exercised). ## Trigger `#| code-fold: true` (collapsed by default) or `#| code-fold: show` (expanded by default). Optional `#| code-summary: "Custom Label"` (default: "Code"). ## Output (HTML)
Code
…
Important composition rule (from Q1's DecoratedCodeBlock pattern): when both filename AND fold are present, the fold's
wraps OUTSIDE the filename header, like this:
Code
…
…
This means the Render transform applies the fold wrapper LAST, after filename wrapping. ## Work 1. Add fold: FoldMode { Off, Hide, Show } and summary: Option to CodeBlockDecoration. 2. Generate transform: read per-block attrs. No doc default in Q1 — keep that. 3. Render transform (HTML): emit
wrapper. Order with filename so the composition rule holds. 4. CSS: port the .code-fold rules from _quarto-rules.scss. 5. Mirror on React side. 6. Composition test: a fixture with BOTH filename and code-fold renders with the correct nesting. ## Tests - Native: single-feature snapshot (fold only). - Native: composition snapshot (fold + filename). - React: integration test for both single-feature and composed cases. - Visual: browser screenshot showing the
twirl works and the filename is visible inside it. ## Acceptance - All tests pass. - cargo xtask verify passes. - Manual: clicking the disclosure triangle reveals/hides the code, filename header included.
notes: Phase 2 (bd-j1trh) closed; Phase 3 unblocked. Read claude-notes/plans/2026-05-19-code-block-features.md §'Hand-off to next session — Phase 3 (code folding), bd-g1prx' FIRST. Key facts: (1) Render's wrap_in_place is now a single-pass cumulative wrap; just add wrap_with_fold_details as the outermost layer. (2) Q1 supports BOTH doc-default and per-block override for code-fold (different from Phase 2's doc-only mirror). (3) <details> RawBlock structuring (single vs split) needs to be cleared with user at kickoff — see plan open question. (4) SCSS is embedded via include_dir; rebuild q2 after .scss edits. (5) Pre-existing tree-sitter regression still trips xtask verify step 4/12 — use --skip-treesitter-tests --skip-treesitter-crlf-tests.

c-dyfdgmr1.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-dyfdgmr1.text:
DECISION on design question 1 (Carlos, 2026-08-14): the document-level default stays CELL-SCOPED. 'code-fold: true' in document metadata folds executed-cell code only, as in Q1. Plain (non-executable) code blocks fold only when the author adds an affirmative per-block attribute — opt-in, never swept in by the doc default. This keeps migration from Q1 behavior-preserving (no document suddenly folds its yaml/bash/scss blocks on upgrade) while still resolving quarto-cli#4693: the capability exists for every code block, the doc-level default just does not reach the plain ones. Consequence for work item 2: the Generate transform reads fold attributes from ANY CodeBlock, but applies the document default ONLY to blocks carrying 'cell-code'. Two distinct rules, not one — worth an explicit test per rule: - doc 'code-fold: true' + plain block, no attribute => NOT folded - doc 'code-fold: true' + cell code => folded - no doc default + plain block with the affirmative attribute => folded - doc 'code-fold: true' + plain block with an explicit opt-out attribute => not folded (per-block always wins) DESIGN QUESTION 2 IS NOW MOSTLY ANSWERED, and cheaply — q2 already parses the fence-attribute form on plain blocks and carries the attributes to the writer. Verified on main @3ac596e0: ```{.scss code-fold="true" code-summary="Show styles"} body { margin: 0; } ``` renders today as: 
body { margin: 0; }
So the affirmative attribute needs NO grammar or parser work — the values already reach the writer intact, and the Generate transform only has to read attributes that are already there. Note the current leak: 'code-fold' surfaces as a 'data-code-fold' attribute in the output. Phase 3 must consume and strip it (Q1's foldcode.lua does exactly this: block.attr.attributes['code-fold'] = nil, same for code-summary), otherwise folded blocks ship a redundant data- attribute. Open sub-question left for implementation: the exact spelling users are told to write. 'code-fold="true"' works today; decide whether a bare boolean form and the Q1 'show' value are also accepted, and document the blessed spelling in docs/.

c-jckm1mho.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-jckm1mho.text:
Context from GH issue #523 (2026-08-14): a third-party user hit 'code-fold: true' being inert in q2 0.20.0 and mis-read it as code-fold overriding execute: echo: false. Two data points for this phase, from a live Q1 comparison (see claude-notes/plans/2026-08-14-issue-523-execute-visibility.md):

1. Q1 does NOT fold plain (non-executable) code blocks - quarto-post/foldcode.lua returns early unless the block carries the 'cell-code' class. Verified empirically: 'code-fold: true' + a plain ```python block produces no <details> in Q1 either. Phase 3 should preserve that.
2. Q1 DOES honor a document-level default via param('code-fold') with per-block override, mapping true -> 'hide' and 'show' -> <details open>, and propagates a 'hidden' class onto the <details> when the block is hidden. That matches the 'doc-default vs per-block' open question in the plan's hand-off section - Q1's answer is 'both'.

Related: bd-nn2fou8h (the actual #523 bug - execute-visibility options ignored by both engines).

c-zswhv43a.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-zswhv43a.text:
DESIGN DIRECTION (Carlos, 2026-08-14) — SUPERSEDES point 1 of my previous comment c-jckm1mho.

That comment said Q2 should preserve Q1's restriction of folding to .cell-code blocks. That is wrong as guidance. Folding NON-EXECUTABLE code blocks is a long-standing Q1 feature request, and Q2 should aim to support code folding at a more foundational position in the pipeline rather than replicating Q1's restriction. Read c-jckm1mho's point 1 as 'here is what Q1 does today, and why', not as a target.

Upstream requests this would resolve:
- quarto-cli#4693 'code-fold for non executable code' (open since 2023-03-08, from discussion #4558): users want to fold highlighted-only blocks (scss, yaml, etc.), which Q1 cannot do because quarto-post/foldcode.lua returns early unless the block carries the 'cell-code' class.
- quarto-cli#8345 'Lua - code-folding should be part of rendering' (2024-01-18): 'we render the code-folding scaffolding too early (in layout), which makes it hard for custom renderers to do the right thing. Instead, we should be rendering that format-specific scaffolding during the rendering part of the pipeline.'
- quarto-cli#4675 'Extend the behavior of DecoratedCodeBlock' (2023-03-07) + #4660 (Confluence code folding): folding is invisible to custom formats because it happens in a specific post- filter; the ask is to make it a property of the decorated block that any writer can handle.

WHY THIS PHASE IS THE RIGHT PLACE: bd-1tl09's architecture is already the fix those three issues ask for. A format-agnostic CodeBlockGenerateTransform extracting a typed CodeBlockDecoration, plus one CodeBlockRenderTransform per format, IS 'code folding as part of rendering, visible to custom writers'. The restriction to .cell-code is an artifact of Q1's filter placement, not a requirement of the feature — so carrying it into Q2 would mean re-importing the exact limitation those issues are filed against, at the one moment we are best placed to drop it.

REVISED WORK ITEM 2: the Generate transform should read the fold attributes from ANY CodeBlock, not only .cell-code ones. Nothing else in the phase changes shape.

DESIGN QUESTIONS this opens (worth settling before implementing):
1. Doc-level default scope. Q1's param('code-fold') default currently reaches only cell code. If Q2 applies the doc default to every code block, a document with 'code-fold: true' suddenly folds its yaml/bash/scss blocks too. Is that the desired reading of a document-level 'code-fold: true', or should the doc default stay cell-scoped with plain blocks opting in per-block ('#| code-fold: true' / a fold attribute)? This is the one place where 'more foundational' could surprise users migrating from Q1, so it deserves an explicit decision rather than falling out of the implementation.
2. Attribute syntax on non-executable blocks. Cell code carries options via '#|'; a plain ```scss block has only the fence attribute form. Confirm the Generate transform reads fold config from fence attributes, and decide whether '#|'-style options are recognized in non-executable blocks at all.
3. Non-HTML formats. Keeping fold in the typed decoration (rather than as emitted HTML) is what lets other writers act on it — worth stating explicitly in the phase's acceptance criteria so a future format author finds it.
4. Interaction with hidden cells: with bd-nn2fou8h fixed, an 'echo: false' cell emits no code block at all, so there is nothing to fold. Folding and echo remain orthogonal; the 'hidden' class propagation Q1 does is only relevant under keep-hidden.

Context for how this came up: GH issue #523, claude-notes/plans/2026-08-14-issue-523-execute-visibility.md.

title: q2 preview: eager sync trigger to close edit-persistence latency + SIGINT race
description: bd-ov4gqk3m ships edit write-back relying on the 5s periodic sync + shutdown sync_all. Two gaps measured during its e2e: (1) up to ~5s latency before an edit reaches disk; (2) an edit committed shortly before Ctrl-C (observed window ~1.5s) can be lost because the WS frame has not reached the server when shutdown begins — the final sync has nothing to flush. Proposal: POST /api/preview/sync-file {path} called by the SPA after each applyEditorOperations (server runs ctx.sync_file; harmless if the WS change has not landed yet, periodic sync still backstops), plus an SPA flush on visibilitychange/pagehide. See claude-notes/plans/2026-06-10-q2-preview-edit-writeback.md §6 + Phase 3 notes.

c-2uuqa9ym.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-2uuqa9ym.text: Implemented on branch beads/bd-g4uw7d8g-q2-preview-eager-sync (3 commits). Full verify green. E2E: edit-to-disk latency now ~0.2s (was ≤5s); edit + immediate tab-hide + SIGINT no longer loses the edit (visibility flush with keepalive). Awaiting Carlos's manual e2e before push.

c-py2jb1o1.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-py2jb1o1.text:
Audit assessment 2026-07-27 (bd-a0eyjshu): NOT subsumed by main — the work is still needed.

Branch beads/bd-g4uw7d8g-q2-preview-eager-sync, 3 commits (24dfa995, 46a10c77, 19e1cb14), base a64d94d3; main is 486 commits ahead. ~573 insertions: POST /api/preview/sync-file (crates/quarto-preview/src/sync_file.rs + 181 lines of integration tests) and the SPA eager-sync scheduler in PreviewApp.tsx (300ms debounce, 1500ms no_changes retry, keepalive visibility flush).

Subsumption check: sync_file.rs is absent from main; the only 'eager' on main is an unrelated eager-CAPTURE driver. Decisive: crates/quarto-preview/src/lib.rs:343 still has sync_interval_secs: Some(5) under the comment 'Light periodic sync — the user can Ctrl-C any time'. The <=5s latency and the Ctrl-C race this strand was filed against are still main's behavior.

Merge check (git merge-tree vs main): one conflict, q2-preview-spa/src/PreviewApp.tsx, and it is SEMANTIC not textual. Main has since gained bd-jit6pdwq Phase 3: a pagehide handler that deliberately disconnects the sync socket on tab-away (PreviewApp.tsx:689). This branch adds a visibility flush that POSTs on tab-away. The ordering needs a decision — flush before disconnect, or the keepalive fetch races a socket we are intentionally tearing down.

Next step: rebase, resolve the pagehide/flush interaction, re-run the e2e (the original one measured 0.2s edit-to-disk), then PR.

title: annotated-qmd: handleConcat reconstructs the wrong string for replacement-bearing concats
description:
`SourceInfoReconstructor.toMappedString(id).value` is wrong for any Concat containing a replacement piece. `handleConcat` builds each piece as `mappedSubstring(pieceMapped, 0, length)` — the first *content-length* characters of the piece's **source** text. For an attribute value `esc="a\\*b"` that yields `"a" + "\\" + "b"` = `a\\b`, not `a*b`.

Root cause is the wire format, not the reader: a concat piece is serialized as [source_id, offset_in_concat, content_length], so the *decoded bytes of a replacement piece are never transmitted*. TypeScript cannot reconstruct them from what it is given.

Discovered during Plan 2 of the provenance epic (task D3, commit 3efcb2c48). After that commit `resolveChain` no longer depends on `handleConcat`, so **ranges are unaffected** — but `toMappedString` is public API and `block-converter.ts` uses it for table caption/head/body/foot/row/cell sources. Those are not escape-decoded today, so no current caller is hit. Latent.

Two candidate fixes: (a) put the decoded content bytes on the wire for replacement pieces; or (b) have handleConcat fall back to the piece's full source text — self-consistent with the range, still not the decoded text.

Outside all three provenance plans: those concern span/range correctness, this is string reconstruction through a wire-format gap.

c-2edupaog.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-2edupaog.text:
Re-scoped 2026-08-23 (provenance Plan 3 design review, claude-notes/research/2026-08-23-provenance-3-design-recommendations.md § 8).

The root cause is not a wire-format gap. SourceInfo — Rust and TS alike — is a map from content offsets to source; it carries neither decoded bytes nor a verbatim tag, so the decoded string is not reconstructible from provenance by design. It lives on the AST node. The wire faithfully transmits everything the Rust value holds.

Fix: let the caller supply the content — toMappedString(id, content?: string) — and build the MappedString as (content, provenance map). When content is omitted, keep today's behaviour for verbatim-only concats and route the detectable mismatch (a piece whose own source extent != its declared length) to errorHandler; a 1->1 fold is undetectable and is the documented limit.

Do NOT (a) ship decoded bytes on the wire (duplicates node text into the pool, makes the pool a second home for content) or (b) fall back to the piece's full source text (value length != content length breaks every content-offset consumer; worse than today).

No current caller is affected: block-converter.ts's six toMappedString sites read combine()-produced Concats, byte-identical by construction. Latent, P2. Stays outside the provenance epic (bd-mxa44voa); owner is the annotated-qmd source-tracking line (bd-1d6io), whose SourceInfoReconstructor contract is already in flux.

title: docs: no user-facing guide for website sidebars
description:
docs/ has no page documenting website sidebar configuration. There is nothing under docs/guides/projects/ or docs/authoring/ covering website.sidebar: — its contents:, auto:, sections, style/collapse-level knobs, or the multi-sidebar id: selection rules.

Surfaced while fixing bd-sidebar-contents-dir-shorthand-z7arvhx8: the 'contents: <directory>' shorthand is a real, Q1-compatible feature that now works, but there is nowhere in the docs to document it. The only user-facing prose touching any of this is the error pages under docs/errors/navigation/ (Q-13-1..Q-13-7), which are troubleshooting pages, not a guide.

Q-13-6.qmd was extended in that fix to explain the scalar-contents shorthand, because the warning can now fire for users who never typed 'auto:'. That is a stopgap in a troubleshooting page, not documentation of the feature.

Scope: a guide page covering website.sidebar:, wired into docs/_quarto.yml. Should cover at minimum: contents: as a list vs as a scalar (the auto: shorthand), auto: with globs vs a bare directory (the latter produces a titled section), nested sections, and how a page picks its sidebar when several are declared (site-sidebar:, the single-sidebar wildcard, containment).

Note docs/ is rendered with Quarto 2 — 'cargo run --bin q2 -- render docs/', never the system quarto binary.

title: Listing record image: uses is_external_src, so a leading / is treated as external instead of project-root
description:
A listing record's `path:` correctly uses the narrow `is_remote_src` (leading `/` = project root, per claude-notes/designs/path-resolution-model.md), but the same record's `image:` goes through `item.rs`'s `rebase_image_from_dir` → `helpers::is_external_src`, which treats a leading `/` as external. Same record, two rules for two keys.

Consequences for `image: /img/x.png` on an inline record: it is not re-anchored at the project root, and it receives no ResourceCopyIntent.

Found by the final whole-branch review of the listing inline-records work (plan claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-listing-inline-contents.md). This is a NEW consumer of the path-resolution convention, so per CLAUDE.md the scope-out is filed here rather than fixed in that branch.

title: runtimelib fork silently swallows ask_jupyter() failures during venv-aware kernel discovery
description: data_dirs_with_jupyter_paths (runtimelib fork, cscheid/runtimed, src/dirs.rs:123-127) does 'let jupyter_response = ask_jupyter().await.ok();' -- .ok() discards any failure from running the jupyter binary entirely. Confirmed concretely: on Chris's Windows machine, jupyter.exe on PATH is an orphaned pipx trampoline (C:/Users/chris/.local/bin/jupyter.exe pointing at a deleted C:/Users/chris/pipx/venvs/jupyterlab/Scripts/python.exe venv) -- running it directly exits 1 with zero output. ask_jupyter() (dirs.rs:14-30) shells Command::new('jupyter').args(['--paths','--json']) and would fail identically, but the failure vanishes at the .ok() call, silently degrading venv-aware discovery to static dirs only. Downstream, KernelspecNotFound's diagnostic (error.rs format_kernelspec_not_found) lists only the static searched dirs with zero indication that jupyter-based path augmentation was attempted and failed vs. never attempted -- so a user with jupyter genuinely absent, a user with jupyter present-but-broken (Chris's case), and a user with jupyter working but missing the requested kernel all see the identical error message, even though the fix differs completely for each. Fix direction: thread the ask_jupyter() error (or a summary of it) through so it can be surfaced as an additional diagnostic line ('note: jupyter --paths --json failed: <reason>; venv-based kernel discovery was skipped') distinct from 'no error, kernel just not found in these dirs.' This is our own fork (cscheid/runtimed, patched via root Cargo.toml [patch.crates-io]), so this is fixable without waiting on upstream.

title: Extract drain-and-flush-or-merge helper out of pass2 renderers
description: Native `render_document_to_file` (`crates/quarto-core/src/render_to_file.rs:264-297`) and WASM `RenderToHtmlRenderer.render` (`crates/quarto-core/src/project/pass2_renderer.rs:343-355`) now have parallel logic: drain Project-scope artifacts, then either flush in-place via the per-page resolver (when `lib_dir` is empty) or merge into the orchestrator's accumulator (when non-empty). Extract a shared helper to dedupe — pure code-cleanup, no behavior change. Discovered while fixing bd-87fu.
close_reason:
Done in PR #430 (commit 478f7c37) alongside bd-v8gx. All 8 CI checks green.

Added quarto-core::artifact_flush::route_drained_project_artifacts and converted all three render sites:
- render_to_file.rs:364-386 (native; the Option<&mut ArtifactStore> accumulator + shared render-wide sink)
- pass2_renderer.rs RenderToHtmlRenderer::render
- pass2_renderer.rs RenderToPreviewAstRenderer::render

The two Pass-2 sites were byte-identical before; each is now a single call. Net -68 lines in render_to_file.rs.

Design note: the helper takes a &mut OutputSink rather than a runtime, so each caller keeps its own sink lifecycle unchanged — render_to_file enqueues into the render-wide sink it shares with Page-scope writes and resource copies (flushed once), while the two Pass-2 sites construct and flush their own. That is what makes this a no-behavior-change extraction; forcing a second sink on render_to_file would have split one validated flush into two and changed write ordering.

This strand's cited line numbers had drifted (render_to_file.rs:264-297 -> 364-386; pass2_renderer.rs:343-355 -> 883-895 / 1170-1182); noted here for anyone reading the old description.

Went further than the strand asked, deliberately: the three write LOOPS were also deduped, not just the drain-and-branch logic. enqueue_artifacts moved into artifact_flush (per-fn cfg gate dropped) and flush_project_artifacts became a thin wrapper over it, so the module now has one loop behind four sink-ownership variants. See bd-v8gx for why the module move was forced rather than optional.

Tests: 4 new tests drive the new seam (accumulate / write-in-place / no-accumulator / merge-conflict diagnostic naming the input document). artifact_flush.rs coverage 98.48% region / 99.39% line.

title: Q-1-20 is double-allocated: pampa meta.rs uses it for markdown-parse failure (matches catalog); quarto-yaml-validation/error.rs uses it for StringLengthInvalid
description:
The catalog (error_catalog.json) defines Q-1-20 as 'Failed to parse metadata value as markdown' and pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs:64,76 emits with that meaning.

But quarto-yaml-validation/src/error.rs:162 also maps ValidationErrorKind::StringLengthInvalid to Q-1-20, and that variant is emitted from validator.rs:356,371 for schema minLength/maxLength violations.

Two different errors share one docs_url. The catalog is authoritative for the user-facing page, so the validation side needs a new code (probably Q-1-29) and the StringLengthInvalid → Q-1-20 mapping should be updated.

Discovered while authoring docs/errors/yaml/Q-1-20.qmd (bd-bj5yp). The page will document the catalog meaning (markdown-parse failure) for now; once this bug is fixed, the page text stays accurate.

title: Proc macro reads its input with fs::read_to_string, so cargo never rebuilds on corpus edits
description:
`include_error_table!` (crates/quarto-parse-errors/error-message-macros/src/lib.rs) read the generated table with `fs::read_to_string`. A proc macro reading a file that way leaves no trace cargo can see, so editing `crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json` did NOT mark pampa dirty. The previously embedded table kept being used, and tests ran against a table that no longer matched the corpus on disk.

This is invisible in normal work because regenerating the table usually accompanies a Rust edit somewhere in pampa or quarto-parse-errors, which forces the rebuild anyway. It shows up the moment someone edits ONLY corpus JSON, runs `scripts/build_error_table.ts`, and then runs the tests: the script's own trailing `cargo build` also does nothing, because cargo sees no changed input.

Found while mutation-testing a new corpus reconciliation test on branch braid/bd-shortcode-no-space-gspu6l5s-shortcode-no-space: removing both `guard` fields from the generated table left the test PASSING, because the stale table was still embedded. With tracking in place the same mutation fails 8 cases.

FIXED on that branch by having the macro emit `const _TABLE_SOURCE: &str = include_str!(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/", <path>));` alongside the table, which is the stable way to declare the dependency (`proc_macro::tracked_path` is unstable). Filed anyway because the fix arrived as a side effect of unrelated work and deserves its own record — and because the window during which corpus edits could have been validated against a stale table extends back to whenever the macro was written.

Audit of the same pattern elsewhere: `crates/pampa/error-message-macros/src/lib.rs` has an identical `fs::read_to_string` at line 66, but that crate (package `error-message-macros`) is an ORPHAN — nothing in the workspace depends on it; both pampa and quarto-parse-errors depend on `quarto-error-message-macros` at crates/quarto-parse-errors/error-message-macros. Worth deleting the orphan separately. No other proc macros in the workspace read files.

title: q2 preview single-file mode does not sync sibling _brand.yml (or other config) into the VFS
description: Discovered during bd-y259zb57 (reveal theme parity). 'q2 preview deck.qmd' on a bare file with no _quarto.yml ancestor uses single-file mode (bd-tnm3k), which deliberately watches/syncs ONLY the target .qmd and not siblings. So a deck with 'brand: _brand.yml' fails brand resolution in preview with 'Path not found: /project/_brand.yml'. This affects format: html brand decks identically, not just reveal. Workaround: put the deck in a project (add _quarto.yml) so quarto-hub discovery walks the dir (now includes _brand.yml after the bd-y259zb57 discovery fix). Real fix: single-file mode should also sync known project-config siblings (_brand.yml, _quarto.yml, _metadata.yml) of the target file, OR the brand path should resolve against the on-disk dir the preview server serves from. Needs a decision on how far to widen the single-file sync without violating the 'don't pull in unrelated siblings' safety property.
close_reason: Fixed: single-file q2 preview now syncs conventionally-named _brand.yml/_brand.yaml siblings into the VFS (commit 9a0da8c6). E2E verified brand applies in single-file mode. Arbitrary brand paths (e.g. ../shared/foo.yml) in single-file mode remain unsupported by design — use a project.

title: Windows: revealjs CLI tests fail — SCSS content doesn't contain layer boundary markers in themes/default.scss
description: revealjs_cli integration tests (front_matter_format_revealjs_yields_reveal_deck, explicit_to_revealjs_yields_reveal_deck in crates/quarto/tests/integration/revealjs_cli.rs) fail on Windows only. q2 render (or --to revealjs) on a temp-dir single-file qmd with format: revealjs errors: Error: SCSS content doesn't contain any layer boundary markers (/*-- scss:defaults --*/, /*-- scss:rules --*/, etc.) in themes/default.scss. That path is built in crates/quarto-sass/src/bundle.rs:387 load_reveal_theme_layer via format!("themes/{resolved}.scss") reading from REVEALJS_RESOURCES, an include_dir! embed of resources/scss/revealjs (crates/quarto-sass/src/resources.rs:68). parse_layer (crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs) is rejecting the content it read for the default theme, meaning either the embedded resource content is wrong/empty on Windows or the include_dir! path lookup for themes/default.scss is resolving to something else on Windows. Not yet reproduced manually with a built q2 binary outside cargo nextest -- next step is cargo build --bin q2 then run q2 render against a temp single-file revealjs qmd directly to see full error/backtrace, then inspect what read_str(Path::new("themes/default.scss")) actually returns on this platform.
close_reason: Confirmed green after PR #374 merge (bd-3fgnmlco CRLF fix, bd-5rl408mv href separator fix). revealjs_cli 2/2 pass on Windows checkout: front_matter_format_revealjs_yields_reveal_deck, explicit_to_revealjs_yields_reveal_deck.

c-1dwhcyt4.author: cderv
c-1dwhcyt4.text: Reorg (pending Chris confirm): PR1 (the layer.rs CRLF fix, bd-3fgnmlco) is authored ONCE in the bd-22rtwdur worktree that owns the root-cause strand; this worktree will NOT edit layer.rs to avoid collision. bd-gl0bufxp is now post-PR1 verification only: after PR1 merges, run revealjs_cli on a Windows checkout, confirm green, close. This worktree may pivot to bd-aamrec3j (output-artifact CRLF, unowned).

c-j79bxxxo.author: cderv
c-j79bxxxo.text: Root cause diagnosed under bd-22rtwdur investigation and split out as bd-3fgnmlco (now blocks this strand). It is NOT empty embedded content and NOT a wrong include_dir lookup - both hypotheses in this description are disproven. themes/default.scss is present and reads fine; the boundary markers are CRLF-terminated on a Windows checkout (autocrlf; resources/scss not covered by .gitattributes) and layer.rs:49-56 $-anchored regexes leave the trailing \r, so parse_layer returns NoBoundaryMarkers. Fix tracked in bd-3fgnmlco (layer.rs CRLF-tolerant regex + .gitattributes LF pin).

c-qbpze66y.author: cderv
c-qbpze66y.text: Manual binary repro confirmed (target/debug/q2.exe, Windows). revealjs deck (format: revealjs, no --to): q2 render errors 'SCSS content doesn't contain any layer boundary markers ... in themes/default.scss', no talk.html produced -- exactly the strand error. HTML doc (format: html, theme: flatly): renders page.html successfully but flatly primary #2c3e50 is absent from output -> silent fallback to base CSS, matching bd-22rtwdur cats 1/2. Confirms one CRLF root cause, two behaviours (revealjs hard-error vs bootstrap silent fallback).

c-s94p1s3c.author: cderv
c-s94p1s3c.text:
Root cause: parse_layer regex not CRLF-tolerant (crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs). LAYER_BOUNDARY_TEST and LAYER_BOUNDARY_LINE both anchor markers with $. Rust regex default (crlf false) treats $ as end-of-text or just-before-\n, so on CRLF the marker line is …--*/\r\n and the \r sits between --*/ and the $ position, giving no match. parse_layer also iterates content.lines(), which strips \n but keeps \r, so ^…--\*/$ fails per-line too.

Trigger on Windows: core.autocrlf=true, git ls-files --eol shows every resources/scss/** file is i/lf w/crlf (LF in index, CRLF in working tree). include_dir! bakes working-tree bytes at compile time, so a Windows-built q2 embeds CRLF SCSS. default.scss line 1 is literally /*-- scss:defaults --*/ yet is_match returns false -> SassError::NoBoundaryMarkers, the observed error.

Why the passing resource test masks it: test_theme_content_has_layer_markers uses content.contains(marker) (substring, tolerates trailing \r). Resource embeds fine; only the regex rejects it.

Feature bug, not test-only: any CRLF SCSS through parse_layer breaks -- embedded resources AND user-authored .scss (a Windows user with autocrlf writing a custom theme hits it). Scope nuance: released binaries build on Linux CI (LF) so the shipped q2 embeds LF and works for end users; this bites Windows-from-source builds (embedded) and any Windows user (user-authored scss).

Shared root cause with bd-22rtwdur (HTML/bootstrap). Same parse_layer, different handling: revealjs load_reveal_theme_layer propagates the error as a hard render failure; the bootstrap load_theme path appears to fall back to base CSS, so theme colours go silently missing (bd-22rtwdur cats 1 and 2). bd-22rtwdur cats 3 (href backslash) and 4 (highlighting) are separate path-separator issues, unrelated.

Fix direction (not yet decided): make parse_layer CRLF-tolerant (normalize \r\n->\n on read, or crlf(true)+\r? in anchors) -- covers embedded and user scss. A .gitattributes resources/scss/** text eol=lf only fixes the embed, weaker complement. Manual binary repro pending (build in progress).

title: hub-sliding-sessions-e2e.mjs still posts to the removed /auth/refresh route

title: Worktrees can poison the main target/ with dead-path build artifacts
description: Observed 2026-06-02 while running 'cargo nextest run --workspace' from the main checkout: deterministic test failures in crates I never touched (quarto-citeproc locale::tests, quarto-error-reporting::schema_drift). Root cause: ~26k objects in target/debug/deps had env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) baked to a DELETED worktree path '.worktrees/bd-3klmk-flaky-test-passoneusesmultiplethreads-asserts/...'. Cargo reused these stale binaries on fingerprint match. Tests that read files via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR (schema_drift -> 'no file on disk') or rust-embed dynamic/debug loading (locale -> silent English fallback) failed; they pass the moment the crate is recompiled, and 'cargo clean' + rebuild makes the full workspace green (9515/9515). The only way the MAIN target/ gets binaries with a worktree's CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR is if a build run from that worktree wrote into the main target/ (shared/redirected target dir or a target symlink). No CARGO_TARGET_DIR env or .cargo/config.toml target-dir is set, so the sharing was likely ad-hoc in that (now-deleted) worktree. Work: (1) determine how a worktree can end up writing into the main target/ and prevent it (git worktrees should each get their own target/ by default); (2) add a note to .claude/rules/worktrees.md warning that a shared/symlinked target across worktrees poisons the cache with dead-path artifacts, and that 'cargo clean' is the recovery; (3) consider a doctor/lint check that greps target/*/deps for paths under .worktrees/ that no longer exist. Recovery for anyone hitting this now: 'cargo clean'.

title: Selection-sync: e2e verify + docs + changelog + close
description: Real browser session vs running hub: record invocation + observed caret/selection mirroring per CLAUDE.md end-to-end policy. hub-client changelog (two-commit). Close epic. Phase 6 of bd-6dib1198.

title: Lua API: Pandoc parity for AST constructors & marshaling — mismatch catalog + conformance harness
description: Quarto 2's Lua API deviates from Pandoc's in a long tail of small ways, most of which manifest as SILENT errors in user filters (values dropped, attrs ignored, no-op returns). Catalog the mismatches systematically, build a conformance/differential testing infrastructure usable as a feedback loop, and fix iteratively — starting with AST-node constructors (pandoc.Div, pandoc.Span, pandoc.Blocks, ...) and the filter-return marshaling boundary. Where we deliberately stay stricter than Pandoc, errors must be actionable Q-coded diagnostics with source locations (qmd + filter file:line). title: Jupyter engine output not spliced into hub-client preview (knitr works)
description:
In the hub execution-provider flow, clicking Run on a jupyter document produces a capture (the CaptureRef sidecar arrives and the preview status bar correctly reads 'Showing executed output'), but the computed output is NOT spliced into the preview — the {python} cell still renders as source (e.g. '2 + 3' with no '5'). The identical flow with engine: knitr splices correctly: '1 + 1' -> '[1] 2', cat(...) -> the R version string, sum(1:10) -> '[1] 55'.

So the provider executes and writes a capture for both engines, and the consumption/splice path works for knitr — the defect is specific to how the Jupyter engine's capture output is produced and/or how CaptureSpliceStage matches/applies it. Likely in the EngineCapture post-engine markdown shape for jupyter vs the (content-hash, occurrence-index) matching the splice relies on.

Reproduce with the local Option-B harness (claude-notes/hub-execution-e2e/): hello.qmd (engine: jupyter) shows no output on Run; the added r-demo.qmd (engine: knitr) splices correctly. Browser-verified 2026-07-01 during bd-yai4w8ly.

Part of bd-sfet3264 (Phase 1 capture consumption / splice).

title: comrak-to-pandoc: NodeValue::Text offsets computed against raw sourcepos over decoded text
description:
Independent instance of the bd-mxa44voa bug class, in a decoder that strand does not mention. Found while sizing the audit for that class.

THE BUG. crates/comrak-to-pandoc/src/inline.rs:49-52, the NodeValue::Text arm:

    NodeValue::Text(text) => {
        let base_offset = ctx.start_offset(&ast.sourcepos);
        tokenize_text_with_source(text, base_offset, ctx.file_id())

tokenize_text_with_source (crates/comrak-to-pandoc/src/text.rs:90-140) then computes base_offset + byte_idx for every char_indices() position in `text`, building a per-word SourceInfo::original(file_id, start, end).

ast.sourcepos is comrak's RAW-SOURCE byte range for the node. `text` is comrak's DECODED NodeValue::Text string: CommonMark unescapes backslash escapes and resolves entity references inside text nodes. So the two are in different coordinate spaces, and every offset after the first escape in a text node is shifted by the collapse width -- one byte per backslash escape, more per entity.

Same shape as the YAML and div-attribute instances in bd-mxa44voa: a decoded string indexed against a raw span. Different decoder, different escape rules, same defect.

REACHABLE IN PRODUCTION. crates/pampa/src/readers/commonmark.rs::read() is called from crates/pampa/src/main.rs:334 under `pampa --from commonmark`. Not test-only, not feature-gated.

SCOPE. Only the Text arm does per-offset arithmetic. The other NodeValue arms (Code, Link, Emph, ...) use whole-node sourcepos_to_source_info, which involves no offset math and is safe. So the fix is local to one arm plus tokenize_text_with_source.

STATUS: confirmed by code reading, NOT yet test-verified. First step is a failing test: a CommonMark source with a backslash escape or an HTML entity inside a paragraph, asserting the resulting Str node's SourceInfo resolves to the true byte position of that word. Expect it to be off by the collapse width.

FIX DIRECTION. Same as the rest of the class: drive the run-accumulating provenance builder (to be added to quarto-source-map -- verbatim(src_range) / replacement(src_range, out_len) / finish() -> Concat) with comrak's entity/backslash rules, instead of doing base + byte_idx arithmetic. See bd-mxa44voa for the shared design.

CRASH RISK. Like every path in this class, a drift that lands inside a multi-byte character used to abort the render outright. That is now caught defensively by the char-boundary snapping in quarto-error-reporting (bd-ariadne-config-span-char-boundary-panic-rkqmhzrg), so the symptom here is a wrong span rather than a crash -- but the wrong span also feeds preimage_in, and therefore the incremental writer's verbatim-copy decision.
close_reason: Absorbed into claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-3-audit-and-fix.md (Phase 1). Plan 3 was rescoped from audit-only to audit AND fix, so the comrak NodeValue::Text instance is now that plan's content. Full diagnosis (inline.rs:49-52 raw sourcepos vs text.rs:90-140 decoded text, reachable via pampa --from commonmark) is preserved in the plan.

title: Mermaid diagrams have no rendering story for docx/pptx (Pandoc targets)
description:
Confirmed 2026-09-18 during the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic's user-facing/backward-compat review.

For a Pandoc target (docx/pptx), a ```mermaid``` code block survives to pandoc unrendered - it
appears in the output as a verbatim code block containing the mermaid source, not a diagram.

Why the "reuse Q1 Lua" trick that works for most excluded B4 transforms doesn't apply here: Q1
has NO Lua mermaid renderer at all (grepped the whole vendored filter tree; mermaid only appears
in quarto-post/ipynb.lua and modules/constants.lua as passthrough). Q1 renders mermaid in
TypeScript, in the language-handler stage (src/core/handlers/mermaid.ts), using Puppeteer to
drive headless Chromium and emit a PNG/SVG for every non-HTML target. Q2 has no equivalent
infrastructure (no headless-browser dependency at all), and Q2's own mermaid support is
explicitly HTML-only (transforms/mermaid.rs: "for HTML-family output").

**Decided (2026-09-18, Gordon):** not implementing Chromium-based diagram snapshotting is
correct for this epic - it's substantial new infrastructure, not wiring the existing
pandoc-hybrid path. Design should stay forward-compatible with adding this later (e.g. don't
architecturally preclude a future MermaidPandocRenderTransform that runs only for Pandoc(fmt)
profiles and produces a PNG/SVG the same way Q1's TS handler does) but this epic ships v1
docx/pptx with mermaid diagrams appearing as visible code-block source text, not a rendering
regression this epic needs to fix. If a user-visible warning/diagnostic on a Pandoc-target
render containing a mermaid code block is wanted before this ships, that's a much smaller ask
than the render mechanism itself - consider scoping *just* that warning into the epic
separately if desired, without waiting for this strand.

See claude-notes/designs/pandoc-hybrid-architecture.md for the epic context.

title: q2 preview: engine capture never reaches the browser pane (julia doc renders without results)
description: User repro (2026-07-02, worktree ts-engine-extensions @9e2b0bd1f, fresh WASM+SPA+binary): 'q2 preview --allow-edit example.qmd' in ~/docs/julia (julia doc, Plots violin, fig-format svg, NO daemon:false). One of those links is broken or the SPA's staleness/canonical-input check rejects the capture. Next debug steps: (1) run preview with RUST_LOG=debug and check for set_capture/sidecar errors after eager capture completes; (2) check the SPA console for onCapturesChange firing + ungzip/splice errors; (3) verify canonical input_qmd hash agreement between capture key and what the WASM computes; (4) hub-client playwright infra could automate. description: Chrome profile of hub-client on a moderately-sized document shows a large hotspot on <quarto_source_map::source_info::SourceInfo as core::cmp::PartialEq>::eq, entered from parse_qmd_to_ast (crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:757). title: Default project render regression and project-level diagnostics
description: Post-websites-merge: presence of `_quarto.yml` with `project: { type: default }` causes `q2 render` to silently produce zero output, and `q2 render index.qmd` to fail with a misleading 'excluded from render list' error. Three goals: (1) fix the discovery regression so default projects walk the tree like websites do; (2) add a clear project-level diagnostic when the render set is empty so we no longer silently no-op; (3) add a project-level diagnostic surface that both the CLI and hub-client can render, since today only file-level diagnostics flow to hub-client. title: Rich-text editor: select-all + bold commit can drop content (spurious hardBreak)
description: During end-to-end verification of bd-7pxub583 (rich-text editing of tight-list Plain items), committing a *bold* edit could lose content. Observed in q2 preview --allow-edit ?richText=1 on a tight bullet-list item: real keyboard cmd+a, cmd+b (item visibly bolded in the editor), cmd+Enter -> the on-disk item became EMPTY (e.g. '- banana' -> '-'). Instrumented capture of the commit showed the serialized ProseMirror doc was 'paragraph[hardBreak]' (text gone), so docToMarkdown correctly produced an empty string. Root cause is UPSTREAM of the serializer and Rust commit path, BOTH of which are verified correct: serializer emits 'paragraph[strong "x"]' -> '**x**' and 'paragraph[strong "x", hardBreak]' -> '**x**'; pampa apply_node_edit replaces a tight-list Plain with '**BOLD**' -> '* **BOLD**' preserving tightness (node_edit_tests.rs). The fault is that the editing/commit produced a doc whose text was replaced by a bare hardBreak. NOT Plain-specific: the RichTextEditor, astToProseMirror, and serializer are type-agnostic (Para and Plain both map to a 'paragraph' node and share the seed/edit/serialize/commit code). A synthetic reproduction on a Para also injected a spurious hardBreak, confirming the behavior is shared with the pre-existing Para path (bd-sjb4pzx8) and predates bd-7pxub583. Simple TEXT edits round-trip fine (verified 'banana' -> 'banana XX', tight preserved). Needs: a clean real-user reproduction, root-cause of the spurious hardBreak / text-drop in the tiptap doc on select-all+bold commit, and a regression test. Investigate whether it is a tiptap selection/serialization edge case or a commit-time doc snapshot issue.
close_reason: Merged in #377 (squash 4963674e). Fixed the Mod-Enter/HardBreak keymap collision that dropped selected content on commit via (A) a high-priority commit keymap + (B) disabling HardBreak's Mod-Enter. Fast unit + Playwright e2e regression tests added; cargo xtask verify + all 8 CI checks green.

(A) RichTextEditor.tsx: Esc/Mod-Enter/Enter moved into a high-priority tiptap keymap (q2CommitKeymap) via a handlers ref; racy DOM keydown listener removed (focusout-commit kept). Tests: new editorConfig.test.ts (fast jsdom, guard-verified red->green); e2e repro q2-preview-richtext-bold-content-loss.spec.ts now GREEN (bold round-trips to **banana** / **Hello world paragraph.**, no content loss) on BOTH list item and paragraph. c-l7lv37cf.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-l7lv37cf.text: RELIABLE REPRO + ROOT CAUSE confirmed. Repro: hub-client/e2e/q2-preview-richtext-bold-content-loss.spec.ts (Playwright, real keyboard). With ControlOrMeta (=Meta on mac, matching ProseMirror Mod), bolding a tight-list item drops content ('- banana' -> '-') AND bolding a paragraph deletes it entirely. Reproduces on BOTH Plain and Para -> shared type-agnostic path, pre-existing, NOT from bd-7pxub583 (confirmed). ROOT CAUSE: tiptap's HardBreak extension binds Mod-Enter -> setHardBreak() (verified in @tiptap/extension-hard-break). RichTextEditor also uses Mod-Enter for commit via a DOM addEventListener that runs AFTER ProseMirror's keymap. So Mod-Enter: (1) tiptap replaces the current selection with a hardBreak (select-all+bold leaves the text selected -> text deleted), (2) RichTextEditor's preventDefault fires too late, commits paragraph[hardBreak] -> md ''. With a collapsed cursor it only appends a harmless trailing hardBreak (why simple text edits looked fine). Earlier 'passing' runs used Control (wrong modifier on mac) so bold never fired. Fix direction: stop Mod-Enter from inserting a hardBreak (disable HardBreak's Mod-Enter binding, keep Shift-Enter; and/or move commit into tiptap's keymap so it wins deterministically). Writing plan doc next.

title: preview parity: localized UI strings not applied (callout title / theorem Proof)
description:
Fixtures: localization/lang-es-callout.qmd (render "Nota", preview "Note"), localization/lang-es-theorem.qmd (render "Demostración.", preview "Proof."). ## Evidence (lang-es-callout.qmd) render.norm.txt: ```
"Nota" ``` preview.norm.txt: ```
"Note" ``` ## Evidence (lang-es-theorem.qmd) render.norm.txt: ```

"Demostración." " Se deja como ejercicio." ``` preview.norm.txt: ```

"Proof." " Se deja como ejercicio." ``` ## Root cause React hardcodes English display strings instead of consulting the document's language table: - `ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/custom/Callout.tsx:84-90` — `DEFAULT_TITLES` is a hardcoded `Record` (`note: 'Note'`, etc.), consumed by `defaultTitle()` at line ~92 and used at line ~188 for the injected default title. - `ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/custom/Proof.tsx:112` — the no-user-title branch hardcodes the literal string `'Proof.'`. The Rust source of truth is the language term table: `resources/language/_language-es.yml:39` (`callout-note-title: "Nota"`) and `resources/language/_language-es.yml:104` (`environment-proof-title: "Demostración"`). Consumers: `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/callout_resolve.rs:69` (`use crate::language::LanguageTerms;`, localized default titles applied around line ~107) for callouts, and `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/crossref_render.rs:1012-1019` (`terms.and_then(|t| t.get("environment-proof-title")).unwrap_or("Proof")`) for the Proof label. Neither `callout-resolve` nor the Proof-labeling logic in `crossref-render` is excluded from the preview pipeline in a way that hands React a pre-localized string — React needs its own access to the resolved language terms (or the terms need to be threaded through in `plain_data`) rather than relying on hardcoded English defaults. Fix should end with `dom-parity: true` on the fixture(s). Found by the DOM parity harness (whole-corpus survey, 2026-08-24). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-preview-render-dom-parity-harness.md

description: On Windows, BrandLogoResource::with_path_relative_to (crates/quarto-brand/src/types.rs:536) joins base.join(raw) and converts via to_string_lossy(), which yields native backslash separators. Two integration tests fail as a result: logo_test::resolve_path_relative_joins_against_brand_dir and logo_test::resolve_path_preserves_alt (expected forward-slash path, got backslash-joined path). Same root-cause family as bd-picv (fixed in pampa quarto_api, PR #340): production code must emit forward slashes via quarto_util::to_forward_slashes, and Path::is_absolute() at line 538 should be quarto_util::is_rooted() per the has_root()-vs-is_absolute() convention (is_absolute() misfires on wasm32 targets). quarto-brand currently has no quarto-util dependency; needs to be added to Cargo.toml. Surfaced 2026-07-07 during Windows test-fix campaign (cargo nextest run --workspace).

title: Revealjs auto-stretch parity for crossref figures in interactive preview
description: Visual-only parity gap. In native render, auto-stretch (now Finalization-phase, after crossref-render) stretches a single-image crossref figure to section>img.r-stretch. In the WASM interactive preview (q2 preview + hub-client), the float stays a FloatRefTarget CustomNode: the Rust auto-stretch transform skips Block::Custom (count_images doesn't recurse into it) and FloatRefTarget.tsx renders a plain <figure> with no r-stretch. So a crossref figure fills the slide in render but shows at natural size in preview. (Plain non-crossref figures DO stretch in preview - they stay Block::Figure.) Recommended approach (deferred from bd-zecehtnc): make RevealAutoStretchTransform CustomNode-aware - detect single-image-slide FloatRefTarget, mark it (plain_data flag / r-stretch on inner image), and have FloatRefTarget.tsx honor the mark (render section>img.r-stretch). Single source of truth for the single-image-slide decision across both pipelines. Discovered-from bd-zecehtnc.

title: Lint: enforce that all three samod git pins stay identical
description:
Three crates pin the samod fork by git branch and must match EXACTLY, or samod (and its automerge) resolve to a second copy:

- crates/quarto-hub/Cargo.toml:50        (features tokio, axum, tungstenite)
- crates/quarto-hub-provider/Cargo.toml:19 (features tokio, tungstenite)
- crates/quarto-preview/Cargo.toml:26    (features tokio)

All three are currently version = "0.12.1", git = https://github.com/quarto-dev/samod.git, branch = access-policy.

Nothing enforces the invariant. It is documented only as a prose comment, and the comment (quarto-hub-provider lines 16-18) names TWO crates while three exist — quarto-preview was added later with its own differently-worded comment. A partial bump yields duplicate samod AND duplicate automerge, surfacing as type errors far from the cause.

Proposed: a cargo xtask lint rule (crates/xtask/src/lint/) that parses the three manifests and fails if the samod version/git/branch triple diverges. Same shape as the existing external-sources-in-macro and metadata-as-str rules.

Discovered 2026-07-27 while investigating bd-v9s8311y (samod fork rand 0.10 bump), which has to move all three pins in one commit.

title: Float/layout DOM class taxonomy for HTML figures, tables, layout panels

Today crossref_render.rs::render_float_ref_target deliberately emits native <figure> with no classes ('avoids needing a CSS class taxonomy right away', crossref_render.rs:232). This strand IS that later pass. Whether we adopt Q1's class names verbatim or a cleaner Q2 taxonomy is the central design question; Q1-verbatim maximizes CSS-port reuse. title: Heading id written as {id="..."} emits two id attributes instead of setting the identifier
description:
Pandoc's heading-attribute syntax accepts the identifier in two forms — the {#shorthand} and the key-value {id="..."} — and treats both as THE identifier. q2 handles the shorthand correctly but treats the key-value form as an ordinary attribute, so the element ends up with q2's auto-generated slug AND the author's value, both spelled id:

    ## List API keys {id="get-/v1/users/-guid-/keys"}

    pandoc      <section id="get-/v1/users/-guid-/keys" class="level2">
    Quarto 1    <section id="get-/v1/users/-guid-/keys" class="level2">
    q2 0.23.0   <section id="list-api-keys" class="section level2" id="get-/v1/users/-guid-/keys">

A duplicate attribute is an HTML parse error; the spec drops the later one, so the section is identified by the slug and the author's anchor lands only on the inner <h2>. Browsers mostly hide the damage (the fragment still finds AN element), but the document is invalid, tools disagree about which ids exist (lychee reads the later duplicate, browsers the earlier), and anything keying on the section identifier gets the slug. A {#shorthand} heading in the same document renders correctly — this is a bug in the key-value path, not a design difference about identifiers; the repro includes plain pandoc (--section-divs) as the authority.

ROOT CAUSE AREA. crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs, the with_header arm: when a heading's content ends in an Inline::Attr, the merge at ~:967-974 does `header.attr = inline_attr.attr` verbatim — the reserved `id` key stays in the key-value map (attr.2) and the identifier slot (attr.0) stays empty. Everything downstream then behaves 'correctly' on wrong input: the heading counts as unidentified so an auto slug is generated from its text, sectionization carries both, and the HTML writer emits the identifier-derived id= and the kv id= side by side. Other trailing-Attr merge sites share the verbatim pattern (~:1390, ~:1618 figure captions); spans ([]{id="x"}) currently escape visible damage only because nothing auto-assigns span ids — their identifier slot is still wrongly empty in the AST.

SUGGESTED FIX. Promote reserved keys when an attribute block is materialized into an Attr (at the single choke point where Inline::Attr's attr is built, if there is one; otherwise at the merge sites): a kv `id` moves to attr.0, kv `class` values append to attr.1, matching pandoc's attribute semantics. With the identifier slot populated, the existing auto-id path (which already keys on attr.0being empty), the include-boundary dedup pass, and the writer all do the right thing with no further changes.

REAL-WORLD HIT (Posit Connect docs port). api/index.html — the generated API reference — carries 1,364 elements with duplicate id attributes (the Q1 render of the same page: zero), and lychee --offline --include-fragments reports 159 broken fragments on the q2 side that are all this bug: at 0.23.0 it is the ENTIRE remaining fragment-level diff between the Q1 and q2 renders of the 451-page site. The generator (quarto-openapi extension, lib/markdown.ts heading()) must use the key-value form: the project sets openapi.anchor-style: path, so anchors like get-/v1/users/-guid-/keys contain slashes, which the {#...} shorthand cannot express (pandoc reads the slash as heading text; q2 hard-errors 'unexpected character or token here'). The kv form is the only syntax for these documented public deep links, and Quarto 1 honors it.

REPRO (local machine): /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/heading-id-attr-duplicated/ — `q2 render index.qmd --to html`; compare committed index-q1.html and the pandoc invocation in its README. Contains the slashy real-world anchor, a plain-word {id="plain-explicit"} (also duplicates — the slash is irrelevant), and a {#shorthand-id} control that renders correctly.

Origin strand: br-heading-id-attr-duplicated-fl8f35pp in the Connect-docs-port skein. Observed on q2 0.21.0; re-verified failing on 0.22.0, 0.23.0, and confirmed untouched at origin/main 0c3542d0 (2026-08-18).

title: Auto-generated heading ids drop quoted spans, links, math and every other unhandled inline
description:
When a heading carries no explicit `{#id}`, q2 derives one from the heading text — but the text collector handles only five inline kinds and silently discards every other one *without recursing into it*. The result is that whole words disappear from the anchor id. The heading itself renders correctly; only the id is wrong, so the failure is invisible until a deep link 404s.

## What happens vs Quarto 1

| heading source | Quarto 1 id | q2 0.20.0 id |
|---|---|---|
| `## Using a "raw" volume` | `using-a-raw-volume` | `using-a-volume` |
| `## See [the docs](https://example.com) now` | `see-the-docs-now` | `see-now` |
| `## Use ~~strike~~ here` | `use-strike-here` | `use-here` |
| `## Math $x+y$ inline` | `math-xy-inline` | `math-inline` |
| `## Small [caps]{.smallcaps} here` | `small-caps-here` | `small-here` |
| `## Use *emphasis* and **strong** and `code` here` | `use-emphasis-and-strong-and-code-here` | same (control) |

The last row is the control: emphasis, strong and code are three of the five kinds that are handled, and they survive. No diagnostic is emitted for any of the failures.

Note this is not the "does the id strip punctuation" question — Pandoc keeps the inner *text* of a quoted span or a link and strips only the markup. q2 drops the text too.

## Root-cause area

`collect_text` in crates/pampa/src/utils/autoid.rs:9, the helper behind `auto_generated_id` (autoid.rs:34):

```rust
Inline::Str(s)    => { write!(result, "{}", s.text).unwrap(); }
Inline::Space(_)  => { write!(result, " ").unwrap(); }
Inline::Emph(e)   => { collect_text(&e.content, result); }
Inline::Strong(s) => { collect_text(&s.content, result); }
Inline::Code(c)   => { write!(result, "{}", c.text).unwrap(); }
_ => {
    // Skip other inline types for ID generation
}
```

`Quoted`, `Link`, `Span`, `SmallCaps`, `Strikeout`, `Superscript`, `Subscript`, `Math`, `Underline` and `Cite` all reach the catch-all. For `## Using a "raw" volume` the collector produces `Using a  volume`; the slug filter at autoid.rs:42-57 then lowercases, drops non-alphanumerics and collapses the empty segment, giving `using-a-volume`.

Call sites:

- crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:943, in the `.with_header(...)` filter — applied only when `header.attr.0.is_empty()`, then deduplicated via `seen_ids` (`-1`, `-2`, …) at :946-952. Note the interaction: two headings that differ only inside a dropped span now collide and get `-1` suffixes they should never have had.
- crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:649, where the qmd writer compares `header.attr.0` against `auto_generated_id(&header.content)` to decide whether an explicit `{#id}` is redundant and can be omitted. The same gap makes qmd round-tripping asymmetric for these headings.

`Quoted` is created by the reader (`process_quoted`, crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/quote_helpers.rs:101), so it is already present in the tree when the header filter runs — this is not an ordering problem.

## Suggested fix direction

Give `collect_text` the same coverage `pampa::toc::inlines_to_text` already has (crates/pampa/src/toc.rs:409): recurse through every container inline (`Quoted`, `Link`, `Span`, `SmallCaps`, `Strikeout`, `Super`/`Subscript`, `Underline`, `Cite`, `Image`, `Insert`, `Highlight`), push text for `Math`, and skip only the kinds that genuinely have no textual form (`Note`, `NoteReference`, `RawInline`, `Attr`, `Delete`, `EditComment`, `Custom`). Making the match exhaustive rather than leaving a `_` arm would keep the next new inline kind from silently regressing this.

Two judgement calls for whoever picks this up:

1. Whether the quote *glyphs* should reach the collector at all. Pandoc strips them during slugification anyway, so recursing into `Quoted` content without emitting delimiters gives the right answer either way — but the two paths should be decided together with the TOC one.
2. Whether these two helpers plus the copies at crates/quarto-core/src/template.rs:1064 and crates/pampa/src/citeproc_filter.rs:935 should collapse into one shared inlines-to-plain-text function. Four hand-maintained match statements over the same enum is how this class of bug keeps reappearing; today all four disagree.

## Real-world hit in the Connect docs

`admin/getting-started/off-host-install/configure-helm-chart`, heading `Option 2: Using a “raw” NFS volume`, whose id goes from `option-2-using-a-raw-nfs-volume` (Quarto 1) to `option-2-using-a-nfs-volume`. That is the only affected heading in the corpus — no Connect page contains a heading with a link, span, strikeout or math, so the wider bug class is currently unexercised there, and no page links to that anchor internally. The exposure is external: published Q1 URLs pointing at the anchor would silently stop resolving after the port.

## Repro

/Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/heading-id-drops-inline-content/

Run `q2 render` there and compare with `quarto render --output-dir _site-q1`; then `grep -o '<section id="[^"]*"' _site/index.html` against `grep -o 'data-anchor-id="[^"]*"' _site-q1/index.html`. The two engines place the id differently (q2 on the wrapping `<section>`, Quarto 1 on the heading's `data-anchor-id`) — that is unrelated; compare the id *values*.

Observed on q2 0.20.0 (released binary; HEAD 0dcd7e83). Found while verifying br-toc-smart-quotes-pw1vkzj8 in the q2-connect-docs skein; origin strand there: br-heading-id-drops-inline-content-lxwiqh33.

## Related

bd-toc-smart-quotes-6nro57ed is the same heading failing in the TOC via `pampa::toc::inlines_to_text`, which recurses correctly but drops the quote glyphs. Worth fixing together — the disagreement between these two helpers is exactly what lets a TOC label and the anchor it targets diverge.

Also related historically: bd-ellipsis-not-smart-48bv2pe6's closing note recorded "q2's heading-id algorithm does not strip punctuation" as a deliberately unfiled low-priority finding. This is a different and more severe defect in the same function — content loss rather than a punctuation-stripping difference — so it is filed rather than folded into that note.
close_reason:
Fixed on main in commits 62773ee6 (collector + empty-id fallback) and fcdd5424 (dropNonLetter, bd-sdalit9y folded in). NOT pushed -- awaiting permission.

collect_text's match is now exhaustive over Inline; the '_' arm is gone, so a new inline kind fails to compile there instead of silently vanishing from anchor ids. Every skip is explicit and carries its reason. 'Exhaustive' deliberately is not 'recurse everywhere': Note and RawInline were already correct and stay excluded, matching Pandoc's deNote and its handling of raw inlines.

Two things the description did not predict:
- Image and Cite are affected too. Pandoc keeps image alt text and the citation as written.
- Cite needed more than recursion. Pandoc keeps a citation's SOURCE inlines as Cite.content; pampa populates content only for the author-in-text form and otherwise keeps everything in . The id is now reconstructed from prefix + id + suffix per citation when content is empty. Prefix/suffix already carry their own spacing (the second citation in '[@a; @b]' has a Space prefix), so no separator is invented. This was found by a failing test, not foreseen.

Judgement calls from the description, both settled with the user:
1. Quote glyphs do NOT reach the collector. Pandoc's deQuote emits them and the slug filter then strips them, so recursing without delimiters is byte-identical. Recorded as a constraint on any future shared helper in a comment on the Quoted arm -- the TOC wants the glyphs (bd-toc-smart-quotes-6nro57ed), an identifier does not.
2. Fixed in place rather than consolidating. bd-zzke stays deferred; a doc comment records why an identifier helper may stay separate even after consolidation (it wants math source text, no quote delimiters, no line-break semantics).

Verification:
- TDD: 20 of 30 new tests failed against the unmodified collector; the 7 controls passed throughout. The smoke-all fixture was separately checked against the pre-fix collector restored from HEAD and failed there too.
- cargo nextest run --workspace: 11872 passed.
- cargo xtask verify (full, WASM leg included): all steps passed.
- Snapshots: 0 added, 0 modified, 0 removed. No .snap.new written.
- End-to-end through the binary: 'cargo run --bin q2 -- render .' on the repro gives using-a-raw-volume / see-the-docs-now / use-strike-here / math-xy-inline / small-caps-here / use-emphasis-and-strong-and-code-here -- an exact match with Quarto 1's data-anchor-id values in the upstream _site-q1.
- Wider sweep: 37 headings across five probe files covering every inline kind plus the dedup sequences are byte-identical to pandoc 3.9.0.2 on every row.
- docs/ rendered before and after: 1250 section ids across 238 files, zero changes.

Plan and every measured table: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-13-heading-id-drops-inline-content.md and heading-id-drops-inline-content-investigation/.

Discovered and left open: bd-2wv8431v (p4) -- heading ids do not reflect shortcode expansion, a deliberate Q1 divergence noted in a comment on the Shortcode arm and pinned by test_auto_id_excludes_shortcode.

title: source-map line/column layer assumes LF
description:
The source-position line/column layer assumes LF only and counts carriage return as an ordinary column character, so on CRLF content byte offsets stay correct but line and column drift by one per CRLF line. There are THREE LF-only converters in Rust, not one: (1) crates/quarto-source-map/src/utils.rs:8 offset_to_location (scans '
' at :22 and :52); (2) crates/quarto-source-map/src/file_info.rs:85 FileInformation::offset_to_location, whose line-start table is built scanning only '
' at file_info.rs:36; (3) crates/comrak-to-pandoc/src/source_location.rs:28 SourceLocationContext::new, line-start table scanning only b'
' at :36. The hub TS converter is handled separately in bd-b1291v6g. NOTE a likely redundancy: utils.rs:8 and file_info.rs:85 are two implementations of the same offset-to-location conversion — consider consolidating to ONE CRLF-aware converter rather than fixing both in parallel. Blocked-by the column-semantics decision (bd-hn2ddyhf): once a line ending is defined as one logical unit, make the surviving converter(s) CRLF-aware. The provenance test surface is currently LF-only (zero CRLF offset assertions), so CRLF offset tests here are net-new. TDD: build CRLF source, assert line/column match the decided convention. Refs: claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-prior-art.md hub section.

title: Default table rendering parity with Quarto 1 (render + preview)
description:
## Problem

`q2 render` and `q2 preview` produce visually-bare `<table>` markup that does not match Quarto 1's output. A doc as simple as a 3-row `::: list-table` renders with no Bootstrap styling, no `<thead>`/`<th>`, no row striping, a collapsed (content-width) table, and an empty `<colgroup>`. Same behavior in both render and preview pipelines (they share the HTML writer).

## Evidence (2026-05-20)

Compared three renders of `~/Desktop/daily-log/2026/05/20/tables.qmd` in Chrome DevTools:

- Q1 (target): `<table class="caption-top table">` with proper `<thead>`, `<th>`, `tr.odd/.even`, Bootstrap CSS, `body.quarto-light`. Cells: 8.5px padding, header font-weight 700, border-bottom on header.
- Q2 render: bare `<table>`, no thead, no th, no row classes, empty `<colgroup>`, body just `fullcontent`. Browser-default cell padding (1px).
- Q2 preview: identical DOM to render; different (also minimal) CSS bundle.

Screenshots and computed-style dumps captured under `/var/folders/.../T/{q1-render,q2-render,q2-preview}.png`.

## Plan

`claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-table-default-rendering-parity.md`

Phased: markup parity (D1-D6) → render-side CSS (D7) → preview-side CSS (D8). Sub-issues to be filed under this epic as each phase is started.

title: D3: HTML writer suppresses empty <colgroup>
description:
## What

`crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:1383` emits `<colgroup>` whenever `table.colspec` is non-empty, even if every entry is `(Alignment::Default, ColWidth::Default)`. Quarto 1 / Pandoc HTML writer omits the colgroup in that case (no information to convey).

## Fix

Add a check: skip the colgroup if every colspec entry is fully default. Still emit when any alignment or width is non-default.

## Tests (TDD)

1. Snapshot: list-table with no widths/aligns → no `<colgroup>` in output.
2. Snapshot: list-table with explicit `widths: 1,2` → `<colgroup>` present with the appropriate `<col>` widths.
3. Snapshot: pipe table with `:---` alignment → `<colgroup>` present with alignment attrs.

## Plan

title: Listings: YAML-file item source (contents: items.yml) — Q1's third contents kind
description:
Q1 treats a contents: entry that resolves to a .yml/.yaml file as a list of listing-item records (array → one record per element; object → one record), each processed like an inline record but with relative path: values resolved against the YAML file's directory (website-listing-read.ts readContents @808-855). q2 has no such source: globs resolve against ProjectIndex::profiles(), a YAML file has no profile, so 'contents: items.yml' matches nothing and Q-12-19 misreports it as a pattern that matched nothing.

Deliberately scoped OUT of bd-listing-inline-contents-tyy446ze (inline records), which builds the record→item path this needs. That strand's record parser takes (map, provenance) so a YAML-file record is 'a record with a different base dir' — the parser is reusable as-is. What remains here is the non-listing plumbing:

1. Discovery: match contents: globs against the project file tree (not only profiles) to find non-document files.
2. Render-time file I/O inside the generate transform via SystemRuntime (VFS-aware for hub-client; same problem as bd-tmka custom-template loading), parse with quarto-yaml into ConfigValue.
3. Dependencies: editing items.yml must re-render the host — the dependency graph's nodes are documents, so a YAML source needs a resource-style node/edge, and q2 preview's cross-doc invalidation (bd-56b0) must watch it.

Until this lands, the inline-records strand emits a specific 'YAML-file listing contents are not yet supported' diagnostic for a literal .yml/.yaml contents: entry so users are not misled by Q-12-19. No known real-world consumer yet (the Positron site uses inline records only).

title: Audit other navigation/metadata surfaces for source-location-driven path resolution
description:
bd-qor9a applied source-location-driven path resolution to navigation surfaces (sidebar / navbar / page-footer / page-nav) — paths declared in a doc's frontmatter now resolve relative to the doc's directory, not the project root.

Other YAML positions that still treat hrefs as project-root-relative regardless of authoring location:

1. **Body links** — `[text](foo.qmd)` in markdown body. Already source-aware via `resolve_doc_relative_href` (source_relative parameter) but does not yet plug `SourceInfo` into the Q-13-4 diagnostic. Lightweight follow-up.

2. **`AutoSpec::Paths` / `AutoSpec::Path`** — sidebar `auto:` scope paths. Today treated as project-root-relative; could be source-aware.

3. **`format.html.css` / `theme` / `template` / `include-in-header` / `bibliography`** — already largely covered by `adjust_paths_to_document_dir` when authored with `!path` tags. Audit which still use bare strings in doc frontmatter.

4. **Listing `contents:` paths** — `listing.contents: foo/` could be source-aware.

5. **Crossref absolute-file references** — `{#fig-x}` references that point at sibling docs.

Scope each surface separately if non-trivial. Sub-issues are fine.

Out of scope: changing the project-root-relative interpretation of values declared in `_quarto.yml`. Those keep working because `_quarto.yml`'s hash-based FileId isn't in any document's SourceContext, so the helper degrades to today's behaviour for them — exactly what we want.

Plan: to be written when work begins.

c-c7381c7a.text: Field evidence for item (1), the full Q1 palette catalog, from porting the Posit Connect documentation (352 pages) to q2 0.23.0. No new strand filed — this is the same gap, and this strand already names both palettes involved. WHAT A PORTED PROJECT SEES The Connect docs extension (_extensions/posit-dev/posit-docs/_extension.yml) declares the ordinary Q1 pairing: format: html: highlight-style: light: github dark: arrow Both are Quarto 1 built-ins, not user files, and both are in this strand's adaptive-pair list. q2 0.23.0 warns twice and renders every page with the default palette: Warning: [Q-14-5] Unknown highlight style `highlight-style: github` does not name a highlight palette shipped with Quarto; the default palette is used instead. ℹ Available palettes: default, a11y-light, a11y-dark. The diagnostic itself is good — source span on the offending key, the available list, one warning per distinct unknown name. WHY IT MAY DESERVE MORE THAN P3 This is now the ONLY diagnostic left in the entire Connect docs render. 0.23.0 was a large step for that port: format.html.css copying, the light/dark themes, and tabsets all landed, and the render went from exiting 1 with a multi-thousand-warning flood to exiting 0 with exactly this. The full render line reads Rendered 352 of 352 files — 704 warnings and all 704 are these two config lines, counted once per page (that per-page counting is a separate, known summary issue). So the last thing standing between this port and a clean render is the palette catalog. The user-visible half is that all 352 pages render with default code colors instead of the docs' chosen light and dark ones. Not broken, but a visible regression against the Q1 site, and one an adopting team will notice immediately because code samples are most of what these pages contain. Worth stressing that nothing around the catalog is at fault. Swap the two names for a11y-light / a11y-dark in the same map and everything works: the warning clears, both variants compile, and the light and dark stylesheets carry genuinely different token colors (.hl-keyword #d91e18 vs #ffa07a). Stage 1's machinery is sound; the catalog is just short, exactly as this strand says. CONFIRMS THE TRANSLATOR IS THE RIGHT SHAPE Comparing renders of the same source shows why a .theme translator (item 1) is needed rather than shipping pandoc's files as-is. Q1 emits pandoc/skylighting's token vocabulary and q2 emits its own: Q1: def greet(name: str) … q2: def greet(name: str) … q2's is strictly finer-grained — it distinguishes function name, parameter and type where Q1 has nothing for the first two — so the Pandoc-token-to-tree-sitter-capture mapping table this strand proposes is doing real work, not a rename. REPRO /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/highlight-style-palettes/ A two-file website declaring light: github / dark: arrow over a light/dark theme pair. title: Decide: column semantics under preserve (is a line-ending one logical unit?)
description: Owns the single decision that gates the line/column layer under the preserve policy. Today three converters count carriage return as an ordinary column char, so on CRLF content byte offsets stay correct but line/column drift by one per CRLF line. The decision: is a line ending (CRLF, lone CR, or LF) ONE logical column unit that does not advance the column, or does each byte count? Key forcing input: Monaco (the hub editor) excludes the line ending from its line/column model, so if hub positions must match Monaco then the line-ending-is-one-unit answer is forced for the whole layer. This strand resolves the question once; the two implementations (Rust source-map and TS hub) consume the answer. Decision inputs to record: Monaco position semantics, comrak Sourcepos semantics (original-relative, tracks column_offset), and the LSP UTF-16 encoding the hub uses end to end. Refs: claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-prior-art.md hub + LSP sections.

c-m0bb983c.author: cderv
c-m0bb983c.text: Sharpened by 2026-06-26 probes: the failure is not 'counts CR as an ordinary column char' but that astContext.line_breaks is LF-only and omits bare CR entirely. A bare-CR doc parses as Header+Para+SoftBreak in the grammar, yet line_breaks records only the injected trailing LF, so line/column misattributes every lone-CR line. Tests should assert line_breaks includes CR/CRLF/lone-CR boundaries. See research note 2026-06-26-line-ending-gap-characterization.md.
