title: HTML comment closed with '--->' never terminates, swallowing the rest of the document
description:
WHAT HAPPENS. An HTML comment whose closing delimiter is written `--->` never terminates its HTML block. Everything from that comment to the end of the document — or to the next line containing a well-formed `-->` — is absorbed into a single raw-HTML paragraph, so no markdown in that region is parsed. Input: PARAGRAPH-AFTER ## HEADING-AFTER *emph after* q2 0.17.0:

PARAGRAPH-AFTER ## HEADING-AFTER *emph after*

Quarto 1 (and CommonMark): the comment ends on its own line; the heading is an `

`, the emphasis is an ``. CommonMark HTML block type 2 begins at ``. The string `--->` contains `-->`, so the block ends there. `` is a common house style for section-marker comments. The opening delimiter is irrelevant: `` (three dashes open, two closed) behaves correctly. Only the closing `--->` triggers it. WHY THIS HIDES. Prose inside the swallowed region still appears on the page — raw HTML passthrough emits it verbatim — so nothing looks wrong unless the region contained markdown that needed parsing. And the block does terminate at the next well-formed `-->`, so a file whose comments come in `` … `` pairs is broken in some places and fine in others. There is no diagnostic. The only signal is incidental: an include shortcode inside the swallowed region fails to expand and Q-17-4 fires. That warning's hint — "put the include shortcode in its own paragraph, surrounded by blank lines" — actively misleads here, because blank lines make no difference; the include in the repro already has them. WHERE IT LIVES. The HTML-block end condition in the block scanner, crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/ — the rule appears to require the line to end with, or to match, `-->` exactly rather than to contain it, so the extra dash in `--->` defeats it. (Not pinned to a line; the symptom is precise enough to bisect quickly from the repro.) SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION. Match CommonMark: terminate the comment block at the first line containing the substring `-->`, wherever it occurs on the line. Worth checking the same end-condition style for the other HTML block types with multi-character terminators (`?>`, `]]>`) while in there. REAL-WORLD HIT (Posit Connect docs). licenses/index.md wraps its two generated-license includes in `` / `` markers. Neither include expanded, so the entire Go and dashboard license inventories were missing from the published page, and the "Dashboard components" and "Documentation components" headings rendered as literal `##` text. That page was the last remaining Q-17-4 in the full 352-page docs render. It was originally filed on the docs side on the assumption that blank lines around the include would fix it — they do not; the docs are worked around by switching those four comments to `-->`. REPRO. /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/html-comment-triple-dash-close/ — run `q2 render` there. index.qmd closes its comment with `--->`; control.qmd is the identical document closing with `-->`. Both contain a heading, emphasis and an include after the comment, so the swallowed region is visible in the output diff. README.md has the markup side by side. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-dwy29onc (filed there as a docs bug before the q2 cause was understood). Observed with q2 0.17.0 / origin/main @ 001cb6a5.

title: Non-deterministic diagnostic output: HashMap iteration in produce_diagnostic_messages (issue #222)
description:
GitHub issue #222 (reported by @rundel): pampa emits a different second diagnostic across runs of the same binary on the same input (`printf -- 'The "_blank" word.' | cargo run --bin pampa -- --no-prune-errors`).

Root cause: crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/tree_sitter_log.rs:48 declares `processes: HashMap<usize, TreeSitterProcessLog>`. crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs:44 iterates `parse.processes.values()` and a (row, column) dedupe at lines 46-49 picks whichever GLR version's error state arrives first. Default RandomState means iteration order varies per process.

Triage: claude-notes/issue-reports/222/triage.md
Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-issue-222-deterministic-diagnostics.md

Fix scope: swap HashMap for hashlink::LinkedHashMap in tree_sitter_log.rs (one import swap + Cargo.toml dep add); add a regression test that parses the issue-222 input N times and asserts byte-identical diagnostic output across runs. LinkedHashMap matches the convention already used in pampa/src/readers/json.rs and 7 other crates in the workspace.

Branch: issue-222 (worktree at .worktrees/issue-222).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #227 (squash-merged as bed7f5ed): swapped HashMap for hashlink::LinkedHashMap in tree_sitter_log.rs to make GLR diagnostic emission deterministic. Regression test in crates/pampa/tests/test_diagnostic_determinism.rs (50 iterations, asserts byte-identical output) lands on main. Follow-up audit: bd-x5tx2.

title: Jupyter kernels leak as orphan processes from test runs (2338 accumulated)
description: Found 2026-08-10: 2338 orphaned 'Python -m ipykernel_launcher -f ~/Library/Jupyter/runtime/kernel-<uuid>.json' processes (PPID 1) plus 4932 stale kernel-*.json connection files accumulated on a dev machine. Reproduced live: a burst of 8 orphans appeared at 11:28:46-47 during concurrent 'cargo nextest run' activity (quarto-core integration compile+run in one checkout; a full --workspace run finishing in another). The quarto-core jupyter engine (crates/quarto-core/src/engine/jupyter/, incl. the execute-daemon) spawns kernels that are not shut down when the spawning process exits — they reparent to launchd and idle forever. Each kernel holds ~memory + 5 ZMQ ports. Needs: (a) identify which path leaks (daemon shutdown? test harness teardown? kernel_manager drop?), (b) ensure kernel shutdown_request + process kill on drop/exit, (c) consider a startup sweep or test-suite guard asserting no new orphans. Cleanup performed 2026-08-10: killed all orphans, deleted stale connection files.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #491 (merged to main as a217ab5a). Refcounted KernelScope ties kernel lifetime to the work that spawned it: inner scope per engine run in execute_qmd, outer scopes for q2 render/preview/provide-hub lifetimes; last scope out sends shutdown_request then kills, reaps, and removes the connection file. Also fixed the startup TOCTOU (duplicate kernel spawns under concurrent project renders) and moved sessions onto a shared long-lived ENGINE_RUNTIME, making cross-document warm-kernel reuse actually work. Regression tests: jupyter_kernel_cleanup.rs (record_capture level) + jupyter_kernel_cleanup_e2e.rs (real q2 binary, two-doc project, pins single-kernel reuse). Full workspace suite: 11273 tests, zero orphaned kernels (was ~15/run). Pre-existing rot in the ignored jupyter_integration pipeline tests split off as bd-yaccefzk.

c-1jzpdrgf.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-1jzpdrgf.text:
Root cause identified 2026-08-10 (investigation session). The leak is the global kernel daemon static, and it affects BOTH tests and production renders.

Mechanism: crates/quarto-core/src/engine/jupyter/daemon.rs holds sessions in 'static DAEMON: OnceLock<Arc<JupyterDaemon>>' (daemon.rs:330). Kernel Child processes are spawned with kill_on_drop(true) (daemon.rs:155), so cleanup depends on the Child being dropped — but Rust never drops statics at process exit, so kill_on_drop never fires, the kernel reparents to launchd (PPID 1), and the connection file (deleted in KernelSession::Drop) is left behind. No non-test code calls shutdown_all()/shutdown_session(); cleanup_idle_sessions() has ZERO callers anywhere, so the 5-minute idle reaper is dead code.

Empirical confirmation (both paths reproduced):
(1) Tests: 'cargo nextest run -p quarto-core -E "binary(integration) & test(plain_cell_error_fails_the_render)"' -> exactly 1 new PPID-1 ipykernel orphan, 6 listening sockets, connection file intact (proves Drop never ran). nextest is process-per-test, so each python-executing test leaks one kernel. The ~15/run count matches the python-executing tests without explicit shutdown: engine_error_policy (7) + engine_output_parity (7-8) + capture_splice_engines (2-3); jupyter_integration.rs tests call shutdown_session so they only leak on assert failure. During this session a concurrent workspace run elsewhere leaked exactly 15 orphans, all with cwd in nextest temp dirs — independent confirmation.
(2) Production: 'cargo run --bin q2 -- render doc.qmd' (single python cell) -> 1 orphan whose cwd is the doc dir. EVERY q2 render of a jupyter doc leaks one kernel per (kernel_name, working_dir). This explains the 2338 accumulated — it is not test-only.

Fix directions: (a) tie daemon lifetime to an owned scope (render invocation / CLI main) instead of a static, or call daemon().shutdown_all() at CLI exit + end of test-visible render helpers; (b) KernelSession::shutdown currently SIGKILLs without sending a Jupyter shutdown_request on the control channel — fine as a backstop but should be graceful-then-kill; (c) note q2 preview wants session reuse across renders, so shutdown must hook process exit/signal, not per-render, for that path. Also wire up cleanup_idle_sessions or delete it.

The leak is in this repo's test suite / jupyter engine, not environmental.

title: qmd writer does not escape '&' that forms a valid entity/numeric reference, so escaped literals re-parse as entities
description: Reader: 'x \© y' -> Str "©" (correct, backslash-escaped ampersand). Writer (escape_markdown in crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs) emits '&' unescaped, so the regenerated 'x © y' re-parses as Str "©" — AST changes across a qmd->json->qmd round trip. Verified at 7ef59618. Fix: in escape_markdown, emit '\&' when the '&' begins a sequence the grammar would lex as entity_reference or numeric_character_reference (name from the shared WHATWG table, or &#[0-9]{1,7}; / &#[xX][0-9a-fA-F]{1,6};). Becomes more relevant once the writer itself emits entities for Cf characters (bd-wuiu1of7).
close_reason: Fixed in b15868ed (branch braid/bd-wuiu1of7-zero-width-entities): escape_markdown emits \& when the & would lex as entity_reference or numeric_character_reference, sharing the reader's entity_table(). TDD: 4 writer unit tests + ampersand_escaped_entities.qmd round-trip fixture.

title: Preview eager-capture driver iterates all files (binaries, configs), causing thread panic on first binary
description:
## Symptom

```
$ q2 preview   # in a project containing any image/binary
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs:121:35:
start byte index 7748 is not a char boundary; it is inside '�' (bytes 7746..7749 of string)
```

Reproduces deterministically with the project at `docs/` (contains `quarto.png`).

## Root cause

`crates/quarto-preview/src/capture_driver.rs:55` (record_eager_captures) calls `ctx.index().get_all_files()` and iterates every entry. The index map covers *all* tracked project files: qmd, config (`_quarto.yml`), binaries (images), extension files, etc.

The doc comment on the function says: *"Walk the project's .qmd files and record engine captures for any file that has code cells but no existing sidecar entry yet."* The code does not match the comment — it never filters by file kind. Each non-qmd file is shoved through `compute_input_qmd → parse-document`. Two distinct failure modes result:

- `_quarto.yml` → parse-document errors out with "Indented code blocks are not supported". `record_one` returns `Err`, caught at line 109, logged as a WARN — visible noise but not crashing.
- `quarto.png` → tree-sitter parses binary bytes, produces parse errors, then `produce_diagnostic_messages` panics on a non-UTF-8 byte (the lossy-string offset bug tracked in the sibling issue).

The PNG path also tells us the warning-only soft-fail at L109-115 doesn't catch panics — `compute_input_qmd` runs on a tokio worker, and the panic propagates as a worker-thread panic, not an `Err`.

## Fix

Iterate `project_files().qmd_files` instead of `index.get_all_files()`. The currently-unused `_doc_id` from the index map can be looked up if needed, or dropped entirely if the downstream code doesn't need it (check `record_one` — `abs_path` and `rel_path` are the only inputs derived from the iteration item, both reconstructible from a qmd path).

Tests:
- Regression test for the eager driver: project containing both a qmd and a binary, assert no panic and no spurious WARN for the binary.
- Unit test that walks all `ProjectFiles` field combinations to confirm only `.qmd` files reach `record_one`.

End-to-end verification: `q2 preview` on a fixture project with image asset must boot cleanly with no thread panic.

## Out of scope

Defensive hardening of `error_generation.rs` so that even a bug like this one cannot panic the worker. Tracked in sibling issue (link via discovered-from once filed). With the upstream filter in place, the panic still requires bad input to even reach that function.

## Plan file

To be created at `claude-notes/plans/2026-05-19-bd-XXXX-capture-driver-qmd-filter.md` once issue ID is assigned.
close_reason: Implemented in 408f4025 (merged via c8b4ab0b). record_eager_captures now iterates project_files().qmd_files. Verified by regression test capture_driver::tests::binary_files_are_not_fed_to_parse_pipeline and end-to-end: q2 preview on docs/ boots cleanly (no thread panic, no spurious _quarto.yml WARN). Defensive hardening of error_generation.rs tracked separately as bd-6qbto.

title: WASM hub-client recompiles default Bootstrap SCSS on every keystroke
description:
After bd-imiw landed the Q1-parity default theme behavior, hub-client renders re-compile the full Bootstrap + Quarto SCSS layer on every keystroke because the new no-theme code path in CompileThemeCssStage bypasses the runtime cache (unlike the themed path), and the WASM version of compile_default_css has no in-memory cache (unlike the native version, which uses a OnceLock). Users report the editor freezing for tenths of a second after every keystroke on documents with no theme/navbar/footer.

Root cause evidence:
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/compile_theme_css.rs:175-195 — no-theme path calls compile_default() without any cache_get check.
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/compile_theme_css.rs:206-279 — themed path DOES use ctx.runtime.cache_get("sass", ...) then cache_set.
- crates/quarto-sass/src/compile.rs:55,239-276 — native compile_default_css uses DEFAULT_CSS_CACHE OnceLock.
- crates/quarto-sass/src/compile.rs:357-384 — WASM compile_default_css deliberately has no in-memory cache (comment defers to JS SassCacheManager / IndexedDB).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-18-wasm-scss-cache-regression.md
close_reason: Fixed in commit d89d1514 on feature/navigation. Four-item bundle: (1) OnceLock in WASM compile_default_css, (2) stage routes no-theme path through runtime cache, (3) generational purge on SCSS_RESOURCES_HASH mismatch (ensure_namespace_version helper), (4) per-namespace LRU size cap with 10 MB sass budget. 16 new tests, 7550 workspace tests pass, cargo xtask verify green, manually confirmed on hub-client.

title: Pampa pandoc-oracle tests hard-fail on local pandoc newer than allowlist
description: has_good_pandoc_version() in crates/pampa/tests/integration/test.rs uses substring matching against a hardcoded list (3.6-3.9) of pandoc versions. 4 tests (test_html_writer, test_json_writer, unit_test_corpus_matches_pandoc_commonmark, unit_test_corpus_matches_pandoc_markdown) assert on it directly and hard-FAIL instead of skipping when local pandoc is outside the list, rather than skip gracefully like the helper functions that call it internally. CI pins pandoc exactly via PANDOC_VERSION=3.8.3 in .github/workflows/test-suite.yml and is unaffected; only local dev machines with a newer or older pandoc are affected. Chris hit this on 2026-07-02 with pandoc 3.10 installed via scoop/winget.
design: Keep the hard-FAIL signal, it is doing its job: the allowlist in has_good_pandoc_version() is a manual verification ledger (each version in 3.6-3.9 was added by a human confirming the 4 oracle tests still pass against it, see commit 12bca3b5), not a forward-compat assumption. Converting to a graceful skip would hide the signal permanently since nextest shows early-return-plus-eprintln tests as PASS, not SKIP, and stdout for passing tests is not shown by default. That would let the ledger silently rot. CI is unaffected either way since .github/workflows/test-suite.yml pins PANDOC_VERSION=3.8.3 exactly. Fix plan: 1) Replace the fragile version_str.contains("3.x") substring matching in crates/pampa/tests/integration/test.rs with proper major.minor parsing, reusing/sharing logic with pandoc_version_at_least() in crates/xtask/src/dev_setup.rs:239 (currently only a >=3.6 floor check used for a dev-setup warning, no upper bound concept -- the two call sites currently disagree on philosophy and should share one parser). 2) Make the failure message actionable: print the detected version, the calibrated range, and the command to run to verify+bump. 3) Add a cargo xtask command (e.g. cargo xtask pandoc-check) that runs just the 4 oracle tests against the locally installed pandoc bypassing the version gate, and on green, edits the allowlist in test.rs to add the new minor version (or at minimum prints the exact line to add) so bumping is a single command instead of a remembered chore. This turns 'bitten on every local pandoc upgrade' into 'run one xtask command, it self-heals the allowlist when actually compatible, or tells you concretely what broke when not.'

title: q2 preview: converge revealjs CSS source + version with render (kill drift, keep React path)
description:
Preview renders reveal decks via RevealDeck.tsx + @revealjs/react (React components — REQUIRED: preview is a separate format whose components map back to source AST nodes for collaborative-editing AST<->source comms; this duplication is by design). But the preview reveal output DRIFTS from q2 render:

SYMPTOM 1 (grey line under slide titles): the q2-preview iframe injects the compiled HTML-theme/Bootstrap CSS (data-q2-theme <link> in entry.tsx) for ALL docs incl reveal decks; Bootstrap 'h2,.h2 { border-bottom:1px solid #dedede; padding-bottom:.5rem }' leaks onto slide headings. Render's standalone deck has only reveal CSS -> no line.

SYMPTOM 2 (no slide transitions): preview's @revealjs/react <Deck> (config transition:'slide') doesn't animate; render's Reveal.initialize({transition:'slide'}) does. (Investigate: wrapper re-mount on edit vs config vs engine build.)

ROOT (avoidable drift): render uses VENDORED resources/revealjs/ (reveal.js 6.0.0, include_str!) + Reveal.initialize; preview imports NPM reveal.js/*.css + @revealjs/react (npm reveal.js). Two CSS sources + two engine copies + shared-doc Bootstrap = drift.

FIX (user-directed, keep React path): (a) single reveal VERSION source of truth — resources/revealjs/ is copied from node_modules/reveal.js/dist (README); enforce byte-identity (xtask/test) + pin npm reveal.js exactly, so render+preview can't drift; (b) single CSS source — RevealDeck.tsx imports the VENDORED resources/revealjs/{reset,reveal,theme/white,quarto-reveal}.css (add the missing reset.css) instead of npm reveal.js/*.css, so both pipelines use identical CSS files; (c) CSS isolation — suppress the HTML-theme/Bootstrap injection for reveal decks so the deck CSS env matches render (reveal-only); (d) transitions investigation. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-10-preview-reveal-convergence.md
close_reason: Converged q2 preview reveal with render (kept React path): pinned reveal.js 6.0.0 + @revealjs/react 0.2.0 exact with a vendored↔npm byte-identity sync test (A); RevealDeck imports the vendored resources/revealjs CSS incl reset.css (B); entry.tsx suppresses the HTML-theme/Bootstrap link for reveal decks (C). One Bootstrap leak caused BOTH the grey h2 border-bottom AND the dead transitions (its prefers-reduced-motion reboot forced transition-duration .01ms!important); C fixes both (D). Browser-verified parity; full cargo xtask verify green. Commits 6c30e7db, d366924d (+ plan docs). Not pushed.

title: No callouts feature page under docs/ — callout syntax is undocumented for users
description:
There is no callouts page anywhere under docs/ ('find docs -iname *callout*' returns nothing but error pages). Callouts are referenced in passing by docs/guides/authoring/* and docs/presentations/revealjs/index.qmd, but the syntax itself -- the .callout-note/tip/warning/caution/important classes, appearance=, collapse=, icon=, and title= -- has no user-facing home.

Surfaced while implementing bd-callout-custom-title-dropped-9qi1p7iw: that work added title= attribute support and two error pages (docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-43.qmd, Q-2-44.qmd), but there was nowhere to document the feature itself, only the ways it can go wrong.

Worth covering when written:
- the five callout types and their default titles (localized via _language-*.yml)
- title= vs a leading heading, and that the attribute wins (Q-2-43 warns when both are given)
- that title= is parsed as markdown, so inline markup works: title="Use `renv`"
- the two-layer escaping gotcha: a leading # needs TWO backslashes, because attribute values are unescaped before the markdown parse (see Q-2-44.qmd)
- appearance (default/simple/minimal), collapse, icon
- crossref-able callouts (#tip-foo etc.)

Note that docs/ is rendered with Quarto 2, not Quarto 1 -- use 'cargo run --bin q2 -- render docs/'.

title: q2 render: add --json-errors for machine-readable diagnostics
description:
Add a --json-errors flag to `q2 render` so agents (Claude Code first) and other programs driving the binary can consume diagnostics (errors, warnings, info, project-level) in a structured form instead of scraping ariadne text out of stderr.

Scope (per planning conversation 2026-05-22):
- Just `q2 render` in this issue. Pampa's existing --json-errors stays as-is; harmonizing the two CLIs is out of scope.
- Emit the richer JsonDiagnostic shape from quarto-error-reporting (1-based line/col, pre-rendered ariadne snippet, source_file field) — the same wire format hub-client and the preview /api/preview/diagnostics endpoint already use.
- NDJSON on stderr (one JSON object per line). Stdout left free for a possible future RenderOutcome object (deferred).
- Exit codes unchanged. The strict pass-1 contract from bd-creo is unaffected.

Implementation TDD-driven; tests modeled on crates/pampa/tests/test_json_errors.rs. End-to-end verification (real `cargo run --bin q2` invocation, observed JSON lines recorded in the plan file) is required before close per CLAUDE.md.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-22-q2-render-json-errors.md

Related: bd-creo (strict pass-1 exit), k-lckc (uniform error-reporting in render), bd-rqba (JsonPass1Failure shape).

title: q2-preview/q2-debug: AttributionWrap inserts div.q2-attr-wrap between a block and its parent while the Authors overlay is on, breaking parent > child theme rules
description: Same defect class as bd-q2wqj24c (CommentBlock's per-block wrapper), found while investigating it (2026-09-10). framework/attribution.tsx:143 AttributionWrap wraps every attributed block in <div class=q2-attr-wrap data-sid data-attr-actor> (inline: span) so the per-actor colour applies via the cascade. While the Authors overlay is on, every theme rule keyed on a direct child (blockquote > h4, .callout-body > :first-child, li > p:last-of-type, .tab-pane > p, section > section, …) stops matching, and the article DOM diverges from q2 render. Opt-in only (the wrap is a pass-through when no attribution resolves), shared by q2-debug and q2-preview, so it was scoped out of bd-q2wqj24c. Fix direction: paint the colour on the block's host element instead of a wrapper — the same anchor mechanism bd-q2wqj24c introduces for comment chrome (a per-node host registration) can carry data-sid/data-attr-actor onto the host, with the badge overlay (useAttributionHover) already positioned from a measured rect. Inventory of affected selectors: claude-notes/plans/commentblock-wrapper-removal-investigation/theme-direct-child-rules.md. title: Q-12-23 partition drops a YAML contents: entry before glob resolution, changing what a negation-only list renders

The generate transform partitions out literal `.yml`/`.yaml` `contents:` entries (warning Q-12-23) BEFORE calling `resolve_content_globs`. Two consequences:

1. `contents: ["items.yml", "!draft.qmd"]` now leaves only a negation, so `inject_default_positive` fires and the listing goes from empty to every sibling of the host page. The new behaviour is arguably better, but it is a silent change.

title: Body images get no img-fluid class — unsized images render at intrinsic width and overflow the content column
description: q2 never puts Bootstrap's `img-fluid` class on body images, so any image without an author-supplied `width` or `height` lays out at its intrinsic pixel width. A 2680x1720 screenshot in a 850-1000px content column renders 2680px wide: it overflows the column, overruns the margin, and puts a horizontal scrollbar on the page. Quarto 1 emits `` for the same source; q2 emits `` with no class at all. This is not a missing-stylesheet problem. `.img-fluid{max-width:100%;height:auto}` is already present in q2's compiled theme (it comes in with Bootstrap), byte-identical to Q1's. Nothing else in that stylesheet constrains a figure image — the only other width rules are `.img-thumbnail`, `table.quarto-listing-table td.image img`, and `.navbar-brand img`, and there is no bare `img{max-width}` fallback. The CSS is ported; the HTML pass that applies it is missing. Root cause: q2 has no responsive-image transform. Grepping `crates/` for `img-fluid`, `fig-responsive`, or any equivalent pass finds exactly one hit, `crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_attr_source_parsing.rs`, where `.img-fluid` appears as author-written attribute input being parsed — never as a class q2 injects. Quarto 1 does it in a Pandoc filter, `src/resources/filters/quarto-post/responsive.lua:4-16`: Image = function(image) if _quarto.format.isHtmlOutput() and param('fig-responsive', false) then if not image.attr.attributes["height"] and not image.attr.attributes["data-no-responsive"] then image.attr.classes:insert("img-fluid") return image end end end `fig-responsive` defaults to `true` for HTML (`src/resources/schema/document-figures.yml:52`). Note the two deliberate exclusions: an image carrying an explicit `height`, and one marked `data-no-responsive`. Suggested fix: add an image transform for HTML output mirroring that rule — when `fig-responsive` is not `false`, append `img-fluid` to every image that has neither a `height` attribute nor `data-no-responsive`. Q1 additionally puts `figure-img` on images inside a figure; that one is cosmetic (`margin-bottom:.5rem;line-height:1`, already in the theme) but belongs to the same pass and is also absent from q2's output. Real-world hit — the Positron website (positron.posit.co docs), rendered as a 98-page site with q2 0.28.0 and compared against the Quarto 1 baseline. Counting body-content images under `images/` and excluding navbar/footer chrome: both engines emit the same 126 images; Q1 puts `img-fluid` on 125 of them and leaves 0 unconstrained, q2 puts it on 0 and leaves 63 unconstrained across 20 pages. Median intrinsic width of those 63 is 2470px; the widest are `positron-notebook-layout.png` (3404px), `action-bars.png` (3354px), `connections-pane-new-connection.png` (3144px), `download-button.png` (3116px). Worst pages: `action-bars.html` (13 images), `tutorial-ai-notebooks.html` (8), `develop-data-apps.html` (5), `tutorial-get-started-ipynb.html` (5), `tutorial-migrate-from-RStudio.html` (5). The reported symptom was the first screenshot on `welcome.qmd` (`images/astropy.png`, 2680x1720), which fills the column under Q1 and blows well past it under q2. The remaining 63 images escape only because their author wrote an explicit `width=` in the attribute block. That is why the bug hides in real corpora: about half of any given page looks fine, and only the unsized images blow out. Repro: /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/images-no-max-width/ cd /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/images-no-max-width sh check.sh # optional arg: path to the q2 binary It renders four cases with q2 and then with Quarto 1 and prints each `` tag: a plain image (Q1 `img-fluid figure-img`, q2 nothing), one with `width=450` (the near-miss that masks the bug), one with `height=100` (the case Q1 deliberately skips, so both engines agree), and one inline in a paragraph. Q1 tags 3 of 4; q2 tags 0 of 4. The fixture ships its own 2400x600 PNG. Origin: `br-images-no-max-width-00d5vc9h` in the Positron port's skein. Independently found earlier in the Posit Connect docs port and filed there as `br-images-no-max-width-bkxrudxk` (2026-08-21, q2 0.26.0); that strand measured 7 of 31 representative Connect pages overflowing at 1280px and 5 at 390px. Two unrelated corpora, same defect. Observed on q2 0.28.0 and still present at q2 HEAD (103af4445, 115 commits past the v0.28.0 tag) — no responsive-image pass has landed since. Note for whoever picks this up: the text-diff, asset-check and link-check sweeps the porting projects run are structurally blind to this. The markup is well-formed, every asset resolves, and the extracted text is identical between engines. It is visible only in a browser or by diffing class attributes.
close_reason: Shipped in q2 0.29.0. Verified downstream by re-running llms-info/repros/images-no-max-width/check.sh: img-fluid now on 3 of 4 tags, the same three Quarto 1 99.9.9 marks, and correctly withheld from the explicit-height case Q1 also skips. 0.28.0 put it on 0 of 4.

title: {{< include >}} inside a fenced code block is not expanded; fence body becomes ?include
description:
WHAT HAPPENS. An `include` shortcode standing alone inside a fenced code block — the standard Q1 idiom for embedding a source file as a listing — ```{.python filename="app.py"} {{< include app.py >}} ``` renders with the entire fence body replaced by the single token `?include`: 
?include
Quarto 1 splices the included file's raw text into the fence and the listing renders as a syntax-highlighted copy of `app.py`. A Q-17-4 "Include not expanded" warning does fire, so this is not silent — but its hint, "Put the include shortcode in its own paragraph, surrounded by blank lines", is actively wrong here: the shortcode belongs inside the fence, and following the hint would change what the page means. ROOT CAUSE — two halves, and the second is the interesting one. 1. `IncludeExpansionStage` (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/include_expansion.rs) expands includes at block-list positions only. `extract_include_path` matches `Block::Paragraph` / `Block::Plain` whose sole inline is the shortcode, and `child_block_lists_mut` enumerates the containers it descends into — Div, BlockQuote, list items, DefinitionList, Figure, NoteDefinitionFencedBlock, Table cells. A `CodeBlock` has no child block list (its content is a `String`), so it is unreachable by construction. There is an explicit test pinning today's behavior, `extract_include_path_from_non_paragraph`, which asserts a CodeBlock yields `None`; any fix has to revisit it. 2. The `?include` token comes from somewhere else, and it is where the fix most naturally belongs. Since bd-fz6gwfq0 / the 0.16.0 text-level work, `ShortcodeResolveTransform` substitutes shortcodes textually inside code and raw text — crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/shortcode_resolve.rs, the `Block::CodeBlock(code_block)` arm around line 1851, calling `expand_text_in_place` unless `code_shortcode_opt_out` fires (`.cell-code` or `shortcodes="false"`). That pass parses the fence text, finds the include shortcode, and dispatches it. `dispatch_shortcode` has no `include` handler by design (see its comment: includes are meant to be gone by then), so it takes the `shortcode.name == "include"` branch, returns `ShortcodeResult::Error`, and `expand_text_segments` writes `'?'` followed by the shortcode name — hence `?include` in place of the whole body. So the mechanism that already makes `{{< meta … >}}` work inside a fence is the same mechanism that eats the include, and it is operating on exactly the right data: raw text. SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION. Handle `include` in the text-expansion path — read the target file and splice its bytes verbatim into the code text, no parsing, no re-indentation (Q1 performs none either). This is the one context where Q1's textual model is the correct model rather than a legacy quirk, because the destination is raw text and not a block list, so none of the fence-corruption hazards that motivated the AST approach apply. Things to settle while doing it: - Path resolution must match `resolve_include_target(base_dir, project_dir, raw)` in include_expansion.rs — relative to the declaring file's directory, leading `/` meaning project root. - Dependency tracking: `collect_include_paths` and `record_include` feed the `IncludeEntry` list and the preview dependency graph (quarto-preview/src/deps.rs::extract_include_deps reuses `extract_include_path`). A code-fence include must register there too, or editing `app.py` will not rebuild the page that embeds it. Easy to miss. - Recursion and cycles: Q1 re-scans included text textually with a path stack. Simplest defensible v1 is no recursion inside a code fence — a file included into a fence is code, not qmd — but it should be a decision, not an accident. - `code_shortcode_opt_out` must keep winning: `.cell-code` and `shortcodes="false"` still opt out. - Q-17-4 then stops firing for this shape. If it is kept for any code-adjacent position, its hint needs a variant that does not tell the author to move the shortcode out of the fence. An alternative worth weighing and rejecting explicitly: a fence attribute (```` ```{.python include="app.py"} ````) or a dedicated `embed-file` shortcode. Cleaner in isolation, but it makes every existing Q1 document wrong and needs a qmd-syntax-helper migration rule to fix them, whereas supporting the existing spelling costs those documents nothing. It could still be added later as an additional affordance. REAL-WORLD HIT (Posit Connect docs). 21 files, roughly 44 listings, ~1300 lines of embedded source — the single largest remaining content loss in the port. Every cookbook integration recipe embeds its `requirements.txt`, `app.py`, `app.R` or `manifest.json` this way, so the recipes lose the code they exist to show: cookbook/content/integrations/{aws,databricks,github,google,msgraph,palantir,salesforce,sharepoint,snowflake}/**/index.qmd plus cookbook/metrics/*. The worst is cookbook/content/integrations/databricks/viewer/python/index.qmd, which has ten such listings across five framework tabs and now shows `?include` in all ten. A different, docs-fixable shape hits the same Q-17-4: an include placed directly under an HTML comment with no blank line gets swallowed into a raw-HTML block. There the existing hint is exactly right, and the fix is in the document, not here. REPRO. /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/include-in-code-block/ — run 'q2 render' there and compare with 'quarto render'. index.qmd has the code-fence include plus a top-level include as a control (the control works in both engines); app.py is the three-line include target; README.md carries expected vs actual markup and the analysis above. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-4kslym5r. Observed with q2 0.16.0; re-verified against origin/main @ b2b6100c (v0.16.0 plus docs commits), where include expansion is unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #498 (merge 0bc0b657). Includes standing alone on a line inside a fenced code block now splice the target's text into the listing, expanded in IncludeExpansionStage (stage 3) so the target is registered as a dependency before the DocumentProfile checkpoint. Line-strict recognition and no re-indentation match Q1; recursion matches Q1 with canonicalized cycle detection; one trailing newline is trimmed because q2 has no Pandoc markdown re-read to absorb it. shortcodes="false" still opts out. Unhandled includes in code text are now preserved verbatim instead of rendering as ?include. All CI green. Connect-docs corpus: 44 fence includes across 20 files, 352/352 rendered, corpus-wide ?include down to 1 — a raw-HTML shape the strand itself calls docs-fixable. Docs follow-up tracked as bd-cq0xhxg5.

c-704h6dj0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-704h6dj0.text:
Implementation on branch braid/include-in-code-block-f8mvtczn.

Two more design points surfaced during implementation and were settled:

D3 REVERSED (user decision): recursion is ON, matching Q1. 'No recursion' was not implementable as specified — the spliced text still contained {{< include inner.qmd >}}, which ShortcodeResolveTransform turned into ?include one level down, plus a Q-17-4 pointing at a fence the author never wrote an include in. Recursing removes the shortcode before that transform runs. Cycle detection via the existing canonicalized include_stack + Q-17-1. Nested paths anchor at the including file's directory (matching bd-1fz3vh99), NOT at the document as Q1 does — confirmed empirically: Q1 fatally errors on sub/outer.qmd including a sibling, because it resolves against the document dir.

D3b (new): a mid-line include in a fence is deliberately not recognized (line-strict, D2) but the leftover shortcode also produced ?include. Q1 renders it untouched and silently. Fixed by giving expand_text_segments an UnhandledInclude mode; the two code text contexts (Block::CodeBlock, Inline::Code) pass Preserve, which emits the shortcode's source text and suppresses the diagnostic. All other text contexts keep Report. Keys off the dispatch result rather than the name, so a Lua handler named 'include' still wins.

D4a (new, minor divergence): two includes in one fence render as AAA\nBBB for us, AAA\n\nBBB for Q1. Q1's blank line is the same standaloneInclude artifact D4 documents; applying D4's principle uniformly means no separator.

Widened Q1 comparison now matches on: single include, indented include, mid-line non-expansion. Differs on: consecutive-include spacing (D4a), nested-path anchor (D3).

Tests: 19 unit + 8 full-pipeline integration + 1 smoke-all fixture (includes/in-code-fence). Updated 3 preview dep tests that pinned the old 'fence include is not a dep' contract, and docs/errors/include/Q-17-4.qmd. End-to-end verified through 'q2 render' on the strand's repro: three highlighted lines, no ?include, no warning, data-filename preserved.

c-p266djfv.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-p266djfv.text: Design settled with user (commit 92adde4f). D1 fix site = IncludeExpansionStage (agreed). D2 recognition = line-strict. D3 no recursion inside a fence. D5 accept splice-before-execution for authored cells. D6 Q-17-4 unchanged (stops firing by construction). D7 fence-attribute / embed-file alternatives rejected. Two findings from reading external-sources/quarto-cli @ abc6a78ed that correct the strand's framing: 1. Q1 is NOT textually permissive inside code. processMarkdownIncludes splits each cell into lines and tests each with isBlockShortcode, whose regex /^\s*{{< (?!\/\*)(.+?)(?}}\s*$/ is anchored to the whole line. So the strict rule we chose is Q1 parity, not a divergence. Q1 also allows a leading-indented include line and does not re-indent. 2. Q1 DOES recurse into files included inside a fence — standaloneInclude/retrieveInclude is the same code path for both positions and re-scans included text. So D3 is a deliberate divergence, observable when a .qmd is included into a fence to show its source. Filed bd-cq0xhxg5 to document it. D4 (trailing newline) still open, recommendation reverses the initial lean toward verbatim. Q1's source appends a newline (standaloneInclude pushes '\n' or '\n\n'), but a real 'quarto render' of the repro emits exactly 3 highlighted lines with no trailing blank — Pandoc's markdown reader normalizes it away. q2 has no such re-read: the qmd parser yields CodeBlock.text WITHOUT a trailing newline for a content-final fence line, and html.rs:1478 emits escape_html(text) verbatim (measured: 'os\n' vs 'os'). Since nearly all source files end with a newline, a verbatim splice would add a spurious blank final line to essentially every listing, breaking parity for the whole ~44-listing Connect-docs corpus. Recommend trimming exactly one trailing newline; users can still force a blank line by ending the file with two. Also noted, not to be copied: Q1's cycle detection checks the resolved path but pushes the raw filename, and its shortcodes=false opt-out regex only matches a fence whose attributes are exactly {shortcodes=false}. Our equivalents are already correct.

c-verqtdya.text: PR opened: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/498 (branch bugfix/include-in-code-block-f8mvtczn, commit c39cb4d0). Monitoring CI; will merge and close this strand if green.

c-y1iw0z68.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-y1iw0z68.text:
Investigated on main @ bcdbce6b. Reproduces byte-for-byte at HEAD. Plan skeleton at claude-notes/plans/2026-08-10-include-in-code-block.md (commit ec572c46), self-contained repro at claude-notes/plans/include-in-code-block-investigation/.

Key finding that revises the suggested fix direction: ShortcodeResolveTransform runs in AstTransformsStage (pipeline stage 13), which is AFTER DocumentProfileStage (stage 6) drains the include side-channel into DocumentProfile.includes. Since profiles are read-only, a fix at the transform site cannot satisfy the strand's own dependency-tracking requirement. IncludeExpansionStage (stage 3) already holds ctx.runtime, base_dir, project_dir, recorded_includes and the cycle stack, and parse_text_shortcodes is pub and reusable there — so the same textual splice can happen early and Q-17-4 then stops firing naturally, preserving the documented 'includes are gone before transforms run' invariant.

Secondary finding: code_shortcode_opt_out's .cell-code half is engine-produced (jupyter text_execute.rs, runs after stage 3), so it is not visible at include-expansion time; shortcodes="false" is authored and is. Needs a decision, not an accident.

7 design questions await user input before implementation.

title: include-in-header text: holding block markdown is dropped, and Q-5-5 blames the entry form
description:
WHAT HAPPENS. A `text:` value under `include-in-header` (or `include-before-body` / `include-after-body`) whose markdown parses to *blocks* rather than inlines is silently discarded, and the diagnostic that fires blames the entry's shape instead.

Four spellings of the same intent — put a `<style>` block in the document head:

  text: | + ```{=html} fenced block   →  Q-5-5 "Invalid include form", content DROPPED
  text: | + two HTML paragraphs       →  Q-5-5 "Invalid include form", content DROPPED
  text: | + bare <style>…</style>     →  Q-1-20 "Failed to parse metadata value as markdown", content reaches <head>
  text: | + inline `…`{=html} span    →  silent, content reaches <head>

The message reads:

    Warning: [Q-5-5] Invalid include form
     10 │ ╭─▶   text: |
     17 │ ├─▶     ```
        │ ╰───── `include-in-header` entry must be a string path, `{file: <path>}`, or `{text: <literal>}`

The entry *is* `{text: <literal>}`. The message lists three accepted forms, one of which the author demonstrably used, and its span covers the whole YAML entry rather than the value it objected to. Nothing in it suggests the actual rule — that the value has to be inline content.

WHERE IT LIVES. crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/include_resolve.rs.

`literal_html_text` (~line 339) accepts four ConfigValueKinds:

    K::Scalar(Yaml::String(s)) => Some(s.clone()),
    K::Path(s) | K::Glob(s) | K::Expr(s) => Some(s.clone()),
    K::PandocInlines(inlines) => Some(inlines_to_html_literal(inlines)),
    _ => None,

`PandocBlocks` falls into that `_`. The caller (~line 442) routes `None` straight into `push_invalid_form_warning`:

    if let Some(text) = literal_html_text(text_value) {
        out.push(text);
    } else {
        push_invalid_form_warning(diagnostics, key, value);   // Q-5-5
    }

so a single branch serves two unrelated failures: "you didn't use one of the three accepted forms" and "you used the right form but the value parsed to blocks".

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION. Two independent changes; the first is the ask, the second is a judgment call for whoever owns this area.

1. Split the diagnostic. When `text:` is present but not literal-able, say that specifically: name block-level content as the cause, point the span at the value rather than the whole entry, and suggest the inline `` `…`{=html} `` form (or `file:`). Reserve Q-5-5 for entries that genuinely match no accepted form.

2. Consider accepting blocks. A RawBlock of HTML is precisely what include-in-header wants, and a fenced ```{=html} block is the natural way to author a multi-line <style> or <script>. A `K::PandocBlocks` arm mirroring `inlines_to_html_literal` — emitting RawBlock text and recursing into block containers — would make the natural spelling work. Worth weighing: the current working spelling is a single inline code span wrapped around five lines of CSS, which is not something an author arrives at unaided.

NOT A QUARTO 1 PARITY BUG. Quarto 1 drops the fenced form too, and drops it silently — no warning at all. q2 is already ahead in saying anything; the complaint is that what it says points away from the cause, and that the natural spelling works in neither engine.

REAL-WORLD HIT (Posit Connect docs). news/index.md hides its title-block metadata with a `<style>` block in include-in-header.text. Written bare it works but warns Q-1-20, and it is the last remaining Q-1-20 in the whole 352-page render. Wrapping it in a ```{=html} fence to clear that warning trades one warning for another *and* silently drops the style, so the page loses the styling it was asking for. The docs now use the inline-span form — silent and correct, but it reads badly.

REPRO. /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/include-in-header-text-blocks/ — run `q2 render` there. Four documents, one per spelling, each injecting a distinctly-named marker so `grep marker- _site/<file>.html` shows whether the content survived. README.md has the table above, the source pointers, and the Q1 comparison. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path.

Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-td1695mc. Observed with q2 0.17.0 / origin/main @ 001cb6a5.
close_reason: Fixed in e252d3b5 (main, unpushed): literal_html_text accepts PandocBlocks via blocks_to_html_literal; fenced {=html} and multi-paragraph text: values now reach the slot, Q-5-5 no longer fires for text: entries. Code collision follow-up: bd-x9ujtvnt. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-include-in-header-text-blocks.md

c-vnoune61.text: Investigated 2026-08-20: plan skeleton at claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-include-in-header-text-blocks.md; repro reproduces at main@87c0e21a. Additional finding: Q-5-4/Q-5-5 are double-booked between include_resolve.rs and example_embed.rs; catalog documents only the embed meaning.

title: A failed include is dropped but the page is still written, with the included content silently missing
description:
When an {{< include >}} cannot be expanded, IncludeExpansion removes the block
from the AST and the render continues. The page is written to disk missing the
content the include was supposed to supply, and counts toward "Rendered N of M".
Quarto 1 never produces such a page: a broken include aborts the project render
and no output is written at all.

The clearest way to see this is a defect rather than a policy is q2's own
behaviour on the *same* parse error placed inline instead of in an included
file:

  index.qmd   includes _broken.qmd, which has a Q-2-11 unclosed double quote
              -> HTML written, included content missing
  direct.qmd  the identical Q-2-11 inline on the page
              -> no HTML written, document aborted
  good.qmd    includes a file that parses
              -> HTML written, content present
  missing.qmd includes a file that does not exist
              -> HTML written, included content missing

Same diagnostic, same severity; opposite outcome depending only on which file
it lives in. q2 summarises that project as "Rendered 3 of 4 files — 3 errors,
1 warning", exit 1, with index.qmd counted among the three successes.

The missing-file case is the more alarming half. A nonexistent include target
is only a warning (Q-17-2), so a project containing just that page renders
exit 0 with no errors at all — a page that quietly lost its main content and
reports nothing wrong.

ROOT CAUSE

crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/include_expansion.rs. All three failure
arms end the same way:

    // See the circular-include arm for why the block is
    // removed rather than skipped.
    blocks.remove(i);
    continue;

circular include (Q-17-1, warning, line 231), file not found or unreadable
(Q-17-2, warning, line 254), parse failure (Q-17-3, error, line 324).

Removing the block is deliberate and correct — it is the fix from bd-qpvoamvu
/ PR #465, which stopped the leftover shortcode from being misreported
downstream as an unrecognized `include`. This is NOT a request to put the block
back. What is missing is the other half of that story: nothing downstream
distinguishes "expanded every include" from "expanded some and deleted the
rest", so the writer produces the page as if the document were whole.

The Q-17-3 arm is otherwise in good shape — it registers the included file in
both SourceContexts, remaps the child parse's FileId(0) into the parent so the
inner diagnostics render real ariadne snippets, and records the include for
cache invalidation. Only the "and now abandon the document" step is absent.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION

Have the failure arms mark the document as failed rather than merely pushing a
diagnostic, so an unexpandable include takes the same path an inline Q-2-11
already takes: no HTML written, counted against "Rendered N of M". Raise Q-17-2
from warning to error at the same time — a page silently missing its content is
not a warning-grade outcome, and Quarto 1 treats a missing include as fatal.

Whether a circular include (Q-17-1) should also abort is a separate judgement;
the arms share a code path but not obviously a policy.

REAL-WORLD HIT

The Positron docs page migrate-rstudio-keybindings.qmd includes
_rstudio-keyboard-shortcuts.qmd. Under an older q2 that included file failed to
parse, and the page rendered while losing its entire 25-row keybinding table.
That specific instance is FIXED at 0.28.0 — the page now renders with 21 <tr>
elements, matching the Quarto 1 baseline exactly, exit 0. The corpus therefore
no longer contains a failing include, and the repro below is synthetic by
necessity. The swallow-and-continue behaviour it isolates is unchanged.

REPRO

  /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/include-parse-failure-dropped/

  cd <that directory> && sh check.sh

check.sh renders the four-page project with q2 and then with Quarto 1, and
prints per page whether an HTML file was written and whether the included
content reached it. It runs Quarto 1 twice: the first pass aborts the whole
project on missing.qmd's absent include and writes no _site at all, which is
itself the Q1 reference behaviour; the second pass sets that page aside so Q1's
handling of the other three is visible.

VERSION

Verified at q2 0.28.0 and at q2 source main 85e98fb02 (no include-related
commits since the v0.28.0 tag). Quarto 1 reference: 99.9.9.

Origin strand: br-include-parse-failure-dropped-w3wlg2zl in the
q2-positron-docs skein.
close_reason: Shipped in q2 0.29.0 (PR #648). Verified downstream by re-running llms-info/repros/include-parse-failure-dropped/check.sh: 'Rendered 1 of 4 files - 4 errors', and no HTML written for either the broken-include page or the missing-include page, where 0.28.0 wrote both with the included content silently absent. The good-include page still renders with its content.

c-vnemxfm7.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-vnemxfm7.text:
Fixed on braid/bd-include-parse-failure-dropped-u4rdjxru-include-parse-failure-dropped (2bd66e5b3), not pushed.

All three failure arms now fail the document, at both include positions (block-level and code-fence). Q-17-1/Q-17-2 raised warning -> error. No new diagnostic codes.

Decisions beyond the strand:
- Q-17-1 (flagged as a separate judgement) also aborts: Q1's standaloneInclude throws on a cycle as well as an unreadable target, and leaving one arm non-fatal restores the inconsistency the fix removes.
- The code-fence arms move with the block-level ones, because Q-17-1/Q-17-2 are each emitted from two sites and one code cannot carry two severities.
- Q-17-4 stays a warning (placement mistake, not a failed include).

Found and fixed while verifying: resolve_single_file_deps in quarto-preview discarded the entire watch set when expansion errs, so one broken include would strand q2 preview on the broken version with the file being edited no longer watched. Factored the stage body into a public expand_document_includes() that hands the document back regardless of verdict.

Workspace: 13595 passed / 199 skipped, vs 13590/199 on main — +5, exactly the tests added.

title: Regression in 0.18.0: indented continuation line is a hard parse error, dropping the whole page
description:
REGRESSION introduced in v0.18.0 by 92737cdd ('Fix digit/dash/plus-leading continuation line terminating the paragraph', bd-w6tod0gh). v0.17.0 rendered all of the affected inputs; v0.18.0 fails them with

  Error: Parse error — unexpected character or token here

and drops the ENTIRE page from the render, not just the offending block. HEAD (7c964559, the v0.18.0 release merge) still has it.

## What happens vs Quarto 1

Quarto 1 accepts all of these; q2 0.18.0 renders none of them.

  1. one
      1. nested a        <- ordered sub-list indented 4 under a '1. ' item

  This value is in seconds, so to make license leases last
    30 minutes you would use the following syntax.   <- indented digit-leading wrap

  hello
    -5 degrees           <- indented dash-leading prose
    -- em dash

  - one
          - over-indented bullet

## Root cause

The two new peek helpers in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c fail on the fall-through path when the line carries leading indentation. An indent sweep isolates it precisely — the error fires exactly when a NEW peek branch runs on an indented line and returns FALSE:

  para + '  -5 degrees'    (peek_dash_plus_opens_block -> false)  ERROR
  para + '  -- em dash'    (peek_dash_plus_opens_block -> false)  ERROR
  para + '  - item'        (peek_dash_plus_opens_block -> true)   ok
  para + '  *emph* here'   (pre-existing '*' peek)                ok
  para + '  `code` here'   (pre-existing backtick peek)           ok
  para + '-5 degrees'      (same text, indent 0)                  ok

The pre-existing '`' and '*' peeks are fine at the same indentation, so this is specific to the two branches added by 92737cdd, not to peeking in general.

The suspected mechanism is the mark_end bookkeeping at the end of gate 2 (scanner.c ~line 3059). When second_peeked is true, mark_end is deliberately skipped so the peeked run is not swallowed into the SOFT_LINE_ENDING token's range, leaving the range 'where the earlier mark_end put it'. For the '`' and '*' branches that was pre-existing behavior and the earlier mark_end is in the right place; for the two new branches the earlier mark_end appears to sit before the line's consumed indentation, so the parser resumes at a position it cannot reconcile. Indent 0 works because there is no indentation to strand.

Second, independent defect in the same commit: peek_dash_plus_opens_block (scanner.c ~1357) has no indentation guard, while peek_ordered_marker (~1313) opens with 'if (s->indentation > 3) return result;'. So a '- b' line indented 4 past the enclosing item's content column — indented-code territory, where no list marker can form — still reports that it opens a block. That is what breaks the 'over-indented bullet' case above.

## Suggested fix direction

Give peek_dash_plus_opens_block the same 's->indentation > 3' early-out peek_ordered_marker already has, and make the skipped-mark_end path in gate 2 restore the position explicitly for the new branches rather than relying on an earlier mark_end whose placement only happens to be correct for '`' and '*'. The indent dimension is missing from the test corpus: paragraph.txt cases 15-29 added by 92737cdd all sit at indent 0, which is why this got through 572/572 tree-sitter tests.

## Real-world hit

In the Posit Connect documentation port, api/index.qmd — the entire API reference, 53k lines — fails to render, taking the project to 351 of 352 files with 3 errors, plus a cascading [Q-13-2] 'Navbar references missing document' warning on all 351 surviving pages. The offending markdown is the endpoint life-cycle nested ordered list in Connect's own OpenAPI spec (api/public/openapi.yaml:8245-8250). That spec text ships to customers as a downloadable artifact, so reformatting it on the docs side is not an option.

## Repro

  /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/indented-continuation-parse-error/

Run 'q2 render' there: 0 of 3 files render, with 5 parse errors. Run 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1' for the Quarto 1 reference (all 3 render). The README carries the full indent-by-parent-type sweep table.

Observed with q2 0.18.0. Origin strand in the q2-connect-docs skein: br-8wvj5ang.
close_reason: Div-context regression fixed in 062f4f88 and pushed to PR #510. Full xtask verify green; repro variants byte-identical to v0.18.0; div-wrapped nested list improves on 0.18 (parses where 0.18 errored).

c-1rt1h9nm.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-1rt1h9nm.text: REOPENED: branch regression found by the q2-connect-docs agent (repro: llms-info/repros/attributed-div-ws-blank-list). A nested ordered list inside an ATTRIBUTED fenced div silently renders as paragraph text. Isolated: old scanner + new grammar is CORRECT, so the cause is Part B, not the grammar prec.right the repro README suspected. Two defects: (1) claimable_list_indentation breaks its run at FENCED_DIV, but FENCED_DIV/FENCED_CODE_BLOCK/ANONYMOUS match() without consuming anything — they are transparent and must be skipped, so even '::: {.x} / * a / [4sp]1. b' loses the nested list with no whitespace-only line involved; (2) the over-indent verdict at both gates uses the absorbing mark_end emission (else branch), which makes a bogus paragraph-continuation GLR fork viable across whitespace-only lines (token log: SOFT_LINE_ENDING size 7 swallowing ws-line remainder + newline + next line's indent); the old code's skip-mark_end emission left that fork dead. Fixing both here with tests first.

c-4oz3w0zf.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-4oz3w0zf.text:
Independent verification + mechanism refinement (session in main q2 checkout, HEAD 3640eae9).

All sweep rows reproduce exactly as reported. Two additional data points sharpen the mechanism:

1. The suspected cause (skipped mark_end in the peeked soft-break path leaving the token range pre-indent) is CONFIRMED as the trigger, but the reason the pre-existing backtick/star peeks survive is NOT better mark_end placement — their placement is identical. They survive by accident: their continuation lines begin with EXTERNAL-scanner tokens (code-span start, emphasis open) which re-consume the residual whitespace into their own token range on the next scan (CST shows code_span_delimiter spanning cols 0-3 over '  `'). A prose continuation instead hits the INTERNAL lexer, which lexes _whitespace — and the grammar state immediately after _soft_line_ending cannot shift _whitespace (tree-sitter trace: 'detect_error lookahead:_whitespace' at state 2419). So the precise failure condition is: (a) peeked gate branch judges the line prose, (b) after block_continuation consumes any open-block prefix columns there is RESIDUAL leading whitespace, (c) the next token is internal. Evidence: '- a\n  -5 degrees' PASSES (block_continuation size 2 consumes the indent exactly, no residue), while '1. one\n    1. nested' fails with exactly 1 residual space after block_continuation size 3.

2. peek_ordered_marker's 'indentation > 3' guard has different semantics at the two call sites: at gate 1, s->indentation is the RAW column count (match_line has not consumed block prefixes yet), so a legitimate nested marker at raw indent 4 inside a list is misjudged as prose — that is what routes the nested-ordered-list case into the broken soft-break path at all. At gate 2 (post-match_line) the same guard reads post-prefix indentation. Any fix copying the guard into peek_dash_plus_opens_block must account for this, and note the guard alone does NOT fix the over-indented-bullet case — it would just reroute it from 'phantom block opener' into the same residual-whitespace parse error, so the mark_end/residual-indent defect must be fixed first (or a grammar-side fix: allow optional _whitespace after _soft_line_ending in paragraph continuation, which also matches pandoc's stripping of continuation-line leading whitespace).

3. title: Inline R: the documented `{r} expr` spelling is never evaluated, and the native `r expr` spelling gets the wrong escaping default
description: Quarto documents two spellings for inline executable code with deliberately different semantics, and q2 implements neither correctly. The brace spelling `{r} expr` — the cross-engine form quarto-web has recommended since 1.4 — is never evaluated at all. The native knitr spelling `r expr` is evaluated, but with the brace form's escaping default rather than its own. WHAT HAPPENS VS QUARTO 1 Spelling. `{r} release_version` in prose renders as an ordinary code span, {r} release_version. Inside an attribute value it survives as the literal backticked text. No diagnostic of any kind is emitted and the render exits 0. Q1 evaluates it in prose, in a fenced-div attribute value and in a link title. Verified on q2 0.29.0, 0.28.0, 0.27.0 and 0.24.0 — long-standing, not a regression. Escaping. quarto-web docs/computations/inline-code.qmd specifies the two defaults. Section 'Markdown Output': the brace form escapes markdown specials in the value by default, and the engine-specific opt-in for markdown is I() for knitr. Section 'Syntax Compatibility > Knitr': the native spelling 'treats all inline output as *containing markdown*', with the equivalence stated outright — `r radius` is equivalent to `{r} I(radius)`. q2 inverts the native default. With release_version <- '**bold**': case q2 0.29.0 Quarto 1 docs say classic bare escaped markdown classic I() markdown brace I() not evaluated markdown Q1 matches the spec on all three. q2 passes the middle row only because .QuartoInlineRender passes AsIs objects through untouched — i.e. the one case it gets right, it gets right for the brace form's reason. Read the diagonal: q2's classic spelling behaves like Q1's brace spelling. q2 has one inline spelling with one semantics, and it is the brace semantics wearing the classic spelling. ROOT CAUSE crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/preprocess.rs:136: Regex::new(r"(^|[^`\\])`r[ \t]([^`]+)`") resolve_inline_r_expressions rewrites each match to `r .QuartoInlineRender(expr)`. There is no alternation for {r}, so an unmatched brace form is never rewritten and arrives at the markdown parser as a code span. The pass runs over the serialized document (stage/stages/engine_execution.rs:432,495) before knitr sees it; its only callers are engine/knitr/mod.rs:158-159. Blast radius is one module. Quarto 1 is not a superset here, it is the mirror image, which is how both halves went missing at once: - quarto-cli/src/core/execute-inline.ts, executeInlineCodeHandler(language, exec), builds "(^|[^`])`{" + language + "}[ \t]([^`]+)`" — the BRACE form and nothing else. src/execute/rmd.ts:576 calls it with 'r' from the knitr execute: handler at rmd.ts:287, rewriting matches to `r .QuartoInlineRender(expr)`. - The native `r expr` is knitr's own rmarkdown syntax, predating Quarto. Q1 never matches it. knitr evaluates it downstream, and since Q1 installs no knit_hooks$inline, .QuartoInlineRender never touches it — which is exactly why the native form passes markdown through. So Q1's only wrapper insertion is on the brace form, and q2's regex covers exactly the spelling Q1's Quarto layer does not. preprocess.rs's doc comment cites execute-inline.ts as the source of its (^|[^`]) guard: the guard was transplanted off the brace-form matcher onto a classic-form regex, and the spelling went with neither. Note that q2's engine/knitr/resources/rmd/execute.R is byte-identical to Q1's src/resources/rmd/execute.R, so .QuartoInlineRender itself is unmodified. The whole divergence is in which strings get wrapped. SUGGESTED FIX The documented equivalence gives the contract directly, with no new evaluation machinery: `{r} x` -> `r .QuartoInlineRender(x)` (escape by default) `r x` -> `r .QuartoInlineRender(I(x))` (markdown by default), or left unwrapped as Q1 leaves it, which is the same thing Both halves must preserve the existing guards. The (^|[^`\\]) prefix guard and the [ \t] class are load-bearing against display fences — without them a ```r fence anchors a match on its third backtick and the block body is swallowed into .QuartoInlineRender(...), costing the whole page (bd-knitr-inline-r-eats-fence-2ofk91x1). Any brace-form alternation needs to clear the same bar, and the file's regression tests (test_fence_inside_yaml_scalar_not_matched, test_escaped_backtick_fence_not_matched, test_backtick_prefixed_not_matched) are the fence. Worth deciding explicitly: the escaping half is a behaviour change for existing documents that use `r expr` with values containing markdown specials. It is the documented behaviour and matches Q1, but it is a change from what q2 ships today, and no test currently pins either outcome — all 15 preprocess.rs tests assert regex matching only. RELATED bd-u996g8g2 is the jupyter half of the same gap ({python} expr missing from the production text path); it records 'knitr handles inline r expressions natively', which is true of the classic spelling only and is why no R-side counterpart was ever filed. bd-knitr-inline-r-eats-fence-2ofk91x1 owns the same regex and notes in passing that 'Q1's handler covers the braced {r} expr form rather than bare r expr, so it is not a strict 1:1 port'. Nothing in q2's plans, docs or skein states an intent to diverge from Q1 here. Searched: all 1331 claude-notes/*.md (every file mentioning inline R / inline expressions / QuartoInlineRender read), q2 docs/ (inline expressions are not documented; only Q-2-47 and Q-2-50 mention {r}), and the full skein export, 2109 strands by title and description with comments checked on the seven closest. The nearest statements all cut toward parity: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-25-r-display-fence-parse-error.md calls the missing brace form 'a separate parity gap, not this bug'. Going the other way, claude-notes/research/2026-07-04-q1-vs-q2-knitr-jupyter-baseline.md audits the two implementations and records the opposite of what is true — 'Equivalent in both: inline `r expr` wrapping'. REAL-WORLD HIT The Positron website port, download.qmd:100: ::: {#download-hero .download-hero data-version="`{r} release_version`"} The rendered page carries data-version="`{r} release_version`" where Q1 has data-version="2026.08.1-2". That attribute is read by the page's own JavaScript — download.qmd's detectOS() looks up #download-hero and builds the platform download URLs from the version — so the page's primary function breaks. It is the only inline R on the site, which is why one character of source costs the download page. The defect is invisible to every comparative sweep that port runs: text diffing compares visible text and this is an attribute; the asset checker and lychee follow references and data-version is not one; the render log is silent, no diagnostic, exit 0. It was found by reading download.html's markup directly. REPRO /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/inline-r-brace-spelling-not-evaluated/ sh check.sh # q2 and Quarto 1 sh check.sh ~/.local/bin/q2.0.28.0-backup # or any other build Twelve cases in one render: B1-B3 and C1-C3 are three positions (prose, fenced-div attribute value, link title) x two spellings, where the classic column is the control that proves attributes are not the problem; E1-E3 are the escaping defaults; I1-I3 test the documented I() equivalence directly. The README states expected vs actual and carries the full root-cause and provenance analysis. TRAP FOR THE FIXER, found by walking into it: the preprocessing pass runs over the whole serialized document, so an inline expression written inside explanatory PROSE is executed like any other. Adding a sentence containing a literal backtick-r-x to the repro fixture killed the render with "object 'x' not found". Use the escaping quarto-web prescribes (a doubled brace, or an extra enclosing backtick) when writing about this syntax, in fixtures and in docs alike. Origin strand: br-inline-r-brace-spelling-not-evaluated-kucihhme in the Positron docs port's skein (/Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs). Observed on q2 0.29.0 (official release build); q2 HEAD checked at 914f20697, nothing has touched crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/ since the 0.29.0 tag. Q1 reference: quarto dev build 99.9.9.

Both inline spellings now behave as quarto.org documents them. `{r} expr` evaluates and escapes markdown specials in the value; `r expr` evaluates and inserts the value as live markdown, with `I()` bridging the two. All twelve repro cases match Quarto 1, and the rendered markup is byte-identical to Q1's on every measured attribute -- including the download-hero shape that started this.

Three behaviour changes shipped, not the one the strand anticipated: the escaping change, `r NULL` rendering empty rather than the literal NULL, and a knitr document displaying the {r} syntax now failing if the expression doesn't resolve (all three match Q1). The third is only survivable because #657 landed with it -- the nested-cell mask now covers inline expressions, so a markdown block suppresses execution.

c-b86cicpz.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-b86cicpz.text:
Filed as PR #658 -- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/658

STACKED, and the merge order matters. #658's base is bugfix/bd-0gwekaem-nested-cell-mask-inline-expressions (PR #657), not main. #657 must merge first. If #658 were retargeted at main and merged alone, docs/guides/authoring/computations.qmd would tell authors that wrapping an inline expression in a markdown block displays it rather than running it, which is only true once #657's mask extension is in.

Branch braid/bd-inline-r-brace-spelling-not-evaluated-lk9s3iwe-... rebased onto 8e13ecf8b; single commit 8c3b591de; remote feature/bd-inline-r-brace-spelling-not-evaluated-lk9s3iwe. Clean rebase, no conflicts -- no file overlap with #657.

ONE DOCS ERROR CAUGHT BY THE STACK, worth recording because nothing in this branch would have caught it. The section originally said 'a fenced code block is displayed verbatim, so an expression written inside one is shown, not run'. #657 deliberately kept the display-class predicate narrow (info string empty or 'markdown'), so that sentence was wrong for any language-labelled fence. Measured on the stacked build: brace and classic spellings are both displayed verbatim inside a markdown block and inside a bare fence, and both still execute inside a ```r block. The prose now says 'markdown block, or a fence carrying no language at all' and warns about the labelled case. Widening the predicate is bd-tiidc899.

Gate on the stacked tree: workspace 13719/13719, cargo xtask verify (--skip-hub-build --skip-hub-tests --skip-rust-tests) all steps passed, clippy -D warnings clean, xtask lint clean, and #657's t31_masked_text_is_not_claimed_by_the_inline_scanner green under this branch's alternation.

c-c3lnpj4i.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-c3lnpj4i.text:
Fix ready on branch braid/bd-inline-r-brace-spelling-not-evaluated-lk9s3iwe-inline-r-brace-spelling-not-evaluated (worktree .worktrees/workspace-3), one commit c95012e99. Not pushed, no PR yet -- see the blocker below.

WHAT LANDED
Pattern gains a spelling-marker group and the replacement branches on it: `{r} expr` -> `r .QuartoInlineRender(expr)`; `r expr` goes to knitr unwrapped with only its separator normalized to a space (knitr's class is [ #], so a tab-separated expression would otherwise stop evaluating). The suggested `.QuartoInlineRender(I(expr))` form was rejected: I(NULL) errors in R, so it would turn `r NULL` into a failed render. Leaving the expression alone reaches the same markdown-passthrough semantics via knitr, which is also exactly what Q1 does.

All twelve repro cases now match Quarto 1, and the rendered markup is byte-identical to Q1's on every measured attribute including the download-hero shape.

THREE BEHAVIOUR CHANGES, not one -- the strand anticipated only the escaping change:
1. `r expr` with markdown specials now renders as markdown (the documented default).
2. `r NULL` renders empty where it rendered the literal NULL, because knitr's hook replaces the wrapper on this path. Verified byte-identical to Q1.
3. A knitr document that displays the {r} syntax now fails the render if the expression doesn't resolve. Q1 fails identically.

CORRECTION TO THE STRAND'S 'TRAP FOR THE FIXER'
It prescribes 'a doubled brace, or an extra enclosing backtick' for writing about this syntax. Measured: the extra-backtick form does NOT protect anything, in q2 or in Q1 -- `` `{r} x` `` still evaluates. Neither does a display block. Only the doubled brace works, and q2 renders it verbatim ({{r}}) where Q1 collapses it to {r}.

BLOCKED ON bd-0gwekaem
That gap is filed as bd-0gwekaem and dispatched. The docs in this commit teach the fenced-block rule, which only becomes true once the nested-cell mask covers inline expressions, so this branch is meant to stack on that fix rather than merge to main first.

c-c42zz8s8.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-c42zz8s8.text: TS-engine-extensions epic (rebase) resolves the *blocker* behind this strand. The blocker is 'knitr/jupyter don't compose cleanly (knitr claims python cells, jupyter sees no cell).' The epic introduces per-language ownership resolution: engines return kind-tagged claims (Primary/Interop/Fallback), and a tiered resolver assigns each language to one owner; each engine's leave-alone set (handled_languages) is the projection 'everything I don't own.' For 'engine: [knitr, jupyter]' on {r}+{python}, the explicit-Fallback tier routes r->knitr and python->jupyter, and knitr CEDES python via its existing knit_engines passthrough -> jupyter actually runs it. So knitr/jupyter (and any pair of real engines) compose cleanly. The epic also delivers composable engines (the echo engine in Plan 1c, then Julia in Plan 4). The browser E2E still needs writing, but the composition blocker this strand cites is removed. Model: claude-notes/designs/engine-resolution.md (see worked-cases table + §5 enforcement). Tracked as part of the TS-engine rebase.

Build a minimal repro outside q2 and file it against automerge/automerge-repo; re-measure when a newer 2.6 alpha lands.

title: Engine intermediate FileId slot desync: EngineExecutionStage remaps executed AST onto _quarto.yml's dense slot in project renders
description: Verified structurally (bd-nv4p0eb1 audit). Main pipeline order is ParseDocument -> MetadataMerge -> ... -> IncludeExpansion -> ... -> EngineExecution (pipeline.rs:279-323). MetadataMergeStage registers _quarto.yml/_metadata.yml into doc.ast_context.source_context via add_file_with_id (grows SourceContext.files, does NOT grow ast_context.filenames). engine_execution.rs:498 then computes the intermediate's slot as FileId(filenames.len()) while add_file actually assigns FileId(files.len()) — larger by the number of registered config files — and :528-530 remaps every executed-AST id by id.0 + new_slot.0. Result: in any project render with an executable engine, engine-produced blocks carry a FileId that resolves (via get_file's dense indexing) to _quarto.yml or an include, not the engine intermediate. The lock-step comment at :333-334 is false after MetadataMerge. Downstream: trace attribution wrong; diagnostics anchored in engine blocks render config-file text; writers/json.rs:1825 positional filenames[idx]/files[idx] pairing compounds it. Needs a repro fixture (project + _quarto.yml + executable cell) asserting engine-block FileIds resolve to the intermediate slot. Also add debug_assert for the lock-step invariant, and consider retiring the parallel filenames table (see research doc §5). Assessment: claude-notes/research/2026-08-09-fileid-span-integrity-audit.md (finding P1).

title: AST capability: block-level attributes via collected trailing Inline::Attr in writers (Para, list items)

A filter/transform injects a standalone Inline::Attr (typically trailing) into a block's inlines, and the block writers collect those nodes, strip them from rendered content, and apply the merged Attr (id/classes/kvs) onto the emitted element (e.g.

title: qmd writer collapses a 4-backtick raw fence to 3 backticks, so nested content terminates the block
description:
Found while scoping bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj on q2 HEAD eac0c7acf. REPRO: a raw block opened with FOUR backticks whose content contains a THREE-backtick fence: ````{=html} 
    ```{r}
    cat("IN-RAW\n")
    ```
```` The AST is correct — one RawBlock whose text is the whole 
 including the inner fence. But 'pampa -t qmd' writes it back with a THREE-backtick opener, so the inner fence now closes the raw block and the remainder becomes body text. The writer must emit a fence run longer than the longest run appearing in the block's content.

This is independent of any engine. It is the same defect class as bd-knitr-inline-r-eats-fence-2ofk91x1's 'the qmd writer collapses ``` r to ```r'.

COMPOUNDING: with knitr live, the now-unnested {r} fence is executed and knitr injects '::: {.cell}' scaffolding, which then fails to parse — a FATAL render error, not merely wrong output:

  Error: Parse error
    [ raw.knitr.rmarkdown:161:4 ]
  161 | :::
      |    unexpected character or token here

Masking nested fences (the fix on the parent strand) removes the execution half and so removes the fatal error, but NOT this writer defect: the raw block still renders wrong because it still ends early. Explicitly scoped out of that plan (claude-notes/plans/2026-08-31-nested-executable-fence-masking.md, 'Out of scope').
