title: Quarto API: settle the 16 Q1-divergence conflicts blocking JSR publish
description:
Gate for publishing @quarto/types + @quarto/api to jsr.io. JSR is immutable (published versions cannot be deleted) and 'deno bundle' freezes the resolved version into each extension author's bundle, so a divergence from Q1 is wrong PERMANENTLY while an absence is merely unfinished.

Release criterion (not completeness): if Q2 is a strict subtree of Q1, an incomplete SDK is safe to publish -- missing surface is additive later. It is the CONFLICTS that must be settled.

Evidence base: claude-notes/research/2026-08-22-quarto-api-q1-vs-q2-status.md (951 lines, on branch feature/jsr-publish). Section 2 carries the authoritative gate table. Findings were produced partly by DIFFERENTIAL EXECUTION of Q1 vs Q2, not only by reading -- which is how 23 category-D behavioural divergences were found in namespaces a reading-based pass had assessed as clean verbatim ports.

Categories: A absent in Q2 (safe, additive) / B identical (safe) / C same name different signature (blocker) / D same signature different behaviour (WORST -- invisible to any type-level guard) / E Q2-only, no reference to validate against.

16 conflicts survive under the reduced published surface (only 1 of 17 retires). Withholding exports removes NAMES, not CONDUCT: behaviour reaches authors through the injected QuartoAPI, typed by @quarto/types, which is published in full regardless of what @quarto/api exports.

Two things explicitly NOT in scope (do not spend effort here): the 15 unimplemented jupyter capabilities, the dropped Q1 registry, and everything in the research doc's section 8 -- all category A, safe. Also: two divergences are Q1 BUGS that Q2 fixed (shortcode params containing '=', md-indent garbling) -- keep Q2's behaviour, do not 'settle' those toward Q1.

Blocks: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-22-jsr-publish-quarto-api-types.md Phase 4 (first publish, irreversible). Phases 1-3 and 5-6 of that plan are packaging work and are independent of this epic.

title: Phase 9 follow-up: thread user_grammars through RenderToHtmlRenderer
description:
Today render_page_in_project's project-rendering branch drops user_grammars on the floor — the RenderToHtmlRenderer constructs its own per-page RenderContext and there's no path to attach user_grammars there. Single-file projects still wire user_grammars correctly via render_single_doc_to_response.

Threading user grammars through the renderer is straightforward: add a field to RenderToHtmlRenderer holding an Arc<Mutex<Option<JsUserGrammars>>> (or similar) and have its render() method install the provider on the per-page RenderContext.

title: preview vs render: assess grass (native) vs dart-sass (WASM) SCSS compiler split
description: Discovered during bd-4b7f1hr7. CompileThemeCssStage runs in both q2 render (native) and the browser preview (WASM via wasm-quarto-hub-client), and bd-4b7f1hr7's preview_render_css_parity tests now pin that both pipelines assemble IDENTICAL SCSS inputs and (natively) byte-identical CSS. But the compiler itself differs by target: native compiles with grass (pure Rust, crates/quarto-sass/src/compile.rs), wasm32 compiles with dart-sass via the JS bridge (runtime.compile_sass). So the CSS bytes the browser preview ships are NOT guaranteed byte-identical to render's even with converged inputs - grass and dart-sass may differ in output formatting and, in edge cases, semantics. Assess: (1) how different are the outputs in practice for our theme bundle (compile the assembled SCSS both ways and diff); (2) is converging on one compiler feasible/desirable (grass compiled to WASM would give one codepath; dart-sass is the reference implementation Q1 uses - grass may have been chosen natively for speed, dart-sass in browser for fidelity); (3) if not converging, document the accepted divergence and add a coarse regression guard (e.g. selector-set comparison). Reference: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-10-html-preview-css-drift-audit.md.

title: Q-2-32 not emitted for `***` inside pipe-table cells (generic parse error instead)
description: When a pipe-table cell contains `***hello` (e.g. `| ***hello |`), pampa returns the generic 'unexpected character or token here' parse error instead of the structured Q-2-32 'Triple star emphasis disallowed. Consider `*__` instead.' diagnostic that fires at the paragraph level. Verified to be pre-existing (reproduces on main pre-bd-qhb2o); discovered while sanity-checking the bd-qhb2o fix and intentionally left out of scope. Likely cause: Q-2-32.json's `prefixesAndSuffixes` corpus does not enumerate a pipe-table-cell context, so the LR state the parser reaches when it sees `***` inside a cell isn't in the merr-style state->Q-code table (resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json) and the diagnostic falls through to the generic path. Probable fix: add a pipe-table prefix/suffix pair like ["| col |\n|---|\n| ", " |"] to Q-2-32.json and rerun crates/pampa/scripts/build_error_table.ts. Worth scoping as part of a broader Q-2-32 coverage audit — same gap may exist for other inline-receptive contexts not yet enumerated (e.g. footnote definitions, table captions, fenced-div contents, etc.).

title: Investigate cargo xtask dev-setup --locked causing externref mismatch in TS Test Suite
description: cargo xtask dev-setup installs wasm-bindgen-cli with --locked flag. When used in ts-test-suite.yml instead of the hardcoded cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.108 (without --locked), the hub-client WASM tests fail with: CompileError: WebAssembly.instantiate(): call[0] expected type externref, found local.get of type i32. Reverted in PR 109. Root cause unknown — the --locked flag may produce a subtly different binary.

c-xvdu0paa.author: cwickham
c-xvdu0paa.text:
Reproduced headless and confirmed the fix (2026-06-10, macOS arm64, pinned nightly-2026-04-28, wasm-bindgen 0.2.108).

The bad module is genuinely INVALID, independent of any browser or test harness. Building the WASM with the --locked wasm-bindgen-cli and running:

    wasm-tools validate --features=all wasm_quarto_hub_client_bg.wasm

fails with:

    func 1610 failed to validate: type mismatch: expected externref, found i32 (at offset 0x70ba18)

— the same func #1610 / 'expected externref, found i32' as the browser CompileError. So this isn't browser- or vitest-specific; the producer emits a malformed module.

Trigger: 'cargo xtask dev-setup' falls back to 'cargo install --locked wasm-bindgen-cli' when cargo-binstall is absent, yielding the --locked binary.

Fix that worked: reinstall without --locked —

    cargo install -f wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.108

Suggestion: a cheap CI guard would be to run 'wasm-tools validate --features=all' on the built pkg/ wasm in the hub-build leg — it catches this without needing a browser.

title: Highlighted code blocks render a stray empty line at the bottom (trapped pre margin inside div.sourceCode)
description:
Highlighted code blocks (e.g. ```ts) in both `q2 render` HTML output and `q2 preview` show ~one line-height of extra background below the last code line.

Root cause (verified in-browser with Chrome DevTools): Bootstrap's `pre { margin-bottom: 1rem }` survives on `pre.sourceCode`, and `div.sourceCode { overflow-y: hidden }` (resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss) creates a block formatting context that traps that 17px margin INSIDE the gray box. Measured: div bottom - pre bottom = 18px in Q2 vs 1px (border only) in Q1.

Q1 avoids this via Pandoc's baseline highlighting CSS, which Q2 never emits:
  div.sourceCode { margin: 1em 0; }
  pre.sourceCode { margin: 0; }

Fix: add the two rules to resources/scss/html/templates/highlight.scss (Q2's pandoc-baseline equivalent, embedded via quarto-sass load_highlight_layer, so it covers native render AND the WASM preview client).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-03-codeblock-trailing-margin.md
close_reason: Fixed: added div.sourceCode{margin:1em 0} + pre.sourceCode{margin:0} to highlight.scss (Pandoc-baseline parity). Regression test in quarto-sass compile_all_themes_test.rs; verified e2e in q2 render and q2 preview (gap inside div: 18px -> 1px, matching Q1).

title: Config/YAML diagnostic spans are shifted one byte left (start on the opening quote), which is what lands mid-character in the ariadne panic
description: Discovered while fixing bd-ariadne-config-span-char-boundary-panic-rkqmhzrg. That strand's stated root cause was wrong in an important way, and this is the real defect underneath it. MEASURED, not inferred. Instrumenting quarto-error-reporting's render_ariadne_source_context on the minimal repro (a website whose _quarto.yml has navbar.left[0].text: 'Ask AI U+2728') prints, for the two Q-2-9 diagnostics on that line: len=13 start=81 start_is_boundary=true end=94 used_fallback=false slice=Some("''. Label 2 covers 104..111 = "I" at 105..112. The -1 shift is present in BOTH the repro and the control -- it is unconditional for single-quoted YAML scalars. It is merely invisible on ASCII (a caret one column off) and fatal next to a multi-byte character, because value_start-1+inline_offset then lands inside the character. That is the whole explanation for the parent strand's case table: the panic fires exactly when the shifted offset falls inside a multi-byte char, which is why it looked emoji-specific and position-specific and was neither. Visible in current output even after the crash fix, since the fix only snaps to boundaries and cannot recover the lost byte: 7 | - text: 'Ask AI U+2728' | ------┬------ <- highlights ') | ----┬--- <- highlights U+2728) WHERE TO LOOK: the YAML/config path that builds SourceInfo for inlines parsed out of a scalar value -- the offset base appears to be the scalar node's start (which includes the opening quote delimiter) rather than the first byte of its content. Check both quoted forms and the block forms; a plain unquoted scalar has no delimiter and may well be correct, which would make this specifically a quote-delimiter accounting bug. STATUS: the crash is fixed separately in quarto-error-reporting (char-boundary snapping in both renderer paths). That fix is defensive and correct on its own, but it does not fix this -- carets on config diagnostics remain one byte left until this is addressed.
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-mxa44voa, which predates it and covers the same root cause across a wider surface (YAML scalars AND div attribute values). All measurements from this strand — the constant -1 quoted-scalar shift, the compounding multi-line block-scalar drift that misreports the line, and the comrak finding — have been folded into bd-mxa44voa as comment c-wqkls0fr. Work continues there.

c-06vstxjh.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-06vstxjh.text: SCOPE CORRECTION — this strand's description covers only the quoted-scalar case. Measured on a page-footer.center fixture, the same root cause produces a second, WORSE symptom. Behavior by scalar style, all measured against .worktrees/workspace-1 at main: plain correct drift 0 single/double-quoted 1 byte left drift -1, constant block scalar, 1 line correct drift 0 block scalar, N lines REPORTS THE WRONG LINE drift +indent per preceding line, accumulating Three-line repro (_quarto.yml): website: page-footer: center: | line one line two Footer Both Q-2-9 warnings belong on line 9. They are reported at 8:10 and 9:14. The drift is the stripped block-scalar indentation, applied once per preceding line, so it compounds — a longer footer drifts further, and the diagnostic can be attributed to an arbitrary earlier line. Why the styles differ: for a quoted scalar yaml-rust2's marker points at the opening quote, so value_span.start is one byte before the content. For a block scalar the marker points at the content start, so the BASE is right — but the content has had per-line indentation stripped, so base + content_offset drifts once the content crosses a newline. Single-line block scalars never cross one, which is why they look fine. Same root cause either way: q2 adds a content offset to a base that does not correspond to the content. Same fix: quarto-yaml exposes content_span + content_is_verbatim (false for multi-line block scalars and for escaped quoted scalars), and q2 falls back to the whole-scalar span when not verbatim. Note this would also have crashed before the quarto-error-reporting char-boundary fix — an accumulating drift lands mid-character at least as easily as a constant -1. Tracked in claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-diagnostic-span-integrity.md (Phase 3 and Phase 4).

title: A committed hub-client bundle can be rebuilt from stale node_modules, silently reverting a dependency bump
description:
hub-client/quarto-hub-sandboxed-preview/ is a standalone Vite project whose build outputs are COMMITTED: hub-client/public/q2-sandboxed-preview.html (a vite-plugin-singlefile bundle with React + KaTeX inlined) and hub-client/public/serviceWorker.js. Nothing reconciles those artifacts against the sources and pins that produce them, and both had silently drifted on main.

EVIDENCE 1 - a Snyk upgrade was silently reverted. PR #637 (e4a728192) bumped KaTeX 0.18.2 -> 0.18.4 "across all four copies", including this bundle. Then 6549a98ae ("Add github pages note and update sandboxed iframe url", 2026-09-01) rebuilt the bundle against a stale node_modules in that subproject, re-embedding 0.18.2. From then until 546fdd374 (2026-09-03) main's package.json and lockfile pinned 0.18.4 while the shipped sandboxed preview ran 0.18.2. The diff that did it reads as pure minifier identifier churn - the only real signal is the string literal "0.18.2" buried in a 1.8 MB single-line file - so review could not plausibly have caught it. Also note hub-client/changelog.md still carries e4a72819's entry claiming the sandboxed preview bundle was aligned on 0.18.4, which was false for two days.

EVIDENCE 2 - the other artifact drifted the opposite way. 103af4445 ("disable caching in sandboxed preview for now", 2026-09-01) commented the previewOffline cache out of src/serviceWorker.ts but committed only the source. The committed bundle still dated from 0d4043c4c (2026-07-09) and kept precaching, caches.match lookups, and write-through caching of non-VFS requests. So the shipped worker did the opposite of what its source said for two months.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. These are generated files under version control with no generator-vs-output check. cargo xtask verify's hub-build leg does regenerate them, but only as a side effect - a dirty worktree afterwards is not an error, and nobody looks. The failure is invisible in review (minified single line) and invisible in CI.

SHAPE OF A FIX. Two distinct checks, both repo-level reconciliations in the style the tree already uses for error-docs-page-missing, error-docs-sidebar-unlisted and ci-test-suite-unwired (cargo xtask lint, anchored at the offending file):

1. Embedded-version vs pin. For each dependency the bundle inlines and someone might bump (KaTeX at minimum), assert the version string embedded in the artifact equals the version resolved in that subproject's package-lock.json. This is the check that would have caught the Snyk revert.

2. Artifact freshness vs source. Assert the committed bundle is not older than the sources it is built from - e.g. compare the last commit touching hub-client/quarto-hub-sandboxed-preview/src/ against the last commit touching the artifacts it produces, and fail when the source is newer. This is the check that would have caught the service worker.

Worth deciding as part of this: whether these artifacts should be committed at all, or built in CI. Committing them is what creates the drift class; if there is a reason they must be committed (offline builds, include_dir!, fresh-clone bootstrap), record it here so the lint rule is clearly the right answer rather than a workaround.

DISCOVERED during bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj: a full cargo xtask verify regenerated both artifacts as a side effect, which is the only reason the drift surfaced. Corrected on main by 546fdd374 (rebuild) + b93c62c74 (changelog). Both artifacts are currently correct - this strand is about preventing the next occurrence, not about fixing them.

title: q2 preview: Firefox flaky 'Document automerge:<id> is unavailable' on cold start
description:
q2 preview shows a red 'Document automerge:<id> is unavailable' render error in Firefox (Chrome works fine). Reproduces every time on Firefox per user; intermittent/cold-start flavored.

DIAGNOSIS (this session, 2026-06-08):
- NOT stale browser state: each q2 preview run binds a new random port; automerge IndexedDB is keyed by origin (host+port) so storage is fresh every run. Doc always comes over the samod websocket.
- NOT converter content: 0-plain.qmd and full 5-full171.qmd both render perfectly in Chrome (plot/math/tables, no error). q2 render also works.
- Mechanism: ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/client.ts:381 connect() does waitForPeer() then findDoc() -> repo.find()+whenReady(). Against an ephemeral hub with no IndexedDB cache, the handle resolves to 'unavailable' if the doc has not synced when whenReady settles. Doc comment at client.ts:372-379 already flags this cold-start race. SPA mitigates with peerTimeoutMs=5000 (q2-preview-spa/src/PreviewApp.tsx:505) but that only waits for the peer EVENT, not for the doc to actually sync.
- Chrome happy path logs: 'Waiting for peer connection...' -> 'Peer connected - online mode'. Firefox loses the race (likely cold WASM compile of automerge_wasm + wasm_quarto_hub_client blocking the JS event loop / ws message processing past automerge-repo's request window).

NEXT STEPS to confirm + fix:
- Capture Firefox console: does it log 'Peer connected' or 'offline mode'? which doc id is unavailable (index vs qmd vs neither)? is the WS 101/connected?
- Likely robust fix: make findDoc resilient to the 'unavailable' handle state by re-requesting/retrying once the doc later syncs (automerge handles can recover from unavailable), instead of only widening peerTimeoutMs.
- chrome-devtools MCP is Chrome-only; needs manual Firefox capture or a Playwright-firefox e2e.
close_reason: Fixed and merged to main (merge a2fde1ce). Root cause: Firefox serializes WS opening handshakes per IP browser-wide; a hung handshake in any tab starved the preview's 5s peer budget, and the boot failure was permanent. Fix: health-arbitrated boot+reconnect (HTTP /health decides liveness, WS waits indefinitely), memory storage for preview, zombie-adapter terminal disconnect (StoppableWebSocketClientAdapter + Node adapter gate), docId re-fetch per reconnect attempt, Playwright firefox-ws-queue regression e2e (pre-fix fails with production error, post-fix passes). End-to-end verified in real Firefox: blackhole-starved boot renders; kill->banner->restart->auto-recovery; zero WS churn while server gone. Research: claude-notes/research/2026-06-11-firefox-ws-handshake-serialization.md; plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-11-firefox-ws-peer-timeout-fix.md. Upstream disconnect() fix prepared on cscheid/automerge-repo (PR to be opened by maintainers outreach). Follow-up filed: bd-dsgrew1x (pre-existing edit-cell-sizing e2e break).

c-5fyowdxb.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-5fyowdxb.text: ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-06-11 session): Firefox serializes WebSocket opening handshakes per host browser-wide (nsWSAdmissionManager) — only one CONNECTING websocket to 127.0.0.1 at a time across all tabs. Any tab holding a hung handshake (TCP accepted, 101 never sent — wedged/suspended local server) starves all new localhost WS handshakes for up to 20s/attempt (network.websocket.timeout.open). Preview SPA's 5s peer budget expires -> offline mode -> findDoc marks ephemeral doc unavailable -> permanent boot error. Reproduced with Playwright Firefox + blackhole TCP server (exact production error at t=5.29s); Chromium control connects in 59ms under identical conditions; closed-port control (fast RST) does NOT reproduce — a hung handshake is required. Server + clean-Firefox exonerated (10/10 Node handshakes <8ms; 15/15 clean Firefox loads ~260ms). Aggravators: 5s peer budget == adapter 5s retryInterval (first-attempt failure always fatal); no boot recovery when peer arrives late; IndexedDB open gates the WS join (independently verified failure path; preview should use memory storage); stale preview tabs retry dead ports forever. Full writeup + fix directions: claude-notes/research/2026-06-11-firefox-ws-handshake-serialization.md (repro scripts in claude-notes/tmp/).

title: q2: website.navbar / website.page-footer (nested form) not recognised by chrome transforms
description:

Not a Phase F regression — q2 has never supported the nested form. Filed so the docs site authoring loop isn't blocked indefinitely.

title: quarto-yaml: piecewise (Concat) content provenance for multi-line block scalars
description:
Follow-up to the 2026-08-20 diagnostic-span-integrity plan, which ships only the v1 half: content_source_info returns Some(contiguous) for plain and unescaped-quoted scalars, and None for block scalars. This strand replaces the None for multi-line block scalars with a real piecewise map.

WHY A SINGLE SPAN CANNOT WORK. The decoded content of a multi-line block scalar is not a contiguous source range. It is runs of source separated by the stripped per-line indentation:

      line one\n      line two\n      <span...
      |-indent-|        |-indent-|      |-indent-|
                ^^^^^^^^^         ^^^^^^^^^
                content runs (newline included, indent excluded)

A start/end pair can fix the first run and nothing after it. Measured today on a three-line page-footer.center, two Q-2-9 warnings that both belong on line 9 are reported at 8:10 and 9:14. The drift is 6 bytes per line boundary crossed and compounds without bound.

THE MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS. SourceInfo::Concat { pieces } is exactly a piecewise map: each SourcePiece carries offset_in_concat, length, and its own source_info, and map_offset already locates the containing piece and recurses into it. Block-scalar content provenance is a Concat of one piece per line, each pointing at that line's post-indent range. Then map_offset(content_offset) simply works.

VERIFIED PREREQUISITES (checked against quarto-source-map 0.1.0, so this is known-viable rather than hoped-for):

- SourceInfo::concat(Vec<(SourceInfo, usize)>) is PUBLIC and SourcePiece's fields are all pub, so it is constructible from quarto-yaml. NO new quarto-source-map API is needed.
- concat() assigns offset_in_concat cumulatively, so pieces are contiguous in concat space by construction. This disposes of a wrinkle in Concat::map_offset, where length() sums piece lengths while the exclusive-end branch tests last.offset_in_concat + last.length. Those agree for anything built via concat(); they can only diverge in a hand-built Concat.
- block_scalar_len (crates/quarto-yaml/src/parser.rs:853) ALREADY iterates the block line by line, with the indent width and a running consumed offset in scope. Emitting the run list is a refactor of existing code, not new analysis.

NO CONSUMER CHANGE. q2's call site is written in the plan's Phase 4 as a match on Option<SourceInfo> with a precision-fallback None arm. Going from None to Some(Concat) is a pure precision improvement: no signature change, no q2 edit. That is precisely why the plan chose Option<SourceInfo> over a span-plus-verbatim-flag.

Note this class of drift would also have CRASHED before the quarto-error-reporting char-boundary fix (bd-ariadne-config-span-char-boundary-panic-rkqmhzrg): an accumulating drift lands mid-character at least as readily as a constant -1.

title: Perf: SourceInfo::map_offset clones the whole file content per call; process_list calls it twice per list item (quadratic on api/index.qmd)
description: quarto-source-map 0.1.3 mapping.rs map_offset(): 'let content = match &file.content { Some(c) => c.clone(), None => read_to_string }' clones the entire file String only to pass '&content' to FileInformation::offset_to_location, which takes &str. pampa::pandoc::treesitter::process_list calls map_offset(length) up to twice per list item for loose/tight detection. On the Connect docs api/index.qmd (1.1 MB, 15,771 list items) that is ~31k full-file clones: 480 of the 1821 samples on the worker that rendered it (26% of that document's CPU), and that document is the whole-project wall-clock critical path (render api/index.qmd alone = 1.5 s of the 2.0 s parallel render). Whole-project: 3.8% of all CPU, the single largest memmove caller. title: User theme .scss compile error is swallowed: page silently ships DEFAULT_CSS with no diagnostic at any verbosity
description:
A Sass error inside a user-supplied theme .scss file (listed in `theme:`) is swallowed at render time: the page silently ships the ~7KB DEFAULT_CSS instead of the compiled Bootstrap bundle, and nothing reaches the user — not the CLI summary, not `-v`/`-vv`, not `RUST_LOG=quarto_core=debug`. The render reports "Rendered N of N files" with zero warnings. Observed with q2 0.28.0 on macOS, HEAD 85e98fb02.

## Repro

_quarto.yml:

    project:
      type: website
    brand: _brand.yml
    format:
      html:
        theme: [brand, theme.scss]

theme.scss (a perfectly well-formed layered file):

    /*-- scss:defaults --*/
    $grid-body-width: 52rem;

`q2 render` succeeds. `_site/site_libs/quarto/quarto-theme-<fp>.css` is 6996 bytes ("styles.css / Default styles for Quarto HTML documents") rather than ~330KB. Brand fonts, colors, the custom rules — all gone. Changing the value to `830px` restores the full bundle: the grid mixins (resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-mixins.scss, `$grid-body-column-max` and the `calc(830px - 3em)` grid tracks) do arithmetic that fails on rem, so grass raises an incompatible-units error. That is a *user* configuration error with a precise Sass location — exactly the kind of thing that should be a diagnostic.

## Where

crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/compile_theme_css.rs:713-735 (`variant_css`): the Err arm of `compile_with_doc_vars_via_runtime` emits `trace_event!(ctx, EventLevel::Warn, "theme CSS compilation failed: {}, using default CSS", e)` and returns `Ok(DEFAULT_CSS)`. The wrapper (compile_theme_css.rs:1010-1030) stringifies the SassError, so the grass error text (file, line, message) is available but discarded. In practice the Warn trace event is not visible on the CLI at any verbosity I tried, so from the user's seat the failure is completely silent.

## Relationship to existing strands

- bd-36vmz7nk is the policy question (silent fallback vs hard error). This strand is a concrete user-facing data point for it: a one-line unit mistake in the user's own SCSS wipes the whole theme with no signal.
- bd-qmpygp02 covers the InvalidScssFile (missing layer markers) case and explicitly keeps "internal compiler failures" on the fallback. A grass compile error originating in a user theme file is not an internal failure — it is a user error and should get the same structured treatment (a Q-14-x diagnostic carrying the Sass file/line/message).

## Fix shape

Route SassError::Compile (or whatever grass surfaces) through theme_diagnostic as a hard error when the failing input includes a user theme entry, keeping the DEFAULT_CSS fallback only for the no-user-theme default bundle. At minimum, promote the trace event to a real user-visible warning in the render summary so the render is not reported as clean.

Discovered 2026-09-08 while setting up _brand.yml + custom SCSS for cscheid-net-2026.

title: Unresolved footnote reference renders as an invisible empty span with no diagnostic
description:
A named footnote reference `[^id]` whose definition is missing renders as an EMPTY `` — no marker, no text, no diagnostic. The reader sees nothing at all where the footnote should be. ## Mechanism pampa's postprocess lowers `[^id]` into a *contentless* `Span` carrying only `class="quarto-note-reference"` and `data-reference-id=` (see `crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs`, the `.with_note_reference` filter). `FootnotesTransform` then tries to resolve it, and on failure deliberately leaves it alone: crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/footnotes.rs:445-450 if let Some(number) = collector.resolve_reference(&ref_id, source_info.clone()) { *inline = create_footnote_ref(number, &source_info, collector.is_margin); } // If not resolved, leave as-is (broken reference). Because the span it leaves has no children, the writer emits `` — zero visible output. ## What Quarto 1 / Pandoc do Pandoc keeps the literal text `[^id]` in the output AND emits a warning (`[WARNING] Note with key 'x' defined ... but not used.` for the mirror case). Either half would be an improvement here; today q2 does neither. ## Why this matters independently of the parser bug Found while investigating bd-adjacent-footnote-definitions-miif1k1z, which is the parser-side cause of one *particular* unresolved reference. That strand's fix makes adjacent definitions parse correctly — but it does NOT touch this path, so any ordinary typo in a note id will keep vanishing silently after it lands. This is the "silently" half of that strand's title, and it survives the fix. ## Repro Ref[^nosuchnote]. Renders as `

Ref.

` — the reader sees "Ref." with no indication anything was lost. Exit code 0, no diagnostic. ## Suggested direction Two candidate behaviors, not yet settled: 1. Emit a diagnostic (new `Q-*` code — remember the `error-docs-page-missing` lint requires a `docs/errors//.qmd` page in the SAME commit). 2. Fall back to rendering the literal `[^id]` text so the reference is at least visible, matching Pandoc. They are not exclusive; doing both is probably right. title: q2's jupyter text engine partitions cells with a nesting-blind regex; it disagrees with knitr on the same document
description:
Finding 4 of bd-ts-engine-display-fence-joy59gkr. Verified on q2 HEAD 00a1c1702.

crates/quarto-core/src/engine/jupyter/text_execute.rs:128 finds executable cells with

  (?m)^```\s*\{(\w+)\}\s*\n([\s\S]*?)^```\s*$

No backtick-run tracking at all — weaker than the TS breakQuartoMd it sits beside, and weaker than the AST one function call away.

MEASURED (temporary #[test] against the private parse_code_blocks, since jupyter is not installed on this machine — these are function-level results, not end-to-end):

  P1 display block only, no real cell        -> 1 block   (would execute display content)
  P2 real cell + nested display              -> 2 blocks  (executes display content)
  P3 indented {python} cell in a list item   -> 0 blocks  (real cell NEVER runs)
  P4 two real top-level cells                -> 2 blocks  (control)

P3 is the interesting one and it is independent of display blocks: it is a disagreement between two BUILT-IN engines on identical input. The same document shaped for R renders correctly — r5-indented-real.qmd produces a proper <div class="cell"> with cell-output-stdout under knitr (verified end-to-end). Shaped for python, jupyter would silently pass it through unexecuted.

The information is not missing at that point: serialize_ast_to_qmd -> pampa::writers::qmd, and determine_backticks (qmd.rs:1522) emits max_backticks+1, so the string handed to the engine preserves indentation and fence nesting byte-for-byte (confirmed with pampa -t qmd). The AST knew; the engine throws it away and re-derives it badly.

FIX DIRECTION: this is q2's own Rust, with no protocol implications — feed execute_qmd the AST-derived cell ranges instead of having it find them.

WHAT BREAKS: execute_qmd splices outputs by byte offset, and code_start-anchored figure attribution (main #412) keys off the same offsets. Both have to move together.

An end-to-end confirmation of P1-P3 needs a machine with jupyter installed; that is the first task on this strand.

Full analysis: claude-notes/research/2026-08-27-ts-engine-display-fence.md

title: Reader skips warning-collector diagnostics when parse errors are present in the same document
description:
In crates/pampa/src/readers/qmd.rs:144, when tree-sitter parsing produces errors, `read` returns `Err(diagnostics)` *before* invoking `treesitter_to_pandoc` (line 167). The latter is where the warning-collector pass runs — including the Q-2-36 path-A diagnostic site in `treesitter.rs::process_fenced_code_block`.

Effect: a document with **both** a parse-error form (e.g. `\`\`\`{r test}`) and a warning-collector-emitted form (e.g. `\`\`\`{r echo=FALSE}`) reports only the parse error. The user has to fix the parse error and re-run to discover the second issue.

Reproduction (from Q-2-36 Phase 3 verification, 2026-05-14):

\`\`\`
$ printf '%s\n' '\`\`\`{r test}' '1+1' '\`\`\`' '' '\`\`\`{python echo=FALSE}' 'print()' '\`\`\`' | cargo run --bin pampa --
[31mError:[0m [Q-2-36] Old-style knitr chunk options are not supported
   ... (only the {r test} error; the {python echo=FALSE} block is silent)
\`\`\`

Compare to single-block variants — each individually fires Q-2-36 correctly (verified with /tmp/q236-cases/case2-7 individually).

Why this is pre-existing (NOT a Phase 1 regression): the code at qmd.rs:144 has not changed in the bd-j4fe work. At HEAD (`e2d224f6`), the same behavior held — the Q-2-8 *warning* would have been silently dropped when a parse error was present elsewhere in the document. The shape of the limitation just becomes more noticeable now that the path-A site produces an *error* rather than a warning, because users now expect both halves of a 'do not use knitr syntax' diagnostic to fire together.

Possible fixes (not designed yet — needs scoping):

1. Run `treesitter_to_pandoc` regardless of parse-error presence. Risk: the function may panic or produce garbage on ERROR-node-containing trees. Needs an audit + likely some defensive plumbing.

2. A two-pass approach: separate AST construction (which can fail) from warning-collector emission (which is independent). Refactor.

3. Limited fix: walk the tree once for warning emission, then run `treesitter_to_pandoc` only if `had_errors()` is false. Conceptually clean but requires factoring out the warning pass from `process_fenced_code_block`.

This is scope-creep relative to bd-j4fe (Q-2-36); filing as `discovered-from` so it doesn't block the Q-2-36 ship.

Discovered during: bd-j4fe Phase 3 verification (claude-notes/plans/2026-05-14-q-2-36-knitr-style-chunk-options.md).

title: Engine subprocess failures lose their stderr detail in the normal render path
description:
In a normal `q2 render`, a failing knitr subprocess produces an `ExecutionError` whose message is the bare fallback "R process failed" — the actual R diagnostic never reaches it.

**Mechanism (verified in-tree):**
- `ExecutionContext` defaults `quiet: false` (crates/quarto-core/src/engine/context.rs:179).
- `crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/subprocess.rs:371-374` branches on it: `if options.quiet { cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped()) } else { cmd.stderr(Stdio::inherit()) }`.
- With stderr inherited, the classifier sees an **empty** stderr string, so subprocess.rs:485-489 falls through to `"R process failed".to_string()` with no detail.
- Nothing in the render chain ever sets `ExecutionContext.quiet = true`. `RenderToFileOptions::quiet` (render_to_file.rs:91) is a separate *logging* flag and is never threaded into `ExecutionContext`. The `CallROptions::quiet()` call sites at subprocess.rs:922/983/1041 are tests.

**Consequences.** The detailed R message (e.g. `Installation of Python not found…` from reticulate) is real and visible on the *inherited* terminal, so an interactive user sees it scroll past — but the structured error q2 produces carries none of it. Any consumer that isn't a human at a TTY loses the detail entirely: the hub, `q2 preview`, the MCP server, CI logs that capture only q2's own output, the JSON trace, and tests asserting on error content. It also means an error-classification improvement cannot be tested through the real render path.

**How it surfaced.** Task 2 of the nested-cell-masking plan wrote a render-tier test (T5) that needed to distinguish 'the displayed {python} was executed by reticulate' from 'R is broken for unrelated reasons', so it asserted the error mentions python/reticulate. That assertion cannot pass through `render_document_to_file`'s default path. The test was widened to accept either the detailed message or today's documented bare-fallback shape, with the trace recorded in a code comment; it still rejects the failure classes it cares about (missing package, missing runtime, spawn failure, a real knitr message all classify distinctly).

**Fix direction.** Thread stderr capture independently of the quiet/logging concern — capture stderr always (tee it to the terminal when not quiet, rather than choosing between capturing and showing it), so the classifier and the `ExecutionError` get the real text in every path. Tightening T5's assertion back to the detailed message is a good acceptance test for the fix.

Found during bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-02-nested-cell-masking.md

title: Self-heal re-anchor DROPs edit on collaborator insert-above (findReanchorCandidate single-nearest)
description:
findReanchorCandidate (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/lockedTiles.ts ~409) checks only ONE re-anchor candidate: exact (r[0]===anchorR0) else the single nearest r[0]>=anchorR0, and returns null if that one fails content-verify. When a collaborator inserts enough text ABOVE the active edit that a PRECEDING block's new r[0] lands at-or-past the active block's OLD anchorR0, the 'nearest' slot is the wrong (preceding) block -> content-verify fails -> the open editor DROPs and the in-flight edit is silently lost.

BROADER THAN PREVIOUSLY DOCUMENTED: affects TOP-LEVEL Phase-2 blocks, not just nested children. The plan's 'Nested-child self-heal DROP' watch-item claimed 'Phase-2 unaffected (you edit whole containers, which self-match)' -- that is wrong. The jsdom p2-3b-real §3b KEEP test only passes because its fixture insert (4 bytes) is smaller than the inter-block gap (6 bytes); with realistic paragraph sizes (28-byte insert > 19-byte gap) it DROPs. Demonstrated by the browser-tier tripwire test hub-client/e2e/q2-preview-self-heal-on-write.spec.ts (currently test.fail()).

CANDIDATE FIX (a): scan ALL pool entries r[0]>=anchorR0 in ascending order, return the first that content-verifies (instead of giving up after the single nearest). ~5 lines, client-only. Needs a Phase-2 jsdom regression pass. TRADEOFF to assess: duplicate-content blocks (two identical slices + large shift) could mis-anchor instead of drop. CANDIDATE FIX (b): content-addressed relocation via a position-independent AST-subtree hash from q2's reconciliation/coarsen pipeline (heavier).

When fixed: flip the e2e test.fail() -> green guard (Playwright will flag the unexpected pass). Discovered during the 'self-heal on write' task 2026-06-13.

title: Cross-document dedup of identical Lua diagnostics in a project render
description:
During a project render, each document gets its own Lua state (per document, per filter file, per pre/post pass — see filter.rs:250, pipeline.rs:346,348), so a diagnostic emitted by an extension that runs on every page is repeated once per page with no dedup anywhere above the document.

Concretely: the Posit Connect docs' mermaid-zoom extension produced 33 identical Q-11-1 warnings (one per mermaid diagram). Fixing the intra-call ordering bug in add_html_dependency (bd-add-html-dependency-version-5tnub5ds) reduces that to 14 — one per page — but cannot go lower, because the dedup state does not survive the document boundary.

There is no cross-document diagnostic dedup infrastructure today; grep for 'dedup' in quarto-core turns up only artifact-bytes dedup (artifact.rs:328-356). The natural seam is ProjectRenderSummary at the CLI boundary, which diagnostic_policy.rs's module docs already identify as the point every per-document diagnostic passes through on its way to a frontend (it is where --strict's warnings-to-errors promotion happens).

Design questions this needs, none of them settled: what counts as 'identical' (code + message text? + location?); whether to collapse silently or emit something like 'and 13 more occurrences'; whether it applies to errors as well as warnings; and whether suppression (diagnostics: <code>: level: off) interacts with it. Note that Q-11-1 is the generic Lua-diagnostic code stamped on every quarto.warn/quarto.error (diagnostics.rs:379,386), so per-code granularity is blunt for exactly the case that motivated this.

Filed for eventual review, deliberately NOT folded into bd-add-html-dependency-version-5tnub5ds (new infrastructure, separate design).

title: q2 render <large-non-project-dir> also walks the tree before erroring
description:
Symmetric to bd-nmkmi but on the with-arguments path: `q2 render <dir>` where `<dir>` has no ancestor `_quarto.yml` walks the directory tree for `.qmd` files before deciding it's not a project. In `crates/quarto/src/commands/render.rs::classify_inputs` (lines ~206-235), each resolved input is passed to `ProjectContext::discover`, which falls through to the recursive walk on directory inputs without a project marker. The walk's output is discarded by the subsequent `is_real_project` check, then the `is_dir` branch returns `NoRenderableMatches`.

Same fix pattern as bd-nmkmi: short-circuit the "directory input, no ancestor `_quarto.yml`" case using `find_project_root_upward` before calling `ProjectContext::discover`.

Lower priority (P3) than bd-nmkmi (P2) because the user has to explicitly point `q2 render` at a directory to hit it — much less common than the bare `q2 render`. Filed as discovered-from to keep the fix scope-disciplined.

title: q2 preview: logo image (logo: logo.svg) 404s — asset walker misses meta-driven raw-HTML images
description: AUDIT (2026-06-17, confirmed in browser). With footer/logo DOM now emitted (bd-n2w0sxgd), the logo FAILS TO LOAD in q2 preview (naturalWidth 0). Network: GET /logo.svg -> 200 text/html (the SPA shell), i.e. logo.svg is NOT in the preview's served VFS asset set, so the catch-all returns index.html. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): the parent-side asset walker (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/assetWalker.ts::collectImagePaths) only collects AST Image nodes (obj.t === 'Image'). The logo comes from metadata (logo: logo.svg), rendered by RevealFooterLogoTransform into rendered.reveal.logo as a RAW HTML string, injected by RevealChrome via dangerouslySetInnerHTML. It is never an Image AST node, so: 1. buildAssetManifest never mints a blob URL for logo.svg, and 2. the raw bypasses the React component that rewrites src against the manifest. Hence src stays 'logo.svg' -> /logo.svg -> not in VFS -> 404-as-200-html. In native render this works because logo.svg sits next to slides.html on disk; in VFS-mode preview nothing copies/serves it. Note: ResourceCollectorTransform is also a no-op in vfs_root mode (resource_collector.rs:96), by design — the asset walker is the producer in preview. FIX OPTIONS (needs a design decision): (A) Walker also collects meta.logo (+ other known meta image keys) and RevealChrome rewrites the injected src via AssetManifestContext before injection. Targeted; couples RevealChrome to the manifest. (B) Generalize the walker to scan rendered.reveal.* / rendered.navigation.* HTML strings for src=/href= asset refs, mint blobs, and have the injecting slots rewrite. More general (covers footer images, navbar logos, etc.). (C) Represent logo as a real Image AST node somewhere the walker sees it (and render through ). Biggest change. Recommend (B) as the general solution; (A) as a quick win. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-17-revealjs-preview-render-parity-audit.md (F5).

c-0vto1r8b.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-0vto1r8b.text: LAYER 1 DONE (commit bc5b27db, feature/revealjs-preview-render-parity). resolve_single_file_deps now expands document resources: into binary_files (reuses extract_resource_patterns + expand_patterns; globs supported), riding the existing single_file_assets -> with_binary_files VFS sync. Tests: single_file_deps_includes_declared_resources + _glob (8/8 green). E2E: real q2 preview, deck with 'logo: logo.svg' + 'resources: [logo.svg]' (logo NOT a md image) -> 'Discovered project files binary_count=1'; without resources: -> binary_count=0. REMAINING: Layer 2 (serve bytes to the raw ; the logo still 404s without it). Decision pending: (a) per-asset rewrite contained to preview-renderer (walker collects meta.logo/meta.resources -> blob; RevealChrome rewrites src/href via AssetManifestContext), OR defer until (b) the bd-msp0 service-worker path-server (touches hub-client + quarto-hub.com) is on the table. Leaving open for the Layer 2 decision.

c-pg7y4hlp.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-pg7y4hlp.text: FEASIBILITY (user proposal: let asset detection honor document-level 'resources:'). Does NOT already work, but it's feasible and well-aligned with existing code. TWO LAYERS: LAYER 1 — bytes into the VFS (the part the user means; small, clean). The single-file dep resolver crates/quarto-preview/src/config.rs::resolve_single_file_deps (bd-9cyza5vy) already runs the real parse+include stages and collects image deps via collect_referenced_asset_urls(blocks). Adding document-level resources: is a natural extension right there: call quarto_core::project_resources::extract_resource_patterns(&doc.ast.meta, ["resources"]) (already used in document_profile.rs:569 + resource_report.rs) then expand_patterns(canonical_root, deck_dir_anchor, patterns, ResourceOrigin::DocumentMetadata, ResourceScope::...) (already used in THIS file for project resources, config.rs:129-150) and fold matches into SingleFileDeps.binary_files. Reuses the exact publish-path machinery (globs included), so 'declare resources: once -> works for publish AND preview'. Not reveal-specific; helps any single-file doc referencing assets the AST walker can't see (raw HTML, shortcodes, css url(), logo:). Bonus: config.rs:122 notes resources: is already the interim trust boundary for what may upload to a sync server, so feeding it into the VFS sync is on-policy. LAYER 2 — actually SERVE those bytes (necessary; layer 1 alone is insufficient). The logo is a raw injected by RevealChrome; it fetches /logo.svg -> SPA catch-all (200 text/html), never going through (which swaps blob URLs). Options: (a) TS asset walker also mints blobs for meta.resources/logo: and RevealChrome rewrites raw src/href against the manifest (targeted, works now); (b) service-worker VFS-by-path server (bd-msp0 epic) serves /logo.svg from the VFS directly — general, future-proof, no rewriting; this is the 'alleviate a lot of future problems' win. RECOMMEND: do Layer 1 (resources:->VFS) regardless (cheap, publish-parity). Pair with (b) service worker for the general fix, or (a) for a quick interim. Awaiting user direction on scope.

title: [websites] Sidebar vertical border missing (Q1 parity) — needs doc-derived SCSS variables seam
description:
Quarto 1 renders a faint vertical line between a docked sidebar and main content; Quarto 2 does not. Verified visually in examples/websites/03-nested-sidebar (q1-site has it, _site does not). 

Root cause: two missing pieces in Q2.

1. The SCSS rule '.sidebar.sidebar-navigation:not(.rollup) { border-right: 1px solid $table-border-color !important; }' (gated by '@if $sidebar-border') exists in Q1 (quarto-cli/src/resources/projects/website/navigation/quarto-nav.scss:552-556) but was never ported to resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss in Q2.

2. Q2 has no mechanism to inject per-document SCSS variables before the framework defaults. CompileThemeCssStage only reads theme config from doc.ast.meta; it never threads website.sidebar info into the SCSS bundle. Q1's format-html-scss.ts:631-642 synthesizes '$sidebar-border: <bool>;' per-document, defaulting to (style == 'docked').

Customization: end users override via 'sidebar.border: true|false' in YAML (Q1). Color follows the active Bootstrap/Bootswatch theme via $table-border-color (no special handling needed — themes already override it).

Phased plan in claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-sidebar-vertical-border.md:
- Phase 1: port the @if $sidebar-border SCSS rule.
- Phase 2: introduce derive_doc_scss_layer hook in CompileThemeCssStage; emit $sidebar-border per-document. Generic enough to reuse for sidebar/navbar/footer bg+fg later.
- Phase 3: add 'border: Option<bool>' field to Sidebar struct for full Q1 parity.
- Phase 4: end-to-end verification + docs.

Phase 2 also tightens the theme CSS cache key to include the doc-vars layer so two docs with different sidebar configs don't collide on the generic 'default_minified' key.

Plan file: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-sidebar-vertical-border.md
close_reason: Implemented across 4 phases: Phase 1 ported the @if $sidebar-border SCSS rule from quarto-cli quarto-nav.scss:552-556 into resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss. Phase 2 introduced derive_doc_scss_layer() in CompileThemeCssStage and quarto_sass::compile_with_doc_vars() to thread per-document SCSS variables through the bundle ahead of framework defaults. Phase 3 added Sidebar.border (Option<bool>) for full Q1 parity on the sidebar.border knob. Phase 4 verified end-to-end via cargo run --bin q2 -- render on examples/websites/03-nested-sidebar — the rule now appears in the emitted CSS — and documented the knob in docs/navigation.qmd. Follow-up bd-8oqw filed for refactoring cache_key into a structured CompileInputs value type.

title: Parse-error codes are keyed on tree-sitter state, so new failures inherit an unrelated code's wording
description:
The qmd parse-error message table is keyed on {tree-sitter parser state, symbol} rather than on anything about the input, so any input that fails in a state already claimed by a corpus case inherits that case's diagnosis -- with its confident, specific wording.

Mechanism. crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json maps entries like {state: 3603, sym: "pandoc_str_token1"} -> Q-2-34. Lookup is crates/pampa/src/readers/qmd_error_message_table.rs (lookup_error_message / lookup_error_entry over the embedded table). The table is generated by ./scripts/build_error_table.ts, which writes a .qmd per corpus case, runs the parser, and records whatever state each case fails in.

Observed instance. '{{< kbd mac=Command-\u{2192} >}}' is reported as

    [Q-2-34] Unquoted shortcode parameter starting with digit
    Shortcode parameter values starting with digits must be quoted.

Nothing in that input starts with a digit. Q-2-34's own corpus entry (resources/error-corpus/Q-2-34.json) is about 'k=1b' and 'size=1x', which genuinely are digit-initial. The non-ASCII input merely happens to fail in state 3603.

Why this is worse than an uncoded error. An uncoded 'unexpected character or token here' tells the author nothing but is honest. This tells the author something specific and false, and sends them looking for a digit that does not exist. The wording carries a code, so it also looks searchable and authoritative.

Scope -- this is not one bad message. The keying means the misattribution is systemic: every future parse failure that lands in an already-claimed state inherits that state's message, silently, with no signal that the match was coincidental. The corpus grows by feature PRs adding cases; the set of claimed states grows with it.

Suggested mitigation (from the reporting strand): validate at emit time that the captured span actually satisfies the claimed condition, and fall back to the generic parse error when it does not. That keeps the specific messages where they are earned without inventing a new keying scheme. A stronger version would attach a predicate to each corpus entry rather than relying on state coincidence.

Measured non-finding, for whoever picks this up. Widening the shortcode_naked_string token (the fix for the two sibling parse strands) renumbers tree-sitter states and therefore invalidates the generated table. I tested whether that scrambles existing attributions: with a deliberately stale table and a widened parser, the first case of all 33 corpus codes still resolved to the correct code (matched=33, mismatched=0). So the table is more robust to renumbering than the keying suggests, and this bug is NOT a blocker for those fixes -- but ./scripts/build_error_table.ts should still be re-run per the documented procedure in crates/pampa/CLAUDE.md.

Discovered while investigating bd-shortcode-naked-value-nonascii-47fzbmow, which documents this as its 'defect 2'; this strand carries it independently because it survives that strand's grammar fix and affects far more than shortcodes.

c-4nhhrm9c.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-4nhhrm9c.text:
Repro handoff from the shortcode naked-string widening work (branch braid/bd-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-2u79bqp1-shortcode-escaped-gt, commits e223edd52..2477d2816).

THIS STRAND'S ORIGINAL REPRODUCER IS NOW RETIRED. '{{< kbd mac=Command-→ >}}' no longer misreports as Q-2-34 because it no longer fails at all -- the naked-string token was widened from an ASCII allowlist to a blocklist, so non-ASCII parses cleanly. Do not read that as this strand being fixed: the {state, sym} keying is untouched.

REPLACEMENT REPRODUCER (measured on the widened parser at 2477d2816):

    printf '{{< hello\n' | ./target/debug/pampa -t native

reports Q-2-27 'Line Break Before Shortcode Close', message 'Line breaks are not allowed immediately before the shortcode closing delimiter >}}.' The input contains no >}} anywhere -- it is a plain unterminated shortcode, not one whose close was preceded by a line break. Same pattern as the original: a recovery state already claimed by another corpus case lends its confident, specific wording to unrelated input.

ALSO MEASURED, relevant to the third outcome noted in c-jk1na0st: three inputs that still fail after the widening now produce the GENERIC uncoded parse error rather than a wrong code --
    {{< kbd = >}}   (bare '=', the bd-kx25ovmh parity gap)
    {{< kbd > >}}   (bare '>')
    {{< kbd "x >}}  (argument starting with a quote)
Each emits 'Error: Parse error / unexpected character or token here' with no Q- code (verified by grep -oE 'Q-[0-9]+-[0-9]+' returning no match).

CONTROL, still correct: '{{< fa envelope size=2x >}}' -> Q-2-34, the legitimate case for that code (shortcode_number's prec(3) beats the naked token regardless of the widening).

NET: the widening shrank this strand's surface but did not close it. One clear misattribution survives, with a fresh one-line repro.

c-jk1na0st.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-jk1na0st.text: Adjacent case worth designing alongside this: bd-render-failure-unattributed-yxe0v7th. Same table, opposite end of the failure space -- there an input produces a fatal 'Error: Parse error / unexpected character or token here' with NO frame at all (no path, line, column or snippet), three times, while every other parse error in the same render carries a full ariadne frame. So the state-keyed table has three outcomes, not two: claimed state gives a specific message (sometimes the wrong one, this strand), unclaimed state gives the generic message WITH a span, and some path gives the generic message with no span at all. The third is the one that loses the file name entirely, and cost the Positron port weeks of misattribution -- it was read as a freeze bug because nothing in the output pointed anywhere else.

title: Preview: resolve embedded static-asset iframes from the VFS source path
description:
Make .embed-example-iframe iframes resolve in q2 preview AND in real hub-client (Automerge/VFS-backed) projects, the VFS-native way — NOT via a disk HTTP route (that CLI-only shortcut was prototyped and reverted).

Problem: in preview the page renders in-browser via WASM; the iframe src is the artifact-prefixed /.quarto/project-artifacts/examples/.../slides.html (page_url_for vfs mode). The TS iframe post-processor (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/utils/iframePostProcessor.ts) reads /.quarto/ srcs from the VFS and inlines them as data URIs — but the staged deck lives at its VFS SOURCE path (examples/.../slides.html), not the rendered-artifact path, so it misses. Project resources: copying that would place it at the artifact path is native-only (copy_resources_to_output_dir is cfg(not(wasm32))).

Chosen design (confirmed with user): option B — post-processor SOURCE-PATH FALLBACK. When an iframe/asset src is /.quarto/project-artifacts/X and the artifact path misses in the VFS, strip ARTIFACT_ROOT and read X from the VFS source path. Avoids option A (a WASM resource-copy that would re-duplicate ~6MB of decks into the VFS artifact tree on EVERY render — bloating the Automerge doc + sync traffic). Reading source bytes on demand has no duplication.

Two parts:
1. iframePostProcessor.ts (+ maybe assetWalker.ts): artifact-path miss -> source-path read fallback (strip /.quarto/project-artifacts/). TS unit/integration tests already exist for this module (iframePostProcessor.integration.test.ts).
2. Ensure the resource bytes are in the VFS source. Referenced images already are (assetWalker reads them), so confirm the resources: set / static decks are synced too; broaden the q2-preview VFS sync filter (.qmd+config) if needed.

title: qmd writer: position-dependent escapes (`:`, `'`/`"` unbalanced, `1.`/`-`/`+` line-start list markers)
description:
Discovered during the bd-21gu Phase 2 audit (claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-at-escape-qmd-roundtrip.md). The qmd writer's escape_markdown helper is char-by-char and has no position context, so it can't fix escapes that depend on whether a char is at line-start or in unbalanced-quote position. The Phase 2 audit identified four bug classes that all need the same shape of fix:

1. `:` at line start — triggers fenced div parser. Mid-line `:` is fine.
   Repro: a Str body containing ":word" at the start of a line round-trips
   to a parse error.

2. `'` and `"` unbalanced — when a Str body coming from JSON contains a
   literal `'` or `"` (not part of a Quoted node), the writer emits it
   unescaped and the re-parser produces an unclosed-quote error. Mid-word
   apostrophe (`a'b`) round-trips fine via smart-quote handling.

3. `1.`/`-`/`+` followed by Space at line start — Str "1." + Space + Str
   "foo" round-trips to OrderedList. Same for unordered list markers `-` /
   `+` followed by space at line start. The dot/dash itself is innocuous
   mid-word but becomes a list-marker trigger only at line-start with a
   following space.

   Repro:
   printf '1\\. foo\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t native
   → OrderedList (1, Decimal, Period) [[Plain [Str "foo"]]]
   Expected: Para [Str "1.", Space, Str "foo"]

Common requirement: writer needs (a) line-start tracking and (b) lookahead
across adjacent inline nodes to know whether escaping is needed for the
current character. This is a larger refactor than escape_markdown can
absorb — likely a new pass over the inline sequence in write_para or a
position-aware writer-context flag that get_str consults.

title: knitr executes a {r} fence nested inside a display block, and replaces the displayed example with its own cell scaffolding
description:
Finding 3 of bd-ts-engine-display-fence-joy59gkr. Verified on q2 HEAD 00a1c1702 with knitr 1.50. Inherited from Quarto 1 — NOT a q2 regression.

REPRO (r1-real-plus-nested.qmd): one real {r} cell, plus a four-backtick markdown display block whose content is a three-backtick {r} fence. Both bodies execute — 2 REAL-CELL-RAN and 2 DISPLAY-BLOCK-RAN in the HTML.

The damage is worse than 'it also ran'. The display block's content is REPLACED by knitr's intermediate markup and shown to the reader as literal text:

  <pre class="markdown"><code>::: {.cell}
  ```{.r .cell-code}
  cat("DISPLAY-BLOCK-RAN\n")
  ```
  ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
  ...

The author wrote a ```{r} example; the reader is shown ::: {.cell} and {.r .cell-code}. Indented display blocks behave the same (r6-indented-display.qmd).

TRIGGER: reachable only when the engine is ALREADY live. r2-nested-only.qmd — display block, no real cell — executes nothing, because AST-based resolution (computational_languages, resolution.rs:250) correctly declines to start knitr. One added real cell anywhere in the document turns every displayed example into a live cell.

WHY THIS IS FILED AS wontfix-candidate: knitr's own scanner (all_patterns$md$chunk.begin) partitions the string in R. q2 hands it the whole document (engine/knitr/mod.rs:142) and has no seam short of escaping nested fences before hand-off, which would corrupt the display content a different way. Fixing it means negotiating with knitr upstream. Filed so the behaviour is recorded, not because a q2-side fix is proposed.

Contrast: the julia engine gets this right (QuartoNotebookRunner parses in Julia and is nesting- and indentation-correct), and marimo gets the top-level case right via breakQuartoMd's length guard.

Full analysis: claude-notes/research/2026-08-27-ts-engine-display-fence.md

c-9ix72y2a.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-9ix72y2a.text:
IMPLEMENTED — PR #650 (https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/650), remote branch bugfix/bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj, 6 commits off main b93c62c74. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-02-nested-cell-masking.md (all phases reconciled).

This overturns the wontfix-candidate framing. The seam does exist: engine_execution.rs's per-engine loop. mask() rewrites ```{r} to ```{.r q2-nested-executable} before serialize_ast_to_qmd, and the leading dot defeats all three partitioners at once — knitr's chunk.begin, q2's jupyter parse_code_blocks, and the TS breakQuartoMd each require an alphanumeric first character after '{'. unmask() then restores byte-identically over the engine's returned markdown, which is what answers the original objection about corrupting the display content a different way: reconcile keeps the block in blocks_kept with its own source_info instead of replacing it with the .rmarkdown intermediate's.

The language predicate is engine-agnostic (every braced opener, not just the current engine's languages). That is what fixes the worst symptom, which the strand did not name: a displayed {python} example in an R document does not merely render wrong, it kills the render, because knitr hands the unclaimed language to reticulate. Blockquoted display blocks are fixed too — unmask is deliberately not ^-anchored, since knitr's own pattern is ^[\t >]*.

Provenance: masked blocks, and the top-level ancestor of a nested one, get SourceInfo::Generated with by.kind = nested-cell-mask, so map_offset returns None rather than an offset that resolves past the lengthened block into the next block's source. Marking lives only on the short-lived clone.

Deliberate scope-outs: RawBlock (bd-4gzwls31 — the writer emits those unfenced, so masking downgrades 'wrongly executed' to 'silently mangled'), doubled-brace {{lang}} (bd-q250-nested-fence-blind-spot-t68z1lsw, a diagnostics gap rather than an execution one), {=html} openers, and a cell nested inside a real cell.

Verification: 31 new tests across four tiers; full cargo xtask verify green (all 14 steps), workspace run 13621 passed / 199 skipped / 0 failed against a live baseline of 13590 — delta accounted exactly. docs/guides/authoring/computations.qmd expanded, deliberately with no live executable cell: docs/ renders in CI only via release.yml and no workflow installs R, Python, Jupyter or Julia, so a live cell would fail a release rather than a PR check.

c-s0wqfzua.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-s0wqfzua.text:
PLAN WRITTEN — claude-notes/plans/2026-08-31-nested-executable-fence-masking.md, committed as c9a806e6d + d8303320e on worktree workspace-4 (branch braid/bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj-knitr-nested-fence-execution-disabled, off origin/main eac0c7acf). Not yet implemented.

This strand was filed wontfix-candidate on the grounds that q2 'has no seam short of escaping nested fences before hand-off, which would corrupt the display content a different way'. The plan answers both halves.

THE SEAM EXISTS AND IS SINGULAR. engine_execution.rs:432 serialises the AST for each engine via serialize_ast_to_qmd. Masking there covers knitr, q2's jupyter text engine AND TS extensions at once — no per-engine work, and no negotiation with knitr upstream.

THE ESCAPE DOES NOT CORRUPT. All three partitioners require the first character after '{' to be alphanumeric (knitr [a-zA-Z0-9_], jupyter \\w, TS [=A-Za-z]), so a leading '.' alone defeats every one of them. '{r, echo=FALSE}' -> '{.r execution-disabled=true, echo=FALSE}' -> back byte-identical, whitespace included. The marker exists only so the unmask never rewrites an author's own '{.r}'.

TWO MEASUREMENTS THIS STRAND DID NOT HAVE (re-verified at HEAD eac0c7acf, knitr 1.50, not 0.28.0):

- The echo=FALSE case is worse than recorded. The strand documents the example being replaced by ':::{.cell}' scaffolding. With echo=FALSE the author's source vanishes ENTIRELY and only the executed output remains.

- A {r} fence inside a four-backtick {=html} raw block is a FATAL parse error, not merely wrong output: 'Error: Parse error [raw.knitr.rmarkdown:161:4] ::: unexpected character or token here'. Two defects compound — the qmd writer collapses the 4-backtick raw fence to 3 (filed as bd-iu5otya7), so the inner fence closes the block, and knitr then executes it and injects ':::' that will not parse. Masking removes the execution half and so the fatal error; bd-iu5otya7 is needed for the raw block to render correctly.

PROVENANCE, since the masked text is longer than its source. The writer's map is output-indexed — pieces.push((block.source_info(), buf.len() - start)) at pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:3103 — so a longer block shifts nothing for any other block. Within a lengthened block it would drift silently, because Concat::map_offset's Original arm computes start_offset + offset with no clamp to end_offset (quarto-source-map 0.1.3). Fix: on the masked clone only, give changed blocks SourceInfo::Generated, whose map_offset returns None. Future error mapping gets 'location unknown' rather than a confidently wrong offset. The piece table is top-level-only, so a display block nested in a list also marks its top-level ancestor — accepted cost, that container's prose becomes location-unknown too.

Scoped out and cross-referenced: bd-q250-nested-fence-blind-spot-t68z1lsw (doubled braces), bd-knitr-inline-r-eats-fence-2ofk91x1 (inline R), bd-iu5otya7 (writer fence length), bd-breakquartomd-indented-display-fence-1wxmf0bh (masking removes q2's exposure; the TS-side defect remains).

title: R display fences (``` r) are a fatal parse error: the qmd writer collapses them to ```r and the knitr inline-R regex eats them
description:
Any R *display* code block — a fence carrying a language but no braces — is a fatal parse error in a document the knitr engine runs, and the whole page is lost. Quarto 1 renders all of them as highlighted, non-executed code blocks. All three author spellings fail: ``` r (space), ```r (no space), and the canonical Pandoc ```{.r}.

The user-visible symptom is an uncoded "Parse error" citing <doc>.knitr.rmarkdown at a line the author cannot look at (see "undiagnosable" below), plus a second error on an unrelated later block.

## Two stages; neither alone is sufficient

STAGE 1 — the qmd writer collapses every spelling into one. crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:783-786, in write_codeblock (fn at :764), writes the language as a bare word with no separating space:

    if classes.len() == 1 && id.is_empty() && keyvals.is_empty() {
        // Single class, no other attributes: write as bare word
        write!(buf, "{}", classes[0])?;

So ``` r, ```{.r} and ```r all parse to the same CodeBlock and re-serialize identically to ```r.

STAGE 2 — the knitr preprocessor eats that one spelling. crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs:432 re-serializes the AST to qmd via serialize_ast_to_qmd, and :495 hands that string — not the original file — to engine.execute(). KnitrEngine::execute (crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/mod.rs:158-159) then runs INLINE_R_PATTERN over the whole thing. crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/preprocess.rs:38-44:

    Regex::new(r"`r\s+([^`]+)`")

Against ```r the match is: the fence's THIRD backtick, the letter r, `\s+` taking the NEWLINE, `[^`]+` swallowing the entire block body, and the closing fence's first backtick terminating it. Output:

    ```r .QuartoInlineRender(# if you're a pak person (we are!)

## The regex does not match the raw source — stage 1 is what makes this unavoidable

Applying the pattern directly to source text:

    ``` r    -> no match
    ```{.r}  -> no match
    ```r     -> MATCH
    ```R     -> no match (case-sensitive; see workaround)

Only the no-space form is dangerous in isolation. Stage 1 converts the other two into it. Consequence: this is NOT a lint-able source pattern and authors cannot avoid it by spelling.

## The doc comment claims a guard that Q1 actually implements

preprocess.rs:35-37 states:

    /// This pattern intentionally avoids matching inside fenced code blocks
    /// because we process the entire markdown string and inline R is not valid
    /// inside code blocks.

Nothing in the pattern implements this. Quarto 1 does, in quarto-cli/src/core/execute-inline.ts:18-21:

    new RegExp("(^|[^`])`{" + language + "}[ \t]([^`]+)`", "g")

Two independent defenses, either sufficient: (a) `(^|[^`])` requires the match be preceded by start-of-string or a NON-backtick, so a fence's third backtick can never anchor; (b) `[ \t]` rather than `\s+`, so a newline never qualifies. The Rust port carried over neither. (Q1's handler covers the braced `{r} expr` form rather than bare `r expr`, so it is not a strict 1:1 port — but the guard idiom was in the file being ported from.)

## History

Introduced in 748856f50 "partial work in execution engine" (2026-01-07 02:26:35), the only commit that has ever contained INLINE_R_PATTERN (git log -S --all); byte-identical since, the sole other touch being clippy sweep 25c1e1872. The comment was therefore never true — there is no earlier version to have regressed from. preprocess.rs has 15 tests and none contains a fence; "fence" and "code block" appear in the file only inside the comment. The design plan (claude-notes/plans/2026-01-07-knitr-engine-implementation.md:186-196) specifies this exact regex and never mentions fenced blocks.

## Suggested fix direction

Stage 2 is the defect; stage 1 is arguably fine. Port Q1's guard: require the match be preceded by start-of-string or a non-backtick, and use [ \t] rather than \s+ so a newline cannot open an expression. Better still, do the substitution over parsed block structure rather than raw text — the pass currently runs over the entire serialized document including the YAML header (see below), which no regex-level guard fixes.

Stage 1 is conditional and is a plausible secondary intervention point: the collapse only fires under `classes.len() == 1 && id.is_empty() && keyvals.is_empty()` at qmd.rs:783. Adding a second class, an id, or a keyval takes the write_code_attr branch and emits the {...} form, which the regex cannot match — verified: ```{.r .other} and ```{#id .r} both render AND keep <pre class="sourceCode r"> highlighting.

TRAP FOR THE FIXER: the lowercase-only behaviour is deliberate, pinned by test_uppercase_r_not_matched, and is currently the only escape hatch (see workaround). q2's syntax highlighter is ALSO case-sensitive, so making the regex case-insensitive without teaching the highlighter that R means r would close that hatch and turn ```R fatal too.

## Front matter is not excluded either

The pass runs over the whole serialized document including the resolved YAML header, so a `r sequence in any scalar (e.g. title: "```r blocks") splices the entire resolved quarto.language block into the R expression. Fixture yaml-title/ covers this; error reads "! Failed to parse the inline R code: `r .QuartoInlineRender(..." followed by hundreds of lines of language config.

## The cascade points at an unrelated block

The swallowed span leaves the parser out of sync, so a second error fires on the next container terminator in document order — NOT an enclosing one. Verified with a discriminating fixture (outer :::: panel-tabset containing the fence, followed by a sibling ::: callout): the cascade lands on the inner sibling's :::, not the outer ::::. An error nested inside the offending region would at least aim the author at the right part of the page; this one aims elsewhere.

## Undiagnosable from the message

The error cites <doc>.knitr.rmarkdown at a line number in a generated intermediate. Verified: --debug does not retain that intermediate on this failure path and nothing is left under .quarto/, so the author cannot open the file the error names.

## Workaround, and its cost

```R (capital) renders, because the regex is lowercase-only. But it is a degradation, not an escape: q2 emits <pre class="R code-with-copy"> with no .sourceCode box and no highlighting, where Q1 emits <pre class="sourceCode r code-with-copy">. A ```bash control highlights correctly in both engines, confirming the degradation is specific to the capital.

## Real-world hit

Positron website docs (docs-quarto-2/download.qmd:269) uses ``` r to show pak::pak(...) install commands. That one fence loses the entire page, which costs 85 broken download.html references site-wide — every page's navbar carries one — plus a Q-13-4. It is one of only two pages still failing to render in that port at 0.27.0. ``` r / ```r is the standard Pandoc/Q1 spelling for a display R block and is what knitr's own .Rmd output writes, so this hits any knitr-engine project that shows R code without executing it.

## Repro

/Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/knitr-inline-r-eats-fence/

Six fixtures, each its own project; run `q2 render` inside each. repro/ (``` r), nospace/ (```r), attr-fence/ (```{.r}) and yaml-title/ all fail; control/ (```bash) and workaround/ (```R) render. Compare any of them with `quarto render --output-dir _site-q1`, which renders all six. Every fixture declares an executable ```{r} cell — the bug is unreachable without one, since the knitr engine must actually run. NOTE: running Q1 in a fixture rewrites that fixture's tracked .gitignore and deletes HTML left by a prior q2 render; the README documents this.

Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-knitr-inline-r-eats-fence-oqr1n5im. Observed with q2 0.27.0 (official release build); re-confirmed unfixed at q2 HEAD d05e96ee8, where preprocess.rs:43 is byte-identical.

c-8xzxexyo.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-8xzxexyo.text: Investigation plan skeleton committed on braid/bd-knitr-inline-r-eats-fence-2ofk91x1-r-display-fence-parse-error (83e0087a5), in .worktrees/workspace-1: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-25-r-display-fence-parse-error.md. Verdict: ready to design, pending three scoping answers (char class after `r; whether the qmd writer's bare-word fence is in scope; which secondary defects become follow-up strands). Key new evidence: knitr's own inline.code pattern captured from knitr 1.50 is the real contract, and Q1's (^|[^`]) prefix guard is strictly stronger than knitr's lookbehinds — it rejects the yaml-title case knitr itself still eats. Recommend against the AST-based direction: it would drop inline R in front-matter scalars.

c-gamydzyz.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-gamydzyz.text: Fixed on braid/bd-knitr-inline-r-eats-fence-2ofk91x1-r-display-fence-parse-error (7e6e479ba). Pattern is now (^|[^`\\])`r[ \t]([^`]+)` — a guard character plus a single space/tab instead of \s+. All six repro fixtures render; QuartoInlineRender in none of the outputs; display block is <pre class="sourceCode r"> as in Q1. One thing the investigation did not predict: the guard must also exclude a backslash, because when a YAML scalar fails to parse as markdown the .yaml-markdown-syntax-error fallback re-serializes it with every backtick escaped, so the fence's backticks are no longer adjacent — Q1's (^|[^`]) and knitr's lookbehinds both let that through. 11 unit + 6 render-level tests, all watched failing first. cargo xtask verify (full, incl. WASM) green; workspace 13385 passed / 199 skipped vs 13368/199 baseline. Not pushed.

title: Single-file q2 preview does not resolve sibling binary assets (images) referenced by the qmd
description: Discovered while investigating bd-y259zb57/bd-ggvq1j68. In single-file mode (q2 preview deck.qmd, no _quarto.yml), ProjectFiles::single_file populates only qmd_files; binary_files stays empty and the dir is NOT walked (bd-tnm3k safety property). So an image like ![](./sibling-image.png) never reaches the WASM VFS. The SPA assetWalker calls vfsReadBinaryFile(resolved) which fails, the image drops out of the asset manifest, and renders broken (verified E2E: naturalWidth=0; the request falls through to the SPA index.html, content-type text/html). PROJECT mode works (discovery walks the dir -> binary_files synced to automerge -> VFS -> blob URL; verified naturalWidth=320). There is NO on-demand HTTP route serving sibling files from disk (artifact route only serves resources-scoped .html behind a trust boundary, bd-teh4hbli). Same class of gap that _brand.yml had (bd-ggvq1j68), but harder: image paths are ARBITRARY, not conventionally-named, so the with_config_siblings probe-by-name trick does not generalize. Design options: (a) parse the deck's AST/frontmatter for referenced relative asset paths at discovery time and sync exactly those (narrow, respects 'no arbitrary siblings'); (b) add an on-demand HTTP route that serves files under the deck dir with a trust boundary; (c) document as a project-only feature. Needs a decision before implementing.
close_reason: Fixed (commit 3ad1d953). Single-file q2 preview now syncs the binary assets a deck references (parse deck -> collect Image URLs -> resolve under deck dir, reject ../ escapes -> inject as HubConfig.single_file_assets -> ProjectFiles::with_binary_files -> reconcile -> VFS -> blob URL). E2E: sibling image now loads (blob, naturalWidth 320), matching project mode. v1 = load-time, direct image refs only; mid-edit-added refs need reload (follow-up if needed). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-16-single-file-preview-referenced-assets.md
