title: kbd.lua builds <kbd title="..."> as an unescaped RawInline, so a quote in the title emits malformed HTML
description:
resources/extensions/quarto/kbd/kbd.lua:69 concatenates the title directly into an HTML attribute --  '<kbd title="' .. title_str .. '"...' -- and emits the result as an unescaped RawInline. A double quote anywhere in the title closes the attribute early and produces a malformed tag.

Measured end-to-end with './target/debug/q2 render' and read from the generated HTML: both

    {{< kbd a"b >}}        (bare -- newly legal after the naked-string widening)
    {{< kbd "a\"b" >}}       (quoted -- unchanged by that work)

emit the IDENTICAL broken tag:

    <kbd title="a"b" aria-hidden="true" >

PRE-EXISTING, not introduced. The quoted route reaches this on main today; the shortcode naked-string widening (branch braid/bd-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-2u79bqp1-shortcode-escaped-gt, commits e223edd52..2477d2816) only added a shorter route to the same defect, without changing its severity or reachability class. The final whole-branch review on that branch confirmed it should not gate the merge.

Scope note: the title content is the document author's own text, so this is malformed output rather than a third-party injection vector. Fix is to HTML-escape the attribute value before interpolation (or build the element through Pandoc's Lua API rather than as a RawInline).

Filed per the widening plan's own out-of-scope table, which said 'File separately if confirmed at Task 4 Step 3'. It was confirmed there, and the final review caught that no strand had actually been created.

title: Phase F.1: Cross-page navigation + link-rewriting + Bootstrap JS
description:
Foundational sub-task for Phase F (q2-preview website chrome). Three things land together because they're co-dependent:

1. Include link-rewrite in q2-preview pipeline. Removes 'link-rewrite' from Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED at crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:1057. After this, body and chrome hrefs alike are .html URLs.

2. Cross-page click navigation in the SPA. Extend iframePostProcessor.ts to recognize .html URLs that map back to project .qmd files (check against project file index — NOT just the .html suffix, so external https://example.com/foo.html stays untouched). Wire onNavigateToDocument in PreviewApp.tsx — invocation calls setState to switch activeFile. history.pushState so browser back/forward walks the in-SPA navigation. popstate listener to handle back/forward. After activeFile changes and the render fires, scroll the iframe to window.location.hash if present (coordinate with iframe's post-render hook, not the state change, to avoid the race).

3. Bootstrap JS in the iframe. The chrome HTML emitted by navbar-render etc. uses Bootstrap dropdowns/collapses. The WASM pipeline currently excludes BootstrapJsStage (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/bootstrap_js.rs). Two options to evaluate during implementation:
   (a) Include BootstrapJsStage in the WASM pipeline by removing the cfg gate, if state-preservation concerns the original gate guarded against don't apply to q2-preview's iframe model.
   (b) Statically inject bootstrap.bundle.min.js into the iframe template alongside the existing Bootstrap CSS — cleaner for preview because it bypasses any state concerns and lets Bootstrap 5's data-bs-* auto-init handle freshly-rendered chrome DOM.
Pick whichever's cleaner; document the choice.

Reference: math_js.rs at crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/math_js.rs — MathJsStage ships on both native and WASM pipelines because the engine 'typesets once on DOMContentLoaded' and holds no cross-reinit state. Bootstrap can ride the same pattern.

description:

Per Q-C3 the input_qmd recorded is the whole serialized post-include-expansion QMD (matches what EngineExecutionStage feeds to engines today and what ReplayEngine validates on).

description:

Architecture:
- compute_input_qmd truncates the q2-preview pipeline at PreEngineSugaringStage and serializes the AST to QMD. Same output EngineExecutionStage would hand to the engine; byte-equality vs the recorded capture's input_qmd is the staleness signal.
- recompute_staleness reads existing sidecar entry, ungzips + parses the capture binary doc, runs compute_input_qmd on the current file, compares bytes, flips CaptureRef.staleness when needed. Idempotent.
- New OnFileChangedCallback type on quarto_hub::server. quarto-preview registers it from run_with_on_ready alongside the existing on_ready. Pipeline futures are ?Send; dispatches via spawn_blocking + pollster::block_on.

title: Bare '=' as a shortcode argument renders in Q1, produces nothing in q2
description:
'{{< kbd = >}}' renders under Q1 as <kbd title="=" aria-hidden="true">=</kbd> but produces no shortcode output under q2.

Cause. '=' is the key/value separator, so it is excluded from the shortcode_naked_string token in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js. A lone '=' is therefore read as a key/value specifier with an empty key and empty value rather than as a positional string argument.

This is deliberate and correct as far as it goes -- '=' genuinely cannot be admitted to the naked token freely, because 'a=b' would then be ambiguous between one naked value and a key/value pair, and preferring the former would silently reinterpret every existing key=value shortcode in every document. That risk is why the sibling grammar work (bd-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-2u79bqp1 / bd-shortcode-naked-value-nonascii-47fzbmow) deliberately leaves '=' excluded.

The narrow gap is the unambiguous case: a token that is EXACTLY '=' has no key before it, so there is nothing to disambiguate. A targeted rule admitting that single form would close the parity gap without touching the general key/value boundary.

Severity is low and the failure is quiet: after the sibling grammar fix lands, this input renders the document and drops only the shortcode -- the same degradation Q1 applies to characters it cannot place. Before that fix it is fatal, along with eight other characters.

Out of scope here, but worth recording for whoever wants the general problem: the key/value boundary is currently encoded in four places that do not share a formulation --
  - grammar.js:687, the second shortcode_naked_string alternative, which re-admits '=' only after a '?' (the query-string carve-out)
  - crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c:2159, parse_language_specifier, which scans past whitespace looking for '=' to decide key vs value
  - grammar.js:675, _shortcode_key_value_specifier
  - Q1's own rule in external-sources/quarto-cli/src/resources/pandoc/datadir/lpegshortcode.lua:157, which refuses to treat a token containing ':/?=' as a key at all ('so that URLs with = in them are not treated as key/value pairs')
Q1's is the better formulation -- it asks whether the prefix is a plausible key, where q2's asks positionally whether a '?' has been seen. Consolidating onto that would be a real design change, larger than this strand.

title: Migrate pampa to hash-based FileIds for cross-parser interop
description:
Discovered while wiring bd-1pwy8 (SassError::UnknownTheme structured diagnostic): pampa's ASTContext uses sequential FileIds (always FileId(0) for the document's primary file), while quarto_yaml uses hash(filename) FileIds. The two schemes are incompatible — same FileId means different files depending on the producer.

Symptoms / workarounds already in the tree:

- crates/quarto-core/src/theme_diagnostic.rs takes (FileId, &Path) candidate pairs because the caller has to declare which scheme each candidate uses.
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/include_expansion.rs:162-211 maintains TWO parallel SourceContexts and explicitly remaps FileId(0) → new_sequential_id for every included sub-document (with a debug_assert_eq! to catch desync).

Proposed fix: have pampa adopt quarto_yaml::file_id_for_filename so its FileIds are globally meaningful. Eliminates the workarounds and makes any future cross-context diagnostic consumer (hub-client, q2 preview, JSON endpoint) work without out-of-band FileId knowledge.

Coordinate with the parallel source-location workstream before implementing — this touches ~50 hardcoded FileId(0) call sites in pampa. PR review needed, not direct-to-main.

title: Re-examine bd-7hd2gzf1's --retry=2: it may be masking, not tolerating
description:
While fixing bd-yw3mcdkg, --retry was measured to DESTROY the binding of quarto-hub-mcp's exit-drain test: with retry:2 it passed even with the shutdown drain disabled, because the drain-off failure is probabilistic and one of three attempts gets through. A retry that absorbs a probabilistic failure also absorbs the real defect that failure is there to catch.

quarto-sync-client's doc-inventory race carries the same mitigation (--retry=2 in the workflow, per bd-7hd2gzf1). Worth checking whether it has the same problem: disable/revert whatever doc-inventory actually depends on and confirm the test stays red through all three attempts. If it does not, the retry is masking rather than tolerating and needs a different fix.

Second data point: in a 30-iteration sweep under load (bd-yw3mcdkg), quarto-sync-client was 30/30 green WITHOUT --retry, with all 137 tests executing. The ~25% local failure rate quoted in the workflow comment did not reproduce at all, so that figure may be stale or environment-specific.

c-mty5u8mm.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-mty5u8mm.text:
Attempted on the bd-yw3mcdkg PR at the user's request; NOT landed. Recording what was established and where it stalls, so the next attempt doesn't redo it.

CONFIRMED — the mechanism is right, and one competing explanation is ruled out.
I suspected the real cause might be the test's own findDocRetry:{attempts:1} timing out on logo.png under load rather than an index-convergence gap. It is not. Unavailable files DO still appear in getDocInventory (client.ts ~1572-1582), just with role 'file' instead of 'binary-file'. The observed failure has the logo.png entry absent ENTIRELY, not role-mismatched, so the file was never in the index snapshot connect() took. Index convergence it is.

Also confirmed by reading: there is no await between the snapshot (client.ts ~932) and the 'change' listener registration (~953), so that particular gap cannot interleave — the hole is that syncWithFilesHandled is fire-and-forget (void syncWithFiles(...)) and connect() never awaits it.

BLOCKER 1 — cannot reproduce locally. 60 runs of the full sync-client suite, no --retry, across two load regimes: 8 CPU spinners (load average ~10) and 6 concurrent vitest churn loops (load average ~24). Zero failures. The one reproduction I did get was 1/20 of doc-inventory.test.ts alone under 8 spinners, matching the known signature. Rate is far too low and too regime-dependent to verify a fix against.

BLOCKER 2 — cannot build a deterministic binding test. The plan was to create a controlled load window with a dangling index entry (whose findDoc should burn the 5000 ms FIND_DOC_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS) and inject a second, late entry inside it. It does not work: a dangling doc resolves as 'unavailable' promptly (~ms) because the peer answers that it does not have it — the attempt timeout never fires. Measured: connect() with a dangling entry returns in well under 1 s. With no controllable window, and with the fix's behaviour depending on when a sync message lands, a test cannot deterministically distinguish fixed from unfixed.

CANDIDATE FIX (written, verified green against the existing suite, then reverted — saved as a patch, not committed): after 'await loadFileDocuments(files)' in connect(), re-read the index and load any files that appeared, looping until the list stops growing. Strictly additive — it can only load files the index already lists, never drop one, so the worst case is a no-op. It closes the window for entries that have arrived by the time the loads finish; an entry arriving strictly later is still the change handler's job.

Not landed because CLAUDE.md is explicit: stop and ask if you cannot mechanically test the bad behaviour. Shipping an unverified synchronisation change to connect() — the path every project open goes through — on a PR about an unrelated flake is the wrong trade.

WHAT THIS NEEDS: a test seam in ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/test-hub.ts that can withhold or delay part of the index document's sync (the existing holdUpgrades only gates the websocket handshake, which is too coarse — the reader cannot get the index at all). With that, both the bug and the fix become deterministic: withhold the second file entry until after the reader's index handle is ready, release it during the load, and assert connect() does not resolve without it. That is a contained piece of work and is the right first step here.

DO NOT remove --retry=2 from the workflow until the fix is verified — the measured 6%/run rate would otherwise land straight on CI.

c-zte5rjwm.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-zte5rjwm.text:
Evidence upgraded — this strand's premise is now measured, and the description's second data point is WRONG and should be read as superseded by this comment.

The description says quarto-sync-client ran 30/30 green without --retry and that the ~25% rate 'did not reproduce at all'. That was an unlucky-clean sample. A follow-up batch of 20 runs caught the race 3 times. Corrected: 3 failures in 50 no-retry runs = 6% raw per-run rate.

More importantly, the mechanism is now identified, and it makes the case here stronger than 'may be masking':

doc-inventory.test.ts:140 fails with logo.png missing from getDocInventory() entirely (not a state mismatch). In client.ts, connect() awaits findDoc + whenReady(), then takes a SYNCHRONOUS snapshot of the index doc's file list (~line 932) and loads only what that snapshot contains via loadFileDocuments(). The 'change' listener that picks up later-arriving files is registered (~line 953) but never awaited by connect(). So connect() can resolve having seen 1 of 2 files, and the test's very next line sees an incomplete inventory.

That is a production synchronisation gap: connect() resolving does not guarantee its view of 'known files' reflects the converged index. Any consumer calling connect() then immediately reading the file list can hit it — the test is just the first thing that does. So --retry=2 is masking a real bug in shipped code, not tolerating test timing.

Contrast with what was found on bd-yw3mcdkg: there, retry was rejected because it made a data-loss test pass even with the drain deleted (vacuous). Here retry doesn't make the test vacuous — it hides a genuine defect. Different failure modes, same conclusion: the retry should come off once connect() is fixed.

Suggested fix direction (untested): have connect() either wait for a settled index state before snapshotting, or re-read getFilesFromIndex() after loadFileDocuments() resolves and load anything that arrived in between.

title: hub-mcp: no auth classification on WS reconnect — revoked/banned credentials spin the retry loop silently forever
description: NodeWebSocketClientAdapter.openSocket swallows getBearer failures (return; retry re-fires forever) and onClose carries no upgrade status, so a 401/403 WS upgrade is indistinguishable from network failure (ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/NodeWebSocketClientAdapter.ts:181-221). The SPA got an evidence-based probe for exactly this (bd-3o8zmz46 / useAuthProbe); MCP has no equivalent — a mid-session invalid_grant leaves a dead, silent, immortal retry loop. Fix: adapter reports definitive auth evidence (ws 'unexpected-response' status, terminal ReauthRequired from getBearer) via an optional callback; connection-manager owns policy (one forced refresh + reprobe, then invalidate/disconnect/surface ReauthRequired; 403 -> clear terminal message, keyring kept). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-03-bearer-revocation-and-mcp-auth-followups.md (F2).
close_reason: Implemented: adapter reports definitive auth evidence (upgrade 401/403 via ws unexpected-response with self-aborted handshake; ReauthRequired-named refresh failures stop the retry loop), manager owns policy (coalesced forceRefresh+reprobe, fail-fast ReauthRequired gate with self-heal, keyring-preserving HubAccessDeniedError on 403). 17 new unit specs + 2 e2e cases through real hub + real q2 mcp launcher. Merged --no-ff into feature/auth-review-followups.

c-hfzt6o09.author: shikokuchuo
c-hfzt6o09.text: Notable extras discovered during TDD: (1) attaching ws 'unexpected-response' suppresses abortHandshake — handler must drain+destroy or each attempt leaks a connection (pinned by a real-ws test against a raw net server); (2) adapter.disconnect() during CONNECTING crashed the process via unhandled ws error event — fixed with a swallow-only listener.

title: [websites] Honor explicit 'expanded: true' through active resolution
description: Today resolve_active_state always sets expanded=true on ancestors of an active item, overriding any user-supplied 'expanded: false'. The YAML 'expanded: true' override is parsed but active-state unconditionally sets it to true — which is the right default but means a user cannot force a section collapsed when it contains the active page (rare but legitimate). Fix: honor the YAML value where it is 'true', but treat 'false' as a default that active-state can override up, never down.

title: julia-engine leaks QNR worker on execute error (throw before oneShot close)
description: julia-engine.ts executeJulia sends the 'run' command and only sends the oneShot 'close' AFTER a successful response (src/julia-engine.ts:742-749 in the fixture copy). When run fails (e.g. the cell calls error(), as in the frozen J4 test), writeJuliaCommand throws and the close is never sent, leaving the notebook's QNR worker process open on the (global, per-user) control server. Observed empirically during Plan 4 4E: each j4_error_handling_does_not_wedge_host execution leaves one julia worker (verified by lsof: worker CWDs were the deleted nextest TempDirs). The leaked workers also keep the control server from reaching its idle timeout. Upstream Q1 has the same code shape, so this is likely a faithful-port bug worth reporting upstream too. Fix sketch: try/finally around the run so oneShot always closes (or forcecloses) the file's worker. Cleanup for leaked workers: kill the worker PIDs (children of the control-server PID from the transport file) or stop the whole server when safe.

title: Empty-content artifacts are skipped on the VFS flush path but written on both OutputSink paths
description:
In `crates/quarto-core/src/artifact_flush.rs`, `flush_artifacts_to_vfs` skips artifacts whose `content.is_empty()`, because bd-3gtn established that empty content means 'manifest entry' (`Artifact::from_path`) whose write target can alias the user's upload location — 'they must never be written'.

Neither `enqueue_artifacts` nor `flush_project_artifacts` has that skip. They rely on OutputSink's allowed-roots validation instead. For a manifest-entry artifact with a *relative* path that resolves inside an allowed output root, the OutputSink paths would enqueue a 0-byte write over it — the same class of bug bd-cfl67 fixed (q2 render truncating source images to 0 bytes).

bd-cfl67 removed the known producer (ResourceCollectorTransform no longer routes through the artifact store; it emits (src,dest) resource_copies instead), so there may be no live trigger today. But `Artifact::from_path` still exists and nothing enforces the absence of such producers on the OutputSink paths.

Questions to settle:
1. Can any current producer put an empty-content, path-bearing artifact into a Page- or Project-scope store that reaches enqueue_artifacts? (Audit Artifact::from_path / with_path callers.)
2. If not reachable, should the skip still be unified for defense in depth, or should the divergence be documented as intentional?
3. If the skip is unified, does any consumer depend on a 0-byte file being created? (The VFS path already skips, so hub-client does not.)

Deliberately NOT folded into the bd-v8gx/bd-gdhk consolidation branch: that branch is 'no behavior change except one documented scope-filter decision', and this is a behavior question that deserves its own tests.

title: revealjs: actually support code-copy (CSS + Bootstrap Icons + iframe-safe clipboard init)
description:
Follow-up to bd-fu1a5g6l, which SUPPRESSED the code-copy button in revealjs (CopyMode::Off for revealjs targets in CodeBlockGenerateTransform) because reveal shipped none of the supporting machinery. This strand is the opposite direction: properly support code-copy in reveal so decks can have working, styled copy buttons.

What's missing in the reveal output today (vs the HTML path):
1. CSS: the .code-copy-button styling (hover-hide via the $code-copy-selector, top-right positioning, no UA border, the .code-with-copy / .code-copy-outer-scaffold layout). HTML gets this from its theme SCSS; reveal's quarto-reveal layer doesn't include it. Port the copy-button rules into the reveal theme (assemble_reveal_scss / quarto-reveal.scss), scoping under .reveal where needed for specificity (cf. the highlight-layer specificity notes in bd-ehyyfpjj).
2. Icon: the <i class="bi"> clipboard glyph needs the Bootstrap Icons font present in reveal output (HTML bundles it; reveal does not).
3. JS: clipboard.js + the code-copy-init handler. title: hub-client vitest: 23 tests fail under Node 26 — global localStorage is undefined without --localstorage-file
description: Under Node v26.8.1, vitest (environment: 'node', hub-client/vitest.config.ts) prints 'ExperimentalWarning: localStorage is not available because --localstorage-file was not provided' and every test that touches localStorage (usePreference, branchService, SyncStatusBadge, ProjectSelector.import, debugApi, AboutTab — 23 tests across 6 files) fails with 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading clear)'. Node 26 ships an experimental Web Storage global that is defined-but-undefined unless --localstorage-file is passed, so the tests' own polyfill/mocks no longer take effect. This makes 'cargo xtask verify' (hub-client leg) red on machines running Node 26; the Rust leg is unaffected. Surfaced during the bd-jsvetdea pre-flight verify on 2026-09-08. Fix candidates: pin Node via .nvmrc/engines, set NODE_OPTIONS=--localstorage-file=<tmp> in the vitest config, or install a localStorage stub in a vitest setupFiles entry before tests run.

Root cause: Node>=25 defines a globalThis.localStorage accessor (undefined without --localstorage-file); vitest 4.x jsdom env skips window keys already on the global unless allowlisted, and localStorage is not in the allowlist until vitest 5.0.0. Recurrence of the May pin (ca6d47c8): brew upgrade on Sep 4 relinked node to 26.8.1 and nothing enforces .nvmrc/engines. Prototype setupFiles shim using globalThis.jsdom's Storage passes 62/62 affected tests on Node 26; --no-webstorage is rejected by Node 24 so it cannot be the shared fix.

title: Listings lose declared order of explicit contents: entries (Q1 preserves it)
description:
A listing whose contents: is a list of explicit paths renders items in path-alphabetical order regardless of declaration order. Q1 preserves the declared order when sort: is false/absent — curated orderings are a common authoring pattern (all 15 Posit Connect cookbook listing pages rely on it; q2 renders 'Getting Started' 4th instead of 1st).

Root cause area: contents: entries are translated to glob patterns and resolved set-based through the shared glob engine (listing/glob_resolve.rs -> crate::glob::resolve_patterns, single-view matching), which loses per-pattern declaration order; apply_sort with sort:false is correctly a no-op, so the glob engine's ordering leaks through. Suggested fix: order the resolved item set by first-matching-pattern index (Q1 semantics), at least for literal-path patterns.

Second-order effect: post-render description previews extracted from listing-only section pages pick up the wrong first item.

Related quirk worth fixing in the same pass: sorting by a custom field via listing-item.extra works (sort.rs::field_value falls through to extra) but is_known_sort_field doesn't know extra fields, so a working custom-field sort emits a misleading Q-12-3 'values will compare as equal' warning.

Minimal repro (declares Bravo,Alpha; renders Alpha,Bravo): /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/listing-declared-order/ (see README.md; run 'q2 render' there). Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-listing-declared-order-qodof0f6. Observed with q2 0.14.0.

Also flags: q2's absent-sort default (date desc) disagrees with Q1 (order asc, title asc); Q-12-3 false positive on working extra-field sorts.

title: Default listing emits no description for items without explicit description: (Q1 derives one from the first paragraph)
description:
In a default-type listing, an item whose page has no description: frontmatter renders with no description at all — title-only cards. Quarto 1 derives a description from the rendered page's first paragraph (truncated at a word boundary to max-description-length, default 175), so the same project shows meaty cards under Q1 and bare titles under q2.

Root cause: crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/templates/item-default.template wraps the whole description block — including the $description-placeholder-begin$/$description-placeholder-end$ markers — in $if(description)$. When the description binding is empty, the markers are never emitted, so the L7 post-render substitution (post_render_upgrade/reader.rs, the pass that reads the rendered page, extracts the first paragraph, and injects it between the markers — the same pass whose maybe_truncate at reader.rs:187 does the truncation) has nowhere to land. A custom template that emits the markers unconditionally gets derived descriptions just fine, which is the control: the derivation machinery works, the default template just never invokes it for the items that need it most.

Suggested fix, either direction: (a) emit the placeholder-marker block unconditionally in item-default.template (an empty pair costs nothing if the page yields no paragraph), or (b) resolve the derived description before template evaluation so the description binding is never empty for pages with body text. (a) is the smaller change and matches how the working custom-template path behaves.

Real-world hit in the Connect docs: none yet — their listings are all type: custom with templates that emit the markers unconditionally — hence P3. But any Q1 blog-style default listing hits this immediately on porting.

README's 'Notes' section flags this as the third, larger gap. Re-verified failing on q2 0.25.0 (origin/main 1adfebcc has no post-release listing changes). title: Listing ignores an explicit description: and uses the auto-derived first paragraph
description:
WHAT HAPPENS. A listing ignores an author-supplied `description:` on a listed page and shows the auto-derived first body paragraph instead. Quarto 1 shows the declared description and auto-derives only as a fallback.

    ---
    title: Section with an explicit description
    description: EXPLICIT-DESCRIPTION
    ---

    BODY-PARAGRAPH that the autofill uses instead.

  q2 0.17.0   →  "BODY-PARAGRAPH that the autofill uses instead."
  Quarto 1    →  "EXPLICIT-DESCRIPTION"

The description is parsed and does reach the page — the rendered HTML carries `<meta name="description" content="EXPLICIT-DESCRIPTION">`. Only the listing ignores it. No warning.

WHERE IT LIVES. crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/listing_item_info.rs. `autofill_listing_item` calls

    fill_string_if_absent(&mut doc.ast.meta, "description", compute_description(&doc.ast.blocks));

and `fill_string_if_absent` returns early only when `meta.listing-item.description` is already present. A top-level `description:` is a different key path, so it never suppresses the autofill, and the autofilled `listing-item.description` is what the listing reads.

The stage's own doc comments state the intended rule — "Author values are never overwritten" and "Author values always win — the stage strictly fills holes" — so this reads as an oversight about which key paths count as an author value rather than a deliberate precedence choice.

SECOND, SEPARATE OBSERVATION. The repro's second document uses the `listing-item:` form — the key document_profile.rs (~line 152) documents for authors — and it loses to the autofill too. That contradicts the integration test at crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/document_profile_pipeline.rs ~line 602, which sets `listing-item.description` alongside a body paragraph and asserts the author value wins. The test passes, so something differs between it and a real project render; worth chasing separately from the top-level-`description:` issue, and it is the reason a docs-side workaround could not simply switch keys.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION. Treat a top-level `description:` as an author value here: skip the description autofill when `meta.description` is present, or seed `listing-item.description` from it before the autofill runs. The other autofilled fields (image, word-count, reading-time-minutes, date-modified) have no top-level counterpart, so this is specific to `description`.

REAL-WORLD HIT (Posit Connect docs). The cookbook landing page lists 13 section index pages. Nine of them have no body prose — just a title and a custom listing — so each engine derives a description, and q2 derived the first *recipe title* inside the section: the "Users" entry read "Viewing User Information", "Content" read "AWS Service Account Integrations", and so on, where Q1 at least produced a sentence. The obvious fix was to give those nine pages an explicit `description:`. It had no effect, because each section page renders a listing whose first item link becomes a paragraph that the autofill then picks up. The docs worked around it by putting the text in the page body instead — which is what the four sections that already read well (Getting Started, Groups, Vanity URLs, Jobs) happen to do.

REPRO. /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/listing-description-precedence/ — run `q2 render` there and compare with `quarto render --output-dir _site-q1`. Two listed pages, one per key form, each with a body paragraph the autofill would otherwise use. README.md has both engines' output and the analysis above. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path.

Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-zx6111f9. Observed with q2 0.17.0 / origin/main @ 001cb6a5.

title: Listing nits vs Q1: truncated descriptions lose the ellipsis; no hidden 'No matching items' placeholder
description:
Two small Q1-parity gaps in listings, both cosmetic, both affecting every listing page: 1. Truncated auto-derived descriptions lose the trailing ellipsis. When a listing item has no explicit description:, the description is derived from the rendered page's first paragraph and truncated at a word boundary <= max-description-length (default 175). Q1 appends a horizontal ellipsis to the truncated text ('...so that the listing page has to…'); q2 truncates at the same word boundary with no marker, so the text just stops mid-sentence ('...so that the listing page has to'). Root cause: maybe_truncate (crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/post_render_upgrade/reader.rs:187 at v0.24.0) mirrors Q1's truncateText(s, n, 'space') word-boundary cut but not its suffix — Q1's trimAtSpace (quarto-cli src/core/text.ts, truncateText) appends '…' after the cut, first stripping a trailing ',', '/' or ':'. Suggested fix: match Q1 in maybe_truncate — after cutting, trim a trailing ','/'/'/':' and append '…'. 2. No hidden 'No matching items' placeholder. Q1 emits '
No matching items
' on every listing page (from projects/website/listing/_pagination.ejs.md, localized string listing-page-no-matches in _language.yml), and quarto-listing.js reveals it when a filter/search query matches nothing. q2 emits no such div, so a filtered-to-empty listing shows a blank area. q2 already vendors the same JS — resources/listing/quarto-listing.js:91 queries '# .listing-no-matching' and toggles d-none — so only the emitted div is missing; the reveal logic is in place. Suggested fix: emit the hidden div (localized) alongside each listing container, for built-in and custom listing types alike. Real-world hit: every Posit Connect docs cookbook section index (~14 pages of type: custom listings — cookbook/index, cookbook/content/index, cookbook/metrics/index, cookbook/groups/index, cookbook/users/index, ...) shows both nits: derived descriptions stop mid-sentence ('...has already been' vs Q1's '...has already been…') and the no-matching placeholder is absent. Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/listing-ellipsis-no-matching/ (run 'q2 render' there; see README.md; Q1 comparison via 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1'). The ellipsis symptom is on _site/custom.html (custom template emitting the description placeholder markers unconditionally, like the Connect cookbook); the Q1 reference is _site-q1/index.html (2 ellipsis characters; same truncation points). The placeholder symptom: grep listing-no-matching over _site/*.html finds nothing, vs 1 hit per Q1 page. Note _site-q1/custom.html is garbage (the template is a q2 doctemplate, which Q1's EJS engine passes through literally) — ignore it. Related but separate: in default-type listings q2 emits no description at all for items without explicit description: (item-default.template guards the placeholder markers with $if(description)$, so the post-render substitution never runs) — visible on the same repro's _site/index.html, tracked in the origin skein as br-listing-default-no-derived-desc-ywc4zvu8. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-gny8y5v4. Observed with q2 0.16.0; re-verified failing on 0.17.0, 0.20.0, 0.21.0 and 0.24.0 (= current HEAD).

title: A listing div whose id matches its enclosing section's id destroys that whole section, silently
description:
When a listing's explicit slot has the same id as the section it sits in, q2 renders the listing INTO the section element itself, replacing the section's entire contents. The heading and every other block in that section vanish from the output. The render exits 0 and emits no diagnostic of any kind. Quarto 1 keeps all of it. The collision arises naturally: a heading's auto-generated id is its slugified text, so ## Learn more ::: {#learn-more} ::: puts an author's slot inside a section that already carries `learn-more`. Measured on a fixture with ordinary prose around the slot: block q2 Q1 '## Learn more' lost present paragraph BEFORE the listing slot lost present paragraph AFTER the listing slot lost present '## Next section' and its body present present the listing items themselves present present Only content outside the colliding section survives. The listing renders correctly; it simply lands where the section's content used to be. The markup shows it plainly. q2 emits one element carrying both roles:
with no

anywhere. Q1 keeps them separate, giving the listing its own nested container so nothing is displaced:

Learn more

The `data-listing-rendered="1"` on q2's
is the tell. Worth noting for triage: the TOC entry survives and still resolves, because the
anchor exists. So the reader gets a working TOC link to a section with no visible title and, if it had prose, none of its content — which is why this is easy to miss in review. ROOT CAUSE crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/listing_render.rs, `fill_in_blocks` (called via `try_replace_explicit_slot`). It walks the AST for a Div whose id matches the listing id and, on the first match, overwrites its content outright: fn fill_in_blocks(blocks_in: &mut Vec, id: &str, payload: &[Block]) -> bool { for block in blocks_in.iter_mut() { if let Block::Div(div) = block { if div.attr.0 == id { ... div.content = payload.to_vec(); The walk is outside-in. SectionizeTransform (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/sectionize.rs) runs earlier, in the Normalization phase, and has already wrapped the heading in a `Div .section` carrying the heading's auto-id — the same `learn-more`. So the SECTION Div matches before the author's actual ::: slot nested inside it, and the section's whole content is replaced. The heading is collateral damage, not the target. That is also why nothing complains: from the transform's point of view it found its slot and filled it. SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION The recursion itself is deliberate and documented — a slot inside a section is no longer a top-level block by the time listings render, and Q1 recurses too — so the fix is not to stop recursing. Options, roughly in order of preference: - prefer the innermost match rather than the first one encountered, or - skip Divs carrying the `section` class when looking for a host, or - reject a host whose id came from a heading's auto-id rather than from an author's explicit attribute. Independently of which is chosen, emit a diagnostic when a listing id collides with a section id. Today the loss is completely silent, which is most of what makes this P1 rather than a cosmetic parity gap. REAL-WORLD HIT The Positron docs page assistant.qmd:48-51 is exactly this shape and loses its "Learn more" heading. The rendered assistant.html carries `
` with no

. It is one of only nine remaining
text-diff lines against the Quarto 1 baseline across 113 pages, so with the rest of the porting noise gone this is now among the few real content differences left. That particular section contains nothing but the listing slot, so on this corpus only the heading is visibly lost. The fixture with body content shows what the same bug costs a section that has prose in it. INCIDENCE Scanning two independently ported Quarto 1 corpora for a `::: {#id}` whose id matches a heading's auto-id in the same file: Positron docs 1, Posit Connect docs 0 (of 1 id'd div). Rare in practice — but naming a listing slot after the section it sits in is a natural thing to write, the workaround requires knowing the bug exists, and nothing in the output or the render log points at it. REPRO /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/listing-id-collides-with-heading/ cd && sh check.sh Three projects. `collide/` and `distinct/` are identical but for the listing's id, and isolate the collision from headings-adjacent-to-listings generally. `collide-with-body/` adds prose before and after the slot and shows the whole section is destroyed. check.sh renders each with q2 and with Quarto 1 and reports what survived; pass a different binary as $1 to check another build. VERSION Verified at q2 0.28.0 and at q2 source main 9ad1d4420 (no commits touching listing_render.rs since the v0.28.0 tag). Originally found on 0.27.0. Q1 reference: 99.9.9. Origin strand: br-listing-id-collides-with-heading-82udtj7w in the q2-positron-docs skein.

title: Listings with inline contents: records render empty — every record is parsed, then dropped before item construction
description:
A listing whose `contents:` entries are inline metadata records rather than file globs renders empty. Every record is dropped; the page keeps the listing container and loses all of its items.

    listing:
      id: guide-sections
      contents:
        - title: "Get started"
          description: "Download and install Positron"
          icon: "bi-rocket-takeoff"
          link: "download.qmd"
        - title: "Migrate from RStudio"
          ...

Quarto 1 renders one card per record, taking the card's metadata straight from the YAML -- no file needs to exist behind an entry. q2 emits one Q-12-2 per record ('Inline `contents:` records are not yet supported; entry skipped.') and produces a listing with no items. The render exits 0, so a project can ship a page whose main content is missing with nothing worse than warnings.

Root cause: the record is parsed and preserved, then discarded one step later.

  - crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/config.rs:691-698 matches a
    ConfigValueKind::Map entry, pushes the Q-12-2 diagnostic, and still builds
    the record into ListingContents::Inline(map). Nothing is lost here.
  - crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/glob_resolve.rs:45-65,
    resolve_content_globs(), is the consumer. It filters the contents list with

        ListingContents::Glob { pattern, source } => Some(RawGlob::new(...)),
        _ => None,

    so the Inline variant falls through the catch-all and the listing resolves
    to zero items.

(The other two ListingContents::Inline matches in the tree -- config.rs:1095 and glob_resolve.rs:203 -- are both inside #[cfg(test)] modules; config.rs's tests begin at line 1053. They are not the consumer.)

Suggested fix direction: the parsing is already done, so this is not about teaching q2 the syntax. What is missing is a path from an inline record to a listing item that does not route through glob resolution -- the record already IS the item's metadata and needs no file lookup. The likely reason it was deferred is structural rather than incidental: everywhere else an item is derived from a document and carries document-shaped fields (a source path above all), while an inline record has no document behind it. So the work is probably 'construct an item with no backing file' and touches the item type, not just the match arm above. Worth confirming before scoping.

Real-world hit. The Positron website builds all of its landing-page card grids this way: welcome, features, ai-features, tutorials, assistant, assistant-getting-started, language-guides, older-releases. Q-12-2 fires 42 times across 7 of those pages (features x34 -- the page has 34 cards -- welcome x12, ai-features x12, tutorials x10, assistant x6, assistant-getting-started x6, language-guides x4). Those 8 pages carry 127 of the 304 differing lines in that port's rendered-text sweep, about 42%, the largest group after one unrelated page.

Note this strand interlocks with the same site's EJS problem and the two hide each other. Those listings also set `type: custom` with `template: templates/welcome-card.ejs`, which q2 copies verbatim into the page rather than executing (tracked on the porting side as br-ejs-template-dumped-e7491tmf). So today the reader sees raw template source. Porting those templates to q2 doctemplates -- docs-side work that port is otherwise ready to do -- would replace visible EJS with a visibly EMPTY grid, because the items still never arrive. Neither fix produces a working page on its own, which is why this one is the unlock: it is the half the porting project cannot do for itself.

Repro: /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/listing-inline-contents/
Three fixtures, all using the built-in `type: default` listing so that `type: custom` / templates are NOT a variable:

    cd control && q2 render    0 warnings, listing renders both entries
    cd repro   && q2 render    2 Q-12-2 warnings, listing renders empty
    cd mixed   && q2 render    1 Q-12-2 warning; the glob entry survives and
                               only the inline entry is dropped

The `mixed` fixture is the sharpest of the three: one contents list, one glob entry, one inline entry, and only the inline one disappears. Compare any of them with `quarto render` for expected output. README.md has the full YAML and results. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path.

Observed with the official q2 0.26.0 release build (re-verified 2026-08-24 on all three fixtures: 0 / 2 / 1 Q-12-2 warnings respectively); source checkout was at 596ceb572 (v0.26.0-28) at the time. Originally filed against 0.22.0 and unchanged since.

Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-listing-inline-contents-mypodkim.

title: Listings built from inline contents: records lose declared YAML order (default sort alphabetises them; Q1 does not sort them at all)
description:
A listing whose `contents:` is a list of inline records renders them in title-alphabetical order. Quarto 1 renders them in the order they are written in the YAML.

Declaring three records titled Zulu, Alpha, Mike, in that order:

  Q1:  Zulu | Alpha | Mike
  q2:  Alpha | Mike | Zulu

No diagnostic. The items are otherwise correct — every field renders — so nothing in the output signals that an authoring decision was discarded.

## Root cause: not the declared-position code

This is worth stating up front, because the obvious suspect is innocent. `ListingGenerateTransform` assigns each item a declared-position sort key in `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/listing_generate.rs`: glob items get `(pattern_idx, 1)` (:241), inline records get `(globs_before, 0)` (:328), then `ordered.sort_by_key(...)` (:329). That machinery is correct in both shapes. In an all-records listing every record ties at `(0, 0)` and the stable sort keeps push order — which is declared order. In a record/glob/record listing it produces exactly the interleaving D3 of the inline-contents plan specifies (`claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-listing-inline-contents.md`).

Declared order is established correctly, and then destroyed downstream.

`apply_sort` runs afterwards with the default sort, `order asc, title asc` — pinned by `listing_generate.rs::default_sort_is_order_asc_then_title_asc`, introduced by bd-listing-declared-order-3ixcvc4o. `ListingItem.order` is documented at `crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/item.rs:155` as the "author-curated position from top-level `order:` front matter (via `DocumentProfile::order`)". An inline record is not a document and has no front matter, so `order` is `None` for every record. All items tie on the primary key and the stable sort falls through to `title asc`.

Single cause, no interaction with the glob path. It also explains both workarounds exactly: `sort: false` skips `apply_sort` entirely; an explicit `order:` on each record breaks the tie. Both are verified in the repro. `order` is already plumbed through for records — it is a record-owned key (`project/listing/record.rs:23` RECORD_OWN_KEYS, parsed at :49, applied to the item at :150) — so only the *implicit* position is missing.

## What Quarto 1 does differently

Q1 has the same default sort, `order asc, title asc` (`src/project/types/website/listing/website-listing-read.ts:640`), and likewise gives records no implicit order. It differs by not APPLYING the default sort to metadata-only listings (:645-648):

    if (
      sort && !listingHydrated.sort &&
      (sources.has(ListingItemSource.document) ||
       sources.has(ListingItemSource.metadataDocument))
    )

An inline record is classified `ListingItemSource.metadata` (:1008), upgraded to `metadataDocument` only when its `path:` resolves to a real document (:1044). A listing built purely from records therefore has neither qualifying source, gets no default sort, and `sortedAndFiltered` returns `items` untouched (:286-288). Declared YAML order survives by omission rather than by construction — which is why porting the ordering logic faithfully still lost it.

## Suggested fix

Mirror Q1: withhold the default sort when a listing's items come only from inline records. q2 has no `ListingItemSource` equivalent today, but the information is available where items are built — the record branch of the `for entry in &contents` loop in `listing_generate.rs` already knows which items it created, and whether any glob contributed.

An implicit `order` equal to declaration index would also fix the all-records case and is a smaller change, but it diverges from Q1: it would make records sort before documents in a mixed listing under the default sort, where Q1 leaves such a listing sorted by order/title as usual. Worth a deliberate decision rather than picking the smaller diff.

Note the history, because the design was not overlooked: D3 "Ordering: declared position" specifies record ordering in detail, every box in that plan is checked, and it shipped in 0.27.0 (cf88d711c). The design is sound and implemented; it is simply overwritten by a default sort Q1 would not have applied to this listing.

## Real-world hit

The Positron documentation site uses inline records for every custom listing: 11 listings across 7 pages, 42 records. Comparing rendered page text against the Quarto 1 baseline, five of those pages (welcome, ai-features, assistant-getting-started, tutorials, language-guides) are byte-identical in content and differ ONLY in item order; features and assistant are that plus unrelated lines. It is the dominant remaining text difference in that port.

On welcome.qmd and features.qmd the records are a curated narrative on top-level marketing pages — "Get started" first, then "Explore Features" — so alphabetising them is the loss of an editorial decision, not a cosmetic difference. Adding `order:` to all 42 records restores parity exactly (welcome.qmd goes from 12 differing lines to 0), but is 42 hand-maintained integers that must be renumbered whenever a card is inserted.

## Repro

/Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/listing-inline-records-order/

Four projects; run `q2 render` in each and read `_site/index.html`. See its README.md for the one-liner that prints the rendered title order.

  all-records/  the bug, minimal: three records, no globs, no explicit sort:
                expected Zulu|Alpha|Mike, actual Alpha|Mike|Zulu
  mixed/        record, glob, record — the diagnostic case showing the
                declared-position machinery is not at fault
                expected Zulu|Post One|Post Two|Alpha, actual Alpha|Post One|Post Two|Zulu
  with-order/   same as all-records plus order: 1..3 — renders correctly
  sort-false/   same as all-records plus sort: false — renders correctly

Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-listing-inline-records-order-hi0apuk0.
Observed on q2 0.27.0 (release build). Verified not fixed on main as of 2026-08-26 — nothing since v0.27.0 touches listing sort or record construction.
close_reason: Shipped in q2 0.29.0. Verified downstream by re-rendering all four fixtures under llms-info/repros/listing-inline-records-order/: the all-records project now yields declared YAML order 'Zulu | Alpha | Mike' matching Quarto 1 99.9.9, where 0.28.0 alphabetised to 'Alpha | Mike | Zulu'. The with-order, sort-false and mixed fixtures are unchanged and still match Q1.

c-kvefqmhl.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-kvefqmhl.text:
WHERE THE GAP CAME FROM — an observation about the design work, not a criticism of it.

D3's ordering rule is expressed entirely in terms of the record/glob boundary: "a glob item's index is the first positive pattern that matched it, a record's is the count of Glob entries declared before it, and is_glob breaks the tie so a record written before a glob sorts before that glob's items."

That seam then absorbed essentially all of the execution effort. D3 is itself flagged "Amended during execution (Task 5, fix rounds 1-2)", and the three refinements preserved in the code comments at listing_generate.rs:248-292 are each about it:

  - a negated pattern, or one dropped as escaped (Q-12-17) or invalid (Q-12-18), must not advance the counter, "otherwise the two indices drift apart and a record can sort after items it was written before" (review fix, task 5 round 1);
  - the position must come structurally from resolution.entry_index rather than be reconstructed by matching raw pattern text or SourceInfo, "both proved unreliable" (review fix, task 5 round 2);
  - the counter starts at 1 rather than 0 when contents: held only negations and a default positive pattern was injected, that pattern being "defined to precede every declared entry" (team-lead ruling, task 5 round 2).

Three rounds of review, one team-lead ruling, one amended design decision — all on the relative position of records against globs. The resulting code is correct: the repro's mixed/ project (record, glob, record) produces exactly the keys D3 specifies.

The question never asked was what orders a listing with NO seam — no globs, no explicit sort:, no order: — where every record ties and the outcome is decided entirely by whatever runs next. That is the case this bug is, and it is also the overwhelmingly common shape in practice: an author writing a hand-curated card list has no reason to include a glob at all. The deep case got the scrutiny; the shallow case got none, because from inside the record/glob framing it does not look like a case at all.

I want to be precise that this is NOT the mechanism. I initially assumed the all-records tie was itself the defect; it is not, because sort_by_key is stable and ties keep push order, which is declared order. The defect is one layer further out — the interaction between the newly added record item-source and the pre-existing default sort, which no phase of either plan owned.

WHY IT MAY BE WORTH GENERALISING. The same shape could recur wherever a later feature adds a new item source to listings: the new source gets designed against the existing one, and its interaction with apply_sort's defaults is nobody's phase. A cheap guard would be a test asserting that for each item source, a listing built purely from that source and carrying no explicit sort: renders in declared order. Today that test would fail only for records; it would keep failing correctly for whatever is added next.

c-ykdmk9yx.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-ykdmk9yx.text:
FIXED on branch braid/bd-listing-inline-records-order-eq8n2usm-listing-inline-records-order, commit 2afd4caa6. Local only, not pushed.

APPROACH: mirror Q1 (Gordon's call between the two options this strand laid out). A new `ListingItemSource` enum classifies each item as it is built — `Document` for a glob match, `MetadataDocument` for a record whose `path:` resolved to a project document, `Metadata` otherwise — and the default `order asc, title asc` sort is applied only when some source arms it. Sources are recorded during construction, before `apply_filters`, so `include:`/`exclude:` cannot change the decision; that is where Q1 computes its set too.

The `Metadata`/`MetadataDocument` split maps 1:1 onto q2's existing `RecordPath` enum: `RecordPath::Document` requires `is_markdown_document_path` AND a project-index hit, the same two conditions as Q1's upgrade at website-listing-read.ts:1044.

The implicit-order alternative was rejected for the reason this strand gave: documents carry no `order`, missing values sort last, so every record would float above every glob-matched document in a mixed listing.

GENERALISATION (answering the 17:30 comment). The proposed guard — 'for each item source, a listing built purely from that source and no explicit sort: renders in declared order' — is false for the document source, and positron-triage-3 confirmed this independently with a glob-only fixture (titles Zulu/Alpha/Mike over posts/{a,b,c}.qmd renders Alpha|Mike|Zulu on 0.27.0). Q1 sorts document-only listings deliberately. The dangerous outcome is not the red test but someone greening it by suppressing the default sort for document listings. Retracted in both skeins.

What generalises instead is one level up: every item source must carry an explicit decision about whether it arms the default sort. Encoded as `ListingItemSource::arms_default_sort`, an exhaustive match with NO wildcard arm, so a fourth variant does not compile until someone answers the question for it. That is a stronger guard than a test, which only fails after the new source exists and can be deleted to go green. Four tests then pin one variant each.

CORRECTION TO THE REPRO README (fixed upstream, e2c0940): the `mixed/` row's 'expected (Q1)' cell stated plan §D3's declared-position intent, not measured Q1 behaviour. Quarto 99.9.9 actually renders mixed/ as `Alpha | Post One | Post Two | Zulu` — identical to q2 before and after this fix. The glob contributes a document source, which arms the default sort in both systems. mixed/ is a diagnostic, not a parity failure, and must not be 'fixed'.

CORRECTION TO THIS STRAND'S TEXT: 'Adding order: to all 42 records restores parity exactly' describes a measurement taken on one file (welcome.qmd) and reverted, not the state of the docs tree. `git grep -n '^ *order:' -- 'docs-quarto-2/*.qmd'` is empty on main and on the port branch. Nothing becomes redundant when this fix lands.

    mixed        Alpha | Post One | Post Two | Zulu

title: Table listings ignore fields/field-display-names (item-table.template hardcodes Title|Date|Author)
description:
The built-in table listing item template (crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/templates/item-table.template) is hard-coded to '| [$title$]($path$){.no-external} | $date$ | $author$ |'. A listing with 'type: table, fields: [title]' still renders three columns (Date/Author empty when items lack them), field-display-names: is ignored for headers, and each item missing date/author produces per-item 'Undefined variable' doctemplate diagnostics surfaced as one Q-12-10 warning per listing.

Q1 behavior: fields: selects the column set and field-display-names: renames headers (e.g. a single 'How To' column).

Suggested fix: generate the table listing's columns from listing.fields (headers via field-display-names with title-case fallback), tolerating missing per-item values. The binding already carries fields + show.* flags (build_item_map in listing/binding.rs).

Real-world hit: Posit Connect docs how-to/index.md (type: table, fields: [title], field-display-names: {title: 'How To'}) renders Title|Date|Author with two empty columns + 8 undefined-variable diagnostics, vs Q1's single 'How To' column.

Minimal repro (2 items, wrong columns + Q-12-10): /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/listing-table-undefined-date/ (see README.md; run 'q2 render' there). Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-listing-table-fields-hes1dsib. Observed with q2 0.14.0.

title: llms-txt: no way to author a link that targets a markdown companion, or to opt out of the companion retarget
description:
With `website.llms-txt: true`, `LlmsCaptureTransform` (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/llms.rs, end of the Finalization phase) clones the finalized AST and retargets every same-site `.html` link whose target page has a companion to its `.md` sibling. Escapes exist only for drafts, the 404 page, external URLs, and non-page resources — there is no author-facing control over the decision.

Two things an author cannot express today:

1. **Keep this link on the HTML page, even inside the companion.** When the target page's value is its rendered presentation — an interactive demo, a lightboxed figure gallery, anything whose markdown mirror is useless — the companion should still link to the HTML.

2. **Point this link at the markdown companion, from the HTML page.** A docs site that wants a 'view the markdown for this page' affordance, or an agent-oriented reading path linked from human-facing prose, has no way to author it: `LinkRewriteTransform` (start of Finalization) rewrites `[md](guide/index.md)` to `.html`, so the companion is unreachable by authored link.

Proposal: a link attribute honored by both transforms, e.g.

    [text](guide/index.md){link-format="html"}
    [text](guide/index.md){link-format="llms"}

`LinkRewriteTransform` reads it when resolving; `LlmsCaptureTransform` checks it before retargeting. Absent the attribute, behavior is exactly as today — so this is purely opt-in and adds no diagnostics.

Real-world motivation for case 2, from the Posit Connect docs port: that project ships a 'Copy for LLM' / 'View as Markdown' button pair (`_page-actions.html`, injected via `include-in-header`) whose companion URL is computed **in JavaScript** by string surgery on `window.location.pathname`:

    if (path.endsWith('/')) return path + 'index.llms.md';
    if (path.endsWith('.html')) return path.replace(/\.html$/, '.llms.md');

It hardcodes Quarto 1's `.llms.md` naming and therefore 404s against q2's `.md` companions. The docs side has to fix its own hardcoding regardless, but the reason it is hardcoded at all is that Quarto exposes no way to obtain the companion href — so the client-side guess is the only option available, in Q1 and q2 alike.

Context on where this came from: it was first proposed as a fix for a different problem — companions are written to `<page>.md`, which for a project whose pages are `.md` files shadows the source-path namespace in the output tree, so a hand-written source-path link serves markdown instead of 404-ing. As a fix for *that* it does not work: measured on the Connect docs, 1670 in-body `.md` links are already rewritten correctly, 161 config `file:` entries resolve correctly, there are zero raw-HTML `.md` hrefs, and the single escapee is a custom metadata key (`quarto-tiers.url`) that cannot carry a Pandoc attribute. Mandatory decoration plus an undecorated-link warning would be ~100% false positive. The expressiveness gap it exposed is real on its own, and is what this strand asks for.

The companion write side is not at issue here and is working as designed (the `.quarto/llms-manifest.json` ledger plus Q-5-28 correctly refuse to clobber a user file at a companion path — verified).

Observed on q2 0.22.0. Demonstration project (shows the retarget with no available override):
`/Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/llms-companion-shadows-source-links/` — run `q2 render` there and compare `_site/index.html` with `_site/index.md`.

Origin strand in the Connect-docs-port skein: br-llms-link-target-annotation-nf84d314.

title: website.llms-txt is silently ignored — no llms.txt, no per-page .llms.md companions
description:
With 'website: {llms-txt: true}' in _quarto.yml, q2 renders the site normally but emits no llms.txt and no per-page *.llms.md files, and prints no warning — the key is accepted and dropped. Q1 honors it: alongside the HTML it writes _site/llms.txt (a markdown index linking every page as 'title → path/to/page.llms.md') plus one .llms.md companion per page, a plain-markdown rendering of that page's main content extracted from the rendered HTML.

Root cause: the feature has no output-side implementation in q2 at all. Grepping crates/ for 'llms' finds only the input side of the convention — project discovery excluding *.llms.md as agent-instruction files (crates/quarto-core/src/project/discovery.rs) — and nothing that generates them. Q1's reference implementation is quarto-cli/src/project/types/website/website-llms.ts (llmsHtmlFinalizer): an HTML post-render finalizer that skips drafts, extracts main content from the rendered DOM, strips conditional/interactive cruft, converts to markdown, writes <output>.llms.md next to each page, and a site-level pass that assembles llms.txt from page titles.

Suggested direction: a website post-render step (near where sitemap/search artifacts are produced) that, when website.llms-txt is truthy, derives each page's .llms.md from its rendered output and writes llms.txt indexing them. Even before implementing, the silent-drop half is worth fixing: an accepted-but-unimplemented key should at least warn.

Real-world hit: the Posit Connect docs set website.llms-txt: true; Q1's _site ships llms.txt + 348 *.llms.md companions, the q2 port ships none, and the docs landing page (index.md product card) links to llms.txt — so the ported site 404s on its own front page.

Minimal repro (2-page website, one render): /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/llms-txt-unimplemented/ — run 'q2 render .' there and 'find _site -name llms.txt -o -name *.llms.md' comes back empty; see README.md for Q1's expected output. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-llms-txt-unimplemented-qmgjbb46. Observed with q2 0.21.0; confirmed absent at HEAD (3ac596e0).

title: Carry code_fence_content provenance on CodeBlock instead of re-locating the body by search
description:
`process_fenced_code_block` (pampa `crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/fenced_code_block.rs:30`) discards the range that `process_code_fence_content` (`code_fence_content.rs:14-50`) computes for the body: it destructures `IntermediateBaseText(text, _)` and builds the `CodeBlock` with only the whole-node `location`. So every consumer that needs the body's span re-derives it:

- `quarto-core` `crossref/codeblock_shorthand.rs::body_source_for` byte-searches the block's raw text. A body equal to a substring of its own info string mislocated (measured: for ```` ```{python} ```` with body `python`, it returned `4..10` inside `{python}` where the truth is `12..18`). Plan 3 Phase 6a bounded that search to the region between the fence lines (test `body_source_for_locates_the_body_not_the_info_string`), which removes the measured mislocation — but it is still a search, and it still has one measured hole: a body whose last line is made only of fence characters in a block that tree-sitter error recovery left without a closing fence degrades to the whole-block span.
- `quarto-core` `text_execute.rs:304-308` builds `body_source` as `substring(ctx.source_info, code_start, code_start + code.len())` over the engine's *writer* provenance.

Fix: add `text_source: SourceInfo` to `CodeBlock` (`quarto-pandoc-types/src/block.rs:117-122`; precedent: the existing `attr_source`), built with `ProvenanceBuilder` so elided `block_continuation` markers (`> `, list indentation — `code_fence_content.rs:27-45`) become gaps rather than a false verbatim run. `body_source_for` then becomes `cb.text_source.clone()` and `text_execute.rs` can stop deriving body provenance from writer provenance.

Scope: this is a type change, not a consumer fix. `grep -c 'CodeBlock {'` across `crates/` finds 74 construction sites in 45 files, plus JSON writer/reader `r`/`p` wire support, the `annotated-qmd` TS schema, and snapshot churn.

Why outside the epic: the provenance epic's three plans are about *consumers* of provenance and deliberately do not touch AST type shapes; opening this inside the epic would exit it with an unaudited new producer.

Source of the design: `claude-notes/research/2026-08-23-provenance-3-design-recommendations.md` § 1 (option 2). Consumer-side mitigation landed in `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-3-audit-and-fix.md` Phase 6.

title: Hub-client: cross-doc link clicks don't switch editor in website projects
description:
Reproduced 2026-05-01 against the dev server.

In hub-client, clicking a cross-document link inside the preview iframe should switch the active editor file to the link's target. This works in non-website projects (link href ./another.qmd → editor switches) but is broken in website projects.

In a website project, the body-link / nav-href transforms rewrite [About](about.qmd) → <a href="/.quarto/project-artifacts/about.html">. The rewrite is correct for deployed websites and is shared with the hub-client preview so artifact (CSS / image) resolution stays uniform. But the iframe click handler in hub-client/src/utils/iframePostProcessor.ts:140-158 only intercepts hrefs ending in .qmd; the rewritten .html URLs slip through and the click is a no-op inside the about:srcdoc iframe.

Same defect applies to sidebar entries (when the sidebar is visible at vp >= 992 px) — they share the same artifact-rooted .html shape.

Repro:
- localhost:5173 'test website' (project ID prefix 25a55Noy, copy of examples/websites/08-hub-preview/).
- Open index.qmd. Click [About] in body. Hash unchanged at …/file/index.qmd.
- Compare to 'No website' (3ZcKVsWZ): clicking [page](./another.qmd) in index correctly switches the route to …/file/another.qmd.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-01-website-link-navigation.md (Option A recommended: reverse-map artifact-rooted .html → source .qmd at click time using the project file list as the source of truth).

Parent epic: bd-0tr6 (websites).
close_reason: Fixed in 2441ad8d: reverseMapArtifactHref + new postProcessIframe pass intercepts artifact-rooted .html links and reverse-maps to source .qmd. Strict scope (only intercepts when source exists). 10 unit + 7 integration tests; verified end-to-end via Chrome DevTools MCP on test website (about.html / posts/first.html → switch editor) and No website (./another.qmd regression check).

title: Design discussion: no diagnostic for a lone bare [text], and the warning-suppression question underneath it
description:
A lone bare bracket group — [Version TBD], [1], [Posit Connect] — has its brackets silently deleted, with no diagnostic. Q-2-45 and Q-2-46 (added in 0.17.0) cover the other two shapes of reference-link breakage; this third shape stays silent.

**This strand is opened as a design discussion, not a defect report.** The gap is deliberate and documented, and the person filing it agrees the existing reasoning is sound given today's constraints. What is being questioned is one of the constraints. See "Requested discussion" below — Carlos would like to talk this through with whoever picks it up before any implementation.

## What happens vs Quarto 1

    Multiple email support requires Posit Connect [Version TBD] or later.
    Upon an initial user session [1], the server creates a cookie (RSC-XSRF) [2].
    The default subject prefix is "[Posit Connect]".

Quarto 1 renders all of these literally, brackets included. q2 parses [...] as the bracket half of span syntax, finds no attribute block, emits a bare <span>, and drops the brackets — so the reader sees "Version TBD", "1", "2", "Posit Connect". Nothing is reported.

This is the shape that changes meaning without breaking a link, so it is the one a reader is least likely to notice and an author is least likely to grep for. Two Connect pages documented the WRONG default mail subject prefix this way for the duration of the port.

## The existing decision, and why this is not simply an oversight

crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/reference_link_diagnostics.rs, module docs, says so explicitly:

  "A **lone** bare bracket group — `[Version TBD]`, `[1]`, `[Posit Connect]` — is not diagnosed, even though its brackets are silently deleted too. There is no way to tell it apart from a deliberate `[text]` span, so warning on it would fire on legitimate documents. Both triggers below are instead shapes that are *never* intentional qmd."

and notes the downstream consequence: literal-brackets is a run-check-first, opt-in qmd-syntax-helper rule (crates/qmd-syntax-helper/src/conversions/literal_brackets.rs) rather than a diagnostic-code-keyed q_2_NN.rs one, precisely because no Q-code exists for it to key off.

That reasoning is correct as far as it goes. A bare [text] span with no attributes IS legitimate qmd, and a warning that fires on legitimate documents is a bad warning.

## Requested discussion

Carlos would like to discuss, with the design/implementation agent on the q2 side, the wisdom of the general rule this rests on: should q2 decline to warn about a construct merely because someone might use it intentionally?

His expectation is that working this through produces a second, larger design item: **project metadata in Quarto 2 that intentionally suppresses selected warnings**. Note there is no such mechanism today — nothing in crates/quarto-config/src or crates/quarto-error-reporting/src implements warning suppression, allow-lists, or per-code silencing.

That is the crux. The "it would fire on legitimate documents" objection is currently unanswerable, because a project that legitimately uses bare spans has no way to say so. Given a suppression mechanism, the calculus changes: a warning on an ambiguous-but-usually-wrong construct becomes acceptable, because the small number of projects that mean it can opt out once, in one place, instead of every reader of every other project silently getting wrong output.

So the sequencing worth discussing is probably: design the suppression mechanism first, then revisit this diagnostic (and any others that were scoped down for the same reason) against the new constraint.

## Suggested direction, if the discussion lands that way

Warn on a Span with an empty attribute block, pointing at the escape (backslash-escaped brackets) as the fix. That gives the qmd-syntax-helper literal-brackets rule a Q-code to key off in the q_2_NN.rs convention, folding it into the same shape as the other diagnostic-driven rules. Worth pairing with the suppression design so the two ship coherently.

## Real-world hit in the Connect docs

admin/appendix/branding and admin/email (the documented default mail subject prefix is literally "[Posit Connect]" — both pages stated the wrong value), admin/security (the [1]..[4] markers keyed to a numbered diagram), admin/opentelemetry/signal-reference-guide (histogram bucket lists), user/quarto ([Version TBD]).

The docs-side worklist has since been fixed by hand, so the Connect corpus is clean — which is exactly why the diagnostic still matters. Nothing stops the next author from writing "[Posit Connect]" again, and nothing will tell them.

## Repro

/Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/reference-links-unsupported/

Run "q2 render" there. Section A (reference links plus their definitions, lines 7/9/20/21) produces 4 warnings — 2x Q-2-45, 2x Q-2-46. Section B (lines 13/15/16/18, the lone-bracket cases) produces none, and all four render with the brackets gone.

Observed on q2 0.17.0 through 0.19.0 (re-verified against the released 0.19.0 binary; HEAD 1ba0f2ec). Origin strand in the q2-connect-docs skein: br-e7mco18f, related to br-raalju6n.

c-gv4nf8al.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-gv4nf8al.text:
Implemented and committed (d6589498, branch braid/bd-lone-bracket-diagnostic-warning-suppression). Not pushed — awaiting permission.

Carlos's decisions: per-code map with reason encouraged; minimal suppression (off only) + Q-2-49 shipped together; applies everywhere including preview/hub; uncoded warnings unsuppressible in v1 with no lint.

The seam turned out to be run_pipeline (pipeline.rs:811), not the ProjectRenderSummary boundary --strict uses. The summary is CLI-only, so it would have excluded preview/hub — exactly what decision 3 required. run_pipeline's tail is the one expression every per-document diagnostic passes through for every frontend, and applying there also lands strictly before --strict's promotion, so suppress-then-promote falls out rather than needing enforcement. Resolution is split out into MetadataMergeStage, where merged metadata exists.

New codes: Q-2-49 (markdown, lone bare bracket group) and Q-5-23 (project, invalid diagnostics: entry), both with docs pages in the same commit.

Verification: cargo xtask verify full 14/14 green; 11700 workspace tests; lint clean. End-to-end on the repro with the real binary — all four previously-silent Section B cases now warn with precise spans, _quarto.yml suppression removes Q-2-49 and leaves Q-2-45/Q-2-46, --strict exits 0 with everything suppressed, malformed entry reports Q-5-23 and suppresses nothing. NOT verified: a live q2 preview browser session (pipeline covered by unit test only).

One pre-existing test changed deliberately (does_not_treat_a_mid_line_colon_span_as_a_definition). No snapshot files touched.

Follow-ups: bd-91rgxmav, bd-cljk1g5p.

c-xupkbrwx.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-xupkbrwx.text: Investigation done (2026-08-12). Plan skeleton: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-warning-suppression-and-lone-bracket-diagnostic.md on branch braid/bd-lone-bracket-diagnostic-warning-suppression (commit e141e4bf). Verdict: ready to design; suppression first, then Q-2-49. Findings that shape the design: - No suppression machinery exists. But --strict (bd-yjs54ptg) already built the seam: ProjectRenderSummary::promote_warnings_to_errors() (orchestrator.rs:617) applies a severity policy to all four diagnostic sources post-run/pre-print, via OutputDiagnostics::diagnostics_mut(). Suppression is the same shape with a filter instead of a mutation. - A lone bare span renders as text (pampa html.rs:996) — inert HTML. Weakens the 'someone might mean it' objection; residual legitimate use is a Lua filter hooking bare spans. - ~25-30 user-visible warnings carry no code and would be silently unsuppressible. bd-m2w7a is the backfill worklist (now linked as related). - No config schema layer (render.rs:894), so a new key is free but a typo in a suppression list is silent -> unknown-code validation is load-bearing. - render.rs:897 prints config diagnostics via bare eprintln!, bypassing the summary any policy layer would filter. - Preliminary noise probe: zero AST-level lone bare spans in docs/. 7 open design questions await Carlos.

title: Fix toc: false semantics to be an affirmative disable (uniform with navbar/page-footer)
description:
Currently crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/toc_generate.rs only matches toc: true and toc: 'auto' for should_generate; toc: false falls through to 'don't generate', same as absent key. This means a document cannot override inherited toc: true from _quarto.yml with toc: false — users have to write toc: !prefer false.

Fix: treat toc: false after metadata merge as an affirmative disable. Apply identical logic across toc/navbar/page-footer so the rule is uniform.

Tracked alongside bd-imiw (navbar/footer design). See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-18-navbar-footer-design.md Phase 0.

title: Q-12-7 message asserts a `type:` the user never declared
description:
Separate from the source-span defect (bd-9yh3pzfu): the Q-12-7 text itself is wrong for the common input.

Message: '`template:` was set but `type:` is not `custom`; falling back to the built-in template for the declared type.'

For `listing: {template: ..., contents: ...}` with no `type:` key:
1. It asserts the user set `type:` to something non-custom. They set no `type:` at all -- ListingType::Default is Q2's own default (listing/config.rs:398).
2. 'the built-in template for the DECLARED type' names a declaration absent from the document.

The check at listing/config.rs:534 is `l.template.is_some() && l.kind != ListingType::Custom`, which cannot distinguish 'declared default' from 'defaulted'. Fix: track explicit-vs-defaulted type; reword for the no-type case. The genuinely-wrong case (explicit `type: grid` AND `template:`) still deserves today's warning.

Also: docs/errors/listing/Q-12-7.qmd states the Q1-migration cause is 'where some templates were attached to non-custom types in a way Quarto 2 does not preserve'. That is not what Q1 does -- website-listing-read.ts:1316-1320 makes `template:` IMPLY `type: custom`. The docs page needs correcting regardless of the code change.

Open design question: should Q2 adopt Q1's implies-custom rule? Same code site. Deferred here rather than decided; note that with EJS unsupported (see sibling strand) implies-custom mainly changes which diagnostic fires, not whether the page renders.
