title: Lua filters in the returned-table form are silently ignored
description:
WHAT HAPPENS. A Lua filter written in the standard Pandoc returned-table form is read, runs none of its handlers, and produces no error, warning, or diagnostic of any kind:

    -- silently does nothing
    return { Str = function(el) … end }

    -- works
    function Str(el) … end

Both forms are valid Pandoc, and Quarto 1 runs both. The returned-table form is the more common of the two in real filters: it keeps handlers out of the global namespace, and it is the only way to express an ordered list of passes (`return { {Str=…}, {Para=…} }`), which is likewise ignored today.

Verified with identical handler bodies in both forms, for `filters:` declared in project metadata (`_quarto.yml`), in document frontmatter, and on a standalone single-file render — all three behave the same.

The failure mode is the worst available one for a project migrating extensions: a declared filter quietly does nothing, and nothing in the output says so.

WHERE IT LIVES. crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs. `apply_lua_filter` (~line 221) loads the filter chunk with

    lua.load(&filter_source).set_name(…).exec_async().await?;

`exec_async` DISCARDS the chunk's return value, so a top-level `return { … }` goes nowhere. The handler table is then rebuilt from scratch by `get_filter_table` (~line 323), which only ever reads globals: it walks a hardcoded list of ~50 element names and copies any same-named global function into a fresh table.

`get_filter_table`'s own doc comment states the intended contract and describes behavior the code does not implement:

    // Pandoc filters can either:
    // 1. Return a table with filter functions
    // 2. Define filter functions as globals
    // We'll support both by creating a table that checks globals

Case 1 was never wired up.

Nothing downstream needs to change. `apply_full_filter` already takes a handler table as an argument, and the repro proves the table-consuming path works end to end: a filter defining a global `Pandoc` handler that calls `doc:walk{Str = …}` fires correctly and rewrites the marker. The bug is confined to the entry point that throws the returned table away.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION. Load the chunk with `eval_async::<Value>()` instead of `exec_async()` and inspect the result:

  - a table of handlers → use it directly, with no name whitelist (matching Pandoc, so filters may define handlers q2's hardcoded list omits);
  - a SEQUENCE of handler tables → apply them as successive passes, in order. This shape is why authors reach for the returned-table form in the first place, so a fix handling only the single-table case is incomplete;
  - nil / anything else → fall back to the existing globals scan, so the currently-working form keeps working.

`get_walking_order` (~line 88) already reads `traverse` off a filter table, so per-table traversal mode comes along for free.

If the returned-table form is instead meant to stay unsupported — q2's own docs at docs/guides/authoring/lua-filters.qmd show only the top-level function form, so this may be a deliberate subset — then it needs a load-time diagnostic. A chunk that returns a table and defines no recognised globals is unambiguously this mistake, and it is silent today.

REAL-WORLD HIT (Posit Connect docs). The mermaid-zoom extension (_extensions/posit-dev/mermaid-zoom/, declared as `filters: [mermaid-zoom]`) is written in the returned-table form, so it never runs: the pan/zoom overlay for large diagrams is silently absent from all 14 diagram pages, with no hint that a declared filter did nothing. Diagnosing that took a bisect against a hand-written control filter, because there is no signal anywhere in the render output.

ADJACENT FINDING, same investigation, likely worth its own decision. User filters run BEFORE the mermaid transform under q2: a mermaid block is still a CodeBlock with class "mermaid" when user filters see it, and crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/mermaid.rs converts it to a RawBlock later, at TransformPhase::Finalization. Quarto 1 is the other way round — mermaid-zoom.lua's own comment says "By the time user filters run, Quarto has already turned a {mermaid} cell into a RawBlock of HTML", which is why it matches RawBlock. So a ported filter that reacts to diagrams must match CodeBlock under q2 and RawBlock under Q1. Whether that ordering is intended is a separate question from this strand, but it bites the same extensions.

Also noted in passing: quarto.doc.add_html_dependency works (assets land under _files/<name>/), but warns Q-11-1 that field 'version' is not yet supported and will be ignored.

REPRO. /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/lua-filter-table-form-ignored/ — run `q2 render` there. Four documents, identical handler bodies, one per form:

  index.qmd      + table-form.lua     `return { Str = … }`                  → MARKER unchanged, filter did not run
  list-form.qmd  + list-form.lua      `return { {Str=…}, {Str=…} }`         → MARKER unchanged, filter did not run
  control.qmd    + function-form.lua  `function Str(el)`                    → FUNCTION-FORM-RAN, works
  walk-form.qmd  + walk-form.lua      global Pandoc + `doc:walk{Str = …}`   → WALK-TABLE-RAN, works

README.md carries expected vs actual, the root-cause analysis above, and the adjacent findings. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path.

Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-u35hvil9. Observed with q2 0.16.0 and re-verified failing on 0.17.0 / origin/main @ 001cb6a5.
close_reason: Fix merged in PR #508 (24c6a842), shipped in v0.18.0. Verified end-to-end in installed q2 0.19.0 using the q2-connect-docs repro (llms-info/repros/lua-filter-table-form-ignored): returned-table, ordered-list, walk-table, and top-level-function forms all execute. c-fa6qf5xz.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-fa6qf5xz.text:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-11 (main @ 808215fc, commit b457433c). Plan skeleton:
claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-lua-filter-returned-table-form.md
Artifacts: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-lua-filter-returned-table-form-investigation/
(repro copied in-tree so it survives the local-only q2-connect-docs checkout,
plus 11 pandoc probe scripts and run-parity-matrix.sh).

VERDICT: ready to design. Root cause confirmed exactly as filed. Also confirmed
this is not a regression - get_filter_table arrived globals-only with the
original Lua landing (0f9fc8da, 2025-12-02); the 2026-04 async conversion
(e537fb80) only changed exec() to exec_async().

Confirmed the fix needs no whitelist: the walker is fully name-agnostic
(inline_fn/block_fn look handlers up by tag; pass_is_active iterates the
table's own keys). The whitelist is an artifact of the globals path only.
The fix pattern already exists in-tree - the shortcode loader (shortcode.rs:190)
does eval_async + returned-table registration already.

NEW: pinned pandoc's semantics by probe against 3.9.0.2 (the version the
differential oracle is pinned to, so these convert straight into cases). Rule:
no returned value -> globals; ANY returned value wins outright and globals are
never consulted (rawlen 0 -> single filter, rawlen > 0 -> list of passes,
non-table -> error).

That last part makes strict parity a behavior CHANGE, not a pure addition.
Five filter shapes that work today would flip:
  mixed     global Str + return {Str=g}   pandoc TABLE-RAN   q2 GLOBAL-RAN
  empty     global Str + return {}        pandoc nothing     q2 GLOBAL-RAN
  emptylist global Str + return { {} }    pandoc nothing     q2 GLOBAL-RAN
  nilret    global Str + return nil       pandoc ERROR       q2 GLOBAL-RAN
  num       global Str + return 5         pandoc ERROR       q2 GLOBAL-RAN
This is design question 1 in the plan and needs a decision before implementation.

ADJACENT FINDING (ordering) - resolved down to a defaulting question. Verified
by running it: the Q1-equivalent RawBlock view IS reachable today with no code
change. With a plain ```mermaid fence, a filter at the default position sees
CodeBlock[mermaid]; listed after the `quarto` sentinel, or with
`at: post-quarto`, it sees RawBlock html <pre class="mermaid">. So the real
question is only whether pre-quarto is the right default and whether the choice
is discoverable - not a port blocker.

CORRECTION to this strand's write-up: the class is `mermaid` only for the plain
fence. Q1's ```{mermaid} executable-cell spelling keeps the literal class
`{mermaid}` and renders no diagram - but that is NOT a bug: it is a deliberate,
documented syntax decision (claude-notes/plans/2026-07-20-mermaid-regular-rendering.md
section "Syntax decision", guarded by a brace_form_mermaid_cell_untouched test).

Pre-flight: cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build - all 11664 Rust tests pass.
The one failure (hub-client test:wasm, mermaid/basic.qmd expecting
mermaid.min.js) was a stale WASM artifact from --skip-hub-build; after
npm run build:wasm, test:wasm is 131/131 green. HEAD is green.

c-hk482oso.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-hk482oso.text:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11, commit ce813478 on main (NOT pushed; awaiting review).

Filter scripts now follow pandoc's rule end to end:
  - returns nothing      -> handlers from the globals
  - returns any value    -> that value IS the filter, globals ignored
      table rawlen == 0  -> one filter
      table rawlen > 0   -> list of filters applied as successive passes,
                            each honoring its own `traverse`
      anything else      -> Q-11-6 error

Two implementation notes worth carrying forward, both non-obvious and both
places where the obvious reading of the plan is wrong:

  - call_async, NOT eval_async. mlua's eval first tries to compile the source
    as an EXPRESSION and only falls back to a block, which would make q2 accept
    a filter file containing a bare `{ Str = f }` that pandoc rejects as a
    syntax error. call_async compiles strictly as a block, like pandoc's
    dofile. (Note in passing: shortcode.rs uses eval_async and has the same
    latent widening. Not filed - different contract, no pandoc equivalent.)

  - MultiValue, NOT Value. Value collapses "returned nothing" and "returned
    nil" into the same Value::Nil, but those must diverge (globals vs error).
    The classifier switches on a COUNT of returned values.

DIAGNOSTICS. Q-11-6 (invalid script return) and Q-11-7 (unrecognized handler
name, with an edit-distance suggestion), each with catalog entry + docs page in
the same commit. Live output:

  Warning [Q-11-7]: Lua filter 'typo.lua' defines a handler 'Strs', which is
  not an element type Quarto knows about, so it will never run. Did you mean
  'Str'?

Q-11-6 got its own LuaFilterError variant so it renders as
"Q-11-6: Lua filter 'num.lua' returned number, ..." rather than the nested
"Filter error: Lua filter error: runtime error: Q-11-6: ...".

LIMITATION worth knowing: the Q-11-7 warning covers the RETURNED-TABLE form
only. A typo in a GLOBAL handler name (`function Strs(el)` at top level) is
indistinguishable from an ordinary helper function, so it cannot be warned
about. Mitigated in docs by steering authors toward `local` helpers.

bd-18a2r2lp FIXED as part of this. Rather than hand-writing the name list a
second time with a test to keep it in step - which is the arrangement that
caused the bug, just with an alarm on it - tag_name is now generated by an
element_tag_names! macro emitting both the match arms and the list of names it
can return. The match stays exhaustive, so a new AST variant fails to compile
until listed, and the constant cannot disagree with the dispatch. Drift is
unrepresentable rather than merely detected.

TESTS. 13 return-value unit tests + 2 bd-18a2r2lp regressions + 7
warning/edit-distance tests, all observed FAILING first (messages recorded in
the plan's phase log). 8 new differential cases with real pandoc 3.9.0.2
oracles; 0 existing oracles changed. The three error-shaped probes cannot be
oracle cases (the harness compares JSON ASTs, pandoc produces none) so they are
unit tests.

VERIFIED. pampa 4378/4378; workspace 11708/11708; cargo xtask lint clean. Full
`cargo xtask verify` (with the WASM leg, since pampa is in that closure) in
progress. End-to-end: the four-document repro renders TABLE-FORM-RAN and
LIST-FORM-RAN where it rendered an untouched MARKER, and run-parity-matrix.sh
matches pandoc on every AST-shaped row.

Plan + phase log: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-lua-filter-returned-table-form.md
Downstream verification strand in the connect-docs skein: br-vuf8asgk.

c-kyop8war.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-kyop8war.text:
DESIGN SETTLED 2026-08-11 (commit 54a1114d). All four questions answered:

1. Strict pandoc parity, wholesale - no softening for the shapes pandoc treats
   as errors. Every divergent shape is a filter doing two conflicting things at
   once (returning a value AND defining globals), so there is no defensible
   "right" answer to pick between them; matching pandoc is the least harm. All
   five flipping shapes flip deliberately.

2. Invalid script return -> hard error with an actionable diagnostic. Behavior
   matches pandoc; the message does not (ours names the filter path and the
   offending Lua type). Explicit `return nil` errors too. Rationale:
   `return { ... }` is an affirmative choice, whereas a global `Str = function`
   can plausibly be an accidental collision - a script that returns something
   uninterpretable has stated an intent we cannot honor.

3. Warn on unrecognized handler names - adopted into Phase 3, not deferred. The
   argument is regression surfacing more than typo catching: if q2 ever fails
   to recognize a handler name it should support, that reaches the user as a
   visible diagnostic instead of silence.

4. New code Q-11-6 "Invalid Lua Filter Script Return Value", not a widened
   Q-11-4. Docs page ships in the same commit (error-docs-page-missing lint).
   The decision-3 warning needs its own code too, likely Q-11-7.

DISCOVERED while scoping the decision-3 warning: bd-18a2r2lp. The globals
whitelist in get_filter_table has drifted from the walker's actual dispatch
vocabulary (tag_name in types.rs) and silently drops five dispatchable tags:
Attr, BlockMetadata, CaptionBlock, NoteDefinitionFencedBlock,
NoteDefinitionPara. Proven with doc:walk, which hands the walker a table
directly and bypasses the whitelist: the same handler name fires as a table
entry and does not fire as a global. It is a live instance of exactly the class
the warning is meant to surface, and it settles how the warning must be built -
derive the name set from tag_name plus the catch-alls, not a third hand-written
list.

Plan phases are now written (Phase 0 tests-first through Phase 4 docs).
Implementation has NOT started and awaits go-ahead.

title: ReplayEngine miss in q2 preview: server's recorded input_qmd != WASM-produced input_qmd (mtime-derived listing-item.date-modified)
description: After bd-m0mu (project registry plumbing) and bd-4uvv (samod automerge: URL prefix) are fixed, the SPA delivers the recorded capture bytes to the WASM. EngineExecutionStage now constructs ReplayEngine successfully — but ReplayEngine's strict byte-equality miss policy fires: 'replay miss: input QMD does not match recorded input (recorded 579 bytes, got 551 bytes).' 28-byte delta. The recorded input_qmd includes 'listing-item.date-modified: 2026-05-18' (server reads file mtime via NativeRuntime). The WASM-side q2-preview pipeline, running over the same source under WasmRuntime, doesn't have the same mtime in VFS so the listing-item.date-modified line is absent (or different). Net: every q2 preview render of a project with a website-type _quarto.yml hits a replay miss and shows the error overlay instead of rendered output. Repro fixture: ~/Desktop/daily-log/2026/05/15/q2-preview-test-website. Diagnosed end-to-end on 2026-05-18. Design space (pick one, needs user judgment): (a) compute_input_qmd strips mtime-derived metadata before serialization on server; (b) WasmRuntime populates mtimes in VFS so listing-item.date-modified surfaces in WASM too; (c) ReplayEngine loosens miss policy under preview mode (probably wrong — replay is a regression-testing tool); (d) cell-only diff for input_qmd canonicalization (the Phase-C polish path the C.3 plan flagged as Q-C3 v2). Plan §Q-C3 originally accepted whole-QMD byte-equality as a known v1 limitation; this surfaces it as a hard user-facing blocker.

c-huwep91o.text: Design pivoted 2026-05-18 after user clarification: preview should NOT consume captures through ReplayEngine (which is a deterministic regression-testing tool with intentionally strict miss policy). Instead, derive an AST-level transformation from (parse(input_qmd), parse(result.markdown)) and splice it onto the live-edited pre-engine AST. Full design at claude-notes/plans/2026-05-18-q2-preview-project-replay-engine.md. Supersedes bd-m0mu (closed). bd-4uvv stays valid. Key shape per user note: (structural_hash(cell_content), occurrence_index_in_doc_order) to disambiguate repeated identical cells.

title: External scanner lexes '< text >' with inner whitespace as html_element, swallowing inline closers (unclosed-emphasis errors)
description: Repro: '*a < b this text is interpreted as an HTML element.* a > b' fails with Q-2-12 Unclosed Star Emphasis. parse_open_angle_brace in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c scans from '<' to the next '>' and emits a best-effort HTML_ELEMENT token (54 bytes here), swallowing the closing '*' of the emphasis. Deleting the '>' makes the error vanish because the bd-j9cf EOF fallback then emits LT_STR_LITERAL instead. Fix: whitespace immediately after '<' disqualifies HTML_ELEMENT (per CommonMark/HTML an open tag's name must immediately follow '<'), so bare '< ' becomes a literal Str, matching Pandoc. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-07-angle-bracket-inner-whitespace.md
close_reason: Fixed and verified; commit 59d1edf9 on braid/bd-ly83qewg-angle-inner-whitespace (not yet pushed)

c-jwe8sptl.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-jwe8sptl.text: Reproduced and diagnosed. Plan (awaiting review, not yet implemented): claude-notes/plans/2026-08-07-angle-bracket-inner-whitespace.md. Key evidence: 'pampa -v' shows 'lexed_lookahead sym:html_element, size:54' — parse_open_angle_brace's HTML_ELEMENT arm has no whitespace guard (unlike AUTOLINK's could_be_autolink), so '< … >' spanning an emphasis closer swallows the '*'. Pandoc parses the same input as literal Str '<' / '>' with the emphasis closed. Proposed fix: whitespace immediately after '<' disqualifies HTML_ELEMENT; RAW_SPECIFIER path untouched; bd-j9cf LT_STR_LITERAL fallback covers the rest.

c-s9h246v2.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-s9h246v2.text: Fixed on branch braid/bd-ly83qewg-angle-inner-whitespace (commit 59d1edf9). TDD: 3 corpus cases + 3 pampa tests written and verified failing first (repro died with Q-2-12). Fix: html_possible guard + LT_STR_LITERAL fast path in parse_open_angle_brace; RAW_SPECIFIER path unchanged; whitespace-before-'>' deliberately not disqualifying ('<div >' is a valid open tag). Verification: tree-sitter corpus 545/545; full 'cargo xtask verify' green (workspace build+tests, WASM, hub-client); no .snap churn. E2E (output inspected): 'target/debug/pampa repro.qmd' on '*a < b this text is interpreted as an HTML element.* a > b' → [ Para [Emph [Str "a", Space, Str "<", …, Str "element."], Space, Str "a", Space, Str ">", Space, Str "b"] ] — structurally identical to pandoc -t native. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-07-angle-bracket-inner-whitespace.md

title: CSP for the SPA document + hub CSP additions
description:
Add a Content-Security-Policy to the SPA HTML document (served by nginx / the local-prod Node proxy, which the hub never sees, so hub build_csp cannot cover it), and consider the hub-side additions frame-ancestors/base-uri/object-src/form-action.

STATUS 2026-07-28: implemented once, then REMOVED from the branch entirely (history replayed so it was never implemented) because the SPA policy BROKE THE PREVIEW PANES in hub-client. No longer part of the bd-uv8xynxk plan; re-land as standalone work. See the comment below for the diagnosis — read it before re-attempting.

c-3jbt1hti.author: shikokuchuo
c-3jbt1hti.text:
Why the first attempt broke the preview (diagnosis, 2026-07-28)

The SPA policy was applied to EVERY static response, and the preview host
documents are static responses too — not just index.html. Two conflicts,
found by code inspection:

1. style-src lacked blob:. Q2PreviewIframe ships the compiled theme CSS to
   the iframe as a blob URL (URL.createObjectURL,
   ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/iframe/Q2PreviewIframe.tsx:405-433) and
   q2-preview.html consumes it as <link rel=stylesheet href=blob:...>
   (preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/entry.tsx applyTheme). An explicit
   style-src means no default-src fallback rescues it, so the React preview
   loses its theme.
2. srcdoc iframes INHERIT the embedder policy. The HTML preview path assigns
   iframe.srcdoc = html (MorphIframe.tsx:269), so the rendered document runs
   under the SPA script-src, which had no 'unsafe-inline'. Any inline
   <script> in rendered Quarto output is blocked. NOT confirmed against real
   rendered output — verify before re-landing.

Recover the removed code from the pre-rewrite commit 6131a283 (kept locally
on branch backup/auth-hardening-pre-h4-removal):
  git show 6131a283 -- scripts/spa-csp.mjs hub-client/src/utils/spaCsp.test.ts
The H2 follow-up bf394fcc added only a comment to spa-csp.mjs.

A re-land needs: blob: in style-src; a decision on the srcdoc-inherited
script-src; and an audit of EVERY document the static layer serves
(index.html, q2-preview.html, q2-debug.html, q2-raw.html) rather than
index.html alone — a per-document policy is probably the right shape, since
the preview hosts and the SPA shell have genuinely different needs.

Process lesson: the plan called a real browser E2E mandatory for exactly
this reason ('CSP breakage is runtime-only') and it was skipped — no browser
tooling. The curl check confirmed the header was PRESENT, which is not the
same property. Static assertions over index.html could not have caught it,
because the preview hosts load their styles at runtime.

title: q2 preview: project-mode WASM render path drops engine_registry → cell output missing in iframe
description: When q2 preview runs against a project (`_quarto.yml` present), the project-mode WASM render path in `render_project_active_page_to_response` (crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1431) takes `_engine_registry: Option<EngineRegistry>` and never threads it into the pass-2 renderer. `RenderToPreviewAstRenderer::render` (crates/quarto-core/src/project/pass2_renderer.rs:593) then calls `render_qmd_to_preview_ast(.., None)` with a hardcoded `None`. The ReplayEngine built from the capture binary doc is built and discarded — code cells render as raw `<pre><code class="{r}">` source instead of the captured `<div class="cell">` + `.cell-output-stdout` output. Single-file mode is fine; only project mode is broken. Reproduced 2026-05-18 against ~/Desktop/daily-log/2026/05/15/q2-preview-test-website/. title: Perf: merged document metadata (ConfigValue tree) is cloned and dropped whole by several per-document stages
description: Attribution of ConfigValue::clone (7.1% inclusive) + drop_in_place::<ConfigValueKind> across the Connect docs render: ShortcodeResolveTransform clones ast.meta twice per document (meta_snapshot, resolved_meta: 1.4% clone + 0.9% drop), ApplyTemplateStage clones it (1.0% + 0.9% drop), the Lua filter driver clones it per filter (1.3%) plus Block clones (0.8%), quarto_config::website::resolve_website_value / format::resolve_format_config clone sub-trees (0.8% + 0.6%), compile_theme_css rebuilds Vec<Sidebar> from config per doc (0.5%). title: Q-2-31 blames a nonexistent backtick for literal braces in a link/image URL
description:
A literal brace run inside a link or image *destination* is diagnosed as Q-2-31 'Inline Code Execution Not Allowed in URLs', whose detail label reads 'This opening backtick begins an invalid code execution attempt' -- pointing at a backtick that does not exist in the source.

Repro (q2 at 168bcdbae):

    see [text](https://ex.com/{guid}/y) here.

    code    = Q-2-31
    title   = Inline Code Execution Not Allowed in URLs
    problem = Inline code execution syntax (`{language} ...) cannot be used inside image or link destinations.
    detail  = This opening backtick begins an invalid code execution attempt.   <-- there is no backtick
    hint    = Could you instead write an entire image or link as the code result?

The author is told to look for a backtick and for inline code execution, neither of which is present; the actual problem is that '{' is reserved. The right message is Q-2-41's ('curly braces are reserved for attribute syntax ... escape them as \{...\}'), or a URL-specific variant of it.

This is the *wrong-code* half of the state-keyed-diagnostics failure mode, the mirror image of bd-shortcode-naked-value-nonascii-47fzbmow -- not the silent half. It fails at (state 3047, sym _close_block), a state Q-2-31 legitimately claims for the genuine backtick spelling; the brace spelling reaches the same state and inherits the label. So the fix is NOT another corpus case: it needs the emit-time validation the parent strand sketches -- check that the captured span actually satisfies the claimed condition (here: that a backtick is present) and fall back to the generic error, or to a brace-specific case, when it does not.

Why it matters: REST path parameters in URLs ('/v1/content/{guid}/bundles') are exactly the Connect corpus shape that motivated Q-2-41 in the first place, and linking to such a path is at least as common as writing it in prose.

Deliberately out of scope for bd-brace-hint-misses-emphasis-4fzv1n93, which closed the silent/uncoded half across all eleven unclaimed inline-container states. Found while probing brace behaviour in every inline context for that strand.

title: SCSS cache key ignores @import'ed partials: editing _colors.scss (or posit-docs' _posit-colors.scss) serves stale cached CSS
description: compile_theme_css::cache_key hashes only the top-level custom theme file's contents, not the files it @imports. Repro (claude-notes/plans/scss-cache-key-path-investigation/fixture, main @ 35bc11415): theme.scss does @import "_colors"; render, edit _colors.scss ($repro-fg #123456 -> #abcdef), re-render: emitted quarto-theme-*.css still says .repro{color:#123456}, cache dir unchanged. Users must rm -rf .quarto/cache/sass to see partial edits. Fix shape: hash the transitive import closure's contents (mirror grass import resolution: theme dir + load paths, _ partial prefix, .scss/.sass/.css, skip url()/http imports) — option (c) in Q1 of claude-notes/plans/2026-09-13-scss-cache-key-path.md; would also subsume bd-79c4do6g's path-spelling fix by making the key content-addressed.

c-e7ilf1c7.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-e7ilf1c7.text: Investigated on branch braid/bd-m3hga05o-scss-cache-import-closure (room-2 main checkout). Plan skeleton: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-14-scss-cache-import-closure.md. Verdict: ready to design. Repro confirmed at HEAD (edit _colors.scss -> emitted CSS unchanged, cache unchanged; editing theme.scss itself does invalidate). Key finding: grass (RuntimeFs::read) and dart-sass (result.loadedUrls) already know the import closure — recommend recording it at compile time + validating a manifest on lookup, rather than re-implementing import resolution in cache_key. Design questions in the plan.

title: Login screen carries a 'use test data, not real data' disclaimer
description:
quarto-hub.com's landing / sign-in screen (hub-client/src/components/auth/LoginScreen.tsx) should carry a formatted disclaimer: a 'Disclaimer' heading, then two bold lead sentences ('Use test data, not real data.' and 'Anything you enter is not protected, and we won't return it.') each followed by a body paragraph about the live demo, Posit/third-party retention, and no guarantee of confidentiality or return of data. The component today renders flat strings into

, so it cannot express a heading or bold leads. The About tab's changelog/more-info setup (markdown ?raw -> WASM renderContentToHtml -> themed srcDoc iframe) does NOT transfer: the WASM is initialized by Editor.tsx / PreviewRouter.tsx, i.e. only after sign-in, and LoginScreen is what the cold visitor sees before any of that loads. An iframe inside the card also has no natural height and needs the hand-duplicated theme stylesheet (changelogDoc.ts, GH #624). hub-client has no markdown-to-DOM library and dangerouslySetInnerHTML is confined to two render-internal files. Plan: express the structure in strings.ts (landing.disclaimer = { heading, useTestData: {lead, body}, notProtected: {lead, body} }) and render plain JSX (

lead body

...), the same pattern the tagline already uses. Place it above the sign-in button after the invite-only footnote (the component's own 'everything that qualifies the offer sits above the button' rule; tests pin 'nothing below the button'), always visible, at --text-xs with a --text-sm h2, tokens only. Keep it in the auth-error and session-expired states. TDD: LoginScreen.test.tsx + landing-card e2e first. Out of scope: the same notice on InviteLanding cards; reconciling resources/more-info.md's 'DO NOT USE FOR PRIVATE DATA YET' section. title: Q-5-8 pre-render failure diagnostic points at wrong _quarto.yml span for extension-contributed scripts
description: When a pre-render script contributed by an extension via contributes.metadata.project.pre-render fails, the Q-5-8 ariadne diagnostic renders a bogus span in _quarto.yml. Root cause: script_error() in crates/quarto-core/src/project/render_scripts.rs binds the SourceInfo's resolved FileId (a quarto_yaml filename-hash id for the extension's _extension.yml) to ctx.config_path (_quarto.yml), so the extension file's byte offsets are rendered against _quarto.yml content. Observed live in q2-connect-docs (quarto-openapi extension). Same latent pattern exists in other config-anchored diagnostics that assume _quarto.yml.

title: Default project render regression and project-level diagnostics
description: Post-websites-merge: presence of `_quarto.yml` with `project: { type: default }` causes `q2 render` to silently produce zero output, and `q2 render index.qmd` to fail with a misleading 'excluded from render list' error. Root cause: `default_output_dir` returns the project root for default projects, so the discovery walker's output_dir-exclusion check rejects every file. Three goals: (1) fix the discovery regression so default projects walk the tree like websites do; (2) add a clear project-level diagnostic when the render set is empty so we no longer silently no-op; (3) add a project-level diagnostic surface that both the CLI and hub-client can render, since today only file-level diagnostics flow to hub-client. title: Q2 doesn't accept the contributes.format alias (singular) that every real Quarto extension uses
description:
Confirmed 2026-09-18 during the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic's user-facing/backward-compat review.

Q1 accepts both spellings for an extension's format contributions (src/extension/extension.ts):
  const formats = contributes?.formats as Metadata || contributes?.format as Metadata || {};

Q2 reads only the plural (crates/quarto-core/src/extension/read.rs:154-157):
  contributes.get("formats")

Every real journal/template extension checked in Q1's own test corpus uses the SINGULAR key:
tests/docs/extensions/basic/_extensions/quarto-journals/{jss,springer}/_extension.yml, and the
format/academic/* ACS/ACM/Elsevier extensions - all `contributes: format: {...}`. Under current
Q2, every one of these contributes nothing at all: no filters, no shortcodes, no format options,
and no error or warning.

Pre-existing gap, affects HTML today (not introduced by the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic), but
becomes more consequential once docx is a supported target, since a docx-based custom-format
extension would silently render as a bare, unconfigured docx.

**Not epic scope**: small, general Q2 extension-loading fix (accept `contributes.format` as an
alias of `contributes.formats`), unrelated to any Pandoc-specific plan.

See claude-notes/designs/pandoc-hybrid-architecture.md for the epic context that surfaced this.

title: add_html_dependency: 'name' on a script/stylesheet entry is silently ignored (Q1 uses it as the output filename)
description:
quarto.doc.add_html_dependency accepts each scripts/stylesheets entry either as a bare string or as a table. Quarto 1 treats the table form as { name, path }, where 'name' is the filename the file is COPIED AS (init.lua:511-521 fills name from pandoc.path.filename(v.path) when absent; pandoc-dependencies-html.ts:374 does join(targetDir, file.name)). So Q1 supports copying src/zoom.js out as zoom.min.js by passing { name = 'zoom.min.js', path = 'src/zoom.js' }.

q2 drops the sub-field: normalize_dep_file (crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_doc.rs) reads only 'path' and returns a PathBuf, so read_dep_files yields Vec<PathBuf> and the sub-field never reaches Rust. store_html_dependencies (crates/quarto-core/src/dependency.rs) then derives the filename from path.file_name(). Net effect: the table form works, but 'name' is accepted and silently ignored — the output file always takes the base name of 'path'.

Silent is the problem. A Q1 filter that relies on renaming produces a differently-named asset in q2 with no diagnostic, and the emitted <script src> follows the q2 name, so the page still works and the divergence is invisible until someone compares outputs.

Impact is low: renaming on copy is rare, and the common bare-string form is unaffected. Options are (a) honor 'name' for Q1 parity — needs a struct richer than PathBuf threaded from normalize_dep_file through HtmlDependency into dependency.rs; or (b) keep ignoring it but warn, which is cheap and removes the silence.

Found while documenting add_html_dependency for bd-add-html-dependency-version-5tnub5ds (docs/guides/authoring/lua-filters.qmd); the doc text there deliberately describes only the { path = ... } form so it does not promise renaming.

title: Preview→editor scroll sync uses crude ratio matching; should use data-loc like the click path
description:
Scrolling the preview drags the Monaco editor along via SCROLL-RATIO MATCHING (`syncPreviewToEditor` in `hub-client/src/hooks/useScrollSync.ts`): it maps the preview's scroll percentage onto the editor's scroll percentage, with a 50ms debounce and a 300ms smooth scroll. Pre-existing on both preview paths (wired at `ReactPreview.tsx:874` -> `ReactRenderer.tsx:336` -> `Q2PreviewIframe.tsx:228`, and for the HTML preview via `Preview.tsx`).

Problem: the ratio tracks pixel position, not content, so on a document with uneven block heights (code blocks, display math, tables, tall divs) the editor drifts away from whatever is actually on screen in the preview. Measured while working on the click-to-editor-scroll plan: a block at source line 73 of 78 sits at preview scroll ratio 0.17, and an editor placed at ratio 0.17 lands near line 13. Gordon noticed it as 'the editor scrolling in tandem with the preview, with a lag, without clicking anything' (2026-08-21).

Proposed fix, now cheap because the primitive exists: on preview scroll, resolve the topmost visible `[data-loc]` block in the preview and reveal ITS line, the same way the new click path does — `lineForClickTarget` / `revealEditorLine` in `ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/iframe/scrollSyncDom.ts` and `useScrollSync.ts`. `findElementForLine` already does the line->element direction.

Constraints a fix must respect:
- `syncPreviewToEditor` is SHARED with the HTML preview, which the click-to-editor-scroll plan deliberately left untouched (decision D3, because it was the path reported as working). Changing it affects both previews — decide deliberately whether to change one or both.
- U4 in `hub-client/src/hooks/useScrollSync.test.ts` is the regression cover for the current ratio behaviour (asserts `setScrollTop(300, 1)` for ratio 0.5 over a 1000/400 editor, plus the focus gate). Any replacement needs to update or supersede U4 deliberately, not incidentally.
- `revealEditorLine` brackets itself with `isSyncingRef` for 300ms so a post-click reflow can't let ratio sync overwrite a loc-based reveal (see `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-21-preview-click-to-editor-scroll.md`, 'the reveal-then-overwrite race'). A loc-based scroll path should reuse that idiom rather than inventing a second one.

Found while executing claude-notes/plans/2026-08-21-preview-click-to-editor-scroll.md. Out of scope for that plan, which only added U4 as regression cover for the existing ratio path.
close_reason:
Not a defect to fix: ratio scrolling is governed by the existing scroll-sync UI toggle, so a user who does not want the editor dragged along by preview scrolling simply turns it off — and click-to-align still works with the toggle off, because revealEditorLine has no enabledRef gate (unlike syncPreviewToEditor, flushPendingScroll and scrollToLineDeferred, which all check it). Gordon's call, 2026-08-22.

Preserving the finding this strand turned up, since it outlives the strand: ratio matching for the preview->editor leg was NOT a deliberate design choice. The 2025-12-29 matched-scrolling plan (claude-notes/plans/2025-12-29-matched-scrolling-hub-client.md, issue k-suww) specified that leg as 'find topmost visible element with data-loc / parse it to get a line / calculate editor scroll position to show that line', its architecture diagram says 'scroll position -> element -> line', and steps 3-5 were never implemented. The originating commit 1716275d8 (Carlos Scheidegger, 2025-12-30) shipped findElementForLine loc-based for the OTHER leg exactly as designed while substituting 'scrollRatio = previewScrollY / previewMaxScroll' for this one; git log -S'topmost' across hub-client and ts-packages finds no scroll-sync implementation of it at any point in history. That plan is nonetheless marked Status: Completed. Recorded here rather than acted on.

Superseded in practice by claude-notes/plans/2026-08-22-click-align-editor-y.md, which delivers precise loc-based preview->editor positioning on the CLICK gesture instead of the scroll gesture.

c-vdmv73di.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-vdmv73di.text:
ORIGIN TRACED (2026-08-22). This is not a workaround for click-to-editor-scroll — it is an UNIMPLEMENTED HALF of the original matched-scrolling design, shipped as an approximation and then marked complete.

Introduced by 1716275d8 'source location in HTML preview, scroll matching' (Carlos Scheidegger, 2025-12-30), the commit that created useScrollSync.ts. Its design doc is claude-notes/plans/2025-12-29-matched-scrolling-hub-client.md (issue k-suww), **Status: Completed**.

That doc's architecture diagram says the preview->editor leg is 'scroll position -> element -> line', and its algorithm section specifies it explicitly:

    Preview -> Editor:
    1. Listen to iframe scroll event
    2. Debounce 50ms
    3. Find topmost visible element with data-loc attribute
    4. Parse data-loc to get line number
    5. Calculate editor scroll position to show that line
    6. editor.setScrollTop() without moving cursor

Steps 3-5 were never implemented. Verified: the originating commit's useScrollSync.ts already computed 'scrollRatio = previewScrollY / previewMaxScroll' (line 166) for this leg, while implementing findElementForLine (line 47) loc-based for the OTHER leg exactly as designed. A git log -S'topmost' across hub-client and ts-packages finds no scroll-sync implementation of it at any point in history.

So the editor->preview leg shipped loc-based per the design; the preview->editor leg silently substituted ratio matching; and the plan was marked Completed.

This also explains a confusion recorded in claude-notes/plans/2026-08-21-preview-click-to-editor-scroll.md: that plan initially assumed the HTML preview's preview->editor precision came from the click/ratio path, then measured that ratio 'contributes nothing precise' and found the real mechanism was useSelectionSync (loc-based, off selectionchange). The ratio substitution is the root of that whole misreading.

Scope is now much smaller than when this strand was filed: every primitive exists.
- parseDataLoc — exists (the design doc even contains the same function verbatim)
- element -> line — lineForClickTarget in ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/iframe/scrollSyncDom.ts (with the fileId / active-region / section guards already worked out)
- reveal a line without moving the cursor — revealEditorLine in hub-client/src/hooks/useScrollSync.ts (already brackets isSyncingRef so it cannot be overwritten)
The only missing piece is 'find the topmost visible [data-loc]' plus wiring it to the existing scroll handler in place of the ratio computation.

Consider also correcting the Status of the 2025-12-29 plan, since it is marked Completed while step 3-5 of its own algorithm was not delivered.

title: Mermaid %%| cell options are not processed (fig-cap/fig-alt lost in the GFM fence form)
description:
DIRECTION FIRST (Carlos, 2026-08-10): we are standardizing on the GFM diagram spelling — ```mermaid, the way GitHub-flavored Markdown and other processors do it — rather than Q1's ```{mermaid} executable-cell form. The React preview layer already implements it. The sequencing for this strand is: get diagrams working in `q2 render` for HTML formats first, then add the processing that pulls the cell options into the diagram initializer code. Phase one turns out to be largely done already (see below), so the live work here is the second half.

STATE OF PLAY, verified against q2 0.16.0 with a three-section probe:

  A. ```mermaid, no options        -> <pre class="mermaid"> plus the once-per-document
                                      pinned-CDN module script. Diagram draws. WORKS.
  B. ```mermaid, with %%| options  -> diagram draws, but the %%| lines are left verbatim
                                      in the <pre class="mermaid"> body. No <figcaption>,
                                      no accessible description. THIS IS THE GAP.
  C. ```{mermaid} (Q1 form)        -> <pre class="{mermaid} code-with-copy">, braces carried
                                      into the CSS class, rendered as a plain code listing.
                                      Deliberate, per the decision recorded in the source.

So `q2 render` already has HTML diagram support: crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/mermaid.rs (bd-5m4ga0s1, plan claude-notes/plans/2026-07-20-mermaid-regular-rendering.md). It runs at TransformPhase::Finalization ahead of CodeBlockRenderTransform so diagram blocks never grow copy-button chrome, rewrites the CodeBlock to RawBlock("html", ...), and appends the mermaid module to rendered.includes.after-body. It is excluded from the q2-preview pipeline (Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED) because there the raw CodeBlock must survive to the React component at ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/MermaidCodeBlock.tsx, which pins the same mermaid version.

WHAT Q1 DOES, for the part that is missing. Q1 treats %%| lines as cell options: it strips them from the diagram source and applies them, so fig-cap becomes a <figcaption> under the diagram and fig-alt becomes the accessible name. q2 currently passes them straight through. Because %% opens a mermaid comment the diagram still draws, so the failure is quiet: no warning, and the only visible symptom is the option text sitting in the diagram source plus missing captions and alt text.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION (phase two). In transforms/mermaid.rs, before emitting the RawBlock: split leading %%| lines off the source, parse them as the YAML cell-option block they are, and (a) keep them out of the emitted diagram text, (b) route the recognized options into the output — fig-cap wrapping the <pre> in a figure with a caption, fig-alt onto the accessible name. Worth settling while there: which option subset is honored beyond fig-cap/fig-alt (label/fig-align?), whether unrecognized options warn or are dropped silently, and whether the same parsing should feed the React component so `q2 preview` and `q2 render` agree. Note that only *leading* %%| lines are cell options; a %%| further down is an ordinary mermaid comment.

MIGRATION CONSEQUENCE, possibly a separate strand. Every Q1 document in the wild spells this ```{mermaid}. Given the GFM direction, those sources need rewriting rather than q2 growing brace support — a natural qmd-syntax-helper rule (crates/qmd-syntax-helper/, Rule trait in src/rule.rs, conversions in src/conversions/), mechanically rewriting ```{mermaid} to ```mermaid and leaving the body alone. Whether that is tracked here or on its own strand is undecided.

REAL-WORLD HIT (Posit Connect docs). 33 diagrams across 14 pages, all in the Q1 brace form, so today they all render as source text: the 8 admin/reference-architectures/* pages (aws and azure, each single-server / single-server-robust / load-balanced / k8s), user/orientation (4 sequence diagrams and their 4 captions), admin/appendix/off-host/arch-overview (4), admin/public-access, admin/appendix/airgapped. On the reference-architecture pages the diagram is the entire content of the page. Rewriting those files to the GFM spelling gets all 33 drawing immediately; the captions and the fig-alt accessible descriptions — which is what the accessibility of those architecture pages rests on — stay lost until the cell-option work lands.

REPRO. /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/mermaid-cell-options-ignored/ — run 'q2 render repro.qmd' there. repro.qmd is the three-section probe above (A works, B drops the options, C is unrecognized) so all three outcomes are visible in one render; README.md has the table, the source-level explanation, and the docs impact. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path.

Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-mermaid-cell-options-r52f8p3v. Observed with q2 0.16.0; re-verified against origin/main @ b2b6100c (v0.16.0 plus docs commits), where nothing has touched mermaid since v0.15.0.
close_reason: Implemented and merged in PR #499 (main @ a429becc). Mermaid %%| cell options are processed: fig-cap/fig-scap/fig-alt and label all route into the output, with source-mapped Q-2-47/Q-2-48 diagnostics. Follow-ups tracked separately: bd-vg8p5yoj (qmd-syntax-helper migration rule), bd-e3m3rkik (preview copy-button chrome).

c-3g4gaqhi.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-3g4gaqhi.text:
Implemented on branch feature/bd-mermaid-cell-options-9wo3crl0 (9 commits, f44b3a81..cadd7ba3). Not pushed — awaiting review. Plan + verification record: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-10-mermaid-cell-options.md

All six design questions settled with Carlos and recorded in the plan. What landed:

- cell_options::comment_syntax_for learns mermaid's `%%` (Q1 keeps it on the language handler and in constants.lua, not in kLangCommentChars, which is why the port missed it).
- crossref/codeblock_shorthand migrated off its private `#|`-only, split_once(':') matcher onto the shared cell_options facility: the marker now follows the cell language, and options are parsed as real YAML.
- Unlabelled fig-cap emits Block::Figure — the AST-level answer Q1 could not reach, since its cell handling was textual.
- fig-alt is injected as mermaid's native accDescr:, which survives mermaid.js swapping the <pre> for an inline <svg>.
- Q-2-42 / Q-2-43 diagnostics, source-mapped to the offending key, scoped to diagram cells so engine options keep passing through silently.
- Docs section + worked example examples/diagrams/03-mermaid-captions.

Decision 5 is a deliberate behavior change: `#|` in a ```mermaid fence is no longer a cell-option marker. Q-2-43 explains it at the exact source line rather than letting mermaid fail on the leftovers.

`cargo xtask verify` (full, including the hub/WASM leg) passes. No snapshot files changed anywhere in the workspace.

Accessibility verified against real mermaid 11.12.0 under jsdom (both browser routes were unavailable this session): the injected line becomes <desc> inside the SVG with aria-describedby pointing at it; a negative control confirms mermaid rejects accDescr placed before the diagram-type line. Not verified: an actual screen reader, and the q2 preview UI in a live browser.

Fixes the three discovered-from strands: bd-5jcmmj1f (quoted captions), bd-sdpp9rw4 (markdown captions), bd-il6pxq4f (fig-alt dropped). Leaving all four open until the PR merges.

Also filed: bd-vg8p5yoj (qmd-syntax-helper rule for the ```{mermaid} -> ```mermaid migration — the other half of the Connect-docs story) and bd-e3m3rkik (pre-existing: preview gives mermaid blocks copy-button chrome that render suppresses).

c-mtfnju2p.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-mtfnju2p.text:
Investigated 2026-08-10; plan skeleton at claude-notes/plans/2026-08-10-mermaid-cell-options.md (commit f44b3a81 on main), probes under claude-notes/plans/mermaid-cell-options-investigation/.

Key finding: the figure/caption/crossref path already works for a ```mermaid fence — it just keys off the `#|` marker. A mermaid block with `#| label: fig-x` + `#| fig-cap:` renders a full quarto-float figure (figcaption, Figure N numbering, aria-describedby) at HEAD today; only the `%%|` spelling is unrecognized. cell_options::comment_syntax_for has no mermaid entry (Q1 keeps mermaid's `%%` on the handler + constants.lua, not in kLangCommentChars, which is why the port missed it).

Architectural constraint: the work must happen in PreEngineSugaringStage (via crossref/codeblock_shorthand.rs), not in transforms/mermaid.rs — that transform is on Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED (so preview would diverge) and runs after crossref-render (so labels could never be numbered). Doing it pre-engine gives preview/render parity for free.

Three pre-existing defects in the shared `#|` shorthand also surfaced, reproduced on a plain python cell so they are general, not mermaid-specific: quoted YAML values keep their quotes in the figcaption; markdown in captions is not parsed; fig-alt and fig-scap are consumed and silently dropped. fig-alt being dropped is on this strand's critical path.

Six design questions are open in the plan (unlabelled fig-cap, fig-alt markup, scope of the three defects, honoured option keys + unknown-key policy, one marker or two, where the work lands).

title: Mermaid runtime is imported from jsDelivr at page load, not bundled into the site
description:
WHAT HAPPENS. Every HTML page containing a diagram gets a module script that imports the mermaid runtime from a third-party CDN, and nothing is written into the rendered site:

    <script type="module">
      import mermaid from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11.12.0/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs';
      ...
    </script>

    $ find _site -iname '*mermaid*'
    (nothing)
    $ ls _site/site_libs
    bootstrap  quarto

Quarto 1 bundles it instead -- site_libs/quarto-diagram/mermaid.min.js, mermaid-init.js and mermaid.css, referenced relatively -- so a Q1 site is self-contained. Under q2 it is not. Load a rendered page with the network blocked (DevTools > Network > Offline, or a block rule for cdn.jsdelivr.net) and the pre class="mermaid" simply stays as visible diagram *source text*: no SVG, and nothing surfaced to the reader explaining why.

Three consequences worth separating, because only the first is about offline:

- Air-gapped and closed-network hosting. The rendered site cannot be archived or served where outbound HTTPS is unavailable.
- A third-party runtime dependency in published documentation. Pages served under a vendor's domain execute code fetched from a CDN at load time -- a review question in most organizations -- and reader IP addresses reach the CDN.
- Availability. A CDN outage or a corporate block silently degrades every diagram page.

ROOT-CAUSE AREA. crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/mermaid.rs: MERMAID_VERSION is pinned to "11.12.0" and the emitted module script hard-codes the jsdelivr URL (the format string around line 170; a unit test around line 287 asserts that exact URL). The script is appended once per document to rendered.includes.after-body via the MERMAID_JS_SENTINEL. Unchanged on origin/main at v0.17.0.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION. The machinery already exists: crates/quarto-core/src/dependency.rs::store_html_dependencies writes assets to _site/site_libs/libs/{name}/{filename} and is what quarto.doc.add_html_dependency goes through. The mermaid transform currently bypasses it. Registering the runtime as an ordinary HTML dependency and emitting a relative import instead of the CDN URL would put it on the same footing as Bootstrap and the quarto JS.

The genuinely open question is where the bytes come from, and it deserves a decision rather than a default: vendor the mermaid ESM build into the repo the way Q1 vendors mermaid.min.js (simple, offline-correct, but adds a multi-megabyte binary asset to the tree and a manual bump whenever MERMAID_VERSION moves), or fetch it at build time into the resources dir. Note that crates/quarto-core/resources/ currently holds only styles.css, so there is no vendored-JS precedent in that crate to follow -- the hub-client's Monaco fix went through npm/vite, a different pipeline that does not apply to `q2 render`. If bundling by default is judged too heavy, an opt-in project/format key would at least give closed-network projects a supported answer.

PRIOR ART IN THIS REPO. bd-yvz2xqrm (closed) was the same class of problem for the hub client: Monaco loaded from jsDelivr at runtime and the editor hung when the CDN was slow, blocked, or offline; fixed by bundling in PR #411. A comment on that work says explicitly, "Mermaid's lazy jsDelivr import noted as out of scope" -- so this dependency was seen at the time and deferred, not judged acceptable. This strand is that follow-up.

REAL-WORLD HIT (Posit Connect docs). 14 pages, 33 diagrams. The sharpest case is admin/appendix/airgapped/index.qmd -- the guide to running Posit Connect *without internet access* -- which itself contains two mermaid diagrams that now need internet access to render. Next worst are the 8 admin/reference-architectures/* pages, where the diagram is essentially the entire content of the page; each renders as a block of diagram source when the CDN is unreachable.

REPRO. /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/mermaid-runtime-not-bundled/ -- run 'q2 render' there. One page with one diagram; the README shows the emitted CDN URL, the empty `find _site -iname '*mermaid*'`, the contrasting contents of site_libs, and how to verify the offline failure in DevTools. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path.

Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-u5v95mpd. Observed with q2 0.16.0; the emitting code is unchanged on origin/main at v0.17.0.
close_reason:
Implemented and merged in PR #504 (merge commit 808215fc). The runtime is vendored at resources/mermaid/mermaid.min.js (upstream npm 11.12.0, SHA-256 07e37dfa...), embedded via include_str!, registered as an ArtifactScope::Project artifact at mermaid/mermaid.min.js, and referenced from each page with a resolver-computed relative URL. Rendered sites are self-contained; no jsDelivr reference remains in q2 render output.

Key correction to the original analysis: dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs (the file we imported) is a 26 KB stub over a 146-file / 13 MB chunk tree with per-diagram-type lazy imports, so vendoring "the file we already import" would not have worked. The self-contained UMD dist/mermaid.min.js is byte-identical to Quarto 1's vendored copy.

Verified end-to-end: 3-page website rendered with the real binary and loaded in Chrome; flowchart, gantt and class diagrams all drew as real SVG (three distinct chunks under the ESM build) with zero external network requests; nested pages resolve ../site_libs/ and share one copy.

Scope deliberately left open in follow-ups: bd-1vwtdwtq (q2 preview / hub-client still CDN-dependent), bd-43gpsd7c (compressed compile-time embedding, prompted by the 2.62 MiB binary cost and the measured +7.3% WASM growth), and mermaid theming, which is tracked by the pre-existing bd-sehm2rha / bd-nj25kgbu.

c-4vbvgrl9.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-4vbvgrl9.text:
Design settled 2026-08-11 (commit e9422bea). Decisions:

1. 2.62 MiB unconditionally in the q2 binary: accepted for now. Compressed compile-time embedding (include_compressed_str!-style) filed as bd-43gpsd7c.
2. Bundle by default -- no opt-in key.
3. This strand covers the 'q2 render' path only. Preview/hub-client filed as bd-1vwtdwtq, with the direction NOT to bundle mermaid into the client (2.62 MiB, only some docs use it) but to serve the same vendored bytes as an HTML dependency to preview projects that contain diagrams.
4. Mermaid CSS/theming parity with Q1 filed as bd-93ensbpn.
5. Version-bump ergonomics follow the reveal.js precedent (vendored dir + README procedure + node_modules drift test), no bespoke xtask step, so all vendored assets stay on one mechanism.

Correction recorded in bd-1vwtdwtq: the direction in (3) was framed as 'like we do for revealjs', but revealjs does not do this today -- render embeds vendored resources/revealjs/ via include_str!, while preview gets its JS from the bundled npm packages (@revealjs/react + reveal.js) and only its CSS from the vendored files. So it is a new mechanism to design, not a pattern to copy.

This strand is now ready to implement.

c-66a43ul3.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-66a43ul3.text:
Investigated on main @ 001cb6a5; plan skeleton at claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-mermaid-runtime-not-bundled.md (commit 6d9ecc32). Verdict: ready to design.

Two premises in this description are wrong in ways that change the plan:

1. There IS a vendored-JS precedent -- repo-root resources/revealjs/ (README + include_str! + register_reveal_assets() storing Project-scoped artifacts to site_libs/ + a node_modules drift test). The description checked only the crate-local crates/quarto-core/resources/.

2. dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs -- the file we import today -- is a 26 KB stub, not the runtime: 10 static chunk imports plus ~25 dynamic per-diagram-type ones over a 13 MB / 146-file tree. So vendoring 'the file we already import' would not fix anything, and today's CDN path already makes an extra round trip per diagram type (a flowchart-only offline test would pass while a gantt page fails).

The stated open question ('where do the bytes come from') resolves cleanly: upstream npm mermaid@11.12.0 dist/mermaid.min.js is self-contained (2,748,992 B, zero dynamic imports, exports globalThis.mermaid) and is SHA-256 identical (07e37dfa...) to the copy Quarto 1 vendors. So 'vendor the upstream UMD' and 'do what Q1 does' are the same decision -- no esbuild step, no build-time fetch.

Also confirmed AstTransformsStage bridges RenderContext.artifacts both directions (ast_transforms.rs:182 and :227), so the transform can register the asset with no new plumbing. That was the plan's only feasibility risk.

Open questions for the user are in the plan: (1) is 2.62 MiB unconditionally in the q2 binary acceptable; (2) bundle by default vs opt-in key; (3) does scope include the TS preview path (MermaidCodeBlock.tsx has its own jsDelivr import + a version-parity test); (4) also port Q1's mermaid CSS/theming; (5) version-bump ergonomics (xtask sync vs README procedure).

c-t9iczsk1.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-t9iczsk1.text:
Implemented on branch braid/bd-mermaid-runtime-not-bundled-vxejw159 (commits 095cb39c, eeb1eb7d). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-mermaid-runtime-not-bundled.md. Not yet pushed.

WHAT LANDED. The runtime is vendored at resources/mermaid/mermaid.min.js (upstream npm 11.12.0, 2,748,992 B, SHA-256 07e37dfa...), embedded via include_str!, registered as an ArtifactScope::Project artifact at mermaid/mermaid.min.js, and referenced from each page with a resolver-computed relative URL. Rendered sites are now self-contained.

TWO DESIGN POINTS WORTH KNOWING.

1. The artifact is keyed `mermaid:runtime`, NOT `js:`. The first cut used js:mermaid:... following the dependency.rs/reveal convention, and the integration tests immediately caught two <script> tags per page: ApplyTemplateStage emits a head <script> for every js: artifact (apply_template.rs:167), so the 2.6 MiB bundle loaded twice. The fix is not "let the template emit it" either, because the reveal scaffold collects only js:revealjs:* (apply_template.rs:305) -- a js:-keyed runtime would emit NO tag in a deck, silently breaking every diagram in a presentation. So the transform owns its own emission into the after-body slot, which both the Bootstrap template and the reveal scaffold wire up. Pinned by runtime_is_not_keyed_as_a_template_script (unit) and revealjs_deck_bundles_the_runtime (integration).

2. Staleness guarding deviates from reveal.js on one point, deliberately. Reveal compares embedded bytes against node_modules because it has two live sources that must agree; mermaid has one, and adding mermaid as a devDependency purely to anchor a comparison would pull 66 MB / 793 files into every npm install. Instead: two always-on guards (the bundle's embedded version:"..." must equal MERMAID_VERSION; the bundle must contain no `import(` and no `chunks/`), plus the reveal-style npm byte-compare that skips while mermaid is absent from node_modules, so it starts working automatically if bd-1vwtdwtq adds it. Mechanisms 1-4 of the precedent (vendored dir, README, include_str!, Project-scoped registration) are followed exactly.

The self-containment guard is the one that matters most: dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs is a 26 KB stub that lazily imports a chunk PER DIAGRAM TYPE, so vendoring the wrong dist file would break offline rendering in a way a flowchart-only test would miss.

Details and rationale for not cfg-gating it are in the plan's "Measured cost" section, and passed to bd-1vwtdwtq (comment c-00tq71p6), where it makes that strand's chosen design cheaper.

title: Sidebar renders below page content — body class & grid placement wrong
description:
Q2 website rendering places the sidebar at the bottom of the page (below `<main>` and below the prev/next strip) instead of in a left column.

Root cause (verified against examples/websites/01-minimal rendered with q2 vs q1):
1. Body class is hardcoded `fullcontent` in crates/quarto-core/src/template.rs:162. The website pipeline never sets the `body-classes` template variable, so we never get `nav-sidebar` or `floating`/`docked`.
2. resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss keys the grid layout off body classes: `body.floating .page-columns { @include page-columns-float-wide(); }` produces a 150px sidebar column on the left, while `body.fullcontent:not(.floating):not(.docked)` produces no sidebar column.
3. Without that column, the sidebar wrapper (`#quarto-sidebar-container` placed at `grid-column: body-content-start / body-content-end`, `grid-row: auto`) gets auto-placed in an implicit row after `<main>`, so it appears below the page content.
4. Secondary structural difference: Q1 places `<nav id=quarto-sidebar>` directly as a grid child; Q2 wraps it in `#quarto-sidebar-container`. The SCSS in resources/scss expects the Q1 layout.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-29-website-sidebar-layout.md

Out of scope: search bar (Q1 default that we are not adding yet).

title: Frontmatter reader splits on every `---`, so a `---` inside a YAML value truncates the metadata (GH #671)
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/671

extract_between_delimiters in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs does input.split("---") and keeps parts[1], so any `---` inside a value ends the YAML there. The tree-sitter scanner is correct (the metadata node spans the whole block; it only recognises `---` at column 0 followed by optional whitespace and a newline). Pandoc reads all of these cases fine.

Symptoms: plain scalar `Hello --- world` silently drops every later key; quoted scalar `"a --- b"` fails with Q-0-99 (unterminated quote). The qmd writer emits every em dash as `---` since PR #290, so any document with an em dash in a markdown-parsed frontmatter string fails to round-trip.

Fix is reader-side: extract by delimiter *lines* (first line + first subsequent column-0 `---` line), and compute the YAML source offset directly instead of block.text.find(content). No writer change needed: the writer's YAML is valid in every probed shape (yaml_rust2 already quotes scalars that begin with ---).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-10-frontmatter-delimiter-split-gh671.md

title: Design: how should engines/extensions declare additional pipeline stages?
description:
build_html_pipeline_stages() in crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs is a hardcoded ~19-stage list. Stages can be gated by config (e.g. native-only), but no engine, extension, or plugin can register a new stage. **More relevant after PR #238 (sequential multi-engine execution).** With engines as first-class pipeline citizens, the natural mechanism for 'format-agnostic engine output + format-specific emission' is to let an engine declare a per-format AST pass on its output. For mermaid: 'when emitting HTML, run this transform on my output blocks.' For graphviz/plantuml/dot later: same shape. A proper extension API would let engines/extensions declare: - a stage name + input/output kinds - a position (after-X / before-Y, or by precedence) - a per-format applicability predicate - a per-engine attribution back-reference (so trace events name the engine that contributed the stage) **Known beneficiary: the mermaid engine (bd-gwfdo).** Mermaid ships first under B1 (the engine emits RawBlock(HTML, '
...
') directly — format-locked but acceptable while Q2 is HTML-only). A source-code comment in crates/quarto-core/src/engine/mermaid/ flags the TODO. **When bd-mqk49 lands, follow up on the mermaid engine** to refactor: the engine should emit a marker Div (e.g. Div.mermaid wrapping the source code block) and declare an HTML-conditional AST pass that turns the marker into the 
 output. This removes the format coupling and makes the mermaid engine PDF-ready.

Discovered during mermaid engine design — see claude-notes/plans/2026-05-28-mermaidjs-engine-design.md gap G3.

title: Hub-client preview resource resolution via service worker (epic)
description:
Long-term direction: replace the iframe post-processor's resource-rewriting passes (CSS data-URIs, image data-URIs, the disabled <script> inlining block) with a service worker scoped to /.quarto/project-artifacts/ and project-relative paths. The SW intercepts fetch events and serves from the VFS, giving us:

- Single resolution path shared between top-frame and iframe.
- No data-URI churn on every render (iframes routinely carry hundreds of KB of inline base64 stylesheets today).
- Clean answer for the in-project image redirection bug.
- Plausible path for executing real JS bundles in preview iframes (Bootstrap collapse, search, copy-button, etc.) once SW + sandbox + COEP/COOP are set up correctly.

NOT in scope: cross-doc link click → editor navigation (bd-lnd3). That's a DOM-event concern, not a fetch concern; about:srcdoc iframes drop link clicks silently regardless of network resolution. The click-interception path stays in iframePostProcessor.ts even after the SW arc lands.

Children candidates (file as separate issues when this epic gets traction):
- SW bootstrap + scope registration in hub-client.
- VFS → fetch handler.
- Migration of CSS resolution (remove data-URI rewrite from iframePostProcessor).
- Migration of image resolution (remove data-URI rewrite + fixes the in-project image redirect bug).
- JS bundle execution in preview iframes (subsumes bd-e7b7 native+incremental constraints).
- Sandbox / COEP / COOP setup as required.

Parent epic: bd-0tr6 (websites, since the immediate motivation is the website rendering pipeline, but the SW infrastructure is broadly useful).

title: Star-marker continuation lines share the over-indent defect fixed for dash/digit (bd-j7be7kuc)
description: The gate-1/gate-2 '*' peeks in scanner.c (predating 92737cdd) have no indentation guard, so 'hello\n     * item' (star marker at indent 5) is still a hard parse error: the peek declares a block opener, no soft break is emitted, and the line then fails to form a block (indented-code territory). CommonMark: the line is lazy paragraph continuation -> Str '*', Space, Str 'item'. Fix shape is identical to bd-j7be7kuc Part B: guard the gate-1 star peek with s->indentation <= claimable_list_indentation(s) + 3 and the gate-2 star peek with residual <= 3, skipping the peek on over-indent. Not fixed alongside bd-j7be7kuc to keep that P0 regression fix scoped to the branches 92737cdd added (one bug at a time). Note '*' has extra wrinkles the dash fix did not face: a star run can also be emphasis, and unclosed emphasis is a deliberate qmd error (Q-2-27 family), so sweep expectations need care to separate marker cells from emphasis cells. See claude-notes/instructions/scanner-indentation-contexts.md for the required indent x context sweep.

title: Pin pampa fixtures and snapshots to LF via .gitattributes
description: Pin pampa test fixtures and snapshot files to LF via .gitattributes so the line-ending tests are deterministic regardless of core.autocrlf, mirroring the doctemplate precedent in crates/quarto-doctemplate/.gitattributes. There is currently no .gitattributes under crates/pampa, so 704 tracked files (390 qmd, 210 snap, plus rs/md/json) flip to CRLF on a Windows checkout, producing the 7 failing pampa snapshot, roundtrip and corpus tests. Add text eol=lf for the fixture and snapshot globs, then run git add --renormalize and re-checkout (renormalize stages the index conversion but leaves the working tree CRLF until a re-checkout). Replaces bd-238o fix 2 (normalize on test read), which is wrong under the preserve policy. INVARIANT: pinning .snap files to LF is safe only while no snapshot ever captures CRLF-preserving output; CRLF round-trip assertions must live in-source (inline expected strings), never in a .snap, or this pin will silently flatten them. See claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-handling-analysis.md.

title: Port cursor->slide sync to the q2-preview iframe for revealjs
description:
Convergence (bd-vwp4y5ku) routed the hub-client live editor's 'format: revealjs' through the shared q2-preview iframe, fixing theme parity. But the q2-preview branch in ReactRenderer does not forward currentSlideIndex/onSlideChange to Q2PreviewIframe, so cursor->slide navigation (driven by useCursorToSlide in Editor.tsx) is disconnected for revealjs. The hand-rolled RevealjsSlideAst supported it via the reveal API.

Also verify the preview does not reset to slide 1 on every keystroke (UPDATE_AST re-render) — if it does, that is a worse regression than losing cursor sync.

Port needs a SET_SLIDE (parent->iframe) + SLIDE_CHANGED (iframe->parent) postMessage channel across 5 files: RevealDeck.tsx (useReveal() -> reveal.slide(n) on currentSlide change + 'slidechanged' listener, mirror the RevealChrome escape-hatch pattern), PreviewRoot.tsx (thread currentSlide/onSlideChange to RevealDeck), q2-preview/entry.tsx (handle SET_SLIDE state + post SLIDE_CHANGED), Q2PreviewIframe.tsx (currentSlideIndex/onSlideChange props + post/handle), ReactRenderer.tsx (forward the two props it already receives). Additive/optional so q2 preview is unaffected.

Retiring RevealjsSlideAst + the reveal branch wiring should land with this (deck is dead in the path but kept until slide-nav is restored so no released state loses the feature).

Browser-verified inbound (SET_SLIDE moves the deck's .present section); both directions unit-tested (RevealNavSync + ReactRenderer forwarding). RevealjsSlideAst retired with it.

title: Hub-client: active-page parse error renders as 'Project render produced no output for the active page'
description:
When a website document has a Pass-1 parse error AND it is the active page in hub-client, the preview overlay shows the literal string 'Project render produced no output for the active page' instead of the actual parse diagnostic.

Repro: examples/websites/08-hub-preview/about.qmd has an unescaped apostrophe (line 11, 'pages\\'') that the strict Q2 markdown parser rejects with [Q-2-10] Closed Quote Without Matching Open Quote. The CLI shows the full ariadne-style snippet via 'warning: profile-pass skipped about.qmd: ...'. Hub-client shows only the generic message.

Root cause (located): crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1374-1428 — render_project_active_page_to_response() checks summary.pass2_failures but never checks summary.pass1_failures. When the active page failed Pass-1, both summary.outputs and summary.pass2_failures are empty, so the L1393 fallback fires.

Fix: in the L1381 'no output' branch, look up summary.pass1_failures for an entry whose input matches the active path; if found, build a RenderResponse with success: false, error from the failure summary, and diagnostics: failure.diagnostics mapped to JsonDiagnostic.
