Cross-reference from bd-add-html-dependency-version-5tnub5ds (plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-14-add-html-dependency-version.md).

That strand is implementing the 'version' field on quarto.doc.add_html_dependency, and the ONLY justification for honoring it is freeze. Recording that here because this is currently the skein's sole freeze-related strand, so a future freeze design session is most likely to find it first.

The requirement freeze inherits: two renders at different times can produce different versions of the same HTML dependency, and both sets of assets must survive in _site so an older frozen page keeps working. To buy that, the artifact key in quarto-core/src/dependency.rs gains the version and the layout becomes libs/{name}/{version}/{file} (unversioned deps keep libs/{name}/{file}).

This decision was made before freeze existed and is freeze's to revisit — it is two format! calls and a key, and q2 makes no _site layout longevity promise.

One divergence worth resolving when freeze is designed: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-27-multi-engine-execution.md:349-353 records that 'Quarto 2's freeze will instead reuse the trace directly — roughly engine: replay as freeze', while the 2026-08-14 discussion on the other strand described reworking the execution-output automerge sidecar into a more portable, likely .ipynb-based format. These may converge (a committed trace file could be that format) but they are not obviously the same plan, and the trace-replay framing is over a year older.

title: Nested-parse source mapping drifts when the inner text was unescaped (attribute values, YAML scalars)
description:
SourceInfo::substring composes a purely AFFINE map -- resolve_byte_range does parent_start + start_offset (quarto-source-map-0.1.0/src/source_info.rs:388-403), with no validation and no clamping -- and the nested reader supplies byte offsets into the inner string (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/location.rs:213-218). That is only correct when the inner string is a byte-identical prefix-aligned slice of the parent span. It is not, in at least two places:

1. Div attribute values. Attr.2 stores the value UNESCAPED and unquoted (extract_quoted_text + unescape_punctuation, crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/text_helpers.rs:28-59, called from treesitter.rs:1207-1212), while AttrSourceInfo.attributes[i].1 spans the RAW quote-inclusive text (the grammar token includes the delimiters: crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js:580-585; range recorded at commonmark_attribute.rs:39-51).

2. YAML scalars. quarto-yaml's compute_scalar_len deliberately spans the quotes while the DECODED scalar is what gets handed to parse_config_string_as_markdown (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs:59-66 and :240-330). Nothing compensates.

Measured on a real render: for title="Say \"hello\" now" the stored value is 15 bytes and the span is 19. For title="Use `renv` today" the code span sits at inner bytes 4..10, maps to 85..91, and is actually at 86..92 -- off by one before any escape is involved, and one more byte per collapsed escape. Fails silently: no panic, no clamp, just wrong rows/columns. Beyond diagnostics, SourceInfo::preimage_in feeds the incremental writer's verbatim-copy decision, so a drifted range can copy the wrong bytes.

The constraint is already documented: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-20-ipynb-surface-syntax-design.md:73-92 states that Substring/Concat compose only affine maps, notes that a Transformed variant existed and was removed as unused, and says the YAML analogue 'currently punts'. Its prescribed workaround is to unescape once at ingestion and register the logical text as its own ephemeral SourceFile. The one exemplary in-tree case is cell options (crates/quarto-core/src/cell_options/mod.rs:33-43), exact precisely because it never unescapes.

Proper fix: carry an offset map through the unescape and emit SourceInfo::concat pieces around each escape, or adopt the ipynb doc's ephemeral-SourceFile approach. Either way this is shared infrastructure needed by the attribute path, the YAML path, and ipynb.

Discovered while designing the callout title= fix (bd-callout-custom-title-dropped-9qi1p7iw), which works around it: it derives the exact parent from lengths alone when no escape was collapsed, and falls back to the whole-value span otherwise (bounded error, cannot leave the attribute). Evidence and worked examples: claude-notes/plans/callout-title-attribute-investigation/escape-drift-probe.md
close_reason: Provenance epic complete: Plans 1-3 all landed on feature/yaml-provenance. Plan 1 shipped quarto-source-map 0.1.2/0.1.3 (piecewise content provenance + ProvenanceBuilder); Plan 2 made q2's YAML and attribute decoders drive it (callout.rs workaround deleted, @quarto/annotated-qmd 0.2.0); Plan 3 audited the remaining surface and fixed the comrak NodeValue::Text drift, the codeblock-shorthand body search, the is_gapless narrowing and the diagnostic-render panic guard, and recorded the rest (cell_options constraint, quarto-xml dead-code precondition, use_cmd/config.rs's byte-equality refusal). All four children closed 2026-08-21. Follow-ups live on separately as discovered-from strands: bd-6392eba3, bd-8hrjqcx0, bd-lm75ion7. Evidence: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-{1,2,3}-*.md and claude-notes/research/2026-08-21-provenance-audit-findings.md.

c-if3b704m.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-if3b704m.text:
PRIOR ART: q2 contains THREE independent hand-rolled defenses against this bug class. That is the strongest available argument for fixing it at the source with shared machinery rather than continuing to work around it per-site.

1. crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/callout.rs:400-444 (attribute_value_source) -- the one this strand was discovered from. Derives the exact parent from lengths alone when no escape was collapsed (span_len == value_len, or == value_len + 2 for quotes), and falls back to the whole-value span otherwise. Bounded error, cannot leave the attribute.

2. crates/quarto/src/commands/use_cmd/config.rs:229 (scalar_value_span) -- newly found. Byte-compares the raw span's text against the decoded value and returns None on mismatch rather than assuming alignment:

       let start = entry.value_span.start_offset();
       let end = entry.value_span.end_offset();
       if self.text.get(start..end)? == parsed.as_str() { Some((start, end)) } else { None }

   Its doc comment names the problem outright: "source text is not literally its value -- the caller then reports that it cannot repoint the declaration, which is honest and leaves the user's file alone." So a third author independently hit this, understood it, and routed around it.

3. crates/quarto-core/src/cell_options/mod.rs:196-228 -- avoids the bug structurally by never decoding: it concatenates raw byte slices and pairs each with a SourceInfo::concat piece of exactly matching length. Cited in this strand already as the exemplary case. Worth noting it is exemplary precisely BECAUSE it uses the concat-piece approach this strand proposes generalizing.

Each of these costs real capability. (1) and (2) degrade to whole-span or to refusing the operation; (3) constrains its input format. All three would collapse to a single call against correct provenance.

--

Q2 IMPACT OF THE PLANNED quarto-yaml 0.2.0 (verified at HEAD, both by a subagent and by direct re-check):

- Production call sites of YamlWithSourceInfo::new_scalar / new_scalar_with_tag in q2: ZERO.
- Test-only call sites: 15 -- crates/quarto-config/src/convert.rs:116,120,197 (cfg(test) opens at :110) and 12 sites in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs:501..772 (cfg(test) opens at :463). Each needs one extra SourceInfo argument. Mechanical.
- No q2 crate re-exports YamlWithSourceInfo or YamlHashEntry, so nothing propagates to downstream consumers of q2's own crates.
- No struct-literal construction of YamlHashEntry in q2 (only YamlHashEntry::new at convert.rs:199, test code).
- The only production is_scalar() use on a quarto-yaml node (crates/quarto-core/src/crossref/codeblock_shorthand.rs:563) operates on parsed nodes, not self-built ones. Unaffected.

Beware a grep decoy: ~50 hits for "new_scalar" in q2 are ConfigValue::new_scalar (crates/quarto-pandoc-types/src/config_value.rs:423), an unrelated method on q2's own type. quarto-pandoc-types has no quarto-yaml dependency at all.

FORWARD-LOOKING: only TWO sites in q2 should switch to content_source_info(), and both were already known -- crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs:59 (parse_yaml_string_as_markdown_to_config) and its caller crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/config_markdown.rs:289. A sweep found no others. Explicitly ruled out as false positives, recorded so the work is not repeated: project_resources.rs:215/224 (whole-node span, no sub-offset arithmetic), use_cmd/config.rs:229 (already defensive, see above), lua/config_value.rs:610-618 (different provenance path -- see bd-x0o0pem3), theme_diagnostic.rs:331/405 (synthetic test spans).

SEMVER NOTE: q2 pins quarto-yaml = "0.1.2" as a version dep, so ^0.1.2 applies. A breaking 0.1.3 would be pulled in silently by a routine cargo update and break q2's test build with no Cargo.toml signal; 0.2.0 requires an explicit edit and is therefore the SAFER choice in practice as well as the semver-correct one.

c-wqkls0fr.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-wqkls0fr.text:
SESSION 2026-08-19/20 — measurements from the Positron-docs ariadne crash, folded in here per the dedupe decision. bd-jfl1ba13 (filed this session before this strand was found) is CLOSED as a duplicate of this one; bd-jmquuiqh and bd-th2ah982 are re-parented under it.

This strand's analysis was correct and is confirmed independently. Adding four things it did not have.

1. THE YAML BRANCH HAS A SECOND, WORSE SYMPTOM THAN ESCAPES. The quoted-scalar case is a constant -1 (base is the opening quote, not the first content byte). But MULTI-LINE BLOCK SCALARS drift by one indent-width per line crossed, and it compounds. Measured on a three-line page-footer.center, two Q-2-9 warnings that both belong on line 9 are reported at 8:10 and 9:14 -- the drift is large enough to attribute a diagnostic to the WRONG LINE. Single-line block scalars are correct (they never cross a newline); plain scalars are correct (no delimiter). So the YAML branch is wrong for quoted (constant) and multi-line block (accumulating), and right otherwise.

2. IT CAN CRASH, NOT ONLY MISPOINT. When a drifted offset lands inside a multi-byte character, the diagnostic renderer panics and aborts the whole render:

    thread 'main' panicked at ariadne-0.6.0/src/write.rs:84:59:
    end byte index 37 is not a char boundary; it is inside U+2728 (bytes 35..38 of string)

Real-world hit: one U+2728 in the Positron docs navbar made every full-project render exit 101 with a truncated diagnostic log, while _site/ was written correctly. Tracked as bd-ariadne-config-span-char-boundary-panic-rkqmhzrg and now FIXED defensively in quarto-error-reporting (char-boundary snapping in both renderer paths, commit 4da3385 on fix/diagnostic-span-char-boundary). That fix stops the abort but cannot recover the lost byte -- carets remain wrong until THIS strand is fixed. Note the crash risk applies to every drifting path here, not just YAML.

3. A THIRD DECODER HAS THE SAME BUG, INDEPENDENT OF THE TWO LISTED HERE. crates/comrak-to-pandoc/src/inline.rs:49-52 (NodeValue::Text arm) passes comrak's RAW sourcepos as base into tokenize_text_with_source (crates/comrak-to-pandoc/src/text.rs:90-140), which does base_offset + byte_idx over comrak's DECODED text -- CommonMark unescapes backslash escapes and resolves entity references in text nodes. Every offset after the first escape in a text node is shifted. Reachable in production via pampa --from commonmark (crates/pampa/src/main.rs:334). Other NodeValue arms use whole-node spans and are safe; only the Text arm does per-offset arithmetic. Filed separately and linked.

4. A FOURTH, PROBABLY-INERT SITE. crates/pampa/src/lua/config_value.rs:601-631 (the quarto.config.md Lua API) has the same call shape as meta.rs, but its base is filter_source_info() = SourceInfo::Generated with an empty anchor list, so resolve_byte_range()/map_offset() return None and the bad arithmetic never resolves to a byte position. UNVERIFIED: whether any append_anchor call site attaches an Invocation anchor to that Generated before it is read. Needs a liveness check before it is worth fixing.

AGREED FIX DIRECTION (this strand's first option, chosen after independent rederivation): carry an offset map through the decode and emit SourceInfo::concat pieces. Factoring decided: a small run-accumulating builder in quarto-source-map (verbatim(src_range) / replacement(src_range, out_len) / finish() -> Concat), with each decoder driving it using its own escape rules -- YAML in quarto-yaml, backslash-escapes in pampa's attribute path, entities in comrak-to-pandoc. The escape rules are not shareable; the run-tiling machinery is.

VERIFIED PREREQUISITES (against quarto-source-map 0.1.0): SourceInfo::concat(Vec<(SourceInfo, usize)>) is PUBLIC and SourcePiece's fields are all pub, so no new enum variant and no upstream API is needed -- consistent with the ipynb doc's finding that the closed SourceInfo enum need not change. concat() assigns offset_in_concat cumulatively, so pieces tile contiguously by construction; this also disposes of a latent wrinkle where Concat::length() sums piece lengths while the exclusive-end branch of map_offset tests last.offset_in_concat + last.length.

WHY THE EPHEMERAL-SOURCEFILE ALTERNATIVE WAS NOT CHOSEN for these paths: it is right for ipynb (users want positions relative to the CELL) and wrong for config (users want _quarto.yml:7:16, not a position inside an anonymous decoded-scalar file). Same mechanism, opposite desired user-visible outcome. Both approaches can coexist per-path.

SUGGESTED PRIORITY BUMP: this is currently P2. The description's own note that preimage_in feeds the incremental writer's verbatim-copy decision means a drifted range can copy the WRONG BYTES into output -- a correctness bug in rendered output, not only in diagnostics. crates/pampa/src/writers/incremental.rs does copy byte ranges verbatim from original_qmd. I did not trace the exact wiring end to end, so this is a recommendation rather than a confirmed escalation.

title: q2 preview end-to-end verification for mermaid blocks
description:
Verify the MermaidEngine survives the q2-preview round trip (capture-splice path).

**This task effectively closes PR #238's bd-iq0hp** — PR #238 documented that a browser E2E of multi-engine preview was not possible at PR time because the default registry uses real engines, FixtureEngine is test-only, and knitr/jupyter don't compose cleanly (knitr claims `{python}` via reticulate). Mermaid + knitr is the first real-engine pair with disjoint cell-class ownership (`{r}` vs `{mermaid}` never overlap).

Test matrix:

1. Document with mermaid block only — q2 preview renders the diagram.
2. Document with engine: [knitr, mermaidjs], knitr block + mermaid block, with recorded captures — both render in preview.
3. Edit the mermaid block — preview updates without re-running knitr's capture (capture invariance on engine 1's input).
4. Confirm the jsdelivr script include arrives in the preview's HTML body. If C1 (inline RawBlock in engine markdown) is the chosen approach (per plan v2), this should Just Work because capture-splice preserves result.markdown. If C2/C3 is chosen instead, bd-cp3em becomes a blocker.

title: q2 preview: deck-level footer/logo + has-logo absent (RevealDeck)
description:
format: revealjs deck with footer:/logo: renders the footer (.footer.footer-default), logo (img.slide-logo) and .reveal.has-logo in q2 render, but NONE of them in q2 preview.

Repro: cargo run --bin q2 -- render examples/presentations/10-footer-logo/slides.qmd (footer+logo present, .reveal.has-logo) vs q2 preview same file (all absent).

Root cause: ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/RevealDeck.tsx never reads meta.rendered.reveal.footer / .logo and never adds has-logo. The data IS present: RevealFooterLogoTransform (name reveal-footer-logo, pipeline.rs footer_render_stage(is_revealjs=true)) runs in the q2-preview pipeline (not in Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED), so ast.meta carries rendered.reveal.{footer,logo}.

Native contract: crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs render_revealjs_document — footer/logo are DIRECT children of .reveal OUTSIDE .slides (position:fixed survives reveal's per-slide transforms only there); .reveal gains has-logo.

Fix (TDD per /preview-render-parity): failing q2-preview.integration.test first asserting .reveal.has-logo > .slide-logo and .reveal > .footer.footer-default outside .slides; then inject the two raw-HTML slots outside <Deck>'s slide children + add has-logo to the deck container.

title: crossref: float caption prefix skipped when caption_long starts with Plain (attr-form figures, caption-form tables); caption block shape not canonicalized
description: Reported 2026-09-17 via ~/Desktop/daily-log/2026/09/17/fig-test/test.qmd: '![cap](plot.png){#fig-test-2}' renders <figcaption>This is another figure</figcaption> while the code-cell fig-cap figure renders 'Figure 1: ...'. Refs resolve fine ('See Figure 2'). Q1 prefixes both. Root cause: FloatRefTargetSugarTransform normalizes every float shape into the same FloatRefTarget custom node, but the caption_long slot keeps the producer's block type verbatim — Paragraph for the div-form trailing paragraph and the #| fig-cap Div wrapper, Plain for Pandoc-native Figure captions, Table captions, and the #| fig-cap Figure wrapper. crossref_render::prefix_caption (and crossref_index::extract_caption_inlines, and the preview's FloatRefTarget.tsx) only act on a leading Paragraph, so Plain-first captions silently lose the 'Figure N: ' prefix. Q1's decorate_caption_with_crossref is shape-agnostic (tprepend on caption_long.content). Consolidates bd-uwv2eec2, bd-hb9a9ik8, bd-4vbd3b7g, bd-51k5yz4e (same root cause, filed 4x, never fixed). title: q2 format-variant support: format matching uses the Quarto format string where Q1 uses pandoc's writer name, and the format-string grammar is a subset of Q1's
description:
Found 2026-09-18 while prevalidating test seams for the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic (P8 companion findings F1 and F5). Decided with Gordon: file a strand, do not fix inside that epic. Documentation consulted per Gordon: quarto-web docs/authoring/conditional.qmd + its _format-aliases.md include, and Q1's own parseFormatString grammar comment. All claims below were measured or read against quarto-cli tag v1.11.3 and pandoc 3.8.1, not inferred.

THREE DISTINCT GAPS, smallest first.

(1) MATCHING USES THE WRONG STRING (the F1 bug). q2's ConditionalContentTransform computes its format via the string-only lua_format_for (crates/quarto-core/src/format.rs:164-170), which passes any non-pseudo target_format through VERBATIM. Q1 instead matches against pandoc's FORMAT global, which is the pandoc WRITER name. So for `format: acm-docx` (which q2 accepts at format.rs:418-429, yielding identifier=Docx but target_format="acm-docx"), lua_format_for returns "acm-docx" and is_format_match("acm-docx","docx") is FALSE (crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_doc.rs:74-90: the exact-match arm misses and "docx" is not one of the six alias families). Consequences, both directions:
  - `::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}` is SILENTLY DROPPED in an acm-docx render. Q1 shows it.
  - `when-format="acm-docx"` is TRUE in q2 but FALSE in Q1 (Q1's FORMAT is "docx"; no alias branch matches "acm-docx").
The canonicalizing helper already exists and is already correct: Format::lua_format() (format.rs:383-389) uses self.identifier.as_str(). Its own doc comment scopes its agreement with lua_format_for to "the pseudo-format and base cases" -- i.e. tightly enough to exclude exactly this case.
NOT Pandoc-specific and NOT new: `acm-html` + when-format="html" is broken today on the HTML leg by the identical mechanism, as is llms_view_active (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/llms.rs:124) for any extension HTML format. Two independently-reachable occurrences known, no user report yet.

(2) THE ALIAS TABLE IS A PROPER SUBSET OF Q1'S (the F5 gap). Q1 (src/resources/pandoc/datadir/_format.lua:244-287 at v1.11.3) additionally handles odt/opendocument as synonyms, matches ANY query containing "epub" via the Lua pattern `to:match "epub"`, and recognizes confluence, docusaurus/docusaurus-md, email, dashboard, hugo/hugo-md, gfm. q2 (quarto_doc.rs:80-88) has none of these. Measured divergences: when-format="opendocument" under --to odt, and when-format="epub3" under --to epub2, are both false in q2 and true in Q1. The documented contract is quarto-web docs/authoring/_format-aliases.md, which is the table to implement against (note it documents `html` as also aliasing dashboard and email, and `markdown` as aliasing hugo-md and docusaurus-md).

(3) THE FORMAT-STRING GRAMMAR IS A SUBSET (found during this research; wider than F1/F5). Q1's authoritative grammar, verbatim from src/core/pandoc/pandoc-formats.ts:126-129 at v1.11.3:
    baseName+<variants | modifiers>-<variants>[<extension>]
    "Where modifiers and variants can be in any order and basename must start
     the string and extension must end the string"
with its own worked examples: acm-pdf+foo, gfm-raw_html, acm-2023-pdf+foobar, pdf, acm -- and acm-gfm-raw_html explicitly NOT allowed. There is also a bracket-extension form, `format: pdf[aspa]` (pandoc-formats.ts:101).
q2's parse_format_descriptor (crates/quarto-core/src/extension/discover.rs:252-271) implements only `<extension>-<base>`, splitting on the LAST hyphen and requiring the suffix to be in KNOWN_BASE_FORMATS (discover.rs:241-250, just 8 entries: html pdf docx epub typst revealjs gfm commonmark). So `gfm-raw_html`, `acm-pdf+foo` and `pdf[aspa]` all fall through to Format::from_format_string's catch-all and are REJECTED outright ("Unknown format", format.rs:449) -- not mismatched, unparseable. Relatedly, q2 has no `variant` render key at all (grepped), where Q1 documents one ("Enable and disable extensions for markdown output (e.g. +emoji)", src/resources/schema/document-options.yml:338) and appends it to the pandoc writer string at src/command/render/output.ts:134-140.

SCOPE NOTE ON THE +/- SUFFIXES, measured so nobody re-derives it: pandoc STRIPS +EXT/-EXT before setting FORMAT. Verified with pandoc 3.8.1 -- `--to gfm+emoji` yields FORMAT=[gfm], `--to markdown+smart-raw_html` yields FORMAT=[markdown]. So pandoc variants do NOT affect format MATCHING in either Q1 or q2; they matter only for gap (3), parsing. That means gap (1) is strictly about the extension-PREFIX shape, and gaps (1) and (3) can be fixed independently.

SUGGESTED SEQUENCING (not a decision): gap (1) is a one-line change at conditional_content.rs:142 (lua_format_for -> ctx.format.lua_format()) plus the same audit at llms.rs:124 and any other lua_format_for caller, and is the only one with a known silent-content-loss symptom. Gap (2) is a table extension against a documented contract. Gap (3) is real work and should probably wait on Q2's extension/format story (cf. bd-vhd3lugq, which defers the related question of how html-based extension formats should preview).

NOT covered by existing strands (checked all 768): bd-vhd3lugq is about PREVIEWING extension formats, bd-mamqirfz is about the contributes.format config-key alias. bd-fu16z22k is closed and is cited in quarto_doc.rs only as the provenance of sharing is_format_match with the when-format attribute path, not as an open format-matching issue.

title: [websites epic] Unify nav config placement across features
description:
Nav config placement across features. Phase 3 (2026-04-24) refined the framing: rather than 'unify everything into one namespace,' the principle is now "placement follows feature semantics."

Current placement (post-Phase 3):
- 'navbar:' — top level (feature-scoped; works in single-doc + project)
- 'page-footer:' — top level (same; revealjs/etc. legitimately use it)
- 'website.sidebar:' — under website. (sidebar is inherently a multi-page website feature)
- 'site-sidebar:' (per-doc override selecting which sidebar applies) — top level
- 'website.title:' / 'website.site-url:' / 'website.favicon:' — under website. (site-scoped)

The only remaining tension is 'site-sidebar' being a doc-level override for a website-scoped feature. Options:
(a) rename to 'website.sidebar-id' (canonical; website.sidebar-id already accepted in Phase 2 as an alias)
(b) keep 'site-sidebar' since it's a per-doc override like 'draft:' / 'date:' and those also live at the top level

Not a blocker for MVP; land before docs-facing release. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-24-websites-phase-3.md §Decision 1 for the framing shift.

title: Named HTML entity references silently dropped in prose (>,  , ...)
description:
Named entity references in markdown prose are dropped from the output without any diagnostic: 'A > B < C & D "E" F G © H.' renders as 'A  B  C  D E FG  H.' — every named reference vanishes. Numeric references (>, <, &) work correctly. Q1/Pandoc/CommonMark resolve named references to their characters (https://github.github.com/gfm/#entity-and-numeric-character-references).

Root cause: the tree-sitter-qmd grammar produces entity_reference inline nodes (crates/tree-sitter-qmd/common/common.js ~line 41, regex generated from html_entities.json) alongside numeric_character_reference, but the pampa converter (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs) only has a match arm for 'numeric_character_reference' (~line 845, process_numeric_character_reference in treesitter_utils/numeric_character_reference.rs) — 'entity_reference' has no arm and falls through to the default, dropping the node.

Suggested fix: add an 'entity_reference' arm mirroring process_numeric_character_reference, decoding via a named-entity table (the grammar's html_entities.json already carries name->codepoint data, so both sides can share one source of truth;   must decode to U+00A0). A unit test over a few multi-codepoint entities (e.g. ≂̸) would pin the table lookup.

Real-world hit: Posit Connect docs use named entities in 13 files (21x >, 16x  ) — UI breadcrumbs like '**APIs & Services** > **Credentials**' on admin/integrations/oauth-integrations/google/index.qmd render as 'APIs & Services Credentials', losing the navigation separators.

Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/named-entities-dropped/ (see README.md; run 'q2 render repro.qmd' there; Q1-verified expected output). Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-named-entities-zu8jp8pw. Observed with q2 0.15.0; checked origin/main (0cb8abce): no entity-related fixes.
close_reason: Implemented: entity_reference match arm in pampa decoding via the shared WHATWG table (tree_sitter_qmd::HTML_ENTITIES_JSON); also fixed qmd writer escaping of straight double quotes. Commit 9509f8d2 on main. Follow-ups: bd-v8qc9zyc (grammar regex), bd-96fswwce (combining marks).

title: Navbar logo unstyled: theme ships no .navbar-logo rule and brand markup drops Q1's navbar-brand-logo structure
description:
A website navbar logo (website.navbar.logo) renders at the image's natural size — a 512px SVG swallows the whole navbar — instead of Q1's 24px-tall logo beside the title. Two independent defects: 1. No default sizing rule. Q1's theme bundle ships '.navbar-logo { max-height: 24px; width: auto; padding-right: 4px }' (quarto-cli src/resources/projects/website/navigation/quarto-nav.scss:196). q2 emits class="navbar-logo" on the img (crates/quarto-navigation/src/render_html.rs:390 at v0.24.0) but no stylesheet ever targets it — no .navbar-logo rule exists anywhere in crates/, and the generated site_libs/quarto/quarto-theme-*.css contains none (the only 'navbar-logo' hits in the repo are tests asserting the img tag is emitted). 2. Brand markup structure differs, killing the Q1 user-CSS override path. Q1 wraps the brand in '
' with the logo in its own '' (containing light-content/dark-content img variants) followed by a separate title anchor. q2 inlines the img into the single title anchor: ' Title'. User CSS keyed on Q1's documented hooks (e.g. '.navbar-brand-logo .navbar-logo { height: 28px }') silently stops matching, so even after fixing (1) the default can't be overridden the Q1 way. 'navbar-brand-logo' and 'navbar-brand-container' appear nowhere in crates/. Suggested fix: add the .navbar-logo default rule to the navbar styles the theme bundle emits, and restructure the brand markup in render_html.rs to Q1's shape (navbar-brand-container wrapper, separate navbar-brand navbar-brand-logo anchor for the logo, separate title anchor). The light-content/dark-content variant pair can be tracked with theme/dark-mode support generally, but the container + hook classes are what user CSS keys on. Real-world hit: the Posit Connect docs show the Connect mark at full SVG size in the navbar of every page, most visibly the landing page; the docs' own styles.css override can't compensate because its selector targets Q1's markup hooks. Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/navbar-logo-unstyled/ (run 'q2 render' there; see README.md; compare with 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1'). Expected: 24px logo beside the title. Actual: 512px logo, navbar blown up; grep of the generated quarto-theme-*.css for navbar-logo comes up empty. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-navbar-logo-unstyled-varhly4s. Observed with q2 0.21.0; re-verified failing on 0.22.0 through 0.24.0; both defects confirmed still present at HEAD (= v0.24.0).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #561 (merged): theme bundle ships the navbar brand CSS, render_brand emits Q1's navbrand markup hooks, and light/dark logo variants are supported. Deferred pieces tracked in bd-y5y10oir (ordering system + width clamp).

title: Nesting-blind language detection is exposed to engine authors (getLanguages, containsMarimoFence) — latent, not reachable today
description:
Finding 1 of bd-ts-engine-display-fence-joy59gkr. Verified on q2 HEAD 00a1c1702. NOT a live bug — filed so it is not rediscovered as one.

getLanguagesWithClasses (ts-packages/quarto-api/src/markdownRegex/index.ts:378) is a flat per-line scan with no fence state:

  /^[\t >]*```+\s*\{([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_.]*)([^}]*)?\}\s*$/gm

It reports 'r' for a document whose only {r} sits inside a display block (probe A_nested_only), and its [\t >]* prefix class means a display block inside a BLOCKQUOTE reports its language too (probe F_blockquote).

marimo's containsMarimoFence (marimo-engine.ts:44) is the same shape — split('\n').some(line => MARIMO_CELL_REGEX.test(line)) — and returns true for a display-only document (probe M1, verified).

WHY IT IS NOT LIVE, on two counts:

1. Nothing calls getLanguages / getLanguagesWithClasses. Repo-wide they appear only in their own tests, in the @quarto/types interface declaration, and in quarto-engine-host-deno/src/quarto-api.ts where they are EXPOSED to engines. Neither shipped fixture engine uses them.

2. containsMarimoFence feeds claimsFile, and claimsFile is never asked about a native file. source_conversion.rs:203 iterates engines with .filter(|_| !is_qmd_or_md), and NATIVE_EXTENSIONS (project/discovery.rs:94) is ["", "qmd", "md", "markdown"] — the Q-2-51 refusal at :188. marimo declares validExtensions [.qmd, .md]; both are refused. Its content scan is dead code from q2's side.

Confirmed end-to-end: m1-display-only.qmd renders with the display block passed through and nothing executed.

Also dead: julia-engine.ts:147 calls quarto.markdownRegex.partition inside partitionedMarkdown, for which there is NO wire message in ts_protocol.rs. q2 never calls it.

WHAT TO DO: make the exposed predicates fence-aware (or delegate them to breakQuartoMd, which already tracks backtick runs) so the next engine author who reaches for them does not inherit the defect. Cheap; do it opportunistically alongside bd-breakquartomd-indented-display-fence-1wxmf0bh. Do not frame it as a live bug.

Full analysis: claude-notes/research/2026-08-27-ts-engine-display-fence.md

title: smoke-all E2E harness does not normalize source-location attributes (3 fixtures born red)
description:
New nightly smoke-all E2E failure as of run 31469233698 (2026-08-11): quarto-test/callout-title-attribute.qmd [html] fails with 'expected pattern "NoteOff-Host Execution" to match in HTML'. Introduced by PR #496 (dfe651c1, 'Callout: honor the title= attribute', bd-callout-custom-title-dropped-9qi1p7iw), merged AFTER v0.16.0 was cut -- so it first ships in v0.17.0. The feature is correct in 'q2 render': rendering the fixture natively emits
NoteOff-Host Execution
and the assertion regex matches. The failing path is the hub preview pipeline (Automerge -> VFS -> WASM render -> Preview), which is what smoke-all.spec.ts exercises. So this is a preview-vs-render parity question, and q2 preview ships in the released binary. Leading hypothesis: hub-client/e2e/helpers/smokeAllAssertions.ts:stripSourceTrackingSpans only unwraps TEXT where TEXT contains no nested tags ([^<]*), in that exact attribute order. The title inlines are newly parsed as markdown by #496, so their source-tracking spans may nest or carry different attributes and survive stripping. If so the feature is fine in preview and the harness needs to normalize better -- but that is unverified. Next step: run the smoke-all E2E locally for this one fixture and diff the WASM-rendered HTML against the native render. Also note: the fixture's second ensureFileRegexMatches entry ['callout-title-container flex-fill">\\s*Note\\s*'] does not match the native render either, and q2 emits a warning parsing that pattern as markdown during render.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #503 (merged 2026-08-11T16:01:47Z), branch bugfix/bd-nhn7snpg-smoke-all-source-location.

Three fixtures now carry [^>]* slots plus !str so their patterns hold under both renderers; the callout fixture's negative guard got the same treatment because it was vacuous under source-location (it could never match the regression it guards). CI now runs the Playwright smoke-all leg on PRs touching crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/**, closing the loop that let all three land red.

Verified before merge: 12 positive patterns + the negative guard checked against real renders under both plain and source-location: full (with stripSourceTrackingSpans applied) — 4 failures confirmed first, 0 after; negative guard confirmed to catch its regression via constructed markup; full native smoke-all 118/0; hub-client test:wasm 131/131; cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build all 14 steps.

Two follow-ups NOT filed (raised with the user, awaiting their call):
1. Assertion strings under _quarto.tests are markdown-parsed, so [...] and <...> emit warnings that fail noErrorsOrWarnings fixtures. !str is the workaround; arguably these strings should not be markdown-parsed at all.
2. smokeAll.wasm.test.ts renders WITHOUT source-location, so it exercises WASM but not preview's config — it will keep passing on exactly the failures it looks qualified to catch.

c-2do3xv9u.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-2do3xv9u.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED — harness bug, not a product defect. The preview renders the callout title correctly. Reproduced natively by rendering the fixture with preview's own config (format.html.source-location: full), which is what hub-client sets (see crates/quarto-system-runtime/src/wasm.rs:226). The emitted title container is:
NoteOff-Host Execution
After stripSourceTrackingSpans (hub-client/e2e/helpers/smokeAllAssertions.ts:42), which only unwraps TEXT with no other attributes, this becomes: NoteOff-Host Execution The fixture pattern expects NoteOff-Host Execution. It fails only because source-location: full puts data-sid ON the screen-reader-only span itself — an element the writer emits with a class, so it is not a pure wrapper and is correctly left alone by the unwrapper. The visible content is right; the attribute is the only difference. Same defect hits the fixture's renv assertion: preview emits renv, which also survives stripping. FIX DIRECTION (test-only, no shipping code): after unwrapping pure wrapper spans, also strip leftover data-sid/data-loc ATTRIBUTES from remaining tags. That is general — it fixes this class of failure for every fixture, not just callouts. Worth checking whether it also explains the two long-standing extensions/contract-* nightly reds. RELEASE IMPACT: none. q2 render and q2 preview both emit correct callout titles. This does not block v0.17.0.

c-t16hk0ev.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-t16hk0ev.text: AUDIT (2026-08-11). Scope is wider than the original title; retitled. Two corrections and one verified generalization. CORRECTION 1 — I was wrong about the fixture's second assertion array. I wrote that callout-title-attribute.qmd's entry ['callout-title-container flex-fill">\\s*Note\\s*'] 'does not match the native render either', implying a fixture bug. It is not a bug. parseTwoArraySpec (hub-client/e2e/helpers/smokeAllDiscovery.ts:187) reads the two-array form as [matches, noMatches], so that array is a NEGATIVE assertion: it asserts the bare-'Note' title container (the pre-#496 dropped-title behavior) does NOT appear. It correctly does not appear. That assertion is fine and passing. Disregard that paragraph of the original description. VERIFIED — the same root cause explains all three failing fixtures, and it is not specific to callouts. Control experiment, all with the same binary: WITHOUT source-location (plain q2 render): contract-doc-shortcodes 'strong>_bringit_' -> MATCHES contract-return-coercions 'strong>RET-INLINE' -> MATCHES WITH format.html.source-location: full (what hub-client sets): _bringit_ -> pattern FAILS RET-INLINE -> pattern FAILS So the defect is general: stripSourceTrackingSpans unwraps pure wrapper spans but never removes data-sid/data-loc ATTRIBUTES from elements that carry anything else. Any fixture pattern asserting across a tag boundary ('strong>X', 'renv', 'NoteOff-Host') fails under preview's config while passing under q2 render. Note the two contract patterns fail on a plain with only a data-sid — the element does not even need a class. NOT A REGRESSION — all three fixtures were BORN failing: contract-doc-shortcodes, contract-return-coercions added 6ff4221e (#450, 2026-07-31) callout-title-attribute added dfe651c1 (#496, 2026-08-10) The nightly's last green was 2026-07-31 and its first red 2026-08-01 — the night after #450 landed. Nothing broke; fixtures were authored against q2 render output and never passed the preview harness. SYSTEMIC ISSUE (the real finding): a fixture author validates against q2 render, sees green, and lands a fixture that is permanently red in the nightly. The nightly has now been red 11 consecutive nights, so it carries ZERO signal — a genuine preview regression would be indistinguishable from the standing red. That is a bigger risk than any of the three fixtures. FIX: after unwrapping wrapper spans, strip leftover data-sid/data-loc attributes from remaining tags. Test-only, no shipping code. Then confirm the nightly returns to green so it regains signal value.

title: Mermaid theming: --mermaid-* CSS variables + mermaid theme metadata
description: Follow-up to bd-5m4ga0s1 (mermaid as regular rendering feature), which ships with mermaid's default theme regardless of document theme. Port Quarto 1's theming model: (1) the --mermaid-* CSS custom properties (--mermaid-fg-color, --mermaid-node-bg-color, --mermaid-edge-color, etc.) derived from Bootstrap SCSS variables (Q1: src/resources/formats/html/_quarto-rules.scss, e.g. $mermaid-edge-color: $secondary), passed as themeCSS to mermaid.initialize — wire into quarto-sass; (2) explicit 'mermaid: theme: default|dark|forest|neutral' document metadata pass-through to initialize(), which disables the CSS-variable path when set (Q1 semantics); (3) the React preview component reads the same metadata / CSS variables so preview matches render. Reference: Q1 mermaid-init.js themeCSS handling, embed-mermaid.css, external-sources/quarto-web docs/authoring/_mermaid-theming.qmd.

title: highest_version_node dead-code fails clippy on Windows (-D warnings)
description: fn highest_version_node in crates/quarto-mcp-launcher/src/node.rs:231 is called only from the non-Windows branch of node_search_paths (lines 207-213). The #[cfg(windows)] branch does not call it and the fn itself is not cfg-gated, so on Windows it is dead code and cargo xtask verify fails at the clippy stage under -D warnings. CI (Linux/Mac) uses the fn so it is green there; only Windows dev is affected. This blocks cargo xtask verify locally on Windows at HEAD 51cf3707. Fix: gate the fn with #[cfg(not(windows))] to match its call sites, or add a justified #[allow(dead_code)]. Discovered during bd-i9i5ad2t pre-flight verify.
close_reason: Gated highest_version_node with #[cfg(unix)] to match its only call site (unix branch of node_search_paths); verified with cargo clippy -p quarto-mcp-launcher --all-targets -- -D warnings

title: Q-12-17's message says an escaping pattern 'matches nothing', untrue for a record path:
description:
Q-12-17 is reused for a listing record's `path:` that escapes the project. Its message is templated for globs (`glob/diagnostics.rs`) and says the pattern 'matches nothing' — but an escaping record path keeps its item and links as written. The docs page was updated for the record case in the inline-records branch; the emitted message was not.

Plan-mandated reuse, deferred deliberately. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-listing-inline-contents.md

title: pampa HTML writer can emit duplicate title= on Link/Image (attr kv before target title)
description: crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs Link arm (:966) and Image arm (:977) emit write_attr(&attr) — including any title=... kv — and then unconditionally append the target title when non-empty. A link like [l](u "T1"){title="T2"} therefore renders <a href="u" title="T2" title="T1"> — invalid HTML (duplicate attribute); browsers keep the first occurrence, so the kv silently wins over the target title, the opposite of pandoc's HTML writer (target title wins). Found while fixing the nav renderer's attr drop (bd-footer-link-attrs-dropped-1axx82op), where the chosen policy is: target title wins, kv title suppressed when a target title is present. The body writer should adopt the same rule. Low priority: hard to author a double-title document intentionally.

title: qmd reader drops whitespace between code_span and html_element (issue #182)
description:
Reader silently drops leading/trailing whitespace on bare html_element nodes when they're converted to RawInline, so AST loses the Space between adjacent Code and RawInline siblings. Writer then collides backticks and round-trip fails to re-parse.

Reproduction, root cause, and recommended fix scope are documented in claude-notes/issue-reports/182/triage.md on branch issue-182 (worktree .worktrees/issue-182). Short version: the html_element visitor's anchor-shorthand branch already handles leading_ws/trailing_ws correctly by emitting adjacent Space inlines; the sibling RawInline branch in the same match arm does not. The fix mirrors that pattern.

Localized in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs (html_element arm). TDD-first per crates/pampa/CLAUDE.md: add a roundtrip fixture and an AST assertion before changing code.
close_reason: Fixed in f2867bb1 on branch issue-182. Reader now emits leading/trailing Space inlines around RawInline when the html_element node carries surrounding whitespace, mirroring the anchor-shorthand branch in the same match arm.

title: Cargo: upgrade deno_core v0.376.0 → v0.400.0

title: Project-type extension 'preview.serve': delegate preview to an external dev server
description: Q1 contributes.project fragments can declare preview.serve {cmd, ready, env} so 'quarto preview' launches an external dev server (hugo serve, docusaurus start) and proxies it. Q2's custom project types (bd-ad7i1pc6) merge the fragment but nothing consumes preview.serve; q2 preview always uses its own server. Implement alongside default-base custom types for static-site-generator wrappers.

title: q2 render with no args walks cwd before checking for _quarto.yml
description:
`q2 render` invoked with no arguments in a directory with no `_quarto.yml` (and no `_quarto.yml` in any ancestor) eventually emits the correct "No input given and no `_quarto.yml` found at or above <cwd>" error — but only AFTER recursively walking the entire cwd looking for `.qmd` files.

In an empty directory the error appears instantly. In a large tree (q2 repo root: ~64k entries in `target/`, more under `external-sources/quarto-cli/`), the command appears to hang for many seconds because the walker descends into `target/` and `external-sources/` (`is_excluded_component` excludes only `_*`, `.*`, and `node_modules`).

The walk's output is then thrown away — `classify_no_inputs` decides we have no project anyway.

Measured warm-cache cost in the q2 root: 0.3s. Cold-cache cost (or with `external-sources/quarto-cli/` fully populated): multi-second freeze.

**Root cause:** `crates/quarto/src/commands/render.rs:331-346` (`classify_no_inputs`) calls `ProjectContext::discover(&cwd, ...)` before checking whether a real project exists. `ProjectContext::discover` does the upward `_quarto.yml` search (cheap), and on miss falls through to `discover_project_files` → `walk_qmd` (recursive cwd walk).

**Fix:** Short-circuit `classify_no_inputs` — do the cheap upward `_quarto.yml`/`_quarto.yaml` ancestor search first, and only call `ProjectContext::discover` when a real project is known to exist. Inline the upward loop (six lines, only uses `runtime.path_exists`) rather than exporting a new helper for one caller.

**Plan:** claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-render-no-project-skip-walk.md
close_reason:
Implemented in commit 58d2bd34.

Approach: added `find_project_root_upward` (parsing-free
`path_exists`-only ancestor walk) and made `classify_no_inputs` call
it before delegating to `ProjectContext::discover`. The expensive
`discover_project_files`/`walk_qmd` fall-through is now skipped
entirely when no `_quarto.yml` ancestor exists.

E2E timing (warm cache, debug build):
  q2 root:       0.318 s → 0.021 s  (15×; cold-cache delta larger)
  /tmp/empty:    unchanged (~6 ms)
  docs/:         renders normally (unchanged)
  docs/<sub>/:   renders normally (Test 3 e2e)

Error text byte-identical: "No input given and no `_quarto.yml`
found at or above <cwd>".

Regression coverage: `classify_no_inputs_does_not_walk_cwd` asserts
`dir_list_count == 0` via a `RecordingRuntime` wrapper around
`NativeRuntime`. `classify_no_args_from_project_subdir_returns_full_project`
pins the cwd-inside-project case.

Verification: `cargo nextest run -p quarto` 100/100 pass;
`cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` all 12 steps green.

Out-of-scope follow-up: bd-k4ahh tracks the symmetric `q2 render <dir>`
with-arguments path (lower priority, filed discovered-from).

title: Execute-visibility options ignored: jupyter drops echo/output/warning/include; knitr overrides document-scope execute: with hardcoded defaults
description:
GH issue #523 (third-party): https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/523

Reported as 'code-fold: true silently overrides execute: echo: false'. The symptom is real; the attributed cause is not. Verified on main @3ac596e0 (identical to 0.20.0 on these paths) against Q1 (quarto 99.9.9, external-sources/quarto-cli @45caede32).

VERDICT
- code-fold has ZERO effect on q2 output: fold.html and nofold.html are byte-identical (diff exit 0). code-fold is entirely unimplemented (bd-1tl09 / bd-g1prx), so it cannot override anything. The reporter's isolation step did not reproduce.
- The real defect is wider than reported:
  * jupyter ignores the WHOLE execute-visibility family - echo, output, warning, include - at BOTH document scope (execute:) and cell scope (#|). render_cell (text_execute.rs:412) always calls echoed_source_fence; format_outputs always emits everything.
  * knitr ignores document-scope execute: entirely and actively OVERRIDES it: build_format_config (engine/knitr/mod.rs:255) discards document metadata and ExecuteConfig::with_defaults hardcodes echo: true. Per-cell #| echo: false does work there (knitr/R handles it below q2).
- Q1 honors echo: false in all tested variants.

ROOT CAUSES
1. text_execute.rs:412 render_cell - unconditional echo. The machinery exists: resolve_allow_errors (:324) already does cell-over-doc merge_cell_over_scope for error:; echo was never wired to it (bd-ohvl879u scoped itself to error:).
2. engine/knitr/mod.rs:255 build_format_config ignores ctx metadata; format.rs ExecuteConfig::with_defaults hardcodes echo/warning/include = true.
3. ExecutionContext (engine/context.rs) carries no merged execute: scope. Jupyter works around it by re-parsing its own serialized front matter (document_execute_scope, :278); knitr cannot reuse that (its config crosses a JSON boundary to R). engine_execution.rs:375 has the merged AST in hand.

Q1 CONTRACT: src/core/jupyter/tags.ts shouldInclude/shouldHide - cell option wins over execute scope, absent both = format default (echo: true for plain HTML, cf bd-cymkcyaf). keep-hidden emits .hidden instead of dropping; echo: 'fenced' is a third value.

PLAN (phased, TDD; awaiting review): claude-notes/plans/2026-08-14-issue-523-execute-visibility.md
Phase 0 tests-first visibility matrix; Phase 1 plumb merged execute: scope into ExecutionContext; Phase 2 jupyter resolve_visibility mirroring shouldInclude; Phase 3 knitr build_format_config reads the scope; Phase 4 workspace + xtask verify + e2e through the binary on the issue's exact fixture.

OPEN SCOPE QUESTION for review: do the whole visibility family in one pass (recommended - one resolver, one test matrix) vs echo-only with three follow-ups. keep-hidden and echo: 'fenced' proposed as deferred follow-ups.

c-1opbuxnl.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-1opbuxnl.text:
Committed 31d25d93 on braid/bd-nn2fou8h-execute-visibility-options-ignored. Full cargo xtask verify passed (all 14 steps incl. the WASM/hub-client leg). No snapshot (.snap) files added, modified, or removed by this change.

PREVIEW VERIFIED IN A REAL BROWSER (the render path passing proves nothing about preview — cf. the 2026-05-20 stale-WASM incident). Chain run: cargo xtask verify (rebuilds WASM + q2-preview-spa dist) then cargo build --bin q2 to re-embed. Single-file q2 preview of an 'execute: echo: false' doc, iframe DOM read via CDP: div.cell=1, .cell-code=0, pre.sourceCode=0, one .cell-output-stdout with the output. Page text is prose / output / prose — no source anywhere.

That session also turned bd-42202ipf from a code trace into a reproduced bug, and proved it pre-existing by reproducing the identical DOM under knitr (whose include:false path this work does not touch). Evidence recorded there.

Awaiting push approval. Not yet done, deliberately: replying on GH issue #523 to correct the code-fold attribution.

c-ls4dthaw.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ls4dthaw.text: Pushed to origin as bugfix/bd-nn2fou8h-execute-visibility; PR #530 opened: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/530 (commit 31d25d93). Awaiting CI.

c-ubw04xln.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ubw04xln.text:
Implementation complete through Phase 4 verification (2026-08-14), branch braid/bd-nn2fou8h-execute-visibility-options-ignored. Scope as approved: whole visibility family (echo/output/warning/include), BOTH engines.

PHASE 0 (tests first). New crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/engine_visibility.rs, 19 tests, modelled on engine_error_policy.rs (real engines via record_capture, skip when unavailable). Confirmed 15 fail / 4 pass BEFORE any implementation, every failure semantic rather than harness ('expected source echoed = false, got true'). The 4 that passed were the two no-execute-key default guards, knitr cell-scope echo (knitr resolves #| itself), and jupyter cell-echo-true-over-doc-false (vacuous while echo was always on).

PHASE 1. ExecutionContext gains execute_scope: Option<ConfigValue> + with_execute_scope(), populated in engine_execution.rs from ast.meta per engine iteration (so engine 2 in a sequence sees the front matter it is actually handed). Retired text_execute.rs::document_execute_scope + front_matter_range — the jupyter engine used to recover the scope by re-parsing the front matter of its own serialized input; that existed only because the field didn't.

PHASE 2 (jupyter). resolve_cell_options replaces resolve_allow_errors and returns the merged map once; error: now reads off the same path. New CellVisibility { echo, output, warning } mirroring Q1's shouldInclude; include: false collapses to HIDDEN (Q1's early bail). output: false also silences warnings (Q1 suppresses all outputs under it). format_outputs filters stderr streams via is_warning_output (Q1's isWarningOutput). The .cell wrapper is now suppressed when neither source nor any output survives — Q1 builds its div opener but writes it only 'if there is actually content in the div'. 9 new unit tests, no kernel needed.

PHASE 3 (knitr). ExecuteConfig::overlay_document_scope() in format.rs + build_format_config applies it over with_defaults(). KEY FINDING: the R side needed NO change — resources/rmd/execute.R:307-335 already reads format$execute for echo (incl. 'fenced'), warning, message, include, output (false -> results/fig.show hidden), eval, error. Nothing had ever populated it. TRAP AVOIDED: execute.R uses isTRUE() for warning/include, so an absent key reads FALSE — passing the document map through verbatim would have set include=false for every chunk and blanked the document. Hence overlay-onto-defaults, never replace. String reads use as_plain_text(), not as_str(): 'echo: fenced' in front-matter context is PandocInlines, where as_str() returns None and the option would vanish (the metadata-as-str lint's trap). freeze deliberately not forwarded — no R consumer. 8 new unit tests cover the numeric/keyword/string paths the integration tests don't reach.

BONUS PARITY FIX: doc-level 'execute: error: true' now reaches knitr too. Previously with_defaults pinned error:false, so the engines disagreed — jupyter honored the doc-level allow (bd-ohvl879u) and knitr did not. Two tests added to engine_error_policy.rs (the allow, and the mirror that an un-annotated knitr error still fails).

VERIFICATION. 19/19 engine_visibility green (both engines, both scopes, precedence both directions, no-empty-wrapper, plus a regression test pinned to the issue's exact fixture). cargo nextest run --workspace: 11954 passed / 0 failed. clippy 0 warnings, cargo fmt clean, cargo xtask lint clean. E2E through the real binary on the issue's exact fold.qmd now emits ONLY the output div — no sourceCode block — matching Q1; three more fixtures verified (knitr doc echo, include:false leaving zero cell markup with prose intact, warning:false dropping the stderr div). Full cargo xtask verify running.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED: bd-42202ipf (capture-splice mis-pairs a hidden cell with the NEXT cell's wrapper when two cells are adjacent — PRE-EXISTING, knitr has always emitted nothing for include:false; this work makes it reachable in more documents) and bd-tskkw5dq (deferred keep-hidden + jupyter echo:'fenced'; note knitr's fenced half already works via this change, so the engines currently disagree there).

Plan + full evidence: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-14-issue-523-execute-visibility.md

title: Glob support in project.nav-dependencies declarations
description: Today `project.nav-dependencies` accepts a flat list of paths. Some users may want `project.nav-dependencies: [posts/*.qmd]` or `[chapters/**/*.qmd]`. v1 doesn't support globs (open question 5 in the Phase 8 plan). title:
preview parity: included list item content wrapped in

on preview, bare text on render
description:
Fixture: includes/nested/nested.qmd. `{{< include >}}` inside a tight bullet-list item. Render: `
  • ` → bare text `"NESTED-LIST-MARKER-XYZ included item content."` (no wrapper). Preview: `
  • ` → `

    ` → same text. ## Evidence render.norm.txt: ```

    • "NESTED-LIST-MARKER-XYZ included item content."
    • "plain second item" ``` preview.norm.txt: ```

      • "NESTED-LIST-MARKER-XYZ included item content."

      • "plain second item" ``` ## Root cause: unknown — two hypotheses, needs investigation This is NOT an excluded-transform case (unlike strands 1/2/4 above) — the include machinery runs identically in both native and WASM builds. Two candidate splice sites both take the same shape: splice whatever `Block`s the included content parsed as directly into the list item slot, with no explicit downgrade from `Paragraph` to `Plain`: - `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/shortcode_resolve.rs:1656` — `blocks.splice(i..=i, new_blocks)` inside `resolve_blocks`, the generic block-context shortcode splice (`ShortcodeResult::Blocks` arm). - `crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/include_expansion.rs:412` — `blocks.splice(i..i + 1, children)` inside the stage-level include expansion (doc comment at `:801-803` explicitly notes tight list items hold `Plain`, not `Paragraph`). Neither site's code differs between render and preview, and `crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs`'s `write_list_item`/`write_blocks_inline` (around lines 1366-1389) render blocks verbatim with no tight-list Paragraph→Plain downgrade either — so if render truly shows bare text, the AST block at that position must literally be `Block::Plain`, not `Block::Paragraph`, by the time the HTML writer sees it. It is not yet established whether: (a) the AST is actually the same (`Paragraph`) in both pipelines, and the divergence is in the React rendering leaves — `ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/Plain.tsx` (renders no wrapper — inlines flow into the surrounding context) vs `.../blocks/Para.tsx` (always renders `

        {...}

        `), i.e. preview renders a `Paragraph` where it should render as a `Plain`; or (b) the include splice genuinely yields different Block types (`Paragraph` on one path, `Plain` on the other) between the native and WASM/preview include-resolution code paths, before either the writer or React leaf ever sees it. Needs actual AST inspection (e.g. `q2 render --show-ast` or debug-printing the WASM AST) to determine which. Fix should end with `dom-parity: true` on the fixture(s). Found by the DOM parity harness (whole-corpus survey, 2026-08-24). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-preview-render-dom-parity-harness.md

title: Investigate tree-sitter grammar CRLF handling on Windows
description: Cargo xtask verify step 4 (tree-sitter test) fails 5/451 pipe-table tests on Windows but passes on ubuntu-latest CI. Surfaced during PR 109 Windows verification on 2026-04-24. Root cause is ambiguous between a test-corpus CRLF issue (Scenario A, .gitattributes fix) and a grammar CRLF-handling bug (Scenario B, grammar.js fix). Must investigate before remediating — fixing the test would mask a real Windows-user bug if Scenario B applies. See design for reproducer and both scenarios. Related to bd-tjbr (sibling Windows dev-ergonomics work). Target branch feature/dev-setup-improvements or its own branch.
design:
Failure mode. cd crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown && tree-sitter test reports 451 parses, 446 successful, 5 failed on Windows. All 5 failures are pipe-table tests: Example 201 (GFM), Pipe table can precede content (two variants), Pipe table can follow content, Pipe table with blank-line caption. file test/corpus/pipe_table.txt shows CRLF line terminators (426 CR paired with 426 LF). git ls-files --eol confirms i/lf w/crlf — stored as LF in the index, materialized as CRLF on Windows checkout via core.autocrlf=true. Same mechanism caused the quarto-doctemplate failures catalogued in q2-windows-verify-tests memory note.

Scenario A — test-corpus CRLF. Grammar is CRLF-agnostic. Parse trees for LF and CRLF inputs are identical. Tests fail only because the corpus .txt file embeds both the input text AND the expected S-expression AST, and the expected AST was written assuming LF parse output. Remediation is a scoped .gitattributes entry: crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test/corpus/*.txt eol=lf. One line, followed by git rm --cached then git checkout to normalize existing files. Real Windows user qmd content continues to parse correctly regardless of line endings.

Scenario B — grammar CRLF bug. Grammar does not treat carriage-return-linefeed as a block boundary where it should. Real Windows user qmd content with CRLF endings parses incorrectly — pipe tables do not detect captions as separate blocks, block boundaries drift. This is a user-facing bug; only a Windows contributor running pampa against CRLF content catches it. Remediation is in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js — typically adding carriage-return to newline character classes or the external scanner logic. .gitattributes would mask this bug instead of fixing it.

Reproducer. Two layers, both diagnostic. Layer 1 tests grammar.js directly via tree-sitter parse. Layer 2 tests the full pampa pipeline that real users hit. Fixtures are written into the tree-sitter-markdown directory so tree-sitter parse picks up the configured grammar without an init-config step.

Layer 1 (grammar.js):

printf 'before\r\n\r\n| a | b |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| 1 | 2 |\r\n\r\nafter\r\n' > crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-crlf.qmd
printf 'before\n\n| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |\n\nafter\n' > crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-lf.qmd
cd crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown
tree-sitter parse test-crlf.qmd > test-crlf.parse
tree-sitter parse test-lf.qmd > test-lf.parse
diff test-crlf.parse test-lf.parse

Layer 2 (pampa end-to-end):

cargo run --quiet -p pampa --bin pampa -- crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-crlf.qmd > pampa-crlf.out
cargo run --quiet -p pampa --bin pampa -- crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-lf.qmd > pampa-lf.out
diff pampa-crlf.out pampa-lf.out

Notes on the prior reproducer in this design field. pampa has no parse subcommand — it is cargo run -p pampa --bin pampa -- input.qmd, with default -f markdown -t native. Git Bash /tmp resolves to %TEMP% but native Windows binaries resolve /tmp to C:\tmp\, so the previous version would have created files Git Bash could not find later. Use repo-local paths.

If both diffs are empty then Scenario A applies. If either diff is non-empty then Scenario B applies. Layer 2 also tells us whether the bug propagates past pampa's input handling into the Pandoc AST that real users render from.

Broader git cross-platform context. The 2026 consensus is that most projects do not need .gitattributes. core.autocrlf=true plus LF-tolerant tooling handles 99 percent of cross-platform cases. quarto-cli is an example — no .gitattributes and no CRLF-related failures. .gitattributes is for files that must be a specific line ending (shell scripts, batch files), binary files misdetected as text, and whitespace-sensitive test corpora where the consuming tool is itself correct. Over-restrictive patterns like * text=auto eol=lf force LF everywhere and are worse for cross-platform dev than no config. The target for this project is minimal, scoped .gitattributes only where the test harness cannot be fixed — and only in Scenario A.

Out of scope. Broader .gitattributes sweep for the whole repo. Fixing the 8 quarto-doctemplate CRLF failures already catalogued in q2-windows-verify-tests (separate work). Tree-sitter CLI changes (upstream, not ours).
acceptance_criteria: Reproducer runs and classifies failure as Scenario A or Scenario B. If Scenario A then .gitattributes entry added for test/corpus/*.txt and cargo xtask verify step 4 passes on Windows. If Scenario B then follow-up beads issue filed for grammar.js fix at higher priority and this investigation issue closes with evidence. q2-windows-verify-tests memory note updated with resolution and link to fix PR or follow-up issue. No regression in CI — tree-sitter tests continue to pass on Linux.
close_reason: Scenario B classified. Follow-up bd-0gsj filed at P1 for the grammar.js fix; full evidence in that issue's design and in the closing comment here.

c-d152rz75.author: cderv
c-d152rz75.text:
Investigation complete. Result: Scenario B (real grammar CRLF bug). Layer 1 (tree-sitter parse on grammar.js) showed pipe_table extents diverge between CRLF and LF inputs — CRLF case absorbs the trailing paragraph as a malformed table row. Layer 2 (cargo run -p pampa) confirmed pampa does not normalize line endings before parsing, so the bug propagates to the Pandoc AST that drives every output format. Real Windows users with default core.autocrlf=true and the common pattern of a pipe table followed by content render structurally wrong documents. .gitattributes alone would have masked this.

Follow-up filed at higher priority: bd-0gsj — Fix CRLF handling in tree-sitter-qmd grammar.js for pipe tables (P1, bug). Full evidence and reproducer carried over to bd-0gsj design field.

title: Audit SourceInfo-FileId vs SourceContext mismatches systematically; consider API change to make wrong-file binding unrepresentable

c-wizb6oha.text: Audit complete; assessment + design proposals written to claude-notes/research/2026-08-09-fileid-span-integrity-audit.md. Headline: (1) beyond the two PR #478 sites, one SUSPECT diagnostic site remains (doc-level resource_error_to_parse_error, filed bd-x113wg9v) plus one correct-only-by-call-ordering site (project_type_error); (2) the bug class extends beyond diagnostics — verified live: EngineExecutionStage computes the intermediate's FileId from filenames.len() while MetadataMerge has already grown SourceContext.files, misattributing engine blocks in every project render with an executable engine (filed bd-itj2mjkr); also incremental-writer foreign-offset slicing fallback, caption-hull construction without same-file checks, attribution gate on raw literal fid 0. (3) Five FileId namespaces share one usize space and SourceContext::get_file's positional fallback lets FileId(0) dummies render against the primary doc. (4) quarto-yaml: parse_with_parent's contract is unchecked and its own doc example violates it; wasm32 truncates the hash to 32 bits where a collision panics add_file_with_id. quarto-yaml-validation (latent): diagnostics can be constructed with one SourceContext and rendered with another; SourceRange mixes parent-relative offsets with root filenames. Design: Option A (guard+lint, q2-only) / B (bind_path derives id inside SourceContext, kill positional fallback, reserved UNKNOWN id, typed resolve_byte_range) / C (Original carries Arc<SourceFileHandle>; rebinding becomes unrepresentable, remap_file_ids and content drift disappear). title: Audit listing config parsing for PandocInlines / yaml-markdown-syntax-error fallthrough
description:
Discovered while writing L5 (bd-5vsr) snapshot test #33. Quarto YAML often parses bare frontmatter strings as PandocInlines (e.g. when a glob like 'posts/*.qmd' confuses the markdown sublexer and lands as a Span carrying the 'yaml-markdown-syntax-error' class). 'parse_contents' (config.rs:572) was matching only Scalar/Glob/Array variants, so 'contents: "posts/*.qmd"' silently parsed as an empty Vec, and apply_type_defaults then injected the default '*.qmd' glob — making cross-directory listing globs invisible at runtime even though the unit tests passed.

Fix in L5: route 'parse_contents' through 'as_plain_text' first, mirroring 'parse_listings' top-level shorthand handling. Two new unit tests lock the behavior (contents_pandoc_inlines_string_parses_as_glob, contents_array_with_pandoc_inlines_items_parses).

Audit asks: what other listing-config parser branches in config.rs are still vulnerable to the same trap? Likely candidates from a quick read: parse_filter_list, parse_string_list, parse_sort, parse_field_types — any branch that matches on ConfigValueKind::Scalar(Yaml::String(_)) directly without a PandocInlines fallthrough should be reviewed and either rewritten to use as_plain_text first or have explicit PandocInlines handling added. Add unit-test coverage for each PandocInlines path discovered.

Out of scope but related: this is also a signal that the YAML parser's 'PandocInlines wrapping for any string with markdown-special chars' choice imposes a hidden tax on every config consumer in the tree. A broader design pass on whether such strings should be unwrapped before reaching consumers (or whether consumers should always use as_plain_text by convention) would be worth doing.

title: q2 preview: code cells render unhighlighted; include CodeHighlightStage + teach React CodeBlock to read data-hl-spans

Two-part fix: (1) remove from the exclusion list so the AST nodes get annotated; (2) update React CodeBlock component (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/CodeBlock.tsx) to read data-hl-spans, decode via the JSON triple-array format, and emit nested tokens mirroring the HTML writer's behavior in crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:write_highlighted_body. Wire format: data-hl-spans="[[start_byte, end_byte, capture_name], ...]". Capture-to-class: replace '.' with '-' (function.builtin → hl-function-builtin). WASM safety: quarto_highlight::annotate_pandoc and built-in grammars (including r) are WASM-safe; only user-grammars are native-only and they're not in scope here.

title: Windows: embedded SCSS @import resolution drops path separator, breaks bootstrap/theme compilation
description: On a Windows build, grass resolves @import by Path::join-ing our virtual embedded load path (default_load_paths() returns PathBuf::from("/__quarto_resources__/bootstrap/scss") etc.) with the import name. Path::join inserts the OS separator at the boundary, so on Windows the candidate becomes '/__quarto_resources__/bootstrap/scss\vendor/_rfs.scss'. EmbeddedResources::strip_prefix (crates/quarto-sass/src/resources.rs:168) does path.to_string_lossy() and strips prefixes with trim_start_matches('/') only, yielding relative key '\vendor/_rfs.scss', which does not match the forward-slash-keyed embedded file set (keys like 'vendor/_rfs.scss' from include_dir). is_file/read return false, grass reports 'Error: Can't find stylesheet to import' for @import "vendor/rfs", and ALL bootstrap/theme compilation fails on Windows-from-source builds. Linux (all '/') matches, so CI is green. Verified empirically: PathBuf::from(prefix).join("vendor/_rfs.scss").to_string_lossy() = '...scss\vendor/_rfs.scss' on Windows; strip_prefix result '\vendor/_rfs.scss' != 'vendor/_rfs.scss'. Same Windows path-separator family as bd-5rl408mv (href) and bd-dff27o04 (JSON writer), different site (embedded @import resolution). Was masked by the parse_layer CRLF bug (bd-3fgnmlco); fixing that uncovered this (quarto-sass suite went 128/76 -> 175/30, the residual 30 are all this vendor/rfs failure). FIX: normalize backslashes to forward slashes at the top of strip_prefix (path.to_string_lossy().replace('\', "/")), making embedded lookup separator-agnostic. Test in-source by feeding a backslash-containing path to is_file so it runs on Linux CI. This blocks bd-22rtwdur smoke-all theme tests going green on Windows.
close_reason: Implemented + verified (commit 4ab5cab7, merged in PR #374). quarto-sass 206/206, quarto-core 94->21 (all deltas wins), smoke_all 21->1 pre-fix, now 0 (bd-5rl408mv landed same PR).

c-4zjsy74d.author: cderv
c-4zjsy74d.text: IMPLEMENTED + verified on a Windows checkout (commit 3a13b6b1). Fix = reuse quarto_util::path::to_forward_slashes (added quarto-util dep to quarto-sass) at EmbeddedResources::strip_prefix + collect_files/collect_directories; RuntimeFs untouched. TDD: RED = test_is_file_tolerates_backslash_separators (inline '\'-joined virtual path, runs on Linux CI too) failed with is_file=false; GREEN after fix. Results: quarto-sass 206/206 (was 128/76 pre-parse_layer, 175/30 after parse_layer alone -- the 30 residual @import vendor/rfs failures now all pass). END-TO-END: full smoke_all suite on Windows went from 21 failures to 69 passed / 20 skipped / 1 failed. The single remaining failure is category 3 (backslash in HTML <link href="../../shared/styles.css">), which is bd-5rl408mv (PR2), a separate cause NOT in this fix's scope. Design review (roborev job 1776) passed after fixing its one finding. quarto-core downstream regression check running. Do not close until quarto-core is green + Chris confirms.

c-9bskyf0j.author: cderv
c-9bskyf0j.text: SCOPE CORRECTION (decided with Chris): this is NOT a one-line strip_prefix fix -- it needs a dedicated design/brainstorm session because embedded SCSS @import resolution is TWO divergent implementations that must both stay correct: (1) NATIVE (cfg(not(wasm32))): grass (Rust) -> RuntimeFs (sass_native.rs) -> EmbeddedResources::strip_prefix (resources.rs:168). Uses OS Path::join, so Windows injects '\' -> lookup miss (the confirmed bug). (2) WASM/hub: dart-sass in JS via js_compile_sass_impl (wasm.rs:552-584); load_paths serialized as forward-slash strings and resolved by a JS importer (not yet located; wasm.rs comment points at hub-client /src/wasm-js-bridge/). strip_prefix is never called on wasm32. VFS path contract uses /project/ prefix + forward slashes. The proper feature = a documented virtual embedded-resource path contract (forward-slash, RESOURCE_PATH_PREFIX-rooted) + a single canonicalization boundary on the native side (OS path -> virtual key), with the WASM JS importer confirmed to honor the same contract (or its correctness verified separately). Plan to be produced by a multi-agent brainstorm: agent A maps native resolution end to end, agent B maps WASM/JS importer + VFS, agent C researches best practice (grass Fs trait, dart-sass importer API, cross-platform embedded-FS path handling). Do NOT ship the replace('\','/') bandage without that design. Root cause + empirical proof remain as documented in the description.

c-eiodvnxs.author: cderv
c-eiodvnxs.text: Design complete (2026-07-03, with Chris). Root cause source-verified against grass_compiler 0.13.4 (visitor.rs:858-859 load_path.join injects '\' on Windows; canonicalize at :891 runs AFTER find_import so is NOT a pre-lookup hook; include_dir_macros 0.7.4 normalizes keys to '/' at build time). DECISIONS: (1) Fix = a single documented to_virtual_key(&Path)->String canonicalization fn (normalize '\'->'/' , collapse '//'), NOT a scattered replace and NOT a VirtualPath newtype yet. (2) Placement = EmbeddedResources::strip_prefix + collect_files/collect_directories ONLY; RuntimeFs stays untouched because its std::fs fallback must keep native Windows paths (C:\...) intact -- this corrects the research suggestion to also normalize in RuntimeFs. (3) WASM latent divergences (Bootstrap-only VFS pool; dead sass-utils path) documented + deferred -> new strand. (4) windows-latest CI job deferred -> new strand. Full design + native/WASM contract + agent research recorded in claude-notes/designs/embedded-resource-virtual-path-contract.md. Implementing now via TDD on the bd-22rtwdur worktree branch (stacked on the parse_layer commit 0e3cd389).

Mostly engine/env-dependent; a couple are path-family (candidates for bd-5rl408mv / bd-oejuizi9 or the broader bd-22rtwdur Windows catalog), none caused by this SCSS fix. Net verified state: quarto-sass 206/206; quarto-core 94->21 (all deltas are wins); smoke_all 21->1 (residual = href backslash, bd-5rl408mv). title: Surface a cause-naming diagnostic when an extension needed by a render fails to load (not a silent WARN)
description: When read_extension returns Err, discover.rs (scan_extension_entry) logs only tracing::warn!('Failed to read extension ...') and discover_extensions returns Vec (not Result), so nothing surfaces to the user. The document then renders with the extension's engine/filter/shortcode missing — e.g. a marimo/julia cell renders as raw code, or a shortcode renders as the unknown-shortcode fallback '?greet' — misattributed to the user's own document with no actionable cause. This remains true even after bd-8b0af414 relaxed over-required fields: a genuinely malformed _extension.yml (or a real quarto-required mismatch) still fails silently. Proposal: when an extension that a render actually depends on (referenced format/engine/shortcode/filter) fails to read, emit a real cause-naming diagnostic (Q-* error or at least a user-visible warning naming the extension, the file, and the specific parse/validation failure) instead of a buried tracing WARN. Discovered while fixing bd-8b0af414; out of scope for that bug (which only relaxed the field requirements).

title: Listing `template:` treats a leading `/` as filesystem-absolute, contradicting the path-resolution contract (project root)
description: load_custom_template (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/listing_render.rs, ~:398-401) does `if template_rel.is_absolute() { template_rel.to_path_buf() }`, so `template: /templates/card.template` resolves against the filesystem root, not the project root. claude-notes/designs/path-resolution-model.md says a leading `/` means the project root, never the filesystem root. Pre-existing; noticed while documenting the new 'Custom templates' section of docs/guides/projects/listings.qmd (which says template: resolves relative to the declaring page and is silent on `/`). Deliberate scope-out from bd-custom-template-not-templated-e5t6m0i0 per the CLAUDE.md path-resolution rule — fix should use the shared resolution helper the contract names, and add the `/` case to the docs sentence.

title: Single-variant adaptive highlight resolution: compiled-CSS darkness sentinel
description: Item (3) of bd-hl-theme-translator-2mdgh4k6, deferred by design decision 6 (2026-08-18): for custom-SCSS single-variant themes, adaptive highlight names resolve via BuiltInTheme::is_dark (builtin_darkness in quarto-sass config.rs), an approximation. Q1 instead greps the compiled CSS for a darkness sentinel (blackness($body-bg) > threshold), which handles custom SCSS that darkens a light base. Requires moving the adaptive decision after (or into) the variant compile, or a pre-compile probe. See claude-notes/plans/2026-08-18-highlight-theme-translator.md § Deferred.

title: Connection-gated auth + local-first documents (hub-client)
description:
Move hub-client auth from an app-entry gate to a connection-only gate: the SPA opens with no login gate, documents live in browser IndexedDB, and auth is required only when the user connects to a hub.
