title: pampa's Lua bridge doesn't expose/walk custom nodes to user filters
description:
Confirmed 2026-09-18 during the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic's user-facing/backward-compat review.

crates/pampa/src/lua/types.rs:1288-1289 has the comment "Custom nodes are not exposed to Lua
filters yet" - Block::Custom/Inline::Custom only expose {tag, clone} to a Lua filter, and
crates/pampa/src/lua/walk.rs:308 treats Block::Custom as a walk terminal (does not descend into
its slots).

Consequence for the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic: a user Lua filter running at a `Post` entry
point (a first-party, documented pattern - filters: [quarto, f.lua], or an extension declaring
at: post-render/post-quarto/post-finalize, e.g. Q1's own bundled docusaurus/orange-book
extensions) cannot see or traverse into ANY custom node's content for a Pandoc-target render,
where CustomNodes (Callout, Tabset, Theorem, Proof, FloatRefTarget) are still standing at that
point (crossref-render/callout-resolve etc. don't run for Pandoc(fmt) profiles). A filter that
would normally transform e.g. every Strong element in the document (a common pattern - smallcaps,
translation passes, link rewriters) silently skips everything inside a callout, tabset, theorem,
proof, or figure caption, with no error and exit 0.

By contrast, Q1's own scoped_walk (ast/scopedwalk.lua) DOES descend into a custom node
scaffold's children (skips dispatching handlers on the scaffold itself, but still walks into
its slots) - so this is a real Q2-vs-Q1 behavioral gap, not a design choice both share. It also
predates and is independent of the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic (native Q2 HTML rendering already
resolves all custom nodes to plain HTML before UserFiltersStage::post() runs, so today's Q2
users never hit this - the gap only becomes reachable once Pandoc-target rendering ships,
because that's the first Q2 render path where CustomNodes survive to the point user filters
run).

**Decided (2026-09-18, Gordon), consistent with the epic's "no new functionality" scope**: not
implementing Lua-bridge custom-node walkability as part of the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic - it's
a real extension to pampa's Lua bridge, not wiring the existing path. Accepted as a known v1
limitation for Pandoc-target renders with post-position user filters; consider a diagnostic
(warn when a user filter resolves to Position::Post for a Pandoc target while CustomNodes are
still present) as a much smaller, epic-scoped mitigation if desired, without waiting for this
strand.

Scope for whoever picks this up: extend crates/pampa/src/lua/{types,walk}.rs so
Block::Custom/Inline::Custom expose slot content and the walker descends into it, matching
Q1's ast/scopedwalk.lua semantics (skip dispatching a handler on the scaffold itself, but do
walk its children).

See claude-notes/designs/pandoc-hybrid-architecture.md for the epic context.

title: Format-extension theme/css paths not rebased: contributes.formats.html.theme silently drops bundled SCSS
description: A format extension declaring 'contributes: formats: html: theme: [cosmo, fmt-theme.scss]' with fmt-theme.scss bundled next to _extension.yml silently loses the theme: the bundled scss is never compiled into the output CSS and no diagnostic is emitted. Root cause: extension/read.rs PATH_VALUED_KEYS only marks template/template-partials/shortcodes (+filters) as Path-kind, so theme/css/include-in-header values in contributes.formats stay Scalar and are never rebased from the extension dir; the theme stage then can't find the file (relative to the document instead) and drops it silently. Repro: single doc with 'format: fancyfmt-html', _extensions/fancyfmt contributing the theme above — rendered doc_files/styles.css lacks the extension rule. Candidate fix: apply the same existence-driven rebase used for contributes.project fragments (project/mod.rs rebase_fragment_paths, bd-ad7i1pc6 Phase 4) to contributes.formats values at read/merge time — and emit a diagnostic when a theme entry resolves to no file instead of dropping it silently. Discovered during bd-ad7i1pc6 Phase 4 verification.

title: Jupyter engine ignores error policy: embeds cell errors and continues where knitr fails the render
description: Discovered during bd-gthycd33 parity-suite work (2026-07-02). With a plain failing cell (no #| error: true), q2's knitr path fails the pipeline ('Execution failed in knitr: R process failed', no capture produced) — matching Q1's default execute.error=false policy. q2's jupyter path (text_execute.rs format_outputs) instead embeds the error as .cell-output-error output and reports success, unconditionally. The engines should agree: a cell error without error: true should fail the render for jupyter too; with #| error: true both should embed. Note: q2 jupyter currently doesn't parse #| cell directives at all, so fixing this requires directive awareness in the jupyter text path. The cross-engine parity suite (crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/engine_output_parity.rs, parity_error_output) pins the error-output SHAPE under #| error: true; this strand is about the POLICY divergence. See claude-notes/plans/2026-07-01-bd-gthycd33-jupyter-cell-wrapper.md.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #363 (merged): shared cell_options facility (language-aware #| partition with exact source attribution + scoped ConfigValue resolution) + jupyter engine error policy — un-annotated cell errors now fail the render like knitr/Q1; #| error: true or execute: error: true embed the error; option lines stripped from kernel input and echo. Full evidence in claude-notes/plans/2026-07-02-bd-ohvl879u-cell-options-error-policy.md. Follow-ups: bd-eizgnxlx, bd-1gty7f7o, bd-2xkpy5ra, bd-moef1ec4, bd-2lc8qu6e.

c-0ktxw34b.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-0ktxw34b.text: Decisions 1-7 locked with Carlos (2026-07-02). Notable: (3) upgraded from 'read error off the YAML' to SCOPED RESOLUTION — convert cell options YamlWithSourceInfo -> ConfigValue (pampa's yaml_to_config_value, source-info preserving) and merge against the document's already-merged metadata execute scope (merge_with_diagnostics); cell error: overrides doc execute: error:, absent both = false. This starts infrastructure for scoped document-metadata resolution in cell options, a longstanding Q1 limitation. Verified the pieces exist: yaml_to_config_value (pampa meta.rs:139), merge_with_diagnostics (quarto-config materialize.rs:188), and the engine input's front matter carries merged metadata (MetadataMergeStage runs before EngineExecutionStage). (4) accepted for v1 with corrected framing — locations in the serialized engine input are the same coordinate system the pipeline already reconciles at the AST level (quarto-ast-reconcile); documented in the plan as mechanism, not problem. (5) strip #| from kernel input + echo. (6) malformed options = hard error with mapped location. (2,7) error-only scope; crossref migration is follow-up. Plan updated; awaiting go-ahead.

title: xtask create-worktree: auto-detect integration branch (or warn) instead of defaulting to main
description:
Today `cargo xtask create-worktree <bd-id>` defaults `--base main`. For sub-task work inside an active epic (the dominant use case for create-worktree per .claude/rules/worktrees.md), main is almost always the wrong base — the convention is to branch off `feature/<epic-name>`. Silent default leads to a worktree at the wrong base that must be `git reset --hard`ed after creation, which is what happened during bd-kw93.1 setup on 2026-05-14.

Options:
1. Auto-detect: if the beads issue has a parent-child to an epic whose branch can be inferred (e.g. the epic title or labels record it), use that branch as the base.
2. Warn-on-default: when `--base` is not passed and the issue has a parent epic, print 'Using default base `main`; sub-tasks of <epic-id> typically branch off feature/<name>. Re-run with --base if needed.' and prompt or exit.
3. Make `--base` required when the issue is a sub-task (has parent-child to a non-closed epic).

Option 2 is the lowest-friction nudge. Option 1 needs a way to recover the integration branch name from the epic (could be a beads label, an external_ref, or just a convention scan).

Related friction: `switch-task` already does the right thing for sequential sub-task work but is under-discoverable when you've reached for create-worktree first. Cross-reference in the rules file or in xtask help text might help.

Acceptance: pick one option, ship, no longer silently defaults to main when context says otherwise.
close_reason: fetch_beads_metadata now reports parent_epic from the dependencies array; create-worktree warns when --base is at its default and the issue has an open parent epic. 5 new unit tests + 3-case binary smoke (warning fires; --base main silences; no parent = no warning). Workspace nextest 8864/8864. Merged to main as commit 28f1a18b.

title: Normalize EOL in revealjs vendored-asset drift test (Windows CRLF false-positive)
description: vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package test fails on Windows: resources/revealjs/*.css checked out CRLF (core.autocrlf), byte-compared against LF node_modules/reveal.js copy in crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs:576. Same class of fix as bd-mv2ggmr5 (pampa) and quarto-citeproc/.gitattributes: add repo-root .gitattributes entry pinning resources/revealjs/** (or the specific vendored files) to text eol=lf.

c-4eqy2aym.author: cderv
c-4eqy2aym.text:
Reconsidered the approach; did NOT pin resources/revealjs to LF. Root distinction: the reveal assets are served VERBATIM (include_str -> artifact bytes -> file), so line endings survive to output; but a CRLF reveal.css is functionally identical to every browser, and nothing in q2 states bit-reproducible builds as a goal (the other ~9 embedded vendored dirs are all unpinned and would already violate it). The failing test's real job is content/version drift (re-sync when reveal.js bumps), and it was over-strict: byte-eq where it meant content-eq. Line endings were noise in a drift test.

Fix shipped: vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package now normalizes CRLF->LF on both sides before comparing (crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs). Removes the false-positive at its source with zero per-file .gitattributes maintenance and no need for a coverage guardrail. Verified TDD on Windows: converted the 4 vendored files to CRLF (simulating a core.autocrlf checkout) -> test RED on EOL; added the normalize -> GREEN with the CRLF files still on disk; restored files to LF. Full revealjs module 108/108 green.

Companion finding (SCSS, the original worry that prompted the review): user-CRLF SCSS mixed with internal-LF SCSS is a non-issue. It is normalized twice already -- q2's parse_layer() strips CRLF (layer.rs:112, with a test at :407-427 and a comment matching this same 'SCSS keeps no byte-offset map' reasoning) and grass's lexer collapses CRLF/CR/form-feed to LF at the char level before parsing (grass_compiler 0.13.4 lexer.rs:128-146; empirically confirmed on windows-msvc: 8 CR in -> 0 CR out, expanded + compressed). No SCSS change needed.

c-b25l7gtk.author: cderv
c-b25l7gtk.text:
Root cause confirmed: REAL cross-platform build bug, not a test-only artifact.

resources/revealjs/{reset.css,reveal.css,reveal.js,theme/white.css,quarto-reveal.css}
are pulled in via include_str! at crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs:29-35,
embedded verbatim into the compiled binary as artifact content served by both
`q2 render` and `q2 preview` (assemble.rs:817-824 explicitly asserts they are NOT
inlined into HTML - they ship as separate served files, byte-for-byte from the
constant). Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true (default) rewrites these
committed-LF files to CRLF on disk; a Windows-built q2 binary then embeds
different bytes than a Linux/Mac-built binary for the same source tree. This
breaks build reproducibility across platforms, which is exactly the invariant
the failing test asserts ("q2 render and q2 preview must use identical reveal
assets").

Web research (per codebase-research.md "research ecosystem precedent" rule):
include_str! deliberately does NOT normalize line endings. rust-lang/rust#63681
proposed \r\n -> \n normalization in include_str! and was REJECTED by the lang
team - rationale: include_str! is used to embed non-Rust binary-sensitive
content (Windows batch files needing literal \r\n, JSON/YAML, hash/signature
payloads), so any implicit conversion is unacceptable breakage. Official
position: fix line-ending consistency at the git-checkout boundary
(.gitattributes), not inside the macro or the consuming code.

This confirms our fix is the ecosystem-canonical answer, and matches existing
repo precedent for the exact same failure class:
- crates/pampa/.gitattributes (test fixtures/snapshots)
- crates/quarto-citeproc/.gitattributes (CSL conformance lockfile, same
  byte-compare-against-generated-string shape as this bug)
- crates/quarto-doctemplate/.gitattributes (template fixtures)

Fix applied (uncommitted, awaiting go-ahead per CLAUDE.md push policy):
- Added to root .gitattributes: `resources/revealjs/** text eol=lf`
  (pins the whole vendored reveal.js asset dir - covers all 5 files consumed
  by include_str!, plus reset-scoped.css/LICENSE/README for consistency,
  though those aren't currently embedded).
- `git add .gitattributes && git add --renormalize resources/revealjs`
  staged with ZERO content diff vs HEAD for the resources/ files - confirms
  the committed blobs were already LF (npm-sourced); only the Windows
  checkout conversion was ever wrong. Nothing to fix upstream in the blobs
  themselves.
- `git restore --worktree` did NOT rewrite the already-present CRLF files
  (git skipped write, presumably because content hash matched cached stat).
  Had to `rm` the 5 files (including theme/white.css, easy to miss on first
  pass) + `git checkout --` to force a fresh smudge-filtered checkout to LF.
- Verified: `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package`
  passes. Full `revealjs::` module (62 tests) passes.

State at handoff:
- Only `.gitattributes` is staged (+7 lines). resources/revealjs/* show
  no git diff (expected - see above). NOT committed, NOT pushed.
- Still needed before commit per CLAUDE.md: cargo build --workspace,
  cargo nextest run --workspace, cargo xtask verify (at least
  --skip-hub-build, since quarto-core is on the WASM dependency path -
  wasm-quarto-hub-client also include_str!s nothing extra here but consumes
  quarto-core, so the hub-build leg is worth including if time allows).
- No other test/snapshot found referencing these constants' literal bytes
  (grepped for .snap files under revealjs - none; hub-client only
  string-references "resources/revealjs" in comments, no embed).
- This strand sits under the line-ending epic (bd-eehxwr29) as a
  parent-child, but is a DISTINCT mechanism from that epic's document-
  processing-engine CRLF work (qmd source preservation) - this is a
  vendored-build-asset reproducibility bug, fixed purely at the git
  attributes layer, no q2 code changes.

title: Migrate postprocess.rs hull sites off preimage_in onto the map_offset pair
description:
Q2-side. Discovered while executing Plan 3 Phase 2
(claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-3-audit-and-fix.md), which is comments-only, so
the code change was deliberately deferred here rather than made in that phase.

LATENT, NOT BROKEN. The provenance audit
(claude-notes/research/2026-08-21-provenance-audit-findings.md) section 4 triages all
three sites as "safe by shape, but a drift amplifier". Nothing misbehaves today. This is
an accessor-discipline migration, not a bug fix -- schedule it accordingly.

THE SITES (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs)
  hull_source_infos                  -- SourceInfo::original(f1, s, e)               ~:317
  contiguous_hull_for_run            -- SourceInfo::original(fid, .., ..)            ~:669
  math_with_attr_span_source_info    -- SourceInfo::original(fid, math_start, attr_end + 1) ~:1833
(Line numbers drifted when Phase 2 added doc comments; find them by function name.)

THE DISCIPLINE THEY VIOLATE
Findings section 1 states the rule flatly: file id -> root_file_id(); positions ->
map_offset; A HULL -> THE map_offset(0) / map_offset(length()) PAIR; never preimage_in for
a hull. All three sites use preimage_in to build a hull.

Why the rule exists: on a Concat, preimage_in returns an OFFSET CLAIM, not a byte-identity
claim -- see quarto-source-map-0.1.3/src/source_info.rs:410-457, "a Some(hull) licenses
locating a position in target -- it does not license copying bytes from it". These sites
then flatten that offsets-only answer into a SourceInfo::original, which reads downstream
(notably the writer's Verbatim-copy decision) as BOTH. Separately, since 0.1.2 preimage_in
REFUSES (returns None) for a Substring over a Concat, so these sites silently take their
coarse combine() fallback in cases where the map_offset pair would have produced a tight
hull.

WHY IT IS SAFE TODAY
Section 4's verdict is about the inputs these functions are reached with today, not a
property of the flattening. Each site falls back to a lossless combine() when preimage_in
declines, so the failure mode is coarsening rather than a wrong span. That is what makes
this latent.

SCOPE OF THE WORK
Replace the preimage_in hull arithmetic with the map_offset(0)/map_offset(length()) pair
at all three sites, keeping the combine() fallbacks. Note that map_offset returns a
position, so the end of the hull is map_offset(length()) -- read findings section 1 before
starting.

EXPECT SNAPSHOT MOVEMENT, and budget for it. This is the reason it was kept out of a
comments-only phase: the sites are on pampa's live tree-sitter postprocess path (list-table
cells, caption-extended table spans, abbreviation coalescing, math-with-attribute spans),
pampa has 212 .snap files, and tightening a hull that previously coarsened to combine()
changes emitted spans. Per CLAUDE.md, report the count, summarize what changed, and flag
anything surprising.

DO THIS SEPARATELY, AND FIRST IF BOTH ARE SCHEDULED
math_with_attr_span_source_info also hardcodes `attr_end + 1` on the unchecked assumption
that the closing '}' is the next raw byte. Phase 2 recorded that in the code but did not
fix it. It interacts with this migration -- if attr_end stops being a raw-source coordinate
the +1 lands somewhere else -- so re-derive it from the closing delimiter's own span if
that becomes reachable, rather than carrying the arithmetic across the migration.

title: Listing sort: allow sorting by arbitrary front-matter fields, not just built-ins
description:
Q2's listing sort (crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/sort.rs:117) only accepts a fixed set of built-in fields: title, subtitle, description, author, date, date-modified, image, image-alt, filename, path, output-href, reading-time, word-count.

Q1 supports sorting by arbitrary front-matter field names. Without this, a listing of pages with custom front-matter (e.g. error-doc pages with 'code', 'subsystem', 'status' fields) can only sort by the built-ins — losing the natural sort axes the document author defined.

Repro: any qmd with 'sort: code' (where 'code' is a front-matter field) emits 'Warning [Q-12-3]: Unknown sort field code; values will compare as equal.'

Workaround: sort by 'filename' if the filename encodes the sort key. Brittle but works for our error-doc pages where filenames are e.g. Q-1-10.qmd (sorts ~mostly correctly, though alphanumeric not numeric: Q-1-10 comes before Q-1-2).

Discovered while authoring docs/errors/index.qmd as part of bd-nvlxn (error-docs foundation).

c-yoapj1df.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-yoapj1df.text: Widening evidence from bd-wcmk1fsq (2026-08-18). This strand is filed as a *sort* limitation, but the root cause is broader and the user-visible damage is already live. ROOT CAUSE IS ONE GAP, NOT TWO. Top-level front-matter keys never reach ListingItem at all. `item.extra` is populated only from an explicit `listing-item: extra:` block (crates/quarto-core/src/document_profile.rs:200-213, 'Authors populate this struct via a top-level listing-item: key'). Both resolvers fall through to that same map: - sort key: crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/sort.rs:117 `_ => item.extra.get(field)` - table column: crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/binding.rs:586 `_ => extra_field_value(&item.extra, field)` So a bare `code:` key is invisible to sorting AND to display. LIVE SYMPTOM ON THE DOCS SITE. docs/errors/index.qmd declares `fields: [code, title, subsystem, status]`. In docs/_site/errors/index.html all 207 rows render Code, Subsystem and Status as EMPTY cells; only Title (a built-in) appears. No filter-ui, sort-ui or category markup is emitted either. The error reference's 'canonical browse surface' is a table with 3 of 4 columns blank. E2E REPRO (scratch project, 6 pages, top-level `code:`, `sort: code`): Warning [Q-12-3]: Unknown sort field `code`; values will compare as equal. code ... <- empty cell order: Q-1-1, Q-1-10, Q-1-11, Q-1-2, Q-1-20, Q-1-3 Adding `listing-item: extra: {code, subsystem}` fixes the columns and silences Q-12-3, confirming the diagnosis. Q1 PARITY. Q1 merges the whole merged document metadata into the item with no allowlist -- website-listing-read.ts:1184-1187 `const item: ListingItem = { ...documentMeta, ... }`, and `ListingItem extends Record` (website-listing-shared.ts:210). Arbitrary fields are both sortable and displayable there (item-default.ejs.md otherFields loop; listing-table.ejs.md renders every `fields` entry). So merging top-level front matter into ListingItem is genuine Q1 parity and fixes the empty columns as well as the sort key. DO NOT ADD A NUMERIC-AWARE BUILD-TIME COMPARATOR. Tempting, because sorting Q-1-10 after Q-1-2 is what the error index actually needs -- but Q1 does not have one. Q1's build-time sort is lodash orderBy -> plain relational operators (lodash@4.17.21/_compareAscending.js:23,30); no localeCompare, no {numeric:true}. Verified empirically: Q1 also yields Q-1-1, Q-1-10, Q-1-11, Q-1-2. Q1's only numeric-aware sort is CLIENT-side (List.js string-natural-compare), interaction-only, so even Q1's first paint is lexicographic. Adding one to Q2 would be deliberate divergence and should be argued separately, not folded in here. CONSEQUENCE FOR SCOPE: fixing this strand fixes the empty columns but NOT code-number ordering. The workaround for ordering in both Quartos is a hand-maintained numeric `order:` per page, which Gordon rejected as not worth a redundant integer field (2026-08-18). So the error index stays in filename order for now; bd-wcmk1fsq backfilled the sidebar and added an `error-docs-sidebar-unlisted` lint rule that deliberately does not police order.

title: q2 preview: persist React-preview edits back to the source .qmd on disk (--write flag)
description: Edits made via the inline block-editing surface (PR #260) in the q2-preview SPA currently stop at the in-browser WASM VFS and are lost on the next sync event. Route them into the per-file Automerge document so the existing quarto-hub fork-and-merge sync (sync_document, 5s periodic + final sync_all on SIGINT) persists them to the .qmd on disk. Gated by a new opt-in CLI flag --allow-edit; when absent the preview is fully read-only (editingDisabled threaded through Q2PreviewIframe/PreviewContext suppresses the edit affordance entirely), and HubConfig.disk_write_back gates the merged-content disk write in sync.rs as server-side defense in depth. SPA learns the flag via GET /api/preview/config. Includes moving the pure diffToEditorChanges helper from hub-client into ts-packages/preview-runtime. Design agreed 2026-06-10; full analysis and phased TDD work items: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-10-q2-preview-edit-writeback.md
close_reason: Implemented and verified: q2 preview --allow-edit persists React-preview block edits to the source .qmd via the per-file Automerge doc + existing fork-and-merge sync; without the flag the preview is fully read-only (no affordance, DiskWritePolicy::ReadOnly server-side). E2E verified in the real binary; Carlos tested and approved. Merged to main as a --no-ff merge. Follow-ups: bd-g4uw7d8g (eager sync), bd-f8d753iq (automated e2e).

title: Q-12-24 EJS sniff: no escape hatch for a doctemplate that legitimately prints `<%`, and resolver-pulled partials are not sniffed
description: Two sides of one gap in the Q-12-24 check (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/listing_render.rs, check_custom_template_is_templated). (a) The `<%` content sniff runs over the raw top-level template source, so a custom listing template that legitimately emits a literal `<%` (e.g. a listing of EJS code samples) is flagged and skipped, and Q-12-24.qmd documents no way around it. (b) The sniff covers only `custom.source`; partial bodies pulled in by the FileSystemResolver are never sniffed, so a half-ported sibling partial still holding `<% … %>` renders the EJS unflagged. (b) is also the de-facto escape hatch for (a) — resolve both together, not separately. Candidate: sniff resolved partials too, and offer an explicit opt-out (e.g. a doctemplate comment marker) documented on the Q-12-24 page. Flagged by the final review of bd-custom-template-not-templated-e5t6m0i0 (2026-08-25); decisions 1/6 on that strand (skip; sniff) were settled with Gordon and are not to be re-litigated here.

title: Wire hub-client lint:css into CI
description: lint:css is referenced by design-system.md as the token/physical-prop enforcement, but no GitHub workflow runs it (grep of .github/workflows finds nothing). ConnectionStatusDialog.css landed 2026-08-27 (5d31edf6b) with 9 violations one day after the lint rule itself merged (c8115e9ca, #605) because nothing gated on it. title: Diagnose unsupported EJS listing templates (Q2 uses doctemplate)
description:
Q2 deliberately does not support Q1 EJS listing templates -- doctemplate replaced EJS so untrusted contexts (hub-client) never execute arbitrary JS. But nothing tells the user that.

Today, a listing with `type: custom` + a Q1 `.ejs` template renders the raw EJS into the output HTML with NO diagnostic at all:

  $ cargo run --bin q2 -- render index.qmd
  $ grep -o '<%[^>]*' index.html
  <% for (const item of items) { %
  <%- item.path %
  <%= item.title %

load_custom_template (quarto-core/src/transforms/listing_render.rs:355-401) reads any file that exists; doctemplate does not recognize <% ... %> as markup, so it passes through verbatim. Q-12-9 only matches the `.ejs.md` suffix, not plain `.ejs`.

Scope: detect EJS at load time by extension (.ejs, .ejs.md) AND by content sniff (<% / %>) -- the sniff catches the renamed-but-not-ported file, exactly the trap a user falls into partway through a migration. Emit a warning and fall back to the built-in default, matching Q-12-8/Q-12-14 (decision: user agreed with plan design question Q3). Point the message at the EJS -> doctemplate porting guide (bd-hzsi).

Open: new code (Q-12-15) vs widening Q-12-9. Q-12-9's current framing is 'deprecated extension'; the real problem is 'unsupported template language'.

Context: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-06-q12-7-listing-template-diagnostic.md

Decisions carried over and revised there: detection is an AST 'no directives' check plus the `<%` content sniff proposed here; degraded behaviour is SKIP (Q-12-10 precedent), reversing the fall-back-to-default decision recorded here; new code is Q-12-24 (Q-12-15 was taken in the meantime) and Q-12-9 is widened to `.ejs` with a 'Quarto 1 EJS template' framing. title: preview parity: callout drops title= and data-appearance= attributes
description:
Fixtures: quarto-test/callout-title-attribute.qmd (render outer div has `title="Off-Host Execution"`), quarto-test/callouts-matrix.qmd (render has `data-appearance="simple"`).

## Evidence (callout-title-attribute.qmd)

render.norm.txt:
```
<div class="callout callout-style-default callout-note callout-titled" title="Off-Host Execution">
```

preview.norm.txt:
```
<div class="callout callout-style-default callout-note callout-titled">
```

## Evidence (callouts-matrix.qmd)

survey.json firstDiff (line 79):
```
render:  <div class="callout callout-style-simple callout-tip callout-titled" data-appearance="simple">
preview: <div class="callout callout-style-simple callout-tip callout-titled">
```

## Root cause

The Rust side forwards the *entire original user-authored Div attr* (id, classes, and all kvs — including arbitrary ones like `title=` or `data-appearance=` that the user wrote directly on the `::: {.callout-note title="..." data-appearance="simple"}` fence) verbatim through to the final rendered div:
- `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/callout.rs:299` — `CustomNode::new("Callout", div.attr.clone(), div.source_info.clone())` clones the full original `Attr` (id, classes, kvs) onto the CustomNode.
- `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/callout_resolve.rs:310` (`let (orig_id, orig_classes, orig_attrs) = &custom.attr;`) and `:316` (`let outer_attr: Attr = (orig_id.clone(), classes, orig_attrs.clone());`) forward `orig_attrs` (the kvs) onto the final outer `Div`'s attr, which the HTML writer emits verbatim.

React's `ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/custom/Callout.tsx` never reads `node.attr[2]` (the kvs) at all — it only reads `node.attr[0]` (id, at line 159) and builds its own `classList` from `plain_data` (lines 150-157). Any user-authored kv on the callout's attr (title=, data-appearance=, or anything else) is silently dropped.

Fix should end with `dom-parity: true` on the fixture(s). Found by the DOM parity harness (whole-corpus survey, 2026-08-24). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-preview-render-dom-parity-harness.md

title: resource_error_to_parse_error binds wrong file for extension-contributed project.resources
description: crates/quarto-core/src/project_resources.rs:864 resource_error_to_parse_error() unconditionally registers source_file (the project _quarto.yml) under whatever FileId the diagnostic's SourceInfo resolves to. project.resources can be contributed by an extension via contributes.metadata.project (FRAGMENT_PATH_PATTERNS includes [project, resources]), in which case the FileId is the hash of the extension's _extension.yml path and the resulting Q-5-1/Q-5-x snippet renders _quarto.yml content at the extension file's byte offsets (misleading span), or drops the snippet when offsets exceed the file. title: page-footer item text: a lone image is dropped, and no link or image target inside it is resolved
description:
q2 parses a page-footer item's text: as markdown — bold, emphasis, code and links all render. Two things then go wrong independently, neither of which warns. DEFECT 1 — AN ITEM WHOSE text: IS A LONE IMAGE RENDERS EMPTY text: '![lone image](/images/logo.svg)' ->
  • text: '![lone image, relative](images/logo.svg)' ->
  • text: '[![wrapped in a link](images/logo.svg)](https://x)' -> text: '![image](images/logo.svg) beside text' -> beside text An image that is the item's only content disappears; wrap it in a link, or put any other inline beside it, and it survives. Two-step mechanism. with_paragraph in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs desugars a single-image paragraph into a Figure. Then block_inlines in crates/quarto-navigation/src/render_html.rs — how render_text gets inlines out of a parsed-markdown ConfigValue — matches only Plain, Paragraph and Header and returns None for everything else, Figure included, so render_text yields the empty string. Any sibling inline keeps the block a Paragraph, which is exactly why the workarounds work. A footer item is an inline context, so the fix is presumably to unwrap the Figure back to its image rather than to teach block_inlines about figure captions. DEFECT 2 — NOTHING INSIDE AN ITEM'S text: IS RESOLVED Not only images and not only root-absolute paths: no Link or Image target inside an item's text: is rewritten at all. The control is a REGION-level text: carrying the identical markdown, in the same footer of the same render, on a page two directories deep: page-footer.center: '![x](/images/logo.svg) … [y](/index.qmd)' -> src="../../images/logo.svg" href="../../index.html" resolved page-footer.right[0].text: (the same string) -> src="/images/logo.svg" href="/index.qmd" untouched The region-level side rebases the path AND rewrites .qmd to .html. The item-level side does neither, so every such reference 404s on any page below the site root. crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/footer_render.rs shows why, and that the intent was the opposite. Its call site is commented "Rewrite hrefs in each Items region, and Link/Image targets inside Text regions' parsed markdown (bd-root-relative-paths-design-fc5pvkcv, Case C — the AST body's Phase-6 rewriter never sees footer inlines, which live in metadata, so this transform owns their resolution)". rewrite_region_hrefs then splits: FooterRegion::Text(cv) -> rewrite_config_inlines(...) walks inlines, rewrites both node kinds FooterRegion::Items(items) -> rewrite_items_hrefs(...) touches item.href, recurses into item.menu, never looks at item.text So the machinery exists and is invoked one branch over; item text was never routed through it. The fix looks like running rewrite_config_inlines over each item's text inlines inside rewrite_items_hrefs, symmetrically with the menu recursion already there. NO DIAGNOSTIC, AND THE ASYMMETRY EXTENDS TO THEM. An identically broken reference in the document body raises Q-5-6 "Referenced resource not found" — the repro's footer items point at exactly the same missing file and the render is clean, exit 0. REAL-WORLD HIT The Posit Connect documentation is served from https://docs.posit.co/connect/, a subdirectory, and its _quarto.yml page-footer carries four tags — two Posit logos and two cookie-preferences icons — with src="/images/…". They reach all 352 rendered pages verbatim and resolve outside the site in production. Quarto 1's rendered output for the same sources contains zero root-absolute paths, because its deno-dom post-render pass rewrites the emitted HTML; q2 deliberately has no such pass, which is the subject of bd-root-relative-paths-design-fc5pvkcv. Defect 2 is what makes that port's obvious workaround fail. The plan was to move those four tags out of raw HTML into markdown images, the form q2 owns and can resolve. Measured, that does not help: as markdown they are either dropped (defect 1) or left unrebased (defect 2), which is no better than the raw HTML they would replace. Unlike the raw-HTML case, these are ordinary Image AST nodes q2 already holds, so this one is fixable without parsing HTML — fixing it would let that project's footer be correct without a post-render rewrite step. Filed P2 to match the origin strand, but worth noting it is the blocker under a P1 there. REPRO /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/page-footer-image-items/ Run `q2 render` and read _site/deep/deeper/index.html, a page two directories down where a correct path has to read ../../images/logo.svg. The footer's center region is the region-level control, right is the item-level comparison, and left holds the five lone-image variants. README.md has both tables. Caveat recorded there: _site-q1/ is NOT a control for defect 1. The Quarto 1 dev build used (99.9.9) does not parse footer text: as markdown at all, emitting the literal ![…](…) source, so it has no opinion on how a lone image should render; released Q1 behaves differently again, since the frozen Connect docs render shows its footer images working. For defect 2 it IS a clean control, and a pointed one — Q1 rewrote src="/images/logo.svg" to ../../images/logo.svg inside a string it was otherwise emitting literally. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-page-footer-image-items-sjto1juf. Observed with q2 0.23.0; q2 origin/main at 3c60bd80 has nothing touching either defect.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #551 (merged 2026-08-19): lone-image items render via the lone-Figure unwrap; item text: Link/Image targets resolve on all three nav surfaces; blocks-shaped config text rewrites and renders; missing footer images raise spanned Q-5-6 once per project. Follow-ups: bd-70krno7a, bd-0jo6fnb7.

title: Navigation item text: is HTML-escaped; bare-string page-footer item becomes an empty link
description:
WHAT HAPPENS. Navigation item `text:` written in `_quarto.yml` is HTML-escaped instead of rendered, and a bare-string page-footer item is treated as a file path rather than display text. Five defects, none of which emits a warning: 1. `text:` is escaped, so markup shows as literal text — `<img src="logo.svg"…>` where Quarto 1 renders the image. 2. A bare-string footer item ("- Copyright © 2015-… All Rights Reserved.") is placed in `href=` with an EMPTY link body, so the text is invisible and the item is an unusable link. Q1 renders it as plain
  • text. 3. Shortcodes are not evaluated in item strings — `{{< env CURRENT_YEAR >}}` stays literal. 4. Named entities are not resolved there either — `©`. 5. An item with `text:` but no `href:` is still wrapped in ``. Q1 emits no wrapping anchor for a href-less item. Once (1) is fixed, the common cookie-preferences pattern (markup carrying its own ) would produce NESTED ANCHORS, which is invalid HTML — so (5) wants fixing in the same pass as (1), not later. NOT PAGE-FOOTER-SPECIFIC. The same `text:` field is escaped identically in the navbar and the sidebar; the repro covers all three. page-footer item text: q2 `Copyright © <b>bold</b> *emph* {{< env … >}}` Q1 `Copyright © bold emph 2026` navbar item text: escaped identically Q1 `Navbar © bold emph 2026` sidebar item text: escaped identically Q1 `Sidebar © *emph*` — entity resolved, markdown NOT parsed Note the last row: Q1 itself does not parse markdown in sidebar item text, only entities. Worth matching deliberately rather than assuming the three regions behave alike. Also note that `page-footer.center` already works today — markdown, raw HTML, entities and shortcodes all correct — so two regions of the same feature currently disagree. WHERE IT LIVES. Two independent causes, one per symptom group. Defects 1, 3, 4 are an INTERPRETATION problem, not a rendering one. The renderer is already correct: render_text in crates/quarto-navigation/src/render_html.rs (~line 691) walks ConfigValueKind::PandocInlines and only escapes when the value is a literal scalar. The problem is that item `text:` arrives as a literal scalar. Untagged strings take a context-dependent default in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs (yaml_to_config_value, ~line 222): DocumentMetadata parses as markdown, ProjectConfig keeps the literal. A `_quarto.yml` is ProjectConfig, so item `text:` stays literal. The fix mechanism already sits between those two branches: crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta_annotations.rs holds a per-key-path annotation table (ANNOTATIONS, bd-v7ixzsp5 / GH #456) that overrides the untagged default. It currently has two entries, both for listing.contents, and its module docs ask for "one entry per key whose misinterpretation is an actual observed bug". This is one. Proof that interpretation is the whole story for 1/3/4: tagging the identical string `!md` makes q2 render it correctly — `Tagged © 2026 emph 2026`. The repro ships that as a separate control project. Nothing in the renderer needs to change for those three. Defects 2 and 5 are the item model and the footer renderer. NavigationItem::from_config_value in crates/quarto-navigation/src/item.rs (~line 76) treats any bare scalar as a FILE PATH and stores it in href with text: None — right for navbars and sidebars, where `- about.qmd` means "link to this page", wrong for page-footer regions, where Q1 treats a bare string as display text. enrich_navigation_items (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_enrich.rs) would normally fill text from the project index, but a copyright sentence matches no document, so text stays None and the anchor body is empty. render_footer_item (render_html.rs ~line 674) then emits `
  • …
    • ` unconditionally, defaulting href to "#" when absent — defect 5. SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION. 1. Add annotation entries for navigation item text so untagged strings are interpreted as markdown regardless of config context — the footer/navbar `text` key paths (website.page-footer.left.text and siblings). Mind that table's path semantics: array elements are transparent, map fields are not, so an item record's field is at `…left.text`. Decide deliberately whether the sidebar joins them, given Q1 parses no markdown there. 2. Teach the footer path that a bare scalar is text, not a path. A footer-specific constructor (or a flag on from_config_value) is cleaner than changing the shared bare-scalar rule that navbars and sidebars depend on. 3. In render_footer_item, emit the label directly in the
  • when the item has no href, instead of wrapping it in ``. REAL-WORLD HIT (Posit Connect docs). All 352 pages. Its `_quarto.yml` puts the Posit logo (two variants for light/dark) and the cookie-preferences control in page-footer items, and the copyright line as a bare string. Under q2 the footer shows raw `` markup as literal text on the left, an empty link where the copyright line belongs, and raw `…` markup on the right. Every page, on the most-seen chrome on the site. REPRO. /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/page-footer-items/ — run `REPRO_YEAR=2026 q2 render` there and compare with `REPRO_YEAR=2026 quarto render --output-dir _site-q1`. The config covers all five defects plus a working `center:` control and the navbar/sidebar spread; README.md has expected vs actual markup side by side and the analysis above. The `!md` control is a separate project at md-tag-control/ because Quarto 1 rejects the q2-only !md tag and would refuse to parse a config containing it. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-l6zngxfr. Observed with q2 0.16.0 and re-verified failing on 0.17.0 / origin/main @ 001cb6a5.

title: Fix Windows path-separator assumptions in pampa quarto_api path tests
description: On Windows, ~10 tests in crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_api.rs (test_normalize_path_simple, test_normalize_path_with_dots, test_normalize_path_with_dotdot, test_normalize_path_with_dotdot_at_root, test_normalize_path_relative, test_normalize_path_relative_with_dotdot, test_quarto_utils_resolve_path_relative, test_quarto_utils_resolve_path_relative_with_subdir, test_quarto_utils_resolve_path_with_dotdot, test_script_dir_stack_resolve_path_uses_top) fail because expected paths are hardcoded with forward slashes ('/some/extension/dir/data.json') while the Windows implementation joins with backslashes via Path::join. Different category from bd-3pe8 (PR #95) which fixed Lua source-string path interpolation; these are output-comparison failures. Need to decide: (a) normalize quarto.utils.resolve_path output to forward slashes in production (matches quarto-cli pathWithForwardSlashes convention), or (b) write tests with platform-correct expectations using PathBuf::join. Surfaced 2026-04-28 while running cargo nextest -p pampa on Windows. Same set of tests run twice (library + bin/pampa integration), so 18-20 visible failures from one root cause.
close_reason: Merged via PR #340

c-gwq9f1qy.author: cderv
c-gwq9f1qy.text: Fresh investigation 2026-06-24: reframed. Root cause is normalize_path/resolve_path emitting native separators (backslashes on Windows). Functionally NATIVE Windows is fine (io.open/fs::read/dofile accept backslashes); failure is test-assertion only. WASM already forward-slash. Separately found latent bug: resolve_path uses p.is_absolute() at quarto_api.rs:360, but codebase convention (bd-vxl8) is quarto_util::is_rooted() because is_absolute() misfires on wasm32 for /project VFS paths. No current caller triggers it (extension lua uses relative names). Canonical helper to_forward_slashes exists in quarto-util. Recommend production normalize (option a) + is_rooted swap, not cfg-gated test expectations (option b). Pending design alignment.

title: Subfloat support: parent/child crossref ids and nested numbering (Figure 1a)
description:
Deferred by design in claude-notes/plans/2026-04-15-crossref-design.md (see its two "Subfloats deferred" paragraphs, lines 77 and 405), which says the work "needs its own plan" / "gets its own follow-up plan". That plan was never written and no strand existed, so this is it. Parented to bd-jsbg (the crossref epic that owns that design plan).

WHAT IS MISSING. Parent/child id assignment, nested numbering ("Figure 1a"), and fig.subplots-style engine output. Q1 reference per the design plan: src/resources/filters/quarto-pre/parsefiguredivs.lua:41-60.

CONFIRMED DORMANT, not partially working (verified 2026-09-18 while prevalidating test seams for the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic):
- CrossrefEntry.parent exists and is documented — crates/quarto-core/src/crossref/index.rs:97, "For subfloats: the identifier of the parent float. None for top-level".
- It is only ever set to None — crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/crossref_index.rs:304, literally `parent: None, // subfloats deferred`.
- It has ZERO readers. Grepping `.parent` across crates/quarto-core/src/crossref/ and the crossref transforms returns no consumers at all.
So the struct anticipates subfloats and nothing populates or reads the field. Same shape as the sibling `in_appendix: false, // deferred` on the adjacent line.

WHY IT SURFACED NOW (context, not scope). The pandoc-hybrid epic's P6 plan (Finding 5) argued that nested subfloats inside a Route-R Tabset would "get the same treatment for free", because Q1's customnodes/floatreftarget.lua:221 calls prependSubrefNumber(caption_content, float.order) and reads .order generically off whatever table it is handed. Reading the surrounding branch shows it is reached only for a float Q1 recognizes as a SUBfloat, which requires a parent. Since no Q2-produced wire node can ever carry a parent link, that branch is unreachable from Q2 — so any Tabset-containing-subfloat fixture exercises top-level numbering of a nested figure, never subfloat lettering. P6's Finding 5 has been re-scoped to say "dormant", matching its own verdict on the adjacent in_appendix case, and references this strand.

NOT part of the pandoc-hybrid epic. Per CLAUDE.md's braid-vs-plans rule this is out-of-plan work: subfloat support is a feature none of that epic's eight plans implements, and the epic's Pandoc leg would inherit it for free once the wire format carries a parent (Q1's Lua side already handles subfloats). Deliberately NOT added to any plan checklist.

RELATED, for whoever picks this up: claude-notes/designs/float-layout-class-taxonomy.md already specifies the intended HTML surface for subfloats — line 55-56 (subfloats swap quarto-float-<ref> to quarto-subfloat-<ref>, caption gains quarto-subfloat-caption), line 74 (quarto-layout-cell-subref), and line 131 (data-qf-subfloat keyed on float.parent_id ~= nil). So the presentation contract is designed; it is the index/numbering half that is missing.

title: annotated-qmd: stale published metadata and vestigial package-lock.json

title: Named footnote refs [^id] never resolve (Span.quarto-note-reference left unresolved)
description:
Named/reference-style footnotes [^id] with a block definition (::: ^id ... :::) never resolve in ANY format, including plain format: html (not reveal-specific). Repro: --- format: html --- Ref.[^bk] ::: ^bk Note. ::: Output: (unresolved); the def text is collected/removed but the ref is never turned into a footnote. Root cause: pampa's parser postprocess (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:1134-1146) converts the parsed reference into an Inline::Span(class=quarto-note-reference, kv reference-id=) with EMPTY content during parsing, before any quarto-core transform runs. But FootnotesTransform (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/footnotes.rs) only resolves the typed Inline::NoteReference variant (process_inline's NoteReference arm) — it never looks at Span.quarto-note-reference. collect_note_definitions DOES collect the NoteDefinitionFencedBlock/Para (so the def is removed from the body), but resolve_reference is never called for the Span form, so the ref renders unresolved and the collected definition is silently dropped. The inline ^[...] form works because it parses directly to Inline::Note, which FootnotesTransform handles. Likely fix: either (a) have FootnotesTransform treat Span.quarto-note-reference[reference-id] the same as Inline::NoteReference (collect order, resolve, replace), or (b) convert Span.quarto-note-reference back to Inline::NoteReference before FootnotesTransform. Pre-existing comment acknowledging the gap: crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:2312-2320 ('Nothing downstream resolves those Spans ... pre-existing gap'). Distinct from bd-1kly (which is reference-location: block/section numbering). Impact on revealjs 2e-ii (bd-9aknlx1j): per-slide footnote coalescing consumes FootnotesTransform's resolved output, so it already coalesces inline ^[...] footnotes correctly; once [^id] refs resolve to the standard Span#fnref form, they will coalesce automatically with no further reveal work. TDD: add a failing plain-html test (Ref.[^id] + ::: ^id ->
/ fnref) first.
close_reason: Fixed and merged via PR #264 — named footnote refs [^id] now resolve through FootnotesTransform.

title: Per-project capture cache for cross-session reuse
description:
Phase C.7 (bd-kw93.7) shipped the per-doc capture filesystem cache in <data_dir>/captures/ — the same tempdir that gets deleted when q2 preview exits. So closing and re-opening preview against the same project always misses the cache, even though the inputs are bit-for-bit identical.

A per-project cache location (e.g. <project_root>/.q2/captures/, ignored by .gitignore convention) would unlock cross-session reuse. The cache key derivation (sha256 of canonical input_qmd) is already content-addressed and survives across sessions — only the directory choice changes.

Considerations:
- Where: <project_root>/.q2/captures/? Some equivalent under XDG_CACHE_HOME keyed on project root? Discuss before implementing.
- Cleanup: with content-hashed keys, old entries pile up across edits. A simple LRU sweep, or just letting the OS / git ignore handle it.
- Gitignore: cache should not be committed. Either add a .q2/.gitignore on first write or document.
- Concurrency: two q2 preview instances against the same project would race on the cache. Write atomicity is already last-writer-wins (atomic rename); concurrent readers handle a missing file gracefully.
- Sandboxing: the existing loopback-only posture still applies.

See plan §C.7 'Open follow-up'.

title: exit-drain test times out on main since automerge-repo 2.6.0-alpha.5 (TS Test Suite red)
description:
TS Test Suite has failed on every push to main since PR #685 (automerge npm upgrade, bd-d08gpqvu) merged: runs 35245424175 (macos leg) and 35249754405 (ubuntu leg). Failing test: ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp/src/exit-drain.test.ts > 'create_project then immediate stdin EOF must not lose the created docs' — vitest per-test timeout (30 s). PR #685's own CI passed at 19-26 s; on main the test takes 36-39 s. Before the upgrade it took 10-13 s on CI.

Diagnosis (same machine, same probe, dependency trees swapped; drain-to-exit ms per round, 64 x 64 KB files):
- automerge-repo 2.5.6 hub + 2.5.6 client: 1.7 / 2.0 / 4.6 s
- 2.6 hub + 2.5.6 client: 9.8 / 8.0 / 9.5 s
- 2.5.6 hub + 2.6 client: 7.4 / 22.8 / 26.2 s
- 2.6 hub + 2.6 client: 10.3 / 20.9 / 33.1 s
Checking the hub's repo directly shows the 64 docs only finish arriving ~13 s after create_project returns on the 2.6/2.6 tree; once they have landed the drain exits in <1 s. So this is raw sync throughput between two automerge-repo 2.6 JS peers, not a drain-signal bug. Zeroing saveDebounceRate on the test hub does not help.

Production relevance: against the real Rust hub (samod, target/debug/hub) the drain takes ~5.0 s with both the 2.5.6 and the 2.6 client — no regression observed. The slow path needs a JS automerge-repo peer as the *server*, which only the in-process startTestHub() stand-in is.

Options: (a) raise the per-test timeout for this one test (test already sets QUARTO_MCP_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS=30000 and waits up to 35 s for exit, both longer than the 30 s vitest timeout, so the hang-detector bound can never fire today — fix that inconsistency at the same time); (b) chase the throughput regression upstream in automerge-repo 2.6 (DocSynchronizer rewrite) and report it; (c) both. Not a candidate: shrinking the payload (see the measured floor in the test's header comment).
close_reason: Fixed by PR #691 (merged): exit-drain test budgets sized to automerge-repo 2.6 JS-to-JS sync throughput

display fence (the bd-knitr-inline-r-eats-fence-2ofk91x1 repro), at
claude-notes/plans/2026-08-25-r-display-fence-parse-error-investigation/fixture/
on branch braid/bd-knitr-inline-r-eats-fence-2ofk91x1-r-display-fence-parse-error.

    $ q2 render --debug
    Error: Parse error
         ,-[ .../fixture/index.knitr.rmarkdown:151:1 ]
     151 | ```r .QuartoInlineRender(pak::pak(c("usethis", "cli")))```
         | `-- unexpected character or token here
    exit=1

Everything left in the project directory afterwards, `--debug` included:

    ./.quarto/render-manifest.json
    ./.quarto/cache/profiles/4da5631da0a6e4d14a4d8705079c0d95ca473d15d3847223e18f333cc1c81e23

No `index.knitr.rmarkdown`, and nothing matching `*knitr*` anywhere under the
project. Note also that the cited line 151 is meaningless against a 15-line
source, so the line number gives the author nothing either.

## Why this is worth its own fix

It is what turns a merely-unhelpful error into an undiagnosable one. The
diagnosis is obvious *once you can see the intermediate* — the mangled fence
is right there on the cited line. Without the file there is no thread to pull:
the message is an uncoded "Parse error" (no Q- code, so no docs page to search
for) naming a path that does not exist.

Retaining the file is also far cheaper than the real fix for the error's
provenance, which is to map engine-error positions back to the source
document. That work is not this strand. A warning for whoever takes it on:
`ctx.source_info` is currently consumed only by the jupyter/ts engines and
never by knitr, and the knitr inline-R regex runs *after*
`serialize_ast_to_qmd` (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs:432),
so the `SourceInfo` handed to `ExecutionContext` describes the
pre-substitution string while knitr executes the post-substitution one —
every offset after a wrapped inline expression is short by the 21 bytes of
`.QuartoInlineRender()`. Harmless today because nothing reads it; a silent
bug the moment knitr is wired to that machinery.

## Suggested scope

Retain the intermediate under `--debug` when the engine's output fails to
parse (or, at minimum, print its path before deleting it). Scope is the debug
retention only — not the error code, not the source mapping.

## Related, deliberately not filed

Two sibling defects were surfaced in the same investigation and Gordon chose
not to file them (2026-08-25): the uncoded "Parse error" / no Q- code, and
```R rendering unhighlighted because
crates/quarto-highlight/src/registry.rs:148 registers ("r", &[]) with no
aliases and the lookup at :87 is an exact HashMap hit. Both are written up in
claude-notes/plans/2026-08-25-r-display-fence-parse-error.md.

title: Edit chrome (rich-text toolbar + standalone breadcrumb chip) cropped at top of viewport for a first/top block
description:
When the very first block of a title-less document (or any block scrolled near the viewport top) is edited, the floating rich-text toolbar — positioned absolute bottom:100% above the edit box — lands above the iframe viewport top (scrollTop already 0) and is cropped; only a sliver is visible. Applies to both the rich-text toolbar and the standalone breadcrumb chip. Measure-in-useLayoutEffect (mirrors the chip's existing geometry pattern); compute placement from the editor's stable top to avoid a flip/re-measure loop. title: Q-1-20 discards the underlying markdown diagnostic for config values (author sees only 'could not parse')
description:
When a config metadata value fails to parse as markdown, the author gets only the generic Q-1-20 'Failed to parse metadata value as markdown — Could not parse ... as markdown' (plus the !str hint), with a span onto the YAML. The underlying parser diagnostic — which explains WHAT is wrong with the markdown — is discarded. Observed with a page-footer text containing {width="65px" .light-content}: the same text in a document body produces Q-2-3 'Key-value Pair Before Class Specifier in Attribute' with a precise two-part span ('This key-value pair cannot appear before the class specifier' / 'This class specifier appears after the key-value pair'); as a config value it produces only the generic Q-1-20, so the author has no way to learn what to fix.

Root cause: crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs, parse_config_string_as_markdown (~lines 90–150 at origin/main 87c0e21a). The Err(_parse_errors) match arm receives the underlying diagnostics and discards them (the leading underscore says it), then builds a fresh generic message in both the !md-tagged (error) and untagged (warning) branches. The Ok arm one branch up already propagates recursive-parse warnings into the DiagnosticCollector, so the forwarding plumbing exists. Suggested fix: attach the underlying diagnostics — nested as details under Q-1-20, or emitted alongside it — with their spans remapped into the config file the way Q-1-20's own span already is (the parse is seeded with the scalar's SourceInfo, so the child spans should already be in config coordinates).

Why this matters for porting: Pandoc and Quarto 1 accept either attribute order, so kv-before-class is markdown that worked for years in Q1 configs; the stricter attribute grammar is a deliberate q2 decision (Q-2-3). Anyone porting a Q1 site hits that strictness *inside config values* and gets only 'could not parse'. Hit in practice while rewriting the Posit Connect docs footer logos from raw HTML to markdown images, where the first attempt naturally used Q1's attribute order and the render gave no clue why it would not parse.

Repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/q120-masks-config-md-diagnostic/ — q2 render shows both diagnostics in one run (Q-1-20 for the footer config, Q-2-3 for the identical text in body-control.qmd); quarto render --output-dir _site-q1 shows Q1 rendering the same footer fine. README states expected vs actual. Observed on q2 0.25.0. Origin strand in the q2-connect-docs skein: br-q120-masks-config-md-diagnostic-irbgj5ht.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 4e116ba5 (main): Err-path diagnostics reroot through parent_source_info in readers::qmd::read, and parse_yaml_string_as_markdown_to_config folds the child diagnostics into Q-1-20 as located details. Verified end-to-end on the committed repro fixture; full cargo xtask verify green.

title: Q-2-49's message drops links and emphasis from the quoted label: false 'reader sees' claim and a link-destroying remedy
description:
Q-2-49 ("bracketed text renders without its brackets") quotes the offending label back to the author and offers a rewrite. Both strings come from `label_text()` in `crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/reference_link_diagnostics.rs:137`, which keeps only `Str`, `Space` and `Code` inlines and maps everything else to the empty string:

    .map(|i| match i {
        Inline::Str(s)   => s.text.clone(),
        Inline::Space(_) => " ".to_string(),
        Inline::Code(c)  => c.text.clone(),
        _                => String::new(),   // Link, Emph, Strong, Math, RawInline, ...
    })

Any label containing a link, emphasis, or other non-text inline is therefore reported as if it were empty.

WHAT THE AUTHOR SEES

Source line:

    - [[#13991](https://example.com/13991), [#11772](https://example.com/11772)] Two links.

Reported:

    Warning: [Q-2-49] `[, ]` has no attribute block, so it renders as an empty
    span and the brackets are discarded — the reader sees `, `. Write `\[, \]`
    to keep the brackets literal, or `[, ]{.class}` if a span was intended.

Three separate problems in one message:

1. The quoted source is wrong. `[[#7380](url)]` is reported as `[]`.

2. The message states something false. "the reader sees ``" claims nothing
   survived. The reader actually sees `#7380` — a live link. Only the brackets
   were dropped.

3. The suggested remedy is destructive. An author who follows the printed hint
   and writes `\[\]` deletes the link. Verified: `- \[\] Console: cleaned up.`
   renders as "[] Console: cleaned up."

The underline in the snippet points at the correct span, so intent is recoverable — but every string the diagnostic quotes back has had its links silently removed. The worst case is (3): the message tells the author to do something that loses content, and it does so most confidently on the shape where it is most wrong.

ROOT CAUSE AND SUGGESTED FIX

`label_text()` is a lossy AST-to-string walk being used for two different jobs: matching (where dropping inlines is harmless) and author-facing display (where it is not). Only the display use is broken.

Reconstruct the label from source text rather than from the AST walk. The span already carries a source span — `source_info(span)` is called two lines below the message construction in `lone_bracket_warning()` — so the original slice is available at the point of need. Failing that, render inline children to their markdown surface form so a `Link` becomes `[#7380](url)` rather than an empty string.

Either way the remedy string must escape only the outer pair:

    \[[#7380](url)\]

which is exactly what `qmd-syntax-helper convert -r literal-brackets` already emits. The autofix is correct today; only the human-facing message is wrong. The two currently contradict each other, which is a bad place for a tool that is asking the author to hand-edit source.

The `reference_use_warning()` path above it uses the same `label_text()` for `[label][ref]` and looks susceptible to the same problem when the label holds non-text inlines; worth checking while in here.

REAL-WORLD HIT

The Positron docs port carries 974 instances across 14 files — 13 `release-notes/release-*.qmd` plus `release-notes/release.md` (included by `release-notes.qmd:18`). Every entry is written as

    - [[#14654](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/14654)] Connections: added ...

854 are the single-link shape and 57 the multi-link shape, so 911 of the 974 Q-2-49 warnings that project emits print a false "reader sees" claim and a link-destroying remedy. It is the largest single block of diagnostics in that render.

REPRO

/Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/q249-message-drops-inline-content/

    cd /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/q249-message-drops-inline-content
    q2 render repro.qmd

Five cases: single link, two links, emphasis, plus two controls (plain text, and text with a code span) that print correctly. The controls isolate the fault to non-text inlines. The README tabulates message-says vs reader-actually-sees for each.

NOT A DUPLICATE OF

- bd-lone-bracket-diagnostic-mxu41qbt (in_progress) — asks whether to warn on a
  lone bare `[text]` at all. Filed 2026-08-12, before Q-2-49 shipped, and its
  premise that q2 has no warning-suppression mechanism is now stale
  (`diagnostics: Q-2-49: off` exists in `diagnostic_policy.rs`). This strand is
  about the content of the message once it does fire.
- bd-reference-links-unsupported-ddc4skac (closed) — shipped the rules and the
  diagnostic. This is a defect in what it prints.

Origin strand: br-q249-message-drops-inline-content-01chm6kx (q2-positron-docs skein).
Observed on q2 0.27.0; confirmed still present at q2 source HEAD 3e45bdd2b.

c-ay6hsi0v.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-ay6hsi0v.text:
Fix in PR #617 (https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/617), branch bugfix/bd-q249-message-drops-inline-content.

label_text() split into label_source() (qmd markdown surface form, for the quoted source and remedies) and label_rendered() (pandoc-stringify, for 'the reader sees'). Q-2-45 and Q-2-46 shared the walk and are fixed by the same split - [*the docs*][gcc] was reported as [][gcc], as suspected in the strand.

Two findings beyond the report:
- Case 5 was not a clean control. [see `config.yml` now] was quoted as [see config.yml now], so that remedy deleted the code span too. The defect is not only about link/emph inlines; it is that one string served both the source quote and the reader-sees claim.
- Exact autofix parity needed a pampa change. write_inlines escapes # and > unconditionally (no line-position context), which would have spelled the label [\#7380](url). New write_inlines_fragment escapes those two only where they actually begin a line; write_inlines is untouched.

Verified: printed remedies diff byte-identical against qmd-syntax-helper convert -r literal-brackets for all five repro shapes; applying the remedy renders the brackets literally with the link live and re-renders with 0 warnings. Workspace 13475 passed / 0 failed; cargo xtask verify green including the WASM leg.

title: Q-2-50 covers only top-level doubled-brace fences; the whole real corpus is the nested form and goes undiagnosed
description:
This is not a claim that bd-escaped-executable-fence-uuvv37pk got the design wrong. It is one measurement that its plan could not have had, and which bears on decisions 3 and 4.

WHAT WAS DECIDED, AND WHAT WAS KNOWN

claude-notes/plans/2026-08-17-doubled-brace-escape.md lists both failure modes, nested first: "Inside a displayed fence - silently wrong output: the doubled braces survive verbatim, so the reader is shown ```{{python}}, which is not valid Quarto syntax, presented as the thing to copy. No diagnostic."

Decision 4 then gives the render-time diagnostic to the top-level fence only, and the plan's safety argument says why: a class literally containing braces can only come from a doubled-brace opener, because "fence content (including the Jinja counter-case and displayed inner fences) is never a class. Matching on the class string has no false-positive surface." Excluding fence content was the point — it is what protects the Jinja counter-case. Decision 3 separately declined a qmd-syntax-helper rule, calling it "an (at most) temporary defeat".

So the nested case was seen and consciously left undiagnosed, on the estimate that the strand carried: "8 blocks across 3 pages".

WHAT THE FULL CORPUS SAYS

Re-measured across the whole Posit Connect docs port at 0.23.0, not just the pages the original triage had sampled:

  61 doubled-brace fence openers, across 7 files
  61 of 61 are nested inside an outer display fence
   0 are top level
   0 Q-2-50 diagnostics in the full 352-page render

The estimate was 8; the real number is 61. More to the point, the split is not "mostly nested" — it is entirely nested, which follows from what the escape is FOR. An author reaches for the doubled brace precisely when displaying a cell, and displaying a cell means an outer fence. The top-level spelling that decision 4 diagnoses is the one that has no reason to exist.

Net effect for a porting project: q2 is silent on 100% of the occurrences, and the pages keep showing readers ```{{python}} as the syntax to copy. Those are pages whose SUBJECT is how to write Quarto cells (user/quarto, user/rmarkdown, how-to/publish-databricks-quarto-notebook, and four cookbook dashboard fragments), so the wrong thing is the thing being taught.

A NARROWER PREDICATE THAN THE ONE THAT WAS REJECTED

The plan's false-positive worry is real, but it is a worry about "a doubled brace appearing in fence content" — which does hit the counter-case. A much narrower predicate does not: a fence-content line that is ITSELF a fence opener with doubled braces, i.e.

  ^\s*`{3,}\{\{

Measured on the same corpus, that pattern matches exactly the 61 intended occurrences and nothing else. In particular it matches zero lines of user/fastapi/index.md, the Jinja counter-case that shaped decision 1 — whose `{{ name }}` and `{{ request.headers[...] }}` sit on ordinary content lines inside a ```{.html filename="..."} block and in a prose code span, never at a fence-opener position. The set is identical to a plain grep for the doubled-brace opener, so the narrowing costs no recall either.

That is a different risk profile from the one the plan weighed, and it is available without touching the class-matching check that exists.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION

Extend the existing Q-2-50 site rather than adding a mechanism. crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:1091-1135 already walks code blocks with with_code_block and warns when a class starts with `{{`. The same closure has the block's content in hand: scan it for a line matching the opener pattern above and emit the same Q-2-50 with the same two hints, located at that line. The existing early `break` after the class match keeps one warning per block; the content scan should do the same.

Two calls for the q2 side to make:

- Whether to gate on the outer block's language (markdown / unlabelled display fences) or accept any code block. Gating is tighter; accepting any is simpler and, on this corpus, identical.
- Whether this reopens decision 3. It should not: a diagnostic is a much lower bar than the qmd-syntax-helper REWRITE that was declined, since it asks a human to look rather than silently editing source. The plan's reasoning against the rule was about Q1's heuristic handling of nested and mixed brace counts, which is an argument against rewriting, not against pointing.

If the q2 side would rather hold the line and leave both the nested case and the helper rule alone, that is a legitimate answer — but it should be made against 61-and-none-diagnosed rather than against 8.

REPRO

/Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/escaped-executable-fence/

(Shared with the closed origin strand br-xa5oawj0; rewritten for this one.) index.qmd now shows the same opener four ways - nested with doubled braces, top level with doubled braces, nested with single braces (the sanctioned spelling), and a no-brace control. Run `q2 render` there: exactly one Q-2-50 fires, on the top-level form, and the nested form renders ```{{python}} silently. README.md carries the table and the measurement above.

Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-q250-nested-fence-blind-spot-cc26hye5, split out of br-xa5oawj0 (closed there as resolved-by-design once Q-2-50 landed). Observed with q2 0.23.0; q2 origin/main at 5b6774d1 has nothing past the 0.23.0 tag touching this.

c-5a0sxw1d.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-5a0sxw1d.text:
CROSS-REFERENCE from the ENGINE side (bd-ts-engine-display-fence-joy59gkr, worktree workspace-2). Not a claim on this strand's scope — this one owns the DIAGNOSTIC, that one owns EXECUTION. Two measurements from it that bear on the argument here.

1. The nested form is not merely the common spelling — under q2 it is the DANGEROUS one, for a reason independent of Q-2-50. Verified on q2 HEAD 00a1c1702: a document with one real ```{r} cell plus a four-backtick markdown display block containing ```{r} EXECUTES BOTH. knitr's own R-side scanner is nesting-blind, and q2 hands it the whole document string. Worse than 'it also ran': the display block's content is replaced by knitr's intermediate markup, so the reader is shown '::: {.cell}' and '{.r .cell-code}' where the author wrote an example. Filed as bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj (P3, no q2-side seam — knitr upstream owns it).

2. That strengthens the mechanism argument already in the 2026-08-27 comment here. Q1 executes nested cells, so the doubled brace was the author's only escape. q2 executes them too. So an author who reaches for ```{{python}} to avoid execution is right to, on both versions — and gets no diagnostic on q2 for the one spelling that actually matters. The frequency count (61 of 61 nested) and the mechanism now point the same way from two independent codepaths.

One thing the engine side does NOT support: the trigger is asymmetric. Remove every real cell and NOTHING executes, because AST-based engine resolution (computational_languages, resolution.rs:250) correctly declines to start an engine off a nested fence. A pure documentation page showing cells is safe today; it is one added real cell away from executing its own examples. If this strand's diagnostic ever wants to say 'this would execute', that gate is the thing to key off.

Full analysis, six filed strands, and the reproduction probes: claude-notes/research/2026-08-27-ts-engine-display-fence.md on branch braid/bd-ts-engine-display-fence-joy59gkr.

c-5z2zz42u.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-5z2zz42u.text:
FIX VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. Agent q250-nested-fence-blind-spot reports the fix committed as ec2181db5 on workspace-6 (not pushed, no PR). Confirmed against that branch's own debug build:

- The repro at /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/q250-nested-fence-blind-spot/ behaves exactly as its README specifies: 2 warnings total, at index.qmd:8:1 (F1, the nested opener — the bug) and index.qmd:15:5 (F2, top level — already worked). F3 (sanctioned single-brace nesting), F4 (plain fence) and F5 (Jinja false-positive guard) are silent. Exit 0.
- Coordination was done properly: it asked implement-self-documenting before writing code and got 'not mine, nothing in flight'. That session's own plan (claude-notes/plans/2026-09-02-nested-cell-masking.md) lists doubled-brace under 'Out, deliberately' and names this strand as owner.

TWO CORRECTIONS to the dispatch brief, both traceable to stale text in this strand's parent epic (bd-98m98wg8) rather than to the agent: the spike it cites, c5d1754b0 on spike/nested-cell-mask, is stale — current work is braid/bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj-mask; and the epic branch braid/bd-98m98wg8-self-documenting-cells-epic exists locally only, with no remote, so there is no shared integration line. Worth fixing in the epic.

ONE PROBLEM WITH THE COMMIT, not the fix. ec2181db5 sweeps in three files unrelated to the diagnostic: hub-client/public/q2-sandboxed-preview.html (38 lines), hub-client/public/serviceWorker.js, and crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/Cargo.lock. These are checked-in build bundles that a test/verify run regenerates — main refreshes them deliberately from time to time (587721bba 'hub-client: refresh stale q2-sandboxed-preview bundle', #573), so they are volatile under any build. They should come out of this commit before it becomes a PR: 38 lines of minified bundle churn in a diagnostic change is confusing to review and risks clobbering intent on paths main has touched recently (103af4445, 6549a98ae). title: Render summary counts warning occurrences (diagnostics × files), not distinct diagnostics
description:
Cosmetic, low priority; park until the diagnostics system gets its next round of design work.

A project-level diagnostic — one raised by a single key in _quarto.yml or an extension's _extension.yml — is attached to every page that renders under that config. The display side handles this well: the diagnostic is printed once, with an 'Affected files: a.qmd, b.qmd, index.qmd' (or '… (and 349 others)') trailer. But the trailing summary clause sums per-page occurrences, so a 3-page site with one bad 'highlight-style: no-such-style-xyz' ends with

    Rendered 3 of 3 files to … — 3 warnings

when the terminal above it shows exactly one problem. At scale the mismatch is what misleads: the Posit Connect docs (352 pages) rendered with a single cosmetic config notice and reported '352 warnings', and at 0.23.0 two Q-14-5 notices from one highlight-style key produced '704 warnings'. The number reads as a project in trouble. Quarto 1 has no equivalent summary, so there is no Q1 behavior to match — this is about the summary agreeing with q2's own deduplicated display.

Root cause: DiagnosticCounts::add_diagnostics in crates/quarto-core/src/project/orchestrator.rs tallies every DiagnosticMessage on every page output. Its own doc comment says the counts are 'diagnostic-level … an estimate of how many distinct problems a user must resolve', so the implementation is out of step with the stated intent. The summary clause is formatted by format_counts_clause in crates/quarto/src/commands/render.rs.

Suggested direction: either count distinct diagnostics (same identity key the display already uses to collapse into one block with Affected files), or report both — '1 warning (3 occurrences)'. Either makes the headline match what is printed above it.

Repro (3-page website, one unknown highlight-style in _quarto.yml):
  /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/br-q29-warning-flood-r6yl14ei/
  cd there and run: q2 render
Expected '— 1 warning' (or '1 warning, 3 occurrences'); actual '— 3 warnings'. README in that directory.

Origin: br-q29-warning-flood-r6yl14ei in the q2-connect-docs skein (closed there; not blocking the Connect docs port). Observed at q2 0.25.0; q2 HEAD v0.25.0-22-ga19d36ea unchanged.

title: q2-preview: CommentBlock wraps every commentable block in a positioned <div>, breaking parent > child theme rules and DOM parity (blockquote > h4, .callout-body > :first-child, li > p, .tab-pane > p …)
description: Re-scoped 2026-09-10 after diagnosis (was: 'heading inside blockquote not blockquote > h4'). Sectionize is correct: the live q2-preview DOM for the div-heading-becomes-section fixture is blockquote > div[style=position:relative;box-shadow…] > h4#quoted. The div is CommentBlock's wrapper (custom/CommentBlock.tsx ~line 980): every commentable block is wrapped so the comment bubble can be position:absolute against it and so the wrapper's onMouseMove/onMouseLeave can drive the hover '+' affordance and the glow. The parity harness never sees it (read-only mount, no PreviewContext), which is why the fixture carries dom-parity: true yet fails in the iframe. Theme CSS with direct-child selectors that no longer matches in the live preview: .callout-body > :first-child (2 rules), .callout-body > div (3), li > p:last-of-type, li > a/span/ul, .tab-pane > p/pre, section > section. Fix direction: remove the wrapper's box — display: contents on the wrapper (events still bubble through it) with the bubble positioned from the BLOCK element's measured rect against a positioned ancestor, the hover half-test and glow reading the block element instead of the wrapper. The relayout pass already measures rects each layout, so the geometry hook exists; the change is contained to CommentBlock.tsx but touches its positioning/hover core (nudges, reveal scale). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-09-hub-client-default-q2-preview.md Phase 4b.
