title: Perf: WASM render re-flushes ALL artifacts into the VFS on every render
description:
Surfaced while scoping the embed-iframe preview work (bd-z1smhvuo). The WASM render entry point re-flushes the ENTIRE artifact set into the VFS on EVERY render, with no change-detection:

  crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1417-1425
    for (_key, artifact) in ctx.artifacts.iter() {
        if artifact.content.is_empty() { continue; }
        let vfs_path = resolver.on_disk_path_for(artifact.scope, artifact_path);
        runtime.add_file(&vfs_path, artifact.content.clone());   // <-- clone + insert, every render
    }

ctx.artifacts is rebuilt per render (theme CSS, fonts, shared JS, plot images, ...). add_file (crates/quarto-system-runtime/src/wasm.rs:266 / :532) is an in-memory HashMap insert that CLONES the content. So every edit-triggered re-render re-clones and re-inserts every accumulated artifact regardless of whether it changed. For a doc with a large theme + webfonts this is a non-trivial per-keystroke CPU/alloc cost scaling with total artifact bytes. Suspected to contribute to observed preview perf issues.

Investigate / address:
1. Quantify: with QUARTO_PERF_STATS-style instrumentation (see claude-notes/instructions/performance-profiling.md), measure per-render artifact bytes re-flushed and the clone/insert time on a theme-heavy doc; scale geometrically.
2. Confirm the blast radius: does anything propagate these VFS writes into the Automerge document (doc growth + sync traffic), or do they stay in-memory-ephemeral in WasmRuntime.files? (My earlier 'Automerge bloat' claim was unverified — pin this down. If they DO sync, the cost is much worse.)
3. Fix direction: content-hash / change-detection so only changed artifacts are re-flushed (skip unchanged theme CSS/fonts/JS); or move stable project-scope artifacts out of the per-render path entirely (flush once, reuse across renders — the Phase-9 VFS-is-load-bearing-across-renders contract already assumes persistence).
4. Watch the bd-3gtn empty-content skip + the iframe post-processor's read-back contract when changing flush behavior.

Read claude-notes/instructions/performance-profiling.md FIRST (native-proxy-first workflow). Reference: bd-z1smhvuo embed plan + 2026-04-27 websites Phase 9 plan (VFS artifact contract).
close_reason: Implemented + measured. Skip-if-byte-identical flush landed on main (merge 8330451a): shared quarto_core::flush_artifacts_to_vfs replaces two inline loops, VirtualFileSystem::add_file_if_changed gives zero-allocation steady state, WasmRuntime::file_write covers the flush_site_libs path. Measured verdict: flush was ~0.02% of a render natively — not the suspected preview perf contributor; fix kept for structural value (dedup, tests, allocation elimination on the wasm heap). Q2 (Automerge blast radius) answered: writes are in-memory-ephemeral, no doc growth. Findings + e2e record: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-09-wasm-vfs-artifact-reflush.md. Follow-ups: bd-rrnn3se8, bd-w5qyuzeg (backlogged with numbers), bd-ye90x1ga.

title: Display math inside a blockquote retains '> ' continuation prefix in content (issue #181)
description:
Tree-sitter grammar rule `pandoc_display_math` (crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js:367) matches its body as a single regex `/([^$]|[$][^$]|\\$)+/` between the two `$$` delimiters. When the math block is inside a blockquote, the interior `> ` block-continuation markers are never consumed by the grammar's `block_continuation` machinery; they end up verbatim inside the captured node text and then inside `Math.text` (see crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:502-513). The qmd writer then correctly re-prefixes every line of the math body with `> ` when emitting it inside a blockquote, producing `> > p = q` and adding one more `> ` level on each round trip.

Fix is at the grammar level: make `pandoc_display_math` line-structured (loop over `$._newline | _math_line`) the way `pandoc_code_block` already is (grammar.js:828, with `_newline` consuming `block_continuation` at grammar.js:886). The writer is already correct; do not change it.

Triage doc and minimal repros live at claude-notes/issue-reports/181/ on branch issue-181. See triage.md there for full evidence including CST output and a contrasting fenced-code-in-blockquote case that parses cleanly.

title: preview parity: OrderedList omits type="1" for Decimal style
description:
Found by the preview<->render DOM parity harness
(hub-client/src/services/smokeAllParity.wasm.test.tsx) on fixture
crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/appendix/footnotes-heading.qmd.

render:  <ol type="1">
preview: <ol>

Native writer: crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:1502-1510 emits `type`
unconditionally, mapping ListNumberStyle::Decimal -> "1" (with a
`_ => "1"` catch-all for any other unmapped style).

React: ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/OrderedList.tsx:28-32
has no Decimal key in styleToType, and its doc comment at :16 explicitly
claims "DefaultStyle / Decimal: no `type` attr (browser default)" — this
claim contradicts the writer's actual behavior.

The footnotes transform builds its list with ListNumberStyle::Decimal
(crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/footnotes.rs:542), which is how this
surfaced in the footnotes fixture, but the divergence applies to any
Decimal-style ordered list.

Decision point: Pandoc's own HTML writer emits `type` whenever the style
is not DefaultStyle, so Decimal -> type="1"; that matches the native
writer, not React's styleToType map. Whichever way this is resolved, one
side must change since they currently disagree about their shared
reference (Pandoc) — the React comment describes behavior the writer
does not have. Absent a decision otherwise, React is the side to change
to match the writer/Pandoc.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-preview-render-dom-parity-harness.md

Fix should end with `parity: true` on the fixture.

title: Rich-text editor: place caret at click position on first activation
description: When clicking a paragraph/heading to activate the tiptap rich-text editor in q2 preview --allow-edit (&richText=1), the cursor lands at the END of the block (autofocus: 'end' in RichTextEditor.tsx) instead of where the user clicked. A second click at the same spot correctly moves the caret (ProseMirror handles it natively once mounted). Capture the activating mouse-click viewport coordinates and use editor.view.posAtCoords() at mount to place the caret at the clicked position. Keyboard activation keeps end-of-block. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-24-richtext-caret-at-click.md
close_reason: Implemented and end-to-end verified; caret lands at click on first activation for paragraphs, headings, and clean click-switch. Commits 151be676, 410885a3, 5a70eec5. Not yet pushed.

c-ltg1xc75.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ltg1xc75.text: Implemented + e2e verified. Commits 151be676 (feature), 410885a3 (autofocus race fix + jsdom test polyfill), 5a70eec5 (plan done). Key finding: caret-at-click geometry was fine immediately (caretRangeFromPoint resolved correctly); the caret pinned to end because tiptap autofocus:'end' applies its end-selection in a rAF that beat our placement on the same frame. Fix: autofocus:false + mount effect owns the opening caret (posAtCoords at click, else focus('end')). Browser-verified in q2 preview --allow-edit &richText=1: paragraph clicks at 40%/10% and heading at 50% land caret exactly at click (delta 0/-1); clean click-switch P1->P2 lands at click; keyboard activation stays end-of-block. Tests: 3 jsdom files (capture/helper/consume) + setup polyfill for Text/Range getClientRects. Full preview-renderer suites green (490 unit + 498 integration), tsc clean, hub-client build:all passes. NOT pushed (awaiting permission).

c-pre95pqh.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-pre95pqh.text: Investigated. Root cause: RichTextEditor.tsx:93 uses autofocus end. Activation: useBlockEditHover.onPointerUp -> activate() -> ctx.setEditTarget (React state) -> RichTextEditor mounts after the original mouse event is gone, so ProseMirror never translates the click to a doc position; the 2nd click works because the editor is already mounted. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-24-richtext-caret-at-click.md -- capture clientX/Y at the mouse activation site into a new write-once pendingClickCoordsRef, consume at mount via editor.view.posAtCoords + setTextSelection, fall back to end-of-block for keyboard/touch/null. Awaiting go-ahead.

c-vvc0dskk.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-vvc0dskk.text: Scope decision (user): fold in editor-to-editor click-switch (clicking block B while editing A) too. Good news -- it needs NO extra capture code: both fresh-open and click-switch open B via onPointerUp -> activate(B), so the single coords write in onPointerUp covers both. Clean-A switch places caret at click. Dirty-A switch commits A, reflows, may re-anchor B -> remount consumes-once -> falls back to end-of-block (correct: viewport coords are stale after reflow). Plan updated with a Click-switch coverage section + e2e step 5.

title: cargo xtask create-worktree DWIMs remote-tracking branch as base, doesn't create requested branch
description:
Symptom: 'cargo xtask create-worktree --issue 152 --base bugfix/issue-184' printed 'Branch: issue-152' but the worktree was actually checked out on a freshly-created local 'bugfix/issue-184' branch (tracking origin/bugfix/issue-184). No 'issue-152' branch was ever created; 'git rev-parse refs/heads/issue-152' returns exit 1 immediately after the xtask reports success. Reflog confirms.

Reproduction (best-effort, from this session):
- main worktree at .worktrees/issue-184/ already exists on a local 'issue-184' branch
- remote bugfix/issue-184 exists; no local bugfix/issue-184 yet
- cargo xtask create-worktree --issue 152 --base bugfix/issue-184
- Result: .git/worktrees/issue-152/HEAD reads 'ref: refs/heads/bugfix/issue-184'
- Expected: HEAD reads 'ref: refs/heads/issue-152'

Likely cause: the underlying 'git worktree add -b issue-152 .worktrees/issue-152 bugfix/issue-184' invocation may interact poorly with git's DWIM when the start-point is a remote-tracking branch. Worth a small repro test in crates/xtask/.

Recovered in-place via 'git checkout -b issue-152' inside the worktree (user-approved during triage). The xtask still claimed success in stdout, so the bug is silent — that's the most user-hostile part.

Discovered during: triage of issue #152 / bd-j4fe.

title: Preview: knitr/jupyter engine-generated images missing (capture lacks supporting-file bytes)
description: Engine execution results with images (e.g. knitr/ggplot figures in <doc>_files/figure-html/) render correctly under q2 render but are broken images in q2 preview and hub-client q2-preview. Root cause: the EngineCapture recorded for preview replay serializes ExecuteResult.supporting_files as paths only (Vec<PathBuf>), never the bytes; the browser-side replay has no access to the recording machine's disk, and the q2 preview server only serves declared resources: (RESOURCE_DISK_MAP), so figure requests fall through to the SPA index fallback (200 text/html). Fix direction: embed supporting-file bytes in the capture binary doc and materialize them into the WASM VFS at replay time so the existing assetWalker blob-URL mechanism picks them up. Repro, diagnosis, and plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-23-preview-engine-supporting-files.md

c-1891fhef.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-1891fhef.text: Diagnosis confirmed by live repro: capture cache .bin contains supporting_files as an absolute path string only; browser request for hello_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png returns 200 text/html (SPA index fallback). Divergence point: copy_resources_to_output_dir (orchestrator.rs:928-964) is cfg(not(wasm32)); WASM flush_artifacts_to_vfs flushes ctx.artifacts only, never resource_report. Fix direction: embed supporting-file bytes in EngineCapture (serde-default field), materialize into VFS at capture load in wasm-quarto-hub-client (vfs_add_binary_file exists); existing assetWalker/iframePostProcessor resolvers then work unchanged. Full plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-23-preview-engine-supporting-files.md

title: Perf: cache_get_lru rewrites the LRU index file on every cache hit (1.2% of render CPU, concurrent from 16 workers)
description: quarto-system-runtime cache_lru.rs cache_get_lru(): on a hit it load_index -> touch(key) -> store_index (rewrite the JSON index) — so every document's CompileThemeCssStage sass cache hit costs an index read+write: store_index 154 samples (1.24%) + load_index 25 in the warm Connect docs profile, executed concurrently by 16 rayon workers (which is also the lost-update race bd-ddahjqr1 describes). Fix: touch in memory and flush the index once per render (or debounce), or drop recency tracking on hits. Related: bd-ddahjqr1. title: Parse error on `***` inline code content (regression from bd-ilv8p)
description: Inline code content of exactly three asterisks (e.g. ```***```) fails to parse with 'unexpected character or token here'. Pandoc accepts it as Code "***" and pampa accepted it before commit 38e889ad (bd-ilv8p, 2026-05-24). Trigger is narrow: a run of exactly 3 consecutive asterisks at the start of inline-code content (```***```, ```***x```, ```***x***```). Four+ asterisks or asterisks after other content (```x***```, ```*x***```) parse fine. Likely cause: the new third alternative in the pandoc_code_span content rule (`alias($._soft_line_break, $.pandoc_soft_break)`) shifted parser-state precedence so the inline emphasis tokenizer's Q-2-32 'triple star' token beats the content regex inside code spans. See claude-notes/plans/2026-05-24-inline-code-triple-asterisk-regression.md for repro, characterization table, root cause hypothesis, and TDD work plan.
close_reason: Fixed: gate TRIPLE_STAR emission on valid_symbols[EMPHASIS_OPEN_STAR] in scanner.c. Inline code spans containing literal *** now parse as Code, while paragraph-level Q-2-32 diagnostic still fires correctly. See claude-notes/plans/2026-05-24-inline-code-triple-asterisk-regression.md.

title: Preview navbar brand link points to artifacts VFS root and dead-ends iframe
description:
In hub-client / q2 preview, the navbar brand anchor (the title 'Quarto 2' in docs/) renders as <a class="navbar-brand" href="/.quarto/project-artifacts/">.

Live repro 2026-05-20 (chrome-devtools MCP against q2 preview docs/):
clicking it fires beforeunload on the iframe, iframe location moves to
/.quarto/project-artifacts/, and NO NAVIGATE_TO_DOCUMENT postMessage fires —
stranding the SPA on a URL the preview server doesn't serve.

Both TS link handlers reject the trailing-slash form:
- iframeLinkHandlers.ts::parseArtifactHref (used by q2-preview SPA, this is the path that runs in q2 preview docs/)
- iframePostProcessor.ts::reverseMapArtifactHref (used by hub-client HTML iframe)
Both require .html suffix on the stem.

Native q2 render is correct (href="./"). Bug is preview-only.

Fix in both TS link handlers — recognize the bare-directory artifact-root form as the project home (index.qmd). Resolver semantics unchanged.

See plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-preview-navbar-brand-artifacts-link.md
close_reason:
Fixed in commit ebcc7f3e. Two-surface fix in TS:

- iframeLinkHandlers.ts::parseArtifactHref (q2-preview SPA path,
  always-intercept) — empty-stem branch returns
  { qmdCandidate: 'index.qmd', anchor }.

- iframePostProcessor.ts::reverseMapArtifactHref (hub-client HTML
  path, strict projectFilePaths lookup) — empty/null-stem branch
  tries each RENDERABLE_EXTS as 'index'+ext against projectFilePaths;
  returns first match or null per surface policy.

Resolver semantics in quarto-core unchanged — the trailing-slash
directory URL is correct for static-served sites; the adaptation
belongs at the SPA-specific interception layer.

E2E verified against docs/ via chrome-devtools MCP (post-fix
signature exactly inverts the 2026-05-20 repro): default prevented,
no beforeunload, iframe stays at /q2-preview.html,
NAVIGATE_TO_DOCUMENT fires with path=index.qmd, SPA route updates,
heading after click is "Quarto 2".

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-preview-navbar-brand-artifacts-link.md

title: behave f4 crash-relaunch e2e: witness-2 assertion races the async stderr launch marker (CI flake)
description: Seen on PR #560 CI (ubuntu-latest, run 32279995673, 2026-08-19) — an unrelated lockfile-only PR. behave_engine_e2e::f4_crash_yields_process_crashed_then_transparently_relaunches failed at behave_engine_e2e.rs:681: expected count_containing("BEHAVE_LAUNCH_MARKER:1") == 2, got 1. Captured messages show BOTH 'engine-host spawned' events (witness 1 passed, it fires synchronously on the calling thread) but only process #1's launch marker — process #2's marker is delivered by the background stderr-forwarding thread (ts_process.rs stderr_loop) and had not landed when the bare count_containing ran. Same race class as the F3 flake fixed 2026-08-18 in ae01254ce (which introduced wait_for_count_containing and used it for F3's ':2' witness) — F4's witness-2 was left as a bare count. Fix: use wait_for_count_containing("BEHAVE_LAUNCH_MARKER:1", 2, 10s) at :681; consider the same treatment for the pre-execute-2 crash-marker/marker:1 checks at :636-:656 which rely on a fixed 200ms sleep (the wait helper's trailing settle preserves the == upper bound). Not a product bug: the 'crash' in the log is the fixture's intentional BEHAVE_CRASH, and the relaunch demonstrably happened (two spawns, execute-2 returned before the assertion).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #562, merged to main as eccf31466. All async-marker assertions in behave_engine_e2e.rs now use the bounded-poll wait_for_count_containing helper; fail-first verified via injected stderr delay reproducing the exact CI signature. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-19-behave-f4-launch-marker-race.md

title: InvalidScssFile still falls back silently to DEFAULT_CSS in compile_theme_css

title: reader: remove silent CRLF to LF rewrites
description: Two reader paths silently rewrite CRLF to LF, violating the preserve policy: inline-math soft-break handling in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs around line 476 (text push newline), and strip_continuation_prefix around lines 422 and 428 which splits on newline and rejoins with newline inside lists and blockquotes. Both are the same mechanical move: rejoin with the original convention instead of a hardcoded line feed. Make both preserve the input convention. TDD: CRLF inside inline math and inside nested list and blockquote content, assert convention preserved. Note treesitter.rs:1371 was checked and is byte-correct on CRLF, not in scope. SCOPE: this strand covers ONLY the two tree-sitter-qmd post-extraction sites above. It does NOT include the comrak/commonmark reader (readers/commonmark.rs): comrak's CRLF-to-LF normalization is spec-mandated with no opt-out, handled separately as the strategy-3 boundary decision (bd-1ll7kj9e). Do not attempt to de-normalize comrak here. See claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-handling-analysis.md.

title: span_assert: Substring-wrapped gappy Concat piece yields a wrong Ok (accepting-direction gap)
description:
concat_pieces_are_contiguous (crates/quarto-config/src/span_assert.rs:211-239) recurses into a piece only when that piece's source_info is a BARE SourceInfo::Concat:

    if let SourceInfo::Concat { pieces: nested } = &piece.source_info

A piece whose source_info is Substring { parent: Concat { gappy }, .. } never enters that branch. Its endpoints are then map_offset(0) -> the first sub-piece's start and map_offset(length()) -> a position past the gap, so the piece's own extent straddles a gap nothing checks, and neighbour contiguity is measured against those straddling endpoints.

This is an error in the ACCEPTING direction: a wrong Ok whose hull covers source bytes belonging to no piece. That is the worst kind of error for this epic — resolve_span exists to refuse rather than guess.

MEASURED (2026-08-23, on span_assert's own concat_fixture, CONCAT_CONTENT = "0123456789ABCDEF"):

    inner   = Concat[(Original(6,10), 4), (Original(12,15), 3)]   // content "6789CDE", gap at 10..12
    wrapped = Substring(inner, 0, 7)                              // the whole of it
    outer   = Concat[(wrapped, 7)]
    resolve_span(&outer, &ctx)
      => Ok(ResolvedSpan { path: "concat-fixture.txt", line: 1, column: 7, text: "6789ABCDE" })

Nine source bytes for seven content bytes, silently including the gap bytes "AB" that belong to neither sub-piece. The honest content is "6789CDE"; the honest answer is Err(SpanProblem::Concat).

REACHABILITY, and its relation to Plan 3 Phase 6c:

The defect PREDATES Phase 6c's is_gapless narrowing -- concat_pieces_are_contiguous's loop body is unchanged by that commit (63936764b). The narrowing is NOT the cause and is NOT defective.

But the narrowing makes the hole MORE REACHABLE, and that is why this is filed now. Before Phase 6c, a top-level Substring over a gappy Concat was refused wholesale regardless of what its pieces contained. After it, such a span resolves whenever the pieces the queried sub-range touches pass -- so a Substring-wrapped gappy piece among those touched pieces can now produce the Ok. The reachability increase is a CONSEQUENCE of a correct narrowing, not a defect in it.

BLAST RADIUS: test-only. The span-assert feature is declared at quarto-config/Cargo.toml:29 and enabled only under [dev-dependencies] (quarto-core:127, quarto-config:34, pampa:93). A wrong Ok here makes a test assert against the wrong text -- visible in a failing assertion, never in a rendered caret. No production path reaches it.

FIX SKETCH: make the recursion peel Substring layers before matching Concat -- i.e. check the piece's own extent with the same sub-range machinery is_gapless_over already has (is_gapless_over(&piece.source_info, None, ctx)), rather than pattern-matching one shape. Needs a test binding the wrong Ok above to Err(Concat) first (TDD), plus a check of all span_assert consumers.

DOCUMENTED AT: the residual-imprecision block in concat_pieces_are_contiguous's doc comment (span_assert.rs), which names this as the one known accepting-direction gap and cites this strand.

Found in review of Plan 3 Phase 6c; plan claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-3-audit-and-fix.md.

title: Resolve metadata paths relative to the file they were declared in (source-location-driven)
description:
Reproducer: `docs/guide/index.qmd` defines a sidebar in its frontmatter:

```yaml
sidebar:
  contents:
    - text: "Introduction"
      href: introduction.qmd
    - text: "Markdown"
      href: ../authoring/markdown/index.qmd
```

Both targets exist relative to `docs/guide/index.qmd` (`docs/guide/introduction.qmd` and `docs/authoring/markdown/index.qmd`). Today `q2 render` warns:

  Sidebar references missing document information for 'introduction.qmd'
  Sidebar references missing document information for '../authoring/markdown/index.qmd'

because `SidebarGenerateTransform` treats sidebar hrefs as project-root-relative regardless of where the YAML was written.

Root cause: `SidebarEntry::from_plain_string` (`crates/quarto-navigation/src/sidebar.rs`) and the bare-string code path in `SidebarEntry::from_config_value` strip `ConfigValue.source_info`, then `SidebarGenerateTransform` calls `index.lookup_by_source(Path::new(h))` on the bare string. There is no way at lookup time to know whether the href was written in `_quarto.yml` (project-root-relative) or in a doc's frontmatter (doc-relative).

Fix direction (chosen): hybrid 'known path-shaped keys' — the sidebar/navbar parser treats strings in href/file/contents/section-href positions as if they were `!path`, retaining the `ConfigValue.source_info` long enough to resolve them against `dirname(source_info.file)` at Generate time. Authors don't have to write `!path` tags. Mirrors the existing `adjust_paths_to_document_dir` machinery for directory metadata, extended to per-document frontmatter.

Scope: sidebar, navbar, page-footer entries (hrefs + contents items). Project-config / `_quarto.yml`-rooted values resolve to project-root-relative (unchanged behaviour). Per-doc / `_metadata.yml`-rooted values resolve to dirname-of-that-file, then normalized via `resolve_to_project_root`.

This issue also lands the SourceInfo plumbing through to the navigation diagnostics that bd-8d6rk migrates to the structured form — once the parser retains source_info, the diagnostic gets a real location and `--json` consumers can show the offending YAML line.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-bd-PLACEHOLDER-metadata-path-resolution.md (to be created)

Blocks-on bd-8d6rk: the structured-diagnostic surface should exist before we wire SourceInfo into it.
notes: Plan outline written: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-bd-qor9a-metadata-path-resolution.md (draft, awaiting iteration. Will be fleshed out in detail after bd-8d6rk lands)
close_reason: Implementation complete. RenderContext now carries source_context; NavigationItem / SidebarEntry::Section / Navbar carry href_source paired fields; resolve_metadata_path resolves hrefs against the YAML file they were authored in; sidebar/navbar/footer/page-nav generate+render pass href_source through to Q-13-* diagnostics. End-to-end verified on docs/guide/index.qmd (zero warnings; sidebar links resolve correctly). cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build clean. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-bd-qor9a-metadata-path-resolution.md (all phases checked). Follow-up bd-hjv5o tracks broader generalization. Changes uncommitted pending user review.

title: Display math column-strip uses wrong column source, mishandles inline-wrapped and labeled math (issue #181 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to bd-q6ed / issue #181, with revised diagnosis after a second-pass investigation (see `claude-notes/issue-reports/181/triage.md` § "Second-pass investigation").

## Symptom

Two reporter-supplied edge cases (rundel, 2026-05-12):

1. **Labeled display math inside a blockquote** — `> $$\n> p(x)\n> $$ {#eq-p}` round-trips with a literal `> ` left in `Math.text` after the second pass.
2. **Labeled display math at top level** — `$$\na\n  b\n$$ {#eq-x}` loses one column of leading whitespace from interior lines on each round trip.

Subsequent probing revealed both are instances of a broader brittleness in the column-strip introduced by bd-q6ed:

3. `_$$\na\n  b\n$$_` (emph wrapping multi-line displaymath) loses one space on **first** parse — no round trip needed.
4. `> _$$\n> a\n>   b\n> $$_` (same inside a blockquote) leaks `> ` AND loses interior whitespace on first parse.

## Root cause

`strip_continuation_prefix` in `crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs` uses `node.start_position().column` (the column of `$$`) as the strip width. That column equals the cumulative block-continuation prefix width **only when `$$` is the leftmost non-prefix character on its line**. Anything that precedes `$$` on the same line (`_`, `**`, `[`, the writer's own `[` for `quarto-math-with-attribute` Spans, etc.) shifts the column while the body bytes' source layout does not change. The strip then either eats real content (when the prefix is all whitespace/`>`) or refuses to strip real prefix (when the column overshoots into real content).

## Constraint

`DisplayMath` must remain an inline AST node — there are large existing corpora with display math nested inside paragraphs, and the grammar restructure proposed in the original triage would break those documents.

## Fix shape (reader-side, no grammar change, no AST shape change)

Change the strip-width source from `math_node.start_position().column` to the start column of the **enclosing block-leaf ancestor** (`pandoc_paragraph` / `pandoc_plain`). The cumulative block-continuation prefix width equals the paragraph's start column, which is constant across all interior lines of the paragraph regardless of what precedes `$$` on the opening line.

Pandoc's markdown reader uses this exact strategy (verified empirically). The fix matches Pandoc's behaviour on all probed cases — including lazy-continuation, nested blockquotes, list-item indent, and inline-wrapped multi-line math. The existing conservative `bytes ∈ {>, space, tab}` guard in the helper continues to handle lazy continuation correctly.

This single-input change subsumes:
- bd-q6ed canonical case (paragraph col = math col, identical result)
- bd-qpa2 edges A and B (paragraph col reflects true bq/top-level width)
- Inline-wrapped multi-line math at any block context

## Regression coverage to add

Fixtures under `crates/pampa/tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/`:

- `labeled_display_math_in_blockquote.qmd` (bd-qpa2 edge A)
- `labeled_display_math_top_level_indented.qmd` (bd-qpa2 edge B)
- `emph_around_multiline_display_math.qmd`
- `emph_around_multiline_display_math_in_blockquote.qmd`

Reference inputs preserved at `claude-notes/issue-reports/181/exp-labeled-math-in-bq.qmd` and `exp-labeled-math-toplevel.qmd`.

## Worktree / branch

Implementation on its own branch with plan file at `claude-notes/plans/2026-05-12-displaymath-column-strip-fix.md`. Upstream: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/181.

## Out of scope (separate issue if desired)

The writer's `[$$…$$]{attr}` emission for `quarto-math-with-attribute` Spans is suboptimal — Pandoc emits the natural form `$$\n…\n$$ {attr}` for the same AST. Switching to that form would improve readability and Pandoc compatibility, but with the reader fix above it is no longer required for round-trip correctness.

title: quarto-hub MCP can't reach projects on a non-default sync server (e.g. sync.automerge.org share links)
description:
The quarto-hub MCP tools (connect_project/list_files/read_file/patch_file/...) resolve a project by automerge index doc id but only against the MCP's own/default sync server. A project shared via a hub-client share link that uses a different sync server (e.g. ?server=wss://sync.automerge.org) is unreachable: list_files returns 'project index document automerge:<id> is unavailable on the sync server — cannot open the project (verify the project id and the sync server URL)'.

Impact: an agent (or MCP consumer) cannot act as a collaborator on, or inspect, projects hosted on a non-default sync server — including the share links hub-client generates. Surfaced 2026-06-22 while trying to drive a two-window _brand.yml repro for bd-4jjckvwt; had to fall back to driving both browser tabs directly.

Desired: let connect_project (and the file ops) accept/resolve a sync server URL (mirroring the hub-client share URL's ?server= param), or otherwise reach projects on arbitrary sync servers. Investigate where the MCP picks its sync server (ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp + quarto-sync-client) and whether a per-call/per-project server override is feasible. Needs design before implementation.

title: build_source_map can emit an all-unmappable source map, crashing QuartoNotebookRunner
description:
`build_source_map` (crates/quarto-core/src/engine/ts_engine.rs:671) maps each input line via `ctx.source_info.map_offset(...)`. Its own doc comment states the invariant: an all-unmappable input makes the Julia engine's `buildSourceRanges` send an *empty* `sourceRanges` array to QuartoNotebookRunner, which crashes QNR's `compute_line_file_lookup` (`maximum` over an empty collection). Nothing enforces that invariant — the function will happily emit entries that are every one `source: None`.

Reachable shape: a document whose sole top-level block is a Div containing both a live `{julia}` cell and a block whose SourceInfo is `Generated`. The qmd writer's piece loop is top-level only (`for block in &pandoc.blocks`, pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:3104), so one Generated top-level piece makes every line unmappable.

Found during Phase 0 of the nested-cell-masking plan (bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj), whose H7 top-level-ancestor rule widens reachability by marking a display block's top-level ancestor `Generated`. Decision on that plan (Gordon, 2026-09-02): ship the mask as planned and defend this invariant separately — it is build_source_map's own contract, not the mask's job.

Candidate mitigation considered and NOT chosen there: anchoring the first entry at file offset 0 when every entry is unmappable. It fixes the class but emits a location that is not true, contradicting the 'unknown beats wrong' principle the surrounding provenance work is built on. A better fix likely reports the degenerate state rather than fabricating a position.

Unverified link: QuartoNotebookRunner is not vendored in this repo, so `compute_line_file_lookup` was not read directly. The in-repo doc comment is the authority and reads as written from experience. Confirm against QNR before designing the fix.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-02-nested-cell-masking.md

title: Unify on rustls: drop native-tls/openssl from the q2 dependency tree
description:
q2 links TWO TLS stacks today. rustls + aws-lc-rs arrives via reqwest (hyper-rustls); openssl arrives via native-tls, whose sole root is tokio-tungstenite/tungstenite pulled by crates/quarto-hub-provider (Cargo.toml:48, features=["native-tls"]) and by samod. samod is OUR fork (quarto-dev/samod, branch access-policy) and hard-wires it: samod/Cargo.toml:13 defines the 'tungstenite' feature as [..., "tungstenite/native-tls", "tokio-tungstenite/native-tls"], so cargo feature unification makes openssl unavoidable from q2's side alone.

Work: switch samod's tungstenite feature to the rustls variants, mirror the change in quarto-hub-provider, confirm openssl-sys/openssl/native-tls leave Cargo.lock (cargo tree -p quarto -i openssl-sys should find nothing), then delete the now-pointless 'vendored-openssl' feature from crates/quarto/Cargo.toml and the --features vendored-openssl cargo_flags from the linux legs of .github/workflows/release.yml.

Payoff: one TLS stack instead of two (smaller binary, faster builds, one CVE surface), and the linux release legs stop building openssl from source entirely. Requires a change to the samod fork, so it is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE of bd-dofxhzaj (the musl switch), which keeps vendored-openssl working as-is. Identified in the original S2 spike (claude-notes/plans/2026-06-12-q2-github-releases-bundled-mcp.md, 'longer-term sound alternative') and re-confirmed during the bd-dofxhzaj investigation.

title: DocumentProfile: add includes: Vec<PathBuf> for incremental-rebuild invalidation
description:
Surfaced during the main -> feature/websites merge (bd-xfwx) that threaded IncludeExpansionStage before the DocumentProfile checkpoint.

Problem: after the merge, DocumentProfile.outline (and any other AST-derived fields) can be populated from headings / code / crossref targets spliced in via {{< include child.qmd >}}. The profile therefore depends on the contents of every included file, but the profile struct itself records no trail back to those files.

For incremental rebuilds (Phase 8 of the websites epic, bd-*) and for the future 'freeze' feature, the cache-key computation needs to invalidate a parent document's cached profile when ANY of its (transitive) includes change. Without tracking the include set on the profile, that is impossible.

Proposal: add a field roughly of the form

    includes: Vec<PathBuf>   // or Vec<IncludeEntry { path, hash }>

to DocumentProfile. Populated by IncludeExpansionStage (or by DocumentProfileStage reading a side-channel set that IncludeExpansionStage populated on the DocumentAst). Bump profile_version on the serialized shape.

Scope:
- Decide on the shape (bare PathBuf list vs. (path, content-hash) pairs). For Phase 8 we'll likely want the hash too so nav-state invalidation can compare without re-reading the files.
- Populate from IncludeExpansionStage.
- Extend contract doc (claude-notes/designs/document-profile-contract.md).
- Tests: profile records every included file (direct + transitive); round-trip serialization.

Non-blocking for the website-epic MVP; becomes a hard prerequisite for Phase 8.
close_reason: Closed as part of Phase 8.0 — DocumentProfile.includes added (v2). Verified by editing_include_invalidates_parent_profile (incremental_rebuild.rs).

title: cargo xtask stage-doc-examples stages into the main checkout when run from a worktree
description:
`repo_root()` in the stage-doc-examples xtask resolves via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, which always points at the main repo checkout rather than the invoking worktree. Running `cargo xtask stage-doc-examples` from a worktree therefore populates `docs/examples/` under the MAIN repo, leaving the worktree's own `docs/examples/` empty. Since `docs/_quarto.yml` declares `resources: - examples`, a subsequent `cargo run --bin q2 -- render docs/` in that worktree renders against missing resources unless you hand-copy the staged tree across.

Found while verifying the docs render for the listing inline-records work (plan claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-listing-inline-contents.md) in .worktrees/workspace-5; worked around by copying the generated (gitignored) tree into the worktree. Nothing leaked into that branch's commits.

Likely fix: resolve the repo root from the invoking worktree (e.g. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) rather than the common git dir, for output paths.

title: Q-2-35 is assigned to two unrelated diagnostics; its docs page describes the wrong one
description:
Two unrelated diagnostics share the code Q-2-35:

1. **Indented code blocks are not supported** — emitted by the parser. The tree-sitter scanner emits `INDENTED_CODE_BLOCK_DISALLOWED` (scanner.c:2664, declared 152/267; grammar.js ~1223-1231 documents the known limitation), and the corpus entry is crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/Q-2-35.json titled 'Indented code blocks are not supported'.

2. **Invalid List-Table Structure** — a warning built in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:932 and :1123.

The catalog (crates/quarto-error-catalog/error_catalog.json, single Q-2-35 key) and the docs page (docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-35.qmd) both describe only #2.

**User-visible consequence.** Verified by rendering a file with a 4-space indented block:

    cargo run --bin q2 -- render <file>.qmd
    warning: profile-pass skipped ...: Error: [Q-2-35] Indented code blocks are not supported
      ... Quarto Markdown does not support 4-space indented code blocks. Use a fenced code block (```) instead, or remove the leading indentation.

The diagnostic prints its docs_url unconditionally, so a user who follows it reads a page about `::: {.list-table}` divs — unrelated to the error they hit.

**Why the existing lints miss it.** `error-docs-page-missing` reconciles catalog codes against page existence and docs_url format; `error-docs-sidebar-unlisted` reconciles pages against sidebar entries. Neither checks that a code's catalog/page text matches what the code is actually emitted for, and neither notices two emitters sharing one code. A rule that reconciles the error-corpus titles against the catalog titles would catch this class.

Fix requires deciding which diagnostic keeps Q-2-35 and allocating a new code for the other, then updating catalog + docs page + sidebar + corpus together.

Found while verifying a plan assumption during bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj (the plan claimed empty-class CodeBlocks 'cover a 4-space indented code block'; qmd in fact rejects them outright).

title: qmd-syntax-helper rule: migrate reference-style links and escape literal brackets
description: SCOPE FIRST, so nobody starts down the wrong path: this is NOT a request to make the qmd parser accept reference-style links. Decided 2026-08-10 (Carlos): [...] is reserved for span syntax and the parser will not support reference links in general. The ask is a **qmd-syntax-helper migration rule** that rewrites the source, plus an open question about a diagnostic (below). WHAT HAPPENS. q2 parses [...] as the bracket half of span syntax ([text]{.class}); finding no attribute block it emits a bare and discards the brackets, and link reference definitions are never collected. Three shapes, all silent — no warning, no error: input q2 0.16.0 Quarto 1 [label][ref] (+ [ref]: url) labelref label [ref]: url (definition line) rendered as a visible paragraph consumed, never rendered [Version TBD] (no definition) Version TBD — brackets gone literal text [Version TBD] The user-visible results are "the RedHat documentationgcc-toolset" and "noexecnoexec" where a link should be, a stray paragraph of "gcc-toolset: https://... noexec: https://..." at the end of the document, and quietly vanishing brackets in ordinary prose. WHERE IT LIVES. crates/qmd-syntax-helper/. The tool already anticipates this exact converter: its README lists "Reference-style links -> inline links" under **Future Converters**. Rules implement the Rule trait in crates/qmd-syntax-helper/src/rule.rs (name/description/check/convert, registered through RuleRegistry) and live in crates/qmd-syntax-helper/src/conversions/. Named rules (grid_tables.rs, definition_lists.rs, apostrophe_quotes.rs, attribute_ordering.rs) sit alongside diagnostic-code-keyed ones (q_2_NN.rs); this one is a named rule today because q2 emits no diagnostic to key off. SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION. One rule, three rewrites, only the first two mechanical: 1. Reference WITH a matching definition — [label][ref], [label][], shortcut [ref] — becomes the inline form [label](url), and the "[ref]: url" definition line is dropped once its last use is gone. Title-bearing definitions ('[ref]: url "Title"') carry over as [label](url "Title"). 2. Bracketed text with NO matching definition — [Version TBD], [1], "[Posit Connect]" — must be escaped to \[Version TBD\], otherwise the brackets are silently deleted. Verified in both directions: q2 0.16.0 renders \[...\] as literal brackets, and so does Quarto 1, so the escaped form is safe to write into sources that still have to build under both engines. 3. Genuine span syntax — [text]{.class} — left alone. The escaping pass in (2) must therefore skip any ']' followed by '{', and also '(' and '[', so it does not corrupt inline links or the references already handled in (1). Caveat for whoever writes it: (2) is the destructive-if-wrong case, because an escape is a source edit that cannot later be distinguished from an author's intent. A --check mode enumerating every bracket it would escape, run before any --in-place pass, is worth having. OPEN QUESTION — diagnostic, possibly a sibling strand. q2 emits nothing at all for any of the three shapes; the brackets just vanish and stray definition lines render as text. That is why this went unnoticed until a full-site text diff against the Q1 render. A diagnostic for a block-level line matching the link-reference-definition shape would make the breakage self-reporting AND give the rule a Q-code to key off, matching the q_2_NN.rs convention. Whether that rides on this strand or a separate one is undecided. REAL-WORLD HIT (Posit Connect docs, ~7 pages). Broken links plus a leaked definition paragraph: admin/process-management (the "[the RedHat documentation][gcc-toolset]" link and a "[`noexec`][noexec]" mount-option link) and admin/integrations/package-manager ("[portable-binaries]"). Silently deleted brackets, three of which change meaning rather than formatting: admin/security, where the CSRF explanation refers to a numbered diagram via "[1]" and "[2]" and now reads "upon an initial user session 1, the server creates a cookie (RSC-XSRF) 2"; admin/appendix/branding and admin/email, where the documented default mail subject prefix is literally "[Posit Connect]" and renders as "Posit Connect", i.e. the docs now state the wrong value; admin/opentelemetry/signal-reference-guide, whose histogram bucket lists "[1, 5, 15, ...]" lose their brackets; and user/quarto ("Posit Connect [Version TBD] or later"). REPRO. /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/reference-links-unsupported/ — run 'q2 render' there and compare with 'quarto render'. index.qmd covers all three shapes with the definitions at the bottom; README.md has expected vs actual markup side by side plus the full routing rationale above. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-raalju6n. Observed with q2 0.16.0; re-verified against origin/main @ b2b6100c (v0.16.0 + docs commits), where nothing has touched reference-link or bracket handling.
close_reason: Implemented and merged in PR #497 (def51475). Two qmd-syntax-helper rules — 'reference-links' (mechanical) and 'literal-brackets' (opt-in escaping) — sharing an AST-based detector, plus Q-2-45/Q-2-46 render-time warnings with catalog entries and docs pages so the breakage is self-reporting. 55 new tests; full cargo xtask verify green; all 8 CI checks green. End-to-end on a copy of the real Connect docs (383 files): found 12 issues across exactly the 7 pages named here plus three uncatalogued ones, converted only those 7 files, and re-check reported 0. Rendered output inspected before/after — the RedHat link is a real <a href>, the leaked gcc-toolset definition paragraphs are gone, and admin/email now documents '[Posit Connect]' rather than the wrong value 'Posit Connect'. Codes are 45/46 not 42/43: main claimed 42-44 for conditional content and callout titles while the branch was in flight.

c-06bi9jgb.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-06bi9jgb.text: Design settled with Carlos 2026-08-10; plan is now implementable (claude-notes/plans/2026-08-10-reference-links-migration.md @ 991787ea). Decisions: image arm folded in; TWO rules split by risk — 'reference-links' (mechanical, safe) and 'literal-brackets' (destructive escaping, opt-in so 'convert -r all' never fires it unasked); diagnostic in this strand; decline-and-report on adjacency runs of 3+. Two probes done since: (a) image detection is structurally PARALLEL to span detection — the predicate is Inline::Image with an empty url, its SourceInfo range covers '![alt]' including the bang and both brackets, and the following [ref] span touches it exactly, so the SAME adjacency test handles ![alt][ref] and [label][ref]; ![real](u.png) is excluded by its non-empty url just as [x]{.cls} is by its non-empty attr. The image escape form is '!\\[solo\\]' and produces no Image node in q2, so it is idempotent, and Q1 renders it identically. (b) Corpus grep for [a][b][c] chains across both Connect trees: two hits, BOTH inside fenced code blocks (response['data']['data'] and response.json()['results'][0]) — zero real chains in prose, so the 3+ guard is cheap insurance, not load-bearing. One limitation recorded explicitly in the plan: the diagnostic's two triggers (definition-shaped line; two adjacent bare spans) catch the reference-links shapes but NOT lone bare brackets like [Version TBD] — diagnosing every bare span would be noisy since [text] -> <span> can be deliberate. That means the three meaning-changing Connect pages (admin/security, branding, email) are all lone-bracket cases the diagnostic will not catch, which is precisely why literal-brackets stays check-first and opt-in. Next free error code is Q-2-42 (Q-2-41 is highest allocated). Implementation starts at Phase 0, tests first.

c-bef0pt6y.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-bef0pt6y.text: All six phases implemented on branch braid/bd-reference-links-unsupported-ddc4skac (fa102fa0). cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build green. NOT pushed, no PR. Shipped: (1) qmd-syntax-helper rules 'reference-links' (mechanical) and 'literal-brackets' (opt-in escaping), sharing an AST-based detector; new Rule::opt_in_only() keeps the destructive arm out of 'convert -r all' while 'check -r all' still reports it. (2) Q-2-42 / Q-2-43 render-time warnings so the breakage is finally self-reporting, with catalog entries and docs/errors/markdown pages. 55 new tests. End-to-end on a copy of the real Connect docs (383 files): check found 12 issues across exactly the 7 pages named in this strand, plus three uncatalogued ones ([3]/[4] in admin/security, a second [version TBD] in user/quarto, [PositConnect] in branding); convert touched only those 7 files; re-check reports 0 issues. Rendered output inspected before/after -- the RedHat link becomes a real <a href>, the two leaked gcc-toolset definition paragraphs disappear, and admin/email now documents '[Posit Connect]' instead of the wrong value 'Posit Connect'. Three things worth flagging for review. (a) The diagnostic went into a quarto-core Normalization transform rather than qmd-syntax-helper: the error-corpus machinery maps parse STATES to messages and these documents parse fine, and the closest precedent (Q-2-30) is qmd-syntax-helper-only, which would have left q2 render silent -- the exact gap this strand complains about. Detection turned out to be AST-only (two consecutive bare-Span siblings; a line-initial bare Span followed by Str ':'), so it needed no new pampa API. (b) The diagnostic deliberately does NOT fire on a lone [Version TBD] -- indistinguishable from a deliberate [text] span -- so the three meaning-changing pages are not covered by it; that is precisely why literal-brackets stays check-first and opt-in. (c) Two behaviours to sanity-check: reference-links DELETES unused definitions (Q1 renders them as nothing, q2 as a stray paragraph, so deleting restores parity but does remove an authored line), and definition destination/title splitting follows Pandoc's rule -- peel a trailing quoted title, keep everything else including spaces as the destination -- verified against quarto pandoc in all four combinations, because the naive split-at-first-space silently drops definitions.

c-nu4jxg5w.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-nu4jxg5w.text: Investigated 2026-08-10 on main @ 05c2454e. Plan skeleton: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-10-reference-links-migration.md; probes + findings in claude-notes/plans/reference-links-migration-investigation/. Verdict: ready to design. Three findings that change the shape of the work: (1) detection can be AST-based rather than regex — pampa gives every Span an empty-or-not Attr plus a SourceInfo byte range that includes the brackets, so [x]{.cls}, [link](u) and code spans are excluded structurally and the ']' lookahead in the description becomes unnecessary; (2) escaping is idempotent (\\[..\\] produces no Span at all) and renders as literal brackets in both q2 and Q1, re-verified in both directions — this matters because 'convert' defaults to -r all and iterates up to 10x; (3) there is a FOURTH damage shape not in the description: ![alt][ref] and bare ![alt] emit — a broken image, not lost text — which needs an Image-keyed arm. Open questions for Carlos are in the plan: image arm in scope?, how to gate the destructive escaping arm (I lean: separate named rule so 'convert -r all' never escapes unless asked), diagnostic here or sibling strand?, rule name(s), and [a][b][c] ambiguity.

title: A page can fail with no attribution at all: bare 'Parse error' with no file, line or frame
description:
A page can fail during a project render with no attribution at all: the render reports errors, drops the page, and never names the file. Two observed shapes.

SHAPE 1 -- a fatal diagnostic emitted with no source span at all.

The Positron website's download.qmd on the 0.26.0 release. knitr executes it successfully -- the log shows 'processing file: download.rmarkdown' then 'output file: download.knit.md', with no R error anywhere in a 2733-line transcript -- and then q2 emits, three times:

    Error: Parse error
    unexpected character or token here

No ariadne frame, no path, no line, no column, no source snippet. download.html is never written. The only other trace is a downstream 'Warning: No markdown companion content for download.html'. The string 'download.qmd' does not appear anywhere in the render output.

What makes this specifically a bug rather than a hard case: every OTHER parse error in the same render carries a full frame -- file, line, column, caret, and the offending source line. These three carry nothing. Whatever path emits them has lost the span, or never had one, and the generic fallback prints the bare message rather than declining to print an unlocatable error.

Reproduced in isolation: a directory containing only download.qmd, _download.html, _environment and a minimal _quarto.yml gives exactly the same three bare errors and 'Rendered 0 of 1 files ... 3 errors'. Note _environment must be present -- with it, the R chunk succeeds and you get this bug; without it, RELEASE_VERSION is unset and you get an unrelated (and correctly attributed) knitr failure instead.

SHAPE 2 -- engine failures name the knitr intermediate, never the source.

A chunk that calls stop() in a project render prints its traceback against 'failing.rmarkdown', never 'failing.qmd'; grepping the whole transcript for the .qmd name returns zero matches, and the reported line numbers are offsets into the generated intermediate, not the source. The committed repro pins the boundary empirically -- it is PROJECT CONTEXT, not how many files are being rendered, that flips the behaviour:

    cd control && q2 render failing.qmd    (no _quarto.yml)   names failing.qmd
    cd repro   && q2 render failing.qmd    (has _quarto.yml)  does NOT
    cd repro   && q2 render                (2 files)          does NOT

The standalone path prints 'Rendering single file: /.../failing.qmd' up front, which is what supplies the attribution; the project path prints 'Rendering project: ...' and nothing per-file.

The two shapes probably have different fixes -- shape 1 is a diagnostic emitted without its span, shape 2 is source-mapping from the engine intermediate back to the .qmd -- but they present to the user as the same thing: the render says a page died and will not say which.

Suggested direction: whatever the per-file fix, a project render could also guarantee attribution structurally -- when a document fails, report it against the document being processed, so that even a span-less diagnostic is wrapped in 'while rendering <file>'. That would make both shapes non-fatal to debuggability without needing every emit site audited first.

Real-world hit. download.qmd is one of only four files that still fail to render in the Positron port, and it is the most linked-to page in the site: 83 of 89 rendered pages reference download.html, which makes it the largest single group in both link sweeps (83 broken references; 155 lychee errors). It went misdiagnosed on our side for weeks as a freeze problem, because the render output gave no evidence pointing anywhere else.

Repro: /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/freeze-ignored-silent-failure/silent-failure/
Run 'q2 render' in repro/ and in control/ and compare; README.md at the parent directory carries the boundary table and full transcripts for shape 2. Shape 1's reproduction is described above and is a three-file project; it is not committed because download.qmd fetches release checksums over the network, so it is not self-contained -- ask if a synthetic version would help and I will build one. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path.

Observed with the official q2 0.26.0 release build; source checkout was at 596ceb572 (v0.26.0-28) at the time.

Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-render-failure-unattributed-l1ksf340. Split out of br-freeze-ignored-silent-failure-u0rccol0, which is now scoped to the freeze gap alone and is NOT being handed off (freeze is unimplemented upstream by design, tracked as 'when freeze lands' in bd-mx5x609r).

c-gmykzans.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-gmykzans.text:
Fixed on branch braid/bd-render-failure-unattributed-yxe0v7th-render-failure-unattributed (commit 0e2d6fe8f, worktree workspace-4). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-render-failure-unattributed.md

ROOT CAUSE, SHAPE 1 -- not a diagnostic emitted without a span. The span exists and is correct; it is bound to the wrong buffer.

EngineExecutionStage parses the engine's executed markdown, so those spans index into result.markdown. Its Err path returned a bare StageError, discarding the SourceContext (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs). run_pipeline's generic StageError -> QuartoError::Parse conversion (crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs) then FABRICATES a SourceContext from the original document's bytes and binds the engine-output spans to it. Measured on a 106-byte knit.qmd: span offset 4716, bound buffer 106 bytes. map_offset fails, so ariadne renders nothing AND to_text_with_renderer's 'at <file>:<row>:<col>' fallback is skipped with it -- which is why not even the filename survived.

NEW FINDING, worse than reported. The no-frame case is only what happens when the offset lands past EOF. On a source long enough to contain it, the same bug prints a fully-formed, CONFIDENT ariadne frame at an arbitrary wrong location. Measured on a 14576-byte big.qmd: reported at big.qmd:68:100, caret on the letter 'e' of a filler paragraph containing no shortcode at all. Silently wrong attribution, with nothing to signal it is wrong. Same defect class as the add-file-with-id lint rule's rationale (bd-m6wmztln).

ROOT CAUSE, SHAPE 2 -- print_render_diagnostics_text named the file only for legacy_failures (failures with NO structured diagnostics). Anything carrying diagnostics went through coalesce_by_source, which names files purely via the diagnostic's own span and deliberately omits the 'Affected files:' tail for singleton groups, so the known-good FileFailure.input was discarded. --json-errors was never affected: it reads input structurally as source_file. Only the text path lost it.

FIXES. (1) The stage binds engine-output spans to the buffer they index and returns PipelineError::Structured, which run_pipeline passes through untouched. (2) failure_attribution_line adds 'error: while rendering <path>' when the rendered output does not name the page that failed -- unlocatable spans, plus spans resolving elsewhere. Ordinary parse errors resolve to their own .qmd and are byte-identical, so nothing existing churned.

Note on the agreed predicate: we settled on 'only when unlocatable', but fix (1) changed what that covers -- engine-output errors now resolve perfectly well, against the .rmarkdown. A pure unlocatable test would have gone quiet again on exactly this strand's case, so the predicate is 'output does not name the failing page' instead.

Verified end-to-end through the real binary, output inspected. Shape 1 now:

    error: while rendering /.../knit.qmd
    Error: [Q-2-34] Unquoted shortcode parameter starting with digit
         ╭─[ /.../knit.knitr.rmarkdown:138:23 ]
     138 │ {{< fa envelope size=1x >}}
         │                       ╰── Shortcode parameter values starting with digits must be quoted.

Shape 2 on your committed repro: 'error: while rendering /.../repro/failing.qmd'.

+10 tests (2 engine_execution, 6 render.rs unit, 2 knitr-gated CLI e2e via the marimo_engine_e2e rscript_available/knitr_r_package_available pattern). Workspace 13140 passed / 199 skipped vs a live stashed baseline of 13130; that baseline's one failure (engine::ts_engine::tests::test_race_free_instance_exclusive) is a pre-existing flake, green in the with-changes run.

SCOPED OUT, agreed with you: remapping .rmarkdown line numbers back to .qmd. Filed as bd-1ng2ivis. Both shapes now name the page; shape 2's traceback still cites failing.rmarkdown:133-135, and the new shape-1 frame is anchored in the intermediate. That strand notes serialize_ast_to_qmd already computes a SourceInfo which may be the raw material.

Not pushed -- awaiting your review.

title: Q-5-13 only fires when a render pattern matches NOTHING, so a narrowing pattern silently drops a whole subtree
description:
`project.render: ["*.qmd"]` renders the top-level .qmd files and silently
ignores every subdirectory. That is settled design — `*` matching one
directory level is deliberate, and any positive pattern replaces the default
`**/*.qmd` outright. The behaviour is not the bug. The SILENCE is.

Q-5-13 already exists and already carries exactly the right hint text
("In Quarto 2, `*` matches within one directory level — write `**/` to search
subdirectories"). The problem is its predicate, at
crates/quarto-core/src/project/discovery.rs:~508:

    let matched = selected.iter().any(|doc| {
        doc.input.strip_prefix(project_dir)
            .is_ok_and(|rel| single.matches_path(rel))
    });
    if !matched { /* warn Q-5-13 */ }

It is `any()`, so a pattern that matches SOMETHING is silent no matter how much
it excludes. Demonstrated on a three-file project (index.qmd, sub/a.qmd,
sub/b.qmd):

    (no render: key)                 Rendered 3 of 3   0 diagnostics
    render: ["*.qmd"]                Rendered 1 of 3   0 diagnostics   <- the gap
    render: ["nonexistent-*.qmd"]    Rendered 0 of 0   Q-5-13 fires

So Q-5-13 appears ZERO times in a real render log for the one pattern shape
that actually costs the author pages. It fires only for a pattern that is
already obviously useless.

WHY A NAIVE "YOU EXCLUDED N FILES" WARNING IS WRONG

The obvious fix — compare against what `**/*.qmd` would have selected and warn
on the difference — must be rejected. Authors legitimately render a subset of
their .qmd files, and such a warning would fire on every render of every such
project with no way to silence it. An unsilenceable warning about intentional
behaviour is noise, and noise is what makes real diagnostics get ignored.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MAKES IT ACTIONABLE

q2 supports negative render patterns, and a negation-only list subtracts from
the default (effective_render_patterns, discovery.rs:~250, documented at
:243-247). That gives an author two ways to render a subset, which are
behaviourally identical and semantically different. Measured on the same
fixture, all three render exactly one file:

    render: ["*.qmd"]                 "render top-level qmds" — drops sub/ as a side effect
    render: ["!sub/**"]               "render everything except sub/" — deliberate
    render: ["*.qmd", "!sub/**"]      also deliberate

So the predicate should not ask HOW MANY files were excluded. It should ask
WHETHER THE EXCLUSION WAS EXPRESSED:

  - a renderable file matched by no pattern at all  -> unaccounted for, warn
  - a renderable file matched by a `!` negation     -> the author said so, silent

That makes the diagnostic actionable in the way an "N files excluded" warning
is not. The author who meant it has a real one-line fix — add `!release-notes/**`,
or add `**/*.qmd` back — and it both silences the warning and records the intent
in the config where the next reader can see it. The author who did not mean it
finds out before the pages vanish.

It also stays quiet in the common cases: no `render:` key, negation-only lists,
and any list whose positives and negatives together cover the tree.

Suggested message shape, reusing Q-5-13's existing hint verbatim:

    `project.render` does not match 13 renderable files under `release-notes/`.
    If that is intended, exclude them explicitly with a `!` pattern
    (`"!release-notes/**"`); otherwise widen the pattern.

OPEN QUESTION, worth deciding before implementing

Is there a real project shape where the renderable set is a small enumerated
list and the rest of the tree is many unrelated .qmd files — a monorepo, a
docs site beside a fixture corpus? Enumerating negations there would be worse
than the warning. If that shape is common the honest answer may be an explicit
opt-out (a `render-strict: false`-style key, or the diagnostic being
suppressible by code) rather than a cleverer predicate. Worth a decision rather
than an assumption.

RELATED

- bd-m9rm (goal 2, "add a clear project-level diagnostic when the render set is
  empty") is the ancestor of Q-5-13; this is the same concern one step further
  in — a render set that is not empty but is quietly smaller than the author
  believes.
- bd-98m98wg8 (EPIC: display an executable cell without executing it) is the
  design precedent: q2 deliberately reserves a syntax to mean "do not do the
  thing", and part of that epic is making the diagnostic fire on the form
  authors actually write rather than the theoretical one. Same shape here — `!`
  is the supported way to say "deliberately do not render these", and the
  diagnostic should fire when the author has not used it.

REAL-WORLD COST

The Positron docs `_quarto.yml` carried `render: ["*.qmd"]`. Quarto 1 renders
all 119 pages from that, including 13 under `release-notes/`; q2 rendered 85.
Downstream, older-releases.html linked to 13 nonexistent pages and the sidebar
and pagination lost them. The only warnings in the entire render log were two
Q-12-19 pointing at older-releases.qmd's LISTING globs — the downstream symptom
— so an author following the diagnostics would widen the listing pattern and
fix nothing.

REPRO

  /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/render-glob-not-recursive/

Three projects: repro/ (the narrowing pattern, silent), control/ (the same tree
with `**/*.qmd`), no-render-key/ (the default). Render each and compare the
"Rendered N of M" line and the diagnostic count.

VERSION

Predicate confirmed unchanged at q2 source main 9ad1d4420; behaviour measured
on the 0.28.0 release binary. Originally found on 0.24.0.

Origin strand: br-render-pattern-narrowing-undiagnosed-fh9thmg7 in the
q2-positron-docs skein.

title: website repo-actions: accepted by the schema, never rendered, and no diagnostic says so
description:
website.repo-actions is accepted as valid configuration and then silently ignored: no links are emitted, and no diagnostic says so. Quarto 1 renders each configured action twice per page -- once at the foot of the right-margin TOC, once in the page footer (the footer copy carries d-sm-block d-md-none, so it is the small-screen fallback for the TOC one). With repo-actions: [edit, source, issue] that is six links per page:
  • Edit this page
  • View source
  • Report an issue
q2 0.26.0 renders none of them and exits 0 with no warnings. This is a KNOWN, DELIBERATE MVP exclusion, so the feature request itself should be no surprise: bd-0tr6 lists repo-actions among what the websites MVP "explicitly excludes", and claude-notes/plans/2026-04-27-websites-phase-7.md:1026 repeats it ("No repo-actions (edit-on-github)"). This strand is filed the way breadcrumbs was -- bd-breadcrumbs-missing-1vpuqh34, same exclusion list, filed separately, now closed and implemented -- because that route has already worked once. The part that may be less expected is the silence. crates/pampa/test-fixtures/schemas/definitions.yml:705 declares repo-actions, so the key validates as legal configuration; but grepping crates/ and resources/ for 'repo-actions' or 'edit this page' finds no config field, no template, and no emit site. The author gets neither the feature nor any signal that their configuration was dropped, which is the worst of the three possible states. Even ahead of the feature, a 'configured but not implemented' diagnostic would turn a silent omission into something discoverable -- and would generalise to the rest of the exclusion list, which has the same shape. Suggested fix direction: the data needed is all config plus the page's source path -- repo-url, repo-branch, and the document's path relative to the project root -- and q2 already threads all three for other purposes. The URL forms are {repo-url}/edit/{branch}/{path}, {repo-url}/blob/{branch}/{path}, and {repo-url}/issues/new. Both emission sites are places q2 already authors markup (TOC nav and page footer), so this looks closer to the breadcrumbs shape than to a subsystem. Real-world hit. In the Positron website port this accounts for the entire toc:3 and footer:3 buckets of the chrome comparison: footer:3 on ALL 81 chrome-differing pages, toc:3 on 73 of them (the eight without it have no TOC). Because footer:3 is present on every differing page, it is the first link in that port's chrome chain -- no page clears the comparison until this lands, however much else is fixed. It has the largest page reach of any single strand in that project. Repro: /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/repo-actions-missing/ A two-page website with repo-url, repo-branch and repo-actions: [edit, source, issue], and toc: true so the TOC surface exists. Run 'q2 render' -- exit 0, and 'grep -c "Edit this page\|View source\|Report an issue" _site/index.html' returns 0. Run 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1' and the same grep returns 6 (2 of each). README.md has both Q1 regions in full, the URL-construction table, and the counts. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path. Observed with the official q2 0.26.0 release build; source checkout at 596ceb572 (v0.26.0-28). Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-repo-actions-missing-ivjaa1nd.

c-xsqb3264.author: Gordon Woodhull

title: quarto-json: source-mapped JSON parsing crate (analogous to quarto-yaml) so engine-protocol and other JSON diagnostics can point at a location
description: Motivation: bd-gy2ozix3 (GH #683) surfaces malformed engine results (e.g. knitr's results JSON) with a serde_path_to_error field path (includes.include-in-header) but no source location — serde_json only yields line/column and the value is not source-mapped. A quarto-json crate analogous to quarto-yaml (posit-dev/quarto-yaml) would parse JSON into a source-tracked value so diagnostics could carry a real (if intermediate-file) location, and could serve other JSON consumers (engine protocols, .ipynb, extension manifests). Admittedly the location points at an intermediate artifact; still, it gives quarto-error-reporting a span to render. Deliberately not done for bd-gy2ozix3 — a large change not justified by one internal error message. Scope when picked up: survey JSON parse sites in quarto-core/pampa for consumers, decide whether to extract to a posit-dev repo like quarto-yaml, and whether to reuse quarto-source-map.

title: Tiling auditor never walks ast.meta — metadata provenance is unguarded
description:
audit_source_range_tiling (crates/pampa/src/writers/incremental.rs:1080) calls only audit_block_siblings(&ast.blocks, ...). It never visits ast.meta, so document-metadata provenance is entirely outside the auditor's reach — including the new corpus driver tests/integration/tiling_corpus_tests.rs added for bd-1d6io. A green corpus run means 'no block-content violations', not 'no violations'.

There is a known live defect sitting in that blind spot. bd-mxa44voa (quote-inclusive YAML spans vs decoded scalars) produces shifted inline sub-ranges under meta. For ts-packages/annotated-qmd/examples/academic-paper.qmd, 'author: "Dr. Alice Smith"':

  meta.author      MetaInlines [71,88] '"Dr. Alice Smith"'
  meta.author.c[0] Str         [71,80] '"Dr. Alic'   (text: "Dr.")
  meta.author.c[1] Space       [80,81] 'e'
  meta.author.c[2] Str         [81,86] ' Smit'       (text: "Smith")

c[2] is a Str with a leading space byte its text does not retain — a textbook TightnessViolation the auditor would name exactly, if it looked. So extending the walk to ast.meta would catch bd-mxa44voa for free, which is the main argument for doing it.

SECOND, SEPARATE HOLE found in the same analysis: c[1] is a Space claiming the non-whitespace byte 'e'. The auditor would still miss that even with meta walked, because audit_inline_siblings (incremental.rs:1367) skips Space/SoftBreak/LineBreak wholesale before check_tightness. A Space claiming non-whitespace is a real violation and the wholesale skip is too coarse to see it. See the sibling strand on unifying the two exclusion mechanisms — the retained-text parameter added for bd-1d6io makes a precise version cheap.

Why this was not done under bd-1d6io: out of scope there (that strand is the attr-key tightness fix plus the corpus driver), and it does not block it. Recorded because the branch's central claim — that the corpus auditor asserts a property that cannot be laundered by regenerating a fixture — holds only for block content, and the annotated-qmd fixtures now freeze the known-bad academic-paper meta ranges.

Found during code review of bd-1d6io (branch braid/bd-1d6io-p1-attr-key-tightness).

title: Diagnostics from _variables.yml parsing are discarded (stage/context.rs:911)
description:
Found in the final whole-branch review of Plan 2 of the provenance epic (feature/yaml-provenance, commit 02aced14a).

stage/context.rs:911 builds a FRESH DiagnosticCollector for its yaml_to_config_value call on _variables.yml and then drops it, while the enclosing function already holds `diagnostics: &mut Vec<DiagnosticMessage>`. So every diagnostic produced while parsing _variables.yml is silently lost.

PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to provenance -- all diagnostics from that path were already being dropped. It surfaces now only because Plan 2 added a new signal (the content-provenance desync warning) that is invisible at this site, which is what drew the reviewer's eye.

Fix is presumably to thread the existing &mut Vec through instead of constructing a throwaway collector. Worth checking whether any other call site in stage/context.rs does the same thing.

Filed as out-of-plan: it belongs to no active plan in the provenance epic (Plans 1-3), and Plan 3's scope is the provenance audit, not diagnostic plumbing.

Work complete locally on branch braid/bd-rl9ng0al-remove-leftover-beads-dir, one commit, unpushed and awaiting review. 31 files, 34 insertions, 1763 deletions.
