title: Body links to directories are not page-relativized (the same index-miss fallthrough as nav hrefs)
description:
A markdown link whose target is a DIRECTORY rather than a source file is emitted verbatim, so a site-root-relative form survives into the output and breaks under a deploy subpath. Linking a section landing page by its directory is ordinary authoring, and Quarto 1 rebases it.

From a page two directories down, the same landing page written four ways:

  [dir slash](/target/)            Q1: ../../target/             q2: /target/                  WRONG
  [dir bare](/target)              Q1: ../../target              q2: /target                   WRONG
  [source file](/target/index.md)  Q1: ../../target/index.html   q2: ../../target/index.html   ok
  [root](/index.qmd)               Q1: ../../index.html          q2: ../../index.html          ok

The bottom two rows are the controls: q2 rebases a root-absolute link correctly the moment the path names a file the ProjectIndex knows. Nothing warns about the top two.

Root cause: resolve_doc_relative_href (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_href.rs:308) rebases only through an index hit at :334; '/target/' is not a source path, so it misses and the function returns raw.to_string() at :358 — leading slash and all. The miss is silent because the diagnostic there is deliberately .qmd-only (bd-6d2wj4zp D6, so that a .md miss can be a legitimate static resource).

This is the SAME defect as bd-tef2lm9j, in the sibling function. resolve_href_for_html (:152) does the index lookup at :178 and falls to an identical raw.to_string() at :205, with the identical .qmd-only diagnostic convention. Nav hrefs and body links are two call sites of one unanswered question: what should a resolver do when the index does not know the target? A root-absolute href is never correct verbatim for a site deployed under a subpath, whether or not it happens to name a source file.

Suggested fix direction, and it is the same sentence as bd-tef2lm9j's: on an index miss, route through resolve_root_relative_resource_href (:434) — the thin wrapper over resolve_static_resource_href (:393) that anchors at the project root and page-relativizes — instead of returning raw. That helper already exists, is already documented with exactly this rationale ('one config value serve pages at every depth'), and is already what Case B/C of bd-root-relative-paths-design-fc5pvkcv routes images and config inlines through. Doing it in one place for both functions is what makes this a structural fix rather than two patches.

Connect docs impact: one link, admin/security/server-user/index.md:82 —

  [off-host execution installation instructions](/admin/getting-started/off-host-install/)

Q1 emits ../../../admin/getting-started/off-host-install/; q2 emits the path unchanged. The docs are served from https://docs.posit.co/connect/, so the q2 form resolves outside the site and 404s in production while working in every local _site check — the failure mode is invisible to a local server rooted at _site, which is how the port has been reviewed throughout. It was the only new root-absolute path left in the whole 352-page site after the 0.21.0 path fixes landed; the remaining five are the raw-HTML-in-_quarto.yml case still open under bd-root-relative-paths-design-fc5pvkcv.

Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/root-absolute-dir-link/ (see README.md; run 'q2 render' there and compare with 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1'; deep/deeper/index.html holds all four rows above, two of them as controls). Origin strand in the Posit Connect docs porting skein: br-h5wdib27. Observed with q2 0.21.0; re-verified against main at 3ac596e0, which has no commits touching navigation_href.rs or link_rewrite.rs since the v0.21.0 tag.
close_reason: Fixed on main in the same commit as bd-tef2lm9j — one answer, two call sites, as the strand argued. resolve_doc_relative_href routes non-.qmd misses through resolve_static_resource_href (doc-relative anchoring); trailing slash preserved so [x](/section/) emits ../../section/ exactly like Q1. .qmd misses keep Q-13-4 + verbatim; .md misses stay silent (D6) but now relativize. e2e: four-row repro verified through the real binary, output inspected.

c-42mxkdrp.author: Claude (q2-connect-docs)
c-42mxkdrp.text:
Filed as the body-link half of a pair. Linked related: bd-tef2lm9j (the nav-surface half) and bd-root-relative-paths-design-fc5pvkcv (the design question both sit under). bd-breadcrumbs-missing-1vpuqh34 is blocked on this strand and on bd-tef2lm9j — see below for why that ordering is deliberate.

The two halves are the same six lines in two sibling functions of crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_href.rs:

  resolve_href_for_html      :152   lookup :178   miss -> raw.to_string() :205   (bd-tef2lm9j, nav hrefs)
  resolve_doc_relative_href  :308   lookup :334   miss -> raw.to_string() :358   (this strand, body links)

Same .qmd-only diagnostic convention on both misses (bd-6d2wj4zp D6), same verbatim fallthrough, same consequence: a site-root-relative href survives to output and breaks under a deploy subpath. They are worth fixing in one pass, because the substantive question — what should a resolver do when the ProjectIndex does not know the target? — has one answer, and answering it twice invites the two call sites to drift.

Line numbers are against main at 3ac596e0.

title: Design: site-root-relative paths — three cases, and what replaces Q1's deno-dom rewrite for raw HTML
description: DESIGN SESSION. Three separate defects share one symptom — a path that survives into the rendered page unchanged, works when the site is served at a domain root, and 404s when it is served from a subdirectory. Two are ordinary gaps with an obvious fix. The third cannot be fixed the way Quarto 1 fixed it and needs a deliberate decision. Filing them together because fixing the first two without settling the third produces a site that is *almost* portable, which is worse than one that is visibly not. Everything below was verified on q2 0.20.0 against Quarto 1 (99.9.9) on the same sources. ## The shared consequence Quarto 1 rewrites every site-root-relative path into a page-relative one, so a site keeps working under a deploy subpath. Its rendered output for the Posit Connect documentation contains ZERO root-absolute paths. q2's output for the same sources keeps six on every page. That site's site-url is https://docs.posit.co/connect/ — a subdirectory — so all six resolve outside the site in production. They all resolve fine from a local server rooted at the output directory, which is how every check in that porting project had looked at them. Nothing warns. This class of bug is invisible to a rendered-text diff, so it survived six release sweeps and surfaced only when someone opened a page in a browser for an unrelated reason. ## Case A — navbar logo is never rebased (simple gap) website.navbar.logo is emitted verbatim on every page: page Quarto 1 q2 0.20.0 index.html ./images/logo.svg images/logo.svg deep/deeper/index.html ../../images/logo.svg images/logo.svg Not an HTML-parsing problem: q2 authors that itself from its own config. And it rebases correctly in the same navbar — on a four-deep page in the Connect docs the nav links come out ../../../../index.html, matching Q1 exactly. Only the logo src is passed through. The asymmetry is visible in the struct. crates/quarto-navigation/src/navbar.rs:106-112: pub logo: Option, pub logo_alt: Option, pub logo_href: Option, /// `SourceInfo` of the YAML scalar that produced `logo_href`. /// bd-qor9a — paired with `logo_href` so the resolver knows which /// YAML file the brand link was authored in. pub logo_href_source: SourceInfo, logo_href has a paired source and goes through resolve_metadata_path (navbar_generate.rs:89) then resolve_href_for_html (navbar_render.rs:102). logo has neither, and no resolution anywhere. ## Case B — root-absolute paths rebase for links, not for images (ordinary gap, but the module docs are wrong) Same paragraph, page two levels down: [root](/index.qmd) -> ../../index.html (q2 correct, matches Q1) ![](/images/x.svg) -> /images/x.svg (Q1: ../../images/x.svg) -> /images/x.svg (Q1: ../../images/x.svg) The link row is the control that makes the image row a defect rather than a choice: both are ordinary AST nodes and q2 already resolves one of them. crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/link_rewrite.rs excludes images deliberately, and the stated reason is factually wrong. Its module docs, under "What it leaves alone": //! - `Image::target.0` — images point at static resources, not //! project documents (Q1 doesn't rewrite them either). Q1 does rewrite them. The parenthetical is true for RELATIVE image paths — those are already correct relative to the page and need no work — and false for root-absolute ones, which is the case that matters. Whatever this session decides, that comment should stop asserting Q1 parity it does not have. ## Case C — root-absolute paths inside raw HTML (the actual design question) This is the one that needs grappling with, and the reason this is a design strand rather than three bug reports. Quarto 1 catches these by parsing the rendered output with deno-dom and rewriting every src/href it finds, regardless of where the markup came from. Quarto 2 does not want to parse HTML to discover or rewrite resources. So the mechanism Q1 relied on is not available, and the question is what replaces it — including the possibility that the answer is "nothing, and here is the diagnostic that tells authors so". What this breaks in practice, from the Connect docs. Six root-absolute references survive into every rendered page, and all six originate in raw HTML in _quarto.yml: src=/images/posit-logos-2024_horiz-full-color.svg page-footer logo src=/images/posit-logo-fullcolor-TM.svg page-footer logo (dark) src=/images/cookie.svg cookie-preferences icon src=/images/cookie-copy.svg cookie-preferences icon href=/admin/licensing/index.md#product-tiers product-tier badge, 49 pages The page-footer entries are inline ``{=html} spans; the badge URL is a custom `quarto-tiers` metadata key read by that project's project type. The badge link is doubly wrong — still absolute AND still pointing at .md rather than the rendered .html. Q1 emits ../../../../admin/licensing/index.html#product-tiers for it. Note the same target written as an ordinary markdown link in a document body resolves correctly under q2, so the failure is specific to the config-declared raw-HTML form. ### The structural problem to grapple with A config-declared path is used by pages at every depth, so it CANNOT be authored as a page-relative literal. There is no string the author can write that is correct on both / and /a/b/c/. That is precisely why Q1 rewrites. Under q2 as it stands, an author whose markup is raw HTML has no correct option at all: - page-relative: impossible, the config value is shared across depths; - root-absolute: correct only when deployed at a domain root; - full URL from site-url: works, but hard-codes the deploy origin and, for versioned docs, the version segment. So "just don't write root-absolute paths in raw HTML" is not currently actionable advice. Options worth weighing, none of which I want to pre-judge: 1. A site-root-relative marker in config that q2 rebases per page — a YAML tag, or a documented convention that a leading `/` in a q2-owned config value means site-root and gets resolved. Handles the footer/badge cases without touching raw HTML at all, since q2 owns those config values even when their content is opaque. 2. Resolve the config value's raw HTML narrowly — not general HTML parsing, but a targeted rewrite of src/href attributes in q2-authored config strings. Cheap; needs an explicit decision that this is not the thin end of parsing HTML everywhere. 3. Emit nothing and diagnose: a Q-code for a root-absolute path reaching the output, pointing at whichever alternative the session settles on. At minimum this converts a silent production 404 into a build-time warning. Given warning suppression now exists (diagnostics:), a project that genuinely deploys at a domain root can opt out. 4. Site-url-derived absolute URLs as the documented answer, with the versioned-docs caveat spelled out. Also worth deciding in the same session, because it is the same boundary: which config-declared assets q2 copies. Today it copies exactly one — website.favicon, via copy_favicon in crates/quarto-core/src/project/website_post_render.rs, which even warns when the source file is missing — and nothing else. The navbar logo gets neither the copy nor the warning. In the Connect docs, before project.resources was declared, the ONLY file in the site's images/ directory was favicon.ico, put there by that function. Either favicon is deliberately special or the boundary drifted; worth stating which. ### Machinery that already exists q2 already has the function this needs, with exactly the right documented rationale, and one caller. crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_href.rs:382, resolve_static_resource_href, whose doc comment reads: /// This is what keeps an iframe `src` (or any embedded static path) /// portable: a page two directories deep emits `../../assets/x.html` /// rather than a host-absolute `/assets/x.html` that breaks under a /// deploy subpath. Its only caller outside its own module is example_embed.rs:386. Cases A and B both look like "route through this too". Case C is the one it cannot reach, because there is no AST node to hand it. Related: crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/resource_collector.rs walks the AST to collect resources for copying, which is why raw-HTML-referenced files are not copied either — the same blind spot, on the copy side rather than the URL side. title: Hub-client: parse error in another file is misattributed as 'Sidebar/Body link references unknown document'
description:
When a sibling page (e.g. about.qmd) fails Pass-1, opening a *different* page (e.g. index.qmd) shows two confusing warnings:
- 'Sidebar references unknown document about.qmd'
- 'Body link references unknown document about.qmd'

The file *exists*; it just failed to parse. The CLI also emits these warnings, but it additionally prints the underlying 'profile-pass skipped about.qmd: <diagnostic>' so a user can connect cause and effect. Hub-client never surfaces the Pass-1 failures at all — the diagnostics live on summary.pass1_failures[i].diagnostics and never cross the WASM boundary.

Root cause (located): crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1374-1428 ignores summary.pass1_failures entirely. The 'unknown document' warning itself is emitted at crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_href.rs:88-96 whenever ProjectIndex.get_profile(target) returns None.

Resolved fix shape (decisions D1, D2 in plan):
1. Add a dedicated 'pass1_failures' field to RenderResponse (per-entry { source_file, error, diagnostics }). Do NOT fold them into 'warnings'. Engine stays policy-free; consumers choose strict-vs-lenient (CLI: bd-creo; preview: this issue).
2. Add JsonDiagnostic.source_file: Option<String> so project-scoped warnings can be attributed.
3. PreviewErrorOverlay grows a section listing Pass-1 failures with source attribution and ariadne-style formatting.
4. navigation_href.rs wording change: 'references unknown document' → 'missing document information for' (proximal improvement; richer pass1-aware rewrite is a future task, not under this plan).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-01-hub-client-website-render-ux.md (Bug 1 + decisions D1/D2).

Note: bd-mwtf (active-page case) is the narrower routing fix; bd-creo is the CLI-strictness sibling sharing the same wire-shape change.

title: hub-client: cssVersion re-reads+re-hashes styles.css per render; use RenderResponse.theme_fingerprint instead
description: ts-packages/preview-runtime/src/wasmRenderer.ts:1091-1099: after every render, the TS side does vfsReadFile('/.quarto/project-artifacts/styles.css') + computeHash(content) to derive a cssVersion appended as an HTML comment (forces MorphIframe to re-apply CSS when only the theme changed). Two problems: (1) per-keystroke cost — a full read + hash of the CSS artifact on every render, O(artifact bytes); (2) likely wrong path for themed docs — CompileThemeCssStage stores the theme at quarto/quarto-theme-<fingerprint>.css (compile_theme_css.rs:541), so the styles.css read may only ever see the default (no-theme) CSS, silently degrading cssVersion to 'default' or a stale hash for themed projects. RenderResponse.theme_fingerprint (wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs extract_theme_fingerprint, plan 2A item 11) already carries exactly this change-signal, computed for free from the artifact key. Fix: switch cssVersion to result.theme_fingerprint (fall back to 'default' when None) and delete the VFS read + hash. Verify the MorphIframe re-apply-on-theme-change behavior still works (the original motivation for the comment) in a browser session.

c-htvief1z.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-htvief1z.text: Nuance from bd-q3bxnq2e Phase 2 (vitest env discovery): when theme SCSS sources are unavailable (or the doc has no theme), the compiled CSS lands at /.quarto/project-artifacts/styles.css and the wasmRenderer.ts read is CORRECT — it is not always the wrong path. theme_fingerprint is still present in both cases (fallback fp = default-bundle fingerprint), so switching cssVersion to theme_fingerprint remains the right fix: it covers themed AND fallback cases without the per-render read+hash.

title: Monaco qmd cell rule mismatched-brace colour (regression from bd-yrl8vqbg)
description: PR #307 fixed the executable-cell tokenizer crash by folding the opening { into the 'string'-typed capture group 1. Monaco ignores brackets inside string-typed tokens, so the closing } (in the 'attribute.value' group) reads as an unmatched bracket and renders in the mismatched-bracket colour. Fix: capture { into its own neutral non-string group so it matches its } symmetrically; keep nextEmbedded routing (shifts to $3). Same bug class as the documented [ / ] asymmetry.
close_reason: Mismatched/red-brace regression resolved by reverting #307 in PR #308 (merged). Baseline left as-is per user decision; the proper rule fix (Option B) was deliberately deferred — refile if ever wanted (design preserved in this strand's comments).

c-0cpnj9ct.author: shikokuchuo
c-0cpnj9ct.text: Reverted both the delimiter.curly approach (this session) AND PR #307 entirely. Restored quartoTheme.ts, quartoTheme.test.ts, changelog.md to pre-#307 baseline (fbd13884). delimiter.curly made the braces real Other-type brackets, so Monaco bracket-pair-colorization painted them bright red (likely unexpectedBracket) -- still undesirable. NOTE: reverting reintroduces the bd-yrl8vqbg crash (an r/python brace cell blanks the editor). Seeking a clean fix that (a) captures all chars so no Monaco array-action throw, and (b) keeps BOTH braces invisible to the bracket engine (symmetric string-typed groups, or single-action whole-line token) so there is no mismatch and no red. Strand stays open until the clean fix lands.

c-8dhph9jg.author: shikokuchuo
c-8dhph9jg.text: DECISION (2026-06-18): leave the baseline as-is. PR #307 is reverted; the qmd cell rule keeps the original (?:\{) form which throws when Monaco tokenizes a brace cell. This is NOT a session crash -- Monaco safeTokenize absorbs the throw (onUnexpectedError + plain-token fallback), so the only effect is console-error noise and that one fence line rendering unhighlighted. Option B (fold both fence braces into string-typed groups) was designed and ready but deliberately deferred. Do not re-implement without checking with the user. Session-safety is separately covered by the <Editor> error boundary (bd-c5j0ocgl).

c-fqvjafve.author: shikokuchuo
c-fqvjafve.text: Fixed in quartoTheme.ts: executable-cell rule now /^(\s*`{3,})(\{)([\w-]+)([^}]*\}.*)$/ with actions ['string','delimiter.curly',{token:'attribute.name',nextEmbedded:'$3',next:'@codeblock'},'attribute.value']. The { is its own non-string group (delimiter.curly → standardTokenType Other) so Monaco treats it as a real bracket matching the }. nextEmbedded shifted $2→$3. All chars still captured consecutively so the bd-yrl8vqbg crash stays fixed. Added bracket-symmetry test (mirrors Monaco toStandardTokenType) — failed before, passes after. Full hub-client vitest 601/601 + strict production build green.

title: Plan 3: q2-preview website-links fixture surfaces non-idempotent link rewriting (block 0 hash differs across runs with different project roots)
description:
Surfaced by Plan 3's idempotence gate (`crates/quarto-core/tests/idempotence.rs::website_links`). Reproduce:

  cargo nextest run -p quarto-core --test idempotence website_links

Panic message:
  fixture website-links (ProjectOrchestrator): non-idempotent
    blocks: 58bea67d61ea7d0a vs 5b51945d38f146e1
    meta:   94dc6be205c977cb vs 94dc6be205c977cb
    first divergence: Block { index: 0, hash_a: 18150854589991019955, hash_b: 8368855784726903601 }

Meta is stable across runs (hashes match). Blocks diverge at index 0, which is the paragraph containing `See [the other page](other.qmd) for more.`.

Hypothesis: the link-rewrite or link-resolution stage captures something path-dependent into the AST when it should produce a path-independent relative URL. Each `run_q2_preview` call creates a fresh `TempDir`, so the two runs see *different* project roots but identical fixture contents. For Plan 3's pipeline-determinism contract, structural AST should not depend on the absolute project root — only on its contents and relative layout. If the link's resolved target captures an absolute path or canonicalized tempdir form, two runs disagree.

Likely surfaces in:
- `LinkRewriteTransform` (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/link_rewrite.rs)
- `LinkResolutionStage`
- whatever populates Link.target after these run.

Note: SingleFile mode is not exercised here because website-links is orchestrator-only (chrome / link-resolution transforms need ProjectIndex). If the same bug bites SingleFile through a different fixture later, the fix should cover both.

Investigation starting points:
1. `find_first_divergence` already names the block index — dump the actual `Inlines` of `doc_1.ast.blocks[0]` vs `doc_2.ast.blocks[0]` and diff. The plan's panic message tells you where to start.
2. Inspect what the Link.target string looks like after `LinkRewriteTransform`. If it differs across runs, that's the immediate cause; trace back.
3. The fix should canonicalize at the source: emit a path-independent relative URL (or a path-relative-to-project URL) into the AST, with the absolute-path machinery confined to source_info.

This blocks closing `website_links` in the Plan 3 gate. Failing fixtures are the triage backlog per the plan's long-lived-integration-branch policy.

Refs:
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-3-builtin-filter-idempotence.md
- branch: feature/provenance

title: preview-renderer Equation test fails under the pinned katex 0.18.1 (\tag{N} .tag element gone)
description:
`ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/custom-components.integration.test.tsx` > 'Equation > appends \\tag{N} to the LaTeX when plain_data.order is set' fails at line 664 (`expect(tagEl).not.toBeNull()`) when node_modules matches the committed lockfile.

Root cause is a dependency drift, NOT a code change. Both root `package.json` and `hub-client/quarto-hub-sandboxed-preview/package.json` pin katex EXACTLY at 0.18.1, and `package-lock.json` resolves `node_modules/katex` to 0.18.1. Under 0.18.1, KaTeX no longer emits the `.tag` element the test queries, so `span.querySelector('.tag')` returns null.

The pin reached 0.18.1 via the Snyk PR 669ad7534 ('[Snyk] Upgrade katex from 0.18.0 to 0.18.1', #571). That PR bumped the version without updating this assertion.

Verified 2026-08-21 by running the same file at the same source commit in two checkouts:
- main checkout /Users/gordon/src/q2 (node_modules stale at katex 0.17.0): 53/53 PASS

title: Release workflow: publish standalone quarto-hub-mcp bundle as a GH release artifact
description:
Attach the esbuild bundle of ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp to each GitHub Release as a standalone, downloadable artifact, so users can run the Hub MCP server directly (node index.mjs) without installing the q2 binary.

CONTEXT
The release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) ALREADY builds the bundle per-target in the build matrix (lines 278-282: 'npm run bundle -w ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp' with KEYRING_PLATFORMS per matrix leg). Today dist-bundle/ is only embedded into the q2 binary via include_dir! and then discarded -- it is never packaged or uploaded. The hard parts (per-platform keyring .node staging, npm-pack fallback for non-host addons, fail-closed verification) are done and exercised every release.

CHOSEN APPROACH: Option B -- one UNIVERSAL bundle (user decision 2026-06-19).
- index.mjs is byte-identical across platforms (esbuild output is platform-independent); only node_modules/@napi-rs/keyring* differs.
- The keyring loader does runtime platform/arch/libc detection and stage-keyring.mjs supports co-staging every platform ('co-staged platforms coexist by design').
- So a single dedicated job (modeled on the existing web-payloads job, runs on ubuntu) builds one bundle with KEYRING_PLATFORMS set to the full cross-platform list (darwin-x64,darwin-arm64,linux-x64-gnu,linux-x64-musl,linux-arm64-gnu,linux-arm64-musl,win32-x64-msvc,win32-arm64-msvc). Non-host addons are fetched via npm pack -- a path the release already relies on (macOS runner fetches musl addons today).

WORK ITEMS
- [ ] New release.yml job (e.g. hub-mcp-bundle), ubuntu-latest, Node 24, npm ci, run 'npm run bundle -w ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp' with full KEYRING_PLATFORMS list.
- [ ] Tar dist-bundle/ -> quarto-hub-mcp-${VERSION}.tar.gz (include index.mjs, build-info.json, node_modules/@napi-rs/*). Write .sha256. upload-artifact.
- [ ] Add a short README + LICENSES/NOTICE inside the tarball: runner hint 'node index.mjs --help', REQUIRES Node 24+ (raw bundle has no MIN_NODE_MAJOR guard, unlike the launcher path), and attribution for inlined deps (MCP SDK, jose, oauth4webapi, automerge, ws).
- [ ] Extend the release job: download the new artifact, add the tarball to the minisign signing loop (currently globs artifacts/q2-*.tar.gz at release.yml:463 -- name to match or add explicitly), add to checksums.sha256 combine step, and add to 'gh release create' file list (release.yml:529-537).
- [ ] Update release notes generation to mention the standalone MCP bundle + its Node 24 requirement.
- [ ] Update release-runbook (claude-notes/instructions/release-runbook.md) to document the new artifact.
- [ ] Verify end-to-end on a dry-run tag: download the universal bundle on at least 2 OS/arch combos and confirm 'node index.mjs --help' works and keyring resolves.

NON-GOALS
- npm/npx publishing -- tracked separately by bd-3tak0lyy (related). The tarball needs no npm org/publish secrets; decide later whether npm makes the tarball redundant or whether we ship both.
- Per-platform bundles (Option A) -- rejected in favor of one universal bundle.

REFS
- Handoff guide: claude-notes/research/2026-06-19-hub-mcp-bundle-handoff.md
- Bundler: ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp/scripts/bundle.mjs + scripts/stage-keyring.mjs
- Design doc: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-11-q2-mcp-hub-auth.md (bd-81cfshmw)

title: Non-http URI schemes (positron:, vscode:, javascript:) are path-normalized: `//` collapses to `/` and nav hrefs gain `../` per level
description:
Any href whose URI scheme is not on a hardcoded 7-entry allowlist is classified as project-relative and run through path normalization. Quarto 1 emits all of them unchanged. Two visible symptoms, one root cause.

## Symptom 1: `//` collapsed to `/` (body links and nav)

  [x](positron://settings/foo)  ->  href="positron:/settings/foo"
  [x](vscode://schemas/settings) -> href="vscode:/schemas/settings"

https:// and mailto: are untouched. Every such deep link is dead in the output.

## Symptom 2: nav hrefs additionally gain `../` per directory level

A navbar/sidebar item on a page one directory deep:

  navbar href:                q2 top level          q2 one level deep            Q1 (both)
  javascript:void(0);         unchanged             ../javascript:void(0);       unchanged
  mailto:someone@example.com  unchanged             unchanged                    unchanged
  positron://settings/...     positron:/settings/   ../positron:/settings/...    positron://settings/...

Note the third row: on a subdirectory page both defects apply to the same href. Body links get symptom 1 only; nav hrefs get both, because the nav call sites also relativize against page depth.

## Root cause

crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_href.rs:228-239:

    pub fn is_external(href: &str) -> bool {
        href.starts_with("http://")
            || href.starts_with("https://")
            || href.starts_with("mailto:")
            || href.starts_with("tel:")
            || href.starts_with("ftp://")
            || href.starts_with("//")
            // data: URIs are URL-shaped, not path-shaped — running one
            // through path normalization would mangle it into a relative
            // URL (bd-root-relative-paths-design-fc5pvkcv).
            || href.starts_with("data:")
    }

A hardcoded prefix allowlist. Anything not on it — positron:, vscode:, javascript:, and every other registered or custom scheme — falls through to the path-normalizing branch. It gates five call sites (lines 166, 266, 336, 423, 777) covering both nav hrefs and body links, which is why one predicate produces both symptoms.

Two things worth noting about that function:

1. Its doc comment says "Matches Quarto 1's cheap heuristic". Q1 renders all of these correctly, so whatever it matches, it is not Q1's observable behaviour for these schemes.

2. The `data:` arm's comment already states this exact failure mode — "URL-shaped, not path-shaped — running one through path normalization would mangle it into a relative URL". So this class was hit before, diagnosed correctly, and fixed by appending one more allowlist entry rather than generalizing. positron:/vscode:/javascript: are the next instances of the same class.

## Suggested fix direction

The workspace already has a correct generic implementation: quarto_util::is_external_url (crates/quarto-util/src/path.rs:43-58) does real scheme detection — find the first ':', require at least 2 preceding chars, require the scheme to start with an ASCII letter and contain only alphanumerics plus '+', '-', '.'. It is already used at 8+ sites (website_post_render.rs, format_paths.rs, website_config.rs, website_favicon.rs, listing/feed/reader_ext.rs).

Replacing the allowlist in navigation_href::is_external with a call to it (retaining the leading-`//` case, which is_external_url also handles) fixes both symptoms and closes the class rather than adding an eighth prefix. Its doc comment already acknowledges the one ambiguity this introduces: a relative path with a colon in its first segment (`my:file.png`, legal on Unix) would be read as a URL — judged acceptable there, and the same trade-off applies here.

## Real-world hit, Positron website docs

Symptom 1 is the severe one. Measured on the current build (96 of 98 pages rendering): 241 collapsed `positron:/` hrefs across 52 pages, and 0 intact `positron://`. The Q1 baseline has 253 intact. Every settings deep link on the site — the docs' main interactive affordance — is dead.

It is also invisible to every automated check that port runs: visible-text diffing does not see hrefs, and both the asset checker and lychee ignore non-file schemes. It was found by hand.

Symptom 2 hits _quarto-positron.yml's navbar "Ask AI" button (href: "javascript:void(0);"), dead on all 12 rendered subdirectory pages.

## Repros

/Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/custom-scheme-slash-collapsed/  — symptom 1. `q2 render`, inspect _site/index.html; compare `quarto render --output-dir _site-q1`. Two repro links and two controls (https, mailto) sit four lines apart in one file, so no project-level difference can explain the divergence.

/Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/nav-scheme-href-relativized/  — symptom 2. One navbar with five items, a top-level page and a sub/ page; compare index.html against sub/page.html.

Origin strands in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-custom-scheme-slash-collapsed-k0o20szw (symptom 1) and br-nav-scheme-href-relativized-x2d7f2lu (symptom 2). Both re-verified failing on q2 0.27.0 (official release build); origin/main == v0.27.0 == d05e96ee8 as of 2026-08-25, so nothing post-release addresses it.

title: Heading-id slug filter diverges from Pandoc: no dropNonLetter, no empty-id fallback
description:
Two divergences from Pandoc in `auto_generated_id`'s slug filter (crates/pampa/src/utils/autoid.rs:42-57), both *after* the text-collection stage and both independent of the content-loss bug in `collect_text` that bd-heading-id-drops-inline-content-fl84n3ql covers.

Measured 2026-08-13 against pandoc 3.9.0.2 (`pandoc -f markdown+smart -t html --section-divs`) on q2 main @ b677afd4. Fixtures and full tables:
claude-notes/plans/heading-id-drops-inline-content-investigation/ (probes/probe2.qmd, probes/probe4.qmd; observed-2026-08-13.md sections 3 and 4).

## 1. `dropNonLetter` is missing

Pandoc's `inlineListToIdentifier` ends with `dropNonLetter`, which strips every leading character up to the first *letter*. q2 has no equivalent, so an id can begin with a digit or a `.`.

| heading | Pandoc | q2 |
|---|---|---|
| `## 1 leading digit` | `leading-digit` | `1-leading-digit` |
| `## .leading dot` | `leading-dot` | `.leading-dot` |

## 2. No empty-id fallback

When the derived text is empty, Pandoc falls back to `section`, then `section-1`, `section-2`. q2 emits a section with **no `id` attribute at all** (an unlinkable heading), after which the `seen_ids` counter at postprocess.rs:946-952 hands out `-1`, `-2` to the following ones.

`probes/probe4.qmd`, two headings that are nothing but an image with empty alt:

| | Pandoc | q2 |
|---|---|---|
| section 1 | `<section id="section">` | `<section class="section level2">` -- no id |
| section 2 | `<section id="section-1">` | `<section id="-1">` |

Fixing `collect_text` does NOT remove this: a heading that is only an empty-alt image, or only a footnote, still collects to the empty string.

## Why filed separately

The parent strand explicitly disclaims the punctuation question ("this is not the 'does the id strip punctuation' question"), and both items here are slug-filter behaviour rather than content loss. Keeping them apart also keeps the two snapshot diffs separable. They may still ship in the same PR as the parent -- that is scope question 3/4 in claude-notes/plans/2026-08-13-heading-id-drops-inline-content.md, awaiting the user's call.

Note for whoever picks this up: `dropNonLetter` changes ids for headings that begin with a number, which is common ("## 1. Setup", "## 2026 roadmap"). Blast radius here is larger than the parent's and needs its own sweep of docs/ and the fixture corpus.
close_reason:
Fixed in commit fcdd5424 on main (not yet pushed). Folded into bd-heading-id-drops-inline-content-fl84n3ql's session at the user's request ('fold in to avoid forgetting the followup'), but kept as its own commit so the two diffs stay separable.

Both items shipped:
(1) dropNonLetter -- auto_generated_id now trims leading non-letters, so '## 1 leading digit' gives 'leading-digit' and '## .leading dot' gives 'leading-dot'. Drops non-*letters*, so '## Ünicode leading' keeps its Ü.
(2) Empty-id fallback -- shipped in the parent commit 62773ee6 because it lives inside auto_generated_id alongside the collector fix. A heading collecting to nothing now gets 'section', 'section-1', ... instead of no id attribute at all followed by '-1'/'-2' on its siblings.

Ordering matters and matches Pandoc: dropNonLetter runs BEFORE the fallback, which is why '## 123' yields 'section' rather than '123'.

Blast radius measured, not assumed: docs/ rendered before and after, all 1250 <section id=...> values across 238 files diffed -- no change. The one docs heading that looked at risk ('## `--force` and `--trust` are different permissions') is a callout title, not a section heading. Full workspace suite 11872 passed, 0 snapshots touched, cargo xtask verify green including the WASM leg.

Tests: test_auto_id_drops_leading_digit, _drops_leading_dot, _drops_leading_number_prefix, _keeps_leading_non_ascii_letter, _all_digits_falls_back_to_section, _empty_falls_back_to_section, _repeated_empty_headings_are_deduplicated in crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_heading_auto_id.rs, plus the smoke-all fixture crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/markdown/heading-auto-id.qmd. All four dropNonLetter tests failed before the change with exactly the predicted values.

title: Code-cell shorthand: markdown in fig-cap is not parsed into inlines
description:

Affects every `#|` code cell, not just mermaid — reproduced on a plain ```python cell (claude-notes/plans/mermaid-cell-options-investigation/probe3.qmd) and on a ```mermaid fence (probe2.qmd, section C3).

title: Mermaid theming CSS: $mermaid-* SCSS vars + :root --mermaid-* bridge
description: Port _quarto-rules.scss L701–742: the $mermaid-{bg,edge,node-fg,fg,label-*,node-bg}-color / font vars (with $body-* fallbacks) and the :root --mermaid-* CSS-var bridge. Q2's mermaid feature (transforms/mermaid.rs, landed 5d6fe82b) emits <pre class=mermaid> + CDN script but ships zero theming CSS, so diagrams ignore the document theme. Carlos authored the Q1 mermaid theming and wants this as its own strand/session. Check how Q2's client-side mermaid init consumes theme vars (Q1 passes them into mermaid's themeVariables via JS — the CSS vars alone are only half the story). Vars documented in quarto-web docs/authoring/_mermaid-theming.qmd. Inventory row 27.

c-3bt2tj26.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-3bt2tj26.text:
Two notes from the bundling work (bd-mermaid-runtime-not-bundled-vxejw159, merged as PR #504) that affect how this is implemented:

1. DOM POSTPROCESSOR CAVEAT. Q1's mermaid resource set includes mermaid-postprocess-shim.js, which is a DOM postprocessor. Q2 emits HTML directly from the Pandoc AST and has no post-Pandoc DOM-mutation stage (CLAUDE.md, "No DOM postprocessor -- port Quarto 1 DOM postprocessors as AST transforms"). Whatever that shim does must be re-expressed as an AST transform or as emitted markup; do not port it as-is or introduce a postprocessor stage for it.

2. THERE IS NOW A REGISTRATION HOOK FOR MERMAID ASSETS. crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/mermaid.rs gained `register_mermaid_assets(&mut ArtifactStore)`, which stores the vendored runtime as an ArtifactScope::Project artifact at mermaid/mermaid.min.js -> _site/site_libs/mermaid/. A CSS artifact registered alongside it is the natural place for the theming stylesheet; crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs::register_reveal_assets is the model for registering CSS and JS together with cascade-ordered keys.

   One trap when adding that CSS: do NOT key it under the `css:` prefix without checking the reveal path. ApplyTemplateStage collects `css:` artifacts for the Bootstrap template (apply_template.rs:166) but the reveal scaffold collects only `css:revealjs:*` (apply_template.rs:303), so a `css:mermaid:` stylesheet would be silently absent from decks. The runtime JS hit exactly this and is keyed `mermaid:runtime` with the transform emitting its own tag into the after-body slot; see the MERMAID_ARTIFACT_KEY docs in mermaid.rs.

Also note bd-93ensbpn was filed as a duplicate of this strand and bd-nj25kgbu during that design discussion; it is linked with `duplicates` edges and recommended for close.

description: Design + implement a mode where a user running the q2 binary can connect (with auth) to an existing hub-client / quarto-hub.com collaborative session, announce itself as willing to execute code, and on request run engines (knitr/jupyter) and deposit results into the automerge session so all players see executed output. c-08oxh7wn.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-08oxh7wn.text:
Decisions locked with user 2026-06-30 (detail in plan):
D1 Hybrid (C): Node owns auth, Rust owns sync+execution+capture-writing via a BearerDialer.
D2 Hybrid channel: ephemeral 'execute now' + ephemeral capability beacon; persisted CaptureRef.state/staleness for durable status. Beacon liveness TIMEOUT = 1.5 x INTERVAL (proposed 3s/4.5s, tunable).
D3 Content-addressed + dedup now; capture docs EXCLUDED from zip export (cache, not content); real GC design is immediate follow-on strand.
D4 Surface-to-all, allow-all by default (providing execution = offering machine to the room). Optional owner-only mode is feasible: per-project actor id = HMAC(server_secret, sub||project_id), stable across devices, from GET /auth/actor; owner-only == request.actorId==self.actorId.
D5 Multi-executor: heartbeat claims (stale -> auto-reclaim, handles offline) + cooperative --force takeover (higher generation; displaced executor stands back; safe because executors are our trusted binary). Lean per-request claim keyed by (path, generation).
D6 Per-doc clear first; clear-all deferred; confirmation+in-flight race settle at Phase 4.
Q6 quarto-hub.com only v1; engine-agnostic mechanism. Q7 working name 'q2 provide-hub' (avoid 'connect' -> Posit Connect). Q8 per-doc clear.
Remaining in-phase opens: auth-bridge token hand-off (Node->Rust), beacon/claim DocHandle+wire format, final subcommand name. Awaiting go-ahead to start Phase 1.

c-hqctn1gm.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-hqctn1gm.text:
Design plan written: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-29-remote-execution-provider.md

Key finding from code study: the execution-RESULT transport in q2 preview is already automerge-native and shareable — captures are separate binary automerge docs referenced by a CaptureRef sidecar in the IndexDocument (NOT VFS files, NOT loopback HTTP). The hub already relays both to all peers. So 'deposit results visible to other players' is mostly done.

Real new work: (1) execution TRIGGER must move off loopback HTTP to an automerge channel (ephemeral message + capability beacon); (2) the executor must be a samod CLIENT peer dialing out (not the hub owner) — needs a BearerDialer for auth since samod's dialer can't set headers; (3) hub-client must start CONSUMING captures (today source-only); (4) capture RETENTION for long-lived projects (samod has no doc-delete API → content-addressed dedup); (5) authorization/consent (this is RCE on the volunteer's machine).

Central decision D1: executor as native Rust vs TS launcher vs hybrid (recommend hybrid: Node owns auth, Rust owns sync+execution via BearerDialer). Awaiting user review of D1–D5 before implementation.

c-m5e97ux3.author: Carlos Scheidegger

Phase 3 BearerDialer feasibility SPIKE done (de-risk before plan-commit). Verified against the ACTUAL dep: quarto-dev git fork samod@q2 v0.9.0 (not crates.io 0.10). Result: BearerDialer viable with ZERO fork changes.
- Repo::dial(backoff, Arc<dyn Dialer>) is public (dial_websocket is just a wrapper). 
- Dialer::connect() is called per (re)connect → fetch fresh Bearer each time (the per-connect refresh we need).
- Transport + Transport::new(stream,sink) public; only ws_to_bytes (~25 lines, tungstenite Message<->bytes) is private → replicate in our crate.
- Header injection standard: url.into_client_request() + AUTHORIZATION header + tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(request). Our crate uses its own tokio-tungstenite (no version coupling beyond Transport).
Verdict: no plan change; D1=C proceeds. Optional later: upstream dial_websocket_with_request into the fork to drop the ws_to_bytes replica (needs fork bump; not v1). Recorded in plan under 'Phase 3 — BearerDialer feasibility spike'.

c-mmto5fi8.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-mmto5fi8.text:
Phase 4a COMPLETE (execute-on-request + capability beacon), committed f19e00b3 on feature/hub-execution-provider. Full cargo xtask verify green.

The native provider now runs code: after join it broadcasts exec/beacon every 3s on the index DocHandle ephemeral channel and, on exec/request, materializes the VFS to a temp dir, runs the uncached record_capture (decision #4 always-fresh), and writes the capture binary doc + CaptureRef sidecar back over automerge (the Phase 1 editor transport).

New in crates/quarto-hub-provider:
- exec_channel.rs: Rust mirror of the TS wire format. ExecMessage internally-tagged enum (camelCase) via ciborium; a test asserts the CBOR shape is a standard map with the exact keys TS parseExecMessage checks (cbor-x useRecords:false interop proven).
- materialize.rs: read-only VFS->temp-dir (text via doc.text, binary via resource::read_binary_content) + ../absolute path guard.
- execute.rs: Provider (Arc) run loop = beacon-broadcast + ephemeral request-listen; execute_document (materialize->discover->record->write capture doc->set_capture); AuthzPolicy (AllowAll/Deny); write_capture_doc mirrors re_execute.rs; local CAPTURE_MIME_TYPE const.
- join.rs refactored: join() returns live (Repo, IndexDocument); join_and_list_files builds on it.

AUTHZ decision (user 2026-07-01): mechanism-first, FAIL CLOSED. q2 provide-hub is fail-closed by default (connect+list+exit); serves only with --allow-all. Real provider-only default (gate on provider's own per-project actor id) needs the hub to accept a Bearer on GET /auth/actor (cookie-only today) + a provider HTTPS fetch -> deferred to Phase 5. AuthzPolicy is the seam (add ProviderOnly{self_actor_id}).

E2E: scripted integration test (tests/integration/execute.rs) drives the real provider loop vs a real samod acceptor -> editor broadcasts exec/request -> capture syncs back to server (gunzipped to EngineCapture engine_name=test-passthrough). Deny companion writes nothing. 27 provider tests green.

c-ykx7okio.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ykx7okio.text: Added D6 to the plan: user-facing 'clear execution results' affordance in hub-client. Key findings: (1) clearing = automerge MAP-KEY delete on the IndexDocument captures map, NOT a document delete — sidesteps samod's missing doc-delete API; we drop the CaptureRef reference, the binary doc bytes remain for separate server GC. (2) Rust IndexDocument::remove_capture(path) already exists (index.rs:307), used only by tests. (3) TS sync client has NO capture-mutation API yet — only new code is a small SyncClient.clearCapture/clearAllCaptures that does indexHandle.change(d => delete d.captures[path]). (4) Clearing is a pure CRDT op any peer can do with NO executor and NO server round-trip — so it's executor-independent and ships in Phase 1 alongside capture-consumption. Separated D3's two concerns: 'remove reference' (D6, cheap, user-facing) vs 'reclaim storage' (server GC, hard). Sub-decisions to settle: granularity (per-doc + clear-all), confirmation UX (affects all players), in-flight race (running capture re-added after clear).

c-lcuf89ue.text:
HANDOFF (2026-07-13 session end, for the next agent).

CONTEXT. Epic bd-grkrb9nj; read claude-notes/plans/2026-07-13-lua-api-pandoc-parity.md (Phase 2c items S1-S5 + Decisions incl. NEW Decision 6) and the catalog. S0 (vendoring) is DONE — the 58 new xfails at the bottom of xfail.txt are this strand's failing tests (TDD step 1 done). Oracle-probe pandoc 3.9.0.2 BEFORE each sub-fix, per session convention.

S1. Citation + ListAttributes as userdata (~18 xfails in test-citation.lua / test-listattributes.lua + 2 Cite cases in test-inline.lua). Today pandoc.Citation/pandoc.ListAttributes return plain Lua tables (constructors.rs; ListAttributes ~L1536, Citation nearby): field reads return nil, __eq compares by table identity, no :clone. The helper userdata (LuaCell, LuaTableBody, LuaRow, LuaTableHead, LuaTableFoot in types.rs) have NO UserData get/set implementations — 'attempt to index a LuaCell value'. Needed per upstream tests: typed properties (cell: contents/alignment/row_span/col_span/attr; body: body/head/row_head_columns/attr; row: cells/attr; head/foot: rows/attr), attr aliases (identifier/classes/attributes — reuse the element alias machinery), __eq, and :walk. For :walk use the NEW engine: crates/pampa/src/lua/walk.rs — add walk_cell_children/walk_row_children etc. reusing walk_rows/walk_caption already there (Cell:walk = walk over cell.contents blocks; the LuaWalker trait makes this ~10 lines per type). S4. pandoc.Pandoc + pandoc.Meta* (~17 xfails in test-pandoc.lua / test-metavalue.lua). BIGGEST DESIGN ITEM — q2 metadata is ConfigValue, not pandoc Meta (catalog F2). Do NOT implement the legacy representation. pandoc.SimpleTable raises an actionable Q-coded error (q2 does not support the pre-pandoc-2.10 simple-table API; use pandoc.Table); registry entry; the 2 test-simpletable.lua xfails become permanent '# DIVERGENCE' entries (mechanism shared with bd-9p2686pc — coordinate the Q-code allocation there).

title: Escaped '\>' in a naked shortcode argument is an uncoded hard parse error, dropping the whole page
description: A backslash-escaped character in a naked (unquoted) shortcode argument is a hard parse error that fails the whole file. The canonical case is a literal '>', which cannot be written unescaped because it would close the shortcode: | {{< kbd \> >}} | Switch to command mode | q2 reports 'Error: Parse error / unexpected character or token here' with the caret on the backslash. The diagnostic is uncoded (no Q-n-n), so it cannot be searched for by code, and the whole document is dropped from the render. Q1 renders it: the kbd shortcode receives '>' and emits >>. Not the same as Q-2-34 ('unquoted shortcode parameter starting with digit'): different input, and that one at least carries a code. The sibling rows of the same table are all fine under q2 -- {{< kbd @ >}}, {{< kbd # >}}, {{< kbd : >}} render -- so this is specifically the backslash, not punctuation arguments in general. Root cause. The naked-string token has no escape alternative: crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js:686 shortcode_naked_string: $ => choice(token(prec(1, /(?:[A-Za-z0-9_.~:/?#\]@!$%&()+,;-]|\[)+/)), ...) '\' is not in that class, and neither is '>', so '\>' matches nothing and the shortcode rule (grammar.js:663) fails. Compare the url rule at grammar.js:433, which does admit escapes: /[^ {\t)]|(\\.)+/. The Rust side mirrors the character set in crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs (is_shortcode_naked_char, ~line 2245), whose doc comment states that '>', '<', '{', '}', '\'', '"', '\\' etc. are *deliberately* excluded -- so the exclusion is by design and the writer already quotes such values on the way out. Consumption is crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:984 -> process_shortcode_string_arg in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/shortcode.rs. Suggested fix, two viable directions: (a) Compatibility: add an escape alternative to shortcode_naked_string, e.g. allow (\\.)+ as the url rule does, and unescape in process_shortcode_string_arg so the shortcode implementation sees '>'. This accepts Q1 source unchanged. The writer already round-trips such a value as a quoted string, which stays correct. (b) Diagnose instead of accept: if the naked-string set is meant to stay closed, this deserves the k-371 treatment -- an error code plus a hint that names the fix, since the quoted form ALREADY works in both engines: {{< kbd ">" >}} and {{< kbd '>' >}} both render under q2 0.24.0 and under Q1, byte-comparable output. Today the author gets an uncoded 'unexpected character or token here' pointing at a backslash, with nothing to act on. A qmd-syntax-helper conversion rule rewriting an escaped naked argument to its quoted form would then make this migratable automatically, which it currently is not (the helper's check reports the file as an uncoded parse issue and offers no fix). Real-world hit. The Positron website's command-palette.qmd:31 uses the form above to document the Command Palette prefix keys. The page is lost from the q2 build, and it is the most cross-linked page in that site: 65 of 89 rendered pages link to it, making 'command-palette.qmd' the single largest group of broken references in the port's asset sweep (x65 broken references, x77 lychee errors). It is one of only four files in the whole site that still fail to render. Repro: /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal/ Run 'q2 render' there: index.qmd (the failing row, verbatim from the Positron docs) fails while control.qmd (the sibling @ / # / : rows) renders, so the boundary of the bug is executable. 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1' renders both. See README.md for expected vs actual output. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path. Observed with q2 0.24.0 (the released binary) and reproduced against a HEAD debug build reporting 0.26.0 (source 328e176fb, 2026-08-23), so it is live upstream, not fixed post-release. Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-4nxwhy9m.
close_reason: Naked token widened to a blocklist with escape support; \> now reaches the shortcode as >. Grammar e223edd52, reader 1d1a3c586, writer 2477d2816. Verified end-to-end: the committed repro renders with rc=0 emitting <kbd title=">">, matching Q1. Full cargo xtask verify 14/14 incl. WASM; workspace nextest 13148 passed/199 skipped (+18).

That one is non-ASCII in a naked value ('{{< kbd mac=Command-→ >}}'), this one is a backslash escape ('{{< kbd \> >}}'). Both fail the whole file; both are fixed by widening the same rule, so they are worth designing together. title: Non-ASCII in a naked shortcode argument is fatal, and is misreported as Q-2-34 (digit-initial value)
description:
A non-ASCII character anywhere in a naked (unquoted) shortcode argument is a hard parse error that fails the whole file, and in key=value position it is reported under the wrong error code.

    - Pressing {{< kbd mac=Command-→ win=Ctrl-→ linux=Ctrl-→ >}} to accept the suggestion word-by-word...

q2 reports '[Q-2-34] Unquoted shortcode parameter starting with digit -- Shortcode parameter values starting with digits must be quoted.' Nothing in this input starts with a digit. The document is dropped from the render.

Q1 renders it:
<kbd title="linux: Ctrl-→, mac: Command-→, windows: Ctrl-→" aria-hidden="true" data-linux="Ctrl-→" data-mac="Command-→" data-windows="Ctrl-→">

Measured boundary (q2 0.24.0 and a HEAD build reporting 0.26.0, identical):

    {{< kbd mac=Command-→ >}}      Q-2-34, file lost
    {{< kbd mac=Ctrl-é >}}         Q-2-34, file lost   <- not about arrows; any non-ASCII
    {{< kbd → >}}   (positional)   uncoded 'Parse error', file lost
    {{< kbd mac=Command-X >}}      OK
    {{< kbd mac=Command-Left >}}   OK
    {{< kbd mac="Command-→" >}}    OK
    {{< kbd mac='Command-→' >}}    OK

So there are two defects here.

DEFECT 1 -- non-ASCII is not accepted in a naked shortcode value. Root cause is the same token rule as bd-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-2u79bqp1: shortcode_naked_string in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js:686 is a closed ASCII-only class,

    /(?:[A-Za-z0-9_.~:/?#\]@!$%&()+,;-]|\[)+/

with no non-ASCII range and no escape alternative. 'Command-' matches, '→' matches nothing, and the shortcode rule at grammar.js:663 fails. The Rust mirror is is_shortcode_naked_char in crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs (~line 2245), whose doc comment enumerates the deliberate exclusions -- all ASCII punctuation; non-ASCII is not discussed there at all, which suggests it was not a considered case rather than a decision. One grammar change plausibly closes both this strand and bd-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-2u79bqp1; they are worth looking at together.

Suggested fix direction: admit non-ASCII word characters to the naked-string class (Q1 accepts anything up to the closing delimiter, so anything short of that is a narrowing), and extend is_shortcode_naked_char to match so the qmd writer does not start gratuitously quoting values it round-trips.

DEFECT 2 -- the error code is wrong for this input, and the mechanism will misattribute other inputs the same way. Q-2-34's corpus entry (crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/Q-2-34.json) is about 'k=1b' and 'size=1x' -- genuinely digit-initial values. This input gets that code because the parse-error table is keyed on tree-sitter parser state + symbol rather than on the input: crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json maps {state: 3603, sym: "pandoc_str_token1"} -> Q-2-34, and 'mac=Command-→' happens to fail in state 3603. See crates/pampa/src/readers/qmd_error_message_table.rs (lookup_error_message / lookup_error_entry over the embedded table).

That is worth attention beyond this one message: any future input that fails in a state already claimed by some corpus case inherits that case's diagnosis, with confident and specific wording. Here the author is told to look for a digit that does not exist. A cheap mitigation would be to validate at emit time that the captured span actually matches the claimed condition, and fall back to the generic parse error when it does not.

Real-world hit. Three occurrences in two files of the Positron website, costing more than three lines:

- assistant-completions.qmd:22 -- the page is lost from the site. 64 of 89 rendered pages link to it, one of the four largest groups of broken references in the port.
- _rstudio-keyboard-shortcuts.qmd:17-18 -- this one is an INCLUDE, so the failure propagates: migrate-rstudio-keybindings.qmd and tutorial-migrate-from-RStudio.qmd both render with the entire keyboard-shortcut table silently missing, 25 diff lines each, the second-largest visible-text difference in the whole port.

Repro: /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/kbd-unquoted-param/
Run 'q2 render' there: index.qmd (the failing line, verbatim from the docs) and positional.qmd (the same character with no code attached) both fail while control.qmd (ASCII values and quoted non-ASCII values) renders -- 'Rendered 1 of 3 files ... 2 errors'. 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1' renders all three. README.md has the full boundary table. That repo is local-only, hence the absolute path.

Observed with q2 0.24.0 (released binary) and reproduced against a HEAD debug build reporting 0.26.0 (source 328e176fb, 2026-08-23), byte-identical diagnostics, so it is live upstream.

Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-kbd-unquoted-param-5pvk8wtu. Sibling: bd-shortcode-escaped-gt-fatal-2u79bqp1 (same token rule, backslash instead of non-ASCII).
close_reason: Defect 1 (non-ASCII fatal in naked args) fixed by the same blocklist widening; {{< kbd mac=Command-→ win=Ctrl-→ >}} now renders data-mac/data-windows correctly. Defect 2 (state-keyed error-code misattribution) survives this change and is tracked independently as bd-kaa2jzf9, which now carries a replacement reproducer (comment c-4nhhrm9c) since this fix retired its original one.

c-ngryrbgt.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-ngryrbgt.text: Defect 1 fixed in PR https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/590. Defect 2 (state-keyed error-code misattribution) is untouched and lives on in bd-kaa2jzf9, which now carries a replacement reproducer since this fix retired the original one.

title: Missing-space shortcode delimiters are an uncoded cascading parse error, and the closing form is misattributed to Q-2-34
description:
A shortcode written without a space after the opening delimiter — '{{<fa plus>}}' — is a fatal, UNCODED parse error: 'Error: Parse error / unexpected character or token here'. The whole file is lost. The closing delimiter is equally fatal: '{{<fa plus >}}' fails the same way, and '{{< fa plus>}}' fails too but is reported as [Q-2-34] 'Unquoted shortcode parameter starting with digit — Shortcode parameter values starting with digits must be quoted', when the parameter is 'plus' and there is no digit anywhere on the line. Quarto 1 accepts all four spellings.

To be clear about what is and is not the bug here: REQUIRING THE SPACE IS CORRECT AND SHOULD STAY. _shortcode_sep (crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js:650) is a choice with no empty alternative, required at line 655 immediately after the opening delimiter, so the separator is mandatory by construction. That is a good rule — '{{' is also Jinja/Handlebars territory, and requiring '{{< ' keeps a shortcode lexically unambiguous from templating braces. Q1 accepts the tight form only because its shortcode handling is regex-based and tolerates it incidentally. This strand asks for the error to be DIAGNOSED well, not for it to stop being an error.

Four things are wrong. (1) It is uncoded, so it is absent from the diagnostic histogram, unsearchable, and has no documentation page. (2) The message names no construct — it does not say a shortcode was being parsed or that a separator was expected. (3) It offers no remedy, though the fix is one space; compare Q-2-41, which q2 already gets right, naming the rule and offering two concrete rewrites. (4) It cascades: one missing space produces three errors, the third blaming the closing ':::' of a perfectly valid callout five lines below the real mistake, aiming the author at correct syntax in an unrelated construct.

Severity matrix on the committed repro, q2 0.28.0, one form per file:
  {{<fa plus>}}      1 error    uncoded
  {{< fa plus>}}     1 error    [Q-2-34]  <- wrong code, remedy fixes nothing
  {{<fa plus >}}     1 error    uncoded
  {{< fa plus >}}    1 warning  [Q-16-3]  <- parses, page renders
  {{< fa 2plus >}}   1 error    [Q-2-34]  <- correct; the true-positive control
Note the shape: a shortcode q2 cannot resolve AT ALL gets a coded warning and a rendered page, while one merely missing a space gets an uncoded fatal error and no page. The last row proves Q-2-34 is a real rule being over-matched onto any tight closing delimiter rather than a mislabelled catch-all. The column is right in every case — 7:14 is exactly where the space belongs; the failure is entirely in what the message says.

Suggested fix direction: (a) give it a code and a remedy on the model of Q-2-41 — '[Q-x-y] A shortcode's opening delimiter must be followed by a space. Write {{< fa plus >}}.'; (b) recover at the shortcode instead of desynchronising the parser, so one mistake yields one error; (c) gate Q-2-34 on a parameter actually starting with a digit; (d) add a qmd-syntax-helper autocorrect rule. On (d): the registry is RuleRegistry::new() at crates/qmd-syntax-helper/src/rule.rs:112-163 and the 26 conversions live in crates/qmd-syntax-helper/src/conversions/. The rule must space BOTH delimiters — '{{<name' -> '{{< name' and 'value>}}' -> 'value >}}' — because spacing only the opening side converts row 1 of the matrix into row 2, which still fails. It is engine-neutral: the spaced form is what Quarto 1 emits and both engines accept it, so a converted corpus still builds under Q1. Note an ordering dependency: rules are named after their diagnostic code (q-2-28, q-2-33) or descriptively (literal-brackets, grid-tables), so (a) comes first or the rule takes a descriptive name. There is precedent and a cautionary tale — a div-whitespace rule for the sibling defect ':::{.callout-note}' used to exist and was un-registered in a 'make tests pass' commit; the name survives as a fossil in a doc comment at rule.rs:56 and in claude-notes/how-to-use-samply.md, but there is no div_whitespace.rs in conversions/.

Real-world hit in the Positron docs: managing-interpreters.qmd (7 occurrences), data-explorer-summary-panel.qmd and positron-notebook-editor.qmd were each lost entirely to this. They render today only because the source was migrated by hand, so there is no live outage — the cost falls on other Quarto 1 projects during migration, which is exactly when an undiagnosable cascading error is most expensive and when the autocorrect rule would pay for itself.

Minimal repro: /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/shortcode-no-space/ — run 'sh check.sh' there (it takes an optional path to a q2 binary, defaulting to ~/.local/bin/q2, and prints each fixture's summary, blamed positions and diagnostic codes). Fixtures: repro.qmd (tight open), control.qmd (spaced, renders), cascade.qmd (three errors from one cause), delimiters.qmd (the five-form matrix above, including the Q-2-34 true-positive control).

Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-shortcode-no-space-dn01dnz5. Observed with q2 0.28.0 (official release build); re-checked against q2 HEAD eda49bc4e, where none of grammar.js, scanner.c or qmd-syntax-helper has changed since v0.28.0 and _shortcode_sep still stands unmodified at grammar.js:650.
close_reason: Shipped in q2 0.29.0. Verified downstream by re-running llms-info/repros/shortcode-no-space/check.sh: the error is now coded Q-2-52 where it was uncoded; the D2 misattribution to Q-2-34 is gone while genuine Q-2-34 cases still report Q-2-34; the cascade is fixed (3 errors down to 1, with a note that parsing stopped); and the message carries both the corrected spelling and the qmd-syntax-helper converter invocation.

c-frrztg72.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-frrztg72.text:
Correcting the mechanism, since the strand's account was inferred from black-box behaviour and would mislead the next reader.

Q-2-34 is not 'over-matched onto any tight closing delimiter'. The error table (crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json) is keyed on (LR state, lookahead symbol), and '{{< fa plus>}}' fails at state 3603 on 'pandoc_str_token1' — exactly the key all three of Q-2-34's corpus cases resolve to. Q-2-34 was the only entry at that key, so it answered by default. Nothing was matching a delimiter; the key was simply too coarse to tell two mistakes apart.

The tight *opening* delimiter is a different story: state 3212, absent from the table entirely, hence uncoded.

The cascade is real desynchronisation, not a grouping artifact in the pruner. From the CST: recovery from the tight '{{<' leaves a bare '}}', and the ERROR node opening there runs to [6,4] — it swallows the callout's opening ':::' and reads it as three pipe_table_align_left tokens. The third error is the *closing* ':::', now genuinely unmatched.

Fixed on branch braid/bd-shortcode-no-space-gspu6l5s-shortcode-no-space (commits 6889d3f87, 49bbf0435). Q-2-52 covers 67 parser states — the opening delimiter needs one per inline container, the closing one needs one per argument shape plus a container family after a bare name. The table gained two mechanisms: a per-entry source-text 'guard' for contended states, and a per-code 'desynchronizes' flag that drops diagnostics after an error known to wreck the parse. Q-2-34 keeps '{{< fa 2plus >}}' and also '{{< fa 2plus>}}', where the digit-led value is the earlier fault.

Also filed bd-xfqx2tuc: shortcode syntax inside a code span or fenced block is expanded rather than shown literally, which is why this code's docs page writes its bad examples with escaped braces instead of in code blocks.

c-nlv2ueyd.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-nlv2ueyd.text:
Mechanism correction from the workspace-6 investigation, recorded here because the description above will otherwise mislead the next reader. The description says Q-2-34 is 'over-matched onto any tight closing delimiter' — that was inferred from black-box behaviour. The actual cause: the tight-close form errors at LR state 3603 with lookahead pandoc_str_token1, which is exactly the (state, sym) key all three of Q-2-34's corpus cases resolve to. The error table is keyed on (state, sym) alone, so Q-2-34 is the only entry at that key and wins by default rather than by any pattern match. Consequence for the fix: (a) and (c) are one defect, not two — giving the tight-close form its own code adds a second entry at the same key, and lookup_error_entry would then pick between them essentially arbitrarily via max_by(diagnostic_score). The tight-OPEN form is a different state (3212) and is simply absent from the table, hence uncoded.

Cascade cause, same investigation: recovery from the tight '{{<' leaves a bare '}}', and the ERROR node opened there swallows the callout's opening ':::' and reads it as three pipe_table_align_left tokens; the third error five lines down is the closing ':::' now genuinely unmatched. Real desynchronisation, not a grouping artifact — the three ERROR nodes are siblings and the pruner keeps one diagnostic per node by design.

Additional evidence sent to the implementing session: a digit-initial token can precede a tight close legitimately, so a guard requiring merely 'digit-initial token before the error offset' does not suffice. '{{< video a.mp4 width=640 >}}' (spaced) is accepted with only an unrelated Q-16-6 warning, proving the value is legal, while '{{< video a.mp4 width=640>}}' (same value, space removed) draws Q-2-34. Also '{{< video a.mp4 width="640">}}' — quoting the value, which is exactly what Q-2-34's message instructs — does not fix it and additionally loses the code, turning a wrong code into no code. Rows suggest Q-2-34's real scope is positional arguments rather than key=value values; offered as a hypothesis for the implementer to check against the corpus, not as a spec.

title: Shortcodes unevaluated inside fenced code blocks (Q1 substitutes them)
description:
Quarto 1 substitutes shortcodes inside fenced code blocks by default: a .gcfg config example containing '[Section "corporate {{< meta vendor >}}"]' renders '[Section "corporate LDAP"]' (verified against Q1 dev, no attribute needed). q2 0.15.0 leaves the shortcode literal in the rendered code block (HTML-escaped: '{{< meta vendor >}}'), with no warning. Body-text shortcodes work fine.

Root cause: ShortcodeResolveTransform (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/shortcode_resolve.rs) treats Block::CodeBlock(_) as a leaf with no shortcode scanning (~line 1086, 'Leaves — no nested AST to walk', also ~1539); Inline::Code(_) is likewise skipped (~line 941, ~1726). Shortcodes only exist as parsed AST nodes in prose contexts, so code-block text is never examined.

Suggested fix direction: scan CodeBlock (and check Inline::Code against Q1 during the fix) text for shortcode syntax and substitute resolved values, preserving Q1's escape form ('{{{< ... >}}}') for intentionally displaying a literal shortcode. This is a text-level scan since code content is plain text, not nested AST.

Real-world hit: Posit Connect docs admin/authentication/ldap-based/include/_users.qmd (shared by 5 LDAP authentication pages) uses '{{< meta authentication.vendor >}}' inside a .gcfg config example — the rendered configuration snippet shows the raw shortcode instead of the vendor name.

Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/shortcodes-in-code-blocks/ (see README.md; run 'q2 render repro.qmd' there; Q1-verified). Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-shortcodes-in-code-blocks-v9bxqbtk. Observed with q2 0.15.0; checked origin/main (adc2281f): no fix. Related: bd-shortcodes-in-metadata-bp06aub8 (shortcodes in config strings / HTML includes — different contexts, same family).
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-fz6gwfq0 (code-block slice); repro + real-world-hit context folded into that strand, work continues there

title: Shortcodes not evaluated in website.title, page-footer, or HTML include files
description:
q2 0.15.0 evaluates shortcodes in document body text and document metadata (e.g. subtitle), but passes them through literally in three project-level contexts that Quarto 1 evaluates: (1) website.title — the literal '{{< env NAME >}}' text appears in every page's <title> and navbar brand, with any HTML in the title string (e.g. <small>) additionally escaped and shown as text in the navbar; (2) website.page-footer text — footer shows '{{< env NAME >}}'; (3) include-in-header / include-before-body / include-after-body files — file contents are injected verbatim with shortcodes intact. No warning is emitted in any of the three.

Root cause area: shortcode resolution is an AST transform (ShortcodeResolveTransform, crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/shortcode_resolve.rs) that runs on document content/metadata; project config strings flow to navbar/footer generation (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navbar_generate.rs, footer_generate.rs/footer_render.rs) without passing through it, and IncludeResolveStage (crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs ~293) treats include files as opaque text.

Suggested fix direction: run shortcode expansion over the relevant website config strings when they are parsed as markdown for navbar/footer/title emission, and over header/body include file contents at IncludeResolveStage time (Q1 substitutes shortcodes in include files — its rendered output proves it, see repro README).

Real-world hit: Posit Connect docs use '{{< env CONNECT_VERSION >}}' in website.title, page-footer, and a version-toast include-before-body HTML file — all 352 pages show the raw shortcode text in navbar, footer, and toast (navbar also shows escaped '<small>' markup as text).

Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/shortcodes-in-metadata-and-includes/ (see README.md; run 'REPRO_VERSION=2026.08.0 q2 render' there — body text substitutes, title/footer/banner stay literal). Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-shortcodes-in-metadata-due080a1. Observed with q2 0.15.0; checked origin/main (8518ac79): no shortcode handling for config strings or include files. Related: bd-environment-files-372u9qbs (_environment files not loaded).
close_reason: Implemented and merged in PR #487: shortcodes now resolve in all metadata values, website presentation config strings (registry-driven ConfigMarkdownTransform), and include files (text-level expansion); composes with _environment file loading (bd-environment-files-372u9qbs). E2E verified against Q1 reference output.

title: Evaluate Temml as a third math engine for HTML output
description:
MathJax (default) and KaTeX shipped in bd-w5ov. Temml is a KaTeX fork that emits MathML directly (~80 KB bundle, native browser rendering, best a11y story). MathML support is now near-universal (Chromium since 2023, WebKit + Firefox always).

Investigate whether to add Temml as a third 'html-math-method' option:
- Output contract differs from MathJax/KaTeX (MathML in markup vs TeX delimiters).
- Could be added as a parallel arm in MathEngine / from_meta() / render_math_slot().
- Decide: does q2 ship TeX-source delimiters and let Temml convert client-side, or do server-side TeX→MathML conversion at render time?

Out of scope: making Temml the default. Default stays MathJax for parity with Quarto 1.

title: Sidebar contents: <directory> shorthand renders a broken sidebar instead of auto-generating entries
description:
A website sidebar whose contents: is a bare directory name renders no usable navigation. Quarto 1 treats the directory as an auto-generation source: it emits a collapsible section titled after the directory, holding a link to every document in it. q2 treats the same string as a single href and emits one dead link — and in a multi-sidebar project it emits no sidebar element at all.

Verified side by side on the minimal repro (a website whose only sidebar is 'contents: guides', over guides/first.qmd and guides/second.qmd):

  Q1: <nav id=quarto-sidebar> with a 'Guides' sidebar-item-section
      containing 'First Guide' and 'Second Guide'.
  q2: <div id=quarto-sidebar> containing a single entry whose text is
      the literal string 'guides' and whose href does not resolve.

Root cause is one branch in parse_contents (crates/quarto-navigation/src/sidebar.rs:528). It special-cases exactly one bare string — 'auto' -> SidebarEntry::Auto(AutoSpec::All) — and sends every other bare string to SidebarEntry::from_plain_string (same file, :288), which classifies a 3+-dash run as a separator and everything else as an href. So 'contents: guides' becomes SidebarEntry::Link { href: 'guides' }.

The machinery the shorthand needs already exists and is one enum variant away: AutoSpec::Path(glob) (:116) is documented as 'auto: docs (everything beneath docs/)' and resolves through q2's shared glob semantics. Suggested fix: in parse_contents, route a bare string that is neither 'auto' nor a separator to SidebarEntry::Auto(AutoSpec::Path(s)) rather than to from_plain_string, and confirm the expansion produces Q1's section-with-title shape (directory name as the section label) rather than a flat run of links. The one judgement call is whether a bare string that names an actual document ('contents: intro.qmd') should stay a Link; deciding by extension, or by whether the path resolves to a file vs a directory, both express that without changing the glob semantics. Note the same shorthand is accepted in book chapters and in listing contents:, so it is worth checking whether those paths share this code.

Real-world hit: the Posit Connect documentation's _quarto.yml configures its How To Guides sidebar as 'contents: how-to' (one line, no list). Under Q1 that section's five pages get a 'How To Guides' sidebar with all four guides plus prev/next pagination. Under q2 the rendered pages carry no #quarto-sidebar element whatsoever and no pagination — note this is a harder failure than the repro's, because with several sidebars configured the unresolvable single entry costs the whole sidebar rather than leaving a visible dead link. The five pages are how-to/index and its four guides (deploy-single-page-apps, publish-databricks-quarto-notebook, run-content-as-the-current-user, use-renv-for-reproducible-r-deployments).

One scope note on pagination: prev/next is downstream of sidebar entries, so it returns with them, but the minimal repro does not demonstrate it — neither engine emits pagination there, since the repro does not enable page navigation. The Connect docs do, which is where the loss shows.

Repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/sidebar-contents-dir-shorthand/ — run 'q2 render' there and compare with 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1'; README.md states expected vs actual. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-sidebar-contents-dir-shorthand-8rvnztv6. Observed with q2 0.19.0 and re-verified failing on 0.20.0; q2 HEAD (152ed8fb, the v0.20.0 release merge) has nothing newer touching crates/quarto-navigation.
