c-mmtva0gi.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-mmtva0gi.text:
Investigated at main @ 152ed8fb (pre-flight cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build green). Plan skeleton: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-sidebar-contents-dir-shorthand.md, committed as 48b12a7d.

Root cause confirmed exactly as described (sidebar.rs:528). Read Q1's source to settle the two open questions in the description:

- The shorthand is SCALAR-ONLY. Q1's normalizeSidebarItems (website-sidebar-auto.ts:96) turns a scalar contents: into [{auto: <string>}]; a bare string that is an ARRAY ELEMENT goes through normalizeSidebarItem (project-config.ts:24) and becomes {href} if the path exists, {text} otherwise — never auto. Ordering confirmed at website-navigation.ts:1051-1058, and expandAutoSidebarItems recurses into nested contents:, so nested sections get the shorthand too.
- No file-vs-extension judgement call is needed at the parse site. Q1 makes no special case: 'contents: intro.qmd' is just auto: intro.qmd, which expands to that one file.

Two findings beyond the description:

1. Routing the bare string to AutoSpec::Path is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. collect_candidates (sidebar_auto.rs:200) hardwires AutoSpec::Path to Scope::Flat, so expansion yields flatten_as_links — a flat run of links, not Q1's titled section. section_for_dir (:320) already builds exactly Q1's shape (it matches the repro's Q1 output precisely, including the no-href header when the dir has no index.qmd), but only AutoSpec::All reaches it. Note Q1's auto: <dir> ALSO produces a section (isAutoDir re-shuffle), so q2's auto: diverges from Q1 today too — pinned by test auto_path_scopes_to_subdir (:504). Whether to change auto: as well is design question Q1 in the plan.

2. A SECOND, PRE-EXISTING DEFECT blocks the Connect-docs fix. sidebar_for_page runs at sidebar_generate.rs:89 but expand_auto only at :127, so selection sees unexpanded contents, and contains_source_path ignores SidebarEntry::Auto(_) (sidebar.rs:663). This explains both reported symptoms as one root cause: the minimal repro survives via the Rule-2 single-sidebar wildcard (:637) and shows the dead link, while a multi-sidebar project falls to Rule 3 containment and loses the sidebar entirely. Verified by rendering a committed probe (two id-bearing sidebars, one 'auto: how-to'): all three how-to pages get sidebar=0, other/alpha.html gets sidebar=1. Filed as bd-4feoon8u (discovered-from this).

Scope notes resolved: listings are unaffected (independent parse_contents at listing/config.rs:631, scalar -> Glob is already correct); q2 has no book chapters: parser yet (ProjectKind::Book is only an accepted string), so nothing to check there.

Verdict: ready to design. Four questions await the user — (1) should auto: <dir> also become a section, (2) how should selection see through auto:, (3) decide directory-ness from the project index rather than the filesystem, (4) fold bd-4feoon8u in here or split.

c-wzy599bl.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-wzy599bl.text:
Implemented on branch braid/bd-sidebar-contents-dir-shorthand-z7arvhx8 (commits 726bc59e, 0a3a99fa, 27915ca4, d8c55a95). Not yet pushed — awaiting review.

Design settled with the user: full Q1 parity for auto: <dir> (not just the new shorthand); expand all sidebars before selecting; decide directory-ness from the ProjectIndex rather than the filesystem; fix bd-4feoon8u here.

The fix turned out to be three changes, not one:

1. quarto-navigation parse_contents — a scalar contents: now routes to Auto(Path(s)), matching Q1's normalizeSidebarItems. Scalar-only: array elements stay Links (fenced by a test).
2. quarto-core collect_candidates — a bare-directory AutoSpec::Path now selects Scope::Grouped instead of Scope::Flat. Not a new code path: when all candidates share a first path component, group_with_subdirs already collapses to one section via section_for_dir. Directory-ness is index-driven (no glob metacharacter + at least one matched doc beneath), never filesystem — WASM-safe. Renamed Scope::All -> Scope::Grouped.
3. quarto-core SidebarGenerateTransform — sidebars are now href-resolved and expanded BEFORE sidebar_for_page picks one, with per-sidebar diagnostics so unselected sidebars' Q-13-5/Q-13-6 warnings don't fire on every page. This is the bd-4feoon8u fix and is what the Connect docs actually needed.

End-to-end verified through the q2 binary, output inspected:
- minimal repro now emits Q1's structure — sidebar-item-section titled 'Guides', aria-expanded=true, sidebar-section depth1 show, both guides nested, current page active. Previously a single href='guides' dead link.
- multi-sidebar probe goes from sidebar=0 to sidebar=1 on all three how-to pages, each getting the CORRECT sidebar (how-to/one.html -> 'How To' with How To Index/Guide One/Guide Two; other/alpha.html still 'Other').

Gates: cargo xtask lint clean; cargo nextest run --workspace 11834 passed; cargo xtask verify EXIT=0 across all 14 steps including the WASM/hub-client leg. Note the unskipped verify aborts at step 4/14 on tree-sitter grammar failures that are PRE-EXISTING — main gives the identical 601/590/11 (98.17%) — so those were skipped after confirming the baseline.

Behavior change worth release notes: projects relying on auto: <dir> producing a flat list now get a titled section. Q1 parity, but user-visible.

Follow-ups filed rather than folded in: bd-gba8n0r2 (docs/ has no sidebar guide at all, p2) and bd-dje564or (auto: expansion is one level deep where Q1 nests arbitrarily, p3, pre-existing and inherited).

title: Sidebar contents: <dir> shorthand only recognizes index.qmd — an index.md landing page is not promoted to the section header
description:
The sidebar 'contents: <directory>' shorthand handles the directory's own landing page correctly only when that page is index.qmd. With index.md — same files, same content, same _quarto.yml, only the extension differs — the landing page is not recognized: the section header falls back to the capitalized directory name instead of the landing page's title, and the landing page is listed as an ordinary child instead of being promoted to the section header. Q1 promotes the landing page regardless of extension. Prev/next pagination follows the entry list, so inserting the landing page as a child also shifts which entry is first and changes the pagination links.

Root cause: section_for_dir in crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/sidebar_auto.rs (line ~354 at v0.24.0) builds the index path by string concatenation with a hardcoded extension, and says so in a comment: '// Find the directory's own index.* if present. Only .qmd is discoverable by Phase-1 project walking; that's fine for MVP.' — 'let index_src = format!("{}/index.qmd", dir)'. The premise no longer holds: crates/quarto-core/src/project/discovery.rs renders .md whenever an explicit project.render pattern matches it (documented there as a deliberate divergence from Q1), so an opted-in project has .md profiles in the ProjectIndex and lookup_by_source misses them. The same hardcoded literal drives the child filter a few lines below ('.filter(|p| source_fwd_slash(p) != index_src)'), which is the second symptom: index.md is not excluded from the children.

Suggested fix: resolve the directory's index profile by stem rather than by hardcoded extension — find any profile in the ProjectIndex whose source is <dir>/index.<ext> — and use that resolved source for both the header href and the child-exclusion filter. Both symptoms are one fix.

Real-world hit: the Posit Connect docs set 'contents: how-to' and every Connect landing page is .md, so all five How-To pages show a section labelled 'How-to' instead of 'Posit Connect How To Guides', with the landing page as a sibling of the guides rather than their header; how-to/deploy-single-page-apps also emits one pagination link where Q1 emits two. These are the only sidebar differences left in the whole 451-page site.

Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/sidebar-dir-shorthand-index-page/ (run 'q2 render' there; see README.md; inspect guides/alpha/index.html's #quarto-sidebar). Expected (Q1): section header 'The Guides Landing Page' with children Alpha Guide, Beta Guide. Actual: section header 'Guides' with the landing page as a third child. Renaming guides/index.md to index.qmd makes q2 match Q1 exactly.

Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-l18qnflo (follow-up to the dir-shorthand feature, bd-sidebar-contents-dir-shorthand-z7arvhx8). Observed with q2 0.21.0; re-verified failing on 0.22.0 through 0.24.0; hardcoded literal confirmed still present at HEAD (= v0.24.0).

title: Sidebar item with text: + file: + contents: renders the page title, ignoring text:
description:
A sidebar entry configured with text:, file: (or href:), and contents: displays the linked page's title in the sidebar instead of the configured text:. Q1 uses the configured text: for such section-with-landing-page items; q2 falls back to the page title, so a deliberately short sidebar label is replaced by the full page heading on every page of the site.

Root cause: SidebarEntry::from_config_value (crates/quarto-navigation/src/sidebar.rs) treats any object with contents: as a Section and takes display text from the section: key only ('let section_text = cv.get("section").cloned(); ... let text = section_text.filter(...)'). When the entry uses text: instead of section:, the Section's text comes out None and rendering falls back to the target file's page title. Verified still present in the Section branch at current HEAD. Items with text: + file: but no contents: parse as leaf links and render correctly.

Suggested fix: in the Section branch, fall back to text: when section: is absent, e.g. 'section_text.or_else(|| cv.get("text").cloned()).filter(|v| v.as_plain_text().is_some())'. Q1 accepts both spellings for a section's display text.

Real-world hit: in the Posit Connect docs port, the Cookbook sidebar's landing item is configured as 'text: Cookbook' with a landing file and contents; q2 renders 'Posit Connect Cookbook' (the page title) across all ~109 cookbook pages.

Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/sidebar-item-text-ignored/ (run 'q2 render' there; see README.md). Expected: the sidebar entry for landing.qmd reads 'Short Name'. Actual: it reads 'The Much Longer Landing Page Title'. Q1 comparison via 'quarto render --output-dir _site-q1'.

Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-sidebar-section-text-ignored-yr34ofdu. Observed with q2 0.19.0; re-verified failing on 0.20.0 through 0.24.0.

title: Sidebar title is emitted even when a navbar is present; Q1 suppresses it (sidebar.ejs gates on !navbar)
description:
When a website declares both a navbar and a titled sidebar, q2 renders the sidebar's `title:`; Quarto 1 does not. q2 emits, inside
:
Guides
Q1 emits no sidebar-title element at all in that configuration. ## What the rule is (corrected 2026-08-25) An earlier version of this description said "the site title is already shown in the navbar, so the sidebar repeats it." **That is wrong**, and it is wrong in a way that invites a bad fix — do not narrow this to a string-equality check against `website.title`. Q1's gate is `!navbar`, full stop. Evidence, from a matrix run against the real Q1 binary (99.9.9), one fixture varying only navbar presence and sidebar logo: navbar logo | sidebar-title sidebar-header sidebar-logo title text shown no no | 1 1 0 yes no yes | 1 1 3 yes yes no | 0 0 0 no yes yes | 0 1 3 no Three things follow: 1. It is not about the logo. The logo controls the *wrapper* (`sidebar-header`); row 4 emits the wrapper and the logo and still no title. 2. It is not about string duplication. In the repro fixture `website.title` is "Site Title" and the sidebar title is "Guides" — different strings, still suppressed. And the Positron site that surfaced this sets `navbar: title: false`, so its navbar has no brand text at all — still suppressed. 3. Sidebar titles are not broken in Q1. They render whenever there is no navbar, which is the ordinary case for books and sidebar-only doc sites. The actual rationale is **navbar-item duplication**. The Positron navbar has `- text: "Guides" href: welcome.qmd`, and the sidebar titled "Guides" is the one containing welcome.qmd. That navbar item is rendered active on every page the sidebar covers, so the navbar is already showing the reader which section they are in; a "Guides" banner atop the sidebar restates it. The markup confirms the intent — the element is ``, a home link, and Q1 defaults `sidebar.title` to `website.title`. It is site/section branding for when there is no navbar to carry it, not a heading for the sidebar's contents. q2 marks navbar items active too (`navbar_generate.rs:146` `mark_active`; `render_html.rs:671` emits `nav-link active`), so the premise holds here and suppressing the title does not remove the reader's only position indicator. **`- section:` labels inside `contents:` are NOT affected** — only the sidebar's own `title:`. Verified against Q1: a top-level `- section: "Error reference"` renders normally under a navbar. A sidebar keeps its whole structure; it loses only the banner above it. ## Root cause Q1 gates the whole block on the absence of a navbar — src/resources/projects/website/templates/sidebar.ejs:51: <% if (!navbar) { %> <% if (sidebar.title) { %>
and the enclosing wrapper on `sidebar.logo || (sidebar.title && !navbar)` (:34). `nav-before-body.ejs` passes `navbar: !!nav.navbar` into the partial. q2 gates only on the title resolving to a concrete value — crates/quarto-navigation/src/render_html.rs:410: if let SidebarTitle::Text(ref title_cv) = sidebar.title { Q1's title block needs three conditions at once: a sidebar exists, `sidebar.title` is truthy, and `!navbar`. q2 honours the first two (SidebarTitle::Default when there is no website.title to substitute; SidebarTitle::Hidden for an explicit `title: false`, both unit-tested) and misses the third. q2's `Sidebar` has no `logo`/`tools`/`search` fields, so Q1's two nested gates collapse into the one q2 already has — adding `&& !has_navbar` is a faithful port, not a partial one. ## Suggested fix Add the navbar check to the same condition. `rendered.navigation.navbar` is already in scope at that point in the pipeline (NavbarRenderTransform is pushed immediately before SidebarRenderTransform), and `quarto_nav_js.rs` already uses a "non-empty rendered navbar" predicate for the same question. ## Collateral: this repo's own docs site (MEASURED, corrected 2026-08-25) Rendered docs/ with the pre-fix binary at 99e7db175 and counted, rather than reasoning from the YAML. 258 of 265 pages carry a sidebar-title today: rendered title pages source Error reference 223 explicit title: on the `errors` sidebar (:84) Quarto 2 34 AUTO-SUBSTITUTED website.title on the sidebars that have NO title: (`Guides`, `Authoring`) Presentations 1 explicit title: on the `presentations` sidebar (:77) (none) 7 pages carrying no sidebar --- 265 The 34 `Quarto 2` pages are the pure bug case -- nobody authored that; it is the default substitution restating the navbar brand. An earlier version of this section called it "two headings" and described the two `title:` sidebars as stragglers to clean up first. That was wrong on both counts. A sidebar with no `title:` does not render blank: SidebarGenerateTransform substitutes website.title (sidebar_generate.rs:168-172). Verified against the pre-fix binary -- a sidebar with no title: and website.title "Quarto 2" emits
Quarto 2
so deleting `title: "Error reference"` BEFORE the gate would turn 223 pages from "Error reference" into "Quarto 2" -- worse, not preserved. **There is no ordering that avoids the docs headings going away; the gate removing them IS the fix.** The two `title:` deletions are dead-config cleanup and must travel in the SAME commit as the gate, never before it. Also note `- id: guide` is dead config: its only entry points at docs/guide/index.qmd, which does not exist, so no page selects it. Editorial note, not blocking: "Error reference" is a banner on 223 pages, but the gate removes a DUPLICATE of that label, not its only instance -- the errors sidebar's first content entry is errors/index.qmd, whose own page title is "Error reference". After the fix the sidebar still opens with an "Error reference" link. Keeping the banner would mean converting title: to a `- section:`, nesting the sidebar a level deeper and interacting with collapse-level across 223 entries. ## Scope of the code change Beyond the one-line gate: - `quarto-navigation` gains a public `SidebarRenderOptions` struct; `sidebar_to_html_with_appended` is REMOVED in favour of `sidebar_to_html_with_options` (2 external call sites, both in quarto-core; not re-exported from lib.rs). `sidebar_to_html` keeps its signature. - `quarto-core` gains `transforms::config::page_has_navbar`, and `quarto_nav_js.rs`'s inline copy of the same predicate is folded onto it. - `shortcode_config_pipeline.rs`'s `full_fixture` is split so `sidebar_title_shortcode_substitutes` gets a navbar-free fixture -- it is the one existing test the gate breaks (verified: exactly one). - `q2 render docs/` needs `docs/examples/` staged, and `cargo xtask stage-doc-examples` stages into the MAIN repo even when run from a worktree (stage_doc_examples.rs:43 -> create_worktree::repo_root()). ## Repro Two projects, identical except that one declares a navbar; same sidebar, same website.title, same pages. In each: `q2 render`, then `quarto render --output-dir _site-q1`, then count 'sidebar-title' in index.html. fixture q2 Q1 with-navbar/ 1 0 without-navbar/ 1 1 without-navbar/ is the control: with no navbar the engines agree, so this is specific to the navbar-present case rather than to sidebar titles in general. Fixture inlined in the plan; upstream copy with committed Q1 output at /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/sidebar-title-with-navbar/. ## Real-world hit The Positron website docs declare one navbar and one sidebar titled "Guides". Every page carrying that sidebar renders the extra title — 81 pages. After the other chrome-affecting differences in that port were fixed, this is the SOLE remaining chrome difference between its Q1 and Q2 builds: a chrome sweep across 105 pages reports sidebar:1 on all 81 and no other bucket. Not a duplicate: bd-jgeu ("Home-link relativization for sidebar title + navbar brand", closed) concerns the href inside the element, not whether the element should exist. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-25-sidebar-title-with-navbar.md Origin strand in the Positron-docs porting skein: br-sidebar-title-extra-k6rs9ueq. Observed with q2 0.27.0; base for the fix is origin/main == 99e7db175.
close_reason:
Fixed on branch braid/bd-sidebar-title-with-navbar-82wxow6m-sidebar-title-with-navbar @ ad96db741 (7 commits on c11aa0e4d). NOT YET MERGED OR PUSHED -- closed at Gordon's explicit direction; the branch lives in .worktrees/workspace-3.

The fix: added `&& !opts.has_navbar` to the sidebar-title gate in crates/quarto-navigation/src/render_html.rs, porting Q1's sidebar.ejs:51 `!navbar` condition, plus the plumbing to carry the signal -- a SidebarRenderOptions param bag (modelled on Q1's nav-before-body.ejs bag) and a shared page_has_navbar predicate in quarto-core transforms::config, which also absorbed quarto_nav_js.rs's inline duplicate of the same question.

Implemented as the boolean rule, NOT narrowed to a string-equality check against website.title -- see the description's matrix for why that narrowing would not have fixed the reported bug.

Verified end-to-end through the real binary: with-navbar -> 0 sidebar-title, without-navbar -> 1 (control unchanged), navbar-brand and sidebar-menu-container both still present. Docs site 259 pages -> 0 while inner `- section:` labels survive (Reveal.js 5, >yaml< 1). Workspace suite 13454 passed / 199 skipped (= pre-branch 13447 +7, every new test accounted for). cargo xtask verify FULL (WASM + hub-client legs) exit 0. cargo xtask lint clean.

Preview/render parity preserved: SidebarRenderTransform is registered unconditionally, so q2 preview and the hub-client preview gain the same gate. Ordering (SidebarRender after NavbarRender) is pinned by test_sidebar_render_registered_after_navbar_render, which asserts both phase and relative position.

See comment c-aa4972pd for an important correction to this strand's own description: the docs/_quarto.yml "dead-config cleanup" was not dead, regressed llms.txt headings, and was reverted.

Known follow-ups, not filed: (1) sidebar_to_html still carries a load-bearing has_navbar: false, documented rather than removed -- moving it to #[cfg(test)] would eliminate the trap; (2) sidebar_heading's raw-id fallback; (3) sidebar.alignment parity gap (q2 hardcodes text-left vs Q1's alignCss).

c-aa4972pd.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-aa4972pd.text:
CORRECTION (2026-08-26, at close): the "dead-config cleanup" claim in this description and in comment c-coamgs69 is FALSE, and was caught by the final whole-branch review after the deletion had already landed.

Deleting `title: "Presentations"` and `title: "Error reference"` from docs/_quarto.yml is NOT inert once the gate lands, because sidebar.title has a SECOND consumer that never sees the gate:

    crates/quarto-core/src/project/llms_post_render.rs::sidebar_heading
        SidebarTitle::Text(cv) => cv.as_plain_text()
        _                      => sidebar.id            <-- raw id, NOT website.title

docs/_quarto.yml sets llms-txt: true, so with the titles deleted the docs site's llms.txt H2s degraded from

    ## Presentations   ->   ## presentations
    ## Error reference ->   ## errors

Confirmed empirically in the branch's own rendered docs/_site/llms.txt. Per CLAUDE.md that file is the source for agents-docs-dist/ and ships embedded in `q2 docs llms` / `q2 agents-info` -- so this was a user-visible (agent-visible) regression, not a cosmetic one.

The deletions were REVERTED in the fix wave; docs/_quarto.yml is byte-identical to pre-branch. Re-verified after the revert: 0 pages carry sidebar-title (the gate suppresses explicit titles fine -- title presence is necessary but not sufficient), and the llms.txt headings are restored.

Note the shape of the error: this strand's own analysis correctly identified that sidebar.title has non-HTML consumers, and the plan chose to gate at the RENDERER (design decision D1) precisely so the data model would stay intact for them -- then deleted the model values those consumers read. Same defect class as the original bug: a value's second consumer went unconsidered.

The SEQUENCING argument in the description is unaffected and still true: a deletion may not precede the gate (it would substitute website.title and flip 224 pages to "Quarto 2"). What changed is that the deletion should not happen at all.

Also worth a separate strand: sidebar_heading's raw-id fallback means three of five docs sidebars are still headed by ids (## Guides, ## Authoring, ## guide). Pre-existing, not caused by this work.

title: q2-debug placeholder loses CustomNode type_name
description:
q2-debug's Block/Inline dispatchers (`hub-client/src/components/render/q2-debug/dispatchers.tsx`) currently render the miss path as `Not registered: CustomBlock` (or `
...
` for blocks) — using only `args.node.t`, which discards the CustomNode `type_name` discriminator. For CustomBlock / CustomInline AST nodes, the rendered debug placeholder should include the type_name so developers can see *which* CustomNode hit the fallback path. Example: `Not registered: CustomBlock(Callout)` instead of `Not registered: CustomBlock`. ~5 LOC change. Pattern: in the dispatcher, when `args.node.t === 'CustomBlock' || args.node.t === 'CustomInline'`, append the type_name to the displayed text. **Why**: q2-preview's parallel placeholder (`q2-preview/dispatchers.tsx` post-Plan-2C) already includes the tag name; q2-debug's debug-mode visualization should be at least as informative. **Discovered**: while reviewing Plan 2C (q2-preview customnode rendering, `claude-notes/plans/2026-05-09-q2-preview-plan-2c-customnode-rendering.md`). Not in 2C scope — q2-debug is a separate format. Filing as a follow-up.

title: Rich-text (tiptap) block editor for q2-preview — feasibility spike
description: Explore replacing the monospaced textarea in the q2-preview block editor with a tiptap/ProseMirror rich-text component. Approach (confirmed with user): keep ALL existing detection + commit machinery unchanged; replace only the EditTextarea UI. Seed the editor from the markdown byte-slice, edit as rich text, and on commit serialize the ProseMirror doc back to markdown text committed through the existing commitTextEdit -> parse_qmd_content -> apply_node_edit path. Quarto-specific constructs (shortcodes, ::: divs + {attrs}, math, @crossrefs, raw HTML, citations) round-trip as opaque ProseMirror 'chip' nodes (verbatim renderText). Fidelity target v1: prose-rich, Quarto-opaque. Opt-in flag, experimental branch; eventual fallback to textarea for unsupported syntax / new-block creation. Deliverable this session: throwaway round-trip spike (markdown -> PM doc -> markdown) on real qmd fixtures to de-risk the core unknown. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-23-tiptap-rich-text-block-editor.md

title: native writer: escape carriage return in write_safe_string
description: The native writer string quoter write_safe_string in crates/pampa/src/writers/native.rs lines 11 to 23 escapes backslash, double-quote and newline but not carriage return, so a raw CR byte leaks verbatim into serialized CodeBlock and other string fields. Pandoc native (Haskell show) escapes carriage return. Add a carriage-return arm. This is bd-238o fix 1. TDD: feed a CRLF code block constructed in source, assert the serialized output escapes the CR rather than emitting a raw 0x0d byte. Reference claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-handling-analysis.md.

title: quarto-sync-client logs to stdout, corrupting MCP stdio protocol
description: quarto-sync-client has 12 console.log sites (client.ts: 'Waiting for peer connection...', '[createNewProject] ...', 'Peer connected - ...') that write to stdout. When the sync client runs inside quarto-hub-mcp (stdio MCP server), these lines interleave with JSON-RPC frames on stdout and corrupt the protocol. Confirmed empirically during bd-81cfshmw Phase 0 spike. Fix: injectable logger in sync-client (default console.log for browser; hub-mcp redirects to stderr) + defense-in-depth stdout guard in hub-mcp.
close_reason: Fixed in 0404368f on beads/bd-81cfshmw-q2-mcp-launcher: injectable logger seam in quarto-sync-client (setSyncLogger), all 12 console.log sites routed through it; hub-mcp redirects to stderr + rebinds console.log as defense in depth. Regression tests: stdout-purity integration test against in-process sync peer + source-level no-console.log invariant test.

title: preview renders math with KaTeX while render defaults to MathJax (engine-level divergence)
description: Discovered during bd-4b7f1hr7 (audit item 3: divergences beyond per-node parity). The q2-preview format typesets math unconditionally with bundled KaTeX (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/inlines/Math.tsx, katex.renderToString) - it does not consult html-math-method. Render's default math engine is MathJax 3 (MathEngine::default_engine in crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/math_js.rs); KaTeX is only used when the user sets html-math-method: katex. So with default settings, preview and render typeset math with DIFFERENT engines (fonts/spacing/feature coverage differ; MathJax supports more LaTeX). KaTeX-in-preview is plausibly deliberate (synchronous + fast for live editing), but the divergence should be a decision, not an accident. Options to assess: (1) document KaTeX as the preview's typesetter and accept the visual delta; (2) have preview honor html-math-method (MathJax in an iframe is feasible); (3) flip render's default to KaTeX. Note bd-4b7f1hr7 already pinned the KaTeX version (0.16.28) across render's CDN URL and the preview bundles, so WHEN both sides use KaTeX they now match exactly. Reference: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-10-html-preview-css-drift-audit.md.

title: Decide: should Q2 support metadata-files / metadata-file in _quarto.yml?
description: Q1 supports 'metadata-file(s):' in _quarto.yml (external YAML merged into project config at load time, resolved by quartoYamlProjectConfigResolver before profile merging). Q2 has no support at all — discovered during the project-profiles port (bd-fu16z22k). Decide whether to port it or deliberately drop it. Points to weigh: (a) Q1 wart: metadata-files inside _quarto-<profile>.yml are NOT resolved (documented callout in quarto-web docs/projects/profiles.qmd:91-95 tells users to inline the contents) — if we port, we should fix that asymmetry rather than replicate it; (b) overlaps with Q2's existing _metadata.yml directory layers and with profile overlays themselves, so the feature may be redundant; (c) if we drop it, we need a good diagnostic when users bring Q1 projects that use it (unknown-key today is silently ignored since Q2 has no schema layer). Either outcome needs docs.

Three modes: beads ID (reads br show), --issue N (reads gh issue view), --upgrade (date-based). CLAUDE.local.md holds context only (worktree location, beads pointer, GitHub URL, plan placeholder) — beads tracks status. title: lua: resolve_path returns module dir, not extension root, inside a required file (GH #588)
description: GH https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/588. register_scoped_require (quarto_api.rs, added in #450) pushes the loaded module's directory onto _quarto_script_dir_stack while the module executes; quarto.utils.resolve_path reads the same stack, so a relative path resolved at module load time gains the module's directory segment (_modules/greet.lua -> _modules/_modules/greet.lua). title: qmd-syntax-helper: AST-based rules report unparseable files as clean
description:
The AST-based qmd-syntax-helper rules — reference-links and literal-brackets, and anything else built on bracket_analysis::analyze — report a file that fails to qmd-parse as clean. 'check -r literal-brackets -r reference-links <file>' prints '✓' for it, counts it as a clean file, and folds it into 'Success rate: 100.0%', indistinguishable from a file with no findings. The operator of a scoped sweep gets an actively misleading all-clear: the rules never saw an AST at all.

Root cause: crates/qmd-syntax-helper/src/conversions/bracket_analysis.rs, analyze() — the parse result is matched with 'Err(_) => return Ok(Analysis::default())', silently converting a parse failure into an empty (= clean) analysis. The parse rule that would have caught it exists, but nothing connects it to a scoped '-r' run.

Suggested fix direction: make unparseable distinct from clean. Either (a) surface the parse failure as a CheckResult from the AST-based rules themselves ('file failed to parse; rule not applied'), or (b) have analyze() return the error and mark the file unanalyzable in check/convert output and summary counts (not ✓, not part of the success rate). Convert should refuse the file rather than silently no-op for the same reason.

Real-world hit (Connect docs port): pre-migration admin/security/index.md fails to parse with 3× Q-2-10 stray-apostrophe errors, so a bracket sweep of the affected pages reported it clean while it contains four literal [1]–[4] brackets keying prose to a numbered diagram — exactly the content the literal-brackets rule exists to save. Running 'convert -r apostrophe-quotes' first unmasked all four. The masking cost nothing there only because the page was already known-affected from a hand migration.

Repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/syntax-helper-parse-masking/ (local-only repo, absolute path required). input.qmd holds a Q-2-10 apostrophe error plus one literal bracket, one reference link, and its definition; 'check -r literal-brackets -r reference-links input.qmd' reports clean. input-parseable.qmd is identical with the apostrophe escaped and yields both findings. Helper built from this checkout at f8df9521 (v0.22.0) with cargo build --release --manifest-path crates/qmd-syntax-helper/Cargo.toml --target-dir <outside-the-checkout>.

Origin strand: br-syntax-helper-parse-masking-fmwvbmq8 in the q2-connect-docs skein (discovered while validating the reference-link migration workflow guide there). Observed at q2 0.22.0 / HEAD f8df9521.

title: Omitting sort: still alphabetizes a listing; Q1 preserves declared contents: order
description:
bd-listing-declared-order-3ixcvc4o (commit e48f6331, in main) preserved declared `contents:` order and set the default sort to Q1's 'order asc, title asc'. But the two halves interact: with NO `sort:` key at all, the default sort still runs and alphabetizes by title, so declared order survives only when the author writes `sort: false` explicitly.

Q1's rule is the opposite (website-listing-read.ts ~1306): 'If the user hasn't provided a sort, the list will be unsorted following the order provided in the listing contents.'

Measured on branch braid/bd-listing-inline-contents-tyy446ze at 39a4c130c, fixture with two documents declared zebra-then-alpha:
- `contents: [zebra.qmd, alpha.qmd]`, no `sort:` → renders Alpha, Zebra (alphabetized)
- same plus `sort: false` → renders Zebra, Alpha (declared order)

PRE-EXISTING, not caused by the inline-records work: globs and inline records behave identically here, so that branch is internally consistent. It does raise the stakes, because a hand-curated list of records is exactly the shape an author expects to stay put — e.g. the Positron docs, where only one listing of many sets `sort:`, so its curated welcome cards render alphabetically.

Found by the final whole-branch review of plan claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-listing-inline-contents.md; that branch documents the current behaviour in docs/guides/projects/listings.qmd rather than changing it, since the semantics are this strand's call.

title: smoke-all runner doesn't clean up _site/ for type: website fixtures
description:
The crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all runner cleans up only the output file and <stem>_files/ after each fixture run. It has no cleanup path for type: website project fixtures, which render into a _site/ directory instead.

Filed per the branch's final review (M7): "gitignoring is a workaround for a runner that does not clean up after project-type fixtures, and this branch is the first to need it. Worth a strand against the smoke-all runner, not against this branch."

title: Document inline executable expressions in q2's docs/
description:
q2 now implements both Quarto inline expression spellings with their documented, deliberately-different semantics (bd-inline-r-brace-spelling-not-evaluated-lk9s3iwe): `{r} expr` escapes markdown specials in the value; knitr's native `r expr` inserts the value as live markdown, equivalent to `{r} I(expr)`.

Nothing in q2's own docs/ says so. The strand's provenance search found inline expressions are undocumented there — only Q-2-47 and Q-2-50 mention {r} at all — so a q2 user has to read quarto.org (which describes Q1) or the source to learn which spelling to reach for.

Worth covering:
- the two spellings and the escaping split, with the I() equivalence
- that a value inserted via the classic spelling is live markdown, and therefore live HTML: untrusted input should use the brace spelling
- how to *write about* the syntax without executing it (doubled brace, or an extra enclosing backtick). This is a live trap: a knitr document displaying an unresolvable brace expression inside a fence now fails the render, matching Q1.
- the one q2/Q1 divergence found while fixing this: an empty brace expression `{r}   ` in prose renders as a literal code span in q2 rather than erroring, because q2's pass runs over the serialized AST (which normalizes the trailing whitespace away) where Q1's runs over raw source. It errors in both in an attribute value.

Contract and rationale: crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/preprocess.rs module docs.

Note bd-u996g8g2 is the jupyter half of the spelling gap ({python} expr); if that lands, this page should cover both engines rather than being R-specific.

The jupyter half stays with bd-u996g8g2; the display-block escape gap is bd-0gwekaem.

title: Crossreferenceable Example blocks (@-ref the embed-example-iframe)
description:
Make the .embed-example-iframe block a first-class CROSS-REFERENCEABLE Quarto 2 type, like figures/tables/theorems. When the author adds a crossref id with the right prefix (e.g. ::: {.embed-example-iframe #PREFIX-03-fragments file=...}), the example gets auto-numbered and prose can reference it (@PREFIX-03-fragments -> 'Example 1' link), resolved through the same crossref index/resolve/render machinery as figures and theorems.

KEY CONFLICT to resolve: the prefix 'exm' the user proposed is ALREADY a built-in ref-type — it maps to the theorem-like .example environment ('Example N'), see crates/quarto-core/src/crossref/registry.rs:90 and transforms/theorem.rs:67. So the new runnable-demo Example needs a DISTINCT prefix (e.g. xmp / demo / eg) and a kind decision (reuse 'Example' kind vs a new 'Demo' kind to avoid two 'Example N' sequences).

Architecture (per research): an embed-example is structurally a FLOAT (container + numbered caption), like a figure. Plan: restructure ExampleEmbedTransform from immediate Div->iframe rewrite into a crossref-aware sugar transform producing a CustomNode that populates plain_data {ref_type, kind, identifier} + holds the iframe content/caption/source-link in slots; let the existing CrossrefIndex/Resolve handle numbering + @ref; add a dedicated render step (finalization) that emits the iframe + numbered 'Example N: caption' + source link. Id-optional: with #PREFIX- id -> numbered + crossreferenceable; without -> plain embed (current Phase 1/2 behavior). Register the new prefix as a built-in ref-type. Backward compatible/additive.

Builds on bd-z1smhvuo Phases 1-2 (transform + staging + page-relative src). Design plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-09-crossreferenceable-examples.md (to be written).

c-4p5ku4ei.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-4p5ku4ei.text: Implemented + committed (8a1ca4d5) on branch beads/bd-z1smhvuo-embed-example-iframe. Decision: prefix 'demo', kind 'Demo', caption 'Demo N: ...'. title: Headings nested inside tabset panels leak into the TOC and point at hidden content
description:
Follow-up to bd-toc-tabset-titles-zq93gjvf, which landed panel-tabset support in 0.23.0. That strand fixed the tab-TITLE leak: the level-N Headers that become tab buttons are consumed by PanelTabsetTransform before sectionize and TOC, exactly as intended. Headings written INSIDE a tab body still reach the TOC, and they should not.

WHAT HAPPENS

Given a two-tab tabset where each tab body carries a #### heading — the shape you get whenever per-provider or per-language tabs share a boilerplate sub-section:

  ## Configuration
  ::: {.panel-tabset}
  ### Azure
  #### Create the integration
  ### Google
  #### Create the integration
  :::
  ## Next steps

Quarto 1's TOC:  #configuration, #next-steps
q2 0.23.0's TOC: #configuration, #create-the-integration, #create-the-integration-1, #next-steps

Three reader-visible problems:

1. The extra entries are indistinguishable. Both read "Create the integration"; the one piece of context that would tell them apart — which tab they belong to — is exactly what the TOC drops.

2. Every entry past the first tab is a dead link. #create-the-integration-1 sits in <div id="tabset-1-2" class="tab-pane"> with no `active` class, i.e. display:none. Clicking the TOC entry scrolls to nothing, and stays that way until the reader independently clicks the Google tab. On a grouped tabset it can be un-reachable in one gesture from the TOC at all.

3. The hierarchy is skewed. With the tab-title level consumed, a #### inside a tab becomes a direct child of the enclosing ## in build_hierarchy, so the TOC tree shows a two-level jump that is nowhere in the document.

ROOT CAUSE

PanelTabsetResolveTransform (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/panel_tabset_resolve.rs) is pushed at crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:1248, immediately after the parse half and well before SectionizeTransform (:1333) and TocGenerateTransform (:1387). Its output — documented in the module header — puts only the nav bar in RawInline; the panes themselves are real AST:

  Div (.panel-tabset)
    Plain [RawInline(ul.nav-tabs ...)]
    Div (.tab-content)
      Div (#tabset-N-M, .tab-pane[, .active])
        [content blocks...]

So by TOC time the in-tab headings are ordinary Headers inside ordinary Divs. SectionizeTransform wraps them in section Divs, and collect_toc_entries (crates/pampa/src/toc.rs:341) recurses into every Div — the `is_section_div` branch for sections and the else branch for everything else — and collects them.

Quarto 1 differs precisely here, and by accident rather than by design: src/resources/filters/customnodes/panel-tabset.lua returns raw HTML for the whole tabset, so pandoc's TOC pass sees an opaque blob and nothing inside a tabset can reach the TOC. Note this is the mirror image of the note in bd-toc-tabset-titles-zq93gjvf: there, the collector was correctly NOT at fault and the fix belonged in the transform. Here the transform is doing the right thing structurally (real AST beats a raw-HTML blob for every other consumer — search, llms companions, link rewriting) and the collector is the piece that has no way to know it is inside a tabset.

SUGGESTED FIX

Two defensible directions; the first is small and restores Q1 parity, the second is strictly better for readers.

(a) Do not descend into tabsets when collecting. In collect_toc_entries' Div arm, skip recursion when the Div carries the `panel-tabset` class. Two lines. The wrinkle is layering: pampa should probably not know the name of a quarto-core construct, so consider having PanelTabsetResolveTransform mark the subtree with a generic opt-out that the collector already understands — toc.rs documents an `unlisted` class that excludes a heading — or add a generic "do not descend" class that pampa owns and quarto-core applies.

(b) Keep the entries but make them work: qualify each with its owning tab title, and have the TOC link activate that tab before scrolling (the pane ids are already deterministic, tabset-N-M, and tabsets.js already owns tab activation and group sync). More work, and it needs a design call on how a qualified entry reads.

Either is fine. What is not fine is the current state: listed, unlabelled, and dead.

REAL-WORLD HIT

Posit Connect docs port: 25 of 451 pages, 44 leaked TOC entries, 18 of them targeting an inactive pane. Measured structurally — for every page with a tabset, resolve each nav#TOC data-scroll-target against the ids a nesting-aware parse places inside a .tab-pane.

Worst page is admin/integrations/oauth-integrations/microsoft/index.html: a five-tab provider tabset where each tab includes the same _azure_intro.qmd, which carries an "#### Create integration in Posit Connect" heading. The TOC grows five identical entries under "Connect configuration". On that page they are not even disambiguated — see the separate strand for the include-boundary id collision — so all five point at the first tab. admin/integrations/oauth-integrations/google/index.html is the same shape with four.

This is also the entire residual toc:N bucket of the port's chrome sweep, which is how it surfaced: implementing tabsets took the sweep from 122 of 451 differing pages to 32, and 23 of the 32 are this. (23, not 25: the sweep compares extracted text, so a leaked entry whose text coincides with a line Q1's TOC already has does not register.)

REPRO

/Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/tabset-headings-in-toc/

Run `q2 render` there and compare _site/index.html against the committed Q1 render in _site-q1/ (regenerate with `quarto render --output-dir _site-q1`). Expected: 2 TOC entries. Actual at 0.23.0: 4, of which #create-the-integration-1 resolves into a .tab-pane with no `active` class. README.md states expected vs actual and both fix directions.

Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-tabset-headings-in-toc-udrziana. Observed with q2 0.23.0; q2 origin/main at 5b6774d1 has nothing past the 0.23.0 tabset work that touches this.
close_reason: Fixed via direction (B) -- the TOC is the section tree. Connect docs port (451 pages): exact TOC parity with Q1 421 -> 444; 44 entries removed, 0 added; 25 pages closer, 0 further. All 44 removals were inside a div.tab-pane; 20 sat in a pane with no active class. cargo xtask verify (full) green. Follow-ups bd-ca17fck0 and bd-tebu6o4a remain open. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-18-tabset-headings-in-toc.md

c-alvmzjao.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-alvmzjao.text:
FIXED on branch braid/bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7 (not pushed). Took direction (B): the TOC is the section tree. Five commits: Phase 0 regression net (58dd896c), Phase 1 conditional-content unwrap (8c7def63, bd-wbnaa2ud), Phase 2 sectionize recursion + pandoc's absorb rule (6955454e, bd-26nryuwh), Phase 3 the walk stops at a non-section Div (175ff023, also closes bd-8yjvs3bj), Phase 4 docs (cbf65a6b).

NOTE FOR THE RECORD: this strand's stated ROOT CAUSE was wrong. Q1's render_tabset returns real AST, not a raw-HTML blob, and Q1's own render of the repro contains <section id="create-the-integration" class="level4"> inside the pane. The real mechanism is pandoc's sectionToListItem matching only Div(_,_,Header:rest), so the walk stops at Div(.panel-tabset) whose first child is Plain(nav). That reframing is what produced direction (B) instead of the two options the description proposed, and it turned up a third leaking container the description did not name: callout bodies.

VERIFICATION. cargo xtask verify (full) green; 12328 Rust tests. Connect docs port, 451 pages, clean double render: exact TOC parity with Q1 421 -> 444; 44 entries removed, 0 added; 25 pages closer to Q1, 426 unchanged, 0 further. All 44 removals were inside a div.tab-pane (HTML-parsed); 20 sat in a pane with no active class, i.e. links a reader could not follow. Strand predicted 44 leaked and 18 dead; measured 44 and 20. The strand's repro now matches Q1 exactly: ['configuration','next-steps'].

The 7 pages still differing from Q1 are pre-existing and byte-identical to baseline (two are a Q1-side unresolved-shortcode id defect where q2's ids are the correct ones; one em-dash slug; four with a pre-existing extra entry).

Follow-ups filed: bd-ca17fck0 (profile outline lists callout titles the rendered TOC omits), bd-tebu6o4a (reveal skips sectionize, so a future reveal TOC would be empty). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-18-tabset-headings-in-toc.md. Awaiting review; not pushed.

c-n5nmjlcg.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-n5nmjlcg.text: Investigated 2026-08-18: plan skeleton at claude-notes/plans/2026-08-18-tabset-headings-in-toc.md (commit b6134978 on main), probe fixture under claude-notes/plans/tabset-headings-in-toc-investigation/div-toc-probe/. Verdict: ready to design, but this strand's stated ROOT CAUSE is wrong — Q1's render_tabset returns real AST, not a raw-HTML blob, and Q1's own render of the repro has <section id="create-the-integration" class="level4"> inside the pane. The real rule is that Pandoc's TOC is exactly the section tree (sectionToListItem matches only Div(_,_,Header:rest), so the walk stops at Div(.panel-tabset) whose first child is Plain(nav)). q2 has two cancelling divergences: collect_toc_entries recurses into every Div AND BlockQuote; sectionize_blocks recurses into neither. Hence a third fix direction beyond the strand's (a)/(b): match Pandoc's section-tree rule in both, which also fixes an unfiled blockquote TOC leak and the div-vs-section DOM divergence, with no panel-tabset knowledge in pampa. Five design questions pending user alignment.

title: revealjs skips SectionizeTransform, so a future reveal TOC would be empty
description:
Found while implementing bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7 Phase 3.

collect_toc_entries (crates/pampa/src/toc.rs) now walks only the section tree: a Div that is not a section terminates the walk, matching pandoc's sectionToListItem. Its precondition is therefore that callers pass blocks that have been through sectionize_blocks.

SectionizeTransform is pushed only in the non-reveal branch (crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:1332), while TocGenerateTransform is ungated (:1387). On revealjs the collector would find no section tree and see only top-level Headers -- and reveal wraps slides in Divs, so it would find nothing at all.

NOT A LIVE BUG: verified that q2 emits no <nav id="TOC"> for revealjs today (rendered a two-slide deck with toc: true; no TOC nav, no toc-active, no quarto-toc marker). So nothing is broken now.

THE TRAP is for whoever adds a reveal TOC, or lands bd-y5j0m376 (reveal tabsets): they would get an empty TOC with no obvious cause. Fix is to run sectionize for reveal too, which is a real change to reveal's slide DOM and wants its own testing, or to give reveal a TOC path that does not depend on the section tree.

The precondition is documented in pampa::toc's module docs.

title: Nav hrefs to static (non-document) files are not page-relativized
description: resolve_href_for_html (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_href.rs) resolves .qmd hrefs through the ProjectIndex and page-relativizes the result, but a nav href pointing at a static file (e.g. navbar href: assets/report.pdf, or a pre-rendered .html) misses the index and falls through to raw.to_string() — emitted verbatim. From a page in a subdirectory the browser resolves it against the page dir and 404s; a leading-/ form survives to output and breaks under a deploy subpath (same class as bd-root-relative-paths-design-fc5pvkcv Case B, which fixed this for body images). Likely fix: on index miss for a non-.qmd path, route through resolve_root_relative_resource_href instead of returning raw. Discovered during the Case A investigation; see claude-notes/plans/2026-08-13-site-root-relative-paths.md.
close_reason: Fixed on main (commit 848c80e7 lineage — see 'Relativize non-.qmd index misses in nav and body href resolvers'). resolve_href_for_html now routes non-.qmd index misses through resolve_root_relative_resource_href; nav hrefs to static files page-relativize at every depth. TDD (7 failing tests first), e2e-verified through cargo run --bin q2 -- render on claude-notes/plans/index-miss-relativize-investigation/repro (navbar assets/report.pdf emits ../../assets/report.pdf from a depth-2 page). c-a1rrcigs.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-a1rrcigs.text: Final commit hash on main after amends: 57f89387 (the close reason cited a pre-amend hash). Breadcrumbs (bd-breadcrumbs-missing-1vpuqh34) landed on top in 66bd2284, consuming the settled resolver.

c-jk90jh5j.author: Claude (q2-connect-docs)
c-jk90jh5j.text:
Now paired: bd-root-absolute-dir-link-58eh8834 is the body-link half of this same defect, filed from the Posit Connect docs port with a Q1-verified repro. Linked related.

The two are the same fallthrough in sibling functions of navigation_href.rs (line numbers against main at 3ac596e0):

  resolve_href_for_html      :152   lookup :178   miss -> raw.to_string() :205   (this strand — nav href to a static file)
  resolve_doc_relative_href  :308   lookup :334   miss -> raw.to_string() :358   (bd-root-absolute-dir-link — body link to a directory)

Both misses are silent for the same deliberate reason (.qmd-only diagnostics, bd-6d2wj4zp D6). The fix direction already recorded here — route the non-.qmd miss through resolve_root_relative_resource_href (:434) rather than returning raw — applies verbatim to the other one, which is the argument for doing them together rather than as two patches.

One check worth recording since it could have gone the other way: this strand's suggested helper, resolve_root_relative_resource_href, does exist on main at :434 (a thin project-root-anchored wrapper over resolve_static_resource_href :393). It is absent from a v0.20.0-era checkout, so a session reading a stale tree may conclude the suggestion names a phantom. It does not.

c-ucvublxh.author: Claude (q2-connect-docs)
c-ucvublxh.text:
Linked related: bd-breadcrumbs-missing-1vpuqh34 (website breadcrumbs not rendered).

Breadcrumbs are unimplemented, so they are not a second symptom of this bug — they are a future consumer of the code it changes, which is why the link is worth having before either is designed. A breadcrumb trail is a list of nav-surface hrefs, and section crumbs have no href of their own: they resolve to the section's first descendant document (Q1's rule). So breadcrumbs will lean on the same resolve_href_for_html / index-miss behaviour this strand is about, and building them before the miss branch is settled would replicate the defect across every crumb on every page.

Also worth folding into the same decision: the body-link face of this fallthrough. A markdown link whose target is a DIRECTORY — [text](/guide/) — misses the index for the same reason a static file does (a directory is not a source path), falls to the same raw.to_string(), and is emitted root-absolute. Q1 rebases it. That is filed in the Posit Connect docs porting skein as br-h5wdib27, with a Q1-verified repro at /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/root-absolute-dir-link/ isolating it against three controls; it has not been handed off here yet. Its Connect impact is one link that 404s under the /connect/ deploy subpath.

So the miss-branch question now has three known faces: nav hrefs to static files (this strand), body links to directories (br-h5wdib27), and breadcrumb crumb hrefs (bd-breadcrumbs-missing-1vpuqh34, prospective). The fix direction already suggested here — route non-.qmd index misses through the root-relative resource helper instead of returning raw — would cover all three if it is made the shared answer rather than a nav-surface patch.

title: Security: decouple 'what uploads to the sync server' from resources: (publish control)
description:
Surfaced wiring up embed-iframe preview (bd-kjrpya2d). To make embedded .embed-example-iframe decks resolve in preview, we sync resources:-visible static assets into the Automerge VFS. But resources: is a PUBLISH control (what lands in _site), NOT an upload/trust control. Reusing it to decide what gets uploaded to the sync server conflates two trust boundaries and is a footgun:

- A user narrows a resources: glob expecting to control PUBLISHING, not realizing it now also governs what gets UPLOADED to the sync server. They might inadvertently upload sensitive files, or expect a narrow glob to PREVENT such upload.
- Today the q2 preview sync server is local + ephemeral, so the blast radius is small. But it is easy to see a future change routing uploads to a REMOTE sync server (hub-client cloud), at which point a publish-glob silently becomes an exfiltration surface.

Goal: make it hard to do the wrong thing. Introduce an EXPLICIT, separate control for 'what may be uploaded to the sync server' (safe-by-default: deny unexpected types; opt-in for static assets needed by preview), decoupled from resources:. Consider: an allowlist of preview-syncable types/paths; a clear warning when resources globs would upload non-obvious files; never auto-upload outside an explicit set; and a hard boundary at the local/remote sync-server seam. Audit every path that vfsAddFile/uploads from the project so the trust boundary is centralized, not scattered.

Blocks/relates: the resources:-scoped .html VFS sync done for bd-kjrpya2d is the interim 'good enough' that this strand tightens. Reference: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-09-preview-embed-vfs-resolution.md.

title: Support nested website.navbar in addition to top-level navbar
description:
Today q2 only reads navbar config from a top-level `navbar:` key in `_quarto.yml` (alongside `project:`). Quarto 1 and the more natural project-level shape places it under `website:` (`website.navbar:`). Both forms should work:

- Top-level `navbar:` is useful for non-website projects that want a navbar (e.g. a single-doc with custom navigation).
- Nested `website.navbar:` is the natural project-level config home (matches Q1, matches `website.sidebar`).

Discovered while smoke-testing the bd-4eyf Bootstrap JS work — a fixture written with the natural `website.navbar:` shape silently produced no navbar markup (no error, no warning), which is a usability cliff. See claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-bootstrap-js-injection.md ("Browser smoke log" section, navbar follow-up note).

Scope:
- Reader/parser: accept `website.navbar:` as an alias for the existing top-level `navbar:`. If both are present, decide precedence (top-level wins? merge? error?) and document.
- Same treatment for `website.page-footer` if not already supported.
- Tests: extend navbar_footer_pipeline.rs with the nested shape; ensure existing top-level shape still works.
- Possibly a deprecation/migration nudge for the top-level shape if we end up preferring nested.
close_reason: Implemented in d66ff31c (alongside bd-jjep). website.navbar / website.page-footer / website.sidebar now all accepted as aliases for the top-level forms, via quarto_config::resolve_website_value(). Precedence: top-level wins, !prefer escapes the default field-wise merge. Same treatment also applied to website.sidebar's two other readers (SidebarGenerateTransform and derive_doc_scss_layer) for consistency.

title: quarto-yaml: piecewise (Concat) content provenance for escaped quoted scalars
description:
Follow-up to the 2026-08-20 diagnostic-span-integrity plan. Sibling of the block-scalar strand; same root shape, finer granularity, lower urgency.

In a quoted YAML scalar with escapes, decoded content bytes do not correspond 1:1 to source bytes, so a single content-start offset fixes everything before the first escape and drifts by one byte per escape thereafter:

    text: "Ask\tAI U+2728"

    source:   "  A  s  k  \  t  A  I  _  U+2728  "
    content:      A  s  k  ->TAB<-  A  I  _  U+2728
                           ^
             one content byte, two source bytes

Content offset 4 sits at source base+5, not base+4, and each further escape adds another byte of drift. This is not exclusive to double quotes: single-quoted YAML escapes its quote by doubling it, so 'it''s' is 5 source bytes decoding to 4 content bytes.

v1 (shipped by the plan) returns content_source_info = None for any escaped scalar, so q2 underlines the whole scalar rather than the wrong bytes. Correct but imprecise.

THE FIX is the same machinery as the block-scalar strand: a SourceInfo::Concat whose pieces are the verbatim runs between escapes, plus a one-content-byte piece per escape pointing at its multi-byte source sequence. map_offset then resolves every content offset exactly. As with block scalars, going from None to Some(Concat) needs NO consumer change: q2's Phase 4 call site already matches on Option<SourceInfo> with a precision-fallback None arm.

PREREQUISITES are the same as the block-scalar strand and are already verified: SourceInfo::concat is public, SourcePiece's fields are pub, and no new quarto-source-map API is required.

WHY LOWER PRIORITY THAN THE BLOCK-SCALAR CASE: escapes in markdown-config presentation keys are rare in practice, the drift is bounded by the escape count rather than compounding per line, and unlike multi-line block scalars it does not currently misreport the LINE. It is still capable of landing mid-character, which would have crashed before the quarto-error-reporting char-boundary fix.

The relevant escape forms to cover: double-quoted backslash escapes (\t, \n, \", \\, \uXXXX), and single-quoted doubled-quote ('').

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-diagnostic-span-integrity.md
close_reason: Absorbed into claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-1-foundations.md (Phase 2). Same reason as bd-jmquuiqh: Plan 1 became comprehensive, so Concat provenance for escaped quoted scalars is plan content, not a follow-up. The escape-form matrix (double-quoted \t \n \" \\ \uXXXX, single-quoted '') is now a checklist row.

title: Nested-cell mask: decide whether the display-class predicate should widen past empty/`markdown`
description:
Deferred, deliberately, from bd-0gwekaem (inline expressions inside a display block).

The nested-cell mask is in scope for a CodeBlock whose attr classes are empty or exactly ["markdown"] (nested_cell_mask.rs, is_in_scope_for_masking). An author who reaches for a *language* class to get syntax highlighting on the example they are showing — ````r, ````qmd — gets no protection at all, for either the fence-opener rewrite or the inline-expression rewrite bd-0gwekaem added.

MEASURED, on the bd-0gwekaem branch, q2 rendering a knitr document with a live cell defining v:

  display block      classic inline `r v`     nested ```{r} opener
  ````markdown       shown (fixed)            shown
  ````r             EVALUATED                executes

The ````r row is the whole question. It is not a regression and not a q2-vs-Q1 gap: Quarto 1 executes there too (bd-0gwekaem's matrix, row E). So the narrow predicate is parity, and widening would put q2 ahead rather than catching it up.

WHY IT WAS NOT WIDENED WITH THE INLINE FIX

1. It is not inline-specific. The same predicate gates both rewrites, so widening is a change to the *cell* escape as much as the inline one — and 2026-09-02-nested-cell-masking.md scoped it out explicitly ("Display classes — empty or markdown only. An author writing ````qmd gets nothing. Deliberate: Q-2-50's hint names markdown. Widening is a separate decision.").

2. Widening for inline *only* would be worse than either uniform answer: '````r protects your inline expressions but not your nested fences' is a rule nobody can hold in their head.

3. T18 is frozen and revert-bound to the narrow predicate. Its fixture is a ````python block with a fence-opener-shaped substring embedded in its body, asserting the writer's piece pairs are identical to an unmasked run precisely *because* the block's classes keep it out of scope. Widening reddens it, and the plan's test-seam rule is that a green test's assertions are never edited to go green.

WHAT WIDENING WOULD NEED

- A decision on the class set. `markdown` + `qmd` is the conservative step; 'any class that is not itself an engine language' is the ambitious one; 'every code block' is what T18 forbids.
- The engine_cell_lang conjunct in is_in_scope_for_masking stops being dead code the moment this widens — that is exactly why the module doc says to keep it ("It becomes load-bearing the moment the display-class predicate widens past [\"markdown\"]").
- T18 would need a replacement fixture whose out-of-scope-ness comes from something other than a language class.
- Weigh against the cost: masking a ````r block means rewriting inside text an author may well have meant literally. R permits backtick-quoted names, so a displayed df$`r value` is an inline-expression shape that is really just R source. The rewrite is byte-exactly reversible so nothing renders wrong, but the block picks up Generated (location-unknown) provenance for no gain.

Related: bd-q250-nested-fence-blind-spot-t68z1lsw owns the diagnostic side of nested fences.

title: Improve cargo xtask dev-setup: cmake detection and xtask self-build lock
description: Two cross-platform dev-ergonomics improvements surfaced while verifying PR 109 on Windows after rebasing on main. Both are orthogonal to the WASM work and belong in their own PR. Target branch feature/dev-setup-improvements, worktree at .worktrees/dev-setup-improvements. Base branch origin/main. See design and acceptance fields for details.
design:
Background. Main added quarto-highlight (commit 1fa33da0, bd-n7x2 epic) which enables the `wasm` feature on tree-sitter for native builds. That pulls in wasmtime-c-api-impl as a transitive dependency, whose build.rs shells out to cmake. Result: cmake is now a hard prerequisite for `cargo build --workspace` on every platform. GitHub Actions runners have it pre-installed. Local dev boxes frequently do not (confirmed on Chris's Windows setup).

Fix 1 — check_cmake() in crates/xtask/src/dev_setup.rs. Follow the existing check_pandoc() pattern at line 155. Detection via `cmake --version`. If missing, print a warning with platform-specific install commands (scoop/winget on Windows, brew on macOS, apt/dnf on Linux). Unlike pandoc the warning should be stronger because cmake missing means `cargo build --workspace` fails, not just specific tests. No version constraint — any modern cmake works for wasmtime-c-api. Single function, no NativeTool struct abstraction (YAGNI).

Fix 2 — `--exclude xtask` in crates/xtask/src/verify.rs step 3. The current code at line 112 runs `cargo build --workspace`, which re-links target/debug/xtask.exe while the currently-running xtask.exe holds a file lock on Windows. Error: `failed to remove file ... Accès refusé (os error 5)`. Linux/macOS tolerate overwriting a running exe, so this was latent. Change to `["build", "--workspace", "--exclude", "xtask"]`. Step 5 (nextest) is unaffected — it compiles xtask as a test binary at a different path, no conflict. Cross-platform safe.

Fix 3 — CONTRIBUTING.md cmake subsection. Add after the existing "macOS: Homebrew LLVM (for WASM builds)" section. Same shape: one paragraph explaining why, then per-platform install commands. Covers Windows (scoop/winget), macOS (brew — note it bundles with Homebrew LLVM if already installed for WASM), Linux (apt/dnf).

Out of scope. Generic NativeTool struct for future deps. Version floor for cmake. Windows MSVC Build Tools check (Microsoft's canonical Rust-on-Windows guide already covers this).

Related. bd-jakt investigates a different cargo xtask dev-setup issue (--locked causing externref mismatch) — same file, different concern.
acceptance_criteria: check_cmake() runs in cargo xtask dev-setup and reports suitable version when cmake is on PATH. When cmake is absent, dev-setup prints a clear warning with platform-specific install commands but does not fail. cargo xtask verify succeeds on Windows without hitting the xtask.exe file lock. CONTRIBUTING.md lists cmake as a prereq with install commands for all three platforms. No regression in CI (xtask tests still run via step 5 nextest --workspace).

c-situh2oo.author: cderv
c-situh2oo.text:
Design rationale not captured above. The `wasm` feature on tree-sitter exists for runtime loading of user-defined tree-sitter grammars compiled to WASM, on the native side, via wasmtime-c-api. The 12 statically-linked grammars in quarto-highlight (python, R, JS, etc.) do not need it. Browser side uses a different mechanism (web-tree-sitter via wasm-bindgen, Phase 4). Source: crates/quarto-highlight/Cargo.toml:39-45. Already scoped to non-wasm32 targets, so the WASM build itself does not pay the cmake cost.

Can we avoid cmake entirely while keeping native runtime user-grammar loading via WASM? Not today. Tree-sitter 0.25 exposes one WASM-runtime feature: `wasm` -> `wasmtime-c-api` -> `wasmtime-c-api-impl` (the cmake-shelling-out crate). No alternative for wasmer, wasmi, or pure-Rust wasmtime. The choice is hard-wired into tree-sitter's C layer (lib/src/wasm_store.c), not just the Rust bindings, so a Cargo-feature-only fix is impossible. Upstream issue tree-sitter/tree-sitter#4715 ("Consider supporting wasm-c-api") was closed without action; no upstream issue or PR for pure-Rust wasmtime. No third-party fork solves this for the WASM-loading path.

Options.

(1) Contribute upstream pluggable WASM-runtime support or a pure-Rust wasmtime switch. Long path, depends on maintainers.

(2) Feature-gate the `wasm` activation in quarto-highlight (e.g. default-on `user-grammars` feature) so devs without cmake can opt out via `--no-default-features` and lose only runtime custom-grammar loading. Does not avoid cmake for the default build.

(3) Switch native runtime grammar loading from WASM to native shared libraries (.so / .dylib / .dll) using upstream's own `tree-sitter-loader` crate (crates/loader/ in tree-sitter/tree-sitter, published on crates.io). It uses `libloading` for dlopen / LoadLibrary and the `cc` crate to compile grammars to dylibs — only a C compiler, no cmake. This is the same path the `tree-sitter` CLI uses for `tree-sitter parse`. Trade-off: users distribute native dylibs per-platform instead of one portable .wasm.

PR 136 documented and detected cmake without exploring (1)-(3). The trade-off belongs with the lead dev who introduced quarto-highlight in bd-n7x2.

title: StageContext eagerly creates+leaks a temp dir per document (lazy-init fix)
description:
StageContext::new (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/context.rs:215) eagerly calls runtime.temp_dir("quarto-pipeline").into_path() for every document. The dir is created (per-page mkdir, ~2.9% of serial render CPU in the qmd-plans profile) AND leaked (into_path sets cleanup=false). The only production reader is engine_execution.rs:265, gated behind the to_run.is_empty() fast path (line 219) — so pure-markdown docs create+leak it but never read it.

Fix: make temp_dir lazily created on first access via std::sync::OnceLock<PathBuf> + a temp_dir(&self) -> Result<&Path> accessor. Preserves Send+Sync (no new dep). Discovered during bd-3gj56 post-fix profiling; see claude-notes/plans/2026-06-01-render-perf-profiling.md (filesystem bucket).

title: q2 preview --single-file fails when no _quarto.yml ancestor exists
description:
When invoked on a single .qmd file with no _quarto.yml ancestor, q2 preview's single-file fallback sets project_root to the file path itself (a file, not a directory). The chain then fails:

1. crates/quarto/src/commands/preview.rs:270-276 — 'No _quarto.yml ancestor → single-file mode (Phase A semantics). project_root is the file path itself.'
2. crates/quarto-hub/src/discovery.rs::ProjectFiles::discover() walks via WalkDir, which on a single-file root yields exactly one entry: the file itself.
3. path.strip_prefix(project_root) for the same file path returns an empty PathBuf, which is pushed into qmd_files.
4. crates/quarto-hub/src/context.rs:431 reconcile_files_with_index does project_root.join(file_path). With file_path empty, the result is project_root + '/' (a trailing-slash variant of the file path).
5. std::fs::read_to_string fails with ENOTDIR (os error 20) because the OS treats the trailing slash as 'I want a directory here'.

Symptom: the warning 'quarto_hub::context: Failed to read text file, skipping path= error=Not a directory (os error 20)' with an empty path= field fires on every iteration. The preview SPA stays stuck at 'Initializing q2-preview…' indefinitely (no document content ever reaches it).

Reproduction:

    cp /any/file.qmd /tmp/
    q2 preview --no-browser --port 0 /tmp/file.qmd

(must use a directory with no _quarto.yml anywhere above it).

Workaround: place a minimal _quarto.yml ('project: type: default') alongside the file, then q2 preview works correctly.

Likely fix candidates:
- preview.rs:270-276 should set project_root to canonical.parent() (the directory containing the file), and initial_page to the file name. This matches what happens when a _quarto.yml ancestor IS found, modulo where the project root sits.
- Alternatively: detect single-file mode earlier and special-case ProjectFiles to contain exactly that one file with a non-empty relative path.

The cleaner fix is probably the former — there's no real benefit to having project_root be a file rather than its containing directory.

Discovered during bd-s3z1g (React CodeBlock parity verification): noticed the empty path= warning while trying to e2e-test the React change. Pre-existing, not caused by anything in bd-s3z1g.

Related: bd-1tl09 (code-block decorations epic) — many of those features will require working single-file preview.

title: A heading inside a div that carries an id never reaches the TOC
description:
A section heading wrapped in a fenced div that carries an id is emitted correctly but never appears in the page TOC. Quarto 1 lists it. There is no diagnostic and the render exits 0, so the only symptom is a heading the reader can scroll to but cannot navigate to.

WHAT HAPPENS VS QUARTO 1

The trigger is specifically an id on the wrapping div. A div with no attributes, or with only a class, is fine on both engines:

  case                                              q2 0.29.0   Quarto 1
  A  no wrapper, top level                          in TOC      in TOC
  B  ::: {} — no attributes                         in TOC      in TOC
  C  ::: {.someclass} — class only                  in TOC      in TOC
  D  ::: {#someid} — id only                        NO          in TOC
  E  ::: {#someid2 .someclass2} — id and class      NO          in TOC
  F  ::: {#someid3} with a [span]{#id} heading      NO          in TOC
  G  ::: {#someid4}, prose BEFORE the heading       NO          NO
  H  ::: {#outer} wrapping ::: {#inner}             NO          in TOC

B and C locate the trigger: a wrapper alone does not break the TOC, only a wrapper with an id. F rules out the bracketed-span heading as a separate suspect — D, a plain heading, fails identically.

The two engines emit the SAME DOM; only the TOC differs. q2 flattens a class-only div into the section, folding the class onto the <section> so it stays a direct child of the body. An id-bearing div cannot be flattened that way — its id would collide with the section's own — so q2 emits a real wrapper and nests the section inside it:

  <div id="someid"><section id="d-div-id-only" class="section level2">

Quarto 1 emits exactly the same nesting and still lists the heading. So sectionization is correct and should not be touched; only TOC collection is wrong.

ROOT CAUSE

crates/pampa/src/toc.rs, collect_toc_entries (~:365). The walk recurses only into Divs carrying the 'section' class (is_section_div, :401, tests classes for "section"); every other Div falls to the catch-all arm and ends the walk, so the section Div nested inside an author's id-bearing wrapper is never visited.

The comment above that arm justifies it by appeal to pandoc:

  // Only section Divs are walked. A Div that is not a section
  // ends the walk, with no recursion past it — pandoc's
  // `sectionToListItem` matches `Div(_, _, Header:rest)` and
  // returns nothing for anything else.

That reading is incomplete. Pandoc's toTOCTree (Text/Pandoc/Chunks.hs:368) has a second clause:

  go (Div (ident,_,_) (Header lev (_,classes,kvs) ils : subsecs))
    | … = (Node SecInfo{…} (foldr go [] subsecs) :)
  go (Div _ [d@Div{}]) = go d -- #8402
  go _ = id

The #8402 line descends through a wrapper Div whose sole content is another Div — exactly this case. Measured against pandoc 3.8.1 with --toc --section-divs: case D IS listed.

SUGGESTED FIX

Recurse past a non-section Div into its content when that content is a single Div, rather than ending the walk. Two constraints, both measured, and the repro carries a case for each:

- Do NOT recurse unconditionally into every Div. Case G — a wrapper holding prose before the heading — is excluded from the TOC by BOTH pandoc and Quarto 1. A blanket recursion would list it and diverge from Q1 in the opposite direction.
- Pandoc's clause is not sufficient on its own. It unwraps exactly one level, so it misses case H (an id div nested inside another id div), which Quarto 1 DOES list. Porting #8402 literally is a partial fix; matching Q1 needs the descent to iterate while still stopping at G's shape.

  case                          pandoc 3.8.1   Quarto 1     q2 0.29.0
  D  sole child                 listed         listed       NO
  G  prose before heading       not listed     not listed   not listed
  H  doubly nested              not listed     listed       NO

test_non_section_div_terminates_the_walk in toc.rs's test module pins the current behaviour and will need revisiting rather than being treated as a guard rail. The neighbouring test_blockquote_heading_is_not_collected (bd-8yjvs3bj) is a genuine guard rail and should stay green: a quoted heading is never a section and must never be listed.

REAL-WORLD HIT

The Positron website port, download.html. The page wraps its hero section in ::: {#download-hero .download-hero …}, and the heading inside it is missing from the page TOC while every other heading on the page is present. The section itself renders and is anchorable; only the navigation entry is gone. The same shape appears wherever the site wraps a section to hang CSS or JavaScript off a stable id, which is the normal reason to put an id on a div.

Invisible to text-level comparison sweeps: the heading text is present in the body on both engines, and the TOC entry is a <nav> link, so a diff of visible page text reports nothing. It was found by reading the rendered markup directly.

REPRO

/Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/toc-skips-headings-in-id-div/

  sh check.sh                                  # q2 and Quarto 1
  sh check.sh ~/.local/bin/q2.0.28.0-backup    # or any other build

Eight cases in one render; for each it reports whether the heading was emitted and whether it reached the TOC. A/B/C are the controls that locate the trigger, D/E/F are the failures, G is the negative control and H the depth case. The README carries the mechanism, the pandoc source reading, and the three-engine comparison table.

Origin strand: br-toc-skips-headings-in-fenced-div-np5a1arv in the Positron docs port's skein (/Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs). Observed on q2 0.29.0 (official release build); also reproduces on 0.28.0 and 0.27.0, so it is long-standing rather than a regression. q2 HEAD checked at 914f20697 — nothing has touched crates/quarto-navigation/ or the transforms since the 0.29.0 tag. Q1 reference: quarto dev build 99.9.9.

NOTE ON THE TITLE HISTORY: this was first filed locally as 'a heading inside a fenced div never reaches the TOC', which was too broad — the original fixture used ::: {#wrap .wrap} for both its cases and so could not tell an id from a class. Re-scoped after adding B and C.
