title: TOC entry drops the quote glyphs around a quoted span (heading keeps them)
description:
A heading containing a quoted span renders with curly quotes, but its table-of-contents entry drops the quote characters entirely. The two disagree within one page.

## What happens vs Quarto 1

Source: `## Using a "raw" volume`, with `toc: true`.

| | heading | TOC entry |
|---|---|---|
| Quarto 1 | Using a “raw” volume | Using a “raw” volume |
| q2 0.20.0 | Using a “raw” volume | Using a raw volume |

The words survive; only the delimiters are lost. No diagnostic is emitted.

The controls that make this specific: an apostrophe (`repository's identifiers`) and an en dash (`Gallery -- really`) come through correctly in *both* the heading and the TOC. Those are `Str`-internal rewrites done by `apply_smart_typography`; the failing case is the one that becomes an `Inline::Quoted` node instead.

## Root-cause area

`inlines_to_text` in crates/pampa/src/toc.rs:409, reached from `generate_toc` (toc.rs:251) via crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/toc_generate.rs:139. Its `Quoted` arm at toc.rs:424 recurses into the content and never emits delimiters, ignoring `q.quote_type`:

```rust
Inline::Quoted(q) => text.push_str(&inlines_to_text(&q.content)),
```

`Quoted` is built by the reader, not by a later filter — `process_quoted` at crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/quote_helpers.rs:101 keeps `quote_type` and the inner content while discarding the delimiter children (quote_helpers.rs:96). So by the time the TOC is generated the quote type is known and available; it is simply not consulted.

The HTML writer does the right thing for the same node, which is why the heading itself is correct.

## Suggested fix direction

Emit the delimiters in the toc.rs:424 arm, choosing them from `q.quote_type` (U+201C/U+201D for `DoubleQuote`, U+2018/U+2019 for `SingleQuote`) so the TOC matches the rendered heading. The match in `inlines_to_text` is exhaustive — no `_` fallthrough — so this is a localized change.

Worth a glance while there: the sibling helper `inlines_to_text` in crates/quarto-core/src/template.rs:1064 has the opposite bug in its `Quoted` arm (template.rs:1081-1085) — it emits straight ASCII `"` on both sides regardless of `quote_type`, so a single-quoted span comes out double-quoted. A third copy lives at crates/pampa/src/citeproc_filter.rs:935.

## Real-world hit in the Connect docs

`admin/getting-started/off-host-install/configure-helm-chart`, heading `Option 2: Using a “raw” NFS volume`. That is the only heading with a quoted span in the whole Connect corpus, so the blast radius is small — but the symptom is a visible inconsistency between the TOC and the heading it points at, on a page a reader has open.

## Repro

/Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/toc-smart-quotes/

Run `q2 render` there and compare with `quarto render --output-dir _site-q1`. The first heading is the failing case; headings two and three are the apostrophe and en-dash controls.

Observed on q2 0.19.0, re-verified against the released 0.20.0 binary (q2 HEAD 0dcd7e83). Origin strand in the q2-connect-docs skein: br-toc-smart-quotes-pw1vkzj8.

## Related

The same heading also gets a wrong anchor id, via a different code path that drops the quoted content outright rather than just the glyphs. Filed separately; the two are worth fixing together since the divergence between `pampa::toc::inlines_to_text` and `pampa::utils::autoid::collect_text` is exactly what makes a TOC label and the anchor it targets disagree.

title: Tabsets (panel-tabset) are not implemented — tab titles leak into the TOC
description:
Quarto 1 turns a Div with class .panel-tabset into Bootstrap tab navigation: the level-N Headers inside the Div become clickable tabs, and each tab's content becomes a pane. q2 has no tabset support at all: the Div passes through as a plain
with its Headers rendered as ordinary stacked headings — all tab contents visible at once, nothing clickable. The most visible downstream symptom, and how this was found: the tab-title Headers survive to TOC time, so every tab name appears in the table of contents. In a doc with headings 'Real heading' / 'Another real heading' wrapping a two-tab tabset, Q1's
has exactly those 2 entries; q2's has 4 ('Tab Alpha' and 'Tab Beta' join them). The TOC collector is NOT at fault: pampa's collect_toc_entries (crates/pampa/src/toc.rs:341) correctly recurses into non-section Divs and finds genuine Header nodes there. Q1 has no tabset-exclusion logic in its TOC either — its tabset filter simply consumes the Headers before the TOC is built. The right fix reproduces that, not a special case in the collector. Root cause area: nothing to fix, only to add. The only 'panel-tabset' in quarto-core today is a negative test in transforms/callout.rs (asserting the class is not a callout). Q1's reference implementation is quarto-cli src/resources/filters/customnodes/panel-tabset.lua — notably a custom node there too, which validates the natural q2 shape: mirror the callout pair (CalloutTransform: Div -> CustomNode, CalloutResolveTransform: CustomNode -> HTML structure) with a PanelTabsetTransform + resolve stage. Pipeline placement does the TOC work for free: CalloutTransform sits at crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:1232, before SectionizeTransform (:1317) and TocGenerateTransform (:1371); a tabset transform in the same neighborhood consumes the tab-title Headers before sectionize or TOC ever see them. Target markup (verbatim shape from Q1's committed render of the repro):
    with
  • per tab, followed by
    holding
    panes. q2 already ships bootstrap.bundle.min.js on every HTML page, so basic tab switching needs no new JS once this markup exists. Q1 also emits an empty
    sibling for margin-content hoisting; deferrable. GROUPED TABSETS ARE IN SCOPE, not a nice-to-have — this is an explicit requirement from the Connect docs port. A tabset may carry group="language" (etc.); Q1 puts data-group="language" on the panel div, and a small JS module (Q1's site_libs/quarto-html/tabsets/tabsets.js, ~95 lines) syncs every same-group tabset on the page when a tab is selected and persists the choice in localStorage under 'quarto-persistent-tabsets-data' (getTabSettings/setTabState/toggleAll/setupSelectorSync). In the Connect docs ~166 of ~185 tabsets are grouped (group="language" dominates, then "apm", "distro", "shell", "framework") — a reader picks Python once and every page follows. Port that module (or equivalent) along with the markup; without it grouped tabsets degrade to independent ones, which is not acceptable parity for this port. Real-world hit: ~115 of the 352 Connect docs pages have tabsets; every one renders as stacked headings with a polluted TOC (e.g. the OpenTelemetry pages list Datadog / Grafana / Pseudo-query after every real heading). It is the single largest chrome-sweep noise source in the port — of 123 differing pages in the 0.21.0 triage, all but three were this. Minimal repro: /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/toc-tabset-titles/ — run 'q2 render' there and compare _site/index.html against the committed Q1 render in _site-q1/ (expected: 2 TOC entries and nav-tabs markup; actual: 4 TOC entries, bare panel-tabset div). The grouped-tabset markup to match can be seen in /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/docs-quarto-1/_site/admin/upgrade/index.html (data-group="distro") and the sync module at docs-quarto-1/_site/site_libs/quarto-html/tabsets/tabsets.js under the same root. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-toc-tabset-titles-e47klspv. Observed with q2 0.19.0; re-verified failing on 0.20.0, 0.21.0 and 0.22.0; q2 origin/main (60cc579e, 2026-08-17) has no tabset work.

title: qmd parser/writer: round-trip `Str "@{some-key}"` (inline brace forms unsupported)
description:
Discovered while implementing bd-21gu. The qmd parser rejects bare `{...}` and `\\@{...}` in inline contexts:

  printf 'foo {some-key} bar\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t native
  → Parse error (column 6, '{')
  printf '\\@{some-key}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t native
  → Parse error

This means a `Str` whose body contains `@{some-key}` (e.g. coming in via JSON) cannot be round-tripped, even though the writer-side `@` escape (bd-21gu) lookahead does include `{` so it would emit `\\@{some-key}` — the resulting qmd then fails to re-parse.

Two possible fixes (require investigation):
  1. Parser: accept bare `{...}` as a literal (inline-brace context disambiguation).
  2. Writer: escape `{` and `}` defensively for `Str` inlines (parallel to the @ fix).

Defer until needed by a real-world case.

title: Engine-extension boundary is raw-text-based: can a TS engine tell an executable cell from one inside a display block?
description:
INVESTIGATION ONLY — analysis first, no fix until reviewed.

q2 uses two different parsers for two jobs and they disagree about nested fences.

  crates/quarto-core/src/engine/resolution.rs:250 — computational_languages(ast: &Pandoc) is AST-based and CORRECT: a ```{r} fence nested inside a ````markdown display block does NOT activate knitr. (Quarto 1 gets this wrong and does activate.)

  The knitr execution preprocessor is raw-text-based and INCORRECT: once knitr is live for a document, it also picks up the nested fence and EXECUTES it. Observed on the official v0.28.0 release build: a document with one real {r} cell plus a display block containing ```{r} renders 4 cell-output blocks — both bodies run. Quarto 1 produces the identical wrong result, so this is inherited behaviour, not a q2 regression. The bug is reachable only when the engine is already active: remove the real cell and nothing executes, because AST-based detection correctly declines to start the engine.

TS engine extensions are exposed MORE severely than the built-ins, because they do their own language detection AND their own cell splitting, both from raw text:

  crates/quarto-core/src/engine/ts_protocol.rs — TsExecuteOptions.input is a String; TsExecuteResult.markdown is a String. The engine never receives the AST.
  ts-packages/quarto-api/src/markdownRegex/index.ts — the host API q2 hands engines for this job. Note the name. getLanguagesWithClasses (~line 378) uses a flat per-line regex; breakQuartoMd (~line 768) uses endCodeRegEx = /^\s*(```+)\s*$/, which may not enforce CommonMark's rule that a fence closes only on a fence of at least equal length.
  Consumers: crates/quarto-core/tests/fixtures/extensions/julia-engine/src/julia-engine.ts and .../marimo/src/marimo-engine.ts.

QUESTIONS TO ANSWER WITH EVIDENCE
1. Does getLanguages / getLanguagesWithClasses report a language for a document whose ONLY cell of that language sits inside a display block? If so an extension's claimsLanguage path can claim a document with no real work in it.
2. Does breakQuartoMd honour CommonMark fence-length nesting (a fence opened with N backticks closes only on >= N)? Test a ````markdown block containing a ``` fence.
3. What does an extension engine actually DO with the resulting chunk — is display content executed, mangled, dropped, or passed through? Run the julia and marimo fixtures.
4. Is there a split-brain — cases where the AST resolver says 'no cells of language L' while the engine's regex scan disagrees, or vice versa?
5. Should the protocol carry an AST-derived cell list, or authoritative cell byte-ranges, instead of a raw String? TsExecuteOptions already carries a source_map — is that the right seam?

DELIVERABLE: for each of 1-5, what was tested, the exact input, the observed output, and whether it is correct. Then a recommendation on where a fix belongs (markdownRegex partitioner / protocol shape / per-engine) and what would break.

COORDINATION: bd-q250-nested-fence-blind-spot-t68z1lsw covers the DIAGNOSTIC side of nested fences and is under active investigation on worktree workspace-1. This strand is the ENGINE side. Cross-reference, do not pre-empt.

All observations above are from v0.28.0; re-verify against HEAD before concluding.

c-aacqxt04.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-aacqxt04.text:
ANALYSIS COMPLETE — committed as b7dc25ba8 on braid/bd-ts-engine-display-fence-joy59gkr (worktree workspace-2). No production file changed; no fix written. Six strands filed, all discovered-from this one.

ANSWERS TO 1-5 (all re-verified on HEAD 00a1c1702, not the 0.28.0 release)

1. YES, getLanguagesWithClasses reports a language whose only cell is inside a display block (and inside a blockquote too — the [\t >]* prefix class). marimo's containsMarimoFence does the same. BUT the claimsLanguage/claimsFile path is NOT reachable: nothing in q2 or the Deno host calls getLanguages*, and claimsFile is refused for every native extension by the Q-2-51 gate at source_conversion.rs:188 (.filter(|_| !is_qmd_or_md)). Hypothesis confirmed at the function level, refuted as a live defect. -> bd-nesting-blind-claim-predicates-u275w9cd (P4).

2. YES, breakQuartoMd honours fence-length nesting — index.ts:946-948 compares the closing run against the opening run, which is set from m[1].length or tickCount. The prompt's reading of endCodeRegEx missed the comparison. Two real defects in its place: (a) the comparison is === not >=, and when no exactly-equal close arrives the OPENING fence line is dropped from output entirely -> bd-breakquartomd-equal-length-close-figbquo2; (b) the actual bug, a leading-whitespace asymmetry — startCodeRegEx is /^```/ at column 0 while startCodeCellRegEx and endCodeRegEx both allow indentation, so an INDENTED display block never sets inCode and its contents are split out as cells -> bd-breakquartomd-indented-display-fence-1wxmf0bh (P1).

3. Ran both fixtures for real. julia: correct on both nesting and indentation (it partitions in Julia, not TS; its markdownRegex.partition call is dead — no partitionedMarkdown wire message exists). marimo: correct on top-level nesting; on the INDENTED shape with a second real cell after the display block, the display block renders EMPTY, cell B's island is spliced where the display cell was, and cell B's source is left as dead literal text. Exit 0, engine's own console.warning never surfaces. knitr: executes nested display content AND replaces the displayed example with '::: {.cell}' / '{.r .cell-code}' scaffolding -> bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj.

4. YES, and wider than AST-vs-regex — FIVE partitioners disagree. The one nobody flagged is q2's OWN Rust: parse_code_blocks (text_execute.rs:128) has no backtick tracking at all AND requires column 0, so it executes nested display content and MISSES indented real cells. r5-indented-real.qmd executes correctly under knitr; the same document shaped for python would silently not run. Two built-in engines, identical input, opposite answers -> bd-jupyter-parse-code-blocks-regex-z1ehfla6. (Function-level only — no jupyter on this machine; end-to-end confirmation is the first task on that strand.)

5. NO, source_map is the wrong seam — TsSourceMapEntry is provenance ({start,length,file,file_offset}), tiles the whole document, and carries no cell identity. Recommend a new additive optional field on TsExecuteOptions carrying AST-derived cell byte ranges + language + first_class; the walk in computational_languages already has them and discards them -> bd-ts-execute-cell-ranges-2i5d6izs.

RECOMMENDED ORDER: (1) fix breakQuartoMd's whitespace asymmetry — the only live destructive defect; (2) give q2's jupyter engine the AST; (3) design the protocol field. Explicitly NOT recommended: fixing knitr from q2's side.

Cross-referenced onto bd-q250-nested-fence-blind-spot-t68z1lsw with the two measurements that bear on its argument, without touching its scope.

title: TsExecuteOptions hands engines a raw String; add an AST-derived executable-cell list so extensions stop reimplementing CommonMark
description:
Finding 5 of bd-ts-engine-display-fence-joy59gkr.

TsExecuteOptions.input (ts_protocol.rs:362) is a plain String and TsExecuteResult.markdown comes back a String, so every engine re-derives 'what is a cell' from text. The analysis found FIVE independent partitioners disagreeing on the same document — pampa's AST (correct), knitr in R (nesting-blind), q2's own jupyter regex (nesting-blind AND indentation-blind, in the other direction), breakQuartoMd in TS (nesting-correct, indentation-broken), and QuartoNotebookRunner in Julia (correct).

source_map is NOT the right seam. TsSourceMapEntry (ts_protocol.rs:335) is { start, length, source: Option<{ file, file_offset }> } — a PROVENANCE map answering 'which original file did these bytes come from', for include expansion and error attribution. It carries no cell identity, language, or executability, and its entries tile the whole document rather than marking a subset. Overloading it means adding a discriminant, at which point it is a new structure wearing the old one's name.

PROPOSAL: a new, additive, optional field on TsExecuteOptions — an AST-derived list of executable cells, each at minimum { start, length, language, first_class }, as byte ranges into the same input string the engine already receives.

Byte ranges rather than cell contents, because: the engine still needs the surrounding markdown verbatim to reassemble its output; ranges compose with the existing source_map; and an engine that ignores the field keeps working unchanged.

The data already exists — the walk inside computational_languages (resolution.rs:250) has the locations in hand and currently discards them, keeping only language names.

WHAT BREAKS: nothing immediately, which is the point of additive. The cost is that q2 commits to a cell-identity contract across the wire; the first engine to RELY on it makes it load-bearing. Worth doing if the answer to 'should extensions be able to get this right' is yes.

Blocked on nothing, but only worth designing once bd-breakquartomd-indented-display-fence-1wxmf0bh has settled what the shared partitioner is expected to do.

Full analysis: claude-notes/research/2026-08-27-ts-engine-display-fence.md

title: Execute visibility: keep-hidden mode and jupyter echo: fenced
description:
Deferred follow-ups from bd-nn2fou8h (agreed scope call, 2026-08-14). That strand implemented echo/output/warning/include for both engines; these two Q1 behaviours were left out because neither has a consumer in q2 today.

1. keep-hidden (render: keep-hidden: true). In Q1, hidden content is still EMITTED but tagged with a .hidden class instead of being dropped — shouldHide() in src/core/jupyter/tags.ts, applied at three sites in jupyter.ts (cell div, code fence, each output div). q2 currently drops hidden content outright. Implementing this needs (a) the render.keep-hidden flag plumbed to the engines — ExecutionContext now carries execute_scope but not the render scope — and (b) the .hidden CSS, which q2 has not ported from Q1's _quarto-rules.scss. knitr already has the wire field (RenderConfig::keep_hidden in engine/knitr/format.rs) but nothing populates it.

2. echo: 'fenced' for jupyter. Q1's third echo value re-emits the cell as a fenced block INCLUDING its YAML option lines (echoFenced() in tags.ts, plus the ticks bump to 4 backticks in jupyter.ts). q2's CellVisibility.echo is a bool, so 'fenced' currently reads as 'not false' -> normal echo. NOTE the knitr half already works: bd-nn2fou8h forwards the raw value and resources/rmd/execute.R sets fenced.echo = identical(format$execute[['echo']], 'fenced'). So this is jupyter-only, and the engines currently DISAGREE on echo: fenced — worth fixing for that reason alone.

Both are small next to the main visibility work, and both have clear Q1 references to port from.

title: Lint: every error_catalog.json code needs a docs/errors/<subsystem>/<code>.qmd page
description:
Each entry in crates/quarto-error-catalog/error_catalog.json carries a docs_url of the form https://quarto.org/docs/errors/<subsystem>/<code>, and the site serves those from docs/errors/<subsystem>/<code>.qmd. Nothing checks that the page exists, so a diagnostic can ship pointing at a 404.

Two codes reached main in that state and were caught by eye rather than by tooling:
- Q-2-42 (Invalid Conditional Content Attribute) — still missing a page as of main @ a429becc.
- Q-2-47 / Q-2-48 (diagram cell options) — shipped page-less in PR #499, fixed in a follow-up.

Suggested shape: a `cargo xtask lint` rule (crates/xtask/src/lint/) that parses error_catalog.json, derives the expected path from subsystem + code, and reports any missing file. Cheap, no network, and it fires in the same place the other repo-specific rules do. Could also flag the reverse — a .qmd page whose code is not in the catalog.

Worth deciding while there: whether every code truly needs a page (the `status: stub` frontmatter suggests a page can be minimal but should exist), and whether the rule should be an error or a warning.

Discovered while shipping bd-mermaid-cell-options-9wo3crl0.
close_reason:
Implemented and merged in PR #502 (main @ daaa3f9d). cargo xtask lint now fails when a code in error_catalog.json has no docs/errors/<subsystem>/<code>.qmd page, or when its docs_url is not the canonical https://quarto.org/docs/errors/<subsystem>/<code>. It runs standalone, as step 1 of cargo xtask verify, and in CI — so it fires before a PR opens, which was the requirement. Verified live on main after the merge: exit 0, 955 files checked.

Rule at crates/xtask/src/lint/error_docs.rs, called from lint::run_check. First repo-level rule in that module (the other three grep one Rust file each), so run_check grew a whole-tree seam; violations anchor at the catalog entry's line.

Backfilled the 28 pages that had accumulated: extension Q-16-1..9 (the directory did not exist), project Q-5-8..12 + Q-5-17..22, lua Q-11-2..5, writer Q-3-42/43, theme Q-14-3, markdown Q-2-42. Fixed Q-3-42/Q-3-43's docs_url, which omitted the subsystem segment. No allowlist and no warn-first mode — the gate went on only after the tree was clean.

The rule proved itself mid-flight: rebasing onto v0.17.0 made it fail immediately on Q-2-47/Q-2-48, which had shipped page-less in the release. Carlos wrote those two pages by hand on main in parallel (fc2895b2), which is exactly the by-eye process this strand set out to replace — the lint would have blocked PR #499.

Scope deliberately narrow. bd-8otua stays open and owns orphan pages, misplaced pages, front-matter Mismatch, health rollups, and the 'new <Q-X-Y>' generator that docs/errors/README.md still advertises as unshipped; when it lands it should absorb lint/error_docs.rs rather than duplicate it. Page title is free to differ from catalog title. No opt-out for internal codes.

CI on #502: all 8 checks green. One macOS job failed first time on the bd-eb2wnxkp case-fold flake (2Y vs 2y), unrelated to this change and reproduced as such; re-run passed, and bd-eb2wnxkp's own fix merged in #501.

Docs: CLAUDE.md lists the rule under Current Lint Rules; docs/errors/README.md gained an Enforcement section, dropped the 'once the audit tool ships' framing, and had two dead crates/quarto-error-reporting/ links repointed post-externalization.

Plan + full verification record: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-error-docs-page-coverage-lint.md
Discovered work: bd-8meeijgq (figures.qmd references 14 images that do not exist) — still open.

c-nk8ypy1f.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-nk8ypy1f.text:
Investigated 2026-08-11 on main (commit eb8e241b). Plan skeleton: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-error-docs-page-coverage-lint.md; reconciliation probe under claude-notes/plans/error-docs-page-coverage-lint-investigation/. Pre-flight 'cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build' green at d05e021e.

Verdict: ready to design, but two corrections to the framing.

(1) The drift is 28 missing pages, not two: project 11 (Q-5-8..12, Q-5-17..22), extension 9 (Q-16-1..9), lua 4 (Q-11-2..5), writer 2 (Q-3-42/43), theme 1 (Q-14-3), markdown 1 (Q-2-42). 193 catalog codes vs 165 pages. docs/errors/extension/ does not exist at all. git log -S dates each cluster to the feature PR that added the codes (#450, #448, #393, fc422255, 896b017c, 73f92e0e) — chronic drift, not a fresh regression. No orphan pages, nothing misplaced; front-matter drift is 2 pages differing only in title case.

(2) bd-8otua ('cargo xtask error-docs' audit/health/new, plan 2026-05-22-error-docs-tooling.md) already specifies this check verbatim as the first of five problem classes, is unblocked now that bd-nvlxn is closed, and docs/errors/README.md references it three times as a promised command. Its plan even pre-answers the error-vs-warning question, deferring the decision until bd-an6z4 was mostly complete — bd-an6z4 is now closed. Recommendation is to land bd-8otua's audit and call it from lint::run_check (inheriting the CI + verify wiring) rather than write a narrow fifth lint rule, then close this strand as subsumed. User's call.

Second-order finding: Q-3-42 and Q-3-43 carry docs_url = https://quarto.org/docs/errors/Q-3-42 with no <subsystem> segment, so a file-existence-only check would pass them while the diagnostic link stays a 404. Argues for including docs_url conformance in whatever ships.

Shape note: every existing lint rule is a per-Rust-file grep over crates/**/*.rs with a file:line:column anchor. A catalog<->docs reconciliation is a whole-repo check and needs a new seam in lint/mod.rs, or violations anchored at the catalog entry's line.

Five design questions in the plan: (1) new lint rule vs land bd-8otua; (2) backfill 28 pages before gating, warn-first, or shrinking allowlist; (3) how much beyond file-existence the check verifies; (4) is title-case drift an error; (5) confirm every code needs a page.

Also added the two missing graph edges: discovered-from bd-mermaid-cell-options-9wo3crl0, related bd-8otua.

c-odpjsjk6.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-odpjsjk6.text:
Implemented on main: ebfa7f22 (content), 191872eb (lint rule), 45f833bc (verification record). Not pushed — awaiting review.

All five design questions settled with Carlos and recorded in claude-notes/plans/2026-08-11-error-docs-page-coverage-lint.md. What landed:

1. A narrow repo-level rule at crates/xtask/src/lint/error_docs.rs, not bd-8otua's full audit. It checks exactly two things: the page exists at docs/errors/<subsystem>/<code>.qmd, and docs_url equals https://quarto.org/docs/errors/<subsystem>/<code>. Called from lint::run_check, so it fires in "cargo xtask lint", in step 1 of "cargo xtask verify", and in CI — which is what the strand was actually asking for (catch the agent who adds a code and skips the page, before the PR opens). First repo-level rule in that module; the other three grep one Rust file each, so run_check grew a whole-tree seam. Violations anchor at the catalog entry's line.

2. Backfilled all 28 missing pages with real prose at status: stub — extension Q-16-1..9 (new directory; the subsystem was entirely undocumented), project Q-5-8..12 + Q-5-17..22, lua Q-11-2..5, writer Q-3-42/43, theme Q-14-3, markdown Q-2-42. No allowlist, no warn-first mode: the gate went on only after the tree it guards was clean.

3. Fixed Q-3-42/Q-3-43's docs_url, which omitted the <subsystem> segment. A file-existence-only check would have passed those two while the link stayed a 404 — that is why docs_url conformance is in the rule.

TDD: six synthetic-fixture tests plus the_real_catalog_and_docs_tree_agree, which failed against main with all 28 missing pages + 2 URL drifts before the backfill.

End-to-end verified through the real binary, not just tests. Injected a fake Q-2-99 with no page: "cargo xtask lint" exits 1 and names the file to create, anchored at line 464 (Q-2-99's own catalog line). Deleting an existing page gives the same shape. "cargo run --bin q2 -- render docs/" gives exit 0, 225/225 files, 25 warnings — identical to a stashed baseline render of unmodified main (11 Q-13-4 in brand.qmd + 14 Q-5-6 in figures.qmd, all pre-existing). The 28 new pages contribute zero warnings; all 193 codes resolve in the listing.

"cargo xtask verify" (full, including the hub/WASM leg) passes: 11491 tests, exit 0. No snapshot files added, modified, or removed anywhere in the workspace.

Two authoring traps worth knowing before the next error page is written, both real bugs in my first draft: (a) bare shortcodes are executed even inside fenced code blocks — the first render fired 15 genuine Q-16-3/Q-16-5 diagnostics from the pages documenting those very codes; the repo convention is the triple-brace form, though sibling pages Q-2-27/Q-2-28 instead use a {.markdown shortcodes="false"} fence attribute, and standardizing on one would be worth doing. (b) A trailing possessive apostrophe ("the scripts" + apostrophe) parses as an opening single quote, failed Q-5-12 with Q-2-7, and took the page out of the render entirely.

Docs: CLAUDE.md gains the rule under Current Lint Rules; docs/errors/README.md gains an Enforcement section, drops the "once the audit tool ships" framing, and has two dead links repointed (crates/quarto-error-reporting/ no longer exists post-externalization).

bd-8otua stays open and unblocked — it still owns orphan/misplaced/front-matter-drift checks, health rollups, and the "new <Q-X-Y>" generator the README still describes as unshipped. When it lands it should absorb lint/error_docs.rs rather than duplicate it. Filed bd-8meeijgq (discovered-from this strand): figures.qmd references 14 images that do not exist; pre-existing, found while establishing the render baseline.

Leaving this strand open until the work is reviewed and merged.

title: Phase C.2 follow-up: in-process Rust integration test for watcher → staleness path
description:
Drafted in tests/staleness.rs during C.2 (bd-kw93.4) but dropped from the merge because the test is flaky under `cargo nextest run` on macOS. Symptoms:

- Passes standalone (`cargo nextest run --test staleness`) in <1 second.
- Passes under `cargo test -p quarto-preview --tests` (single-process multi-test).
- Passes under `cargo nextest run --no-capture` (all 17 tests).
- Fails (30 s timeout) under `cargo nextest run` (default capture, all tests) — staleness flag never flips even though the file watcher demonstrably works (binary smoke confirms).

Suspected interaction between notify-rs's FSEvents backend and nextest's stdout capture across multiple test processes. The watcher arms, the file edit happens, but the change event never reaches `run_file_watcher` in this configuration.

What's covered without this test:
- 5 unit tests for `recompute_staleness` in capture_driver::tests.
- 4 unit tests for `compute_input_qmd` in preview_record::tests.
- Binary smoke confirming the watcher → sync_file → on_file_changed path on macOS.

What this test would add: end-to-end coverage of the full file-watcher + on_file_changed + recompute_staleness + sidecar-update loop in a single Rust integration test.

Path forward: file again once the Playwright e2e harness lands (Phase D / E) — Playwright drives the binary directly and doesn't have the nextest capture-pipe in the loop. Alternatively, dig into notify-rs's macOS quirks and find a workaround.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-13-q2-preview-phase-c.md §C.2 (acceptance gap).
close_reason: In-process staleness integration test landed in crates/quarto-preview/tests/staleness.rs. Original flake reproduced + traced: parallel nextest processes each arming an FSEvents watcher under default I/O capture causes silent event loss on macOS. Worked around with .config/nextest.toml — puts the three watcher-using integration test binaries (staleness, eager_capture, boot) in a max-threads=1 test group. 5/5 stable reruns; workspace nextest 8952/8952. Merged to feature/q2-preview-command as commit cc180477.

c-q1o2dg2n.author: shikokuchuo

title: qmd writer drops empty bullet-list items / mutates empty list-table cells (issue #195)
description:
Two round-trip bugs in crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs, both reported in https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/195 by @rundel.

(1) write_bulletlist (L461) drops truly-empty items (Vec<Block> of length 0): the is_empty_item check at L480 requires item.len() == 1, so length-0 items fall through to the else branch and write nothing. No bare marker is ever emitted. Round-trip: `[..., []]` becomes `[...]`.

(2) write_list_table (L986) writes literal '- []' for cells whose content is empty (L1129-1133). The reader parses that '[]' as inline text inside a Plain block, mutating the AST from cell content `[]` to `[Plain []]`.

Fix shape (per reporter): emit a bare marker line (e.g. '*\n' or '-\n') for truly-empty items / cells. The reader already accepts bare markers — input '- - X\n  -\n' parses the trailing item as the empty Vec.

In scope:
- write_bulletlist empty-item branch
- write_list_table empty-cell branch
- write_orderedlist (no is_empty_item check at all — same root cause; bundle the fix)
- Round-trip fixtures under crates/pampa/tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/ for both AST shapes

Triage record: claude-notes/issue-reports/195/triage.md on branch issue-195. Existing fixture empty_list_item.qmd (covers [Plain []], not []) should keep round-tripping unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed in commit bea39f57 on branch issue-195. write_bulletlist + write_orderedlist now emit bare marker for length-0 items; write_list_table drops literal '[]' for empty cells without attrs. Six new round-trip fixtures under crates/pampa/tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/. cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build --skip-hub-tests passes; end-to-end against reporter's exact repros confirms AST round-trips and writer is idempotent. PR pending.

Single-doc behavior byte-identical (regression-tested). See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-24-websites-phase-5.md.

title: Add quarto-scss-analysis-annotation markers to brand SCSS output

Q2's brand_layer.rs omits them — we have no analyzer that consumes them. Add when an analyzer materializes. Plan ref: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-brand-yml-support.md.

title: hub-client e2e fails: @quarto/quarto-sync-client/dist/index.js not resolvable
description:
Running cargo xtask verify --e2e (or npm run test:all from hub-client) breaks Playwright with: 'Cannot find module .../node_modules/@quarto/quarto-sync-client/dist/index.js imported from hub-client/e2e/helpers/projectFactory.ts'.

quarto-sync-client's package.json declares main: dist/index.js, but dist/ is not built as part of npm install — only the source/import/types entries (pointing at src/) get used by Vitest. Playwright runs the helper in a plain Node process that uses the default resolver, which falls back to main.

Reproduces on:
- this branch (feature/q2-preview-command @ 63e27e8c)
- main @ d0d5d39e (i.e. pre-existing, not introduced by the q2-preview work)

Likely fix shapes:
1. Add a workspace-wide pre-step that builds quarto-sync-client's dist/ (mirror of how WASM is built via 'npm run build:wasm').
2. Switch hub-client's e2e helpers to import via a path that hits the source condition (loader / tsx / different resolver).
3. Set 'imports' / 'exports' on quarto-sync-client so the default Node resolver finds .ts via source.

Discovered while wiring q2-preview-spa's own Playwright suite into 'cargo xtask verify --e2e' (bd-vpsy / Phase A.7); the q2-preview-spa suite is unaffected because it doesn't import quarto-sync-client at all.

title: xtask stage-doc-examples runs in the main checkout when invoked from a worktree
description: cargo xtask stage-doc-examples resolves its root via create_worktree::repo_root(), which uses 'git rev-parse --git-common-dir' — deliberately the MAIN checkout for worktree management, but wrong for staging: invoked from .worktrees/<x>/, it renders the example projects with the main checkout's q2 (cargo run cwd = main root) and stages docs/examples/ there, not in the worktree. The worktree's 'q2 render docs/' then still fails with 'Declared resource docs/examples does not exist'. Observed 2026-08-17 in the bd-llms-link-target-annotation worktree. Fix direction: stage-doc-examples (and any other xtask that means 'this working tree') should resolve the current worktree root ('git rev-parse --show-toplevel'), keeping repo_root() for the worktree-management commands that really mean the main checkout.
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-32c8egkf (same xtask worktree/repo-root bug); detail folded into that strand

title: workspace-ts-suites: first red step still hides every later suite
description:
The workspace-ts-suites job in .github/workflows/ts-test-suite.yml runs ~12 suite tiers as sequential steps with no step-level continue-on-error (fail-fast:false is on the OS matrix only). A failing step skips all later steps, so every red run only ever names the FIRST flake in step order and the suites behind it produce no evidence. When wasm-js-bridge went red, the 5 suites after it never ran, and 'unproven' was read as 'clean'.

A working prototype was built and verified to parse during bd-yw3mcdkg: give each suite step an id plus continue-on-error:true, split the two steps that chain two tiers with && (q2-preview-spa, kanban) so the unit tier stops hiding the integration tier, and add a final gate step that reads each step's outcome, writes a per-suite table to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and exits 1 if any failed. The gate must be bash-3.2 safe (no associative arrays) because macOS runners ship bash 3.2. It was reverted before commit as out of scope for that strand.

Note this changes nothing about merge gating either way: main has no required status checks, so these jobs are advisory already.

title: Jupyter inline expression evaluation ({python} expr) missing from the production text path
description: Q1 supports inline executable expressions in jupyter documents. q2's production jupyter path (text_execute.rs) has never supported them; the only implementation was a prototype in the retired AST-path JupyterTransform (deleted in bd-gthycd33 because the parallel emitter was a shape-divergence source with no production consumer — see claude-notes/plans/2026-07-01-bd-gthycd33-jupyter-cell-wrapper.md, decision 4). knitr handles inline r expressions natively. When implementing, add the emission to text_execute.rs (single emission path) and extend the cross-engine parity suite (engine_output_parity.rs) with an inline-expression case so knitr and jupyter inline output shapes stay congruent. The deleted prototype (git history: crates/quarto-core/src/engine/jupyter/transform.rs, extract_inline_expressions / parse_inline_expression) is a useful reference.

title: L8 follow-up: broader path resolution for YAML-declared paths
description: L8 D2 deferred. The planned !path YAML tag + Q2 metadata-merging design should unify path resolution across _quarto.yml, per-page frontmatter, and listing templates. Listing template paths would resolve relative to the YAML they were defined in. L8 ships host-page-only resolution; this issue records the linkage so when the broader design lands, listing template paths fold in cleanly. See claude-notes/plans/2026-05-07-listings-L8-custom-templates.md §Decisions log D2.

title: L9 follow-up: title placeholder substitution from rendered HTML
description: Q1 substitutes the rendered post title (post-engine) into RSS items, because engine output may contain math etc. that the metadata title doesn't. v1 uses item.title from the profile directly. Subscribers see the metadata title; if a feed item has math in its title, it'll show up as source markup, not the rendered form. File if a user reports this.

title: Nested {{< include >}} retargets relative paths to the including file (should be no-retargeting, relative to original)
description:
VERIFIED E2E 2026-06-16. q2's include expansion resolves a NESTED include's relative path against the including file's directory, not the original (top-level) document. This violates the documented Quarto 1/2 'no path retargeting' design for include shortcodes (https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/includes.html — Carlos authored that feature).

Repro: main.qmd (root) {{< include sub/part.qmd >}}; sub/part.qmd {{< include other.qmd >}}; other.qmd at BOTH root and sub/. q2 render main.qmd includes sub/other.qmd (SUB-OTHER) — i.e. retargeted to sub/. Expected per design: root other.qmd.

Note the ASYMMETRY: image/resource paths ARE correctly un-retargeted (ResourceCollectorTransform resolves over the expanded AST relative to the ORIGINAL deck dir; expand_includes_in_blocks never rewrites URL strings). Only nested INCLUDE paths are wrongly retargeted.

Root cause: crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/include_expansion.rs:248 recurses with current_file = &resolved (the just-included file), so the nested level's base_dir = include_expansion.rs:90 becomes the including file's parent. Fix: thread the ORIGINAL top-level document dir as the include-resolution anchor through the recursion instead of the including file's dir.

Separate-but-related: base_dir.join("/foo.qmd") yields filesystem root /foo.qmd, so recommended project-root-relative leading-slash include notation may not resolve to project root through this path — verify and handle.

Reference: claude-notes/research/2026-06-16-include-shortcode-path-resolution.md. Single-level includes from the deck root are unaffected; only nested includes whose including file is in a subdir with a relative arg. Preview parity work (bd-9cyza5vy) should reuse the real IncludeExpansionStage so it inherits whatever this fix lands on.

c-jlcoavtw.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-jlcoavtw.text: Confirmed against Quarto 1 source: external-sources/quarto-cli/src/core/handlers/include-standalone.ts (standaloneInclude). Every include resolves via the SAME fixed handlerContext.resolvePath(filename); the nested retrieveInclude(params[0]) reuses the same handlerContext, anchored at the original document target.source. So Q1 anchors ALL include paths (top-level + nested) at the original file = no retargeting. Q1 also splices raw TEXT (mappedConcat) and parses the concatenation ONCE, so resource paths are un-retargeted by construction. q2 AST-level splicing (expand_includes_in_blocks, parses each include separately) is where the nested-include asymmetry was introduced. Fix: anchor q2 recursion at the original top-level document dir to match Q1.

title: Smart typography mangles machine-facing metadata strings before engine threading
description: Frontmatter strings in DocumentMetadata context are parsed as markdown (pampa parse_yaml_string_as_markdown_to_config, crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs), and apply_smart_typography (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:566, always-on per the 2026-06-15 em-en-dash plan) converts '--' to an en dash inside every Str. When P1.1b metadata threading lowers the merged meta back to plain text for TS engines (config_value_to_ts_metadata -> as_plain_text, crates/quarto-core/src/project/mod.rs:447), the mangled text is what the engine receives. Observed concretely in Plan 4 Phase 4E/J3: 'julia: exeflags: ["--threads=2"]' reached QuartoNotebookRunner as '–threads=2' (en dash), which QNR treated as a FILE path for the julia worker: 'SystemError: opening file .../–threads=2'. Q1 does not have this problem because it partitions frontmatter with a plain YAML parser, never through pandoc-style markdown parsing. Workarounds: '!str' tag, or values without smart-typography trigger sequences (J3 uses '-t2'). Real fix is architectural: preserve the raw YAML scalar for machine-facing consumers (raw slot on ConfigValue, per-context reader options, or SourceInfo-based recovery at the engine lowering). Affects ALL TsFormatInfo.metadata strings ('...' -> ellipsis, quotes -> curly, '--'/'---' -> dashes), not just julia exeflags.

title: quarto-yaml: Location.column is a byte count where the ecosystem treats it as chars (latent)
description:
UPSTREAM: posit-dev/quarto-yaml. Found while discharging Plan 1's offset->location
hand-off (q2 Plan 3 Phase 2, claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-3-audit-and-fix.md).
Examined at quarto-yaml 0.1.3, the version q2's Cargo.lock pins; the registry source is
byte-identical to ~/src/quarto-yaml at HEAD (4734b46 "Release 0.1.3", tag never pushed).

READ THE PRIORITY BEFORE SCHEDULING THIS: it is currently UNOBSERVABLE. It is filed as a
latent API inconsistency, not a live bug. Nothing in q2 or anywhere else misbehaves today.

THE INCONSISTENCY
parse_impl (src/parser.rs:133-142) builds the whole-file hull Location:

    end: Location {
        offset: content.len(),
        row: content.lines().count().saturating_sub(1),
        column: content.lines().last().map_or(0, |l| l.len()),
    }

`l.len()` is a BYTE count. Location.column is a CHARACTER count everywhere else in the
ecosystem -- both quarto-source-map implementations
(utils::offset_to_location and FileInformation::offset_to_location, which q2's Plan 1
measured disagreeing by one column and then made agree) count chars. A last line
containing any multi-byte character therefore yields a column larger than every other
producer would give for the same position.

Secondary, same expression: `content.lines().count().saturating_sub(1)` drops the empty
final line a trailing newline creates ("a\n".lines().count() == 1), so `row` is one short
whenever content ends in a newline -- while `offset` is content.len(), which IS on that
final line. row and offset disagree about which line the end is on.

WHY IT IS DEAD TODAY, AND WHAT WOULD MAKE IT LIVE
The value is discarded one call later. SourceInfo::from_range
(quarto-source-map-0.1.3/src/source_info.rs:185-191) keeps ONLY range.start.offset and
range.end.offset:

    pub fn from_range(file_id: FileId, range: Range) -> Self {
        SourceInfo::Original { file_id, start_offset: range.start.offset,
                               end_offset: range.end.offset }
    }

row and column never survive the call. So this is dead by virtue of who consumes it, not
by anything quarto-yaml does -- an accident of the current downstream, not a property of
this crate.

It becomes live the moment ANY consumer reads Location.column (or .row) off a Location
that quarto-yaml produced, rather than going through from_range. That includes a future
from_range that preserves row/column, a diagnostic renderer taking the Location directly,
or any new quarto-yaml API returning a Location to a caller.

SCOPE NOTE
quarto-yaml 0.1.3 has NO offset->location implementation at all -- it goes marker -> byte
offset via byte_offset_of_char (src/parser.rs:270), which advances only across UTF-8 lead
bytes and so cannot return a mid-character offset. That was the thing the q2 audit went
looking for and it is genuinely absent; this is the only Location-shaped hazard found.
parse_impl (:133-142) is the crate's ONLY production Location construction -- every other
one is under #[cfg(test)] (the test module starts at src/parser.rs:1242).

SUGGESTED FIX
Count chars, not bytes, and make row agree with offset:
  column: content.lines().last().map_or(0, |l| l.chars().count())
and derive row from the actual newline count rather than lines().count()-1, so a trailing
newline puts the end on the empty final line where its offset already points.

title: pampa: wire Meta and Pandoc filter callbacks in typewise dispatch
description:
Discovered while testing bd-o8pr Phase 3 (Lua filter resource channel).

pampa::lua::filter::filter_names lists 'Pandoc', 'Doc', 'Meta', 'Block', 'Blocks', 'Inline', 'Inlines' as recognized filter handler names — they get copied from globals into the filter table. But the typewise traversal in apply_typewise_filter does not actually invoke them.

This means a Lua filter that does:
  function Meta(meta) ... end
or:
  function Pandoc(doc) ... end

is silently ignored. Para/Str/Header/etc. all work.

This blocks:
- Lua-filter tests for the bd-o8pr 'additivity defense' (filter mutates meta.resources): the unit test in resource_report.rs covers the logic, but an E2E test through q2 render needs Meta callback support.
- General pandoc filter compatibility: many real filters do all their work in Pandoc(doc) or Meta(meta).

References:
- crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs:308 (filter_names list)
- crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs:1730 (apply_typewise_filter)
- crates/quarto-core/tests/project_resources.rs (filter_removing_meta_resources_does_not_drop_author_declaration test note)

title: hub-client: display executed code output in the default format: html preview (only q2-preview shows it today)
description:
hub-client does not display executed code output for `format: html` documents (the default). It works only when the doc declares `format: q2-preview` (or q2-slides/q2-debug/revealjs). Discovered while verifying the remote-execution feature end-to-end (bd-sfet3264): the provider ran the engine and wrote the capture, hub-client showed the "Executor online" + "Showing executed output" bars, but the preview kept showing SOURCE (cat(1,2,3)) instead of the executed output (1 2 3). Switching the doc to `format: q2-preview` made the output appear.

ROOT CAUSE (two layers):
1. Component routing (hub-client/src/components/render/PreviewRouter.tsx:157): `{reactFormat ? <ReactPreview captures=.../> : <Preview .../>}`. getQ2Format (getQ2Format.ts) returns non-null ONLY for formats starting with `q2-` or `revealjs`. A normal/html doc -> reactFormat=null -> `<Preview>`, and PreviewRouter destructures `captures` OUT of the props passed to `<Preview>` (line 148). So the Phase-1 capture-consumption wiring (App->Editor->PreviewRouter->ReactPreview) never reaches the default renderer. The Run button (RunControl) and the "Showing executed output" bar (ClearCaptureControl in Editor.tsx) both work regardless, which makes it LOOK like it should be splicing.
2. WASM HTML branch ignores captures (crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1351 render_single_doc_to_response, comment at ~1360-1362): "The HTML branch ignores it (HTML renders don't consume captures in the WASM today - q2 render natively runs engines instead)". The pipeline_kind == "preview" branch folds captures through CaptureSpliceStage; the HTML branch (render_page_in_project -> RenderToHtmlRenderer) does not. render_page_in_project's TS wrapper + renderToHtml don't thread captureGzJson either (Preview.tsx uses renderToHtml with no captures).

WHY q2 preview never hit this: q2 preview only ever renders in the q2-preview (AST-splice) format, so its capture-consumption path is always the ReactPreview/preview branch. hub-client additionally supports plain `format: html` (and website html pages), which q2 preview does not — that's the untested mode.

SCOPE OF FIX (thread captures through the html/renderToHtml path):
- WASM: make the HTML branch of render_single_doc_to_response / render_project_active_page_to_response fold captures through the splice (CaptureSpliceStage) before/within the HTML render, OR route html-preview through the AST-splice + HTML serialization. Needs a WASM rebuild.
- preview-runtime: renderToHtml/RenderToHtmlOptions + renderPageInProject wrapper thread captureGzJson (the WASM render_page_in_project binding already accepts capture_gz_json — lib.rs ~1130 — but see the html-branch-ignores-it caveat above; verify it actually splices for HTML output).
- hub-client: PreviewRouter passes `captures` to `<Preview>`; Preview.tsx fetches the active capture bytes via getBinaryDocById (mirror ReactPreview.tsx:582-605) and passes captureGzJson into renderToHtml options.
- Add a hub-client test that exercises the DEFAULT (html) preview path with a capture (the Phase 1 tests only covered ReactPreview / q2-preview — that gap is why this shipped).

WORKAROUND for users today: put `format: q2-preview` in the doc's front matter.
close_reason: Landed: 449f93bc..deee0edb on main (format:html capture display, all 5 phases). Audit bd-a0eyjshu.

c-irx45ckk.text:
COMPLETE — all 5 phases implemented, TDD, and verified end-to-end. 7 commits on feature/hub-execution-provider (449f93bc..deee0edb), NOT pushed (awaiting approval). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-01-html-format-capture-display.md.

Layered fix (each phase RED->GREEN):
- P1 quarto-core: HtmlRenderConfig gains captures + shared insert_capture_splice_stage helper (deduped from build_q2_preview_pipeline_stages) + build_html_pipeline_stages_with_captures; render_qmd_to_html uses it when captures present (empty = byte-identical). RenderToHtmlRenderer::with_captures for the website active-page path. Native tests: render_qmd_to_html_splices_captures + integration render_to_html_captures.rs.
- P2 wasm: both HTML branches (render_single_doc_to_response, render_project_active_page_to_response) now thread the already-parsed captures. No new wasm-bindgen signature. WASM vitest captureSpliceHtml.wasm.test.ts.
- P3 preview-runtime: renderToHtml/RenderToHtmlOptions + renderPageInProject forward captureGzJson to the already-capable renderPageInProjectWithAttribution.
- P4 hub-client: shared useActiveCaptureBytes hook (ReactPreview refactored to it); Preview consumes it + threads captureGzJson into renderToHtml; PreviewRouter passes captures to <Preview> (previously dropped). Tests: useActiveCaptureBytes.integration + Preview.capture.integration.

Verification: full cargo xtask verify green (Rust + WASM rebuild + hub-client). Browser e2e (Chrome DevTools): a project with engine:knitr + an {r} cell and NO format: key (default format:html) on sync.automerge.org + a connected q2 provide-hub --allow-all -> click Run -> preview shows cat(1,2,3) then "1 2 3" in a real .cell-output. Exactly the case that previously rendered source-only; the format:q2-preview workaround is no longer needed.

Non-blocking follow-ups (NOT part of this bug; same to_str() pattern as bd-bm0vaetl): the index `identities` map and resource.rs mimeType/hash (for hub-client-uploaded binaries) would also drop JS-authored Text values if a Rust peer reads them. File as separate strands if they surface.

c-zl1lxuk8.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-zl1lxuk8.text: Plan written: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-01-html-format-capture-display.md. Layered fix confirmed by a full code-path map. Key finding: capture bytes already reach Rust (render_page_in_project_with_attribution parses them, lib.rs:1148) but both HTML branches drop them; CaptureSpliceStage is a plain DocumentAst->DocumentAst stage insertable into the HTML pipeline exactly as build_q2_preview_pipeline_stages does it (before EngineExecutionStage). Cell alignment is guaranteed (captures are recorded from the HTML stage list truncated at engine-execution) and there's no phase-ordering contract to satisfy. Phases: (1) Rust captures-aware HTML pipeline + RenderToHtmlRenderer::with_captures, (2) WASM HTML branches use the already-parsed captures, (3) preview-runtime renderToHtml threads captureGzJson, (4) hub-client PreviewRouter->Preview fetch+pass, (5) verify + browser e2e. Awaiting user review before implementing.

title: quarto-hub-mcp tests leak developer auth env into spawned server
description: McpTestClient.start() spawns the server inheriting the full shell env. When a developer has QUARTO_HUB_MCP_CLIENT_ID/SECRET set (real auth config), the spawned test server enables the OS-keychain credential path; with a populated keychain the write fails ('item already exists in the keychain'), making require-online/hub-mcp/exit-drain tests fail locally (21 failures). CI passes because its env is clean. Fix: spawn a hermetic child env (strip the two auth-gating vars) unless a test passes an explicit env; e2e-auth already passes its own isolated env so it is unaffected.

title: qmd writer drops trailing newline inside code blocks (issue #173)
description:
The qmd writer in crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:628-634 emits the closing fence directly after the content text when the text already ends with '\n', collapsing one content-line boundary. As a result, a CodeBlock whose AST text ends in '\n' round-trips with the trailing newline removed.

Triage doc: claude-notes/issue-reports/173/triage.md (on branch issue-173).
Repro: claude-notes/issue-reports/173/repro.sh.

The pampa reader matches Pandoc exactly on this — verified across seven cases including CommonMark spec example 100. So the AST contract is correct; only the writer is wrong. Fix scope is in the triage doc.

Reporter: @rundel. GH issue: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/173.

title: Unify 'is this an external URL' predicates: adjust_paths_recursive still uses a narrow http(s)-only check
description:
bd-97yc added quarto_util::is_external_url (scheme >= 2 chars, so Windows drive letters are not misread as URLs; also covers data:, mailto:, protocol-relative //). quarto-brand's private narrow copy was replaced by it.

Still divergent: crates/quarto-core/src/project/mod.rs::adjust_paths_recursive, the ConfigValueKind::Path rebaser, inlines its own check:

    !path_str.starts_with("http://") && !path_str.starts_with("https://")

That misses data: URIs and protocol-relative URLs, so a '!path' value holding one gets mangled by pathdiff into e.g. '../data:image/png;base64,...'.

Switching it to quarto_util::is_external_url would deduplicate and fix that, but it broadens 'do not rebase' for extension templates/filters/css paths, which is a behavior change unrelated to the favicon work -- deliberately not bundled into bd-97yc. Should be a small, separately-verified change.

Note the predicate is intentionally NOT Q1's /^\\w+:/ (external-sources/quarto-cli/src/core/url.ts:13), which matches a Windows drive letter.

title: Listing contents globs: resolve relative to declaring file's directory (GH #456)
description: GH https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/456 — listing 'contents:' globs are matched against BOTH the host-relative and project-relative path views (matches_any_glob in transforms/listing_generate.rs, mirrored in project/dependency_graph.rs). From a subdirectory host, '*.qmd' also matches project-root documents, producing wrong listing items, broken hrefs (e.g. href="about.qmd" unresolved), silently-wrong links (root index.html resolving to the host's own dir), and spurious Q-13-4 warnings from dep-graph edges. Investigation found 4 related defects across mechanisms (fixtures in scratchpad, to be committed as test fixtures): (1) dual-view OR matching = the reported bug; (2) globs declared in _metadata.yml resolve against the wrong base dir — listing renders empty; (3) '../' parent traversal in contents matches nothing; (4) negation globs like '!index.qmd' are silently ignored (no negation support). Bonus wart: Q-1-20 'failed to parse as markdown' fires on every glob string in contents. Direction per cscheid: resolve globs relative to the directory of the file where the contents entry was declared, using ConfigValue provenance (SourceInfo), not Q1-exact behavior. Plan doc to follow.

title: Rename flush_site_libs to flush_project_artifacts
description: `flush_site_libs` in `crates/quarto-core/src/project/website_post_render.rs` is now called from both `WebsiteProjectType.post_render` (where the name is accurate) and `RenderToHtmlRenderer.render` (where 'site_libs' is misleading — default projects have no site_libs dir). The function body has always been general (it just iterates project_artifacts and calls `resolver.on_disk_path_for(Project, ...)`). Rename + update one error message for clarity. Pure naming hygiene.
close_reason:
Done in PR #430 (commit 478f7c37), branch feature/bd-v8gx-flush-project-artifacts. All 8 CI checks green.

flush_site_libs -> flush_project_artifacts, moved out of project/website_post_render.rs into quarto-core::artifact_flush and reimplemented as a thin wrapper over enqueue_artifacts, so the general name is honest by construction.

Two parts of this strand's original description turned out to be stale:
- The 'one error message' was already gone — bd-cfl67 (ad18adcb) deleted "Failed to create site_libs subdirectory" when OutputSink replaced the manual dir_create+file_write pair.
- The stated motivation (two misleading non-website callers) was dissolved by doing bd-gdhk in the same PR: route_drained_project_artifacts now owns those two call sites, leaving flush_project_artifacts with only post_render, where 'site_libs' had been accurate. The rename is still correct, but for the module-home reason rather than the caller-name reason.

Scope was widened beyond 'pure naming hygiene' with the user's agreement (option c): the move was forced, not cosmetic, because pub mod render_to_file is itself cfg(not(wasm32)) — enqueue_artifacts did not exist on wasm32, which is why the cross-platform flush had to duplicate it instead of calling it.

One deliberate behavior change, documented and tested: the old function forced on_disk_path_for(Project, ..) while enqueue_artifacts filters on artifact.scope, so a stray non-Project entry went from silently misplaced to silently dropped. Since merge_into_project does not re-stamp scope, nothing enforced the invariant; flush_project_artifacts now debug_assert!s it (loud in dev, filtered in release).

Sweep: 31 references across 10 files in 3 crates -> 3 deliberate history notes. Both stale intra-doc links repointed (CI cannot catch those — no cargo doc step, and clippy does not resolve them). Matched the full symbol, never 'site_libs': 142 of 173 occurrences name the real output directory.

Coverage: artifact_flush.rs at 98.48% region / 99.39% line.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-28-rename-flush-site-libs.md

c-kqrbhekp.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-kqrbhekp.text:
Investigated at 581e45c0. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-28-rename-flush-site-libs.md

Verdict: ready to design, with a scope decision. Rename premise holds (function still general, still 3 callers, 2 of them non-website). Three findings:

1. The 'one error message' this strand promises is ALREADY GONE. It was "Failed to create site_libs subdirectory {}: {}", deleted by bd-cfl67 (ad18adcb) when the manual dir_create+file_write pair became OutputSink. Nothing to do for that half.

2. A near-duplicate exists: render_to_file.rs:445 enqueue_artifacts has essentially the same body; difference is sink ownership (flush_site_libs owns+flushes its own sink) and cfg (enqueue_artifacts is native-only, flush_site_libs is cross-platform). Worse, enqueue_artifacts' own doc comment (render_to_file.rs:436-440) claims post_render uses it 'via flush_site_libs' -- that is FALSE; flush_site_libs writes to its own sink directly. Stale doc link worth fixing regardless.

3. Sweep is wider than 3 call sites: 31 occurrences of flush_site_libs across 10 files (3 crates), mostly design comments + intra-doc links + 3 test fn names. CI would NOT catch a stale intra-doc link -- no cargo doc step in workflows, and clippy does not resolve them. Grep is the gate.

Main risk: crates/**/*.rs has 173 occurrences of 'site_libs', only 31 of which are 'flush_site_libs'. 142 (82%) are legitimate references to the real site_libs directory and must be left alone -- a naive sed would corrupt website output paths.

Open with the user: (a) name choice given the enqueue_artifacts collision; (b) pure rename vs. folding in the dedupe (needs lifting a wasm32 cfg gate, eats part of bd-gdhk); (c) whether to move the function out of website_post_render.rs; (d) whether p4 with no dependents is worth doing now or should ride along with bd-gdhk.

Also noted: bd-gdhk's cited line numbers have both drifted (render_to_file.rs:264-297 -> 364-386; pass2_renderer.rs:343-355 -> 883-895/1170-1182).

title: Grammar html_entity_regex() mangles 106 legacy no-semicolon entity names into bogus alternatives
description: html_entity_regex() in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/common/common.js builds regex alternatives with name.substring(1, name.length - 1), which strips the trailing ';' for semicolon-terminated keys but strips the final LETTER for the 106 legacy no-semicolon keys in html_entities.json ('&AMP' -> alternative 'AM', '&AElig' -> 'AEli', ...). Net effect: bogus references like '&AM;' or '&AEli;' parse as entity_reference nodes (and then miss any name lookup on the converter side), while the actual bare legacy forms ('&AMP') don't match — the latter is correct per CommonMark (only semicolon-terminated entities are recognized in markdown), so the fix is to filter the keys to those ending in ';' rather than to support bare forms. Requires 'tree-sitter generate; tree-sitter build' in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown and re-running tree-sitter test. Discovered during investigation of bd-named-entities-w6xbfftj (see claude-notes/plans/named-entity-references-dropped-investigation/investigation-notes.md).
close_reason: Fixed: html_entity_regex() now filters to semicolon-terminated names; parser regenerated; 3 corpus tests pin the CST behavior. Commit on main stacked on PR #489. Full cargo xtask verify green.

title: quarto-highlight forbids syntax injections by design; markdown-with-embedded-R needs them
description: Plan 3 of bd-98m98wg8. Delivers property 4 of the epic's target output, and completes it. Q1's target output highlights the R INSIDE a displayed markdown block as R: cat('foo') That is markdown delegating a fenced block to the R highlighter - a syntax injection. q2 cannot currently do this, and not by omission. crates/quarto-highlight/src/registry.rs:263, builtin_configs_have_no_injection_or_locals, asserts that NO built-in grammar carries an injection or locals query, and its comment says why: 'the captures-only switch is lossless ONLY while every built-in passes empty injection + locals queries: Query.captures() walks just the highlights patterns, and would silently drop any injected highlighting an injection query would request.' It fails loudly by design if one ever does. So this is an architectural change, not a grammar addition. The plan must either move off Query.captures() to a path that honours injections, or handle injection queries explicitly, and then retire or rewrite that test rather than silently weakening it. Blocked on the markdown-grammar strand: there is nothing to inject INTO until markdown highlights at all.

title: samod fork: move to rand 0.10 so consumers can leave rand 0.9
description:
BLOCKS bd-0a3b (quarto-hub rand 0.9 -> 0.10).

Our samod fork (github.com/quarto-dev/samod.git, branch access-policy, version 0.12.1) declares rand ^0.9.1; samod-core 0.12.0 declares rand ^0.9. samod::DocumentId::new takes an 'impl rand::Rng' — a rand 0.9 TYPE in its public API. Any consumer that moves to rand 0.10 therefore fails to compile at every DocumentId::new call site:

  error[E0277]: the trait bound `rand::prelude::ThreadRng: rand::rng::Rng` is not satisfied
    --> crates/quarto-hub/src/access_policy.rs:109:38
    note: required by a bound in `samod::DocumentId::new`

Demonstrated 2026-07-27 by attempting the quarto-hub bump: 8 call sites in crates/quarto-hub/src/access_policy.rs (all inside the #[cfg(test)] module at line 65, but that still breaks cargo clippy --all-targets and therefore cargo xtask verify).

Work: move the samod fork to rand 0.10 (and rand_core 0.10), release a fork version, bump the git pin in crates/quarto-hub/Cargo.toml and crates/quarto-hub-provider/Cargo.toml — note the comment there requiring the two pins to match EXACTLY, else samod and its automerge resolve to a second copy.

Context: upstream samod on crates.io is at 0.12.3, but we consume a fork branch, so an upstream bump is not by itself a path. Worth checking whether 0.12.3 already moved to rand 0.10 before doing the work by hand.

c-1u39np7s.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-1u39np7s.text:
DEFERRED 2026-07-27 by Carlos's call, priority 3 -> 4.

Reason: the 'why bother' question wins. The measured payoff is type coherence at the samod boundary, NOT duplicate reduction (Carlos measured 101 duplicate crates and three rand copies before AND after on bd-0a3b). The cost is a fork rebase + fork release + a cross-repo round trip, and nothing outside bd-0a3b depends on either strand. Right move: ride along the next time we touch the samod fork for a real reason.

CORRECTION to my previous comment: the plan file and investigation artifacts it references (claude-notes/plans/2026-07-27-samod-fork-rand-010.md, .../samod-fork-rand-010-investigation/, commit 60291476) NO LONGER EXIST. main was reset back to dd87a8b5 at Carlos's request, since a plan for deferred work is just drift. - the rand 0.10 Rng->RngExt / RngCore->Rng rename means samod's generic bounds need no text change, only 'use rand::RngExt' where .random() is called

c-gymhmkd1.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-gymhmkd1.text:
INVESTIGATED 2026-07-27 — verdict: ready to design. Plan skeleton at claude-notes/plans/2026-07-27-samod-fork-rand-010.md (commit 60291476 on main), artifacts under claude-notes/plans/samod-fork-rand-010-investigation/. Pre-flight 'cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build' green at dd87a8b5.

ANSWERING THIS STRAND'S OWN OPEN QUESTION: upstream is NOT a path. samod 0.12.1, 0.12.2 and 0.12.3 ALL declare rand ^0.9.1 (crates.io dependency API). Upstream is github.com/alexjg/samod, not automerge/samod; a search of its issues+PRs for 'rand' returns two hits, neither rand-the-crate. Nobody upstream is doing this.

CORRECTION to the description: there are THREE git pins, not two — quarto-hub/Cargo.toml:50, quarto-hub-provider/Cargo.toml:19, and quarto-preview/Cargo.toml:26 (added later, own comment). All three must move in one commit. The must-match-exactly comment names only two. Filed bd-hcipii6t for an xtask lint.

WHY THE FIX WORKS (the interesting part): rand 0.10 renamed Rng -> RngExt because rand_core renamed RngCore -> Rng, and rand's root now re-exports rand_core::Rng as rand::Rng with a blanket 'impl<R: Rng + ?Sized> RngExt for R'. So samod's 'pub fn new<R: rand::Rng>' signatures need NO text change — they silently rebind to the weaker core trait. Bodies calling rng.random() just need RngExt in scope. That is exactly what makes ThreadRng acceptable at DocumentId::new again.

SIZE OF THE JOB, enumerated at fork commit c5a06c3: 16 'R: rand::Rng' bounds in samod-core/src + samod/src (5 public: document_id, storage_id, peer_id, loader, actors/hub), 3 manifest rand declarations, and 3 'from_os_rng()' sites (removed in 0.10 -> rand::make_rng or StdRng::from_rng) at samod/src/lib.rs:1378, :1506, samod-test-harness/src/samod_wrapper.rs:60. StdRng losing Clone does NOT bite (struct Inner doesn't derive it); MSRV 1.85/edition 2024 doesn't bite (samod and q2 are already edition 2024). Fork carries exactly ONE local commit over v0.12.1, and upstream is 4 commits ahead at v0.12.3 — a rebase is cheap.

SIX DESIGN QUESTIONS for Carlos in the plan; the sharpest is #6: is this worth doing now at P3, given Carlos's own measurement that the payoff is type coherence, not duplicate reduction? A defensible answer is defer-and-ride-along next time we touch the fork.

title: Footnotes appendix section omits the visible 'Footnotes' heading that Quarto 1 emits
description:
q2's rendered footnotes appendix has no visible heading. Quarto 1 emits

Footnotes

and q2 emits only the horizontal rule and the ordered list, so the note list appears with no label. ## Observed at HEAD (c28cfd81) `cargo run --bin q2 -- render --to html`:
  1. ... The `
    ` wrapper, the `
    `, the `
      `, the backlinks and the `doc-endnotes` role are all correct — only the heading is missing. ## Nothing in the tree emits it grep -rn '"Footnotes"' crates/ --include='*.rs' returns ZERO hits. This is not a config branch that fails to fire or a heading that gets stripped downstream; the string is simply never produced. Whatever change lands should also decide whether the heading is localizable (Quarto 1 takes it from the language resources, not a literal) — worth checking how the other appendix headings in q2 handle that before hard-coding it. ## Why it was noticed Purely cosmetic, but it is why several Posit Connect doc pages show up in a text diff against the Quarto 1 reference render even when their content is otherwise identical: admin/integrations/tableau, how-to/deploy-single-page-apps, user/publishing-r, user/manifest.
