c-g86ulgvg.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-g86ulgvg.text:
Investigated at de2375f0 on main (pre-flight `cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` green, all 14 steps, exit 0). Plan skeleton + committed repro: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-footnotes-appendix-heading.md (commit 376f78eb). No worktree/branch created — work landed on main. Verdict: ready to design, pending 4 questions in the plan.

Reproduced exactly as filed. Dependency graph is one outgoing discovered-from edge to bd-adjacent-footnote-definitions-miif1k1z and nothing else; that strand's fix touches scanner.c only, this one touches quarto-core transforms — no conflict, no ordering constraint.

FOUR THINGS THE INVESTIGATION ADDS:

1. THE FIX SITE IS ONE LINE, AND THE BUG IS AN ASYMMETRY. appendix.rs:152-156 pushes the extracted footnotes Div verbatim; the branch immediately above it calls wrap_bibliography(). The footnotes branch is simply missing its wrap_footnotes(). Q1 agrees the appendix transform is the right home, not FootnotesTransform: insertFootnotesTitle is called only from inside processDocumentAppendix (format-html-appendix.ts:167), so with appendix-style: none or book: true Q1 emits no heading either. The reveal path (format-reveal.ts:776) does not transfer — q2 coalesces footnotes into per-slide asides and deletes the trailing Div#footnotes entirely.

2. THE STRAND'S <hr /> CLAIM IS FALSE, and this is the most important correction. The description says the <hr /> is correct and only the heading is missing. Q1's prependHeading (format-html-shared.ts:388-410) inserts the heading AND THEN REMOVES THE RULE — the heading replaces the <hr> as the separator. A heading-only fix leaves q2 emitting both, which still differs from the Q1 reference render, so the Connect-docs text diff this strand exists to close would NOT close. Q1 in the plan asks whether to drop the rule; recommendation is yes.

3. THE LOCALIZATION QUESTION HAS A DEFINITE AND BAD ANSWER. The strand asks how q2's other appendix headings handle localization. They don't — all four are hardcoded English literals: 'References' (appendix.rs:247), 'Reuse' (:310), 'Copyright' (:364), 'Citation' (:411) — despite section-title-references/reuse/copyright/citation all existing in resources/language/_language.yml:18-24 and being fully translated across every _language-*.yml. section-title-footnotes: "Footnotes" is already there too. Infrastructure is complete and needs no new plumbing: LanguageResolveStage injects at meta.quarto.language and LanguageTerms::from_meta(&ast.meta) is the accessor; AppendixStructureTransform already holds &ast.meta. toc_generate.rs:122-135 is the idiomatic precedent (user metadata > localized term > English literal, the tail mattering because from_meta returns None in stage-less unit tests). So: do NOT follow the existing appendix headings — they are all the same bug. Q2 asks whether to fix all five in one commit; recommendation is yes.

4. q2 SHIPS THE APPENDIX-HEADING CSS BUT NEVER EMITS THE CLASS. resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss:2235 and :2276 define .quarto-appendix-heading, copied from Q1, and grep -rn 'quarto-appendix-heading' crates/ returns zero hits — the rules are dead and all five appendix headings are unstyled. Q1 applies ["anchored", "quarto-appendix-heading"]. q2 also never emits "anchored" anywhere; the anchor-link mechanism does not exist in q2, so that one should not be added blind. Q3 asks; recommendation is to add quarto-appendix-heading and skip anchored.

MAIN RISK is snapshot churn, scaling with the answers to Q2 and Q3 — Q3 in particular activates dead CSS and is a visual change, not just markup. Final gate should be full cargo xtask verify since quarto-core is in hub-client's dependency closure.

c-he0ao84e.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-he0ao84e.text:
IMPLEMENTED on main, commit 60d42f0e (investigation 376f78eb, design settlement 1ff7d497). NOT pushed — awaiting review. WHAT LANDED. crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/appendix.rs only, plus 3 smoke-all fixtures. Four new helpers: appendix_title (localized lookup), title_inlines (canonical Str/Space split), appendix_heading (the shared level-2 constructor), wrap_footnotes (the missing sibling of wrap_bibliography). The four existing create_*/wrap_* functions now all build their heading through appendix_heading. THE SUBTLE PARTS, in review order: 1. THE
STRIP LIVES IN THE APPENDIX TRANSFORM, NOT IN create_footnotes_section. It must only fire when something actually titles the section. Moving it into the footnotes transform would delete the rule unconditionally and leave appendix-style: none / book: true with no separator at all. Both directions have a test; both passed before AND after the change, which is the point — they are the must-not-change cases. 2. THE PEEK-EQUIVALENT HERE IS THE EMPTY-TERM GUARD. appendix_title filters an empty resolved term before falling back. A language term explicitly set to null round-trips through LanguageTerms::from_meta as Some(""), which would have produced a heading with no text — strictly worse than the English fallback. 3. CANONICAL INLINES. Titles split into Str/Space rather than one Str carrying spaces. This is invisible in English — every appendix title is a single word — and only shows up localized ('Derechos de autor'). My first test helper flattened Space to "" and caught the difference as 'Derechosdeautor', which is a decent illustration that the split is real and not cosmetic. 4. NOT USING pampa's split_string_to_inlines. It exists (crates/pampa/src/lua/types.rs:1957) but is Lua-module-scoped and hardcodes SourceInfo::generated(By::unknown()); the local helper carries By::appendix() provenance. TESTS. 7 new unit tests in appendix.rs + 3 smoke-all fixtures (appendix/footnotes-heading.qmd, appendix/footnotes-heading-style-none.qmd, localization/lang-es-appendix-headings.qmd). All confirmed failing FIRST, and failing in the right places: 6 unit failures + 7 regex mismatches, with the two must-not-change cases passing throughout. SNAPSHOTS: ZERO changed. I checked whether that was real coverage or a blind spot — it is real: no .snap file in the tree contains appendix HTML at all (grep for quarto-appendix / doc-endnotes / quarto-bibliography returns nothing; the appendix is covered by smoke-all + unit tests instead). The plan had predicted churn and was wrong. RESULTS. Full cargo xtask verify (NOT --skip-hub-build): all 14 steps, 11801 passed / 197 skipped, exit 0. END-TO-END, three ways: - cargo run --bin q2 -- render →

Footnotes

, no
. Byte-identical to Q1. - Computed styles read back from a real browser page: font-weight 600, font-size 17px (=1em), margins 0, border-bottom none, opacity .9 — every rule in the previously-dead SCSS block now applies. #footnotes hr → 0. - The user/manifest Connect-docs page re-rendered and compared against docs-quarto-1/_site: was 0 occurrences of quarto-appendix-heading, now matches the Q1 reference exactly. That is the diff this strand existed to close, and it is the check that would have failed had we shipped the heading without dropping the rule. CORRECTION to the plan's Finding 4: I had written that 'font-size: 1em !important' sits under #quarto-appendix.plain. It does not — both blocks in _bootstrap-rules.scss are nested under .default (lines 2225/2229). The compiled stylesheet and the 17px computed size confirm it. Plan updated. INCIDENTAL, FILED SEPARATELY: bd-7ilvb5r2 — the first full verify failed at step 4 on a tree-sitter corpus case this change never touched. Chased down: reproduces on pristine main with the tree stashed, tree-sitter generate yields no diff (so parser.c is in sync with grammar.js), and it passes 3/3 after a forced rebuild. The culprit is the stale gitignored markdown.dylib. Not a grammar bug, not this change. Also worth knowing: 'cargo xtask verify | tail -N' reports tail's exit code, so a failed verify reads as exit 0 — run it unpiped when the status matters. STILL OPEN: bd-5kf2dnw4 (make 'anchored' live) remains the only follow-up; the class is emitted but inert until then.

c-m5gygvr9.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-m5gygvr9.text:
DESIGN SETTLED with the user; plan updated and committed (1ff7d497). Ready to implement — not started.

ANSWERS:
1. <hr> — YES, drop it from the titled footnotes section, matching Q1's prependHeading. It correctly survives when appendix processing is off.
2. Scope — ALL FIVE headings localized via section-title-*. User's framing: the goal is to get Q2 to emit output like Q1 does, and these would have to be fixed somewhere anyway. No separate strand.
3. Classes — EMIT BOTH 'anchored' and 'quarto-appendix-heading', matching Q1's headingClasses exactly. This reverses my initial recommendation to skip 'anchored'; see the research below.
4. Heading id — none, matching Q1.

Q3 RESEARCH (Finding 5 in the plan), done at the user's request — where .anchored is emitted/used in Q1:
- EMITTED document-wide by format-html.ts:828-848, a DOM postprocessor adding it to every h2-h6 / .quarto-figure[id] / div[id^=tbl-] inside main|body, gated on the 'anchors' option, skipping #toc-title and .no-anchor. The appendix pre-applies it (format-html-appendix.ts:98, :363) only because appendix headings are synthesized by a different postprocessor.
- CONSUMED BY ANCHORJS, NOT CSS. quarto-html-after-body.ejs:38-46 does anchorJS.add('.anchored'), injecting a.anchorjs-link. _quarto-rules.scss:147-175 styles .anchorjs-link — the element AnchorJS creates. There is NO .anchored rule anywhere; it is a pure JS selector hook.
- q2 has none of it: no 'anchors' option, no anchor.min.js, no quarto.js, no .anchorjs-link styling.

So emitting 'anchored' in q2 today is COMPLETELY INERT — nothing styles it, nothing reads it — hence zero visual risk, and it is exactly the marker the future feature needs. This inverts the risk ordering I originally gave: 'anchored' is the safe class; 'quarto-appendix-heading' is the one that moves pixels, because its SCSS (_bootstrap-rules.scss:2235, :2276) is substantive — margin-top 0, line-height 1.4em, font-weight 600, opacity .9, border-bottom none, and font-size 1em !important under .plain. Without it appendix headings render as full-size h2 with Bootstrap's border-bottom.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: bd-5kf2dnw4 (feature, p3, discovered-from this strand) — implement the document-wide pass, the 'anchors' option, the exclusions, and the AnchorJS runtime. Its non-obvious constraint: the pass must be an AST transform (q2 has no DOM postprocessor stage), and unlike Q1's idempotent classList.add, pushing onto Vec<String> is not — the appendix headings are h2 and would be caught twice, yielding 'anchored anchored quarto-appendix-heading'. It must also run in Finalization AFTER AppendixStructureTransform or it will miss the synthesized headings entirely.

ALSO NOTED, NOT FILED: .quarto-appendix-contents > *:not(h2) at _bootstrap-rules.scss:2281 implies Q1's div.quarto-appendix-contents content wrapper, which q2 never emits either. Footnotes are unaffected (the sibling *[role=doc-endnotes] > ol selector covers them), so it only touches the other appendix sections. Worth filing if the Connect-docs diff surfaces it.

PLAN now carries a full work-item checklist: Phase 0 tests (TDD, end-to-end entry point — a default-config test would pass vacuously since the heading only exists on the appendix branch), Phase 1 shared appendix_title/appendix_heading helpers, Phase 2 wrap_footnotes + conditional <hr> strip, Phase 3 retrofit the four existing headings, Phase 4 full verify + browser look + snapshot accounting + Connect-docs diff check.

title: source: file brand fonts: files never copied to _site and @font-face URLs resolve against site_libs/quarto (per-document prefix splits theme CSS)
description:
With `source: file` fonts in _brand.yml, a website render produces @font-face rules whose src URLs do not resolve, and the font files themselves never reach the output directory. Every local brand font 404s. Observed with q2 0.28.0, HEAD 85e98fb02, website project, _brand.yml at the project root.

## Repro

_quarto.yml: `project: {type: website}`, `brand: _brand.yml`, `format.html.theme: [brand, theme.scss]`.

_brand.yml (paths relative to the brand file, as guides/authoring/brand.qmd says):

    typography:
      fonts:
        - family: EB Garamond
          source: file
          files:
            - path: assets/EBGaramond-VariableFont_wght.woff2
              weight: 400
              style: normal
      base: EB Garamond

`q2 render` succeeds silently. Result:

1. `find _site -name '*.woff2'` is empty. Nothing copies the referenced files. The only consumers of `typography.fonts` are the SCSS generator (crates/quarto-sass/src/brand_layer.rs:553, `file_font_face_block`) and `q2 use brand` (crates/quarto/src/commands/use_cmd/source.rs:216, install-time copy only). There is no render-time font-asset walker, unlike logos.

2. The emitted rule is `@font-face{font-family:"EB Garamond";src:url("assets/EBGaramond-VariableFont_wght.woff2");...}` — but for a website the compiled theme is written to `_site/site_libs/quarto/quarto-theme-<fp>.css` (compile_theme_css.rs:828), so the browser resolves the URL against that directory: `_site/site_libs/quarto/assets/...` → 404 (even if the file had been copied to `_site/assets/`).

3. The URL prefix is per *document*, not per site: themes.rs:780 computes `pathdiff(document_dir, brand_dir)` with document_dir = the rendered qmd's parent (compile_theme_css.rs:482). Adding `posts/one.qmd` to the same project yields a second theme CSS: index.html links quarto-theme-008f73acb254ec01.css with `url("assets/…")`, posts/one.html links quarto-theme-ad8c89e199746238.css with `url("../assets/…")`. Both are wrong (both live in site_libs/quarto/), and the site now ships N theme bundles for N directory depths, defeating the shared-artifact design.

Also: the block has no `format("woff2")` hint and no `font-display` (there is no `display:` key for file sources; `format:` on a files entry is silently ignored because BrandFontFileEntry::Explicit is an untagged variant without deny_unknown_fields).

## What works today (workaround)

Site-root-absolute paths plus an explicit resource declaration:

    files:
      - path: /assets/EBGaramond-VariableFont_wght.woff2
    # _quarto.yml
    project:
      resources:
        - assets/*.woff2

`join_url_path` (brand_layer.rs:592) uses PathBuf::push, which drops the prefix for a rooted path, so the leading `/` survives on every page and the fingerprint is stable. Verified: files land in _site/assets/, one theme CSS, `src:url("/assets/…")`. Downside: only correct when the site is served from the domain root.

## Fix shape

- Compute the font URL relative to the theme CSS artifact's location (site_libs/quarto/ for websites, the document dir for single-doc `styles.css`), not the document's location. For websites this makes the prefix site-wide and removes the per-directory fingerprint split.
- Copy `source: file` font paths into the output (mirroring logo handling), or at least register them as implicit project resources.
- Consider emitting `format("woff2")` from the path extension and accepting `display:` (or a top-level `font-display`) for file sources.
- Q1 parity note: Q1 has the same document-relative prefix (external-sources/quarto-cli/src/core/sass/brand.ts:155-175) but its theme CSS sits next to the document, so relative paths worked there; the site_libs relocation in Q2 is what breaks it.

Weight ranges for these variable files are a separate strand (bd-5fseopxy). Found 2026-09-08 while moving cscheid-net-2026 from Google Fonts to local woff2.

title: tree-sitter qmd: multi-line block quote inside list item fails to parse
description:
Minimal repro:
```
- > a
  > b
```

Pandoc parses this as BulletList[[BlockQuote[Para[Str "a", SoftBreak, Str "b"]]]]. Our parser fails with a parse error at line 2 col 6.

Root cause: in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c, the LIST_ITEM match() function has a newline branch (line 537-540) that returns 2, causing match_line case 2 (line 1991-1996) to advance past the trailing \n of a content line. When STATE_MATCHING is left set after a SOFT_LINE_ENDING and the next scan() runs at end-of-line-2, this consumes the \n that the line-ending gate (line 2233) needs, breaking the parse.

BLOCK_QUOTE match() has no newline branch and does not advance, which is why bq-in-bq (`> > a\n> > b\n`) works but bq-in-list-item does not.

Affects all list markers: -, *, +, 1., 1), (1), (#).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-11-bq-multiline-in-list-item.md

Approach (option 2 from the analysis): guard STATE_MATCHING re-entry so that when STATE_WAS_SOFT_LINE_BREAK is set and lookahead is \n/\r/EOF, we skip the match_line pass and let the line-ending gate handle it.

TDD: failing corpus tests first.

title: qmd-syntax-helper rule: rewrite ```{mermaid} to ```mermaid
description:
q2 standardizes on the GFM diagram spelling: ```mermaid renders, ```{mermaid} does not (deliberate — knitr claims mermaid in handledLanguages, so brace-form cells stay engine territory; see the module doc in crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/mermaid.rs).

Every Quarto 1 document in the wild spells it ```{mermaid}, so migration needs a mechanical rewrite rather than q2 growing brace support. A qmd-syntax-helper rule is the natural home: Rule trait in crates/qmd-syntax-helper/src/rule.rs, conversions in src/conversions/.

Scope: strip the braces from the info string and leave the body alone. Cell options need no change — bd-mermaid-cell-options-9wo3crl0 made ```mermaid accept `%%|`, which is exactly what Q1 documents already write.

Motivating corpus (Posit Connect docs): 33 diagrams across 14 pages, all brace-form — the 8 admin/reference-architectures/* pages (aws and azure × single-server / single-server-robust / load-balanced / k8s), user/orientation (4 sequence diagrams), admin/appendix/off-host/arch-overview (4), admin/public-access, admin/appendix/airgapped. On the reference-architecture pages the diagram is the entire content of the page.

Worth checking while there: whether the rule should also flag a leading `#|` run inside a ```mermaid fence. q2 warns about that at render time (Q-2-43, added with the parent strand) but a syntax-helper fix would be more useful than a warning.

Split out of bd-mermaid-cell-options-9wo3crl0 as its own strand (that strand handles the rendering half; this one the migration half).

title: Inline brand: block in document front matter always fails with Q-14-1; brand: path warns Q-1-20 (issue #581)
description: GH #581 (mcanouil). Front matter is converted with InterpretationContext::DocumentMetadata, so every untagged string under brand: is parsed as markdown into ConfigValueKind::PandocInlines. quarto-sass extract_single_brand_ref then (a) inline block form: config_value_to_yaml_value rejects PandocInlines -> Q-14-1 'brand block must be plain YAML' at the first string leaf, so any inline brand in front matter fails; (b) path form brand: _brand.yml: works via as_plain_text fallback but the markdown parse of the leading underscore emits a spurious Q-1-20 warning, and values that parse cleanly as markdown are silently rewritten. Same block in _quarto.yml works (ProjectConfig context keeps Scalar). Fix: protect the brand subtree from markdown at load time via the key-path annotation table (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta_annotations.rs, bd-v7ixzsp5 / GH #457) with Interpretation::PlainString; requires extending the table's pattern language with a subtree ('**') form since matching is exact-length today. Triage doc + repro fixtures + full TDD fix plan: claude-notes/issue-reports/581/triage.md on branch issue-581 (worktree .worktrees/issue-581).

title: hub-client: opening an uncached project fails when the peer is slower than the connect budget
description: Observed while verifying bd-97v4znb4 with an artificially delayed WS upgrade (LOCAL_PROD_WS_DELAY_MS=800 in scripts/local-prod-server.mjs). Opening a project whose index doc is NOT in local IndexedDB (share link / first open on this browser) fails outright with 'project index document <id> is unavailable on the sync server — cannot open the project' when the peer has not landed within connect()'s peer budget (400ms in production). Cause: connect() proceeds offline-first after the budget, then findDoc(index) gets automerge-repo's immediate cold-start 'unavailable' (no peers to ask), and the retry loop in client.ts bails on 'if (state.connectedPeers.size === 0) throw err' — so the open errors instead of waiting for the peer that is milliseconds away. Users on slow/high-latency connections cannot open a project they have not opened before; retrying works once the socket is warm. Fix direction: when the index is uncached and the adapter is still connecting, wait for the peer (or retry on peer-arrival) rather than treating zero-peers as proof of unavailability.

c-mgn0k6no.author: Carlos Scheidegger

title: Fix Windows Lua path escaping in pampa io_wasm tests
description: On Windows, 9 tests in crates/pampa/src/lua/io_wasm.rs (test_io_open_append, test_io_open_read_all, test_io_open_read_bytes, test_io_open_read_line, test_io_open_read_number, test_io_open_write_and_close, test_io_open_write_flush_incremental, test_io_type, test_io_write_returns_handle_for_chaining) panic with SyntaxError: invalid escape sequence near '"C:\U'. Tests interpolate file_path.display() into a Lua source string via lua.load(format!(...)), and Windows backslashes are parsed as Lua escape sequences (\U, \t, etc.). Same root cause and same fix as PR #95 (bd-3pe8) which used quarto_util::to_forward_slashes for filter_tests.rs / mediabag.rs / system.rs. io_wasm.rs was either added after that PR or missed. Surfaced 2026-04-28 while running cargo nextest -p pampa on Windows. Documented pattern: memory note Windows Path Escaping in Lua String Contexts. The same pattern must also be applied to crates/pampa/src/lua/io_wasm.rs test code (replace file_path.display() with to_forward_slashes(&file_path) in every lua.load(format!(...)) call).

c-i7infs8k.author: cderv
c-i7infs8k.text:
Fresh-context external review (opus, read the source) verdict: SHIP, not a band-aid. Native testing of the synthetic io is a legitimate strategy (test harness uses the same restricted stdlib as WASM + NativeRuntime, exercising real synthetic code, not a mock; .claude/rules/wasm.md endorses it). Split verdict on the two predicate changes:

- dofile_wasm is_absolute->has_root: GENUINE production WASM bug fix. Both call sites (filter.rs:151, shortcode.rs:84) are cfg(wasm32)-gated; on wasm32 is_absolute('/foo')==false so a rooted VFS path is mis-resolved. Not test-driven generalization.
- io_wasm starts_with('/')->is_rooted: in production WASM this already worked; has_root only adds C:\ recognition that WASM never sees. Benign and WASM-neutral; earns its keep via cross-target correctness + one shared predicate, not by fixing a prod io.open bug.

Two plan corrections applied:
1. My earlier framing wrongly implied the 4 existing dofile tests reach resolve_dofile_path. They do NOT — apply_lua_filter on native builds Lua::new() (real C dofile); the synthetic dofile is only registered under cfg(wasm32). Those tests are untouched. The new TDD test must call resolve_dofile_path DIRECTLY (private fn, reachable from the in-file #[cfg(test)] mod), red-first on Windows.
2. Added a call-site comment at io_wasm.rs:41 explaining why is_rooted, mirroring artifact.rs/output_sink.rs, so a future reader isn't confused by drive-letter handling in WASM-only code.

Plan file updated accordingly. Net: 3-file change, fixes one real (dofile) WASM bug + the Windows test failures, replaces two inconsistent inline absolute-checks with one documented has_root predicate in quarto-util.

c-qdnwz997.author: cderv
c-qdnwz997.text:
Investigation reframed this from a one-line escaping fix into a path-handling design question. Thinking path so far:

1. Original scope (swap file_path.display() -> to_forward_slashes in the 9 io_wasm tests) is INSUFFICIENT. It kills the Lua SyntaxError but the tests then fail differently: io.open resolves absolute-vs-relative with path.starts_with('/') (io_wasm.rs:41), and a Windows temp path 'C:/Users/...' (post forward-slash) does NOT start with '/', so it gets the VFS prefix -> '/project/C:/Users/...' -> NativeRuntime.file_read (plain fs::read) fails.

2. is_absolute() is the WRONG primitive. On wasm32-unknown-unknown (no target_family) Path::is_absolute() returns false even for rooted '/foo' paths; has_root() is the cross-target-correct check. Precedent already in-tree: artifact.rs:119 + output_sink.rs:230 use has_root() with comments citing bd-cfl67.

3. The /project/ VFS resolver is duplicated and inconsistent: io_wasm.rs uses starts_with('/') (ok in WASM, breaks native Windows test); dofile_wasm.rs:31 uses is_absolute() (ok native, latently WASM-broken — double-prefixes a rooted path in real WASM). Neither is correct on both targets. quarto-util has only to_forward_slashes; no shared absolute/rooted predicate.

4. Direction chosen: add one documented predicate (has_root-based) to quarto-util, use it at BOTH io_wasm.rs and dofile_wasm.rs (fixes the real dofile WASM-prod bug too), plus the test escaping fix. Don't build a full resolver (dofile's script_dir branch differs). Don't touch the 3 URL-string starts_with('/') sites (different semantics).

OPEN QUESTION under discussion: these synthetic io/dofile modules are WASM-only in production but documented as test constructs and currently unit-tested NATIVELY (incl. Windows). The native tests catch no prod-relevant bug a WASM test wouldn't, and they manufacture this strand's Windows-path problems. Deciding whether to keep native tests + cross-platform predicate, or move the logic tests to wasm-only. Checking whether a WASM test harness already exists for these lua modules before recommending.

title: qmd-syntax-helper's q-2-23 rule corrupts currency prose: `50$` -> `50$$`, and it runs under `convert --rule all`
description:
`crates/qmd-syntax-helper/src/conversions/q_2_23.rs` fixes Q-2-23 ("Unclosed
Inline Math") by APPENDING a closing `$` at the error location. That location is
the *error state's* position -- end of block -- not the offending `$`.

For genuinely unclosed math the edit is right. For a trailing currency amount it
silently rewrites the author's prose into broken markup:

    $ cat a.qmd
    The upgrade costs 50$

    $ qmd-syntax-helper convert -r q-2-23 --in-place a.qmd
    $ cat a.qmd
    The upgrade costs 50$$

`50$$` still does not parse -- `$$` opens display math -- so the rule takes a
file that failed with a coded, actionable diagnostic and leaves it failing with
an uncoded one, having changed the text. The fixpoint loop cannot recover:
`convert -r all` with the default 10 iterations stalls at the same output.

`Q223Converter` does not override `opt_in_only()`, so **`convert --rule all`
does this today**, unasked. Reproduced at `main` @ d05e96ee8 (v0.27.0).

## Why this cannot be fixed by making the rule smarter

Measured during the parent strand's investigation (full notes:
`claude-notes/plans/dollar-not-math-fatal-investigation/autofix-architecture.md`,
on branch `braid/bd-dollar-not-math-fatal-fpnqrpil-prose-that-not-valid`):

- Nothing distinguishes currency from math. `$20`, `$x + y` and `$abc` all fail
  in the same LR state (3157); the state follows the enclosing inline container,
  never the content.
- The AST-shape technique that makes `bracket_analysis.rs` safe is unavailable:
  it works because `[...]` parses, whereas an unmatched `$` means there is no
  AST. The parser failed precisely because it could not decide.
- The autofix system has no way to offer a choice: `Rule::convert` returns one
  `ConvertResult`, there is no candidate-fix API, no per-violation granularity,
  and no interactive prompt anywhere in the CLI.
- A content heuristic ("`$` followed by a digit means currency") is the
  regex-shaped guess `bracket_analysis`'s header explicitly rejects, and it is
  wrong on both sides: `$2x + 1$` opens with a digit, `$HOME` with a letter.

So the rule cannot pick correctly. It can only stop guessing wrong.

## Options

(a) Mark the rule `opt_in_only()` -- the mechanism added for
    `literal_brackets.rs` (bd-reference-links-unsupported-ddc4skac). One line;
    stops bulk corruption immediately; `check --rule all` still reports. But
    `-r q-2-23` still produces `50$$`.

(b) Flip the fix direction to escape: insert `\` before the opening `$`. That
    offset is already carried in the diagnostic as the `math-start` capture,
    resolved by `error_generation.rs` into a located `DetailItem` (it is the blue
    "This is the opening '$' mark." label); `q_2_23.rs` ignores it and uses
    `location.start_offset()` instead, so no new plumbing is needed. This matches
    `q-2-7` and `apostrophe-quotes` -- the only two escaping rules in the tree,
    and precisely the character whose innocent-prose use dominates its delimiter
    use. It is also the fix `docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-23.qmd` already prescribes,
    and the policy the parent strand settled on (enforce the escape).
    Trade-off: for genuinely unclosed math it yields literal `$x + y` -- wrong,
    but visibly wrong, versus today's silent prose-to-math conversion. Unlike
    (a) it always leaves a parseable document.

(c) Delete the rule.

Fix-direction survey for context: eleven "unclosed X" rules insert the closer
(q-2-5, q-2-11, q-2-12, q-2-13, q-2-15, q-2-16, q-2-17, q-2-18, q-2-21, q-2-22,
q-2-24, q-2-25, q-2-26); only q-2-7 and apostrophe-quotes escape.

## Note on scope

The parent strand (bd-dollar-not-math-fatal-fpnqrpil) was closed as not fixable
as asked -- a `$` in prose is ambiguous and no good diagnostic is possible. This
bug is separate and tractable: it is not about *diagnosing* the ambiguity, it is
about an auto-fix that resolves it wrongly and silently. Worth checking whether
`q-2-11` (unclosed double quote, also an append) has the same exposure.

## TDD

Failing test first: a fixture ending in a bare `$` must survive
`convert --rule all` unchanged (or gain `\$`, per the option chosen), and the
result must parse.

title: Monaco editor auto-closes backtick, inserting doubled ` when wrapping a word
description:

When wrapping an existing word in inline code, the leading backtick inserts one (next char is a word char, no auto-close) but the trailing backtick auto-closes (next char is EOL).

title: q2 preview: engine-written figure FILES (index_files/figure-html/*) are not served — image/png outputs show a broken img
description: Discovered while fixing bd-7hqea3qi. When a julia/jupyter cell's value displays via MIME image/png (no text/html), quarto-api's jupyter to-markdown port (ts-packages/quarto-api/src/jupyter/to-markdown.ts, mdImageOutput ~L427-471) writes the bytes to _files/figure-html/cell-N-output-M.png server-side and emits a path-ref ![](index_files/figure-html/...). In q2 preview the spliced pane then contains an whose src resolves against the SPA origin (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:PORT/index_files/figure-html/cell-2-output-1.png) but nothing serves those engine-written files (not in the VFS — remember /project/ prefix — and not on the preview HTTP server), so naturalWidth stays 0 and the user sees a broken/blank figure. Repro: PC6-FIG's FIG_INDEX_QMD variant with Base.show(io, ::MIME"image/png", ...) instead of text/html — observed imgs: [{src: 'http://127.0.0.1:56507/index_files/figure-html/cell-2-output-1.p…', naturalWidth: 0, rect 1x1}] (evidence in session log 2026-07-03). Plots.jl docs are unaffected in practice because its text/html display inlines the PNG as a data URI (this is why bd-7hqea3qi's user doc worked once the splice recursed). Affected: any engine output whose only display is a binary image MIME (CairoMakie image/png, PNG-only backends, jupyter matplotlib once that engine lands). Candidate fixes (not designed yet): have the preview capture driver ship supporting_files into the capture/VFS and serve them; or teach the preview server to serve _files/ from the project dir; or inline small images as data URIs at capture time. Note ExecuteResult already carries supporting_files/resource_files in the capture JSON.

title: Math-mode rendering for HTML output (MathJax + KaTeX)
description:
Implement math equation rendering for HTML output via MathJax (default) and KaTeX, matching Quarto 1's user-facing surface (html-math-method:) but routed through q2's own pipeline (q2 does not invoke Pandoc).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-math-mode.md
Predecessor handoff: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-math-mode-handoff.md (notes from bd-4eyf session)
Predecessor work: bd-4eyf (Bootstrap JS injection — established the predicate→js:* artifact pattern this builds on)

Scope (v1):
- New MathJsStage in crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/math_js.rs.
- Trigger: AST walk over Inline::Math + CustomNode("Equation") slots.
- Engines: mathjax (default) + katex; html-math-method: bare-string and {method, url} object forms; user URL override skips vendoring.
- New $math$ template slot in MINIMAL/FULL HTML templates, positioned before $for(scripts)$ so inline config block renders before the loader (matches Pandoc's slot order).
- Loader emitted via Project-scoped js:mathjax / js:katex artifact when vendored; via direct $math$-slot injection when user supplies url:.
- Vendor under resources/js/mathjax/ and resources/js/katex/. Bundle size strategy still TBD — see plan Q2 (recommendation: tex-chtml core ~150KB, not full ~10-15MB).
- Hub-client (WASM): include the stage (math is stateless, no iframe-reinit problem like Bootstrap had).

title: Perf: Artifact.content Vec<u8> forces per-render clones of static/cached bytes (consider Cow/Arc/Bytes)
description: Follow-up to bd-q3bxnq2e (VFS flush change-detection). Even with the flush-side skip-if-unchanged fix, one full copy of ~0.7MB of mostly-static artifact bytes survives per render: every render rebuilds RenderContext and re-runs the artifact producers, and Artifact.content is an owned Vec<u8>, so producers must copy. Concretely: BootstrapJsStage (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/bootstrap_js.rs:77) does include_bytes!(...).to_vec() (~81KB), website_bootstrap_icons.rs:37/:41 copies icons CSS (~99KB) + woff (~180KB), clipboard_js.rs:71/:81 (~10KB), and CompileThemeCssStage clones ~200-400KB of compiled CSS out of the SASS LRU cache. Fix direction: change Artifact.content from Vec<u8> to a shareable representation — Cow<'static, [u8]> (zero-copy for include_bytes! statics) or Arc<[u8]>/bytes::Bytes (every clone becomes a refcount bump, including flush-side copies even when content changed). Mechanical but wide refactor of a core type: every Artifact constructor, every .content consumer, merge/dedup byte comparisons (artifact.rs merge_into_project), across quarto-core + wasm-quarto-hub-client. Gate on data: bd-q3bxnq2e Phase 0 instrumentation (perf.vfs-flush gauge + native proxy) measures producer-clone cost alongside flush cost — pick up this strand only if the residual copy is a meaningful share of per-keystroke latency in hub-client (the only perf surface we care about; native is ~40-50x faster than Quarto 1 already). See claude-notes/plans/2026-06-09-wasm-vfs-artifact-reflush.md (design question 4).

c-melh50qc.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-melh50qc.text: Numbers from bd-q3bxnq2e Phase 0/3 (idle machine, native proxy): producer-side clone cost equals flushed bytes — ~400KB/render on a realistic themed doc, i.e. ~10us of memcpy natively (~0.02% of a 51ms render); ~100us even at a synthetic 7MB. Native wall-time impact is negligible. Recommendation: keep at backlog priority unless a WASM browser profile shows allocation pressure (wasm memory growth / GC churn) is a real cost — the in-browser story is the only place this could matter. Full table: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-09-wasm-vfs-artifact-reflush.md Findings.

title: Include shortcode does not resolve project-absolute (root-relative) paths
description: {{< include /path/from/project/root.qmd >}} is passed to the filesystem as an absolute OS path instead of being resolved against the project root, per Quarto path conventions. c-1fymfrqs.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-1fymfrqs.text: Diagnosed. Primary defect: include_expansion.rs:150-152 uses base_dir.join(include_path); Path::join with an absolute RHS discards the base, so a leading-/ (project-root-relative per Quarto convention / glob decision D2) path is read as an OS-absolute path. Secondary site: quarto-preview/src/deps.rs:213 has the same join trap, so leading-/ includes never register as preview deps. Q1 reference semantics: external-sources/quarto-cli/src/core/handlers/base.ts resolvePath (leading / anchors at project.dir, or the source dir for single-file). q2's ctx.project.dir already encodes that anchor in both modes. Fix + TDD plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-07-include-project-absolute-paths.md. Minimal repro verified (project with sub/doc.qmd including /sub/_includes/snippet.qmd -> Q-17-2).

title: iframe-safe code-copy in q2 preview / hub-client (functional copy in the WASM iframe)
description:
Follow-up to bd-lg6t6qfy, which made revealjs code-copy buttons STYLED + hover-hidden in all three paths but FUNCTIONAL (actually copies) only in native q2 render. In q2 preview / hub-client (the WASM/iframe paths), the buttons are intentionally inert: ClipboardJsStage is excluded from the WASM pipeline (pipeline.rs ~1866, 'hub-client iframe reinit'), and the reveal clipboard assets are registered #[cfg(not(target_arch = wasm32))] in reveal_assets() (crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs). This matches plain-HTML preview, where copy buttons are also inert.

To make copy actually work in the WASM iframe, build an iframe-safe, re-runnable clipboard init analogous to RevealChrome's useReveal() escape hatch (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/RevealDeck.tsx): a RevealClipboard React component that, on deck mount, binds clipboard.js (npm dep) to .code-copy-button and re-binds on every edit (the iframe re-renders, blowing away stateful listeners — the reason ClipboardJsStage was excluded). Consider covering plain-HTML preview the same way so reveal and HTML preview behave consistently (otherwise reveal preview would copy while HTML preview doesn't).

CSS + markup already ship in the WASM path (copy-code.scss is bundled unconditionally; the copy scaffold is a shared AST transform), so this is purely the JS-init leg. Verify end-to-end in a real hub-client browser session: hover-reveal, icon paints, clicking actually copies, and copy survives an edit/re-render.
close_reason: Implemented + merged in PR #330. Iframe-safe code-copy: one delegated capture-phase listener on PreviewRoot's previewHostRef covers reveal + plain-HTML preview in q2-preview and hub-client. Browser-verified both paths copy; editor stays closed. CI green.

c-zretgbp2.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-zretgbp2.text:
Implemented + verified. Both reveal AND plain-HTML preview now copy in the q2-preview / hub-client iframe.

Design (simpler than the strand's RevealClipboard suggestion): one delegated, capture-phase listener installed by PreviewRoot on previewHostRef — which wraps BOTH the <RevealDeck> and the plain-HTML <Ast> branch — so a single mount point covers reveal + HTML in both q2-preview and hub-client (both share PreviewRoot). No useReveal escape hatch needed (host already contains the reveal DOM). Iframe-safe by delegation: listener on a stable host, matched by selector, survives edit re-renders.

- New utils/codeCopy.ts (installCodeCopy) — navigator.clipboard.writeText (codebase's existing pattern, no clipboard.js dep); checkmark flash via code-copy-button-checked (SVG ships in copy-code.scss). Capture-phase stopPropagation on pointer/click so a copy click doesn't open PreviewRoot's onPointerUp-driven block editor.
- PreviewRoot: one useEffect installing it on previewHostRef.

TDD: 7 util tests + 2 PreviewRoot integration tests (red→green). Full preview-renderer suite green (456 unit + 493 integration). hub-client build:all (strict tsc -b) + test:ci green.

Browser E2E (real q2-preview iframe):
- Reveal deck: clipboard.readText() returned the exact code.
- Plain-HTML doc: writeText captured the exact code AND the editor did NOT open on the copy click (edit-isolation confirmed). No console errors.

Committed on braid/bd-wa2pgri8-iframe-copy (atop the bd-lg6t6qfy branch). Awaiting push approval. Open question for user: add a hub-client About-section changelog entry? (Change is in ts-packages/preview-renderer, not hub-client/, so the rule doesn't strictly trigger.)

title: Conditional-content Divs are not unwrapped: q2 emits <div class="content-visible"> where Q1 emits nothing
description:
Found while measuring direction (B) for bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7.

Q1 resolves a VISIBLE conditional Div by returning its content -- render_tabset's sibling in customnodes/content-hidden.lua:66, 'return el.content' -- after clearHiddenVisibleAttributes (:211) strips both marker classes and the condition attributes. The wrapper exists only to carry the condition. Spans and CodeBlocks keep their element (':154': 'this is only called on spans and codeblocks, so here we keep the scaffolding element, as opposed to in the Div where we return the inlined content').

q2's ConditionalContentTransform kept the Div AND its marker class, so pages carried a <div class="content-visible"> Q1 never emits. Measured on the Connect docs port: 10 q2 pages retained such a Div; Q1 has 0.

WHY IT MATTERED BEYOND COSMETICS. Under the section-tree TOC walk (bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7 direction B), a surviving non-section Div terminates the walk, so every heading inside a conditional block dropped out of the TOC. Measured: 2 pages (admin/authentication/ldap-based/{active-directory,ldap}-double-bind) lost #using-group-memberships, which Q1 lists. This strand is therefore a hard prerequisite for that one.

FIXED in Phase 1 of claude-notes/plans/2026-08-18-tabset-headings-in-toc.md on branch braid/bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7. Deliberate divergence from Q1: we unwrap only when the wrapper carries nothing of its own after stripping (Q1 unwraps unconditionally, discarding a user's #id and extra classes). The rules coincide for every real use measured.

Regression tests: crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/toc-containers/content-visible-div-unwrapped.qmd and content-visible-span-kept.qmd, plus unit tests bare_wrapper_is_unwrapped / wrapper_with_an_id_is_kept in conditional_content.rs.
close_reason: Delivered by bd-tabset-headings-in-toc-t04ie7f7 Phase 1: resolved conditional Divs are unwrapped and marker classes stripped, matching Q1's content-hidden.lua. Connect corpus: pages with a surviving content-visible/content-hidden Div 10 -> 0 (Q1: 0).

title: docs/_quarto.yml sidebar has no `extension` section — every Q-16-* error page is unlisted
description:
The error-reference sidebar in `docs/_quarto.yml` enumerates every error page BY HAND (153 entries at time of writing, one `- errors/<subsystem>/<code>.qmd` line each, grouped under `- section: "<subsystem>"`).

There is NO `- section: "extension"` block. Every `Q-16-*` page is therefore absent from the sidebar:

    docs/errors/extension/Q-16-1.qmd  .. Q-16-9.qmd   (9 pages, pre-existing)
    docs/errors/extension/Q-16-10.qmd .. Q-16-12.qmd  (3 pages, added by bd-exhbc6h8)

Verify with:  grep -n "errors/extension/" docs/_quarto.yml   -> no matches.

The pages exist, render, and are reachable by direct URL, so the `docs_url` in each
catalog entry resolves and no diagnostic ships a 404. What is missing is *navigation*:
a reader browsing the error reference cannot find them.

WHY THE LINT DOES NOT CATCH IT
`cargo xtask lint`s `error-docs-page-missing` rule reconciles the catalog against
`docs/errors/<subsystem>/<code>.qmd` file existence and checks the `docs_url` field.
Sidebar membership is deliberately outside its scope, so a whole subsystem can go
unlisted while the lint stays green. (bd-8otua`s `cargo xtask error-docs` audit owns
orphan/misplaced-page concerns; sidebar drift may belong there rather than here.)

SCOPE
- Add the `extension` section to the errors sidebar with all 12 pages.
- Check whether OTHER subsystems are also missing -- the count (153 listed) vs. the
  actual page count should be reconciled, not just patched for `extension`.
- Consider whether a hand-maintained list is the right shape at all: a Quarto listing
  or a generated include would make this class of drift impossible. That is the real
  fix; adding 12 lines is the stopgap.

NOTED WHILE doing bd-exhbc6h8 (Q-16-10/11/12). Not fixed there: adding only the three
new pages to a section that does not exist, while nine siblings stay unlisted, would
have been worse than leaving it consistent.

c-i0b2ww6w.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-i0b2ww6w.text:
Scoped and implemented on braid/bd-wcmk1fsq-docsquartoyml-sidebar-has-no (off main).

DRIFT WAS WIDER THAN extension. On main: 207 pages, 153 sidebar entries, 54 unlisted across 9 subsystems. Two subsystems had no `- section:` block at all -- `extension` (12 pages) and `crossref` (1). The rest were partial: project 23 missing (only 5 of 28 listed), markdown 14, listing 3, theme 2, writer 2, navigation 1.

THE 'REAL FIX' QUESTION IS SETTLED -- the answer is no. Investigated whether a listing/glob/auto sidebar could replace the hand-maintained list:
- Q2 supports `auto:` in sidebars (sidebar_auto.rs, group_with_subdirs produces exactly the section-per-subsystem shape), BUT within-section sort falls back to *title* (prose), not code, so it would not produce code order.
- Q1 cannot either. Confirmed against quarto-cli source: Q1 DOES merge arbitrary top-level front matter into listing items (website-listing-read.ts:1184-1187), so `sort: code` is accepted -- but the build-time comparator is lodash orderBy -> plain relational operators (_compareAscending.js:23,30), no localeCompare, no numeric. Q1 sorts Q-1-10 before Q-1-2, same as Q2. Q1's auto-sidebar is the same story: `order:` first, then localeCompare on basename, not numeric (website-sidebar-auto.ts:313-333).
- The only mechanism either Quarto offers is a hand-maintained numeric `order:` on every page. Rejected by Gordon as a redundant per-page integer field not worth it.

So: hand-maintained list stays, backfilled, with a lint rule to keep it honest. Index ordering waits on bd-otmqu.

ALSO FOUND (separate defect, not fixed here): docs/errors/index.qmd renders its Code, Subsystem and Status columns EMPTY -- all 207 rows. Root cause is one gap: top-level front-matter keys never reach ListingItem. `item.extra` is populated only from an explicit `listing-item: extra:` block (document_profile.rs:200-213), and both the sort resolver (sort.rs:117) and the table-column resolver (binding.rs:586) fall through to that same map. Verified E2E with a scratch project: a bare `code:` key emits 'Warning [Q-12-3]: Unknown sort field code' and renders empty cells. Also no filter-ui/sort-ui/category markup on the built page. This is a genuine Q1-parity gap and belongs to bd-otmqu -- worth widening that strand from 'sort' to 'arbitrary front matter must reach listing items for sort AND display'. Do NOT add a numeric-aware comparator to Q2 as part of it: Q1 has none, so that would be divergence, not parity.

title: Stale alias redirect stubs are never cleaned from the output dir
description:
When an entry is removed from a page's 'aliases:' front matter, the redirect stub previously written for it stays in the output directory across subsequent (incremental or full) renders. Nothing tracks which output files the alias pass owns, so nothing knows to delete it.

Quarto 1 has the same behavior, so this is not a regression — it is a known gap deliberately deferred out of the initial aliases implementation (bd-aliases-redirects-missing-sch7cd1g, plan claude-notes/plans/2026-08-12-aliases-redirect-stubs.md, design question 8).

Symptom: an old URL keeps redirecting after the author intentionally retired the redirect. Low severity (a stale redirect is better than a 404) but it makes '_site/' non-reproducible without a clean.

Likely fix shape: record the stub paths the alias pass wrote (a manifest alongside the other project artifacts), and on the next render delete stubs present in the manifest but absent from the current alias set. Must not delete files it did not write.

title: Website TOC title uses toc-title-document ('Table of contents') instead of toc-title-website ('On this page')
description:
On a website project, q2 renders the page TOC heading as 'Table of contents' where Q1 renders 'On this page'. Q1's language catalog has two keys — toc-title-document ('Table of contents') for standalone documents and toc-title-website ('On this page') for website pages — and picks by context. q2's toc_generate transform (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/toc_generate.rs, title precedence block around lines 122-146) always consults toc-title-document, for websites too. The localized data is already there: resources/language/_language-*.yml files ship toc-title-website translations ('Nesta página', 'En aquesta pàgina', …), so only the key selection is missing. The precedence chain (user toc-title metadata > localized toc-title-document > English literal) was a deliberate decision (bd-llhlzd7p, 2026-07-17) but did not distinguish website context; the recent TOC-title markup work (bd-toc-smart-quotes-6nro57ed, 25866ab0) touched the same block without changing the key choice. Suggested fix: in the second arm of the precedence chain, select 'toc-title-website' when the render is a website page and 'toc-title-document' otherwise (ast.meta is the merged project + document metadata, so website-ness is detectable there; Q1 keys off the project type). User-supplied toc-title metadata keeps top precedence either way. Real-world hit: every Posit Connect docs page with a TOC (~324 of 352 pages) shows 'Table of contents' in the right-hand column where the Q1 site shows 'On this page'. The porting project currently masks this in its visual-comparison sweeps. Minimal repro (one-page website): /Users/cscheid/repos/github/cscheid/q2-connect-docs/llms-info/repros/website-toc-title/ — run 'q2 render .' there; _site/index.html has '

Table of contents

' while the committed Q1 comparison _site-q1/index.html has 'On this page'. See README.md. Origin strand in the connect-docs porting skein: br-website-toc-title-q8mgt5gn. Observed with q2 0.19.0, re-verified on 0.20.0 and 0.21.0; unfixed at HEAD (3ac596e0).

c-ld97wrhy.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ld97wrhy.text:
Investigated 2026-08-14 on main @ 094c0a80. Plan skeleton: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-14-website-toc-title-on-this-page.md (commit 0e02e399). Verdict: ready to design.

Confirmed reproducible end-to-end with a fresh binary; localized data already ships (34/36 language files) and LanguageTerms::get has no key allowlist, so only key selection is missing.

Two corrections/refinements to the description's suggested fix:
- Recommend ctx.project.project_kind() == ProjectKind::Website rather than reading website-ness from ast.meta: a stray 'website:' key in merged metadata is not a project-type claim, and custom project types resolve their base kind into project_kind. Costs touching the transform's currently-unused _ctx param.
- Q1 also gates on isHtmlOutput(strict=true), which EXCLUDES revealjs; q2's Format::is_html() INCLUDES revealjs. So format gating is an open design question, not a one-liner. (Q1's !projectIsBook guard needs no q2 equivalent — ProjectKind::Website already excludes Book.)

Also checked: toc-title is the catalog's only -website/-document key pair, so this closes the category. Zero snapshots reference the TOC title.

Awaiting user answers on 4 design questions before implementation.

c-yswdct15.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-yswdct15.text:
Design settled 2026-08-14 (commit 4b3e5e99):
1. Detect via ctx.project.project_kind() == ProjectKind::Website
2. Gate on ctx.format.identifier == FormatIdentifier::Html (matches Q1 isHtmlOutput(strict=true); NOT Format::is_html(), which includes revealjs)
3. Leave the English literal 'Table of Contents' fallback alone (test-only path)
4. Topic branch off main, PR soon

CORRECTION to my earlier comment: I claimed ast.meta could not see project type. Wrong. The 'project' key strip at metadata_merge.rs:146 applies only to extension contribution layers; a probe confirms {{< meta project.type >}} renders 'website', and resolve_project_type rewrites custom types to their base kind. Both routes are viable. ctx chosen on failure mode, not capability: the meta route fails silently (front-matter project.type is PandocInlines -> as_str() trap per bd-y89ihf0i, plus a metadata-as-str lint suppression, plus the merge stage itself calls 'project' a project-config concern), whereas ctx fails to compile.

Preview/WASM parity checked: the two WASM call sites using ProjectConfig::default() are parse_qmd_to_ast_with_attribution and render_qmd_content, both content-string entry points where ProjectKind::Default is correct; project-aware paths use ProjectContext::discover. Verified by reading call sites, not by running a preview.

New Phase 0 case found: a website project with NO 'website:' key in _quarto.yml renders as type: website and still gets 'Table of contents'.

Pre-flight note: verify --skip-hub-build has 1 unrelated failure (quarto-preview config_reports_embedded_asset_manifest_hashes, stale embedded viewer dist). Agreed to file a strand only if it survives a full rebuild.

Ready to implement; awaiting go-ahead for Phase 0.

c-zikbz1hm.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-zikbz1hm.text:
IMPLEMENTED — all phases complete on branch braid/bd-website-toc-title-wn80ymab (6 commits, 0e02e399..fdfa2e27). Awaiting PR. Fix: toc_title_term(ctx) in crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/toc_generate.rs selects toc-title-website when project_kind() == Website AND format.identifier == FormatIdentifier::Html (Q1's isHtmlOutput strict=true, which excludes revealjs — deliberately NOT Format::is_html(), which includes it). Tests: 14 new (8 unit + 6 e2e). TDD red state confirmed first — 5 failed for the right reason, 9 were regression guards. The localized failures reported 'Indice' (pt document term), proving the catalog loaded and the failure was purely key selection. End-to-end through the real q2 binary, output inspected: original repro now emits '

On this page

', matching the committed Q1 reference. Also verified: website with no 'website:' key, lang: pt -> 'Nesta pagina', default project, book project, and bare single-file render all correct. Live 'q2 preview' of a website project confirmed {tocTitleId: 'toc-title', text: 'On this page', tag: 'H2'} inside the renderer iframe — this closes the preview-parity risk that design had verified only by reading call sites. Docs: added a 'Table of Contents Title' subsection to docs/guides/authoring/document-language.qmd. The plan predicted no docs were needed; that was wrong — the change makes toc-title-document silently ineffective on websites, with no diagnostic, so it needs saying. Full 'cargo xtask verify' (incl. hub build + WASM): 14/14 steps, 12077/12077 tests passed. cargo xtask lint clean. No snapshot files touched. Pre-flight failure (config_reports_embedded_asset_manifest_hashes) RESOLVED, no strand filed as agreed — it did not survive a full rebuild. Cause: build:wasm had never succeeded here because wasm-opt/binaryen was added to the build 2026-08-13, one day before this work. Discovered follow-up: bd-aag27gmv (p2) — consolidate accumulated WASM toolchains.

title: Add a markdown grammar to quarto-highlight (13 built-ins, markdown not among them)
description:
Plan 2 of bd-98m98wg8. Delivers property 3 of the epic's target output. MEASURED at q2 HEAD eac0c7acf: a plain four-backtick markdown block containing a heading, emphasis, a link and a nested r fence renders as 
# A heading ...

with ZERO highlight spans. The Q1 dev build renders the same fixture as

  

    # A heading ... [link](x)

BUILTIN_ALIASES / BUILTIN_BUILDERS (crates/quarto-highlight/src/registry.rs:152,170) carry 13 languages: bash css html javascript json julia lua python r sql tsx typescript yaml. markdown is not one.

Independently valuable: this is not about cells or engines. Every fenced markdown block in every Quarto document is currently unhighlighted. Shippable WITHOUT injection support (the sibling strand) - that yields markdown-level spans with any embedded code left plain, which is already most of the visual gap.

Note q2 has a tree-sitter markdown grammar in-tree already (crates/tree-sitter-qmd) - worth evaluating whether it is usable here or whether it is too qmd-specific and an upstream tree-sitter-markdown is the better source.

title: Eliminate serde_json::Value intermediate in pampa JSON writer
description: Native profile of parse_qmd_to_ast (the hub-client's entry) on scaled lorem-ipsum fixtures shows ~50-55% of runtime in memory movement (_platform_memmove) + allocator work, and ~5-7% in indexmap::Core::insert_full. Root cause: pampa::writers::json builds a full serde_json::Value tree (each node a Value::Object backed by IndexMap<String, Value> with fresh String keys for 'c'/'s'/'t'/etc.) and then serializes it to bytes via serde_json::to_writer. Two full passes, enormous intermediate allocation. At 8x the canonical doc, _platform_memmove alone is 41% of wall time. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-22-serde-json-value-intermediate.md. Hypothesis is 'replace the Value tree with direct Serialize impls that stream JSON to the output Writer,' to be validated with the perf-harness driver introduced in the same plan.
close_reason: Streaming JSON writer landed on perf/2026-04-22-json-sourcemap in commits 4e7a43ec (Phase 1 scaffold) and b3e15a47 (Phase 2 cutover). 1.65x-2.3x speedup across 1x-8x fixtures; IndexMap/allocator hotspots eliminated. Browser-verified by Carlos. Remaining memmove cost is the output buffer's amortized doubling — a separate optimization, documented as follow-up in the plan.

title: Authoring guide for the include shortcode (semantics, Q1 differences)
description: docs/ has no user-facing authoring page for {{< include >}} at all (only the docs/errors/include/Q-17-*.qmd error pages). Write one under docs/guides/authoring/: usage, path resolution (relative to the declaring file's directory), the Q2 semantic model (included files are parsed standalone; resulting blocks land inside the containing construct at the shortcode's position), positions where expansion applies (every block-list position once bd-1fz3vh99 lands), the inline-include limitation (Q-17-4), frontmatter of included files being ignored, and the divergences-from-Q1 table (Q1: textual line-based splice, top-level + fenced-div only, silent raw-text passthrough elsewhere; Q2: AST splice, container-safe, no fence corruption, no sibling-item injection). Source material: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-07-nested-include-expansion.md (empirical Q1 matrix + semantic-consequences list).

c-83ey3eny.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-83ey3eny.text:
Offering measured material for this guide's "divergences-from-Q1 table", from the Positron docs Q1->Q2 port. Measured 2026-08-26 against Q1 99.9.9 (dev checkout) and q2 0.27.0. EXTENDED POSITION MATRIX The plan this strand cites (claude-notes/plans/2026-08-07-nested-include-expansion.md) probes four positions. Four more are worth the table, because two of them are the only places q2 loses to Q1: position Q1 q2 top level expands expands fenced div / callout expands expands blockquote `> {{< include >}}` raw passthrough ?include list item `- {{< include >}}` raw passthrough expands --- not previously probed --- indented in list item (blank line first) expands expands continuation line after a list item expands ?include continuation line after a paragraph expands ?include mid-paragraph inline raw passthrough ?include table cell raw passthrough expands Net: q2 handles strictly more positions than Q1. The two regressions are one class — the include sits on a lazy continuation line of an existing block, so it is not the sole content of its paragraph and IncludeExpansionStage skips it. Note it is not list-specific; a plain paragraph continuation behaves identically. A CORRECTION TO THE PLAN'S CONSEQUENCE #2 The plan says, of sibling-item injection: "An included file that is itself a bullet list, included from inside a list item, becomes a *nested* list within that item — it cannot contribute sibling items to the surrounding list. (This was never expressible in Q1 either — includes in list items didn't work — so nothing regresses ...)" The parenthetical is not correct. Sibling-item injection WAS expressible in Q1, and does regress. The plan's probe was `- {{< include >}}` (the include as the item's own content), which indeed never worked in Q1. The form that did work is the continuation line. With `_inc.qmd` = `- item three (from the include)`: source: - item one - item two {{< include "_inc.qmd" >}} Q1:
  • item one
  • item two
  • item three (from the include)
    • q2:
  • item one
  • item two ?include
    • Three siblings in Q1, from a textual splice. Real Q1 documents use this — it is how the Positron docs attach a shared settings bullet to a per-page list (positron-notebook-editor.qmd:125, one occurrence). Same probe, the plan's form, for contrast — q2 is the better engine here: - item one - {{< include "_inc.qmd" >}} Q1:
  • item one
  • {{< include "_inc.qmd" >}}
    • (raw text) q2:
  • item one
  • item three (from the include)
    • So both halves of the plan's claim need one adjustment each: includes in list items DID work in Q1 in one spelling, and sibling injection is a genuine (small) regression rather than a never-was. CONSEQUENCE #4 IS SLIGHTLY NARROW TOO It says Q-17-4 "narrows to inline includes (`text {{< include >}} text`) — the one position that stays unsupported, matching Q1." Q-17-4 also fires on both continuation-line positions, where Q1 did expand. The catalog message ("only expanded when the shortcode is the sole content of its own paragraph") stays literally accurate; it is the "matching Q1" part that does not hold for those two. THE Q-17-4 HINT DESERVES A CAVEAT IN THE GUIDE The hint is "Put the include shortcode in its own paragraph, surrounded by blank lines." That stops the content loss and the stray ?include, but it does not reproduce what Q1 rendered: Q1, continuation form: ONE list of three items q2, after adding blank line: TWO lists — [one, two] then [three] This is the intended "no sibling-item injection" boundary, not a bug. But an author who follows the hint will reasonably believe they have restored the original document, and the structure has quietly changed. Worth one sentence in the guide, and possibly in the Q-17-4 error page. REPRO /Users/gordon/src/q2-positron-docs/llms-info/repros/include-list-continuation-dropped/ — repro plus control (identical except the blank line), with a committed Q1 baseline in _site-q1/ for comparison. `q2 render`, then read _site/index.html. Origin strand: br-include-list-continuation-dropped-4eo254e5 (q2-positron-docs skein, P3, open). Filed there rather than as a q2 bug because the behaviour is by design and already diagnosed; this guide is the right home for it.

title: YAML provenance desync warning when a block scalar containing a multi-byte character is followed by a plain scalar
description:
Pre-existing on main (verified with a main build side by side while working on bd-mjo6ao32); not caused by the frontmatter delimiter change.

Repro (pampa, stderr):
  printf -- '---
description: |
  Quarto —
  smaller.
author: Christophe Dervieux
date: "2026-04-14"
---

x
' | pampa -t json

emits twice: Warning: YAML string scalar has no content provenance — `YamlWithSourceInfo::content_source_info()` returned `None` for a node already established to be a `Yaml::String` scalar. The caret spans from inside `Christophe Dervieux` into the next line.

Conditions found so far: needs (1) a multi-line literal block scalar that contains a multi-byte character (an em dash; replacing it with ASCII `x` silences it), and (2) a following plain scalar (a block scalar alone does not warn). Smells like a byte-vs-char offset mismatch in quarto-yaml's content-provenance derivation for block scalars. In the wild: quarto-web docs/blog/_archive/posts/2026-04-14-chrome-headless-shell/index.qmd emits it 6 times. The warning is the fallback path, so output is still correct; the risk is a misaligned caret in later diagnostics.

title: Treat leading-/ resource paths as project-root-relative
description:
YAML 'resources:' patterns starting with '/' are interpreted as filesystem-absolute and rejected by the project-containment check. They should be project-root-relative (TS Quarto convention). Blocks rendering quarto-web under q2.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-21-resource-path-leading-slash.md

title: Per-project capture cache for cross-session reuse
description:
Phase C.7 (bd-kw93.7) shipped the per-doc capture filesystem cache in <data_dir>/captures/ — the same tempdir that gets deleted when q2 preview exits. So closing and re-opening preview against the same project always misses the cache, even though the inputs are bit-for-bit identical.

A per-project cache location (e.g. <project_root>/.q2/captures/, ignored by .gitignore convention) would unlock cross-session reuse. The cache key derivation (sha256 of canonical input_qmd) is already content-addressed and survives across sessions — only the directory choice changes.

See plan §C.7 'Open follow-up'.

title: Shortcodes in metadata fields (title/subtitle) expand to empty string
description: {{< env CONNECT_VERSION >}} in a document's title: or subtitle: renders as empty in the output HTML (<title>V </title>), while the same shortcode in body text expands correctly. Symmetric across .qmd and .md inputs (verified 2026-08-07 during bd-6d2wj4zp e2e testing with CONNECT_VERSION set in the environment). Affects the Connect docs port, whose website title and several subtitles use {{< env >}}. Repro: doc with title: 'V {{< env X >}}' + body 'Inline: {{< env X >}}' — body expands, title doesn't.

title: Q2's HTML crossref renderer doesn't support crossref presentation options (title-delim, fig-prefix, labels, ref-hyperlink, chapters)
description:
Confirmed 2026-09-18 during the pandoc-writer-hybrid epic's user-facing/backward-compat review.

crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/crossref_render.rs:28-31 hard-codes English defaults for
caption/ref text: "Phase 1 hard-codes the English defaults: '<Kind> <N>: '". A full-tree grep for
`title-delim`/`fig-prefix`/`ref-hyperlink` across crates/ returns exactly one hit: that comment.

Q1's vendored Lua (crossref/format.lua) honors all of these from `crossref:` metadata:
- `crossref.fig-prefix`/`tbl-prefix`/etc. (per-type caption prefix override)
- `crossref.title-delim` (separator between prefix and caption, default ": ")
- `crossref.ref-hyperlink` (whether @refs are hyperlinked)
- `crossref.labels` (e.g. `labels: alpha` -> "Figure A" instead of "Figure 1")
- `crossref.chapters` (section-scoped "1.2" numbering, using `order.section`, which Q2 already
  carries in `Order { section: Vec<u32>, order: u32 }` (crossref/index.rs:124-133) but never
  reads in its own renderer)

Real Q1 fixture exercising all of these: quarto-cli's own tests/docs/crossrefs/options.qmd.

**Decided (2026-09-18, Gordon):** this is an accepted, known asymmetry for the pandoc-writer-hybrid
epic's v1 — the Pandoc/Q1 Lua leg will honor these options (for free, since it reuses vendored
Q1 code) while Q2's native HTML leg does not, until this strand is picked up. The epic's
Definition of done was corrected from "identical [crossref] semantics across HTML and Pandoc
formats" to "identical numbers" specifically because of this gap - presentation options are
out of parity for now. Not epic scope: implementing this is real new Q2 HTML-renderer work, not
wiring the existing pandoc-hybrid path.

Scope for whoever picks this up: teach crossref_render.rs to read the same `crossref.*` metadata
keys Q1's crossref/format.lua reads, achieving actual format parity (not just number parity)
across HTML and Pandoc targets. See claude-notes/designs/pandoc-hybrid-architecture.md for the
epic context.

title: julia_engine_e2e tests race on the shared ambient transport — make them hermetic
description: Discovered during bd-h4rhohhy P3: j1..j6 in crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/julia_engine_e2e.rs all use setup_julia_project() -> the single ambient shared transport file (~/Library/Caches/quarto/julia/julia_transport.txt). Under full-workspace nextest parallelism, concurrent daemon:false server startups overwrite each other's transport entry and clients fail with 'Incorrect HMAC digest' at isopen (rotating victims: j1 one run, j3+j4 the next, on a CLEAN machine with zero orphan processes). Interim fix on branch braid/bd-h4rhohhy-q2-preview-engine-capture: nextest test-group serialization (max-threads=1, precedent bd-u3ze). Proper fix: per-test isolation via the isolate_julia_project()/IsolatedJuliaServerGuard helpers that P3 added for PC4a/PC6 (copies Project.toml+Manifest.toml to a temp dir, re-points QUARTO_JULIA_PROJECT -> per-test transport; JULIA_DEPOT_PATH stays shared so no re-instantiation). Cost: each test boots its own julia server (~5-9s). Relates to the leaked-worker issue bd-l9jhy5u0.

title: qmd writer emits decoded zero-width/format characters raw; output fails to re-parse (GH #672)
description: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/672. Since the named-entity decode (bd-named-entities-w6xbfftj, PR #488) the reader folds ​ (and ­, ‎, ‏, ⁠, ⁡, ⁢, ⁣, and numeric refs like ​) into a Str holding the literal Cf-category codepoint. The qmd writer emits that codepoint verbatim, but the grammar's prose regexes (pandoc_str in grammar.js) accept no Cf character except ZWNJ/ZWJ, so pampa's own output is a parse error; inside a heading superscript it cascades into Q-2-16 Unclosed Superscript. In the wild: quarto-web index.qmd '# Welcome to Quarto^​[®]{.trademark}^'. Verified at 7ef59618: every Cf codepoint probed (U+00AD, U+200B, U+200E/F, U+2060-2064, U+FEFF, U+061C, U+202A-E, U+2066-9) is a hard parse error in prose; code spans, code blocks, link titles and attribute values accept them. Two-sided fix: (1) writer re-encodes Cf chars as named entities (numeric fallback); (2) grammar accepts \p{Cf} raw in prose, mirroring the \p{M} fix in bd-96fswwce (Pandoc parity; deliberately non-canonical at the text level). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-11-zero-width-chars-writer-parser-gh672.md
close_reason: Fixed in caa29d6c (writer: Cf chars -> preferred WHATWG entity or &#xXXXX;, ZWNJ/ZWJ raw; grammar: PANDOC_COMBINING_MARKS widened to \p{M}\p{Cf}, parser regenerated) + b15868ed (bd-i18zoy4n, & escaping) on branch braid/bd-wuiu1of7-zero-width-entities. Full cargo xtask verify green for both commits; end-to-end q2 render of the quarto-web heading inspected. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-09-11-zero-width-chars-writer-parser-gh672.md

title: Tree-sitter scanner over-eagerly excludes *, -, +, #, digits from soft-break
description:
The same class of bug as bd-af1e affects 5 more characters. The scanner's line-break handler at scanner.c:2286-2291 and 2371-2376 excludes these from soft-line-break candidates whenever they appear at the start of a continuation line:
- '*' (could be emphasis, list, thematic break)
- '-' (could be list, thematic break, setext header)
- '+' (could be list)
- '#' (could be ATX header)
- digits 0-9 (could be ordered list)

But each of these only opens a block in specific contexts (most need a trailing space, '#' needs space, '*'/'-'/'+' need space for list, '***'/'---' need 3+ for thematic break, digits need '.' or ')' followed by space). A bare 'X' followed by content is just inline text and should soft-break.

Verified pampa vs pandoc divergence on:
  foo bar
  *emph* baz                 → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  -text more                 → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  +text more                 → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  #hashtag more              → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  123abc more                → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks

Correct exclusions (pampa already matches pandoc for):
  * list item                → BulletList opens (correct)
  - list item                → BulletList opens (correct)
  # heading                  → Header opens (correct)
  1. item                    → OrderedList opens (correct)

Fix approach: same as bd-af1e (peek-count). For each char, peek the trailing context to decide if it actually opens a block:
- '*', '-': count run; if >=3 with all whitespace/eol after, thematic break (interrupt). If '* ' or '*\t', list (interrupt). Otherwise inline.
- '+': only list if followed by whitespace.
- '#': only ATX if followed by whitespace or eol.
- digits: only ordered list if followed by '.' or ')' AND space.

':' (fenced div / definition list) was excluded from this issue because its semantics are more entangled with qmd-specific features and pandoc-mode-specific rules — file separately if regression observed.

Sibling of bd-af1e. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-tree-sitter-backtick-paragraph-split.md for the bd-af1e implementation pattern.
close_reason: Re-scoped: see bd-wv4e replacement for asterisks-only fix. The other characters (-, +, #, digits, :) have a backslash-escape workaround (\-text, \#hashtag, etc.) so are not severe enough to fix in this pass.

title: CVE-prevention: cookie+Bearer dual-credential MUST return 400
description:
Highest-impact item flagged in plan §Phase 2. A request carrying BOTH a session cookie AND an Authorization: Bearer header MUST be rejected with HTTP 400 and body {"error":"conflicting_credentials"} BEFORE any auth-decision logic runs.

Test name: cookie_and_bearer_returns_400 in crates/quarto-hub/tests/auth_bearer.rs.

title: Determine whether the quarto.config.md Lua path's offset arithmetic is live or inert
description:
Liveness question discovered while sizing the audit for bd-mxa44voa. This may be a no-op; the point of the strand is to determine that cheaply rather than leave it unknown.

THE SITE. crates/pampa/src/lua/config_value.rs:601-631 implements the quarto.config.md Lua API (the filter-facing analog of the !md tag). It calls:

    crate::readers::qmd::read(s.as_bytes(), ..., Some(filter_source_info(lua)))

This is the same call shape as parse_config_string_as_markdown in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs, which is the confirmed instance of the bd-mxa44voa bug: a parent SourceInfo supplied as the offset base for a recursive parse of a string, where the string's bytes are not a prefix-aligned byte-identical slice of the parent's span. Of roughly 50 readers::qmd::read call sites in the tree, these two are the ONLY ones in production that pass Some(parent).

WHY IT MAY BE INERT. filter_source_info (crates/pampa/src/lua/types.rs:2291) returns SourceInfo::Generated { by: By::filter(path, line), from: [] } -- a Generated marker with an EMPTY anchor list. SourceInfo::Substring::resolve_byte_range() on a Generated parent delegates to its Invocation anchor; with from: [] there is none, so resolve_byte_range() and map_offset() return None. The defective arithmetic is therefore performed but never resolves to a byte position, and nothing user-visible comes of it.

THE UNKNOWN. Whether any code calls append_anchor to attach an Invocation anchor to a filter_source_info()-derived Generated BEFORE the resulting Substring is read for diagnostics or for preimage_in. If something does, the arithmetic becomes live and the site is a real instance of the class. The audit did not trace all append_anchor call sites across quarto-core and pampa.

TASK.
1. Enumerate append_anchor call sites and determine whether any can reach a filter_source_info()-derived Generated.
2. If NO: close this, and add a comment at config_value.rs:601 recording WHY it is safe, so the next auditor does not have to re-derive it. The safety is non-obvious and depends on an empty anchor list several crates away.
3. If YES: fix it the same way as the rest of the class (see bd-mxa44voa), and write a test that exercises quarto.config.md from a Lua filter with an escaped string.

Either outcome is cheap and removes an open question from the audit.
close_reason: Absorbed into claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-provenance-3-audit-and-fix.md (Phase 2). Plan 3 now audits and fixes, so the liveness question plus its two outcomes (document why inert, or fix if live) are checklist rows there.

title: TS engines don't receive project_env / QUARTO_PROFILE
description:
TS engine extensions do not see the project's `_environment` values, nor `QUARTO_PROFILE`. Built-in knitr does (bd-fu16z22k): `knitr/subprocess.rs:367` applies `.envs(options.project_env...)` when it spawns Rscript. The deno spawn (`ts_process.rs:891`) sets no environment at all, so a TS engine's cells observe neither.

DEFERRED FROM the ts-engine-extensions <- main merge (Phase B4 of claude-notes/plans/2026-08-13-ts-engine-extensions-merge-main.md), which said to do this in-merge IF small and to file a strand otherwise. It is not small, and the reason is architectural rather than a matter of threading an argument:

* knitr spawns a FRESH Rscript subprocess per execution, so applying env at spawn is inherently per-document and correct.
* TS engines share ONE long-lived deno host. The spawn lives in `TsEngineHost::ensure_started`, whose documented contract is that init 'runs at most once across concurrent callers'. There is no `ExecutionContext` in scope there, and there structurally cannot be one: the process is started lazily on first use and reused for every subsequent document and engine.

So a naive `.envs()` at the deno spawn would bake in whichever document happened to start the host first. Under a project render where `_environment` values or the active profile differ per document, that is silently wrong — arguably worse than today's honest 'no env at all', because it would be right often enough to stop checking.

Correct fixes, neither of which belongs inside a merge:
  (a) carry the env per-execute on the wire — add a field to `TsExecuteOptions` (which today has input/source_path/format/temp_dir/cwd/project_dir/lib_dir/quiet and NO env field) and have the deno host apply it around each execute. A protocol change, so it needs an engine-author compatibility story.
  (b) key the host pool by env-set and restart when it changes. Cheaper to reason about, but throws away the shared-process win whenever env varies.

(a) is the likely answer since it keeps one host.

Acceptance: a TS engine observes a value defined in the project's `_environment`, and observes `QUARTO_PROFILE` matching the active profile set, in a project render where two documents resolve DIFFERENT env/profile values — the multi-document case is the whole point, since a single-document test would pass under the incorrect spawn-time fix too.

The first two switch the ratchet off with zero output; the third is loud but misattributed, reporting 'no CI step runs it' against every package rather than 'this workflow is unparseable'.
