title: Optional-variable syntax: $variable?$ shorthand for $if(variable)$$variable$$endif$
description:
When users see Q-10-2 warnings on a variable they intend to be optional, today they have to wrap each reference in $if(variable)$$variable$$endif$. A short $variable?$ form would be cleaner and let authors silence the warning at the use site.

Feasibility (recorded in bd-xdnk plan §Follow-up):
- `?` is unused as a sigil in the current grammar.
- Doesn't collide with any pipe name (`pairs|first|last|rest|allbutlast|uppercase|lowercase|length|reverse|chomp|nowrap|alpha|roman|left|center|right`).
- Pipes already use `/` as separator (`tree-sitter-doctemplate/grammar/grammar.js:84-86`), so `?` doesn't conflict.
- Implementation cost: one grammar token, one `bool optional` field on `VariableRef`, one branch in `render_variable` that returns `Doc::Empty` silently when `optional` is set and the lookup fails.

Open question: should `?` propagate to applied partials (`$var?:partial()$`)? Probably yes — same intent. Not applicable to `$if$` itself.

Discovered while wiring template diagnostics through quarto render (bd-xdnk). Now that template warnings are user-visible, having a clean opt-out becomes more valuable.

title: Audit HashMap/HashSet iteration in user-visible output paths
description:
Follow-up from bd-hwdlq (triage of issue #222). The bd-hwdlq fix addresses one specific instance of non-deterministic diagnostic output caused by HashMap iteration in crates/quarto-parse-errors. There may be others.

Scope: grep across the codebase for HashMap/HashSet whose iteration order is observable in user-facing output (diagnostics, writers, snapshots, JSON emission, source maps, anywhere a Vec/String/file is built from iteration). For each instance, decide whether the iteration order is actually deterministic-by-construction (e.g. all entries are equal under the user-visible projection), or whether it needs to migrate to hashlink::LinkedHashMap / BTreeMap / sorted Vec.

Out of scope: HashMap/HashSet used only for membership tests (contains/insert) where iteration is not observed.

Suggested approach:
1. ripgrep 'HashMap<\|HashSet<' across crates/, filter to non-test code paths
2. For each hit, trace the variable to see if it's iterated (.iter(), .values(), .keys(), for loop, .collect::<Vec>())
3. Of the iterated ones, check whether the iteration result reaches user-visible output
4. File sub-issues or fix directly depending on volume

Consider also adding a CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/ note codifying 'containers iterated to produce user-visible output must have deterministic iteration order.'

title: Windows: vendored bootstrap-icons.css CRLF breaks store_artifacts_uses_project_scope_paths content-prefix assert
description: On Windows checkout, resources/bootstrap-icons/bootstrap-icons.css has CRLF line endings in the working tree (git ls-files --eol shows i/lf w/crlf) because .gitattributes has no line-ending rule for resources/ (repo .gitattributes only pins .beads/issues.jsonl merge driver). include_bytes! embeds the file verbatim with CRLF, so BOOTSTRAP_ICONS_CSS starts with b"/*!\r\n * Bootstrap Icons..." on Windows. Test store_artifacts_uses_project_scope_paths (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/website_bootstrap_icons.rs:114) asserts css.content.starts_with(b"/*!\n * Bootstrap Icons") (LF only) and panics on Windows. Same CRLF-vendored-resource class as the PR #374 cluster (bd-nxxgg0pp flagged website_bootstrap_icons project-scope as one of the 21 residual quarto-core failures at the time). Fix options: pin resources/bootstrap-icons/*.css as eol=lf in .gitattributes (preferred, matches vendored-asset convention used elsewhere per commit 65c8958f revealjs vendored-asset drift test), or normalize the assertion/content read. Branch bd-fn05e8pg-windows-path-separator surfaced this as the next Windows nextest failure after its path-separator fix.
design: SUPERSEDED direction: do NOT pin .gitattributes eol=lf. Per bd-aamrec3j design decision (2026-07-08), verbatim-served build assets (no SourceInfo/byte-offset, never enter automerge, CRLF byte-identical to every browser) are the sanctioned-normalize class, not the pin class. This exact file is already on bd-aamrec3j's AFFECTED list. Fix = normalize \r\n -> \n in the test assertion at website_bootstrap_icons.rs:114 (mirror crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package's norm closure), not a repo-wide gitattributes change.

title: Q-5-4 / Q-5-5 code collision: include_resolve.rs and example_embed.rs emit the same codes for different warnings
description:
WHAT. Two diagnostics share one code, and the catalog documents only one of them.

- Q-5-4: include_resolve.rs "Include file not found" (2026-05-04, 6421c333, bd-8kp3)
         example_embed.rs  "Example Embed Missing \`file=\`" (2026-06-10, cc246ee5, #271)
- Q-5-5: include_resolve.rs "Invalid include form"
         example_embed.rs  "Example Embed Target Is Not a Static Asset"

Emit sites: crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/include_resolve.rs:~513 (Q-5-4), :~537 (Q-5-5); crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/example_embed.rs:~553 (Q-5-5) and its Q-5-4 neighbour.

crates/quarto-error-catalog/error_catalog.json and docs/errors/project/Q-5-4.qmd / Q-5-5.qmd describe the embed meaning only. Every include warning therefore prints a docs_url that lands on an unrelated page. The include stage was the first user; the embed transform reused the numbers without checking.

WHY THE LINTS MISSED IT. error-docs-page-missing checks that a page exists for each catalog code; error-docs-sidebar-unlisted checks sidebar membership. Neither checks that a code has a single emitting meaning, nor that emit-site titles agree with the catalog title. The page exists -- it is just the wrong page.

FIX. Give the include diagnostics fresh codes (highest project code is Q-5-29, so Q-5-30/Q-5-31), each with a catalog entry + docs/errors/project/<code>.qmd page + sidebar entry in the same commit (per the lint rules in CLAUDE.md). Leave the embed transform on the documented codes. Expected to be folded into bd-include-in-header-text-blocks-ins2v6za unless the owner prefers a separate PR (plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-20-include-in-header-text-blocks.md, Q3).

HYGIENE CLASS (for whoever designs the recurring error-code chores). This is the third instance of the same defect class, after bd-be2f7 (Q-10-* citeproc vs doctemplate) and the drift catalogued in bd-fiv9u (Q-3-*). The mechanical check that would have caught all three: for every string literal matching Q-\d+-\d+ in .with_code(...) across crates/, (a) the code must exist in the catalog, (b) all emit sites for one code must share one diagnostic title, and (c) that title must match the catalog title. That is a natural addition to the bd-8otua `cargo xtask error-docs audit` subcommand, or a fourth rule in crates/xtask/src/lint/. A code is 'allocated' the moment it appears in error_catalog.json; authors must take the next free number in the subsystem, never reuse.

title: q2 preview: per-doc sidebar lands at bottom of page (extra <div> wrapper breaks grid)
description:
Symptom: in docs/ website, q2 render places the per-document YAML sidebar (Quarto 2 / Introduction / Markdown) on the left as expected, but q2 preview renders the same sidebar elements at the bottom of the page (below <main>).

Reproduced with /Users/cscheid/rooms/room-1/q2/docs/. Render: nav#quarto-sidebar at x=310 width=250 left of main. Preview: same nav inside <div> wrapper at x=585 width=749 below main.

Root cause: ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/chromeSlots.tsx:53-56 (SidebarSlot, and sibling NavbarSlot/PageNavSlot/FooterSlot) wrap the injected chrome HTML in <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML=...>. The native template at crates/quarto-core/src/template.rs:185-188 emits $rendered.navigation.sidebar$ as a *direct* child of <div id="quarto-content">, no wrapper. The Quarto theme CSS grid on #quarto-content assigns nav#quarto-sidebar to grid-area 'content-top / page-start / page-bottom / body-start' — but only when nav#quarto-sidebar is a grid child. With the extra wrapper <div>, the wrapper becomes the grid item with default placement 'body-content-start / body-content-end' + 'grid-row: auto', stacking below <main>.

Verified by patching `display: contents` on the wrapper at runtime in the preview iframe — sidebar snapped to correct position (x=310, on left).

Existing test PreviewDocument.integration.test.tsx:252 checks `quartoContent.querySelector('nav#quarto-sidebar')` (descendant), not direct-child relationship — missed the bug.

Fix: add `style={{display: 'contents'}}` to the wrapping <div> in SidebarSlot (and apply same fix to sibling slots NavbarSlot, PageNavSlot, FooterSlot for parity — they share the same root cause even if the symptoms are less severe today). Add tests that assert direct-child relationship via `Array.from(parent.children).includes(node)` rather than `parent.querySelector(...)`.
close_reason: Wrapper <div> in chrome slots now display:contents — sidebar/navbar/footer/page-nav are transparent to parent CSS grid/flex layout, matching native template byte-for-byte. Fix verified via failing-first tests (4 new in PreviewDocument.integration.test.tsx) and end-to-end browser check on docs/: sidebar at x=310 width=250 (left), main at x=585.5 — identical to q2 render. cargo xtask verify: all 12 steps green.

title: Shortcodes are expanded inside inline code spans
description: A shortcode written inside an inline code span is expanded rather than left literal. Rendering Literal `{{< fa plus >}}` in code. yields `?fa` — the unknown-shortcode placeholder — instead of the literal text `{{< fa plus >}}`. The tight spelling `{{}}` behaves the same way, so this is not about the separator. The parser is not at fault: a code span containing a shortcode is not a parse error, and the source text is preserved through parsing. The expansion happens after, in shortcode processing, which does not exclude code-span content. Cost: any documentation that shows shortcode syntax in prose gets its examples silently replaced. That includes q2's own docs and the error page for Q-2-52, which shows `{{< fa plus >}}` inside fenced code (fenced blocks may or may not be affected — check both). Found while fixing bd-shortcode-no-space-gspu6l5s: a qmd-syntax-helper test asserts that a tight shortcode inside a code span is left alone by the autocorrect rule, which is correct, and rendering the fixture showed the expansion.

title: q2-slides preview: reveal video iframe not stretched (SPA wraps RawBlock in div, no reveal.js autostretch)
description:
Discovered while fixing bd-5b21rbaq Phase 5 (reveal video sizing).

In NATIVE 'q2 render' revealjs, the video shortcode now emits <iframe class="r-stretch"> as a direct child of <section>, and reveal.js sizes it to fill the slide (verified 778x414).

In the q2-slides PREVIEW (and hub-client), the SAME r-stretch class is correctly present in the AST, but the q2-preview SPA reveal renderer wraps the RawBlock iframe in a bare <div> -> 'section > div > iframe.r-stretch'. reveal's stretch selector ('section > .r-stretch', direct child only) misses it, and the preview does not run the global window.Reveal layout. Result: the preview reveal video stays at ~222x111 (default).

Likely fix: a preview-SPA CSS rule sizing the wrapped iframe (e.g. '.reveal .slides section > div > iframe.r-stretch { width/height ... }'), since the preview can't rely on reveal's JS stretch. Needs its own reproduction + design. Note this also affects how the SPA wraps RawBlocks generally.

Context + measurements: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-22-video-shortcode-preview.md (Phase 5).

CAVEAT: reveal switches to SCROLL view in a narrow/tall preview pane, where the r-stretch wrapper collapses to height 0 (video invisible). This is a general reveal-scroll-mode trait of r-stretch (affects images too), not specific to video — flagged for a possible separate look if scroll view becomes the hub-client default. title: Merge main → feature/websites: IncludeExpansion before DocumentProfile checkpoint
description:
Merge main into feature/websites such that the include-shortcode expansion pipeline stage (main, 215482fb) is wired into the pipeline BEFORE the DocumentProfile checkpoint (feature/websites, e8674612).

Post-merge pipeline order (HTML / WASM / analysis):
  Parse -> MetadataMerge -> IncludeExpansion -> DocumentProfile -> UnwrapProfile -> PreEngineSugaring -> ...

Rationale: statically-knowable information a document declares via {{< include ... >}} (headings, code blocks, crossref targets) must be visible to DocumentProfile so downstream project-level features (sidebars, nav, cross-doc links, incremental rebuilds, future freeze) see a consistent AST.

title: cargo xtask stage-doc-examples stages into the main repo, not the current worktree
description:
`cargo xtask stage-doc-examples` resolves its output root via `create_worktree::repo_root` (crates/xtask/src/stage_doc_examples.rs:33), which shells out to `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`. In a git worktree that path points at the MAIN repository's .git, so the derived repo root is the main checkout — not the worktree the command was invoked from.

Effect: run from a worktree, the command reports success and stages rendered examples into the main repo's docs/examples/, leaving the worktree's own docs/examples/ missing. `q2 render docs/` in that worktree then fails immediately with "Declared resource '<worktree>/docs/examples' does not exist on disk", because docs/_quarto.yml declares `project.resources: [examples]`. The failure looks like a docs bug and the obvious remedy (re-run stage-doc-examples) never works, which costs real time to diagnose — it did during bd-repo-actions-missing-99ezd2fe.

Workaround: copy the main repo's staged docs/examples/ into the worktree (both are gitignored and generated, so no repo state is affected).

Fix direction: stage-doc-examples wants the *current working tree* root, not the common git dir. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` gives that. Note repo_root is shared with create_worktree, where --git-common-dir is arguably the right choice (it wants the main repo to add worktrees to), so this likely needs two distinct helpers rather than changing repo_root in place — check every caller before changing it.

title: Share link project never joins synced project set
description:
Visiting #/share/<indexDocId> opens the project but never adds it to the user's synced project set (profile doc). Later trying to add the same docId via the Connect form fails with a misleading 'may already exist' error.

Root cause is three separate bugs:
1. App.tsx share route gates projectSetActions.addProject on status === 'connected', which is racy against useProjectSet's async init. On initial share-link load the guard almost always fails, the add is skipped, and there is no retry.
2. ProjectSelector renders the list from projectSetEntries when useProjectSet is true, so the share-flow's IDB-only entry is invisible.
3. ProjectSelector.handleConnectProject skips the getProjectByIndexDocId dedupe check that the share route has, and projectStorage.addProject then collides with the IDB unique index on indexDocId. The form also never calls projectSetActions.addProject, so even a successful add wouldn't reach the synced set.

Full analysis and TDD fix plan in claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-share-link-project-not-added.md.

Repro: https://quarto-hub.com/#/share/SNHcgVzUkWpGFmcxkCkpCDfFtmu?server=wss%3A%2F%2Fquarto-hub.com%2Fws&file=%2Felliot%2Findex.qmd&name=Demo+Playground — opens fine but SNHcgVzUkWpGFmcxkCkpCDfFtmu is absent from the reporting user's profile projects map, and manual add via Connect form fails with 'Failed to add project. The document ID may already exist.'

title: Catalog/corpus drift: markdown Q-2-X assignments diverge between error_catalog.json, pampa/resources/error-corpus/, and production-emit sites
description:
While authoring docs/errors/markdown/ pages (bd-lgxdr), found multiple drift cases between the three sources of truth:

1. **Q-2-5**: catalog title 'Unclosed Emphasis' (generic), but corpus Q-2-5.json and production code (json.rs:328) use 'Unclosed Underscore Emphasis'. Catalog says Q-2-14 is the underscore-specific one. Production behavior collapses to Q-2-5; Q-2-14 is never actually emitted with the *with_code* API.

2. **Q-2-35**: catalog says 'Invalid List-Table Structure' (matches production emits at treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:785,976), but corpus Q-2-35.json claims 'Indented code blocks are not supported'. The corpus appears stale.

3. **Q-2-36, Q-2-37, Q-2-38**: present in pampa/resources/error-corpus/ as Q-2-36.json (Old-style knitr chunk options), Q-2-37.json (Line break in link destination), Q-2-38.json (Unclosed Attribute Specifier) — and Q-2-36 is emitted in production (treesitter.rs:1244) — but NONE are in error_catalog.json. The catalog jumps Q-2-35 → Q-2-39.

4. **Q-2-6, Q-2-8**: in catalog but never emitted in production. Reserved for future strict-mode (Q-2-6) and upgraded-to-error-and-renumbered (Q-2-8 → Q-2-36).

Plan: the catalog is authoritative for docs_url; the corpus needs to be reconciled to match. Add missing Q-2-36/37/38 to the catalog (or remove from corpus if they should not exist). Fix Q-2-5 and Q-2-35 corpus titles to match catalog. Decide whether Q-2-14 should be deprecated or whether production should be updated to emit it for the underscore variant specifically.

title: <!DOCTYPE html> and <?xml ?> at line start are a parse error, not raw HTML
description:
A line beginning `<!` followed by a letter (a declaration such as `<!DOCTYPE html>`) or `<?` (a processing instruction) fails to parse:

    $ printf "<!DOCTYPE html>\n" | q2 render -
    Error: Parse error
     1 | <!DOCTYPE html>
       | ^-- unexpected character or token here

CommonMark covers these with HTML block types 3, 4 and 5 (`<?`, `<!LETTER`,
`<![CDATA[`), and pandocs `isBlockTag` likewise treats a leading `!` or `?` as
block-level, so both emit them verbatim.

ROOT CAUSE. In `parse_open_angle_brace` (crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c,
~line 2052), a `<` followed by `!` is routed unconditionally into
`parse_html_comment`. When the text is not a comment that scan fails, and the
only fallback is `LT_STR_LITERAL` — which is not valid in that position — so
the parser reaches the generic "unexpected character or token here" in
crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs:316. `<?` never reaches an
HTML branch at all.

NOT A REGRESSION. Reproduces on released q2 0.28.0 and on main.

SCOPE. Out of scope for bd-block-html-wrapped-in-p-w8qebxig, which fixes the
*reader* (a paragraph opening with a block-level tag lifts to a RawBlock).
This one is upstream of that, in the scanner: the reader never sees these
constructs as raw HTML because the document fails to parse first.
`html_block::starts_block_html` in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/html_block.rs
already returns true for both forms, so once the scanner emits them the lift
needs no change. There is a NOTE recording this at
crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_html_block_lift.rs.

Related: bd-html-comment-triple-dash-close-hoyvu7mq (a comment closed with
`--->` never terminates) is the other known defect in the same comment-lexing
path.

title: MCP server silently creates projects in offline mode with in-memory storage (data black hole)
description: quarto-sync-client's createNewProject defaults peerTimeoutMs to 1ms (browser-IDB-first design) and falls back to offline mode on peer-wait failure. The MCP server passes no timeout and uses memory storage, so create_project against a reachable-but-not-yet-connected hub reports success (returns indexDocId) for documents that exist only in process memory; short-lived agent sessions then exit before the late-arriving peer connection syncs anything, and the project is lost. Auth round-trips (probe + actor + refresh) add enough latency to lose the 1ms race deterministically — found by the bd-81cfshmw Phase 3 full-stack auth e2e (hub audit log showed ws auth_ok while the client logged 'creating project in offline mode'). Fix: requireOnline option in sync-client (typed PeerUnavailableError instead of silent fallback; browser defaults unchanged) + hub-mcp passes requireOnline + 15s peerTimeoutMs on connect and create.
close_reason: Fixed in e219c9cf: requireOnline option in sync-client (typed PeerUnavailableError, adapter teardown before throw, browser defaults locked by test) + hub-mcp passes requireOnline with 15s budget on connect and create. Regression tests in client.require-online.test.ts and require-online.test.ts.

c-iu3qy1vz.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-iu3qy1vz.text:
Mechanism for this now has a plan: Plan 7b's Pass-1 discovery admission tier
(2026-07-08-plan7b-native-content-processors.md, landed on
feature/ts-engine-extensions in 483e2732f / e1174d9f8).

7b makes an engine's file claims STATIC DATA (`claims-files` entries naming a
native content processor), so project discovery can decide admission by running
the processor's `sniff` natively — no engine construction, no subprocess. Its
"one predicate, two sites" invariant guarantees discovery-admits <=> claim-stage-
claims by construction, which is what a discovery extension needs to not drift.

7b's ratified decision 3 is the policy half you were waiting on, and it is
deliberately narrow: a file claimed only via a DYNAMIC claims_file (no declared
processor) is EXCLUDED from project discovery — it stays renderable as an
explicit single-file argument. Rationale: Pass-1 discovery must be 100%
launch-free.

Two caveats for whoever picks this up:
- .ipynb admission policy is Plan 7c's mechanism but still this strand's
  decision — 7c supplies the processor; whether .ipynb is a default project
  input is a separate call (it needs the .md/.Rmd semantics conversation).
- Today the exclusion is already the de-facto behavior but the error message is
  wrong: naming a dynamically-claimed file explicitly INSIDE a project fails
  with "excluded from the render list of project X (check `project.render`)",
  even when project.render lists it. Verified E2E 2026-08-16. The good wording
  already exists on the discovery path (Q-5-13 says "Renderable means .qmd, .md,
  or an extension claimed by an installed engine extension").

c-jbcfjc2e.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-jbcfjc2e.text:
Resolved in the OPPOSITE direction by the ts-engine-extensions <- main merge (D3 of claude-notes/plans/2026-08-13-ts-engine-extensions-merge-main.md), so this strand's note about extending 'the pipeline's SourceType handling' no longer describes the plan.

SourceType has now LOST its Ipynb and Rmd variants rather than gaining behavior for them, and LoadedSource::source_type is Option<SourceType>. q2 processes exactly two kinds of markdown — qmd (executes) and md (does not); everything else is converted to qmd before the parser by SourceConversionStage (renamed from EngineClaimsFileStage in the same merge).

Practical effect for whoever picks this up: do NOT add a SourceType variant for a new input format. Ship an engine that claims the extension. The variants were safe to delete because they never had a behavioral consumer — the intended one was a PipelinePlanner pushing a ConvertNotebook stage (design of 806703bde, 2026-01-06), never built. Removing them completes that design (same pre-parse insertion point) with dynamic engine dispatch instead of static enum dispatch.

title: WS adapters crash the process on any socket error except ECONNREFUSED
description: Upstream automerge-repo's WebSocketClientAdapter.onError rethrows any node error whose code isn't ECONNREFUSED; our StoppableWebSocketClientAdapter inherits it and NodeWebSocketClientAdapter copied the pattern (with redaction). A throw inside an EventEmitter callback cannot reach any caller — it becomes uncaughtException, and hub-mcp's redacting handler then process.exit(1)s. Net effect: a mid-handshake ECONNRESET ('socket hang up'), ENOTFOUND, ETIMEDOUT etc. kills the whole MCP server (and any other node consumer). Found by bd-xnmd5ni1's requireOnline test (test hub destroys upgrade sockets). Fix: log (redacted) and let the close/retry machinery recover; never throw from the handler. Upstream issue should be filed against automerge-repo (their onError throw has the same defect for browser consumers on node).
close_reason: Fixed in b9861b23: both adapters log (redacted) instead of throwing; retry machinery owns recovery. Direct-invocation regression tests for ECONNRESET/ECONNREFUSED/ENOTFOUND. Upstream automerge-repo issue still to file — noted in Phase 4 items.

title: Lockfile missing @esbuild/* platform binaries: every npm ci produced a broken esbuild
description:
Top-level esbuild@0.28.0 entered package-lock.json (via the ts-engine-extensions merge, for quarto-hub-mcp ^0.28.0 and quarto-engine-host-deno 0.28.0) with ZERO @esbuild/* optional platform-dependency entries — only vite's nested, different-version esbuild copy had its platform set recorded. Consequence: any lockfile-driven install (npm ci, incremental npm install) yields an esbuild JS wrapper with no binary, failing with 'The package "@esbuild/<platform>" could not be found' on every platform, not just one machine. First observed 2026-08-19 on darwin-arm64 when cargo xtask verify's ts-packages leg hit the quarto-hub-mcp bundle test (scripts/bundle.mjs). CI exposure: ts-test-suite.yml does npm ci then runs engine-host-deno tests, which pin esbuild 0.28.0.

Fix: delete the stale node_modules/esbuild block from package-lock.json (jq 'del(.packages["node_modules/esbuild"])'), run npm install from the repo root so npm re-resolves esbuild and records the full 26-entry @esbuild/* platform set, verify with a clean npm ci + the previously-failing bundle test, and commit the lockfile. A machine-local 'npm install --no-save @esbuild/darwin-arm64' works around it but leaves CI and colleagues broken — do not stop there. Troubleshooting note added to claude-notes/instructions/coding.md (hub-client section) covering the symptom and the artifact-level repair, for this class of problem (also applies to rollup/swc/parcel platform binaries).

This class of lockfile defect is npm's known optional-deps recording weakness: a lock entry created without its platform optionalDependencies persists silently until something executes the tool from a clean install.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #560: lockfile regenerated with the full @esbuild/* platform set; instructions note added

title: Discovery errors wrap structured diagnostics in 'Project discovery failed' string (double Error: prefix, Q-7-8 masks real codes in --json-errors)
description: Found while implementing bd-sekn481x. classify_inputs flattens every discovery failure to DispatchError::Discover(e.to_string()) at 9 call sites in crates/quarto/src/commands/render.rs. title: Audit: metadata string reads using as_str() that should use as_plain_text()
description:
Sweep for the same class of bug fixed in bd-9ez3ngt1 (PR #265): reading a user-authored metadata string option via ConfigValue::as_str() instead of as_plain_text().

WHY: In document-metadata context a bare YAML string value is parsed as markdown and stored as ConfigValueKind::PandocInlines, NOT Scalar(String). as_str() returns None for PandocInlines (quarto-pandoc-types/src/config_value.rs:641-649); as_plain_text() handles both forms (config_value.rs:675-684). So any option read with as_str() is silently ignored unless the user writes the undocumented !str escape tag. This silently broke reference-location entirely (bd-9ez3ngt1).

DECISION CRITERION per call site: if the value is a user-authored front-matter/metadata STRING that could reasonably be written as a bare scalar (and where markdown-in-value is harmless because we only want its text), switch as_str() -> as_plain_text(). LEAVE as_str() where the code is *deliberately* distinguishing a scalar string from inlines, or where the value is internal (AST plain_data, attrs, computed config) rather than user front matter. Each site needs judgment, not a blanket replace.

SEED INVENTORY (production, non-test; verify each — some may be internal/intentional):
- crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/appendix.rs:80 (appendix-style), :282, :331 (license/copyright text), :374 (citation url)
- crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/toc_generate.rs:117 (toc title)
- crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/website_canonical_url.rs:153, :205, :230 (canonical-url / site url)
- crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/callout_resolve.rs:559
- crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/title_block.rs:132 and metadata_normalize.rs:98 (meta.as_str() — likely INTENTIONAL scalar checks; confirm)
- crossref_render.rs (228/234/325/331/661/667), crossref_index.rs (252/321/326), shortcode_resolve.rs:169, code_block_generate.rs:118 — likely internal AST/attr data, lower priority; confirm not front-matter.
(NOTE: metadata_merge.rs as_str() hits are all in #[test] asserts — ignore.)

Already fixed (do not redo): footnotes.rs:78 and appendix.rs:92 (reference-location), bd-9ez3ngt1 / PR #265.

TDD: for each site that reads a real user option, add a regression render test with the option written as a bare front-matter string before switching the accessor. Consider whether a lint (cargo xtask lint) could flag as_str() on meta.get(...) results to prevent recurrence.

title: No wasm32-target Rust test coverage for synthetic Lua io/dofile/os path resolution
description:
The synthetic Lua modules in crates/pampa/src/lua (io_wasm.rs, dofile_wasm.rs, os_wasm.rs) replace the C-backed io/os/dofile that have no working fopen on wasm32-unknown-unknown. Their WASM-specific code paths run ONLY under cfg(target_arch=wasm32) (registered in filter.rs and shortcode.rs). There is no Rust wasm32 unit-test harness: pampa has no wasm-bindgen-test dependency, no #[wasm_bindgen_test] tests, and no CI job runs cargo test --target wasm32 for it. The only wasm-pack test invocation is a stale Travis config asserting 1+1. WASM is otherwise exercised black-box from TypeScript via hub-client/src/**/*.wasm.test.ts (load the compiled .wasm, drive via JS).

Concrete gap (evidence): bd-vxl8 fixed a latent wasm-only bug in dofile_wasm.rs::resolve_dofile_path where Path::is_absolute() returns false on wasm32 for rooted /foo paths (no target_family), so a rooted VFS path was mis-resolved (joined under script_dir or double-prefixed with /project/). NO Rust or TS test caught this; it was found by reasoning about wasm32 path semantics. A future regression in WASM VFS path resolution would be invisible to cargo nextest and may slip past the TS black-box layer.

Decide whether targeted wasm32 Rust coverage is worth the infra cost. Options to weigh: add wasm-bindgen-test to pampa with a small focused set covering the VFS path-resolution predicates (is_rooted/has_root behavior, /project/ prefixing, dofile/io.open resolution); OR add targeted TS wasm.test.ts cases that drive these paths through the compiled wasm; OR accept the native-proxy + black-box status quo and document it. Low priority: the logic is mostly platform-independent and now uses a cross-target-correct has_root predicate (quarto-util::is_rooted).

title: A listing record's path: is resolved against its declaring file but emitted raw, so writers and browsers disagree
description:
Inline listing records resolve `path:` against the file that declared it (`BaseDirContext::base_dir_for`, per claude-notes/designs/path-resolution-model.md), but a value that does not resolve to a project document is stored and emitted as the **raw author string**.

The two readings then disagree. A record declared in `_quarto.yml` with `path: files/report.pdf` means *project-root-relative* to the resolver, but the emitted `href="files/report.pdf"` is *host-page-relative* to a browser. On a host page in a subdirectory those are different files. A leading `/` has the same split: project root to the resolver, site root to the browser (which is usually right, but by luck rather than design).

Both output paths inherit whatever this settles on — the HTML binding emits the literal verbatim, and the llms.txt companion now does too (bd4073110 plus its follow-up).

Surfaced by the scoped re-review of the final fix wave on the listing inline-records branch; plan claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-listing-inline-contents.md. Deliberately not settled there — the plan (§D4) specifies verbatim emission and says nothing about rebasing a non-document literal.

Related: bd-oejuizi9 (path-resolution bug class).

title: Listing numeric config keys silently ignore unquoted YAML integers (page-size, max-items, grid-columns, ...)
description: parse_listings in crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/config.rs reads numeric options with entry.value.as_plain_text().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()) — but an unquoted YAML integer (page-size: 10) arrives as ConfigValueKind::Scalar(Yaml::Integer), for which as_plain_text() returns None, so the option is silently dropped and the default kept. Only the quoted form ("10") ever worked. Discovered while investigating bd-listing-ellipsis-no-matching-l963osy1, where max-description-length: 40 was silently ignored; that key is fixed on that strand's branch via a new parse_u32_scalar helper (as_int() fallback to plain-text parse). Remaining broken keys to migrate onto the helper: page-size (config.rs:493), max-items (:498), grid-columns (:537) — plus audit parse_feed and any other numeric reads in the listing config for the same pattern. Related: the metadata-as-str lint catches the as_str() variant of this trap but not as_plain_text() on integers; consider whether the lint (or a sibling) should cover numeric reads.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #574 (merge 3b771188f): as_int_lenient/as_f64_lenient accessors on ConfigValue; four listing keys, revealjs margin (Yaml::Real), and the bare-as_int family (order, reading-time/word-count, slide-level, extension priority) migrated. Lint follow-up remains open as bd-clqzz2rl.

title: QMD writer drops shortcode arguments and delimiters
description:
User-reported round-trip failure: `printf '{{< video https://youtu.be/abc width="800" height="450" >}}\n' | pampa -t qmd` produces `{{video}}` — losing the `{{<` / `>}}` delimiters, the URL positional arg, and named keyword args.

Root cause: `crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:1716` `write_shortcode` emits only `{{ + name + }}`, ignoring `is_escaped`, `positional_args`, and `keyword_args`. Even the no-arg form is wrong (qmd syntax requires `{{< name >}}`, not `{{name}}`).

The parser populates the `Shortcode` struct correctly; the JSON / native writers preserve all data via `shortcode_to_span`. Only the qmd writer is broken.

The existing roundtrip suite in `tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/` does NOT catch this: it goes qmd → JSON → qmd, and the JSON writer converts `Inline::Shortcode` to `Inline::Span`, so `write_shortcode` is never exercised.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-shortcode-qmd-roundtrip.md
close_reason: Implemented qmd writer round-trip for shortcodes; switched keyword_args to LinkedHashMap for source-order preservation. End-to-end verified, full xtask verify green.

title: Import Quarto 1 revealjs themes & theming defaults into Quarto 2 (reveal 6)
description: Quarto 2 ships reveal.js 6 with only a precompiled white.css and no SCSS theme-layer system. Q1 users find Q2 revealjs output unfamiliar: title placement, bullet alignment, and theme defaults differ. Goal: bring Q1's revealjs themes + theming defaults into Q2 so output feels 'at home' for Q1 users, adapted to reveal 6 (Q1 was reveal 5) and Q2's SCSS subsystem. Requires: (1) understand reveal 5->6 theming differences, (2) verify/understand how Q1 adapts reveal themes to its SCSS layers, (3) design the adaptation arrow Q1->Q2. Study phase first, assessment into linked plan, then iterate before implementing. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-16-revealjs-themes-q1-to-q2.md

c-ko2ejphf.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ko2ejphf.text: Decisions resolved (2026-06-16): D1 single unified SCSS compilation (with required docs caveat); D2 keep Q1 $presentation-*/$body-* vocabulary (Option 1 - cross-format brand sharing + zero user migration; Option 2 unlocks ~no capability since reveal 6 emits everything as runtime --r-* either way); D3 ship Stage A alone first, each stage on own branch off feature/revealjs-q1-themes; D4 accept both naming, alias white->default/black->dark; D5 'feels at home' not pixel-perfect. TOOLCHAIN EXPERIMENT: grass 0.13.4 compiles all 14 reveal-6 stock themes incl. full module API (@use ...with(...), sass:color, namespaced mixins) -> our native compiler handles reveal 6 fine; migration cost is on Q1 theme *content*, not the build. Integration branch feature/revealjs-q1-themes created. Awaiting go-ahead for Stage A.

c-rsjg85ce.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-rsjg85ce.text: Study phase complete. Assessment written to claude-notes/plans/2026-06-16-revealjs-themes-q1-to-q2.md. Key findings: (1) Q2's reveal branch short-circuits before SCSS entirely; resolve_theme_name collapses every theme to white; the only Quarto reveal CSS (quarto-reveal.css, 1.5KB) has NO title-slide/bullet rules -> that's why output feels un-Quarto. (2) reveal 5->6 changed theme *authoring* (camelCase->kebab Sass vars, @import->@use module system) but NOT visual output or the stable --r-* runtime contract. (3) Q1's adaptation = own kebab vocab in scss:defaults + quarto.scss (1116 lines) mapping to reveal camelCase + two-pass compile via exposer.scss. (4) Lucky convergence: reveal 6 independently adopted kebab vars + stable --r-*, so Q2 can likely do SINGLE-pass and skip Q1's two-pass complexity. (5) Root cause of complaints: Q1 sets $presentation-slide-text-align:left (reveal centers) and $presentation-heading-text-transform:none (reveal uppercases) -- Q2 makes neither override. Awaiting user review of plan + D-series decisions before implementing.

title: Monaco qmd tokenizer crashes editor on executable cells
description: The qmd Monarch base tokenizer (quartoTheme.ts, added in 13c5b98b) used a non-capturing group (?:\{) for the opening brace of an executable cell rule. Monaco's MonarchTokenizer requires array-action rules to capture every matched char in consecutive groups; the (?:\{) consumed { without a capture, so any line like ```{r} threw 'with groups, all characters should be matched in consecutive groups' mid-tokenise and blanked the editor. Fix: fold { into capture group 1, keeping group 2 (the lang name for nextEmbedded $2) unchanged. Added a static invariant test.
close_reason: Fixed in 0e2bb57d: fold opening brace into capture group 1 so Monaco's array-action reconstruction check passes. Static invariant test added; changelog in 16de8df4. User verified manually.

title: Curly braces warn in metadata but parse clean in body (Q-1-20 asymmetry)
description:
A string containing {...} is accepted in document body but emits [Q-1-20] Failed to parse metadata value as markdown when it appears in front matter. Same input, different verdict depending on position. REPRO (verified 2026-08-11 at main 16226f63): # warns --- title: "Set notation {a, b, c}" format: html --- text # clean --- title: t format: html --- Set notation {a, b, c} Observed matrix, all checked against real renders: construct in body in metadata unmatched * ERROR Q-2-12, render fails WARN Q-1-20 + error span
WARN Q-2-9 raw HTML WARN Q-1-20 {a, b, c} CLEAN WARN Q-1-20 <-- the asymmetry [a]b clean clean The * and <...> rows are consistent with qmd's deliberate dialect strictness (unclosed emphasis is a hard error in qmd, so warning on it in metadata is if anything the lenient path) and are NOT part of this report. Only the braces row lacks an explanation. SECOND-ORDER EFFECT: a warned metadata value is emitted wrapped in , so the rendered document carries a semantic error marker on the value. For a title:

Set notation {a, b, c}

The text survives intact and I found no CSS styling that class (it is referenced only from crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs:115 and two test/comment sites), so nothing appears visually broken. But for the braces case the marker is unearned, and it ships in the user's HTML. CAVEAT ON SCOPE: I established that (a) braces warn in metadata, for both 'a{b}c' and 'Set notation {a, b, c}', and (b) 'Set notation {a, b, c}' is clean in the body. I did NOT isolate which brace construct is responsible (attribute syntax? shortcode scanning?) or test the full space of brace forms. Whoever picks this up should confirm the exact trigger before fixing. HOW IT SURFACED: while fixing smoke-all fixture regex patterns (bd-nhn7snpg, PR #503). 'strong.{0,60}>' was one of the candidate patterns and warned for this reason, which sent me down a wrong path before I isolated it. Fixtures now use the !str tag, which suppresses metadata markdown parsing entirely and is the documented opt-out.

title: hub-client: Monaco loads from jsDelivr CDN at runtime — editor stuck at 'Loading...' when CDN is slow/blocked/offline
description: No loader.config anywhere, so @monaco-editor/loader uses its default vs: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/monaco-editor@0.55.1/min/vs. The monaco-editor npm dep (same 0.55.1) is types-only at runtime. The PWA precaches app assets but has no runtime caching for jsDelivr, so an offline-first app hard-depends on a third-party CDN for its core editor: cold profile + slow/blocked CDN = editor pane stuck at the @monaco-editor/react 'Loading...' placeholder (editor never created — distinct from the bd-eakukmlr created-but-empty race; both look like 'editor unusable on open, fine on refresh'). Confirmed the CDN URL ships in built bundles (main-*.js, q2-preview-*.js). Fix: bundle monaco via loader.config({ monaco }) + self.MonacoEnvironment worker wiring (standard Vite pattern), removing the runtime CDN dependency.
close_reason: Fixed in 9d6a764f + bb0337a4 (PR #411, merged as 2d7a88fb): Monaco bundled via loader.config({monaco}) + worker wiring, e2e guard blocks jsDelivr; build heap raised to 4096 for the larger graph.

title: quarto-hub-mcp exit-drain test is flaky on macOS CI
description:
`ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp` > `exit-drain.test.ts` > 'exit drains outbound sync (bd-10deu8h4) > create_project then immediate stdin EOF must not lose the created docs' failed on the macOS leg of `Workspace TS suites` in run 32669594080 (job 97268232287), on a branch that does not touch quarto-hub-mcp. The ubuntu leg passed in the same run.

Surfaced by GH #250 / PR #579, which wired these workspace TS suites into CI for the first time.

NOT the same defect as the wasm-js-bridge cache eviction bug found in the same investigation (that one was a real logic bug in cache.js touch-on-read, fixed in PR #582). This one is a hub-sync/subprocess timing test and is so far uninvestigated — unknown whether it is a genuine race in the drain-on-EOF path (which would be a real bug: created docs lost when stdin closes promptly) or just test timing.

Worth chasing precisely because the failure mode it guards against — losing created docs on immediate EOF — would be a real data-loss bug if the race is in the product rather than the test.

Note when triaging: the `workspace-ts-suites` job runs suites as sequential steps, so a failure skips every later step. Each red run only reveals the FIRST failing suite; the affected surface may be wider than what CI has shown.

c-58yrfqk6.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-58yrfqk6.text:
Fixed on branch braid/bd-yw3mcdkg-flaky-macos-ts-suites (commit ee9de7b9a). Two findings overturn the triage recommendation.

FULL-SURFACE SWEEP (the sampling-bias question). Ran all 12 tiers of workspace-ts-suites to completion, no stop-on-fail, 30 iterations each, under mutual load from 10 concurrent agents (~1,656 tests per pass). Result: 12/12 tiers 30/30 green. Neither known flake reproduced on a 12-core M-series Mac. So the "remaining suites are unproven" worry does not turn up a third bug locally — but note this machine is ~4x a GitHub macOS runner, and the hub-mcp flake provably does not reproduce here either, so local green is weak evidence about CI.

BOTH RECOMMENDED FIXES ARE WRONG (measured, not argued):

  payload             drain-to-exit   still red with the drain off?
  64 x 64 KB (4 MB)   1980-2028 ms    yes
  64 x 48 KB (3 MB)   1478-1490 ms    only sometimes
  64 x 32 KB (2 MB)        -          NO - passes with no drain at all
  64 x 16 KB (1 MB)    506- 612 ms    NO - passes with no drain at all

(b) Reduce the payload: impossible. Below ~3 MB everything is delivered before stdin closes, the drain has nothing to do, and the test passes against a server that never drains. Binding floor ~3 MB vs a ceiling already strained at 4 MB - only ~2x apart on the fastest hardware available.

(a) --retry: actively harmful here. With retry:2 the test passes with drainMs:0 at BOTH 3 MB and 4 MB, because the drain-off failure is probabilistic and one of three attempts gets through. It removes the red while destroying what the test protects.

FIX SHIPPED: a QUARTO_MCP_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS test seam. Default stays 3000 ms; only exit-drain.test.ts sets it. Promptness stays asserted by stdio-hygiene.test.ts (real default, live sync) and by exit-drain's second test (budget actually binding). Binding verified: red 3/3 with the drain disabled through the seam, green 3/3 idle and 6/6 at load average 15-21.

TWO THINGS FOR SOMEONE ELSE TO PICK UP:

1. bd-7hd2gzf1's --retry=2 deserves re-examination. Same reasoning that killed retry here may apply there: if doc-inventory's failure is probabilistic, --retry=2 may be masking rather than tolerating. Also, quarto-sync-client ran 30/30 green WITHOUT --retry in this sweep, all 137 tests executing - the ~25% rate quoted in the workflow comment did not reproduce at all.

2. The CI sampling bias is still open and is NOT fixed by this commit. workspace-ts-suites has no step-level continue-on-error, so the first red step still skips every later one. A prototype (per-step id + continue-on-error + a gate step reading the outcomes, bash-3.2 safe for macOS runners) was built and verified to parse, then reverted at the user's request as out of scope for this strand. Worth filing separately.

c-dw1vjcy0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-dw1vjcy0.text: Also flakes on ubuntu-latest, not only macOS: PR #688 (feature/bd-3qych45b-hephaestus-hep-svg, no ts-packages changes) hit 'create_project then immediate stdin EOF must not lose the created docs' timing out at 30000ms on Workspace TS suites (ubuntu-latest), run 35251510384. Same test timed out on main today (run 35245424175, macos-latest, commit aa92c4b9e).

c-l8pd52r8.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-l8pd52r8.text:
Mechanism pinned.

Failure: `ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp/src/exit-drain.test.ts:82` —
'AssertionError: file doc for q2-mcp-hello-62.qmd must reach the hub — its only copy was in-process: expected false to be true'

Root cause is a fixed-deadline-vs-variable-throughput race, NOT a logic bug:
- `src/index.ts:279` sets `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS = 3000` — a hard real-time budget to flush outbound Automerge sync before process.exit on stdin EOF (the 'exit promptly' contract, bd-9jq2a060).
- The test deliberately sizes its payload to sit near that edge: FILE_COUNT=64 x FILE_BYTES=64KB (~4MB), with an in-file comment saying a single small file 'wins the race by luck'. So the margin is intentional.
- In the failing run the process exited fine within budget; it simply had not delivered all 64 docs when the cutoff hit. hubHasDoc() polled 5000ms/doc afterward and still saw doc 62 missing — the doc's only copy died with the process.

So the product contract works as designed; the TEST rides close to the edge. Whether ~4MB clears a loopback WebSocket + Automerge encode/sync pipeline in <3000ms depends on runner CPU/scheduling at that moment. No OOM/SIGKILL/timeout signatures in the logs. In the failing run the macOS leg took 2:35 vs ubuntu 1:52 for the same 11 steps (usually comparable, e.g. both ~1:53) — consistent with, though not proof of, a noisier runner tipping the race.

Recommended fix is a TEST fix, not a product change. Do NOT raise SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS — that weakens the exit-promptly contract. Either (a) add `--retry` for this suite in the workflow, matching the precedent set for quarto-sync-client's doc-inventory race (bd-7hd2gzf1, ~25% local / ~44% per-PR false-red, mitigated with --retry=2), or (b) reduce payload size/count enough to clear 3000ms reliably on a loaded runner while still exercising the backlog path.

CI record since #579 merged (5 runs): ubuntu 10/10 green every step, every run. macOS 3/5 runs fully green; 2/5 fail, each at a different step.

IMPORTANT sampling caveat: the workspace-ts-suites job has no step-level continue-on-error (fail-fast:false is on the OS matrix only), so a failing step skips all later steps. In the wasm-js-bridge failure the 5 subsequent suites never ran. The observed set is therefore biased toward 'first flake in step order' — the remaining suites are UNPROVEN on macOS, not clean. Worth considering continue-on-error or splitting into independent jobs so one flake stops hiding the next.

c-n0quhx2e.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-n0quhx2e.text:
CORRECTION to my previous comment (c-58yrfqk6), on the quarto-sync-client claim only. The exit-drain findings and the shipped fix are unaffected.

I reported quarto-sync-client as 30/30 green without --retry and said the bd-7hd2gzf1 race 'did not reproduce at all'. That was an unlucky-clean sample. A second batch of 20 runs caught it 3 times. Corrected figures: 3 failures in 50 no-retry runs = 6% raw per-run rate (batch 1: 0/30, batch 2: 3/20). Not 0%, and not the ~25% quoted in the workflow comment — 6% is the better estimate from n=50. All 137 tests executed in all runs and the Rust-hub tier never skipped (grepped for the SKIPPING sentinel across 60 logs: zero matches), so nothing was silently dropped.

The failure is identical on all 3 occurrences: doc-inventory.test.ts:140, 'reports index, text, and binary docs with states and heads'. The logo.png binary-file entry is MISSING from getDocInventory() outright — not a handleState mismatch as the strand description says.

Mechanism traced into client.ts: connect() awaits findDoc + whenReady(), then takes a SYNCHRONOUS snapshot of the index doc's file list (~line 932) and loads only the docs in that snapshot via loadFileDocuments(). The 'change' listener that catches later-arriving files is registered (~line 953) but is never awaited by connect(). So connect() can resolve having seen 1 of 2 files, and getDocInventory() called on the next line sees only one.

That makes it a production synchronisation gap, not test timing — so --retry=2 there is masking a real bug, not tolerating a flaky test. This strengthens bd-l0oc6se2 rather than weakening it. Analytically the retry drops a 6% per-attempt rate to ~0.02%, consistent with the ~3% the workflow comment observed.

Also noted, not filed: all 60 sync-client logs print 'TimeoutNegativeWarning: <N> is a negative number' at startup (e.g. -9, -218) from a setTimeout receiving a negative duration — likely a deadline-minus-now going negative. Never correlated with a failure. The same warning appears in quarto-hub-mcp runs.

title: admin_collect_lifecycle flake: doc id recovered from store differs in case (~1/12 runs)
description:
Symptom: collect_reverification_skips_rereferenced_candidate (and once collect_lifecycle_quarantine_restore_purge) in crates/quarto-hub/tests/integration/admin_collect_lifecycle.rs fail intermittently: manifest.candidates[0].doc_id differs from the created doc's DocumentId::to_string() by exactly one character's CASE (observed 2SZaW31GgRX5XkdH8H6M2yp95AEe vs 2sZaW31GgRX5XkdH8H6M2yp95AEe — flip at index 1).

Repro: run 'cargo nextest run -p quarto-hub --test integration admin_collect_lifecycle' in a loop on macOS (arm64, case-insensitive APFS) — ~2/25 iterations fail, each test in its own nextest process with its own TempDir, so no parallel interference. Failure depends on the random per-run doc id: some ids trigger it, most don't.

Context: the doc id is recovered from the filesystem store by list_doc_ids_filesystem (crates/quarto-hub/src/admin/scan.rs:80), which concatenates the two splayed path segments samod's filesystem adapter creates via key_to_path. Pure string concatenation of directory names cannot flip case, and case-insensitive APFS preserves creation case — so the directory must have been CREATED with the flipped case for some inputs, or the id is re-encoded somewhere between DocumentId and the on-disk path inside samod's adapter.

Not caused by the live-share branch (test and storage code untouched there; automerge pin is the same 0.10.0 plus the #1366 collector cherry-pick). Found during review of PR #464. Unknown whether Linux CI (case-sensitive fs) is affected. Next step: instrument a failing run to log the id at creation vs. the directory names actually written, then pin down where the case changes.

title: figures.qmd shows five cells with no fence opener (top-level doubled braces)
description:
docs/guides/authoring/figures.qmd has five TOP-LEVEL doubled-brace openers at lines 387, 405, 427, 447 and 466, all inside the ::: panel-tabset under 'Layout'. These are a DIFFERENT defect from the nested form fixed in bd-q250-nested-fence-blind-spot-t68z1lsw, and they are not new — they already warn today via Q-2-50's existing class path. WHAT THE READER SEES. A top-level ```{{python}} opener parses into a CodeBlock whose CLASS is the literal string {{python}} and whose text is just the body. Verified in a rendered fixture: it emits 
1 + 1
. So the reader is shown the cell body with NO fence opener line at all, wrapped in a block carrying a bogus CSS class. The page is trying to teach 'here is what a layout cell looks like' and omits the very line that makes it a cell. WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX. The nested form is a character swap ({{python}} -> {python}) because the outer display fence already exists. These five have no outer fence, so each needs WRAPPING in a ````markdown fence as well as de-doubling — a real editorial change per block that alters what the page renders (it adds the fence lines the reader should have been seeing). Five blocks, and they sit inside a panel-tabset, so the tab structure needs to survive the rewrap. SAFETY. Verified on branch braid/bd-q250-nested-fence-blind-spot-t68z1lsw-q250-nested-fence-blind-spot: figures.qmd has NO top-level executable cells — every {python}/{r} opener in the file is already nested inside a display fence — so no engine starts for this document and the rewrap does not risk execution, even before the nested-cell masking of bd-knitr-executes-nested-display-fence-atbtktdj lands. Rendering the page produces no cell-output and no class="cell" scaffolding. SCOPE DECISION. Split out deliberately by Gordon on 2026-09-03: the two NESTED defects (figures.qmd:278, docs/guides/formats/latex/index.qmd:47) were fixed alongside the diagnostic that found them; these five were held back as a separate editorial change.

title: No Python/Jupyter test environment provisioning for q2 (unlike quarto-cli)
description: quarto-cli provisions a full local python env for its jupyter tests: tests/pyproject.toml declares jupyter>=1.1.1 (bundles ipykernel), tests/uv.lock pins versions, tests/configure-test-env.ps1 and .sh run 'uv sync --frozen' to build tests/.venv -- installing ipykernel auto-registers a python3 kernelspec under venv/share/jupyter/kernels/python3, no separate register step. q2 has none of this: no pyproject.toml/uv.lock/venv-setup script anywhere, and .github/workflows/*.yml never installs python or jupyter (test-suite.yml:124 has a comment noting no setup-python step, confirmed by grep across all workflows). Consequence: crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/capture_splice_engines.rs::jupyter_capture_splices_into_preview_ast has never once actually executed in CI -- it always hits the is_available()==false skip path there, so the real jupyter execution path is untested by CI. Fix direction: add a tests/ or dev-env python provisioning script (uv-based, mirroring quarto-cli's pattern) and wire a python/jupyter install step into the relevant CI workflow so the jupyter integration test actually runs instead of perpetually skipping. Note: provisioning a venv with ipykernel would also incidentally make the specific reproduction in bd-zvf3e8n2 stop panicking on Chris's Windows machine, because ipykernel's default kernel name happens to be 'python3' -- but that's a coincidental workaround, not a fix for the underlying kernel-name-matching gap tracked separately in bd-db68qtuf, nor for the skip-guard robustness bug in bd-zvf3e8n2.

title: Audit codebase for String→{String, SourceInfo} refactors; consider WithSourceInfo<T> wrapper
description:
As we add source-info to more data types (e.g. RawResourcePattern in bd-c1et2), we keep introducing ad-hoc wrappers of the shape:

    struct RawFoo { payload: String, source_info: SourceInfo }

A parametric wrapper

    pub struct WithSourceInfo<T> {
        pub payload: T,
        pub source_info: SourceInfo,
    }
    impl<T> WithSourceInfo<T> { /* into_payload, as_ref, as_mut, map, ... */ }

would (a) eliminate boilerplate, (b) compose with iterators/traits, (c) make it easy to thread source info through generic code without writing a new struct each time.

Scope of the audit:
1. Find existing ad-hoc wrappers of this shape across crates (likely candidates: quarto-core, quarto-yaml-validation, quarto-csl, quarto-pandoc-types, quarto-error-reporting). Grep for 'source_info:' adjacent to a payload field; check ConfigValue/ConfigMapEntry shape; check whether RawResourcePattern (bd-c1et2) qualifies.
2. Decide whether unifying them on a common WithSourceInfo<T> is worth the churn — would all sites actually fit, or are some shaped enough differently (e.g. multiple spans per record) that a uniform wrapper would be procrustean?
3. If yes: design the API (which methods, Deref or no, serde behavior, source-info-merging for derived values), prototype on one crate, fan out a small refactor in follow-up issues.
4. If no: document the decision so the next person doesn't re-litigate it.

Not urgent. Pick up when there's slack between user-facing features.

title: Indented backtick/star continuation lines emit a spurious Space after SoftBreak
description: For 'hello\n  `code` here' q2 produces [Str "hello", SoftBreak, Space, Code ...] where pandoc produces [Str "hello", SoftBreak, Code ...] — continuation-line leading whitespace should be stripped (it is for plain prose continuations after bd-j7be7kuc). Mechanism: the gate-1 peeked soft-break path leaves the indentation unconsumed, and the external-scanner token that starts the continuation (code-span start, emphasis open) absorbs it into its own range (CST: code_span_delimiter spans the two spaces + backtick), which the AST builder then surfaces as a Space. Effect is a minor rendering difference (extra space after the line break in HTML). Pinned as current behavior by test_indented_continuation::controls_backtick_and_star_continuations in crates/pampa/tests/integration/ — update those cells when fixing. Predates bd-j7be7kuc; not part of that regression.

title: toc-location: left/body pages still reserve the empty right margin column
description:
A page with `toc-location: left` (or `body`) renders no TOC in the right margin, yet the right margin column is still reserved — the same ~150-200px of permanently empty grid track that bd-no-toc-reserves-margin-column-s8nonx0w fixed for `toc: false` pages. That strand enumerated pages with no TOC at all; it never asked about pages whose TOC is merely somewhere else.

Quarto 1 has the identical gap, so this is not a q2 regression and fixing it is a deliberate divergence from Q1, which is why it was scoped out of PR #643 rather than folded in.

## Where it comes from

Q1 answers "is the right margin occupied?" two different ways, and PR #643 ported both faithfully:

- `fullcontent` (`format-html-bootstrap.ts:1041-1071`) reads `hasToc = !!format.pandoc.toc` — a *config* read, true whenever the author asked for a TOC regardless of where it landed.
- `suggestColumn` (`:1959-1983`) reads `hasContents(kMarginSidebarId)` — a *DOM* read, true only when `#quarto-margin-sidebar` actually has children.

The split looks like an accident of scope rather than a design decision (one function had `format` in hand, the other had `doc`). In q2 the two live at `crates/quarto-core/src/template.rs` as `has_toc` (placement-blind) and `right_used` (placement-aware).

This leaves an internal inconsistency: under `page-layout: full` a left-TOC page *does* get a remedy (`<main class="content column-page-right">`, via the placement-aware predicate), while the same page on `article` layout gets nothing.

## Measured (q2 at PR #643 HEAD vs Quarto 1 dev 99.9.9)

Standalone page, `toc: true` + `toc-location: left`:

    article layout   q2  body=[quarto-light]  main=[content]                     margin-sidebar=0
                     Q1  body=[quarto-light]  main=[content]                     margin-sidebar=1 (empty)
    page-layout:full q2  body=[quarto-light]  main=[content column-page-right]   margin-sidebar=0
                     Q1  body=[quarto-light]  main=[content column-page-right]   margin-sidebar=1 (empty)

Neither engine emits `fullcontent` on the article-layout row; both reserve the empty column. (Q1 emits the margin sidebar element but leaves it childless, which is why its DOM read still reaches `column-page-right` on the full-layout row — the two engines agree there.)

## The change

One line in `render_with_compiled_template` — give `fullcontent` the placement-aware predicate:

    if !(has_toc && !toc_relocated) && !has_margin_categories && !page_layout_full {

Mirror it in `suggestMainColumn`'s sibling compose in `ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/PreviewDocument.tsx` (the `structuralBodyClasses` accumulator) to keep preview and render in agreement.

## Decide before doing

The cost is a diffable divergence from Q1: the porting projects (Positron docs et al.) compare q2's rendered classes against a Q1 baseline, so every `toc-location: left`/`body` page would show a new `fullcontent` delta that a sweep cannot distinguish from a defect. If we take it, it wants a note in whatever baseline those projects diff against.

Related deliberate scope-out in the same area, also inherited: `has_toc` means "rendered TOC HTML is non-empty", so a `toc: true` page with no headings reads as right-margin-free in q2 and right-margin-used in Q1 (the `404.html` case in the parent strand, where q2 is arguably the more correct of the two).

title: revealjs preview↔render parity audit across examples/presentations/*

'center' breaks title-slide vertical centering; 'title-slide' is a theme-CSS hook. Same root cause as F1: RevealDeck never forwards the section Div's Attr (div.c[0]) onto <Slide>/<Stack> — it reads classes only to flip incremental scope.

title: Automerge filesystem storage: doc-id case corrupted when splay prefixes collide case-insensitively (macOS)
description: collect_lifecycle_quarantine_restore_purge flaked once during a full cargo xtask verify run: assertion at crates/quarto-hub/tests/integration/admin_collect_lifecycle.rs:117 failed with left '3sjJPw5AxoWWPmiaj5zdgYQhfie2' vs right '3SjJPw5AxoWWPmiaj5zdgYQhfie2' — identical except the CASE of char 2. Mechanism: the filesystem storage layer splays doc ids into prefix subdirectories (automerge/<prefix>/<rest>); when two random ids differ in prefix only by case ('3s…' vs '3S…'), macOS's case-insensitive-but-case-preserving filesystem resolves the second doc's splay dir to the first's existing directory, and reconstructing ids from paths (list_doc_ids_filesystem / scan) yields an id with the wrong case. Passes in isolation; probability per test run is low (~1e-4 order for a random pair) which matches observing it once across many full-suite runs. Production (Linux, case-sensitive) unaffected, but local macOS dev hubs could mis-associate docs whose id prefixes collide case-insensitively. Suggested direction: reconstruct ids from a case-faithful source (file content/manifest) rather than path components, or make the splay case-insensitive-safe (e.g. lowercase the splay dir while keeping the full id in the filename). Discovered during bd-v8qc9zyc verification.

c-6ot7f2af.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-6ot7f2af.text: Second independent observation, same day: PR #489 macOS CI (github runner, case-insensitive APFS) failed collect_reverification_skips_rereferenced_candidate at admin_collect_lifecycle.rs:205 with '2xLPXb3F25kqoRZauW6zB1uKBsXP' vs '2XLPXb3F25kqoRZauW6zB1uKBsXP' — again a single case flip at char 2 (the splay-prefix position), in a different test of the same file. https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/31409825833/job/93524914291 — confirms this is the long-standing macOS-specific CI flake, hitting whichever admin_collect test draws colliding prefixes.

title: Q-13-13 can fire alongside Q-13-11 and then states something false
description:
crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/repo_actions_render.rs:130-136 pushes the Q-13-13 INFO diagnostic ("page-level repo-actions: true ignored") *before* the repo-action links are built, so it cannot know whether any link actually survives.

Reachable misconfiguration: _quarto.yml with website: {repo-actions: [edit]} and neither repo-url nor issue-url set, plus a page with front-matter repo-actions: true and toc: false. In that render, the author sees Q-13-13 first — whose hint text reads "The actions still render in this page's footer, at every width" — immediately followed by Q-13-11 ("no links can be built"). The Q-13-13 hint is untrue for that render: nothing rendered anywhere.

Likely fix: move the Q-13-13 push (currently at repo_actions_render.rs:130-136) below the links.is_empty() early return at :164, while keeping has_toc computed where it is now (the has_toc computation doesn't depend on link-building, only Q-13-13's *timing* does).

IMPORTANT: this interacts with decision D-11 in the original plan (claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-repo-actions.md), which deliberately reasoned about which early return the diagnostic should sit below relative to the page_flag == Some(true) && !has_toc gate. Re-read D-11 before moving the code — the fix is not a blind relocation, it needs to preserve D-11's reasoning about when the placement-loss INFO is worth emitting at all.

Filed per the branch's final review (M1). Requires two independent misconfigurations at once to reach, so not a merge blocker for bd-repo-actions-missing-99ezd2fe, but worth fixing so the diagnostic doesn't contradict itself.

title: Suppress noisy 'lua error' panic stack traces in WASM (cosmetic — caught control flow)
description:
rust_lua_throw at crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/c_shim.rs:452 panics with 'lua error' as a replacement for Lua's longjmp-based LUAI_THROW. The panics are caught by rust_lua_protected_call (catch_unwind) — this is expected control flow, not a bug. However, console_error_panic_hook prints the full stack trace for every panic, spamming both 'cargo xtask verify' output and hub-client production console (visible to users in browser).

Fix: install a custom panic hook that suppresses panics matching the Lua throw sentinel, while preserving full stack traces for genuine panics.

The hub-client e2e test helper already explicitly tolerates these as transient (hub-client/e2e/helpers/previewExtraction.ts:38-45).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-suppress-lua-panic-noise.md
close_reason: Implemented: LuaThrow sentinel + filter hook. cargo xtask verify clean (0 lua error mentions). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-suppress-lua-panic-noise.md

title: Centralize draft visibility: a single is_linkable predicate on ProjectIndex, and audit every enumeration site
description:
DocumentProfile.draft is enforced by hand at only 5 lines in the workspace (sidebar_auto.rs:219/228/246, aliases.rs:340, llms.rs:152), while 19 of the 25 sites that enumerate or look up profiles through ProjectIndex never check it — so drafts currently leak into the sitemap (website_post_render.rs:514, tracked as bd-4zdf), listings and RSS feeds (listing_generate.rs:184, previously untracked), and every body or nav link that resolves through navigation_href.rs (bd-p4sc). The auto-sidebar section-header leak (sidebar_auto.rs) was fixed by bd-sidebar-dir-index-md-5khf3lds, whose investigation produced the full audit: claude-notes/research/2026-08-19-draft-visibility-audit.md.

Rather than adding another hand-written filter per feature, give ProjectIndex a draft-aware surface — an is_linkable(profile) / linkable_profiles() pair in the shape of llms.rs's profile_has_companion (which already documents itself as 'the single answer ... so they can't drift') — and route every enumeration and link-resolution site through it. Carry a draft: bool on quarto_navigation::NavigationItem so explicit navbar/sidebar/footer entries can be gated the way Q1's navitem.ejs does. Land this before bd-w0o9's draft-mode config surface so that visible/unlinked/gone becomes one policy value read in one place; bd-p4sc (body links) and bd-4zdf (sitemap) then become thin consumers of the predicate instead of independent implementations. Include a guard test asserting no non-test code reads .draft outside the predicate, so the invariant does not silently decay again.

Q1 comparison (see the audit for detail): Q1 factors the policy into projectDraftMode/isDraftVisible in website-utils.ts, carries the draft bit with every resolveInputTarget resolution, and defaults to draft-mode: gone which empties leaked pages at post-process. q2 today is Q1's visible mode with none of the guards.

c-urwb7pz3.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-urwb7pz3.text: When this strand replaces the `item_visible(&DocumentProfile) -> bool` seam (added in the listing inline-records work, `transforms/listing_generate.rs`, currently a constant `true`) with real draft filtering, note the interaction the final review flagged: `item_visible` is applied on the glob path BEFORE the `matched_any` bookkeeping, so a glob whose only matches are drafts will also fire Q-12-19 'matched nothing'. Harmless today because the seam always returns true. The record path has no equivalent — it drops the item with no diagnostic. Decide both when you implement drafts. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-08-24-listing-inline-contents.md

title: Phase 9 follow-up: parallel Pass-1 over project files
description:
On a _quarto.yml edit, the Phase-8 cache-key invalidation propagates to every profile entry simultaneously. The orchestrator's pass_one loop (crates/quarto-core/src/project/orchestrator.rs) is sequential: it runs N head pipelines back-to-back. Trivially parallelizable since per-file work is independent.

Native: rayon + pollster-per-worker (matches the rest of the pipeline's Send-free trait shape). WASM: futures::future::join_all over the WasmRuntime calls.

Phase 9 plan §Risks calls this out — order-of-seconds latency on a 100-file project after a _quarto.yml edit. Active page render still feels snappy on warm-cache edits; this is the genuine cold-path.

title: revealjs auto-stretch image not sized: r-stretch img stays wrapped in
description:
Auto-stretch adds .r-stretch to a lone slide image, but the image is emitted as section > p > img.r-stretch. reveal.js's stretch layout selector is 'section > .stretch, section > .r-stretch' (direct child only), so the

wrapper means the image is never resized — it renders at natural size in the browser. Confirmed in Chrome (computed height stayed at the SVG natural 400px; hoisting the img to be a direct child of section made reveal size it to 443px). Quarto 1 hoists the img out of the

(output: section > img.r-stretch, bare). The code comment in crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/auto_stretch.rs:29-32 claiming nested

stretches correctly is wrong. Fix: convert the standalone Paragraph[Image] to Plain[Image] (writer emits bare img) so structure matches reveal's selector; handle Figure case (caption) too. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-17-revealjs-autostretch-p-wrapper.md
close_reason: Fixed and merged to main (4f4016b2). Paragraph[Image] now unwraps to Plain[Image] so reveal sizes section > img.r-stretch; verified in Chrome (443px vs 400px), Q1-parity confirmed, full cargo xtask verify green. Figure follow-up tracked by bd-38ioql41.

c-47eq9ivw.text: Design decided with user (2026-06-17): (A) scope = Paragraph[Image] case now, Figure case follow-up = bd-38ioql41. (C) AST-only fix in RevealAutoStretchTransform; explicitly NOT a DOM postprocessor — user strongly agrees, bar for ever adding one is 'an extremely strong reason'. Will communicate the anti-pattern via (1) corrected module-doc comment at auto_stretch.rs temptation site + (2) a one-line rule in CLAUDE.md Architecture Notes. (B) centering of bare stretched img to be verified in-browser at acceptance; add a small Q2-side CSS rule only if reveal core doesn't center it. Implementation not started; TDD per plan.

c-56ijr5zy.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-56ijr5zy.text: Implemented (Paragraph case) + verified. Fix: RevealAutoStretchTransform now unwraps a stretched Paragraph[Image] into Plain[Image] via new decide_stretch/StretchOutcome helper, so the writer emits section > img.r-stretch (direct child). Also unwraps author-supplied .stretch/.r-stretch images, matching Q1's hoist-any-stretched-img behavior. Tests (TDD, failing-first then green): lone_paragraph_image_becomes_plain + non_stretched_image_keeps_paragraph (unit), revealjs_auto_stretch_img_is_direct_section_child (render-path). Browser-verified in Chrome: img now stretches (computed 443px vs natural 400px) and geometry is identical to Q1 (parent SECTION, gapLeft 0/gapRight 413) -> design Q B (centering) resolved as no-op since Q1 is also flush-left. Corrected the misleading module comment + added a 'No DOM postprocessor' rule to CLAUDE.md Architecture Notes. Full cargo xtask verify green (all 14 steps; clippy caught 2 collapsible_if, fixed with let-chains). Workspace nextest: 10207 passed. Figure case deferred to bd-38ioql41. Not committed yet (awaiting user push approval per policy).

c-afjygm34.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-afjygm34.text: Confirmed Q1 mechanism: applyStretch (format-reveal.ts:949-1100) is a post-Pandoc DOM postprocessor (deno-dom). After adding .r-stretch it does explicit DOM surgery (lines 1041-1096): if the img isn't a direct child of <section>, it detaches it, removes now-empty ancestors, and re-inserts it at section level (handling figure caption/id/alignment for div.quarto-figure). Q2 has no DOM-postprocessor stage, so we can't port it literally. Proposed: achieve the same final DOM (section > img.r-stretch) at the AST level in the existing RevealAutoStretchTransform by converting the stretched Paragraph[Image] to Plain[Image] (writer emits bare img). Q2 emits no quarto-figure wrappers, so the figure/caption/alignment branch has no current Q2 counterpart. Open design questions: (A) scope paragraph-only now vs paragraph+figure; (B) centering of bare stretched img; (C) AST transform (recommended) vs new DOM postprocessor stage.

title: Engine file-conversion provenance is serialized on the wire but discarded in Rust (A′ remap)
description:
The TS engine host computes and serializes a real source map for engine-converted
files, and the wire type carries it, but the Rust side drops it at three points.
Diagnostics for a converted file therefore carry coordinates in CONVERTED space.

This is a quality gap, not a correctness bug: ParseDocumentStage already
compensates honestly by registering the converted text under a synthetic display
name -- `<foo.ipynb (converted by jupyter)>` -- so the user is told the
coordinates are not in their file. Nothing lies; the mapping is just absent.

WHAT ALREADY WORKS
- TS host serializes provenance: `serializeMappedString` (seam T4),
  ts-packages/quarto-engine-host-deno/src/mapped-source.ts
- Wire type carries it: `TsMappedStringWithMap { value, file_name, source_map:
  Vec<TsSourceMapEntry> }` -- crates/quarto-core/src/engine/ts_protocol.rs:254
- Honest degraded naming: crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/parse_document.rs:104

THE THREE DROP POINTS
1. crates/quarto-core/src/engine/ts_engine.rs:1006 -- matches
   `MarkdownForFileResult { result }`, takes `result.value`, ignores
   `result.source_map` and `result.file_name`, returns
   `SourceInfo::generated(By::unknown())`.
2. crates/quarto-core/src/engine/traits.rs:191 -- `markdown_for_file` returns
   `(String, SourceInfo)`; the doc records the SourceInfo slot as reserved and
   `SourceInfo::default()` in v1.
3. crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_claims_file.rs -- the stage does
   `.map(|(text, _source_info)| text)`, discarding even the placeholder.
   (NOTE: this stage is being renamed to SourceConversionStage in the
   2026-08-13 merge; the drop site moves with it.)

THE DESIGN ALREADY EXISTS (A′)
claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-plan1c-extension-integration.md:1230 specifies it:
register the original bytes under `source.path` as a second FileId
(`original_id`); add a `remap_via_source_info` walker (extend
`quarto_ast_reconcile::remap_file_ids` with a byte-range translator) rewriting
`Original(qmd_id, range)` -> `Original(original_id, mapped_range)`; feed it the
`source_map` already on the wire. plan1a-engine SEAM-3 prefers this generalized
remap path.

WHY NOW
A′ was deferred for two stated reasons, one of which has expired:
- "no consumer yet" -- bd-19nc56ao (.ipynb surface syntax, p1, open) IS the
  consumer: its per-cell coordinate design needs exactly this remap.
- "depends on engines computing real provenance, which they don't" -- still
  partly true, but the TS host now serializes segment provenance, so the
  producer side is no longer empty.

CONSTRAINT
quarto-source-map is affine-only by policy (the `Transformed` variant was
removed) -- see bd-19nc56ao comment c-3wtgfedn. The byte-range translator must
fit that, which is why bd-19nc56ao reaches for a per-cell virtual-file
coordinate system rather than a general transform.

SCOPE / TIMING
Explicitly NOT part of the 2026-08-13 ts-engine-extensions <- main merge
(claude-notes/plans/2026-08-13-ts-engine-extensions-merge-main.md). Gordon's
call: do this before filing the PR for that branch.

.ipynb.

Plan 7b (native content processors: percent + spin) moves conversion into Rust
